Masculine stems. Without the sun. For those ending in long ā, taking the stem viśvapā as the example: to viśvapā, the singular of the first case, su. Since its u is to be elided, it is deleted, and forming it by the sūtras sasajuṣo ruḥ and so on and kharavasānayor and so on: viśvapāḥ. Before au and jas: dīrghāj jasi ca: after a long vowel, before jas and ic. The letter a. Drinker of all. When endings beginning with letters of the ic collection, or jas, follow a long final, prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ, the long similar vowel before the first two cases,

the procedure of that sūtra does not apply here. Instead, by vṛddhi before ec, and by lengthening when ak meets a similar vowel, we get viśvapau and viśvapāḥ. For the singular of the second case: ami pūrvaḥ, before am, the former alone: viśvapām. For the dual: viśvapau. For the plural, śas: āto dhātoḥ, of the ā of a root. Whenever a case ending beginning with an ac, that is, a vowel, follows, from śas of the second case up to sup of the seventh, the ā of a stem that ends in the long ā of a root is elided. With the ā deleted: viśvapaḥ. The remaining case endings are also formed by the procedure just explained. For the third case: viśvapā, viśvapābhyām, viśvapābhiḥ. For the fourth: viśvape, viśvapābhyām, viśvapābhyaḥ. For the fifth: viśvapaḥ, viśvapābhyām, viśvapābhyaḥ. For the sixth: viśvapaḥ, viśvapām. For the seventh: viśvapoḥ, viśvapāsu. For the vocative: he viśvapāḥ, he viśvapāḥ. In the same way, somapā, kīlālapā, śaṅkhadhmā, hāhā, stvā, snā, and many others besides, are treated in the same way as viśvapā. Thus the operations for masculine stems ending in long ā have been explained.

Now I shall explain the operations for masculine stems ending in short i. Hari means the Remover (Hari), the Śiva-drinker, the dyer, the gandharva. For the singular of the first case, su: by the sūtras sasajuṣo ruḥ and khar and so on: hariḥ. To hari, au: by prathamayoḥ, of the first two cases: harī. To hari, jas: jasi ca, and before jas. When jas, the plural of the first case, is seen after the short vowels of the ik collection, the stem, which bears the name aṅga, becomes guṇa: hare plus jas. With the j deleted, by the sūtras for ay and av of the ec vowels and so on: harayaḥ. To hari, the singular of the vocative, which bears the name sambuddhi, su: hrasvasya guṇaḥ, guṇa of a short vowel. Short ik vowels become guṇa before the sambuddhi: he hare plus su. By the rule after a short vowel and eṅ, su is deleted: he hare. The dual and the plural are like the first case: he harī, he harayaḥ. To hari, the am and au of the second case: by ami pūrvaḥ, before am, the former: harim, harī. To hari, śas: with the ś deleted, by prathamayoḥ: harīs. Then by the rule that for śas the s becomes n in the masculine, the s having no vowel: harīn. To hari, ṭā of the third case: śeṣo ghy asakhi, the remainder, other than sakhi, is ghi. Among stems bearing the name nadī and stems in the short vowels of the ik collection, those that are not sakhi, that is, stems ending in a short ik vowel other than the word sakhi: when the remaining case endings follow, those that are not of the first and second cases, beginning with ṭā of the third and running up to sup of the seventh, the final vowel of the stem is given the name ghi, for a purpose. āṅo nā 'striyām, āṅ becomes nā when not feminine. After a stem final bearing the name ghi, āṅ, that is ṭā, becomes nā when the stem is not feminine: hariṇā. In the dual and plural there is no further operation: haribhyām, haribhiḥ. To hari, ṅe of the fourth case: gher ṅiti, of ghi, before what has ṅ as its marker. When a stem final bearing the name ghi meets following case endings bearing the name of those with ṅ as marker, that stem final becomes guṇa: hare plus e. With the ṅ deleted, by the sūtras for ay of the ec vowels and so on: haraye, haribhyām, haribhyaḥ. To hari, ṅasi of the fifth case: hari plus ṅasi. By the sūtra just explained: hare plus as. ṅasiṅasoś ca, and of ṅasi and ṅas. When there is a stem final letter of the eṅ collection, the a that remains when the ṅ marker is deleted from ṅasi of the fifth case and from ṅas of the sixth takes the form of whichever eṅ letter precedes it: hareḥ, haribhyām, haribhyaḥ. To hari, ṅas of the sixth case: being like the fifth, hareḥ. Hari plus os: by the rule for ik before a vowel: haryoḥ. Hari plus ām: nuṭ by the rule after a short vowel and so on; n becomes ṇ by the rule after r and ṣ; and by the rule before nām the stem final becomes long: harīṇām. To hari, ṅi: acca gheḥ, and at for ghi. When ṅi of the seventh case follows a stem final bearing the name ghi, that stem final becomes at, and by the word ca, ṅi too becomes au: hara plus au. By vṛddhi before ec: harau, haryoḥ, hariṣu. In the same way, śrīpati, agni, ravi, kavi, and many others besides, are treated in the same way as hari.

The word sakhi is a little different. To sakhi, the singular of the first case, su, is given: sakhi plus su. anaṅ sau, anaṅ before su. For the word sakhi, before su that is not the sambuddhi given in the sense of the vocative (the lord of glory, fire, the sun, poetry), the stem final becomes anaṅ: sakhan, friend, plus su. alo 'ntyāt pūrva upadhā, the one before the final al is upadhā. The letter before the stem final al, which is a consonant or occasionally even a vowel, bears the name upadhā. sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau, and before a sarvanāmasthāna that is not the sambuddhi. The ac that is the upadhā of the vowelless stem final letter n becomes long before case endings bearing the name sarvanāmasthāna that do not bear the name sambuddhi, the su given in the sense of the vocative: sakhān plus su. apṛkta ekāl pratyayaḥ, a suffix consisting of a single al is apṛkta. A suffix of a single al, that is, a single vowelless consonant, not a letter with a vowel nor two or three letters, is given the name apṛkta, for a purpose. halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal, after hal, ṅī and āp, and after long vowels, the apṛkta hal of su, ti and si. After a stem final hal, that is, a vowelless consonant, after the suffixes ṅīp and āp that form the feminine, and after long vowels, the single letter without a vowel that bears the name apṛkta, left when the u of su, the i of ti and the like, and the i of si are deleted, is to be elided. With su deleted: sakhān. By the rule for elision at the end of a nominal stem, n is deleted: sakhā. sakhyur asambuddhau, from sakhi, when not the sambuddhi. In this context of sakhi, the five case endings from su of the first case, the singular in the vocative sense that is not the sambuddhi, up to auṭ of the second case, which were earlier given the conventional name sarvanāmasthāna, are here given the name ṇit, that is, having ṇ as marker, for a purpose.

To sakhi are given au and jas of the first case, and am and au of the second. aco ñṇiti, of an ac before ñit and ṇit. When something bearing the name of those with ñ or ṇ as marker follows, the stem final ac, that is, the vowel, undergoes vṛddhi. So here too, the purpose of giving au and the rest, these four, the name ṇit is this: the stem final undergoes vṛddhi. By the sūtras for āy and āv of the ec vowels and so on: sakhāyau, sakhāyaḥ, sakhāyam, sakhāyau. To sakhi is given su of the vocative. Because the rule says "not the sambuddhi," the operation just explained does not apply here. Being like the case of Hari above: he sakhe. The dual and plural are formed like the dual and plural of the first case just explained: he sakhāyau, he sakhāyaḥ. In the second case plural, śas, it is like Hari: sakhīn. For the third case: sakhyā, sakhibhiḥ. For the fourth: sakhye, sakhibhyām, sakhibhyaḥ. To sakhi is given ṅasi of the fifth case. khyatyāt parasya, of what follows khi and ti. After a stem final khi, long or short, and ti, long or short, the a that remains when the ṅ is deleted from ṅasi of the fifth case and ṅas of the sixth becomes u: sakhyuḥ, sakhibhyām, sakhibhyaḥ. To sakhi, the sixth case: sakhyuḥ, sakhyoḥ, sakhīnām. To sakhi is given ṅi of the seventh case. aut, au. After a short i or a short u that bears neither the name nadī nor the name ghi, ṅi of the seventh case becomes au: sakhi plus au. By the rule for ik before an ac, yaṇ: sakhyau. In the dual and plural: sakhyoḥ, sakhiṣu.

patiḥ samāsa eva, pati only in a compound: pati outside a compound is like this. The word pati outside a compound, that is, pati by itself, takes only the operations of the word sakhi. But one joined in a compound, for example prajāpati, bears the name ghi, and so all its procedures are like the general case of Hari, the stem ending in short i.

The word kati, ending in short i, takes only the plural (lord); the singular and dual do not apply to it. bahugaṇavatuḍati saṃkhyā: those that bring in the many, vatu (lord of beings), and ḍati are saṃkhyā. Those that bring in the many, that is, those that take only the plural, and the suffixes vatu and ḍati, are given the name saṃkhyā, for a purpose. ḍati ca, and ḍati. Among those bearing the name saṃkhyā explained above, one ending in the suffix ḍati, such as kati, is given in turn the name ṣaṭ. pratyayasya lukślulupaḥ, luk, ślu and lup of a suffix. The elision of a following suffix is called luk, or ślu, or lup. For example, whether one says jas luk, or jas ślu, or jas lup, whichever occurs, it is simply the elision of that jas. To kati are given jas, the plural of the first case, and śas, the plural of the second. ṣaḍbhyo luk, elision after ṣaṭ. After a stem bearing the name ṣaṭ, jas, the plural of the first case, and śas, the plural of the second, are elided. Since the word kati, how many, bears the name ṣaṭ, jas and śas are deleted, and kati and kati are established. pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam, when a suffix is elided, the characteristic of the suffix remains. Although by the general rule the operation of the suffix applies by the characteristic of the suffix that was given, so that the stem final i would become e, there is the exception na lumatāṅgasya, not for the aṅga where elision is by lu. For what has been elided by the words luk, ślu or lup, the aṅga, that is, the stem, undergoes no operation, so it does not become kate but remains simply kati. For the plural of the third case: katibhiḥ. For the fourth: katibhyaḥ. For the fifth: katibhyaḥ. For the sixth: katīnām. For the seventh, and for the vocative: he kati, and so on.

The word tri, ending in short i, is also used only in the plural in the context of counting. So to tri are given the plurals of the first, second, third, fourth and fifth cases, and formed as for Hari above: trayaḥ, trīn, tribhiḥ, tribhyaḥ. To tri is given ām, the plural of the sixth case. trestrayaḥ, of tri, traya. Before ām of the sixth case, the word tri, three, becomes traya: tri becomes traya. nuṭ by the rule after a short vowel; the stem final becomes long by the rule before nām; and n becomes ṇ by the sūtras after r and ṣ and so on: trayāṇām. For the seventh: triṣu. Vocative: he trayaḥ.

The word dvi, ending in short i, is used only in the dual in the context of counting. tyadādīnām aḥ, a of tyad and the rest. For tyad and the rest, that is, the eight from tyad to dvi, whatever case ending follows, the stem final becomes a. To dvi are given the duals of the first and second cases, au. Joining the i of dvi, become a, with au: dvau, dvau. For the third, fourth and fifth cases: dvābhyām, dvābhyām, dvābhyām. For the sixth and seventh: dvayoḥ, dvayoḥ. When the word dvi, two, is preceded by a noun or a prefix, the i of dvi does not become a, all the case endings from su to sup apply, and then its procedure is like the general case of Hari, the stem ending in short i. With this, the class of masculine stems ending in short i has been explained in outline, with its general rules and its exceptions.

Now the masculine stems ending in long ī. vātapramī, a black antelope. su: by the sūtra sasajuṣo ruḥ and the sūtras for khar and so on: vātapramīḥ. To vātapramī, au and jas: by the rule for ik before an ac, yaṇ: vātapramyau, vātapramyaḥ. For the second case: vātapramīm, vātapramyau. For the third: vātapramyā, vātapramībhyām, vātapramībhiḥ. For the fourth: vātapramye, vātapramībhyām, vātapramībhyaḥ. For the fifth: vātapramyaḥ, vātapramībhyām, vātapramībhyaḥ. For the sixth: vātapramyaḥ, vātapramyoḥ, vātapramyām. For the seventh: vātapramī, vātapramyoḥ, vātapramīṣu. Vocative: he vātapramīḥ, he vātapramyau, he vātapramyaḥ, he vātapramyaḥ. These are established, and the procedure is easy to understand. In the same way, devayajī, atilakṣmī, and many others besides, are just like this procedure.

Stems ending in long ī that are roots differ somewhat in their operations. To sudhī, su: sudhīḥ. To sudhī, au and jas. aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau, before an ac, iy and uv for the i and u of śnu, of roots, and of bhrū (one who worships the gods; one supremely excellent). Whatever ac, that is, vowel, follows, the i, long or short, and the u, long or short, of the suffix śnu and of roots (a good mind, or an excellent mind), and of the word bhrū: the i's become iy and the u's become uv. Although by the general rule ik becomes yaṇ before an ac, there is na bhūsudhiyoḥ, not for bhū and sudhī. The ī of bhū and of sudhī does not become yaṇ before a following ac, and by its change to iy: sudhiyau, sudhiyaḥ. For the second case: sudhiyam, sudhiyau, sudhiyaḥ. For the third: sudhiyā, sudhībhyām, sudhībhiḥ, and so on. For the remaining case endings as well, there is no operation before those beginning with a hal, and before those beginning with an ac there is only the change to iy, so they are easy to understand. In the same way suśrī, yavakrī and the rest should be understood.

To pradhī, su: pradhīḥ. To pradhī, au and jas. er anekāco 'saṃyogapūrvasya, of the ī of one with more than one ac, not preceded by a conjunct. The root letter ī or ū at the end of a stem (beautiful form, or glory, or excellence, or happy prosperity; a barley merchant) that does not have a single ac, (supreme mind) that is, one having two or more vowels, and that is not preceded by several letters stacked together, becomes yaṇ before an ac: pradhyau, pradhyaḥ. For the second case: pradhyam, pradhyau, pradhyaḥ. For the third: pradhyā, pradhībhyām, pradhībhiḥ. The remaining case endings follow by analogy. Like this are also didhī, sudhi and the rest.

Because the rule says "more than one ac," the operation just explained does not apply to a stem with a single vowel. For example, nī has a single ac, so the operations of pradhī do not apply to it; apart from ṅi of the seventh case, its whole procedure is like the case of sudhī (holder; good mind): nīḥ, nīḥ, niyau, niyaḥ, and so on by analogy. For ṅi of the seventh case it is a little different: nī plus ṅi. ṅer ām nadyāmnībhyaḥ, ām for ṅi after nadī, āp and nī (leader). Before feminine stems bearing the name nadī, stems ending in āp, and the word nī, ṅi of the seventh case becomes ām: niyām. grāmaṇī too, apart from ṅi, the singular of the seventh case, is like the case of pradhī, and for ṅi it is like nī just explained: grāmaṇīḥ, grāmaṇyau, grāmaṇyaḥ and so on, and for the seventh: grāmaṇiyām.

sakhī and patī, ending in long ī (the village informer), are likewise like pradhī in procedure in all the other case endings apart from ṅasi of the fifth case and ṅas of the sixth. For ṅasi and ṅas, after khī and tī: to sakhī and patī are given ṅasi and ṅas, and by the rule that after khi and ti the following a becomes u, the a of ṅasi and ṅas is joined as u: sakhyuḥ, patyuḥ. The sixth case is also the same in both its form and its manner of formation. The word lūnī too is like the case of nī for ṅi of the seventh case, and like the procedure of pradhī for all the other case endings apart from ṅi. Thus the masculine stems ending in long ī have been explained in outline, with their general rules and their exceptions.

Now I shall explain the operations of masculine (one who reaps a field) stems in short u. To śambhu, su: by the sūtras sasajuṣo ruḥ and khar and so on: śambhuḥ, the Great God (Śiva). To śambhu, au: by prathamayoḥ: śambhū. To śambhu, jas: by jasi ca, u joined as o: śambhavaḥ. To śambhu, am: by ami pūrvaḥ: śambhum. au, being like the above: śambhū. To śambhu, śas: by prathamayoḥ and by the rule that for śas, n in the masculine: śambhūn. To śambhu, ṭā: by āṅo nā 'striyām: śambhunā. With the dual: śambhubhyām. To śambhu, ṅe: by gher ṅiti, u joined as o: śambhave. In the dual and plural: śambhubhyām, śambhubhyaḥ. To śambhu, ṅasi: by the sūtras gher ṅiti and ṅasiṅasoś ca: śambhoḥ, śambhubhyām. To śambhu is given ṅas; being like the case of ṅasi: śambhoḥ, śambhvoḥ, śambhūnām. To śambhu, ṅi: by acca gheḥ: śambhau, śambhvoḥ, śambhuṣu. Vocative: he śambho, he śambhū, he śambhavaḥ. These are established. In general, between the word śambhu ending in short u and the case of Hari ending in short i there is no difference of procedure, apart from small changes due to the different vowels. Viṣṇu, vāyu, bhānu and the rest, that is, all masculine stems ending in short u in general, are like this.

Within the stems ending in short u, the procedure of kroṣṭu differs a little from the general rule. To kroṣṭu, su. tṛjvat kroṣṭuḥ, kroṣṭu is like tṛc. The word kroṣṭu, (Viṣṇu; wind; sun) when there follow those given the conventional name sarvanāmasthāna, from su of the first case that is not the sambuddhi up to auṭ of the second, is alike in operation to stems ending in the kṛt suffix tṛc (jackal), and so its stem final u becomes ṛ: kroṣṭṛ plus su. ṛduśanaspurudaṃśo'nehasāṃ ca, and of ṛt, Uśanas, purudaṃśas and anehas. The stem final of stems ending in ṛt and of Uśanas, purudaṃśas and anehas becomes anaṅ before su that is not the sambuddhi. Since the ṅ goes with the a of na as its marker, it is deleted. By the sūtra "not the sambuddhi," the upadhā becomes long. By hal, ṅī and āp, su is deleted. By the rule for elision of n at the end of a nominal stem, n is deleted: kroṣṭā. To kroṣṭu are given au and jas of the first case, and am and auṭ of the second. ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ, of ṛt before ṅi and the sarvanāmasthāna endings: after stems ending in ṛt. After stems ending in ṛt, before the case endings bearing the name sarvanāmasthāna and before ṅi of the seventh case, the stem final becomes guṇa: ṛ is changed to ar. aptṛntṛcsvasṛnaptṛneṣṭṛtvaṣṭṛkṣattṛhotṛpotṛpraśāstṝṇām, of ap, tṛn, tṛc, svasṛ, naptṛ, neṣṭṛ, tvaṣṭṛ, kṣattṛ, hotṛ, potṛ and praśāstṛ.

For the stem ap, for stems ending in the kṛt suffixes tṛn and tṛc, and for the nine stems svasṛ and the rest, the upadhā becomes long before case endings bearing the name sarvanāmasthāna that are not the sambuddhi: kroṣṭārau, kroṣṭāraḥ, kroṣṭāram, kroṣṭārau. In śas it is like śambhu. To kroṣṭu, ṭā of the third case. vibhāṣā tṛtīyādiṣv aci, optionally before an ac in the third case and the rest. For the word kroṣṭu, whatever endings beginning with an ac follow, from ṭā of the third case up to os of the seventh, both alternatives obtain: the operations of the general case of śambhu, the stem ending in short u, and the change of the stem final to ṛ just explained. So it is treated as optional: kroṣṭrā, kroṣṭunā, kroṣṭubhyām, kroṣṭubhiḥ. For the fourth: kroṣṭre, kroṣṭave, kroṣṭubhyām, kroṣṭubhyaḥ. To kroṣṭu, ṅasi of the fifth case: formed like śambhu, kroṣṭoḥ. On the side of the change to ṛ: ṛta ut, ur from ṛ. For a stem ending in ṛ, when the a of ṅasi of the fifth case and of ṅas of the sixth meets the stem final ṛ, the two together become ur: kroṣṭ plus ur plus s. Then rāt sasya, of s after r: a vowelless s following a vowelless r is to be elided. With s deleted, and r made into visarga: kroṣṭuḥ. Before bhyām and bhyas: kroṣṭubhyām, kroṣṭubhyaḥ. ṅas of the sixth case too has the same operation as ṅasi of the fifth: kroṣṭoḥ, kroṣṭuḥ. Before os: kroṣṭvoḥ, kroṣṭroḥ. To kroṣṭu, ām of the sixth case, formed like śambhu: kroṣṭūnām. In one system: numaciratṛjvadbhāvebhyo nuṭ, nuṭ after those with num, after r with an ac, and after what becomes like tṛc. After stems whose final r has a vowel, after those that have taken the augment num, and after kroṣṭu when it becomes like tṛc, the augment nuṭ is certainly inserted before ām, the plural of the sixth case. With the augment nuṭ given: kroṣṭṝṇām. Before ṅi of the seventh case: kroṣṭari, kroṣṭau. Before os: kroṣṭroḥ, kroṣṭroḥ. Before sup: kroṣṭuṣu. Vocative: he kroṣṭo, he kroṣṭārau, he kroṣṭāraḥ. For śas of the second case, kroṣṭṝn is also found as an alternative. With this, the general rules and exceptions for masculine stems ending in short u have been explained.

Now I shall set out the operations for masculine stems ending in long ū. The word hūhū should be taken as the example. Apart from small changes due to the different vowel, it is like vātapramī. To hūhū are given the endings of the first case, and formed by the procedure above: hūhūḥ, hūhvau, hūhvaḥ. For the second: hūhvam, hūhvam, hūhvaḥ. For the third: hūhvā, hūhūbhyām, hūhūbhiḥ, and so on. Before endings beginning with an ac it changes to uv, and before those beginning with a hal there is no further operation, so it is easy to understand. In the same way aticamū and the rest, that is, all masculine stems in long ū in general, are like this procedure.

To khalapū, ending in long ū, su is given: khalapūḥ. To khalapū, au. oḥ supi, of ū before sup. Whatever ending beginning with an ac occurs, from su of the first case up to sup, the plural of the seventh, (very moving) the root ū becomes simply v. For this, the final ū must have two or three letters or more before it, without letters stacked together: khalapvau, khalapvaḥ. For the second: khalapvam, khalapvau, khalapvaḥ. For the third: khalapvā, khalapūbhyām, khalapūbhiḥ, and so on; the manner of formation follows by analogy. sulū and the rest are also like this.

svabhū is like the case of sudhī. To it, su: svabhūḥ. Before case endings beginning with an ac it changes to uv: svabhuvau, svabhuvaḥ. For the second: svabhuvam, svabhuvau, svabhuvaḥ. For the third: svabhuvā, svabhūbhyām, (a good cutter) svabhūbhiḥ, and so on. kaṭasū (self-existent), svayambhū and the rest are also like this. By na bhūsudhiyoḥ, not for bhū and sudhī, it does not become yaṇ; but as an exception the word varṣābhū, though it ends in bhū, does become yaṇ. To it, su: varṣābhūḥ, varṣābhūḥ. To varṣābhū, au. varṣābhvaś ca, and of varṣābhū. This word varṣābhū becomes yaṇ before the case endings beginning with an ac, of su and the rest. With the change to v: varṣābhvau, varṣābhvaḥ and so on (arising in the rainy season), like the case of khalapū. Since the commentary says, "dṛnbhū, kārābhū and punarbhū are also like varṣābhū," for these too all the operations of adding the case endings are like varṣābhū, and the forms are produced as just explained. Thus the operations for masculine stems ending in long ū have been explained.

Now (the masculine maker arising; arising again) I shall set out the procedures for stems ending in the letter ṛ. To bhartṛ, su. By ṛduśanaspurudaṃśo'nehasāṃ ca, and of ṛt, Uśanas, purudaṃśas and anehas, ṛ becomes anaṅ; by "not the sambuddhi," the upadhā becomes long; by hal, ṅī and āp, su is deleted; and by the rule for elision of n at the end of a nominal stem, n is deleted: bhartā. To bhartṛ are given au and jas of the first case, and am (holder) and au of the second. By ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ, ṛ is changed to ar, and by the sūtra on ap, tṛn, tṛc and the rest the upadhā is lengthened: bhartārau, bhartāraḥ, bhartāram, bhartārau. To bhartṛ, śas: by prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ, the long similar vowel before the first two cases, and by the rule that for śas, n in the masculine: bhartṝn. For the third: bhartrā, bhartṛbhyām, bhartṛbhiḥ. For the fourth: bhartre, bhartṛbhyām, bhartṛbhyaḥ. To bhartṛ, ṅasi: by ṛta ut and rāt sasya: bhartuḥ, bhartṛbhyām, bhartṛbhyaḥ. The singular of the sixth case is also like ṅasi: bhartuḥ. Before os: bhartroḥ. Before ām: nuṭ by the rule after r with an ac and so on, and the stem final becomes long by the rule before nām. Quoted in the commentary: ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam, after ṛ, the change of n to ṇ should be stated.

After the two, r and ṣ, and after the vowel ṛ, n also becomes ṇ: bhartṝṇām. Before ṅi of the seventh case, by the rule of ṛt before ṅi and the sarvanāmasthāna endings, there is guṇa: bhartari, bhartroḥ, bhartṛṣu. Before su of the vocative, by the rule of ṛt before endings bearing the name sarvanāmasthāna, there is guṇa: he bhartaḥ. The dual and plural are like the case of the first case: he bhartārau, he bhartāraḥ. In the same way naptṛ, hotṛ, potṛ and a great many others are like this.

To pitṛ, su: formed as above, pitā. In this case of pitṛ all the other procedures are like the previous case of bhartṛ, but before the endings from au of the first case up to au of the second, the upadhā does not become long. For bhartṛ (grandson; fire offering; fire offering) ends in the suffix tṛc, (male) while pitṛ does not end in tṛc. So: pitarau, pitaraḥ, and so on; the rest follow by analogy. jāmātṛ, bhrātṛ and the rest are also like this. nṛ ca, and optionally for nṛ. The stem nṛ is like the case of pitṛ apart from ām of the sixth case; before ām, the lengthening of the stem final is made optional: nṝṇām, or else nṛṇām. With these, (son-in-law; brother) the operations of masculine stems ending in the letter ṛ have been explained. In this context, stems ending in ṝ, in ḷ and in e are said not to exist.

Of the stems ending in the letter o, the word go should be taken as the example. goto ṇit, ṇit after go. For stems ending in o, such as go, the endings from the first case up to auṭ of the second, earlier given the conventional name sarvanāmasthāna, are here given the name ṇit, that is, having ṇ as marker. To go, su, au and jas: by the sūtra aco ñṇiti, of an ac before ñit and ṇit, the stem final undergoes vṛddhi: gauḥ, gāvau, gāvaḥ. Before am and śas of the second case: auto 'mśasoḥ, from o before am and śas. After a stem ending in the letter o, before am and śas of the second case, the stem final o and the following a together become ā. Before am: gām. Before au: gāvau. Before śas: gāḥ. For the third case: gavā, gobhyām, gobhiḥ. For the fourth: gave, gobhyām, gobhyaḥ. For the fifth: goḥ, gobhyām, gobhyaḥ. For the sixth: goḥ, gavoḥ, gavām. For the seventh: gavi, gavoḥ, goṣu. Vocative: he gauḥ, he gāvau, he gāvaḥ. In the same way sudyo and the rest are also like this. Thus the stems ending in o have been explained.

Now, of the stems ending in the letter ai, taking the word rai as the example: to rai, su. rāyo hali, of rai before hal. After a stem ending in the letter ai, such as the word rai, whatever case ending beginning with a hal occurs, the stem final ai becomes ā. (the sun) rāḥ, rāyau, rāyaḥ. For the second: rāyam, rāyau, rāyaḥ. For the third: (gold, or wealth) rāyā, rābhyām, rābhiḥ. For the fourth: rāye, rābhyām, rābhyaḥ. For the fifth: rāyaḥ, rābhyām, rābhyaḥ. For the sixth: rāyaḥ, rāyoḥ, rāyām. For the seventh: rāyi, rāyoḥ, rāsu. Vocative: he rāḥ, he rāyau, he rāyaḥ.

Of the stems ending in the letter au, the word glau should be taken as the example. Before endings beginning with an ac, au becomes āv, and before those beginning with a hal there is no further operation. So for the first case: glauḥ, glāvau, glāvaḥ. For the second: glāvā, glaubhyām, glaubhyām, and so on. nau and the rest are also like this.

iti pāṇini byākaraṇasya sūtādathanta burliṅgā sāmābhāḥ That is: from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the masculine stems ending in an ac are complete. With these, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down as notes the meaning, procedures, examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the procedures for masculine stems ending in an ac, in outline, with their general rules and exceptions, are for the present complete.

Now I shall explain the procedures for feminine stems ending in an ac. To ramā (the playful one), su: by hal, ṅī and āp, after a long vowel, and so on, su is deleted: ramā. To ramā, au. auṅ āpaḥ, of au after āp. After a feminine stem ending in āp, au, the dual of the first case, and au, the dual of the second, become śī. Since it bears the name śit, the ś is deleted, and by joining: rame. To ramā, jas: by prathamayoḥ: ramāḥ. To ramā, su of the vocative. sambuddhau ca, and before the sambuddhi. A stem ending in āp becomes e before a following sambuddhi; the stem final being e, the sambuddhi is deleted by the rule after a short vowel and eṅ: he rame. The dual and plural are like the above: he rame, he ramāḥ. To ramā, am: by ami pūrvaḥ: ramām. Before au: rame. Before śas, by prathamayoḥ: ramāḥ. To ramā, ṭā of the third case. āṅi cāpaḥ, and of āp before āṅ. A stem ending in āp becomes e before āṅ, that is, ṭā of the third case, and, by the word ca, before os of the sixth and seventh. Joining the stem final e: ramayā. Before bhyām and bhis: ramābhyām, ramābhiḥ. To ramā, ṅe. yāḍ āpaḥ, yāṭ after āp. After a stem ending in āp, when case endings bearing the name of those with ṅ as marker follow, the augment yāṭ is inserted: ramā plus yā plus e. āṭaś ca, and from āṭ. When an augment ending in ā, such as yāṭ, meets a following ending beginning with an ac, vṛddhi results: ramāyai, ramāya, ramābhyām, ramābhyaḥ. For ṅasi of the fifth case, yāṭ is given and formed as above: ramāyāḥ, ramābhyām, ramābhyaḥ. For the sixth: ramāyāḥ, ramayoḥ, ramāṇām. For ṅi of the seventh, yāṭ; by ṅer ām nadyāmnībhyaḥ, ṅi becomes ām: ramāyām. Before os: ramayoḥ, ramāsu. In the same way Gaṅgā, Durgā, Ambikā and many others are like this.

For the feminine stem sarvā, the first case, the vocative and the second case are like ramā just explained: sarvā, sarve, sarvāḥ; he sarve, he sarvam, he sarvāḥ; sarvām, sarve, sarvāḥ. The third is also alike: (she who is hard to approach; the goddess of Nagarakoṭa) sarvayā, sarvābhyām, sarvābhiḥ. To sarvā, ṅe. sarvanāmnaḥ syāḍ ḍhrasvaś ca, after a sarvanāman, syāṭ, and the vowel becomes short. After stems ending in āp that bear the name sarva, when case endings bearing the name of those with ṅ as marker follow, the augment syāṭ is inserted, and the stem final becomes short.

sarvasyai. For bhyām and bhyas: sarvābhyām, sarvābhyaḥ. For ṅasi: sarvasyāḥ, sarvābhyām, sarvābhyaḥ. For the sixth: sarvasyāḥ, sarvayoḥ, sarvāsām. For the seventh: sarvasyām, sarvayoḥ, sarvāsu. In the same way, viśvā and the rest should be worked out by analogy.

The word uttarapūrvā is like sarvā except for the case endings that have ṅ as marker. For those with ṅ as marker, the operations of both the ramā section and the sarvā section apply, so it is optional. uttarapūrvā, uttarapūrve, uttarapūrvāḥ; he uttarapūrve (the variegated one), he uttarapūrve, he uttarapūrvāḥ. For the second: uttarapūrvām, uttarapūrve, uttarapūrvāḥ. For the third: uttarapūrvayā, uttarapūrvābhyām. To uttarapūrvā, ṅe. vibhāṣā dik samāse bahuvrīhau, optionally, for a direction word in a bahuvrīhi compound. A direction word made into a bahuvrīhi compound and ending in āp, before case endings bearing the name of those with ṅ as marker, optionally either receives the augment syāṭ and has its stem final shortened, as in the sarvā section, or receives yāṭ, as in the ramā section: uttarapūrvasyai, uttarapūrvābhyām, uttarapūrvābhyaḥ, and so on.

vibhāṣā dvitīyātṛtīyābhyām, optionally after dvitīyā and tṛtīyā. For dvitīyā and tṛtīyā too, before case endings with ṅ as marker, yāṭ and syāṭ are optional. For example, for ṅe of the fourth: dvitīyāyai, dvitīyasyai; tṛtīyāyai, tṛtīyasyai.

The word ambā too is like the ramā section in every case except the vocative singular (saṃbuddhi). In the vocative it differs slightly: to ambā, the vocative. ambārthanadyor hrasvaḥ, shortening for words meaning ambā and for nadīs. The word ambā and the stems bearing the name nadī have the stem final shortened when the vocative follows: he amba. akkā and allā are also like this. Since the commentary explains, "Even where a word has the meaning of ambā, when a taddhita suffix ḍa, laC or ka is present and the suffix ṭāp is then given to form the feminine, it does not become short in the vocative," for example ambāḍā and ambālā, when the vocative is given, do not become short (Vasudhārā; the goddess who pierces) but are like ramā: he ambāḍe, and likewise he ambāle, he ambike.

The word jarā is like the ramā section before case endings beginning with a consonant (hal). Before those beginning with a vowel (ac), it is optional between jarā becoming jaras and the ramā section. For the first case: jarā, jarasau, jarasaḥ. For the vocative: he jare, he jarasau (old woman), he jarasaḥ. For the second: jarasam, jarasau, jarasaḥ. For the third: jarasā, jarābhyām, jarābhiḥ. For the fourth: jarase, jarābhyām, jarābhyaḥ. For the fifth: jarasaḥ, jarābhyām, jarābhyaḥ. For the sixth: jarasaḥ, jarasoḥ, jarasām. For the seventh: jarasi, jarasoḥ, jarāsu. These are the option in which it becomes jaras; the examples of the option that is like ramā are easy to understand, so work them out by reflection.

The word nāsikā is like the ramā section in the first case endings, in those with a vocative meaning, and in the singular and dual of the second case. Beginning with śas, by the sūtra that begins "pad, dat," which applies to śas and the rest, nāsikā becomes nas. So for śas: nasaḥ. For the third: nasā, nobhyām, nobhiḥ. For the fourth: nase, nobhyām, nobhyaḥ. For the fifth: nasaḥ, nobhyām, nobhyaḥ. For the sixth: nasaḥ, nasoḥ, nasām. For the seventh: nasi, nasoḥ, nasū.

The word niśā is also like ramā from su up to śas. From śas onward, by the sūtra that says "for śas and the rest," niśā becomes niś. For śas: niśaḥ. For ṭā: niśā. niś with bhyām: vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājachaśāṃ ṣaḥ, ṣ for vraśc, bhrasj, sṛj, mṛj, yaj, rāj, bhrāj, ch and ś. The seven beginning with vraśc, and ch and ś, when they are vowelless and stand at the end of a word, become ṣ whenever any letter of the jhal group is seen after them. By the rule "jaś in place of jhal before jhaś," ṣ is turned into ḍ: niḍbhyām, niḍbhiḥ. For the fourth: niśe, niḍbhyām, niḍbhyaḥ. For the fifth: niśaḥ, niḍbhyām, niḍbhyaḥ. For the sixth: niśaḥ, niśoḥ, niśām. For ṅi and os of the seventh: niśi, niśoḥ. niś with su: ś becomes ṣ, and ṣ becomes ḍ. By the rule "after ḍ, before s, dhuṭ," the augment dhuṭ is added; by the rule "car before khar," dh becomes t and ḍ becomes ṭ: niṭ t.

The words māṃsā and pṛtanā are likewise like ramā in all the case endings bearing the name sarvanāmasthāna. From śas onward they are optional, for the commentary says, "māṃsa, pṛtanā and sānu optionally become māṃs, pṛt and snu." So before the case endings śas and the rest, māṃsā optionally becomes māṃs, pṛtanā becomes pṛt, and sānu becomes snu. For śas: māṃsaḥ. For ṭā: māṃsā. For both bhyām and bhis, by the rule "elision of the final of a conjunct," s is dropped: māṃbhyām, māṃbhiḥ, and so on. Likewise pṛtaḥ, pṛtā, pṛdbhiḥ, and so on. snu is like dhenu, which will be explained below. viśvapā, gopā and the like are like ramā. With these, the operations for words ending in long ā that express the feminine have been taught.

Now the operations for feminine stems ending in short i will be explained. mati with su: matiḥ. mati with au: by the rule "of the first two," matī. mati with jas (she who drinks the variegated; the cowherdess): by the rule "and before jas," matayaḥ. mati with am: by the rule "before am, the former," matim. With au: matī. mati with śas, by the sūtra "of the first two": matīḥ. mati with ṭā: since here it is a feminine stem (intelligence), ṭā does not become nā: matyā, matibhyām, matibhiḥ. To mati, ṅe. ṅiti hrasvaś ca, optionally for the short ones before endings with ṅ as marker. Feminine stems in short i and u, and those in long ī and ū that take iy and uv, also optionally undergo the procedures of stems bearing the name nadī when case endings with ṅ as marker follow. āṇ nadyāḥ, āṭ after a nadī. After feminine stems bearing the name nadī, before case endings with ṅ as marker, the augment āṭ is given.

When mati is optionally treated in this way: matyai, mataye, matibhyām, matibhyaḥ. For ṅasi of the fifth it is optional: matyāḥ, mateḥ, matibhyām, matibhyaḥ. For the sixth too: matyāḥ, mateḥ, matyoḥ, matīnām. For ṅi: matyām, matau, matyoḥ, matiṣu. The vocative: he mate, he matī, he matayaḥ. śruti (hearing), smṛti (memory) and buddhi are also like this.

tri with jas. tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ, tisṛ and catasṛ for tri and catur in the feminine. tri, the word for three, and catur, the word for four, in the feminine, when a case ending follows, become tisṛ and catasṛ respectively. (Mind.) tisṛ with jas, catasṛ with jas. aci ra ṛtaḥ, r for ṛ before a vowel. The ṛ that ends tisṛ and catasṛ becomes a vowelless r before case endings beginning with a vowel: tisraḥ, catasraḥ. For śas: tisraḥ, catasraḥ. tisṛbhiḥ, catasṛbhiḥ. For the fourth and fifth: tisṛbhyaḥ, catasṛbhyaḥ. For ām of the sixth, by the sūtra on r before a vowel, nuṭ. na tisṛcatasṛ, not for tisṛ and catasṛ. As a general rule the stem final is lengthened before nām, but as an exception tisṛ and catasṛ do not become long before nām: tisṛṇām, catasṛṇām. For the seventh: tisṛṣu, catasṛṣu. For the vocative: he tisraḥ, he catasraḥ.

When tri has a nominal before it, as in priyatri, tri does not become tisṛ; and not only the plural but all the case endings apply. The procedure is like that explained in the section on the masculine stem Hari, except that ṭā and śas do not take n. Likewise priyacatur (three dear ones) does not become catasṛ; full examples come below. "Yet sometimes even with a preceding nominal it may become tisṛ and catasṛ," says the commentary.

For the word dvi: by the rule giving a for tyad and the rest before case endings (four dear ones), a; by adding to it the feminine suffix ṭāp, dvā is formed. To it the dual case endings are given, and when it is formed like ramā: for the two au, dve; for the three bhyām, dvābhyām; for the two os, dvayoḥ. With this, the operations for feminine stems ending in short i have been explained.

Now the procedures for feminine stems in long ī will be shown. gaurī with su: by the rule "after hal, ṅī and āp," su is deleted: gaurī. With au and jas: gauryau, gauryaḥ. yū stryākhyau nadī, long ī and ū expressing the feminine are nadī. Long ī and long ū expressing the feminine are called nadī. gaurī with the vocative su: by the rule "shortening for words meaning ambā," the stem final becomes short; by the rule "after eṅ and a short vowel," the vocative ending is deleted: he gauri, he gauryaḥ. gaurī with am: by the rule "before am, the former," gaurīm. With au: gauryau. With śas, by the rule "of the first two": gaurīḥ. For the third (the white one): gauryā, gaurībhyām, gaurībhiḥ. For ṅe of the fourth, by the rule "āṭ after a nadī," the augment āṭ: gauryai. For bhyām and bhyas: gaurībhyām, gaurībhyaḥ. For ṅasi: gauryāḥ. For bhyām and bhyas: gaurībhyām, gaurībhyaḥ. For ṅas too: gauryāḥ. For os: gauryoḥ. For ām, by the rule "after a short vowel and a nadī," nuṭ: gaurīṇām. For ṅi: gauryām. For os: gauryoḥ. For sup: gaurīṣu. vāṇī, nadī and a great many others are like this.

Since lakṣmī does not end in the suffix ṅīp, su is not deleted: lakṣmīḥ. The other forms are like gaurī. tārī and tantrī too are like lakṣmī.

The word strī with su: su is deleted: strī. strī with au: striyau, striyaḥ. (Flowing; a river.) Before case endings beginning with a vowel, the ī of the stem strī (the glorious lady) becomes iy: striyau. With jas: striyaḥ. For the vocative: he stri, he striyau (Tārā), he striyaḥ. strī with am (woman). vāmśasoḥ, optionally before am and śas. Before am, the singular of the second case, and śas, its plural, the ī of strī optionally becomes iy: striyam; or, by the rule "before am, the former," strīm. With au: striyau. With śas, by the sūtra just explained: striyaḥ; or, by the rule "of the first two," strīḥ. For the third: striyā, strībhyām, strībhiḥ. For ṅe, āṭ and iy: striyai, strībhyām, strībhyaḥ. For the fifth: striyāḥ, strībhyām, strībhyaḥ. For the sixth: striyāḥ, striyoḥ, strīṇām. For the seventh: striyām, striyoḥ, strīṣu.

śrī (the glorious lady) with su: śrīḥ. śrī with au and jas: by the sūtra that says "before a vowel, of śnu, verbal roots, bhrū," iy: śriyau, śriyaḥ. After śrī the vocative is given: śrī with su. neyuvaṅsthānāv astrī, not those standing in the place of iy and uv, except strī. "Except strī" means that the word strī, though it becomes iy, is still called nadī; but those other than strī that stand in the place of iy and uv, that is, long ī that becomes iy and long ū that becomes uv, are optionally not called nadī here in the feminine. Here, since śrī too is not called nadī, the deletion of the vocative ending, the shortening of the stem and so on are not done: he śrīḥ. For the second: śriyam, śriyau, śriyaḥ. For the third: śriyā, śrībhyām, śrībhiḥ.

śrī with ṅe. Although it is ruled as a general principle that those obtaining iy and uv are not called nadī in the feminine, there is an exception: the commentary on the rule "optionally for the short ones before endings with ṅ as marker" explains that long ī and ū are also optional. So before case endings bearing the name of those with ṅ as marker, both giving āṭ, as in the operation for nadī stems, and becoming iy are obtained: śriye, śriyai. For bhyām and bhyas: śrībhyām, śrībhyaḥ. For ṅasi of the fifth: śriyaḥ, śriyāḥ. For bhyām and bhyas: śrībhyām, śrībhyaḥ. For ṅas of the sixth: śriyaḥ, śriyāḥ. For os: śriyoḥ. śrī with ām. vāmi, optionally before ām. Those obtaining iy and uv are optionally called nadī before ām of the sixth: śriyām; or, treated as nadī, by the rule "after a short vowel and a nadī," nuṭ: śrīṇām. For ṅi of the seventh: śriyām, śriyi. For os and sup: śriyoḥ, śrīṣu. sudhī and the like are also like this. The word pradhī in the feminine as well differs in no way, in all its procedures, from what was explained in the masculine section. With these, the operations for feminine stems ending in long ī have been taught.

Now the feminine stems ending in short u (the good-minded one) will be stated. dhenu with su (the one in between): dhenuḥ. With au, by the rule "of the first two": dhenū. dhenu with jas, by the rule "and before jas": dhenavaḥ. For the second: dhenu with am, by the rule "before am, the former": dhenum. dhenu with au: dhenū. dhenu with śas, by the sūtra "of the first two": dhenūḥ. For the third (the milch cow): dhenu with ṭā; ṭā does not become nā: dhenvā, dhenubhyām, dhenubhiḥ. For the fourth: dhenu with ṅe, by the rule "optionally for the short ones before endings with ṅ as marker": dhenvai, dhenave, dhenubhyām, dhenubhyaḥ. For ṅasi of the fifth: dhenvāḥ, dhenoḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas of the sixth: dhenvāḥ, dhenoḥ. For os: dhenvoḥ. For ām: dhenūnām. For ṅi of the seventh: dhenvām, dhenau. For os: dhenvoḥ; dhenuṣu. For the vocatives, he dheno, he dhenū, he dhenavaḥ are formed. Apart from slight differences of change due to the different vowels, this is like the section on mati explained above. tanu and the like are also like this.

The short-u stem kroṣṭu differs in its operations from what was just explained. striyāṃ ca, and in the feminine. The word kroṣṭu in the feminine becomes ṛ-final, like a stem in tṛc, and so becomes kroṣṭṛ. ṛnnebhyo ṅīp, ṅīp after stems ending in ṛ and n. (The slender one.) After stems ending in ṛ and stems ending in n, the suffix ṅīp, which forms the feminine, applies. When ṅīp is given, it becomes kroṣṭrī (the vixen). All its procedures are like gaurī, explained earlier in the section on feminine stems in long ī. With these, the procedures for feminine stems ending in short u have been taught.

Now the operations for feminine stems ending in long ū will be stated. vadhū with su: vadhūḥ. With au and jas: vadhvau, vadhvaḥ. vadhū with the vocative su: by the rule "shortening for words meaning ambā and for nadīs," the stem final becomes short; by the rule "after eṅ and a short vowel," su is deleted: he vadhu, he vadhvau, he vadhvaḥ. vadhū with am, by the rule "before am, the former": vadhūm. With au: vadhvau. With śas, by the sūtra "of the first two" (the bride): vadhūḥ. For the third: vadhvā, vadhūbhyām, vadhūbhiḥ. With ṅe: vadhvai, vadhūbhyām, vadhūbhyaḥ. With ṅasi: vadhvāḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. With ṅas too: vadhvāḥ. With os: vadhvoḥ. With ām, by the rule "after a short vowel and a nadī," nuṭ: vadhūnām. With ṅi: vadhvām. With os: vadhvoḥ. With sup: vadhūṣu. These are formed like the section on gaurī. Likewise camū (the moving one) and the like are also like this. (She who speaks clearly.)

The word bhrū is like the section on śrī in all its operations; shortening it in the vocative is optional: he bhru, he bhrūḥ. The word punarbhū is like vadhū in all its other procedures. For ām of the sixth: ekājuttarapade ṇaḥ, ṇ when the latter member has a single vowel. When, in a nominal combined by a case compound, the former member contains a cause for n becoming ṇ, such as ṣ or r, and the member after it has a single vowel, that is, just one vowel (she who comes into being again), then, whether absent or, as in the example, present, n becomes ṇ, as in punarbhūṇām.

varṣābhūḥ. With au and jas: varṣābhvaś ca. The word varṣābhū becomes yaṇ whenever a case ending beginning with a vowel is seen: varṣābhvau, varṣābhvaḥ. For the vocative: he varṣābhūḥ, he varṣābhvau, he varṣābhvaḥ. In the other case endings too, before those beginning with a vowel (she who appears in the rainy season?), it becomes uv. Before those bearing the name of having ṅ as marker, āṭ is given. Before those beginning with a consonant there is no further operation. For svayaṃbhū, āṭ is given before those bearing the name of having ṅ as marker; otherwise there is no difference from what was explained in the section on masculine stems. With these, the procedures for feminine stems in long ū have been explained.

Now the exceptional ṛ-final stems. na ṣaṭsvasrādibhyaḥ, not after the ṣaṭ, svasṛ and the rest. To svasṛ and the rest, which by convention are called "bearing the name ṣaṭ," the feminine suffixes ṅīp, ṭāp and the like do not apply. Although the general rule "ṅīp after stems ending in ṛ and n" would obtain, this sūtra prohibits it. Those bearing the name ṣaṭ are these: svasṛ, tisṛ, catasṛ, nanāndṛ, duhitṛ, yātṛ and mātṛ. These seven are called "bearing the name ṣaṭ."

svasṛ with su: by the sūtra beginning "ṛt, Uśanas," anaṅ; by the rule "not in the vocative," the penultimate (upadhā) is lengthened; by the rule "after hal, ṅī and āp," su is deleted; by the rule "elision of n at the end of a nominal," n is deleted (sister; three; four; granddaughter; daughter; young woman; mother): svasā. Before au, jas, am and au, this is like the procedure explained for dhātṛ in the section on masculine stems (sister): svasārau, svasāraḥ, svasārau. śas and ṭā do not take n, because it is a feminine stem. With śas, by the sūtra "of the first two": svasṝḥ. With ṭā: svasrā, svasṛbhiḥ. The rest are also like the section on dhātṛ. All the other seven bearing the name ṣaṭ should be worked out by analogy with this very procedure. With these, the operations for ṛ-final stems have been taught.

Feminine stems ending in o are like the section on go explained among the masculine stems. Those ending in ai are like the word rai. Those ending in au are like what was explained in the section on glau. In short, for stems ending in o and ai there is nothing to elaborate beyond the procedures explained in the section on masculine stems.

iti pāṇinivyākaraṇasya sūtrād ajantastrīliṅgāḥ samāptāḥ: thus, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the feminine stems ending in vowels are complete.

With these, in The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, notes setting down the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the broad outline of the procedures for feminine stems ending in vowels, with their general rules and exceptions, is for the present complete.

Now the neuter stems ending in vowels will be explained. As the general case, let the word jñāna, ending in short a, serve as the example. jñāna with su. ato 'm, am for s after a. After the short a ending a neuter, su of the first case and am of the second become am. su becomes am; by the rule "before am, the former": jñānam. jñāna with au. napuṃsakāc ca, and after a neuter. After a neuter stem, au of the first case and au of the second case (wisdom) become śī, and by convention this is called "bearing the name bha."

au becomes śī. yasyeti ca, and before ī, of what. By the rule "before ī, before what bears the name bha, and before taddhita suffixes, the a and i at the end of the stem are elided," the elision of a would obtain as a general rule; but as an exception the commentary quotes another source: "When au has become śī, a is not elided." So a is not elided, and the sandhi is made: jñāne.

jñāna with jas. jaśśasoḥ śiḥ, śi for jas and śas. After a neuter stem, jas of the first case and śas of the second become śi. śi sarvanāmasthānam, śi bears the name sarvanāmasthāna. The śi into which jas and śas have turned is given the name sarvanāmasthāna. napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ, of a neuter ending in jhal or a vowel. After neuter stems ending in a letter of the jhal group or in a vowel, when something bearing the name sarvanāmasthāna follows, the augment num is given. The purpose of stating u: it means that m is not carried, and that it follows the vowel-final. By the rule "and before what bears the name sarvanāmasthāna, other than the vocative," the penultimate (upadhā) is lengthened: jñānāni. In the second case too, both the way of forming and the forms are the same: jñānam, jñāne, jñānāni. For the vocative, by the rule "after eṅ and a short vowel," the vocative ending is deleted: he jñāna, he jñāne, he jñānāni. All the remaining case endings are like the section on Rāma explained among the masculine stems. In the same way dhana, vana, phala and a great many others are like this.

katara and the like differ in su and am. aḍ ḍatarādibhyaḥ pañcabhyaḥ, aḍ after the five beginning with ḍatara. In the neuter, after the five, that is, katara, ending in ḍatara, katama, anyatara, anyatama (wealth; forest; fruit) and itara, su of the first case and am of the second become adḍ. katara with adḍ results. ṭeḥ, of ṭi. When a suffix with ḍ as marker follows, the ṭi of the stem and the like is to be elided. The ṭi is deleted and the result drawn: kataraḍ. vāvasāne, optionally at a pause. At a pause, that is, when a word ends in a consonant with no vowel, if that letter belongs to the jhal group, it optionally becomes the letter of the car group homorganic with it: katarat, katarad. For au and jas: katare, katarāṇi. The vocative too is like the first case: he katarad, he katarat, he katare, he katarāṇi. In the second case too: katarad, katarad, katare, katarāṇi. The remaining case endings are like the stem sarva explained in the masculine section. In the same way katama, anyatara, anyatama, itara and the rest are also like this.

For the stem ajara, before endings beginning with a vowel, by the sūtra explained earlier, it is optional whether it becomes ajaras or not. For su: ajaram, ajarasam. For au: ajare, ajarasī. For jas, on the option where it does not become ajaras: ajarāṇi. On the other option, ajaras with num and i standing: sāntamahataḥ saṃyogasya, of the conjunct of an s-final and of mahat. The penultimate of a stem ending in s with n joined to it, that is, stacked in a conjunct, and of mahat, such as the n given by num, is lengthened before case endings bearing the name sarvanāmasthāna other than the vocative: ajarāṃsi. For the vocative: he ajara, he ajare, he ajarasī, he ajarāṇi, he ajarāṃsi. The second case is like the first. For the third: ajareṇa, ajarasā, ajarābhyām, ajaraiḥ. For the fourth: ajarāya, ajarase, ajarābhyām, ajarebhyaḥ. For the fifth: ajarāt, ajarasaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For the sixth: ajarasya, ajarasaḥ, ajarayoḥ, ajarasoḥ, ajarāṇām, ajarasām. For the seventh: ajare, ajarasi, ajarayoḥ, ajarasoḥ, ajareṣu.

For hṛdaya, the first case endings, the vocatives, and the singular and dual of the second case are like the section on jñāna: hṛdayam, hṛdaye, hṛdayāni; he hṛdaya, he hṛdaye, he hṛdayāni; hṛdayam, hṛdaye. hṛdaya with śas: by the sūtra that says "for śas and the rest" (the heart), hṛdaya becomes hṛd. By "śi for jas and śas" and "of a neuter ending in jhal or a vowel," num: hṛndi; on the other option, hṛdayāni. For ṭā: hṛdā, hṛdayena. For bhyām: hṛdbhyām, hṛdayābhyām. For bhis: hṛdbhiḥ, hṛdayaiḥ. For ṅe: hṛde, hṛdayāya; bhyām is the same. For bhyas: hṛdbhyaḥ, hṛdayebhyaḥ. For ṅasi: hṛdaḥ, hṛdayāt; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: hṛdaḥ, hṛdayasya. For os: hṛdoḥ, hṛdayayoḥ. For ām: hṛdām, hṛdayānām. For ṅi: hṛdi, hṛdaye; os is the same. hṛtsu, hṛdayeṣu.

udaka too, from su of the first case up to auṭ of the second, is like jñāna: udakam, udake, udakāni; he udaka, he udake, he udakāni. For the second: udakam, udake. For śas: udakāni, udāni. For ṭā: udakena; on the other option it becomes udan (water). By the rule on elision of the a of an, the a of the penultimate is deleted: udnā. For bhyām: udakābhyām; on the other option, by the rule "elision of n at the end of a nominal," n is deleted: udabhyām. For bhis: udakaiḥ, udabhiḥ. For ṅe: udne, udakāya. For bhyām and bhyas: udabhyām, udakābhyām, udabhyaḥ, udakebhyaḥ. For ṅasi: udnaḥ, udakāt; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: udnaḥ, udakasya. For os: udnoḥ, udakayoḥ. For ām: udnām, udakānām. For ṅi: udni, udake; os is the same. For sup: udasu, udakeṣu.

āsana too is like the first case and the rest: āsanam, āsane, āsanāni; he āsana, he āsane, he āsanāni, he āsanāni. For the second: āsanam, āsane. For śas: āsāni, āsanāni. For ṭā: āsnā, āsanena. For bhyām: āsabhyām, āsanābhyām. The remaining forms also, in both ways (seat), are like udaka.

For śīrṣa (head) too, the first five are like jñāna: śīrṣam, śīrṣe, śīrṣāṇi; he śīrṣa, he śīrṣe, he śīrṣāṇi. For am: śīrṣam. For au: śīrṣe. For śas: śīrṣāṇi. The commentary quotes another source: "Before ṭā and the rest, śīrṣa optionally becomes śīrṣan."

The stem śīrṣa, wherever any case ending is seen from ṭā of the third case up to sup of the seventh, optionally becomes śīrṣan. So for ṭā: śīrṣeṇa. When it is changed to śīrṣan, by the rule on elision of the a of an, the a is deleted, and by ṣ, r and the like, n becomes ṇ: śīrṣṇā. For bhyām: śīrṣābhyām; on the other option, by the rule "elision of n at the end of a nominal," n is deleted: śīrṣabhyām. For bhis: śīrṣaiḥ, śīrṣabhiḥ. For ṅe: śīrṣāya, śīrṣṇe; bhyām is the same. For bhyas: śīrṣebhyaḥ, śīrṣabhyaḥ. For ṅasi: śīrṣāt, śīrṣṇaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: śīrṣasya, śīrṣṇaḥ. For os: śīrṣayoḥ, śīrṣṇoḥ. For ām: śīrṣāṇām, śīrṣṇām. For ṅi: śīrṣe, śīrṣṇi; os is the same. For sup: śīrṣeṣu, śīrṣasu.

hrasvo napuṃsake prātipadikasya, the shortening of a nominal in the neuter. Stem-final long vowels become short in the neuter. For example, śrīpā ends in long ā, yet by the sūtra just explained it becomes short: śrīpam, śrīpe, śrīpāṇi, and so on. Every long ā becomes short a, and all the operations on meeting the case endings are like those explained in the section on jñāna, the general case of stems ending in short a. With these (the one who enjoys glory), the operations for neuter stems in long ā and short a have been explained.

Now the neuter stems ending in long and short i will be explained. vāri with su. svamor napuṃsakāt, of su and am after a neuter. "After a neuter stem, su of the first case and am of the second disappear." By this su disappears: vāri. vāri with au: by the rule "and after a neuter," au becomes śī. iko 'ci vibhaktau, of ik before a vowel case ending (water). When a neuter stem ends in a letter of the ik group and a case ending beginning with a vowel occurs, the augment num is given: vāriṇī. For jas: by "śi for jas and śas," by "before a vowel case ending," num, and by the rule "other than the vocative," the penultimate is lengthened: vārīṇi. For the vocative: by the rule "guṇa of a short vowel," and by the rule "after a short vowel and eṅ," the vocative ending is deleted: he vāre, he vāriṇī, he vārīṇi. The second case is like the first. For ṭā: vāriṇā. For bhyām: vāribhyām. For bhis: vāribhiḥ. For ṅe: vāriṇe; bhyām is the same. For bhyas: vāribhyaḥ. For ṅasi: vāriṇaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: vāriṇaḥ. For os: vāriṇoḥ. vārīṇām. For ṅi: vāriṇi; os is the same. For sup: vāriṣu.

anādi too is like vāri up to the case ending ṭā. For the first case: anādi, anādinī, anādīni. For the vocative: he anāde, he anādinī, he anādīni. The second case too is like the first. anādi with ṭā. tṛtīyādiṣu bhāṣitapuṃskaṃ puṃvad gālavasya, in the third and following, like the masculine, if it is also used in the masculine, according to Gālava. After stems ending in a letter of the ik group, before the case endings beginning with a vowel, from ṭā of the third up to sup of the seventh, to follow the procedures explained earlier in the section on masculine stems, and also to give num before vowel-initial endings according to the neuter's own system, is the system of the ancient sage Gālava. anādinā: the form is the same on both systems. On the masculine system ṭā becomes nā; on the neuter's own system num is given and the form drawn. For bhyām and bhis: anādibhyām, anādibhiḥ. For ṅe: anādaye, anādine; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: anādeḥ, anādinaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: anādeḥ, anādinaḥ. For os: anādyoḥ, anādinoḥ. For ām: anādīnām, anādīnām. For ṅi: anādini; os is the same. anādiṣu.

asthi. For au: asthinī. For jas: asthīni. For the vocative: he asthe, he asthinī, he asthīni, he asthīni. The second case is alike. asthidadhisakthyakṣṇām anaṅ udāttaḥ, anaṅ, accented udātta, for asthi, dadhi, sakthi and akṣi. For the neuter stems asthi and the rest, before the case endings beginning with a vowel, ṭā and the rest (bone), the stem final becomes anaṅ, and this is called udātta. asthi with ṭā: the stem final becomes anaṅ; by the rule on elision of the a of an, the a is deleted: asthnā. For bhyām and bhis: asthibhyām, asthibhiḥ. For ṅe: asthne; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: asthnaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: asthnaḥ. For os: asthnoḥ. For ām: asthnām. By the rule "optionally before ṅi and śī," asthani; os is the same. For sup: asthiṣu. dadhi, sakthi and akṣi are also like this. In the commentary there occurs: "priyadadhnā brāhmaṇena, priyasakthnā śūdreṇa, priyākṣṇā sarveṇa, priyāsthnā śunā." These are forms with ṭā given (curd; strength; eye. To the brahmin, curd is dear; to the śūdra caste, strength is dear; to all, the eye is dear; to the dog, the bone is dear).

For sudhī too, by the rule "the shortening of a nominal in the neuter," the stem final becomes short, and su is deleted: sudhi. For au: sudhinī. For jas: sudhīni. For the vocatives: he sudhi (good intellect), he sudhe, he sudhinī, he sudhīni. The second case is like the first. sudhi with ṭā: by the rule "in the third and following," on the neuter's own system num is given: sudhinā; on the masculine system the stem final does not become short, and by the rule "before a vowel" it becomes iy: sudhiyā, sudhibhyām, sudhibhiḥ. For ṅe: sudhine, sudhiye; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: sudhinaḥ, sudhiyaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: sudhiyaḥ. For os: sudhinoḥ, sudhiyoḥ. For ām: sudhīnām, sudhiyām. For ṅi: sudhiyi; os is the same. For sup: sudhiṣu. pradhī and the like are also like this.

With these, the procedure for neuter stems ending in long and short i has been taught.

Now I shall explain the neuter stems ending in u. madhu with su: for the neuter, su and am are elided: madhu. For au, śī; num is added: madhunī. For jas, śi and num; the penultimate is lengthened: madhūni. Vocative: he madhu, he madho, he madhūni. The second case is like the first. For ṭā, num: madhunā, madhubhyām, madhubhiḥ. For ṅe: madhune; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi (madhu meaning honey): madhunaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: madhunaḥ. For os: madhunoḥ. For ām: madhūnām. For ṅi: madhuni; os is the same. madhuṣu. ambu is also like this.

sulū too: the stem final becomes short. In the first case: sulu, sulunī, sulūni. He sulu, he sulo, he sulunī, he sulūni. The second case is like the first. For ṭā: on the neuter's own system, num: sulunā. On the masculine system (sulū meaning one who cuts well) the stem final does not become short, and yaṇ replaces ik before a vowel: sulvā, sulubhyām, sulubhiḥ. For ṅe: sulune, sulve; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: sulunaḥ, sulvaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: sulunaḥ, sulvaḥ. For os: sulunoḥ, sulvoḥ. For ām: sulūnām, sulvām. For ṅi: suluni, sulvi; os is the same. suluṣu. silū is also like this.

For kroṣṭu with su: for the neuter, su and am are elided: priyakroṣṭu. For au, śī: priyakroṣṭunī. For jas, śi: priyakroṣṭūni. Vocative: he priyakroṣṭu, he priyakroṣṭo; the dual and the plural are the same as before. The second case is like the first. For ṭā: on the neuter's own system, num: priyakroṣṭunā. On the masculine system the stem final becomes ṛ, and yaṇ replaces ik before a vowel: priyakroṣṭrā, priyakroṣṭubhyām, priyakroṣṭubhiḥ. For ṅe: priyakroṣṭune, priyakroṣṭre; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: priyakroṣṭunaḥ, priyakroṣṭuḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. ṅas too is like ṅasi. For os: priyakroṣṭunoḥ, priyakroṣṭroḥ. For ām: priyakroṣṭūnām. For ṅi: priyakroṣṭuni, priyakroṣṭari; os is the same. priyakroṣṭuṣu. With these, the neuter stems ending in long and short u have been explained.

The neuter ending in ṛ: jñātṛ with su; su and am are elided: jñātṛ. For au, śī: jñātṛṇī. Vocative: he jñātṛ, he jñātṛṇī, he jñātṝṇi. The second case too is the same. For ṭā: jñātṛṇā, jñātrā; bhyām and bhis are the same. For ṅe: jñātṛṇe, jñātre; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: jñātṛṇaḥ, jñātuḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. ṅas is like ṅasi. For os: jñātṛṇoḥ, jñātroḥ. For ām: jñātṝṇām. For ṅi: jñātṛṇi, jñātari; os is the same. jñātṛṣu. kartṛ is also like this. With these, the neuter stems ending in ṛ have been explained.

Now the stems ending in ec. pradyo with su. By the rule eca igghāsvādeśe: when a short vowel is substituted for ec, it is always made an ik. Neuter stems ending in a letter of the group ec become the short letters of the group ik, so it becomes pradyu. su is dropped: pradyu, pradyunī, pradyūni. He pradyu, he pradyunī, he pradyūni. The second case is the same. From ṭā onward, before endings beginning with a vowel: on the procedure of the neuter's own system, num is given; on the masculine system, ec is replaced by ay, av and so on: pradyunā, pradyavā, pradyubhyām, pradyubhiḥ; pradyune, pradyave; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: pradyunaḥ, pradyoḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. ṅas too is like ṅasi. For os: pradyunoḥ, pradyanoḥ, pradyavoḥ. For ām: pradyūnām, pradyavām. For ṅi: pradyavi; os is the same. pradyuṣu.

prarai, meaning excellent wealth, also becomes prari: prari, prariṇī, prarīṇi. He prari, he prariṇī, he prarīṇi. The second case is the same. For ṭā and the rest: on the neuter's own system, num is given; on the masculine system, ai becomes āy, just as was explained in the section on rai. sunau, meaning a good boat, becomes sunu. Apart from the difference between āy and āv, it is like the case of prarai.

iti pāṇinibyākaraṇasya sūtādajanha napuṃsakaliṅgāni samāptāḥ That is: from the sūtra of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the neuter stems ending in vowels are complete. With these, in the work called The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down as notes the meaning, the procedures, the illustrative examples and so forth of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the operations of the neuter stems ending in vowels, in their general rules together with their exceptions, have for now been completed in broad outline.

Now, among the stems ending in hal, that is, ending in consonants, I shall first explain the masculine stems. First, among those ending in h, there is lih. ho ḍhaḥ: h becomes ḍh. A vowelless h before a letter of the group jhal, and a vowelless h at the end of a word, becomes ḍh. lih with su: by "h becomes ḍh," h becomes ḍh. By the rule beginning "after hal, ṅī and āp, and after a long vowel," su is dropped. By "optionally at a pause," liḍ, liṭ, meaning one who tastes. For au and jas, by "what lacks a vowel is joined to what follows": lihau, lihaḥ. In the second case: liham, lihau, lihaḥ. For ṭā: lihā. For bhyām: by "h becomes ḍh," and by "jaś replaces jhal before jhaś," ḍh is turned into ḍ: liḍbhyām; for bhis: liḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: lihe. For bhyām and bhyas: liḍbhyām, liḍbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: lihaḥ. For bhyām and bhyas: liḍbhyām, liḍbhyaḥ. For ṅas: lihaḥ. For ām: lihām. For ām: lihām. For ṅi: lihi. For os: lihoḥ. For sup: by "h becomes ḍh," and by "car replaces jhal before khar," ḍh is turned into ṭ: liṭsu. The vocatives too are like the first case: he liḍ, he liṭ, he lihau, he lihaḥ. So they are set out.

duh is slightly different. duh with su: bāde rbhāto rghaḥ: gh replaces the h of a root beginning with d. The vowelless h of a root that has d at its beginning becomes gh when any letter of the group jhal follows, and also at the end of a word; so h becomes gh: dugh. su: ekāco baśo bhaṣ jhaṣaṃtasya sdhoḥ: of a monosyllabic root ending in jhaṣ, bhaṣ replaces baś before s and dhv.

That is: in a root of a single vowel that has a letter of the group jhaṣ at its end, the preceding letters of the group baś become the letters of the group bhaṣ that share their own place of articulation. For this, however, there must follow that jhaṣ letter an s or dhv, or a letter of the group jhal, or else it must be at the end of a word. In this case the d, a member of baś, before gh, a member of jhaṣ, becomes dh, a member of bhaṣ. By the rule "hal, ṅī, āp," su is dropped. By "optionally at a pause," gh becomes k or g: dhuk, dhug. For au and jas: duhau, duhaḥ. In the second case: duham, duhau, duhaḥ. For ṭā: duhā. For bhyām: by the rule "of a root beginning with d," h becomes gh; by the rule "of a single vowel," d becomes dh; by "jaś replaces jhal before jhaś," gh is turned into g: dhugbhyām, dhugbhiḥ. In the fourth case: duhe, dhugbhyām, dhugbhyaḥ. In the fifth case: duhaḥ, dhugbhyām, dhugbhyaḥ. In the sixth case: duhaḥ, duhoḥ, duhām. For ṅi: duhi. For os: duhoḥ. For sup: h becomes gh and d becomes dh; by "before khar," gh becomes k; and by the rule "it is changed throughout," s becomes ṣ: dhukṣu. The vocatives are like the first case: he dhuk, he dhug, he duhau, he duhaḥ.

bā druha muha snuha snihāṃ: optionally for druh, muh, snuh and snih. For these, druh and the rest, the change of h into ḍh, as in the case of lih above, and the change of h into gh, as in the case of duh just explained, are both to be made optional. druh with su: dhruk, dhrug, dhruṭ, dhruḍ: thus four forms arise. (muh means to be bewildered.) For au and jas: druhau, druhaḥ. In the second case: druham, druhau, druhaḥ. For ṭā: druhā. For bhyām: dhrugbhyām, dhruḍbhyām. For bhis: dhrugbhiḥ, dhruḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: druhe. For bhyām and bhyas: dhrugbhyām, dhruḍbhyām, dhrugbhyaḥ, dhruḍbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: druhaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: druhaḥ, druhoḥ, druhām. For ṅi and os: druhi, druhoḥ. For sup: dhrukṣu, dhruṭsu. The vocative is like the first case. muh, snuh and snih are also like this.

viśvavāh with su: viśvavāṭ. For au and jas: viśvavāhau, viśvavāhaḥ. He viśvavāṭ, he viśvavāḍ, he viśvavāhau, he viśvavāhaḥ. For am: viśvavāham. For auṭ: viśvavāhau. For śas: vāha ūṭha: ūṭh for vāh. For this word vāha, when viśva has been prefixed, the va becomes ūṭh before the endings beginning with a vowel, from śas of the second case onward. By the rule "before eti, edhati and ūṭh," vṛddhi is made: viśvauhaḥ. For ṭā: viśvauhā. For bhyām and bhis: viśvavāḍbhyām, viśvavāḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: viśvauhe; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: viśvauhaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: viśvauhaḥ. For os: viśvauhoḥ. For ām: viśvauhām. For ṅi: viśvauhi, viśvauhoḥ. For sup: viśvavāṭsu. bhūvaha too is like this.

Among stems ending in the letter h, anaḍuh, meaning an ox, with su: caturanaḍuhorāmudādhaḥ: ām, udātta, for catur and anaḍuh. For catur and anaḍuh, before the endings called sarvanāmasthāna, the augment ām is given, and it is designated udātta. The m of ām means that it goes after the final vowel. anaḍvāh with su: sāvanaḍuhaḥ: for anaḍuh before su. To the stem anaḍuh, before su, the singular of the first case, and before su called saṃbuddhi, the augment num comes: num is given. By "hal, ṅī, āp," su is dropped. By "elision of the final of a conjunct," h is dropped: anaḍvān. For au and jas: anaḍvāhau, anaḍvāhaḥ. anaḍuh with saṃbuddhi: ama saṃbuddhau: am before saṃbuddhi. For both anaḍuh and catur, before saṃbuddhi, the augment am is given. For the si of anaḍuh, num: he anaḍvan, he anaḍvāhau, he anaḍvāhaḥ. For am: anaḍvāham. For au: anaḍvāhau. For śas: anaḍuhaḥ. For ṭā: anaḍuhā. anaḍuh with bhyām and bhyas: basusraṃsūdhvaṃsvanaḍvahāṃdaḥ: d for vasu, sraṃsu, dhvaṃsu and anaḍuh. The finals of vasu, sraṃsu, dhvaṃsu and anaḍuh, the letter h, become d when any letter of the group jhal follows, and at the end of a word: anaḍudbhyām, anaḍudbhiḥ. In the fourth case: anaḍuhe, anaḍudbhyām, anaḍudbhyaḥ. In the fifth case: anaḍuhaḥ, anaḍudbhyām, anaḍudbhyaḥ. In the sixth case: anaḍuhaḥ, anaḍuhoḥ, anaḍuhām. In the seventh case: anaḍuhi, anaḍuhoḥ, anaḍutsu.

śvetavāh is slightly different. Since the commentary says, "For śvetavāh, ukthaśās, puroḍāś and avayāj, the suffix ḍas is added when not at the end of a word," the suffix ḍas is given to these stems before the case endings that begin with a consonant rather than a vowel. Having obtained the letter ḍ (śveta meaning white), since this signifies the elision of ṭi, ṭi is dropped: śvetavas. With su: atvasaṃtasya cādhātoḥ: of what ends in atu or as, not being a root. For what ends in atu and what ends in as, not being a root, the penultimate becomes long before su that is not saṃbuddhi.

śvetavāḥ. For au and jas: śvetavāhau, śvetavāhaḥ. For am: śvetavāham. For au: śvetavāhau. For śas: from śas onward, before the endings beginning with a vowel, the change into ūṭh explained earlier in the case of viśvavāh is optional, made or not made: śvetauhaḥ, śvetavāhaḥ. For ṭā: śvetauhā, śvetavāhā. For bhyām: the suffix ḍas; ṭi is dropped; by "ru for s and sajuṣ," and by "after a, guṇa": śvetavobhyām. For bhis: śvetavobhiḥ. For ṅe: śvetavāhe, śvetauhe. For bhyām and bhyas: śvetavobhyām, śvetavobhyaḥ. For ṅasi: śvetauhaḥ, śvetavāhaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: śvetauhaḥ, śvetavāhaḥ. For os: śvetauhoḥ, śvetavāhoḥ. For ām: śvetauhām, śvetavāhām. For ṅi: śvetauhi, śvetavāhi; os is the same. For sup: śvetavassu. For saṃbuddhi: avayāḥ śvetabāḥ puroḍāśca: also for avayāj, śvetavāh and puroḍāś. Above, in the commentary on "of what ends in atu or as, not being a root," it says "before su that is not saṃbuddhi"; but since here it says, "For these, avayāj, śvetavāh and puroḍāś, the penultimate becomes long in saṃbuddhi," both apply, and so it is taken as optional: he śvetavāḥ, he śvetavaḥ, he śvetavāhau, he śvetavāhaḥ.

ukthaśās and the rest are also like śvetavāh. For su: ḍas; ṭi is dropped; the penultimate is lengthened: ukthaśāḥ. For au and jas: ukthaśāsaḥ. In the second case: ukthaśāsam, ukthaśāsau, ukthaśāsaḥ. For ṭā: ukthaśāsā. For bhyām: ḍas; ṭi is dropped; sandhi is made: ukthaśobhyām, ukthaśobhiḥ. In the fourth case: ukthaśāse, ukthaśobhyām, ukthaśobhyaḥ. For ṅasi: ukthaśāsaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: ukthaśāsaḥ, ukthaśāsoḥ, ukthaśāsām. For ṅi: ukthaśāsi; os is the same. For sup: ukthaśāḥsu, ukthaśāssu. Vocative: he ukthaśāḥ, he ukthaśaḥ, he ukthaśāsau, he ukthaśāsaḥ. avayāj and puroḍāś are also like this.

turāsāh with su: by "ḍh for h," h becomes ḍh. sahessāḍhassaḥ: ṣ for the s of sāh when it is sāḍh. The s at the front of the stem sāh, when it becomes sāḍh, turns into the letter ṣ. By "hal, ṅī, āp," su is dropped. At a pause ḍh optionally becomes ḍ or ṭ: turāṣāḍ, turāṣāṭ. For au and jas (it means the horse of Śakra, that is, Indra): turāsāhau, turāsāhaḥ. In the second case: turāsāham, turāsāhau, turāsāhaḥ. For ṭā: turāsāhā. For bhyām and bhis: turāṣāḍbhyām, turāṣāḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: turāsāhe. For bhyām and bhyas: turāṣāḍbhyām, turāṣāḍbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: turāsāhaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: turāsāhaḥ, turāsāhoḥ, turāsāhām. For ṅi: turāsāhi; os is the same. For sup: turāṣāṭsu. In the vocative: he turāṣāṭ, he turāṣāṭ, he turāṣāḍ, he turāsāhau, he turāsāhaḥ.

Among stems ending in the letter v, sudiv, meaning a fine day, with su: diva auta: au for div. The v of div becomes au before su: sudyauḥ. For au and jas: sudivau, sudivaḥ. For am: since the commentary says, "For the v of div before am, optionally a," on one view the v of div becomes a; by "yaṇ for ik before a vowel," and by "the former for am": sudyām. On the other view: sudivam. For au and śas: sudivau, sudivaḥ. For ṭā: sudivā. For bhyām and bhyas: diva uta: u for div. The v of div becomes u before a case ending beginning with a letter of the group jhal: sudyubhyām, sudyubhiḥ. For ṅe: sudive. For bhyām and bhyas: sudyubhyām, sudyubhyaḥ. For ṅasi: sudivaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: sudivaḥ, sudivoḥ, sudivām. For ṅi: sudivi. For os: sudivoḥ. For sup: sudyuṣu. In the vocative: he sudyauḥ, he sudivau, he sudivaḥ.

Among stems ending in r, the seven plurals are applied to catur. catur with jas: by the sūtra "ām, udātta, for catur and anaḍuh," the augment ām: catvāraḥ. For śas: caturaḥ. For bhis: caturbhiḥ. For both kinds of bhyas: caturbhyaḥ. For ām: ṣaṭacaturbhyaśca: also after ṣaṭ and catur (catur meaning four). To ṣaṭ and catur, before ām of the sixth case, nuṭ is given. By "after r, ṣ and so on," n becomes ṇ; by "after a vowel, r and h," it is doubled: caturṇṇām. For sup: ro sbugi: of r before sup. The r of catur, before sup, the plural of the seventh case, does not become visarga; the r itself is kept: caturṣu. Although by the general rule "after r and h" the ṣ would be doubled, by śaroci, "of śar before a vowel," which says that the letters of the group śar, when followed by a vowel, are not doubled after r and h, by this sūtra of exception it is not doubled. Vocative: he catvāraḥ.

Something like priyacatur takes all the case endings. For su: priyacatvāḥ. For au and jas: priyacatvāraḥ. For am: priyacatvāram. For au: priyacatvārau. For śas: priyacaturaḥ. In the third case: priyacaturā, priyacaturbhyām, priyacaturbhiḥ. In the fourth case (meaning four joys): priyacaturbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: priyacaturaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: priyacaturaḥ. For os: priyacaturoḥ. For ām: except where it is a matter of counting numbers, nuṭ does not apply: priyacaturām. For ṅi: priyacaturi. For os: priyacaturoḥ. priyacaturṣu. For saṃbuddhi, am: he priyacatvaḥ, he priyacatvārau, he priyacatvāraḥ.

Among stems ending in m, praśām with su: monodsātoḥ: n for the m of a root. The m of a root becomes n before the letters of the group jhal and at the end of a word: m becomes n, and su is dropped: praśān. For au and jas: praśāmau, praśāmaḥ. In the second case: praśāmam, praśāmau, praśāmaḥ. For ṭā: praśāmā. For bhyām: praśānbhyām. In the fourth case: praśāme, praśānbhyām, praśānbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: praśāmaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: praśāmaḥ, praśāmoḥ, praśāmām. In the seventh case: praśāmi, praśāmoḥ, praśānsu. He praśān, he praśāmau, he praśāmaḥ.

kim with su: kimaḥkaḥ: ka for kim. The word kim becomes ka whatever case ending is seen: kaḥ, kau, ke and so on, like the masculine stem sarva. Among the pronouns, idam with su: idamomaḥ: m for idam.

The m of idam stays just as it is before su; the purpose is to block the rule "a for tyad and the rest." idamoyapuṃsi: ay for idam in the masculine. The i and the vowelless d of idam, in this case of the masculine stem, become ay before si: ayam. idam with au: by "a for tyad and the rest," m becomes a. atoduṇe: before guṇa after a. After a final a that is not at the end of a word, an a designated guṇa, such as arises when idam becomes ida, takes the form of the preceding: ida. With au: daśca: and of d. The d of idam, whose m has become a and merged into the preceding form, also becomes m whatever case ending is seen: ima. With au: by "vṛddhi before ec": imau. For jas: idam becomes ima; jas becomes śī; after a, guṇa: ime. In the second case: imam, imau, imān. For ṭā: anābyakaḥ: an before āp, when without ka. idam, changed to ida by "a for tyad and the rest," when it does not end in the suffix ka, becomes an before any case ending of the group āp, that is, from ṭā of the third case to sup of the seventh. ṭā becomes ina: anena. For bhyām: halilopaḥ: elision before hal. Although these are among ṭā and the rest, before case endings beginning with a consonant id does not become an; rather i and d are both elided: a with bhyām; by "also before sup," lengthening: ābhyām. For bhis: abhiḥ. nedamdasorkoḥ: not for idam and adas without ka. After idam and adas that do not end in the suffix ka, bhis, the plural of the third case, does not become ais. In the plural, by "e before jhal": ebhiḥ. For ṅe: by "a for tyad and the rest": ida. By "smai after what is called sarva," ṅe becomes smai. By "elision before hal," id is elided: asmai. For bhyām and bhyas: ābhyām, ebhyaḥ. ida with ṅasi: by "smāt and smin for ṅasi and ṅi," ṅasi becomes smāt; by "elision before hal," id is dropped: asmāt. ābhyām, ebhyaḥ. For ṅas: asya. For os: by "an before āp, when without ka," ida becomes ana; by "also before os," the stem final becomes e: anayoḥ. For ām: eṣām. For ṅi: asmin. For os: anayoḥ. For sup: eṣu.

Further, on one view the substitution for idam, ena, is optional before the endings of the second case, before ṭā of the third case, and before os of the sixth and seventh: dvitīyāṭaussvena: ena before the second-case endings, ṭā and os. Before the second-case endings, ṭā, and both kinds of os, idam and etad become ena. In the second case: enam, enau, enān. For ṭā: enena. For os: enayoḥ. Vocatives do not apply to tyad and the rest.

Among stems ending in n, rājan, meaning a king or one who shines, with su: by "also before what is called sarvanāmasthāna, when not saṃbuddhi," the penultimate is lengthened. By "hal, ṅī, āp" and so on, su is dropped. By "elision of the final n of a nominal stem," n is dropped: rājā. For au and jas: by "when not saṃbuddhi," the penultimate is lengthened: rājānau, rājānaḥ. rājan with su called saṃbuddhi: naṅisaṃbuddhyoḥ: not before ṅi and saṃbuddhi. Since this says that before ṅi of the seventh case and before saṃbuddhi the final n of a nominal stem is not elided, n is not dropped: he rājan, he rājānau, he rājānaḥ. For am and au: rājānam, rājānau. rājan with śas: by "elision of the a of an," the a after j is dropped; by "ścu replaces s and tu in contact with ś and cu," n becomes ñ; j and ñ together make jñ: rājñaḥ. For ṭā: rājñā. For bhyām: by "elision of the final n of a nominal stem," n is dropped. nalopaḥsupsvarasaṃjñātugpidhiṣukṛti: the elision of n, with respect to operations on sup, accent, designation and tuk, and before kṛt. After n has been dropped, no further operation applies with respect to sup, that is, the case endings su and the rest, a following vowel, designations, the kṛt suffixes, or augments such as tuk; for example, the lengthening by the rule "before sup" after n has been dropped in the case of bhyām. rājabhyām.
