For bhis: rājabhiḥ. In the fourth case: rājñe, rājabhyām, rājabhyaḥ. For ṅasi: rājñaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: rājñaḥ. For os: rājñoḥ. For ām: rājñām. For ṅi: by "not before ṅi and saṃbuddhi," on one view rājani, or else rājñi. For os: rājñoḥ. For sup: rājasu.

pratidivan with su: pratidivā. For au and jas: pratidivānau, pratidivānaḥ. For am: pratidivānam. For au: pratidivānau. For śas: since the commentary says, "after a has been dropped, the penultimate is long," by "elision of the a of an," a is dropped and the penultimate is lengthened: pratidīvnaḥ. In the third case (meaning shining severally): pratidīvnā, pratidivabhyām, pratidivabhiḥ, and so on, like the case of rājan.

yajvan with su: yajvā. For au: yajvānau. For jas: yajvānaḥ. For am and au: yajvānam, yajvānau. For śas: nasaṃyogādvamaṃtāta: not after a conjunct ending in v or m. Where the penultimate of the stem has the letter v or the letter m stacked in a conjunct, the general elision of the a of an does not apply. (yajvan means one who worships the gods.) The non-elision of a is brought in only for endings beginning with a vowel: yajvanaḥ. For ṭā: yajvanā. For bhyām and bhis: yajvabhyām, yajvabhiḥ. For ṅe: yajvane; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: yajvanaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: yajvanaḥ, yajvanoḥ, yajvanām. In the seventh case: yajvani, yajvanoḥ, yajvasu. In the vocative: he yajvan, he yajvānau, he yajvānaḥ. brahman is also like this.

vṛtrahan with su: sauca: also before su. Before su that is not saṃbuddhi, the penultimate of stems ending in in, and of han, pūṣan and aryaman, always becomes long: vṛtrahā. For au: by "ṇ when the following word has a single vowel," n becomes ṇ: vṛtrahaṇau. (Brahmā; one who destroys growth.) Here, apart from su, before the endings called sarvanāmasthāna the penultimate does not become long. For jas: vṛtrahaṇaḥ. For am: vṛtrahaṇam. For au: vṛtrahaṇau. For śas: by "elision of the a of an," a is dropped. hohaṃterñīnniṣa: for the h of han, before what has ñ or ṇ as marker, and before n. The h of han, from the root han, "to harm," becomes gh before suffixes with the marker ñ or ṇ and before n: vṛtraghnaḥ. For śas: haṃterthpūrbasya: of han, when a precedes. If at, that is, the letter a, stands before the word han, the n does not become ṇ: the purpose is to block the general rule given above, "ṇ when the following word has a single vowel."

vṛtraghnaḥ. In the third case: vṛtraghnā, vṛtrahabhyām, vṛtrahabhiḥ. For ṅe: vṛtraghne; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: vṛtraghnaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: vṛtraghnaḥ, vṛtraghnām. In the seventh case: vṛtraghni, vṛtraghnoḥ, vṛtrahasu. In the vocative: he vṛtrahan, he vṛtrahaṇau, he vṛtrahaṇaḥ. śārṅgin, yaśasvin, pūṣan and aryaman are also like this. For pūṣan, since the commentary says, "before ṅi, ṭi is optionally elided," on one view ṭi is dropped: pūṣi, pūṣṇi, pūṣaṇi; thus three forms arise.

maghavan with su: maghavābahulaṃ: optionally for maghavan. (Glossed: the kṛṣṇasāra deer; abundant; the sun.) The word maghavan, whatever case ending is seen, optionally becomes maghavatṛ. Since ṛ is designated a marker, although it does not remain, it is there for a purpose. ugdicāsarbanāmasthānedhātoḥ (maghavan meaning Śakra): for what has the marker uk, and for ac, before the endings called sarvanāmasthāna, when not a root. For stems that have uk as a marker at their end, that is, the letters u, ṛ and ḷ, and for the stem ac, when these are not roots, the augment num is given before whichever of the endings called sarvanāmasthāna occurs. maghavantṛ with su: by "also of what ends in atu or as, not being a root," the penultimate is lengthened; by the sūtra "hal, ṅī, āp" and so on, su is dropped; by "elision of the final of a conjunct," t is dropped: maghavān. For au and jas: maghavāntau, maghavāntaḥ. For am and au: maghavāntam, maghavāntau. For śas: maghavataḥ. In the third case: maghavatā, maghavadbhyām, maghavadbhiḥ. For ṅe: maghavate; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: maghavataḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: maghavataḥ, maghavatoḥ, maghavatām. In the seventh case: maghavati, maghavatoḥ, maghavatsu. In the vocatives: he maghavan, he maghavāntau, he maghavāntaḥ.

On the alternative in which maghavan does not become maghavatṛ: in the first case, maghavā, maghavānau, maghavānaḥ. For am and au: maghavānam, maghavānau. For śas: igyaṇaḥsaṃprasāraṇaṃ: ik in place of yaṇ is samprasāraṇa. The letters of the group yaṇ become the corresponding letters of the group ik, and this is called samprasāraṇa. śāyuvamaghonāmataddhite: of śvan, yuvan and maghavan, when not before a taddhita. For these, śvan and the rest, before case endings that are not taddhita suffixes and that begin with a vowel, from śas up to sup of the seventh case, samprasāraṇa takes place: v becomes u, giving magha u an, with śas. saṃprasāraṇācca: and after samprasāraṇa. The vowel following the samprasāraṇa also takes the form of the preceding, so a together with u becomes u. By "guṇa with a," it becomes o: maghonaḥ. In the third case: maghonā, maghavabhyām, maghavabhiḥ. For ṅe: maghone; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: maghonaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: maghonaḥ, maghonoḥ, maghonām. In the seventh case: maghoni, maghonoḥ, maghavasu. In the vocative: he maghavan, he maghavānau, he maghavānaḥ.

śvan, meaning a dog, with su: śvā. For au and jas: śvānaḥ. For am and au: śvānam, śvānau. śvan with śas: by "of śvan, yuvan and maghavan," v becomes u: śunaḥ. For ṭā: śunā. For bhyām and bhis: śvabhyām, śvabhiḥ. For the remaining case endings too, those beginning with a vowel are like śas, and those beginning with a consonant are like bhyām.

yuvan with su: yuvā. For au and jas: yuvānau, yuvānaḥ. For am and au: yuvānam, yuvānau. For śas: by the sūtra "of śvan, yuvan" and the rest, v becomes u, giving yu u an, with śas. nasaṃprasārṇisaṃprasāraṇaṃ: there is no samprasāraṇa before a samprasāraṇa. (yuvan means youth, or the prime of life.) Even though a letter of yaṇ stands before an already completed samprasāraṇa, such as the change of v into u, it does not undergo samprasāraṇa: the y before the u does not become i. By "lengthening when ak meets its like": yūnaḥ. For ṭā: yūnā. For bhyām: yuvabhyām, and so on; the rest is to be worked out in the same way.

arvan with su: arvā. For au and jas: arbaṇastrasāvanañaḥ: tṛ for arvan, when not after nañ and not before su. The final n of the stem arvan, when the negative nañ does not stand before it, becomes tṛ before whatever case ending is seen other than su, the singular of the first case, and saṃbuddhi: arvatṛ, with jas. By the sūtra "for what has the marker uk, and for ac," num is added and the penultimate is lengthened: arvantau, arvantaḥ. For am and au as well: arvantam, arvantau. For śas: arvataḥ. In the third case: arvatā, arvadbhyām, arvadbhiḥ. In the fourth case: arvate, arvadbhyām, arvadbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: arvataḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: arvataḥ, arvatoḥ, arvatām. In the seventh case: arvati, arvatoḥ, arvatsu. In the vocative: he arvan, he arvantau, he arvantaḥ. When nañ stands before it, the stem final of anarvan does not become tṛ, and all its procedures are like those explained for the stem yajvan.

pathin with su: pathimthyībhukṣāmāta: āt for pathin, mathin and ṛbhukṣan. The final n of the stems of these words, pathin and the rest, becomes āt before su: pathi ā, with su. itotsarbanāmasthāne: a for i before the endings called sarvanāmasthāna. (pathin means a path.) The letter i of pathin and the rest becomes the letter a before the endings called sarvanāmasthāna: patha ā, with su. thonthaḥ: nth for th. The letter th of pathi and mathi becomes nth before the endings called sarvanāmasthāna: pantha ā, with su. By "lengthening when ak meets its like," and by the sūtras "s and sajuṣ" and so on and "khar" and so on: panthāḥ. For au and jas: panthānau, panthānaḥ. For am: panthānam. For au: panthānau. pathin with śas: bhasyaṭeḥlopaḥ: elision of the ṭi of what is bha. Of pathin and the rest, designated bha, the ṭi is elided before endings beginning with a vowel that are not called sarvanāmasthāna: pathaḥ. For ṭā: ṭi is dropped and the parts joined: pathā. For bhyām and bhis: the final n of the nominal stem is dropped: pathibhyām, pathibhiḥ. In the fourth case: pathe, pathibhyām, pathibhyaḥ. For ṅasi: pathaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: pathaḥ, pathoḥ, pathām. In the seventh case: pathi, pathoḥ, pathiṣu. In the vocative: he panthāḥ, he panthānau, he panthānaḥ. mathin is also like this.

Ṛbhukṣin. For su: pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt: of pathin, mathin and ṛbhukṣin, ā is substituted. n becomes ā. By the rule like akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ, the like vowels merge into a long one: ṛbhukṣāḥ. For au and jas: ṛbhukṣāṇau, ṛbhukṣāṇaḥ. For am and auṭ: ṛbhukṣāṇam, ṛbhukṣāṇau. For śas: bhasya ṭer lopaḥ: elision of the ṭi of what is bha. The ṭi is dropped and the parts joined: ṛbhukṣaḥ. For ṭā, in the word meaning Śakra (Indra): ṛbhukṣā. For bhyām: ṛbhukṣibhyām. And so on: before endings beginning with a vowel the ṭi is elided, and before endings beginning with a consonant only the final n of the nominal stem is elided.

Words ending in n. Pañcan, five. For jas and śas: ṣṇāntā ṣaṭ: those ending in ṣ and n are ṣaṭ. Words with a numerical meaning that end in the letter ṣ, and those that end in the letter n, are given the designation ṣaṭ. The final n of the nominal stem is dropped. Ṣaḍbhyo luk: after ṣaṭ there is elision. Jas and śas are dropped: pañca. In the vocative: he pañca. For bhis and the two bhyas: the final n of the nominal stem is elided. The n is dropped: pañcabhiḥ, pañcabhyaḥ, pañcabhyaḥ. For ām: ṣaṭcaturbhyaś ca: also after ṣaṭ and catur, the augment nuṭ. Nopadhāyāḥ: of the penultimate of what ends in n. Before nām, the penultimate vowel of a word ending in n becomes long: the penultimate is lengthened. The final n of the nominal stem is elided, and the former n is dropped: pañcānām. For sup: pañcasu. For saptan, navan and daśan too, the whole procedure is the same as for pañcan. For these, in the context of counting numbers, only the plural forms of the case endings apply.

Words ending in the letter n. Aṣṭan. For jas: aṣṭana ā vibhaktau: of aṣṭan, ā before a case ending. The ṭi of the stem aṣṭan, as distinct from seven, nine and ten, becomes ā before a case ending: aṣṭā. For jas: aṣṭābhya auś: after aṣṭā, au. After the stem that has become aṣṭā, jas and śas become au. Eight. Jas becomes au. Vṛddhir eci: vṛddhi before the diphthongs: aṣṭau. Since the commentary also explains this as optional, in one view jas is dropped by the rule that there is elision after ṣaṭ: aṣṭā. For śas, too, it is made optional: aṣṭau, aṣṭā. In the vocative: he aṣṭau, he aṣṭā. For bhis: aṣṭābhiḥ. For the two bhyas: aṣṭābhyaḥ, aṣṭābhyaḥ. For ām: aṣṭānām. Aṣṭāsu. The commentary says that, jas and śas optionally not being elided, by the same procedure as for akaḥ, with s turned to r and then to visarga, aṣṭāḥ is also formed. And for ām, since nuṭ is optionally not applied, aṣṭām also occurs.

Words ending in the letter dh. Budh. For su: ekāco baśo bhaṣ jhaṣantasya sdhvoḥ: of a monosyllable ending in jhaṣ, baś becomes bhaṣ before s and dhv. b becomes bh. By halṅyābbhyaḥ, su is dropped. Vāvasāne: optionally at a pause. dh becomes d or t: bhut, bhud. For au and jas: budhau, budhaḥ. In the second case: budham, budhau, budhaḥ. For ṭā: budhā. For bhyām: the stem; b becomes bh. Jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi: of the jhal letters, jaś before jhaś. dh becomes d: bhudbhyām. For bhis: bhudbhiḥ. In the fourth case: budhe, bhudbhyām, bhudbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: budhaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: budhaḥ, budhoḥ, budhām. For ṅi: budhi; os is the same. For sup: b becomes bh. Khari ca: car before khar. dh becomes t: bhutsu. In the vocative: he bhut, he bhud, he budhau, he budhaḥ.

Words ending in the letter j. Yuj. Ṛtvigdadhṛksragdiguṣṇigañcuyujikruñcāṃ ca: of ṛtvik, dadhṛk, srak, dik and uṣṇik, and also of añcu, yuj and kruñc. For these, ṛtvik and the rest, kvin, one of the kṛt and other suffixes that form nouns from roots, applies. kvin is given to yuj: yuj plus kvin. By halantyam, the it n is dropped. Laśakv ataddhite: when not a taddhita, the l, ś and ku letters are it; k is dropped: yuj plus vi. The i is for pronunciation, so it is dropped. Kṛd atiṅ: what is not tiṅ is kṛt. The noun-forming suffixes other than ti and the rest are called kṛt. Ver apṛktasya: of v that is apṛkta. The vowelless single letter that remains after the it of kvin has been dropped is called apṛkta, and it is to be elided: v is dropped. Kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca: kṛt, taddhita and compounds also. What results from a root given a kṛt suffix, and the endings of taddhita suffixes and of compounds, before any case ending has been given, are called noun, stem or word, since they are the domain to which su and the rest apply. For yuj: su. Yujer asamāse: of yuj when not in a compound. When endings designated sarvanāmasthāna follow the stem yuj not in a compound, the augment num comes: yunj. By halṅyāb and the rest, su is dropped. Saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ: elision of the final of a cluster. j is dropped. Kvinpratyayasya kuḥ: ku in place of what has the suffix kvin. The letters standing at the end of what has been given the suffix kvin become the corresponding ku, that is, the velar class, before jhal and at the end of a word: the fifth of the t class becomes the fifth of the k class: yuṅ. For au and jas: yuñjau, yuñjaḥ. For am and auṭ: yuñjam, yuñjau. For śas: yujaḥ. For ṭā: yujā. For bhyām and bhis: by ku in place of what has kvin, j becomes g: yugbhyām, yugbhiḥ. For ṅe: yuje; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: yujaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: yujaḥ, yujoḥ, yujām. For ṅi: yuji. For os: yujoḥ. For sup: j becomes g. Khari ca: car before khar. g becomes k. By iṇkoḥ and the rest, s becomes ṣ: yukṣu. In the vocative: he yuṅ, he yuñjau, he yuñjaḥ.

Yuj in a compound: suyuj. For su: coḥ kuḥ: ku in place of cu. Before the jhal letters and at the end of a word, the vowelless cu, the c class, become ku, the corresponding letters of the k class: j becomes g. By the rule that at a pause it is optional, it becomes k or optionally remains as it is: suyuk, one who worships the gods well; suyug. For au and jas there is no further operation besides joining: suyujau, suyujaḥ. In the vocative: he suyuk, he suyug, he suyujau, he suyujaḥ. In the second case: suyujam, suyujau, suyujaḥ. For ṭā: suyujā. For bhyām and bhis: by ku in place of cu, suyugbhyām, suyugbhiḥ. And so on: before endings beginning with a vowel there is only joining, and before endings beginning with a consonant only the change of cu to ku; the rest should be worked out by analogy with the forms above. Since the commentary says that num does not apply to yuj in the sense of meditative concentration, that word is in this respect like suyuj.

Words ending in the letter j: sañj. For su: by halṅyābbhyaḥ and the rest, su is dropped. Saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ: elision of the final of a cluster. j is dropped. By the principle "when the cause is absent, what is caused by it is also absent," ñ reverts to n: san. For au and jas: sañjau, sañjaḥ. In the second case: sañjam, sañjau, sañjaḥ. For ṭā: sañjā. For bhyām and bhis: elision of the final of a cluster. j is dropped. n becomes anusvāra: saṃbhyām, saṃbhiḥ. In the fourth case: sañje, saṃbhyām, saṃbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: sañjaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: sañjaḥ, sañjoḥ, sañjām. In the seventh case: sañji, sañjoḥ, saṃsu. In the vocative: he san, he sañjau, he sañjaḥ.

Words ending in the letter j: rāj. For su: by the sūtra of vraśc, bhrasj, sṛj and the rest, j becomes ṣ. By halṅyābbhyaḥ and the rest, su is dropped. Optionally at a pause, ṣ becomes ḍ or ṭ: rāṭ, rāḍ. For au and jas: rājau, rājaḥ. In the second case: rājam, rājau, rājaḥ. For ṭā: rājā. For bhyām and bhis: j becomes ṣ. Jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi: of the jhal letters, jaś before jhaś. ṣ becomes ḍ: rāḍbhyām, rāḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: rāje; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: rājaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: rājaḥ, rājoḥ, rājām. For ṅi: rāji; os is the same. For sup: j becomes ṣ, ṣ becomes ḍ. Khari ca: car before khar. ḍ becomes ṭ: rāṭsu. In the vocative: he rāṭ, he rāḍ, he rājau, he rājaḥ. Vibhrāj, devej, viśvasṛj, parisṛj and parivrāj are also like rāj.

Viśvarāj. For su: j becomes ṣ, ṣ becomes ḍ: viśvarāḍ. Viśvasya vasurāṭoḥ: of viśva before vasu and rāṭ. When the word viśva stands before vasu, or before rāj that has become rāṭ, the final vowel of the stem becomes long, as in viśvārāṭ. Before endings beginning with a consonant, rāj becomes rāṣ; and then, apart from the a of viśva, "all," becoming long, the word meaning "shining over all" differs in nothing from what was explained for rāj in its own section. As for vasu, which ends in the letter u, its whole procedure is like that in the section on bhānu. If the word viśva comes before it, then by viśvasya vasurāṭoḥ the vowel becomes long, as for example in viśvāvasuḥ.

Words ending in the letter j: bhṛsj. For su: skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca: also of s and k at the beginning of a cluster, at the end. When the end of a stem is a cluster, that is, two vowelless letters stacked together, and the first of that final pair is the letter s or the letter k, it is to be elided before the jhal letters and at the end of a word: s is dropped. By vraśc, bhrasj and the rest, j becomes ṣ. Optionally at a pause, it becomes ḍ or ṭ: bhṛṭ, bhṛḍ. For au: jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi. Before the j, which is a jhaś letter, the s that precedes it, one of the jhal letters, becomes d, the letter of the same place of articulation. Stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ: the s and t classes become the ś and c classes in contact with the ś and c classes. d becomes j, and the parts are joined: bhṛjjau. For jas: bhṛjjaḥ. For am and auṭ: bhṛjjam, bhṛjjau. For śas: bhṛjjaḥ. For ṭā: bhṛjjā. For bhyām and bhis: by the rule on s and k at the beginning of a cluster, at its end, s is dropped. j becomes ṣ, ṣ becomes ḍ: bhṛḍbhyām, bhṛḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: bhṛjje; bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: bhṛjjaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are the same. In the sixth case: bhṛjjaḥ, bhṛjjoḥ, bhṛjjām. In the seventh case: bhṛjji, bhṛjjoḥ, bhṛṭsu. In the vocative: he bhṛṭ, he bhṛḍ, he bhṛjjau, he bhṛjjaḥ.

Words ending in the letter j: ṛtvij. For su: since ṛtvij is formed with the noun-forming suffix kvin, by ku in place of what has the suffix kvin, j becomes g. Optionally at a pause: ṛtvik, ṛtvig. For au and jas: ṛtvijau, ṛtvijaḥ. In the vocative: he ṛtvik, he ṛtvig, he ṛtvijau, he ṛtvijaḥ. For bhyām: ṛtvigbhyām; the rest should be worked out by analogy.

Words ending in j: ūrj. For su: by ku in place of what has the suffix kvin, j becomes g. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. Except after the letter r, the final of a cluster is not elided. Optionally at a pause: ūrk, ūrg. For au: ūrjau; by this the endings beginning with a vowel should be worked out by analogy. For bhyām: ūrgbhyām; by this the endings beginning with a consonant should be worked out by analogy.

Words ending in the letter d: tyad. For su: tyadādīnām aḥ: a in place of tyad and the rest. d becomes a. By ato guṇe, the two take a single form: tya. For su: tadoḥ saḥ sāv anantyayoḥ: s in place of t and d before su, when they are not final. The t and the d of tyad and the rest that are not final become the letter s before su: syaḥ. For au: tyau. Jas becomes śī: tye, and so on, as was explained in the section on the stem sarva.

Tad, which ends in the letter d, is also like what has just been explained: saḥ, tau, te, and so on. Likewise yad: yaḥ, yau, ye, and so on. For etad: eṣaḥ, etau, ete, and so on, worked out by analogy. A further change in the body of etad, for the second-case endings and for ṭā and os, is by dvitīyāṭausv enaḥ: ena for the second case, ṭā and os. Etad becomes ena. In the second case: enam, enau, enān. For ṭā: enena. For the two os: enayoḥ. This too is one view.

Words ending in the letter d: yuṣmad and asmad. For su: ṅe prathamayor am: am in place of ṅe and of the first two. From the stems yuṣmad and asmad, the first-case endings, the second-case endings and ṅe of the fourth case become am: su becomes am. Yuṣmad plus am, asmad plus am. Tvāhau sau: tva and aha for su, meaning "you" and "I" or "myself." Before su of the first case, the three letters yuṣm of yuṣmad, with ad set aside, become tva, and the letters asm of asmad, with ad set aside, become aha: tva ad am, aha ad am. Śeṣe lopaḥ: elision in the remainder. The d of yuṣmad and asmad is not elided where it becomes ā or y, but where it does not become ā or y it is to be elided: d is dropped. Tva a am, aha a am. By ato guṇe, and by ami pūrvaḥ, the former vowel for am: tvam, aham. Yuṣmad and asmad with au: by ṅe prathamayor am, au becomes am. Yuṣmad am, asmad am. Yuvāvau dvivacane: yuva and āva in the dual. Before the dual endings, yuṣm, with ad set aside, becomes yuva, and asm, with ad set aside, becomes āva: yuva ad am, āva ad am. Prathamāyāś ca dvivacane bhāṣāyām: also in the dual of the first case, in ordinary speech.

Before the dual of the first case, the final of yuṣmad becomes ā: the letter d becomes ā. Yuva a ā am, āva a ā am. By ato guṇe: yuva ā am, āva ā am. By akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ and by ami pūrvaḥ: yuvām, āvām. Yuṣmad and asmad with jas: by ṅe prathamayor am, jas becomes am. Yuṣmad am, asmad am. Yūyavayau jasi: yūya and vaya for jas. Before jas, the plural of the first case, yuṣm, with ad set aside, becomes yūya, and asm, with ad set aside, becomes vaya. Yūya ad am, vaya ad am. By elision in the remainder, d is dropped. By ato guṇe and by ami pūrvaḥ: yūyam, vayam. Yuṣmad and asmad with am of the second case: by the rule "of ṅe and the first two," am becomes am. Yuṣmad am, asmad am. Tvamāv ekavacane: tva and ma in the singular. Before singular endings, yuṣm, with ad set aside, becomes tva, and asm, with ad set aside, becomes ma: tva ad am, ma ad am. Dvitīyāyāṃ ca: also in the second. Before second-case endings too, the final of yuṣmad and asmad, that is d, becomes ā: tva a ā am, ma a ā am. By ato guṇe, by akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ and by ami pūrvaḥ: tvām, mām. Yuṣmad and asmad with au of the second case: by ṅe prathamayor am, au becomes am. In the dual, by yuva and āva: yuva ad am, āva ad am. By "also in the second," d becomes ā. By ato guṇe, by akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ and by ami pūrvaḥ: yuvām, āvām. Yuṣmad and asmad with śas, the plural of the second case: śaso naḥ: n in place of śas. For yuṣmad and asmad, śas, the plural of the second-case endings, becomes a vowelless n: śas becomes n. By "also in the second," the final becomes ā, and by akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ: yuṣmān, asmān.

Yuṣmad and asmad with ṭā of the third case: in the singular, by tva and ma: tva ad ṭā, ma ad ṭā. Yo 'ci: y before a vowel. Before the other endings beginning with a vowel that have not been changed into something else, as au is changed into am, the final of yuṣmad and asmad becomes y: d is turned into y. By ato guṇe, and by joining the y: tvayā, mayā. Yuṣmad and asmad with bhyām of the third case: in the dual, by yuva and āva: yuva ad bhyām, āva ad bhyām. Yuṣmadasmador anādeśe: of yuṣmad and asmad where there is no substitution. Before the other endings beginning with a consonant that have not been changed into something else, as su is turned into am, the final of yuṣmad and asmad becomes ā: d becomes ā. By ato guṇe and by akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ: yuvābhyām, āvābhyām. For bhis: by the rule on yuṣmad and asmad where there is no substitution, d becomes ā, and by akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ: yuṣmābhiḥ, asmābhiḥ.

Yuṣmad and asmad with ṅe: by ṅe prathamayor am, ṅe becomes am. Tubhyamahyau ṅayi: tubhya and mahya for ṅe. Before ṅe of the fourth case, yuṣm, with ad set aside, becomes tubhya, and asm, with ad set aside, becomes mahya: they are changed into tubhya and mahya. By elision in the remainder, d is dropped. By ato guṇe and by ami pūrvaḥ: tubhyam, mahyam. Bhyām is as in the section on the third case: yuvābhyām, āvābhyām. Yuṣmad and asmad with bhyas of the fourth case: bhyaso bhyam: bhyam in place of bhyas. For yuṣmad and asmad, bhyas becomes bhyam: bhyas is changed into bhyam. By elision in the remainder, d is dropped: yuṣmabhyam, asmabhyam.

Yuṣmad and asmad with ṅasi of the fifth case: in the singular, by tva and ma: tva ad ṅasi, ma ad ṅasi. Ekavacanasya ca: also of the singular. Ṅasi, the singular of the fifth-case endings, also becomes at for yuṣmad and asmad: ṅasi becomes at. By ato guṇe, both a's take the form of the former: tvat, mat. Bhyām of the fifth case is also as in the sections on the third and fourth: yuvābhyām, āvābhyām. Yuṣmad and asmad with bhyas of the fifth case: pañcamyā at: at in place of the fifth. For yuṣmad and asmad, bhyas of the fifth-case endings becomes at: bhyas is changed into at. By elision in the remainder, d is dropped. By ato guṇe: yuṣmat, asmat.

Yuṣmad and asmad with ṅas of the sixth case: tavamamau ṅasi: tava and mama for ṅas. Before ṅas of the sixth case, yuṣm, with ad set aside, becomes tava, and asm, with ad set aside, becomes mama: tava ad ṅas, mama ad ṅas. Yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ ṅaso 'ś: aś in place of ṅas after yuṣmad and asmad. After yuṣmad and asmad, ṅas of the sixth case becomes aś: ṅas is changed into aś. Since ś has the designation it, it is dropped. By elision in the remainder, d is dropped. By ato guṇe, both a's take the form of the former: tava, mama. Yuṣmad and asmad with os of the sixth case: in the dual, by yuva and āva: yuva ad os, āva ad os. By yo 'ci, d becomes y. By ato guṇe, the a takes the form of the former, and the parts are joined: yuvayoḥ, āvayoḥ. Yuṣmad and asmad with ām of the sixth case: by elision in the remainder, d is dropped. By āmi sarvanāmnaḥ suṭ, before ām the words designated sarva take suṭ: the augment suṭ. Yuṣma sām, asma sām. Sāma ākam: ākam in place of sām. For yuṣmad and asmad, sām, that is ām of the sixth case together with suṭ, becomes ākam: sām is changed into ākam. By akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ: yuṣmākam.

Asmākam. Yuṣmad and asmad with ṅi of the seventh case: in the singular, by tva and ma: tva ad ṅi, ma ad ṅi. By yo 'ci, d becomes y: tvayi, mayi. Os is as in the section on the sixth case: yuvayoḥ, āvayoḥ. Yuṣmad and asmad with sup, the plural of the seventh case: by the rule on yuṣmad and asmad where there is no substitution, d becomes ā, and by akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ: yuṣmāsu, asmāsu.

A further change in the body of yuṣmad and asmad is this. When the singular of the case endings has been compounded by a compound with an indeclinable, and ati stands before it, then whatever case ending follows, except the singular and plural of the first case, ṅe of the fourth and ṅas of the sixth, yuṣm, with ad set aside, becomes only tva, and asm, with ad set aside, becomes only ma. For example, in tvām ati and mām ati, am, the singular of the second case, is compounded by the compound, with ati before it: atiyuṣmad, atiasmad. Whatever case ending comes, except those mentioned above, yuṣm becomes tva and asm becomes ma. Then each set is formed as shown above. In the singular of the first case: atitvam, atyaham. In the dual: atitvām, atimām. In the plural: atiyūyam, ativayam. In the singular of the second case: atitvām, atimām. In the dual: atitvām, atimām. In the plural: atitvān, atimān. In the singular of the third case: atitvayā, atimayā. In the dual: atitvābhyām, atimābhyām. In the plural: atitvābhiḥ, atimābhiḥ. In the singular of the fourth case: atitubhyam, atimahyam. In the dual: atitvābhyām, atimābhyām. In the plural: atitvabhyam, atimabhyam. In the singular of the fifth case: atitvat, atimat. In the dual: atitvābhyām, atimābhyām. In the plural: atitvat, atimat. In the singular of the sixth case: atitava, atimama. In the dual: atitvayoḥ, atimayoḥ. In the plural: atitvākam, atimākam. In the singular of the seventh case: atitvayi, atimayi. In the dual: atitvayoḥ, atimayoḥ. In the plural: atitvāsu, atimāsu. So it is.

Again, when the dual has been compounded by a compound with an indeclinable, with ati before it, then, setting aside the case endings mentioned above, whatever case ending follows, yuṣm, with ad set aside, becomes yuva, and asm, with ad set aside, becomes āva. For example, in yuvām ati and āvām ati, au, the dual of the second case, is compounded by the compound, with ati before it: atiyuṣmad, atiasmad. Whatever case ending comes, except the four special endings, yuṣm becomes only yuva and asm only āva. Then, when they are formed by their own procedures explained above, for example: in the singular of the first case, atitvam, atyaham. In the dual: atiyuvām, atiāvām. In the plural: atiyūyam, ativayam. In the singular of the second case: atiyuvām, atiāvām. In the dual: atiyuvām, atiāvām. In the plural: atiyuvān, atiāvān. In the singular of the third case: atiyuvayā, atiāvayā. In the dual: atiyuvābhyām, atiāvābhyām. In the plural: atiyuvābhiḥ, atiāvābhiḥ. In the singular of the fourth case: atitubhyam, atimahyam. In the dual: atiyuvābhyām, atiāvābhyām. In the plural: atiyuvabhyam, atiāvabhyam. In the singular of the fifth case: atiyuvat, atiāvat. In the dual: atiyuvābhyām, atiāvābhyām. In the plural: atiyuvat, atiāvat. In the singular of the sixth case: atitava, atimama. In the dual: atiyuvayoḥ, atiāvayoḥ. In the plural: atiyuvākam, atiāvākam. In the singular of the seventh case: atiyuvayi, atiāvayi. In the dual: atiyuvayoḥ, atiāvayoḥ. In the plural: atiyuvāsu, atiāvāsu.

Again, yuṣmān ati and asmān ati. As before, when the plural of the case endings has been compounded by a compound with an indeclinable, with ati before it, then, whatever case ending follows, except the four special endings, the form does not change into another but remains just yuṣmad and asmad, and then the case endings are treated by their own procedures as explained above. Śas, the plural of the second case, is compounded by the compound, with ati before it. In the singular of the first case: atitvam, atyaham. In the dual: atiyuṣmām, atiasmām. In the plural: atiyūyam, ativayam. In the singular of the second case: atiyuṣmām, atiasmām. In the dual: atiyuṣmām, atiasmām. In the plural: atiyuṣmān, atiasmān. In the singular of the third case: atiyuṣmayā, atiasmayā. In the dual: atiyuṣmābhyām, atiasmābhyām. In the plural: atiyuṣmābhiḥ, atiasmābhiḥ. In the singular of the fourth case: atitubhyam, atimahyam. In the dual: atiyuṣmābhyām, atiasmābhyām. In the plural: atiyuṣmabhyam, atiasmabhyam. In the singular of the fifth case: atiyuṣmat, atiasmat. In the dual: atiyuṣmābhyām, atiasmābhyām. In the plural: atiyuṣmat, atiasmat. In the singular of the sixth case: atitava, atimama. In the dual: atiyuṣmayoḥ, atiasmayoḥ. In the plural: atiyuṣmākam, atiasmākam. In the singular of the seventh case: atiyuṣmayi, atiasmayi. In the dual: atiyuṣmayoḥ, atiasmayoḥ. In the plural: atiyuṣmāsu, atiasmāsu.

The way in which yuṣmad and asmad, together with their case endings, change further into other special forms is this. Yuṣmadasmadoḥ ṣaṣṭhīcaturthīdvitīyāsthayor vāṃnāvau: vām and nau in place of yuṣmad and asmad standing in the sixth, fourth and second cases. When not at the beginning of the phrase, yuṣmad and asmad together with their case endings, once formed with the dual of the sixth, fourth and second cases, become vām and nau. For example, yuvayoḥ, yuṣmad formed with the dual of the sixth case, becomes vām, and āvayoḥ, asmad formed with the dual of the sixth case, becomes nau. Likewise, of the forms made with the dual of the fourth case, yuvābhyām becomes vām and āvābhyām becomes nau. Likewise, of the forms made with the dual of the second case, yuvām becomes vām and āvām becomes nau. Bahuvacanasya vasnasau: vas and nas in place of the plural.

Of the forms already made with the plural of the sixth, fourth and second cases, yuṣmākam, yuṣmabhyam and yuṣmān become vas, and asmākam, asmabhyam and asmān become nas. Temayāv ekavacanasya: te and me in place of the singular. Of the forms already made with the singular of the sixth and fourth cases, tubhyam and tava become te, and mahyam and mama become me. Tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ: tvā and mā in place of the second. Of the forms already made with the singular of the second case, tvām becomes tvā and mām becomes mā.

An example of these joined with a verse is this: śrīśas tvāvatu māpīha dattāt te me 'pi śarma saḥ, svāmī te me 'pi sa hariḥ pātu vām api nau vibhuḥ. In our language this says:

May the Lord of Glory (Viṣṇu) protect you, and me as well;
may he grant happiness to you, and to me as well;
that Hari, your master, and mine as well,
the sovereign, protect you two, and us two as well.

Here, tvā, the third syllable of the first line, and mā, the sixth, meaning "you" and "me," are the singular of the second case. Te, the second syllable of the second line, and me, the third, meaning "to you" and "to me" in the sense of "for your sake" and "for my sake," are the singular of the fourth case. Te, the third syllable of the third line, and me, the fourth, meaning "your" and "my," are the singular of the sixth case. Vām, the third syllable of the fourth line, and nau, the fifth, meaning "you two" and "us two," are the dual of the second case.

Likewise, sukhaṃ vāṃ dadātv īśaḥ, "May the Lord give happiness to you two," and sukhaṃ nau dadātv īśaḥ, "May the Lord give happiness to us two": here vām and nau, meaning "to you two" and "to us two," are the dual of the fourth case. Patir vāṃ hariḥ, "Hari is the master of you two," and patir nau guruḥ, "The guru is the master of us two": here vām and nau, meaning "of you two" and "of us two," are the dual of the sixth case. In the examples meaning "May he protect you all" and "May he protect us all too," vaḥ and naḥ, meaning "you all" and "us all," are the plural of the second case. Sukhaṃ vo dadyāt, "May he give happiness to you all," and sukhaṃ no dadyāt, "May he give happiness to us all": here vaḥ and naḥ, meaning "to you all" and "to us all," are the plural of the fourth case. Patir vo hariḥ, "Hari is the master of you all," and patir no buddhaḥ, "The Buddha is the master of us all": here vaḥ and naḥ, meaning "of you all" and "of us all," are the plural of the sixth case.

Further, these substitutions are made if one wishes, but it is not wrong not to make them, so they are optional. Because of the words "when not at the beginning of the phrase," at the first, that is the beginning, of each phrase only the original forms such as tvām and mām are used, and they do not become tvā, mā and the rest. For example, in tvāṃ pātu, "may he protect you," and māṃ pātu, "may he protect me," they do not become tvā and mā. Likewise, an example with the plural of the second case: yuṣmān rakṣatu govindaḥ, asmān buddhaḥ sarvadā pātu, "May Govinda guard you all; may the Buddha always protect us all": these do not become vas and nas. So too an example with the dual of the sixth case: yuvayoḥ putra, āvayoḥ putra, "son of you two," "son of us two": yuvayoḥ does not become vām, nor āvayoḥ nau. The others, such as "May Viṣṇu protect you; may the Buddha always guard me," are to be worked out by analogy with these.

Na cavāhāhaivayukte: not when joined with ca, vā, ha, aha and eva. When they are joined with these five, ca and the rest, those substitutions te, me and the rest are not made. For example: tava ca mama ca maitrī candralekheva vardhate, "The friendship of you and me grows like the waxing crescent of the moon." Here one does not say te ca me ca, but tava ca mama ca. The commentary says that where there would be a fault in the arrangement of the meter or in the fitting of the verse line, the change into te, me and the rest is not prohibited, even where they are joined with ca and the rest.

Paśyārthaiś cānālocane: also with words meaning "see," when it is not seeing with the eye. When they are joined with words meaning "see," if the sense is seeing with the eye, they become te, me and the rest; if it is not seeing with the eye, they do not become te, me and the rest, but remain just tava, mama and the rest.

The commentary states that if two uninterrupted vocatives come before, they become te, me and the rest, but if a single vocative word comes before, they do not become te, me and the rest. For example: devāsmān pāhi nṛhare, viṣṇo 'smān rakṣa sarvadā, "O god, protect us, Man-Lion (Nṛhari); O Viṣṇu, guard us always." Here nas and the like do not occur; instead deva asmān and viṣṇo asmān occur. If two vocatives come before, they change. For example: hare kṛpālo naḥ pāhi, "O compassionate Hari, protect us." Here naḥ occurs after the two vocatives hare and kṛpālo. Even if there is only one vocative, if there is another word before it, they become naḥ and the rest, as in sarvadā rakṣa deva naḥ, "O god, always guard us." Although there is only the single vocative deva, naḥ occurs because the two words sarvadā and rakṣa stand before it.

With these, the procedures for yuṣmad and asmad have been explained. Yuṣmad and asmad may both be applied to an object of any of the three genders, masculine, feminine or neuter, and in fact they have no separate masculine, feminine or neuter forms.

Words ending in the letter d: supād. For su: by halṅyābbhyaḥ and the rest, su is dropped. Optionally at a pause: supāt, supād. For au and jas: supādau, supādaḥ. The vocative is also like the first case. For am and auṭ: supādam, supādau. For śas: supadaḥ. Pādaḥ pat: pad in place of pād. For the stem pād, as in supād, "having beautiful feet," before the case endings beginning with a vowel, from śas onward, the penultimate becomes short: pad.

supadaḥ. For the third case: supadā, supādbhyām, supādbhiḥ. For the fourth case: supade, supādbhyām, supādbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: supadaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: supadaḥ, supadoḥ, supadām. For the seventh: supadi, supadoḥ, supātsu.

Words ending in the letter th: agnimath, "the fire-churner." For agnimath, su. By halṅyābbhyaḥ and the rest, su is dropped. Optionally at a pause, th becomes d or t: agnimat, agnimad. For au and jas: agnimathau, agnimathaḥ. For the second case: agnimatham, agnimathau, agnimathaḥ. For ṭā: agnimathā. For bhyām and bhis: by the rule that a jhal becomes a jaś, th becomes d: agnimadbhyām, agnimadbhiḥ. For ṅasi: agnimathaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: agnimathaḥ, agnimathoḥ, agnimathām. For ṅi: agnimathi. For os: agnimathoḥ. For sup: by the rule that a jhal becomes a jaś, th becomes d; then before khar it becomes a car, d becoming t: agnimatsu. For the vocative: he agnimat, he agnimad, he agnimathau, he agnimathaḥ.

Words ending in the letter c: pra and añcu. By ṛtvik and the rest, kvin. Kvin is dropped entirely. Aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti: of those without the marker i, the penultimate n of a stem ending in a consonant is dropped before what has k or ṅ as its marker. That is: of those that do not have i as a marker and that end in hal, that is, in a consonant without a vowel, the n of the penultimate is to be deleted when a suffix having the marker k, or ṅ, follows. Here, since kvin has k as its marker, the n of the penultimate is dropped. For pra ac, su. Ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ: for those having the marker u and for ac, in the strong case endings, when not a root, num is inserted. Since the u of num is only for that purpose, it is dropped: pra anc, su. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. By saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, the final of a consonant cluster is deleted: c is dropped. By kvinpratyayasya kuḥ, the suffix kvin brings a guttural: n becomes ṅ, giving prāṅ. For au and jas, num: prāñcau, prāñcaḥ. For am and auṭ also, num: prāñcam, prāñcau. For śas: acaḥ, "of ac." When, after the ac whose penultimate n has been dropped, śas and the other endings beginning with a vowel occur, the a of ac too is to be deleted. The a is dropped: pr c, śas. Cau, "before c": before that c of ac whose a has already been dropped, the vowels of the aṇ group, that is, a, i and u where present, become long. Pra is lengthened: prācaḥ. For ṭā: prācā. For bhyām and bhis: by kvinpratyayasya kuḥ, the guttural: c becomes k. By the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, k becomes g: prāgbhyām, prāgbhiḥ. For the fourth case: prāce, prāgbhyām, prāgbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: prācaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: prācaḥ, prācoḥ, prācām. For ṅi and os: prāci, prācoḥ. For sup: by the guttural of kvin, c becomes k. By the rule for substitutes and suffixes, s becomes ṣ. K and ṣ combined make kṣ: prākṣu. For the vocative: he prāṅ, he prāñcaḥ.

Pratyac and the rest are just like this.

Next, how the case forms apply when a prior noun is joined to añc. Viṣvagdevayoś ca ṭer adryañcatau vapratyaye: of viṣvak and deva also, the ṭi becomes adri before añc ending in the suffix v. That is, when the stem viṣvak, deva, or a pronoun comes before a stem ending in the suffix of añc, the ṭi of those stems becomes adri. A and i. Where ac stands: adaso 'ser dād u do maḥ, "of adas, where s does not remain, u after d, and m in place of d." The s of adas has changed, and after d there is u, and that d too becomes m. Among the earlier masters, some hold that both d's become m and u; others hold that only the latter becomes mu. Amumuyac, su. By ugidacām, num. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. By saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, c is dropped. By the guttural of kvin, n becomes ṅ: amumuyaṅ. For au and jas: amumuyañcau, amumuyañcaḥ. For am and auṭ: amumuyañcam, amumuyañcau. For śas: by acaḥ, a is dropped: amumui c, śas. By cau, i becomes long: amumuīcaḥ. For ṭā: amumuīcā. For bhyām and bhis: the guttural of kvin; by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, k becomes g: amumuyagbhyām, amumuyagbhiḥ. For ṅe: amumuīce; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: amumuīcaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: amumuīcaḥ, amumuīcoḥ, amumuīcām. For ṅi and os: amumuīci, amumuīcoḥ. For sup: the guttural of kvin; by the rule for substitutes and the rest, s becomes ṣ; k and ṣ combined make kṣ: amumuyakṣu. The vocatives too are like the first case. Alternatively, only the latter d becomes mu, giving adamuyac, and all the procedures are like those just explained. Alternatively, by the sūtra viṣvagdevayoś ca ṭer adri and the rest, the ṭi of adas becomes adri, and some hold that only the former d becomes m, so that it becomes amudryac; the procedures on meeting the case endings are like those before. Alternatively, the former d is not changed into m either, and the case endings are given to adadryac. These are the four optional forms in which the case endings apply to adas together with ac.

Further, ac preceded by ut. For udac, su, au and jas: udaṅ, udañcau, udañcaḥ. For am and auṭ: udañcam, udañcau. Udac, for śas: uda īt, "after ut, ī." The a of ac preceded by ut becomes ī when the case ending śas and the other endings beginning with a vowel follow: udīcaḥ. For ṭā: udīcā. For bhyām and bhis: udagbhyām, udagbhiḥ. For ṅe: udīce; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: udīcaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: udīcoḥ, udīcām. For the seventh: udīci, udīcoḥ, udakṣu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Samaḥ samiḥ, "sami in place of sam." The prefix sam before the stem ac becomes sami, and for samyac too the procedures are like those for prāc.

Tiras ac, su. Tirasas tiry alopi: of tiras, tiri, when there is no deletion.

That is, tiras becomes tiri when an ac whose a is not deleted follows: tiryac, su. By ugit and the rest, num. By halṅyābbhyaḥ and the rest, su is dropped; by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, c is dropped. By the guttural of kvin, n becomes ṅ: tiryaṅ. For au and jas: tiryañcau, tiryañcaḥ. For am and auṭ: tiryañcam, tiryañcau. For śas: by acaḥ, the a is dropped. By "of tiras, tiri, when there is no deletion," it would become tiri if the a were not dropped; but here, since the a is deleted before the endings beginning with a vowel from śas onward, tiras itself remains as it is, meaning "animal." By the rule that s, in contact with ś or the c class, becomes ś or the c class, s becomes ś: tiraścaḥ. For ṭā: tiraścā. For bhyām and bhis: tiryagbhyām, tiryagbhiḥ. For ṅe: tiraśce; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: tiraścaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: tiraścaḥ, tiraścoḥ, tiraścām. For the seventh: tiraści, tiraścoḥ, tiryakṣu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Nāñceḥ pūjāyām: "not of añc in the sense of worship." In the sense of worship, the penultimate n of añc is not deleted. Pra añc, su. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. By saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, c is dropped. By the guttural of kvin, n becomes ṅ: prāṅ. For au and jas: prāñcau, prāñcaḥ. For am, auṭ and śas: prāñcam, prāñcau, prāñcaḥ. For ṭā: prāñcā. For bhyām and bhis: by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, as is plainly seen, c is dropped; by the guttural of kvin, n becomes ṅ: prāṅbhyām, prāṅbhiḥ. For ṅe: prāñce; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: prāñcaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: prāñcaḥ, prāñcoḥ, prāñcām. For ṅi and os: prāñci, prāñcoḥ. For sup: ṅṇoḥ kukṭuk śari, "before a sibilant, ṅ and ṇ take kuk and ṭuk": the augment kuk. By the rule for substitutes and the rest, s becomes ṣ; k and ṣ combined make kṣ: prāṅkṣu. Alternatively, the augment kuk is not given: prāṅṣu. For the vocatives: he prāṅ, he prāñcau, he prāñcaḥ. Kruñc is also like this.

Words ending in the letter c: for payomuc, su. By coḥ kuḥ, the c class becomes the guttural: c becomes k. Optionally at a pause: payomuk, payomug. For au and jas: payomucau, payomucaḥ. For the second case: payomucam, payomucau, payomucaḥ. For ṭā: payomucā. For bhyām and bhis: by the guttural for the c class, c becomes k; by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, k becomes g: payomugbhyām, payomugbhiḥ. For ṅe: payomuce; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: payomucaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: payomucaḥ, payomucoḥ, payomucām. For the seventh: payomuci, payomucoḥ, payomukṣu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Words ending in the letter c: suvṛśc, su. By skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca, "s and k at the beginning of a final cluster are also deleted," ś is dropped. By vraścabhrasja and the rest, c becomes ṣ. By the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, ṣ becomes ḍ. Optionally at a pause: suvṛṭ, suvṛḍ. For au and jas: suvṛścau, suvṛścaḥ. For the second case: suvṛścam, suvṛścau, suvṛścaḥ. For ṭā: suvṛścā. For bhyām and bhis: suvṛḍbhyām, suvṛḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: suvṛśce; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: suvṛścaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: suvṛścaḥ, suvṛścoḥ. For the seventh: suvṛści, suvṛścoḥ. For the vocatives: he suvṛḍ, he suvṛṭ, he suvṛścaḥ.

Words ending in the letter t: for mahat, su. By ugit and the rest, num. By sāntamahataḥ saṃyogasya, "of what ends in s and of mahat, at the cluster," the penultimate is lengthened. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. By saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, t is dropped: mahān. For au and jas: mahāntau, mahāntaḥ. For am and auṭ: mahāntam, mahāntau. For śas: mahataḥ, meaning "great." For ṭā, and for bhyām and bhis: by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, t becomes d: mahadbhyām, mahadbhiḥ. For ṅe: mahate; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: mahataḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: mahataḥ, mahatoḥ, mahatām. For the seventh: mahati, mahatoḥ, mahatsu. For the vocative: he mahan, he mahāntau, he mahāntaḥ.

For bhavat, the penultimate is not lengthened; all the other procedures are like those for mahat. For dhīmat too, by atvasantasya cādhātoḥ, "and of what ends in atu or as, when not a root," the penultimate is lengthened in the su position; all else is like bhavat. For atrabhavat and tatrabhavat also, in the sense of honor, the penultimate is lengthened in the su position; all else is like dhīmat. Yaśasvat is like atrabhavat. Aghavat and bhagavat both follow dhīmat in all their procedures. In the vocative singular there is an option: on the side where they are like dhīmat, he bhagavan, he aghavan. Or optionally, of bhavat, bhagavat and aghavat, ava optionally becomes o: ava turns into o. Further, the vowelless t becomes ru, whose u is for pronunciation. Bhagavat, "the fortunate one": he bhagoḥ, he aghoḥ.

Ubhe abhyastam: "the two together are abhyasta." Where two similar syllables stand bent together, as in dadat, this is given the technical name abhyasta. For dadat, su. Nābhyastāc chatuḥ: "not after an abhyasta, of śatṛ." After what is named abhyasta, num is not given to words ending in the kṛt suffix śatṛ and the like, even in the endings of the strong cases. Dadat means "giving." Num is not given. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. Optionally at a pause: dadad, dadat. For au: dadatau. All the case endings beginning with a vowel are like this. For bhyām: by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, t becomes d: dadadbhyām. Those beginning with a consonant are like this. The vocatives are like the first case.

Words ending in the letter t, beginning with jakṣat: jakṣity ādayaḥ ṣaṭ, "the six beginning with jakṣ also." The six beginning with jakṣ, and cakās, when ending in the suffix śatṛ, are also called abhyasta, for the purpose of blocking num. Those ending in śatṛ beginning with jakṣ are jakṣat, dīdhyat, daridrat, śāsat, vevyat and cakāsat, and for these all the procedures for joining the case endings are like those for dadat.

Words ending in the letter p: for dharmagup, su. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. Optionally at a pause: dharmagup, dharmagub. For au and jas: dharmagupau, dharmagupaḥ. For the second case: dharmagupam, dharmagupau, dharmagupaḥ. For ṭā: dharmagupā. For bhyām and bhis: by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, p becomes b: dharmagubbhyām, dharmagubbhiḥ. It means "guardian of the Dharma." For the fourth case: dharmagupe, dharmagubbhyām, dharmagubbhyaḥ. For ṅasi: dharmagupaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: dharmagupaḥ, dharmagupoḥ, dharmagupām. For the seventh: dharmagupi, dharmagupoḥ, dharmagupsu. For the vocatives: he dharmagup, he dharmagub, he dharmagupau, he dharmagupaḥ.

Words ending in the letter ś: for tyādṛś, su. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. By the guttural of kvin, ś becomes k. Optionally at a pause also: tyādṛk, tyādṛg. For au and jas: tyādṛśau, tyādṛśaḥ. For the second case: tyādṛśam, tyādṛśau, tyādṛśaḥ. For the third case: tyādṛśā, tyādṛgbhyām. For ṅe: tyādṛśe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: the word means "looking like that"; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: tyādṛśaḥ, tyādṛśoḥ, tyādṛśām. For the seventh: tyādṛśi, tyādṛśoḥ, tyādṛkṣu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Tyadādiṣu dṛśo 'nālocane kañ ca: "after tyad and the rest, to dṛś not meaning seeing, kañ also." To dṛś preceded by tyad and the rest, when it does not mean seeing, the suffix kañ, which forms nouns like the kṛt suffixes, optionally applies. If kañ is given, tyādṛśa is formed, and then the procedures for the case endings are like the case of Rāma, the ordinary stem ending in short a. In the commentary it says: "To dṛś preceded by samāna only kvin applies, and then samāna becomes sa." So for sadṛś, the procedures on meeting the case endings are like those for tyādṛś.

Words ending in the letter ś: for viś, su. By the sūtra vraścabhrasja and the rest, ś becomes ṣ. By halṅyāp, su is dropped. Optionally at a pause: viṭ, viḍ. For au and jas: viśau, viśaḥ. For the second case: viśam, viśau, viśaḥ. For ṭā: viśā. For bhyām and bhis: by vraśca and the rest, ś becomes ṣ; by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, ṣ becomes ḍ: viḍbhyām, viḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: viśe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: viśaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: viśaḥ, viśoḥ, viśām. For ṅi: viśi. For os: viśoḥ. For sup: viṭsu. Alternatively, by ḍaḥ si dhuṭ, "after ḍ, before s, dhuṭ," optionally the augment dhuṭ; by the rule that before khar a car is substituted, dh becomes t and ḍ becomes ṭ: viṭtsu. For the vocatives: he viṭ, he viḍ, he viśau, he viśaḥ.

Words ending in the letter ś: for naś, su. Naśer vā: "of naś, optionally." The ś of naś, before the letters of the jhal group and at the end of a word, optionally becomes k: ś becomes k. Su is dropped. By the pause rule: nak, nag. Alternatively, by vraśca and the rest, ś becomes ṣ, and by the pause rule and the rest: naṭ, naḍ. The word means "disappearing" or "perishing." For au and jas: naśau, naśaḥ. For the second case: naśam, naśau, naśaḥ. For ṭā: naśā. For bhyām, since this is optional: naḍbhyām, nagbhyām. For bhis: naḍbhiḥ, nagbhiḥ. For ṅe: naśe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: naśaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: naśaḥ, naśoḥ, naśām. For ṅi: naśi. For os: naśoḥ. For sup: naṭsu, naṭtsu, nakṣu. For the vocatives: he nak, he nag, he naṭ, he naḍ, he naśau, he naśaḥ.

Spṛśo 'nudake kvin: "to spṛś, when not of water, kvin." To the root spṛś, which means touching, when it does not refer to water, the noun-forming suffix kvin is added. So for ghṛtaspṛś, ending in the kvin thus given, su. By the guttural of kvin, ś becomes k. Su is dropped. Optionally at a pause: ghṛtaspṛk, ghṛtaspṛg. For au and jas: ghṛtaspṛśau, ghṛtaspṛśaḥ. For the second case: ghṛtaspṛśam, ghṛtaspṛśau, ghṛtaspṛśaḥ. For ṭā: ghṛtaspṛśā. For bhyām and bhis: by the guttural of kvin, ś becomes k; by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, k becomes g. It means "touching ghee." Ghṛtaspṛgbhyām, ghṛtaspṛgbhiḥ, and the rest are to be worked out in the same way. When it does refer to water: for udakaspṛś, su. By vraśca and the rest, ś becomes ṣ; by the pause rule and the rest: udakaspṛṭ, udakaspṛḍ, and the rest, like viś.

Words ending in ṣ: for dadhṛṣ, su. By the guttural of kvin, ṣ becomes k. By the pause rule and the rest: dadhṛk, dadhṛg. For au and jas: dadhṛṣau, dadhṛṣaḥ. For the second case, the word meaning "bold": dadhṛṣam, dadhṛṣau, dadhṛṣaḥ. For ṭā: dadhṛṣā. For bhyām and bhis: by the guttural of kvin, ṣ becomes k; by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, the guttural k becomes g: dadhṛgbhyām, dadhṛgbhiḥ. For ṅe: dadhṛṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: dadhṛṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: dadhṛṣaḥ, dadhṛṣoḥ, dadhṛṣām. For the seventh: dadhṛṣi, dadhṛṣoḥ, dadhṛkṣu. For the vocatives: he dadhṛk, he dadhṛg, he dadhṛṣau, he dadhṛṣaḥ.

Words ending in the letter ṣ: for ratnamuṣ, su. Su is dropped. By the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, ṣ becomes ḍ. Optionally at a pause: ratnamuṭ, ratnamuḍ. For au and jas: ratnamuṣau, ratnamuṣaḥ. For the second case: ratnamuṣam, ratnamuṣau, ratnamuṣaḥ. For ṭā: ratnamuṣā. For bhyām and bhis: by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś: ratnamuḍbhyām, ratnamuḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: ratnamuṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: ratnamuṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: ratnamuṣaḥ, ratnamuṣoḥ, ratnamuṣām. For the seventh: ratnamuṣi, ratnamuṣoḥ, ratnamuṭsu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Words ending in the letter ṣ: for ṣaṣ, jas. By ṣaḍbhyo luk, "after the ṣaṭ class, deletion," jas and śas disappear. By the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, ṣ becomes ḍ. By the pause rule and the rest: ṣaṭ, ṣaḍ. For śas also: ṣaṭ, ṣaḍ. For bhis: ṣaḍbhiḥ. For both bhyas: ṣaḍbhyaḥ. For ām: by ṣaṭcaturbhyaś ca, "after ṣaṭ and catur also," nuṭ; the word means "six." By raṣābhyām and the rest, n becomes ṇ. By the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, ṣ becomes ḍ. By yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā, "before a nasal, a yar optionally becomes a nasal," ḍ becomes ṇ: ṣaṇṇām, ṣaḍṇām. For sup: ṣaṭsu, ṣaṭtsu. For the vocative: he ṣaṭ, he ṣaḍ.

When ṣaṣ does not have the sense of counting a number, all the case endings apply, and then the whole set of ways the endings apply is like the case of ratnamuṣ.

Words ending in the letter ṣ: for pipaṭhiṣ, su. Su is dropped. By sasajuṣo ruḥ, "s and the s of sajuṣ become ru," ṣ becomes ru, whose u is for pronunciation: pipaṭhir. Rvor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ: "before r and v, the penultimate ik is lengthened." Before a vowelless r or v, the penultimate letters of the ik group become long: i becomes long. By the rule that before khar and at a pause there is visarga: pipaṭhīḥ. For au and jas: pipaṭhiṣau, pipaṭhiṣaḥ. For the second case: pipaṭhiṣam, pipaṭhiṣau, pipaṭhiṣaḥ. For ṭā: pipaṭhiṣā. For bhyām and bhis, formed as in the su position: pipaṭhīrbhyām, pipaṭhīrbhiḥ. For ṅe: pipaṭhiṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: pipaṭhiṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: pipaṭhiṣaḥ, pipaṭhiṣoḥ, pipaṭhiṣām. For the seventh: pipaṭhiṣi, pipaṭhiṣoḥ, pipaṭhīrṣu. Alternatively, numvisarjanīyaśarvyavāye 'pi: "even when num, visarga or a śar intervenes." Where there is a cause for ṣ, such as the iṇ group, then even if the augment num or a visarga stands between the two, s becomes ṣ before a following śar: s becomes ṣ, pipaṭhīḥṣu. For the vocatives: he pipaṭhīḥ, he pipaṭhiṣau, he pipaṭhiṣaḥ.

Words ending in the letter s: for cikīrṣ, su. By hal and the rest, it is dropped. By saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, s is dropped. R becomes visarga: cikīḥ. For au and jas: by the rule for substitutes and the rest, s becomes ṣ: cikīrṣau, cikīrṣaḥ. For the second case: cikīrṣam, cikīrṣau, cikīrṣaḥ. For ṭā: cikīrṣā. For bhyām and bhis: by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, the word meaning "wishing to do" loses its s: cikīrbhyām, cikīrbhiḥ. For ṅe: cikīrṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: cikīrṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: cikīrṣaḥ, cikīrṣoḥ, cikīrṣām. For the seventh: cikīrṣi, cikīrṣoḥ, cikīrṣu. For the vocatives: he cikīḥ, he cikīrṣau, he cikīrṣaḥ.

Words ending in the letter s: for dos, su. Su is dropped. By sasajuṣo ruḥ, s becomes ru: doḥ. For au and jas: by the rule for substitutes and the rest, s becomes ṣ: doṣau, doṣaḥ. For am: doṣam. For auṭ: doṣau. For śas and the endings that follow: by padannomās and the rest, doṣ becomes doṣan. By allopo 'naḥ, the a of an is deleted: the penultimate a is dropped. By the sūtra raṣābhyām and the rest, n becomes ṇ: doṣṇaḥ. Alternatively: doṣaḥ. For ṭā: doṣṇā, doṣā. For bhyām and bhis: since the form changed into doṣan and the unchanged form come to one and the same, by sasajuṣo ruḥ, ṣ becomes r: dorbhyām, dorbhiḥ. For ṅe: doṣṇe, doṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: doṣṇaḥ, doṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅas: doṣṇaḥ, doṣaḥ. For os: doṣṇoḥ, doṣoḥ. For ām: doṣṇām, doṣām. For ṅi: doṣṇi, doṣaṇi, doṣi. For os: doṣṇoḥ, doṣoḥ. For sup: dorṣu. For the vocatives: he doḥ, he doṣau, he doṣaḥ.

Words ending in the letter kṣ: for vivikṣ, su. By halṅyāp and the rest, su is dropped. By skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca, k is dropped. By the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, ṣ becomes ḍ. Optionally at a pause: viviṭ, viviḍ. For au and jas: vivikṣau, vivikṣaḥ. For the second case: vivikṣam, vivikṣau, vivikṣaḥ. For ṭā: vivikṣā. For bhyām and bhis, formed as for the singular of the first case: viviḍbhyām, viviḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: vivikṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: vivikṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: vivikṣaḥ, vivikṣoḥ, vivikṣām. For ṅi: vivikṣi. For os: vivikṣoḥ. For sup: viviṭsu, viviṭtsu. For the vocatives: he viviṭ, he viviḍ, he vivikṣau, he vivikṣaḥ.

Words ending in the letter kṣ: takṣ too is like vivikṣ in all its procedures. Gorakṣ, in one manner, is like takṣ. Alternatively, by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, ṣ is dropped: gorak, gorag. The case endings beginning with a vowel are like those of vivikṣ. For bhyām: goragbhyām. For bhis: goragbhiḥ. For sup: gorakṣu, and so on. This is a subtle point.

Again, a word ending in the letter kṣ: pipakṣ, su. Su is dropped. By saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, ṣ is dropped. By the pause rule and the rest: pipak, pipag. For au and jas: pipakṣau, pipakṣaḥ. For the second case: pipakṣam, pipakṣau, pipakṣaḥ. For ṭā: pipakṣā. For bhyām and bhis: by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, ṣ is dropped; by the rule that before a jhaś a jhal becomes a jaś, k becomes g: pipagbhyām, pipagbhiḥ. For ṅe: pipakṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: pipakṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: pipakṣaḥ, pipakṣoḥ, pipakṣām. For ṅi: pipakṣi; os is alike. For sup: pipakṣu. The vocatives are like the first case. Here the optional form is not applied.

Words ending in the letter kṣ: dadhakṣ too is like vivikṣ in all its procedures.

Words ending in the letter s: for supis, su. Su is dropped. By sasajuṣo ruḥ, s becomes ru, whose u is for pronunciation. By rvor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ, i is changed into its long form: supīḥ. For au and jas: supisau, supisaḥ. For the second case: supisam, supisau, supisaḥ. For ṭā: supisā. For bhyām and bhis: by sasajuṣo ruḥ, ru; by the sūtra rvor and the rest, the penultimate is lengthened: supīrbhyām, supīrbhiḥ. For ṅe: supise; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: supisaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: supisaḥ, supisoḥ, supisām. For the seventh: supisi, supisoḥ, supīrṣu, supīḥṣu. The vocatives are like the first case. Sunus too is like supis in its procedures.

Words ending in the letter s with the marker u: for vidvasu, su. Since the u serves for num, it is dropped. By ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ, num. By the rule that in the strong cases other than the vocative singular also, the penultimate is lengthened. By halṅyāp and the rest, and by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ and the rest: vidvān, meaning "the learned one." For au and jas: vidvāṃsau, vidvāṃsaḥ. For am and auṭ: vidvāṃsam, vidvāṃsau. For śas: vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam, "of vas, saṃprasāraṇa." Whenever any case ending beginning with a vowel, such as śas, follows the stem-final vas, it is changed back again: the vowelless v becomes u.

Vid u as, śas. By saṃprasāraṇāc ca, "and after saṃprasāraṇa," the a goes into the form of the preceding vowel. By the rule for substitutes and the rest, s becomes ṣ: viduṣaḥ. For ṭā: viduṣā. For bhyām and bhis: by vasusraṃsudhvaṃsvanaḍuhāṃ daḥ, "d in place of the finals of vasu, sraṃsu, dhvaṃsu and anaḍuh," s becomes d: vidvadbhyām, vidvadbhiḥ. For ṅe: viduṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: viduṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: viduṣaḥ, viduṣoḥ, viduṣām. For the seventh: viduṣi, viduṣoḥ, vidvatsu. For the vocatives: he vidvan, he vidvāṃsau, he vidvāṃsaḥ.

Words ending in s with the marker u: for pecivasu, su. By ugit and the rest, num. Su is dropped. The final of the cluster is dropped. By the rule for the strong cases other than the vocative singular and the rest, the penultimate is lengthened: pecivān. For au and jas: pecivāṃsau, pecivāṃsaḥ; for am and auṭ: pecivāṃsam, pecivāṃsau. For śas: by the saṃprasāraṇa of vas, v becomes u. By saṃprasāraṇāc ca, the a goes into the form of the preceding vowel. Since the commentary says, "When vas becomes u, iṭ disappears," the vowel i of c is dropped. By the rule for substitutes and the rest, s becomes ṣ: pecuṣaḥ. For ṭā: pecuṣā. For bhyām and bhis: by vasusraṃsu and the rest, s becomes d: pecivadbhyām, pecivadbhiḥ. For ṅe: pecuṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: pecuṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: pecuṣaḥ, pecuṣoḥ, pecuṣām. For the seventh: pecuṣi, pecuṣoḥ, pecivatsu. For the vocatives: he pecivan, he pecivāṃsau, he pecivāṃsaḥ.

Words ending in s: for jagmivasu, su. Mvoś ca: "before m and v also." Before a suffix beginning with the letter m or the letter v, the m of the root becomes n: m becomes n, giving jaganvasu, su. By ugit and the rest, num; the u serves that purpose. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. The final of the cluster is dropped. By the rule for the strong cases other than the vocative singular and the rest, the penultimate is lengthened: jaganvān. For au and jas: jaganvāṃsau, jaganvāṃsaḥ. For am and auṭ: jaganvāṃsam, jaganvāṃsau. For śas: gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi, "of gam, han, jan, khan and ghas, deletion before what has k or ṅ as marker, but not before aṅ." The penultimate a of gam and these others is deleted before suffixes such as ti that have the marker k or the marker ṅ, other than aṅ, whenever any ending beginning with a vowel occurs, from the case ending śas through os of the seventh case: the a of g is dropped. By the saṃprasāraṇa of vas, v becomes u, and the a separated from v, by saṃprasāraṇāc ca, goes into the form of the preceding vowel. Since v has become u, n turns back into m. By the rule for substitutes and the rest, s becomes ṣ: jagmuṣaḥ. For ṭā: jagmuṣā. For bhyām and bhis: by vasusraṃsu and the rest, d: jaganvadbhyām, jaganvadbhiḥ. For ṅe: jagmuṣe; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: jagmuṣaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: jagmuṣaḥ, jagmuṣoḥ, jagmuṣām. For ṅi: jagmuṣi. For os: jagmuṣoḥ. For sup: jaganvatsu. For the vocatives: he jaganvan, he jaganvāṃsau, he jaganvāṃsaḥ.

Words ending in the letter s: suhiṃs, glossed "living very well." For suhiṃs, su. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. By saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, s is dropped: suhin. For au and jas: suhiṃsau, suhiṃsaḥ. For the second case: suhiṃsam, suhiṃsau, suhiṃsaḥ. For ṭā: suhiṃsā. For bhyām and bhis: by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, s is dropped: suhinbhyām, suhinbhiḥ. For ṅe: suhiṃse; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: suhiṃsaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: suhiṃsaḥ, suhiṃsoḥ, suhiṃsām. For the seventh: suhiṃsi, suhiṃsoḥ, suhiṃsu. For the vocatives: he suhin, he suhiṃsau, he suhiṃsaḥ.

Words ending in the letter s: for puṃs, su. Puṃso 'suṅ: "asuṅ in place of puṃs." The final letter s of puṃs becomes asuṅ before the case ending su and the other strong endings: s becomes asuṅ, with ṅ as a marker. By ugit and the rest, num; the u serves that purpose. By hal and the rest, su is dropped. By saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, s is dropped. The word means "male." By the rule for the strong cases other than the vocative singular and the rest, the penultimate is lengthened: pumān. For au and jas: pumāṃsau, pumāṃsaḥ. For am and auṭ: pumāṃsam, pumāṃsau. For śas: puṃsaḥ. For ṭā: puṃsā. For bhyām and bhis: by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, s is dropped: pumbhyām, pumbhiḥ. For ṅe: puṃse; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: puṃsaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: puṃsaḥ, puṃsoḥ, puṃsām. For the seventh: puṃsi, puṃsoḥ, puṃsu. For the vocatives: he puman, he pumāṃsau, he pumāṃsaḥ.

Words ending in the letter s: for Uśanas, su. By ṛduśanaspurudaṃśo'nehasāṃ ca, "of stems in ṛ, and of Uśanas, purudaṃśas and anehas also," the stem final becomes anaṅ, the a being the vowel of n and the ṅ a marker. By the rule for the strong cases other than the vocative singular and the rest, the penultimate is lengthened. By the rule deleting n at the end of a nominal stem, n is dropped: Uśanā. For au and jas: Uśanasau, Uśanasaḥ. For the second case, the name meaning "the pure one": Uśanasam, Uśanasau, Uśanasaḥ. For ṭā: Uśanasā. For bhyām and bhis: Uśanobhyām, Uśanobhiḥ. For ṅe: Uśanase; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For ṅasi: Uśanasaḥ; bhyām and bhyas are alike. For the sixth case: Uśanasaḥ, Uśanasoḥ, Uśanasām. For the seventh: Uśanasi, Uśanasoḥ, Uśanaḥsu. In the vocative singular three forms arise. In one manner, by hal and the rest, su is dropped, and by sasajuṣo ruḥ and the rest: he Uśanaḥ. Alternatively, since the commentary says, "In the vocative singular the stem final optionally becomes anaṅ, and deleting n or not deleting it is optional," the stem final becomes anaṅ, and n is optionally deleted or not: he Uśana, he Uśanan. The dual and plural are like the first case. For both anehas and purudaṃśas, the option in the vocative singular is not applied; all their other procedures are like those of Uśanas.

Words ending in s: for vedhas, su. Su is dropped. By atvasantasya cādhātoḥ, "and of what ends in atu or as, when not a root," the penultimate is lengthened: vedhāḥ. In the vocative singular: he vedhaḥ. All the rest is like Uśanas. For suvas too, the penultimate is not lengthened in the su position; its other procedures are like those of vedhas just explained.

Among the pronouns of the sarva group, those ending in s. For adas, su. By adasa au sulopaś ca, "for adas, au, and su is also elided": the s at the end of the stem adas becomes au, and su too is elided. So s becomes au, and su is dropped. By tadoḥ saḥ sāv anantyayoḥ, "s for the t and d of tyad and the rest, before su, when not final": d becomes s. By vṛddhir eci, vṛddhi before ec: asau.

For adas: when the suffix akac is given to it, asaka is formed; then by the rule "and u after s," when the suffix akac has been given to adas, the a that follows the d already turned into s becomes u, and asuka is formed. All its procedures with the case endings are in general like those of Rāma, which ends in short a.

For au: by tyadādīnām aḥ, "a for tyad and the rest before a case ending," s becomes a. By ato guṇe, the form of the following vowel. By vṛddhir eci, vṛddhi before ec: adau. By adaso 'ser dād u do maḥ, "for adas, u after d, and m for d": whatever case ending is seen, except su, the singular of the first case, the d of adas becomes m, and whatever long vowel follows the d becomes long ū, and whatever short one becomes short u: amū.

For jas: by tyadādi, ada, jas. By the rule for adas, d becomes m. By jasaḥ śī, śī for jas. By ād guṇaḥ, guṇa after a: ame. By eta īd bahuvacane, "ī for e in the plural": the e arising from a plural case ending of adas, whose d has become m, becomes ī. So e becomes ī: amī.

For am: amum. For au: amū. For śas: amūn. For ṭā: amunā. For bhyām: amūbhyām. For bhis: by neda madasor akoḥ, "not for idam and adas when without k," bhis does not become ais. By bahuvacane jhaly et, e in the plural before jhal. By eta īd bahuvacane, ī for e in the plural: amībhiḥ. For ṅe: amuṣmai. For bhyām: amūbhyām. For bhyas: amībhyaḥ. For ṅasi: amuṣmāt. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: amuṣya. For os: amuyoḥ. For ām: amīṣām. For ṅi: amuṣmin. For os: amuyoḥ. For sup: amīṣu.

iti pāṇinibhyākarṇasya sūtrātyurlidga halantāḥ smābhāḥ That is: the masculine stems ending in consonants, arising from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, are complete.

Thus, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down as notes the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so forth of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the masculine stems ending in consonants, with the general rules and special exceptions of their procedures on meeting the case endings, have for now been completed in their broad outlines.

Now I shall explain the feminine stems ending in consonants. First among these, the feminine stems ending in h. For upānah, su. By naho dhaḥ, "dh for the h of nah": the h of nah becomes dh before the letters gathered in the case-ending abbreviation jhal and at the end of a word. So h becomes dh. By jhalāṃ jaś, jaś for jhal: dh becomes d. By vāvasāne, optionally at a pause: upānat, upānad. For au and jas: upānah, meaning a sandal bound on the foot: upānahau, upānahaḥ. For the second case: upānaham, upānahau, upānahaḥ. For ṭā: upānahā. For bhyām and bhis: by naho dhaḥ, h becomes dh; by jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi, jaś for jhal before jhaś, dh becomes d: upānadbhyām, upānadbhiḥ. For ṅe: upānahe. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: upānahaḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For the sixth case: upānahaḥ, upānahoḥ, upānahām. For the seventh case: upānahi, upānahoḥ, upānatsu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Ending in h: for uṣṇih, su. The suffix. By kvinpratyayasya kuḥ, a velar for a stem with the suffix kvin: h becomes gh. By jhalāṃ jaś, jaś for jhal: gh becomes g. By vāvasāne and the rest: uṣṇik, uṣṇig. For au and jas: uṣṇihau, uṣṇihaḥ, and so on; the case endings beginning with a vowel are to be worked out on the same pattern. For bhyām and bhis: the velar for kvin; by jhalāṃ jaś, jaś for jhal: uṣṇigbhyām, uṣṇigbhiḥ. For sup: the velar for kvin; by khari ca, car before khar: gh becomes k; k and ṣ combined make kṣ: uṣṇikṣu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Ending in v: for div, su. By diva aut, au for the v of div: dyauḥ. For au and jas: divau, divaḥ. For am: the suffix, optionally, as explained: dyām, divam. For au and śas: divau, divaḥ. For ṭā: the suffix: divā. For bhyām and bhis: by diva ut, u for the v of div: dyubhyām, dyubhiḥ. For ṅe: dive. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: divaḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For the sixth case: divaḥ, divoḥ, divām. For the seventh case: divi, divoḥ, dyuṣu. For the vocative: he dyauḥ, he divau, he divaḥ.

Ending in t preceded by div: for dyūrṇut, the commentary quotes from elsewhere that before the letter u the v of div becomes u. So v becomes u; by akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ, the long vowel for a like vowel after ak; by iko yaṇ aci, yaṇ for ik before a vowel. For dyūrṇut, su: by halṅyādi, su is dropped. By vāvasāne, optionally at a pause: dyūrṇut, dyūrṇud. For au and jas: dyūrṇutau, dyūrṇutaḥ, and so on; the endings beginning with a vowel are to be worked out on the same pattern. For bhyām: by jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi, t becomes d: dyūrṇudbhyām. Bhis, bhyām, bhyas and the rest are likewise to be worked out. For sup: dyūrṇutsu. For the vocatives: he dyūrṇut, he dyūrṇud, he dyūrṇutau, he dyūrṇutaḥ.

Ending in r: for gir, su. By rvor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ, "the penultimate ik is lengthened before r and v": long ī; su is dropped: gīḥ. For au and jas: girau, giraḥ. For the second case: giram, girau, giraḥ. For ṭā: girā. For bhyām and bhis: by the rule for r and v, the penultimate is lengthened: gīrbhyām, gīrbhiḥ. For ṅe: gire. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: giraḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For the sixth case: giraḥ, giroḥ, girām. For the seventh case: giri, giroḥ, gīrṣu. For the vocative: he gīḥ, he girau, he giraḥ.

Ending in r: pur, and dhur too; all their procedures are like those of gir.

Ending in r: for catur, jas. By tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ, "in the feminine, tisṛ and catasṛ for tri and catur": it becomes catasṛ. Catasraḥ. For śas: catasraḥ. For bhis: catasṛbhiḥ. For the two, bhyām and bhyas: catasṛbhyām, catasṛbhyaḥ. For ām: catasṛṇām. For sup: catasṛṣu. For the vocative: he catasraḥ.

Ending in m: for kim, by kimaḥ kaḥ, ka for kim. The feminine suffix ṭāp: kā. For su: by halṅyābbhyaḥ, su after ṅī and āp is dropped: kā. For au: by auṅa āpaḥ, śī for au after āp: ke. For jas: by the rule "for the first two cases": kāḥ, and so on. All its procedures are like those explained for the feminine sarvā.

Ending in m: for idam, su. By idamo maḥ, m for idam: the final part does not become a. By yaḥ sau, y before su: the d of idam, in the feminine, becomes y before what follows. So d becomes y; su is dropped: iyam. For au: by tyadādīnām aḥ, a for tyad and the rest: m becomes a. By ato guṇe, the form of the preceding vowel. By daś ca, m for d as well. The feminine suffix ṭāp: imā. By auṅa āpaḥ, śī for au after āp: ime. For jas: imāḥ. For am: imām. For au: ime. For śas: imāḥ. For ṭā: by anāpy akaḥ, an before āp and the rest, id becomes ana. The feminine suffix ṭāp: anā. By āṅi cāpaḥ, "and before āṅ, for āp": anayā. For bhyām: by hali lopaḥ, elision before a consonant, i and d are dropped: a; ṭāp: ābhyām. For bhis: ābhiḥ. For ṅe: idam becomes a, ṭāp; by sarvanāmnaḥ syāḍ ḍhrasvaś ca, "syāṭ after a pronoun, and shortening": syāṭ: asyai. For bhyām and bhyas: ābhyām, ābhyaḥ. For ṅasi: asyāḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: asyāḥ. For os: anayoḥ. For ām: āsām. For ṅi: asyām. For os: anayoḥ. For sup: āsu. As explained, there is an option for the second-case endings, for ṭā and for the two os endings; in that alternative, for the second case: enām, ene, enāḥ. For ṭā: enayā. For the two os: enayoḥ.

Ending in j: for sraj, su. By coḥ kuḥ, a velar for a palatal: j becomes g. Su is dropped. By vāvasāne, optionally at a pause: srak, srag. For au and jas: srajau, srajaḥ. For the second case: srajam, srajau, srajaḥ. For ṭā: srajā. For bhyām and bhis, by coḥ kuḥ, a velar for a palatal: sragbhyām, sragbhiḥ. For ṅe: sraje. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: srajaḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For the sixth case: srajaḥ, srajoḥ, srajām. For ṅi: sraji. For os: srajoḥ. For sup: by coḥ kuḥ, j becomes g; by khari ca, car before khar: srakṣu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Ending in d: for tyad, su. By tyadādi, a. By ato guṇe, the form of the preceding vowel. The feminine suffix ṭāp. By tadoḥ saḥ sāv anantyayoḥ, s for t and d before su when not final: t becomes s. Su is dropped: syā. For au: tye. For jas: tyāḥ, and so on, as with the feminine sarvā. Tad and yad also, both of them, follow in all their procedures what has just been explained.

Ending in c: for vāc, su. By coḥ kuḥ, a velar for a palatal: c becomes k. Su is dropped. By vāvasāne, optionally at a pause: vāk, vāg. For au and jas: vācau, vācaḥ. For the second case: vācam, vācau, vācaḥ. For ṭā: vācā. For bhyām and bhis: by coḥ kuḥ, c becomes k; by jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi, jaś for jhal before jhaś: k becomes g: vāgbhyām, vāgbhiḥ, vāc meaning speech or utterance. For ṅe: vāce. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: vācaḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For the sixth case: vācaḥ, vācoḥ, vācām. For the seventh case: vāci, vācoḥ, vākṣu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Ending in p: ap, water. For ap, the singular forms of the case endings do not occur; only the plural does. For ap, jas: by aptṛn and the rest, the penultimate is lengthened: āpaḥ. For śas: apaḥ. For bhis: by apo bhi, "for ap before bh": the p of ap becomes t before a case ending in bh. So p becomes t; by jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi, t becomes d: adbhiḥ. For the two bhyas: adbhyaḥ. For ām: apām. For sup: apsu. For the vocative: he āpaḥ.

Ending in ś: for diś, su. By jhalāṃ jaś, jaś for jhal: ś becomes j. By coḥ kuḥ, j becomes g. By vāvasāne, optionally at a pause: dik, dig. For au and jas: diśau, diśaḥ. For the second case: diśam, diśau, diśaḥ. For ṭā: diśā. For bhyām and bhis: by jhalāṃ jaś, ś becomes j; by coḥ kuḥ, g: digbhyām, digbhiḥ. For ṅe: diśe. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: diśaḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For the sixth case: diśaḥ, diśoḥ, diśām. For the seventh case: diśi, diśoḥ, dikṣu. The vocatives are like the first case. Dṛś too follows in all its procedures what has just been explained.

Ending in ṣ: for tviṣ, su. By jhalāṃ jaś, jaś for jhal: ṣ becomes ḍ. By vāvasāne, optionally at a pause: tviṭ, tviḍ. For au and jas: tviṣau, tviṣaḥ. For the second case: tviṣam, tviṣau, tviṣaḥ. For ṭā: tviṣā. For bhyām and bhis: by jhalāṃ jaś, ṣ becomes ḍ: tviḍbhyām, tviḍbhiḥ. For ṅe: tviṣe. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: tviṣaḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For the sixth case: tviṣaḥ, tviṣoḥ, tviṣām. For the seventh case: tviṣi, tviṣoḥ, tviṭsu, tviṭtsu. The vocatives are like the first case.

Ending in ṣ: for sajuṣ, su. Su is dropped. By sasajuṣo ruḥ, ru for s and for sajuṣ: ṣ becomes r. By the rule for r and v, the penultimate is lengthened: sajūḥ. For au and jas: sajuṣau, sajuṣaḥ. For the second case: sajuṣam, sajuṣau, sajuṣaḥ. For ṭā: sajuṣā. For bhyām and bhis: sajūrbhyām, sajūrbhiḥ. For ṅe: sajuṣe. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: sajuṣaḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For the sixth case: sajuṣoḥ, sajuṣām. For the seventh case: sajuṣi, sajuṣoḥ, sajūrṣu. For the vocatives: he sajūḥ, he sajuṣau, he sajuṣaḥ. Āśiṣ too is like what has just been explained.

Ending in s: for adas, su. By adasa au sulopaś ca, au for adas, and su is also elided: s becomes au; su is dropped. By the rule for t and d, d becomes s: asau. For au: by tyadādi, a. By ato guṇe, the form of the preceding vowel. The feminine suffix ṭāp: adā. For au: by auṅa āpaḥ, au becomes ī. By ād guṇaḥ, guṇa after a: a and ī make e. By adaso 'ser dād u do maḥ, u after the d of adas, and m for d: amū. For jas: amūḥ. For am: amūm. For au: amū. For śas: amūḥ. For ṭā: amuyā. For bhyām: amūbhyām. For bhis: amūbhiḥ. For ṅe: amuṣyai. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅasi: amuṣyāḥ. Bhyām and bhyas are the same. For ṅas: amuṣyāḥ. For os: amuyoḥ. For ām: amūṣām. For ṅi: amuṣyām. For os: amuyoḥ. For sup: amūṣu.
