In the sense of "the collection of the Upagus," opagabānāṃsamūhaḥ: aupagabakaṃ (su, a), "the collection of the Upagus," which is a gotra. Likewise: aukṣakaṃ, a collection of humped ones, that is, of bulls. auṣakaṃ. buñ: aurabhrakaṃ. buñ: rājakaṃ. buñ: rājaṇyakaṃ. buñ: rājabutraka. buñ: bātākaṃ. buñ: māruṣḍyakaṃ. ājakaṃ.

bṛddhraścca: also from vṛddha. From vṛddha too (to opagaba, buñ, the ñ serving for strengthening), buñ applies when a collection is to be expressed (buñ, the ñ for strengthening, bu becoming aka; and by "of ya, also before i," the a is deleted). (A collection of she-camels; of the bellyless, that is, of butchers.) A collection of kings; a collection of kṣatriyas; a collection of kings' sons; (a collection of calves; a collection of men; a collection of cows; bāṇḍhakraṃ; kedārādyañca).

From kedāra also yañ. From kedāra, when a collection is to be expressed, buñ applies after the sixth-case ending, and yañ as well: kaidārakaṃ, kaidāryaṃ.

yuvornākau: of yu and bu, ana and aka. The affixes yu and bu become ana and aka respectively. A collection of elders: to vṛddha, buñ, the ñ for strengthening, bu becoming aka, su, a, ma.

Cited in the commentary: gaṇikāyāḥyañ: yañ from gaṇikā. When its collection is to be expressed from gaṇikā (a collection of fish, or a collection of fields, or a collection of forests), yañ applies after the sixth-case ending: gāṇikya.

ṭhañkabacinaśca: ṭhañ also from kabacin. From kabacin and from kedāra too, when a collection is to be expressed, ṭhañ applies after the sixth-case ending: kābacikaṃ, a collection of armored men; kaibārikaṃ, a collection of farmers.

brāhpraṇamānababānababāḍabāḍyat: yat from brātmaṇa, māna and bāḍaba. From these, brātmaṇa and the rest (a collection of astrologers' wives, or a collection of courtesans), when a collection is to be expressed, yat applies after the sixth-case ending. yat: byāhmaṇya, a collection of brahmins (for ka, ta, the ñ serving for strengthening; and by "of ya, also before i," the a is deleted. at: mānbyaṃ, bāḍabyaṃ).

grāmajanabaṇbṅkushāyebhyastala: tal, with su, after brāma, jana, bantnu and sahāya. When a collection of these, grāma and the rest, is to be expressed, tal applies after the sixth-case ending (yat, ta, its part), and, the l being a marker, what ends in tal is by its nature feminine. (A collection of brahmin youths; a collection of mares.) A collection of villages: grāmatā (tal, ṭāp). janatā, a collection of people. A collection of relatives or kin: bandhutā. tal, ṇā, pha: sahāyatā, a collection of friends.

Cited in the commentary: gajācca: also from gaja. From gaja too, when a collection is to be expressed, tal applies after the sixth-case ending: gajatā.

acittahastidhenoṣṭhak: ṭhak from what lacks mind, from hastin and from dhenu. From things without mind, from hastin and from dhenu, when a collection is to be expressed, ṭhak applies after the sixth-case ending: ābūpikaṃ (a collection of things given up); hāstikaṃ, ṭhak, a collection of elephants.

isusuktāntatāskaḥ: ka from those ending in is, us, uk and t. After stems ending in the affixes is, us, uk and t, the following affix ṭha becomes ka: dhainukaṃ (a collection of milch cows). Likewise, for abvupa, ṇa, ka, the k serving for exclusion (for laṣa and the rest, ṭhak, the k serving for exclusion; by "of ya, also before i," the i is deleted). sārba(ṣki), a collection of burnt offerings. dhānuṣkaṃ (a collection of gabu).

Cited in the commentary: bṛchatāsuśnātadibhyaḥ (to dhainu, ṭhak, strengthening, ṭhak): from bṛcchata, suṣṇata and the rest. From pṛcchata, suṣṇata and the rest too, when a collection is to be expressed, ṭhak applies after the sixth-case ending: (ṣakapārch)atikana (from sabiṣa, ṭhak, strengthening, ṭhak; to dhanuṣa, ṭhak, strengthening, ṭhak), ṭhak: sauṣṇatikaḥ. taimadgilakaḥ, a collection of great fish. gauñjikaḥ: to thañja, ṭhak. saukhaśāyikaḥ (nukhaśāya, ṭhak). saidnalikaḥ.

bāśādibhyoyaḥ: ya from pāśa and the rest. From bāśa and the rest (a collection of questions), when a collection is to be expressed, ya applies after the sixth-case ending (a collection of rdus; for timarṇe, ṭhak; a collection of red-horned black-headed ones): (ladāśyā) (from the collection of those who lie at ease, a collection of the red-yellow ones; for senale, dha; ya: bātra, batṛṇya).

ūloñpi: ūla also. From bata, when a collection is to be expressed, ūla also applies: bātūlaḥ, ūla.

Cited in the commentary: khalagorathādya: ya from khala, go and ratha. From these, khala and the rest (a collection of nooses), when a collection is to be expressed, ya (a collection of streams; joined with ḍāp, it is by its nature a feminine)

applies. ya: khalyā. ḍbe, a collection of the low or the wicked (lagabyāḍāba, ba; a collection of balanga; a collection of winds). (ya: rathyā; ṭap; a collection of chariots.)

initrakadyacaśca: also ini, tra, ka, dya and ca. From khala, go and ratha, when a collection is to be expressed, ini, tā, ka, dya and ca apply respectively: khaliniṣ (a collection of cattle, or a collection of clans), gotrā, gosdalaḍā, rathakadra, a collection of chariots.

tadasyaṃpraharaṇamitikrīḍāyāṇṇaḥ: ṇa in the sense "with this weapon he plays." In the sense "with this weapon he plays," after the ending of the first case, seven (a collection of those with ... or of the wicked) (for ṣala, sinin, e in the sense of what is uttered, ri, tan, ma, unaccepted, dīr) (for ratha, ka, dya, ca, ca for the vowel) ṇa, having the sense of the ..., applies. In the sense of daṇḍaḥpraharaṇamasyaṃgrīdāyāṃ: to danḍa, ṇa (dāṇḍā; ṇa, ḍā, ga). Likewise: mauṣṭa.

ghañaḥsāsyāṃkrīyetiñaḥ: ña after ghañ, in the sense "this is the action." After a word ending in ghañ that has an action word before it, ña applies in the sense of the seventh case: to śyenapāta, ña: śyenatilasyabāteñe (in this, weapons ... arise; for śyenatila, bṭan, ña). (They play with switches; to muṇṭi, ṇa, removed, ṭāga; the play of khuruba.) When an affix of bwataha follows, the augment mum comes to śyena and tila. The m is the m that does not go, with the sense of following a final vowel (ac), and the u is for pronunciation. (ña, ṭāba: śraināṃpātā.) Likewise: tailaṃbātā, the falling of oil.

tadadhītetadveda: who studies it and who knows it. In the sense of studying it and knowing it, aṇ and the rest apply after the second-case ending: i(ṇḍrā)dayaḥ. In the sense of iṣṭabyākaraṇaṃarhitepāṇirṛṣiḥ: bai (la lha bu na) yākara (to the pāta preceded by tila, ña, strengthening; for what is called śyenatila, na bṭāba) ṇaṃpāṇinirṛṣitha. Likewise: (intna)dayaḥ (aṣṭabyākaraṇaṃbehi: the eight grammars called "Indra and the rest" are the indrakaraṇa, the bibābyākaraṇa, the śākaṭāyaṇabyragaraṇa, the pīṇinibyākara, the mantadhadrabhakaraṇa, the bahechalibyākaraṇa and the manujendrabyrakaraṇa). Indra (and the rest: who reads the eight grammars, the brangspong bāṇaṃba). bāṇinirṛṣiḥ (byākaraṇamaanaeāgamasuyaga). In the sense of "the sage Pāṇini, who reads grammar": aṇ: baiyākaraṇaṃbāṇinirṛṣiḥ, the sage Pāṇini, who knows grammar.

kramādibhyobuna: buna after krama and the rest. From krama and the rest, in the sense of studying it (the sage Pāṇini, who knows the eight grammars beginning with that of Indra) and knowing it, bu applies; the n for the vowel, bu becoming aka. buna: kramakaḥ (who knows rumaba). buna: padakaḥ.

tadasminnastītideśetannāmni: "it is in this," for a country, as its name. In the sense "it is in this," which also makes known the name of a country, aṇ applies after the seventh-case ending. In the sense of udumbarāṇisaṃtiasmindeśe: audumāraḥ.

tenanirbṛttaṃ (knower of words): accomplished by it. In the sense of "accomplished by it," aṇ and the rest apply after the third-case ending. In the sense of kuśuśāmbenaninṛtta: kauśambśi, the city.

tasyanivāsaḥ: its abode (the country in which there are udumāras; udubyara lodba). For dwelling in an abode, as its name, aṇ and the rest apply after the sixth-case ending. In the sense of śibānīnivāsaḥ: śaibaḥ.

adūrabhabaśca (by Ngensel, the not far from Gaṅgā, the city having a treasury; to kuśamā, aṇ, strengthening, dība by ṭita, ḍha and the rest): also from nearness. When nearness is expressed, aṇ and the rest apply after the sixth-case ending. In the sense of bidiṅśāṇāmadurabhabaṃ: baidiśaṃ, aṇ, strengthening. The abode of the Śivas: Śaiva, aṇ removed.

janapadelub: elision in a region. When the affixes with the sense of an abode have the sense of naming a region, they are elided before a plural case ending: paṃcalāḥ, the aṇ being deleted. (The nearness of countries.) baraṇādibhyaśca: also from baraṇa and the rest (countries not far off). The affixes in the sense of nearness to baraṇa and the rest are also elided before a following plural case ending: paraṇaḥ (those near in clan).

śeṣe: in the remainder. (The region of the Pañcālas above.) Beyond the applications explained above, in the remaining, other senses, aṇ and the rest apply. In the sense of cakṣuṣāgṛhyate: cākṣuṣaṃ. aṇ: śrābaṇaḥ. aṇ: rāsanaḥ. aṇ: sbārśanaḥ. After jas, the aṇ is deleted.

tatrajātaḥ: from "born there." In the sense of "born there," aṇ and the rest apply after the seventh-case ending. Born in Mathurā: in the sense of mathurāyāṃ (what is to be seen, the eye) jātaḥ (what is to be seen, aṇ, su, a, mi; what is to be heard, what is to be tasted, what is to be touched), born in Mathurā: māthuraḥ, aṇ, strengthening.

brābṛṣaṣṭhak: ṭhak after prāpṛṣa. From the word prābṛṣa, in the sense of "born there," ṭhak applies after the seventh-case ending: prābṛṣikaḥ.

tatrabahabaḥ: for what exists there. When existence there is to be expressed, aṇ and the rest apply after the seventh-case ending. In the sense of mathurāyāṃbhabaḥ: māthuraḥ.

digādibhyoyat: yat after diśa and the rest. (For diśa and the rest, ṭhak, the k for strengthening, ṭhak becoming eka; those born in summer.) For these, yat applies in the sense of existing. yat: diśyaṃ. yat: bargyi.

śarīrābayabācca: also from a part of the body. (Mathurā itself.) From a part of the body too (Mathurā itself), yat applies in the sense of existing. yat: danhyi. yat: karṇyaṃ. yat: hastyaṃ. auṣṭhyaṃ. yat: pādyaṃ.

Cited in the commentary: adhyātmādeḥ ka (direction itself; the section itself): ṭhak after adhyātma and the rest. From adhyātma and the rest, ṭhak applies in the sense of existing: ādhyātmikaṃ, āthidaiba (teeth themselves, ears themselves, hands themselves, lips themselves, feet themselves) kraṃ, aihalaukikaṃ.

tataāgataḥ: for "come from there." In expressing the sense "come from there," iṇ applies after the fifth-case ending. In the sense of mathurāyāḥāgataḥ (ṭhak, the k for strengthening, ṇa becoming eka; the inner itself; ṭhak, na, acu, śarka, by force both prior and latter strengthened, ga): māthuraḥ. (Having a superior god; happy in the world; ṭhak, strengthening.) ṭhak for "come from an abode."

When "come from an abode" is to be expressed, ṭhak applies after the fifth-case ending (come from Mathurā): ṭhak: āpaṇikaṃ.

so'syanibāsaḥ: for "that is its abode." When "that is its abode" is to be expressed (come from Mathurā), aṇ applies after the sixth-case ending. In the sense of mathuraḥpanibāsosya: māthuraḥ.

tenaproktaṃ: for "proclaimed by him." In the sense of "proclaimed by him," aṇ applies after the third-case ending (come from its own abode). In the sense of bhagabatāproktaṃ, "proclaimed by the Blessed One": aṇ: bhragabati, proclaimed by the Blessed One. (Its abode is Mathurā; one of Mathurā.) mānabaḥ: proclaimed by a human being.

kṛtegranthi: for a treatise composed. In the sense of a treatise composed by him, aṇ applies after the third-case ending. In the sense of pāṇinenakṛgranthaḥ: aṇ: pāṇinogranthaḥ.

tasyedaṃ: for "this is his." In the sense of "this is his," aṇ applies after the sixth-case ending. In the sense of upagorinaṃ: aupagabaḥ.

rathādyat: yat from ratha. From ratha, in the sense of "this is its," yat applies (a treatise composed by Pāṇini): rathasyedaṃ (a treatise composed by Pāṇini). In that sense: rathyaṃ.

grāmādyakhañau: ya and khañ from grāma. From grāma (this too is "near"; this one of the Upagus), ya and khañ apply in the remainder. In the sense of grāmejataḥ, grāmādāgataḥ and grāmebhabaḥ: ya: grāmyaṃ (this chariot); grāmīṇaḥ.

nadyādibhyoḍhak: ḍhak from nadī and the rest (this chariot). From nadī and the rest, in the remainder, that is, in those three groups of senses, "born" and the rest (born in a village; come from a village; the village itself), ḍhak applies (of the village, or come from the village, or in the village; ba, ñ, the ñ for strengthening, kha replaced by īna): nādeyaḥ, born in a river, or come from a river, or of the river itself. yāmuneyaḥ, born in the river Yamunā, or come from the Yamunā, or of the Yamunā. māheyaḥ: to mahī, ḍhak.

dakṣiṇāścatpurastatyak: tyak from dakṣiṇā, paścāt and puras. From these, dakṣiṇā and the rest, tyak applies in the remainder (ḍhak, the k for strengthening, ḍha becoming eya). tyak: dakṣiṇātyaḥ. tyak: pāścātyaḥ (from jñar, the r of jñar deleted; to yamuna, ḍhak). tyak: paurastyaḥ. dyubrāga (born from the earth, or come from the earth, or the earth).

bāgudakpratīcoyat: yat from dib, prāc, abāc, udīc and pratīc. From these, dipa and the rest, yat applies in the remainder (born in the south, or come from the south, or southern; born in the west, or come from the west, or western; born in the east, or come from the east, or eastern). yat: dibyaḥ, born in heaven, or come from heaven, or heavenly. yat: prācyaḥ, born in the east, or come from the east, or eastern. yat: abācyaḥ, born in the west, or come from the west, or western. yat: udīcyaḥ, born in the north, or come from the north, or northern. yat: pratīcyaḥ.

abyayāttyaba: tyap from an indeclinable. From the indeclinables ama, iha and kva, and from words ending in the affixes tasil and tral, tyap applies in the remainder: amātaḥ (tyap, the p for the vowel). tyap: ihatyaḥ. tyap: kvatyaḥ (born from what, or come from what, or what). tyatata (born in the west, or come from the west, or western) tasraḥ. tyap: tatratyaḥ.

tyapneḥdhrube: tyap from ni in the sense of "fixed." From ni, in the sense of "fixed," tyap applies. In the sense of niya(taṃdgrubaṃ) (a minister, or born from a minister): tyap: nityaṃ (born from this, or come from here).

aiṣamohyaḥśvasoñanyatara (born from that, or come from that, or that; born from that, or come from that, or that) syī: optionally from aiṣamas, hyas and śvas. From aiṣamas and the rest, in the remainder (certain or fixed), tyap applies optionally (certain, or fixed, or unmoving). tyap: aiṣamastyaṃ, born from this, or come from this, or this. tyap: hyastyaṃ. tyap: śvasbyaṃ (born from the wind, or come from the wind, or wind). Or else aiṣamastanaṃ and so on, which will be explained below.

vṛdhiḥyasyāmāditastadbṛdthi: that whose first vowel is strengthened is vṛddha. To any stem in which the first of the vowels (ac) has a strengthened letter (born yesterday, or come yesterday, or yesterday's), the designation "named vṛddha" is given. Its purpose is for rules such as "cha from vṛddha."

bṛddhaccaḥ: cha from vṛddha. From what was termed above "named vṛddha," cha applies in the remainder. In the sense of gārgyejataḥ: gārgīyaḥ, the son of Gārga, or born from the son of Garga. āgasteyaḥ. cha becoming īya: śālīyaḥ.

tyadādīnica: also tyad and the rest. From tyad and the rest too, cha applies in the remainder: tyarīyaṃ. cha, ta (born from the son of Śarga; the son of Garga himself; to gargya, cha, cha becoming īya, the ya deleted, being taken as the ... ā of the line of descent; the son of a partridge, or born from the son of a partridge; born in rab, or come from rab, or rag) dīyaṃ (born from that, or come from that, or that). cha, ya: dī(yaṃ, born from which, or come from which, or which) (born from that, or come from that, or that).

pratyayottarapadayośca: also before an affix and a latter word. The yuṣmasma and asma of yuṣmad and asmad, with the d dropped, become tva and ma respectively, both before a following affix and before another following word: tvadīyaḥ (for yuṣyad and asād); madīnayaḥ (born from me, or mine). Before a latter word: tvatputraḥ, batputraḥ.

bhataṣṭhakchasau: ṭhak and chas from bhabat. From bhabat, ṭhak and chas apply in the remainder (cha becoming īla): bhābatkaḥ. To bhabat, chas.

sitica: also when s goes (born from you, or yours) (accepting tyad and the rest, cha; śrasmaca and asma become bu). When an affix that is s-going, or ya and the rest, follows (your son; my son), the base that gives rise to the affix is given the designation pada. (Born from you, or come from you, or yours.) (To bhabata, ṭhak, the k for strengthening; ṭhak by is, us, uk, t and the rest.) Its purpose is that, by the rule "the final jhal become jaś," the t becomes d.

bhapadīyaḥ.

iñaśca: also from iñ. After a word ending in iñ given in the sense of lineage, aṇ applies in the remainder. In the sense of ṅākṣaubhabaḥ and dākṣaujataḥ: iñ, aṇ: dākṣaḥ, of the family of Dakṣa, born from the family of Dakṣa. kṣatraḥ, born from a royal family, or of the royal family. iñ, aṇ.

gahādi(bbyaśya) (to gaha; for bhabat, wa, chas, sa, ta becoming d; cha becoming īya; born from you, or yours): also from gaha and the rest. From gaha and the rest too, cha applies in the remainder: gahīyaḥ.

janaparayoḥkukaca: also kuka from jana and para. Among gaha and the rest, from jana and para, when the affix cha follows (born in a house, or come from a house, or the house; cha becoming īya), the augment kuka applies: janakīyi, a human being, or born from a human being. parakīyaṃ.

Cited in the commentary: dabasyabā: optionally of deba. From deba, when cha follows, the augment kuka applies optionally: debakīyaṃ, a god, or born from a god; debīyaṃ. (To jana and para, cha, cha becoming īya, the augment kuka, the k having the sense of position, the u for pronunciation; other, or born on the other side, or come from the other side.)

yuṣmaddorānyatarasyāṃkhañca: optionally khañ also from yuṣmad and asmad. From yuṣmad and asmad, khañ applies optionally in the remainder, and by the word "also," aṇ, or else cha, applies as well.

tasminnaṇicayuṣmākāsmākau: before that, and before aṇ, yuṣmāka and asmāka. Before a following khañ and aṇ, yuṣmad and asmad become yuṣmāka and asmāka respectively: yauṣmākīnraḥ; yauṣmākaḥ, aṇ, strengthening; cha becoming īya: yuṣmadīyaḥ; khañ, strengthening, kha becoming īna: āsmākīnaḥ; āsmākaḥ, aṇ, strengthening; asmadiyaḥ, cha becoming īya.

tabakamamakāpekabacane: tabaka and mamaka in the singular. Yuṣma and asmad that occur in the singular only (ñ, strengthening, kha becoming īna; you, or born from you, or come from you; you, or begotten by you, or born from you, or come from you; I, or begotten by me, or come from me; I, or born from me, or come from me) become tabaka and mamaka respectively before a following khañ and aṇ, the affixes with the sense of the remainder: tābakīnaḥ; tābakaḥ, aṇ, strengthening; māyakīnaḥ; māmakuḥ, aṇ, strengthening.

maddyānmaḥ: ma from madhya. From madhya, ma applies in the remainder: madhamaḥ.

ādeśca: also from ādi. From ādi too it applies in the remainder: ādimaḥ.

adhaso'stao (khañ, strengthening, laṣa becoming īna; you yourself, or born from you yourself; khañ, strengthening, īna; I myself, or born from me) paśca: and also deletion of the final of adhas. From adhas, in the remainder (the middle one, or born in the middle, or come from the middle), ma applies, and the final is also deleted (the first, or the beginning, or the excellent): adhamaḥ.

asāṃpratrika: a in the sense of "equal." From madhya, in the sense of "equal," a applies: madhyaḥ.

kālātaṭhañ: ṭhañ from a word for time. To a word expressing time, ṭhañ applies in the remainder: māsikaḥ, ṭhañ, strengthening, ika. ārdhamāsikaḥ, ṭhañ, strengthening, ika. sāmātsarikaḥ, thañ, strengthening, ika.

niśāpradoṣā(bhyāṃ)ca (the bad, or born from the bad, or tham): also from niśā and pradoṣa. From niśā and pradoṣa (to ma(ṇḍya), a; by "of ya, also before i," the a is deleted), ṭhañ applies in the remainder (a month, or born from a month; half a month, or come from half a month; a year, or born from a year; the middle, equal, or alike, or similar): naiśikāṃ, ṭhañ, strengthening, ṭha becoming ika; prādoṣikaṃ, ṭhañ, strengthening, ika.

śvasashuctṭa: also tuṭ from śvas. From śvas, ṭhañ applies in the remainder, and the augment tuṭ is also given: to śvas, ṭhañ, tuṭ; the augment ic by (dhā) and the rest; ṭha becoming īka: śaubastikaṃ (wind, or born from wind; night, or born from night, or come from night; evening, or the first part of night, or born from evening, or come from evening).

dvārādīnāṃca: also of dvāra and the rest. When an affix that is the cause of strengthening follows dvāra and the rest, the first vowel of those stems is not strengthened, and the augment aic is given. dvāra and the rest are: dvāra, svara, byalkaśa, śvasti, svadu, mṛdu, śvasu, śvata and spya.

sarbatrāṇacataloparśca: always aṇ, and also deletion of t. From hemanta, aṇ always applies in the remainder, and the t is also deleted: haimanaḥ. Since the commentary says "optionally ṭhañ": haimantikaḥ.

sāyaṃcirambrāhṇeprage'byaye(bhyo)ṣyuḍyulautuṭca: ṣyuṭ and yul from sāyaṃ, coraṃ, prāhṇe, prage and the indeclinables, and also tuṭ. Apart from the aṇ that has the sense of the remainder, it is not the case that wherever aṇ arises the t is to be removed. (Winter, or born in winter; for tamarda; aṇ, strengthening, the t deleted.) (For hemanta, ñ, strengthening, tha becoming ika, su; winter, or born in winter.) To sāyaṃ, ciraṃ, bra(hṇe) and prage, and to the indeclinable stems, when time is expressed, ṣyuṭ and yul apply, and also the augment tuṭ. In the sense of sāyaṃkāla, the evening time: sāyaṃtanaṃ, the evening time. ciraṃtanaṃ. Likewise: brāhṇetanaṃ, pragetanaṃ. The final m and the e of these are established as particles. For an indeclinable: doṣātanaṃ, mṛṣātanaṃ, the constant time; hyastanaṃ, (ṣmuṭ) or yul, tuṭ. In the commentary (for sāyaṃ, ṣmuṭ, ... ṭi, ḍha and the rest, having the binding of ṣa going, yuthalana, rṇbaṭ) optionally yul (a long time, or a long while; the time of the first part of the day; ṣbuṭ or yul, ñaḍ; the early time) is cited.

ciratparutparāribhyaḥtnaḥ: tna from cirat, parut and parāri (phpṣaṭ or phul, tuṭ; the time of night; ṣbuṭ or yul, tuṭ; the time of the day before yesterday). To these, cirat and the rest, when time is expressed, tna applies: a long time: ciratnaṃ (for cira and parut, tna, like jhana, jhar; of these, the ... deleted; sangpanutnaṃ); the year before last, parāritī.

Again cited in the commentary: bragsyagalobaśca: also deletion of the g of praga. From praga, when time is expressed, tna applies, and the g is also deleted: pratnaṃ, the early time.

abrapaścādiman: iman from agra and paścāt. From agra and paścāt, iman applies in the remainder: agrima (iman, the n for the vowel); paścimaṃ (for baśūta, awa, man, the n for the vowel; by bati, ṣa and the rest the ṭi is deleted).

antācca: also from anta. From anta too, in the remainder (bragbatna deleted, su, am), iman applies: antimaṃ, iman, the n for the vowel.

tasyabikāraḥ: for its modification.

(The tip, or born at the tip, or come from the root; the last, or the west, or born in the west, or come from the west.) In the sense of its modification, aṇ and the rest apply after the sixth-case ending. In the sense of subarṇasyabikāro'sau (the end, or born at the end, or come from the end): saubarṇa (this modification of gold; a modification of gold; aṇ, ṇa, strengthening).

abayabacaprā(nyyoṣa)dhibṛkṣebhyaḥ: from living beings, medicinal plants and trees, for a part. From living beings, medicinal plants and trees, when a part is to be expressed, aṇ and the rest apply after the sixth-case ending. In the sense of kapotasyābayabaḥ: kāpotraṃ (the part of a pigeon); aṇ: kārīri; baurbakāṇḍaṃ.

mayaḍaitayobhāṣayamakṣācchādanayoḥ: mayaṭ optionally in the speech, but not for food and clothing. For the modification and the part just explained, which are not in the sense of food and clothing (aṇ, ṇa, strengthening; the part of a pigeon; the part of a sprout; the branch of ...), mayaṭ applies optionally: dūrbamayaṃ. Or else, aṇ: daurba. It does not apply for food and clothing: aṇ: mau(dlaḥ); aṇ: rgāsaṃ.

nityaṃbraṃddhaśarādibhyaḥ: always from the vṛddha and from śara and the rest. From those given the designation "named vṛddha" above, and from śara and the rest (to dūrba, mayaṭ, the sense of ṭa, ṭi, ḍha and the rest; arising from dūrba; arising from pulses and mingka; arising from silk-cotton), mayaṭ always applies for a modification and a part. mayaṭ: āmramayaṃ. mayaṭ: aramayaṃ. mayaṭ: (dantamayaṃ).

Cited in the commentary: ekācoñbimayaṭ: mayaṭ also from what has one vowel. From stems that have one vowel (ac), mayaṭ applies in the sense of a modification and a part: lbādmayaṃ, a modification of speech (arising from the mango; a modification or part of an arrow; a branch of the kunśa; (cinmayaṃ), a modification or part of knowledge).

(tattha)kraṃtibacanemayaṭ: mayaṭ when its own nature is expressed. When its own nature is expressed, mayaṭ applies after the ending of the first case. mayaṭ: dā (to speech and cita, mayaṭ; the sense of ṭa, ṭi, ḍha and the rest) namayaṃ. mayaṭ: śīlamiyaṃ.

Cited in the commentary (again, after that, for one having a nose, one having a nose optionally fitting, and tara, and na): padhānyañapi: also optionally for what is principal. When what is principal is expressed, mayaṭ also applies. mayaṭ: dharmamayaḥ.

goścapurīṣe: from go for dung. When the dung of a cow (having giving as its nature, or arising from ...) is to be expressed, mayaṭ applies. mayaṭ: gomayaṃ.

gobayaṃsoyat: yat from go and bayas. From go and bayas, yat applies for a modification: ga (the principal of the series) byaṃ. yat: payasyaṃ.

paleluka: elision for the fruit. When the sense of a fruit is expressed, the affixes of modification are elided.

lukataddhita (one of the cattle): luka, elision from the elision of the taddhita. When the taddhita affix is elided in a word expressing the sense of fruit, the affixes expressing the feminine are also elided (to go, yat, a following wa as its ending; a cow; milk soup). In the sense of padārlāphalaṃ: mayaṭ: badarñimayaṃ. The mayaṭ is elided by the sūtra. By this sūtra the dipa is elided: badaraṃ. Likewise: āmalakaṃ, the fruit of the bhūrura.

itagonaṇṇaḥ: the it of gonā. From the word goṇī, the taddhita affixes are elided, and the final also becomes it. badāreni, the fruit (the fruit or part of the badare). In "pañcabhiḥgoṇībhiḥkrvṛta," "if it is traded by five" (the fruit or part of the bada): in āmalakīlamyam, it is by mayaṭ and dwap. (If it is traded by five) (pañma)goṇiḥ (taṇmyi, the final it, su).

blakṣādibhyoñna: aṇ from bākṣa and the rest. From pākṣa and the rest, when a fruit is expressed, aṇ applies, and it is not elided. In the sense of bākṣasyapalaṃ: aṇ: plākṣaṃ. Likewise: āśvāttha.

oarañ: añ from u. From a stem ending in the letter u, long or short, añ applies for a modification, and when a fruit is expressed it is elided. In the sense of jambrāphalaṃ: jambauḥ.

jambbāḥbā: optionally from jambu. From jambū (the fruit of the bakṣa; the fruit of the pākṣa; the fruit of the rtagna; aṇ, su, a, ma), aṇ applies for the fruit: the fruit of the jambū, jāmbabaṃ.

lubca: also elision. The aṇ given to jambū in the sense of fruit is optionally elided: the fruit of the jambu, the an being deleted. The fruit of the jambu: jāmbabaṃ; jambūḥ.

harītakyādibhyaśca: also of harītakī and the rest. From harītakī and the rest (from jambu, aṇ, strengthening, the guṇa of u, the aya of the vowel, su), the affixes in the sense of fruit are elided, and the affix expressing the feminine is not elided. In the sense of harītakyāḥphalaṃ (the fruit of the jambū, the aṇ deleted): hārītakī, the aṇ being deleted. drākṣā.

tatraniyukhaḥ: for one appointed there. In the sense of one appointed there, ṭhak applies after the seventh-case ending. In the sense of dvareniyuktaḥ: daubārikaḥ, a doorkeeper. kāruṇikaḥ (the fruit of the arura). śaulkaśalikaḥ (the fruit of the arura; grapes). Since the commentary explains that ṭhak also applies in the sense of what is said, in the sense of svastityahaḥ: saubastikaḥ, one who says "it has turned out well" (one appointed to the door; to drāra, ṭhak, the augment aic of drāra and the rest, ṭha becoming ika; ṭhak, strengthening, ṭha becoming ika; compassionate; customs wool).

nyagrodhasyacakelasya: also of nyagrodha, only for one alone.

Of nyagrodha also: "alone" means with no other word as its companion. "One who says 'it has turned out well.'" When it stands alone, before a taddhita suffix that is the cause of vṛddhi, the augment aic is added without splitting the vṛddhi of what follows (gloss: for svasti, ṭhak; the i of dvāra and the rest; the augment aic; ṭha becoming ika; the suffix causing vṛddhi). In the sense of nyagrodhaphalaṃ, "the fruit of the nyagrodha": to nyagrodha, aṇ and the augment aic: neyagrodhaṃ. If it is not a single word alone, aic is not given: nyagrodhalebhaplaḥ, in the sense of "the root of the nyagrodha"; aṇ is elided: nyagrodhambūlaṃ.

svāgatādīnāṃ ca: also of svāgata and the rest. For āgata and the rest, the augment aic does not occur on a preceding sva either: svāgatekaḥ, svādhvarikaḥ, svādgiḥ, "son of one's own body," byāḍiḥ, "merchant," byebahārikaḥ.

Cited in the commentary (gloss: the root of the nyagrodha): pathyatithibasatisvapateḍhña. For pathi, atithi, vasati and svapati, ḍhañ. To these, pathi and the rest, ḍhañ occurs in the sense of the thing that is proper to it (gloss: vṛddhi of ṭhak by "remainder" and the rest; ṭha becoming ika; a dyer of colour; for ata, iñ, vṛddhi of iñ, son of one who strives; by "remainder" and the rest, vṛddhi of ṭhak, and aika): bābreyaḥ, ātitheyaḥ, bāteyaḥ, svāpateyaḥ.

śvāderiñi. śvāderiñi: of śvan and the rest, before iñ. Before iñ, aic does not occur for śvan and the rest: in the sense of śvabhastasyāpatyaṃ (gloss: aṇ, and iñ by preference, eñ): śrābastiḥ. (Gloss: śvagaṇāṭ ṭhañ ca; śvagaṇa, path, monk; ḍhañ, vṛddhi in the sense of going, ḍha becoming eya, lying.) From that, ṭhañ also: from śvagaṇa, in the sense of moving about, ṭhañ occurs, and by "also" ṭhan as well. In the sense of śvagaṇicarati (gloss: son of one wearing what clothes?): śvāgaṇikaḥ and śvagaṇikaḥ (gloss: son of one wearing Chinese clothes).

padāntasyāharasyāṃ: optionally, for one at the end of a word. Before a taddhita suffix that is the cause of vṛddhi, for śvan and the rest at the end of a word, the augment aic optionally occurs: in the sense of śvabadasya idaṃ (gloss: the moving of a mass of water): śaubapadaṃ (gloss: elided, ṭha becoming ika; a flock of birds moving; ṭha, vowel sense, ṭha becoming ika), or śvabapada. Since the commentary explains that nyaṅku also optionally takes aic: ṇaiyadgabaṃ (gloss: this one, marked by a limb), or nyādkabaṃ.

su sarbārdhāta janabadasya: after su, sarva and ardha (gloss: "this foot of a dog"), aṇ, the augment aic and vṛddhi are optionally to be done. From this "foot of a dog," aṇ, the augment aic and vṛddhi are optionally to be done. "This foot of a dog": of a country. After su, sarva and ardha, the former members, when a country is expressed, aṇ, aic and vṛddhi are optional; with guṇa of u, aṇ occurs and only the latter member takes vṛddhi: (gloss: the good country of the Pañcālas) supāñṭralaḥ (gloss: aṇ, vṛddhi of the latter member, su); sarbapāñcalaḥ, the whole country of the Pañcālas; ardhapāñcālaḥ.

saṃyogādiśca: also a conjunct and the rest. A conjunct means a stem whose penultimate has two or more letters stacked; when aṇ or in follows it, one does not elide the ṭi and the rest: cākriṇaḥ, "son of one with a wheel"; yājvanaḥ (gloss: half the country of the Pañcālas; aṇ, vṛddhi of the latter member, su).

na mapūrbo 'tyeñatyeñabarmaṇaḥ: not for one preceded by ma, other than varman, in the sense of offspring. When the letter ma comes before, other than in varman, and offspring is expressed, it is not that the ṭi is left; it is simply elided (gloss: for cakrin and yajvan, aṇ, vṛddhi, the ṭi not elided; son of one who offers sacrifice). sausāmaṃḥ, son of Fine Poetry; bhadraśramaḥ, son of Fine Virtue. By saying "other than varman," for varman, which is excluded: bhādrabarmaṇaḥ.

Cited in the commentary: karmātaśīle. For karman, in the senses of action and of habit. When action and habit are expressed, aṇ occurs for karman and the ṭi is elided: kārmaḥ (gloss: for susāman and bhadraśāman, an, vṛddhi, the ṭi removed).

aukṣamanapatye: aukṣaṃ, where it is not offspring. For ukṣan (gloss: aṇ, vṛddhi, the ṭi not elided; son of Fine Armor), the form aukṣaṃ, made by adding aṇ, is an irregular particle-word expressing the ox itself, not offspring.

ṣabdurbahandhritarājñāmaṇi (gloss: the manner of karma; aṇ and vṛddhi for kacchan): for those preceded by ṣa, and for han and dhṛtarājan, before aṇ. When the letter ṣa comes before, and for han and dhṛtarājan, the vowel of the penultimate is elided before aṇ: ox, aukṣaḥ; son of the Destroyer of the asuras (Vṛtrahan), bārtabhnaḥ; son of the Holding King (Dhṛtarājan), dhārtarājñaḥ.

prāgvahataṭhaka: ṭhak, before "conveys." Before the "conveys" of the rule "for ratha, yuga and prāsaṅga, that which conveys it," in every sense for which there is no special exception, ṭhak becomes the suffix. (Gloss: son of an ox; for ukṣan, aṇ, vṛddhi, the penultimate a elided; for vṛtrahan, aṇ, vṛddhi, the penultimate removed, the ha of han becoming bha; for dhṛtarājan, aṇ, vṛddhi, the penultimate removed, and by the rule on s and t, ra, ña and ja combine as jña.) This is the general rule.

tendīkhanatijatijitaṃ: in the senses "by it one plays, digs, conquers, has conquered." In these senses, played and the rest, ṭhak occurs after the third-case ending. In the sense of akṣaiḥ dībyatṛ, "one plays with dice" (gloss: ak, vṛddhi, eye): ākṣikaḥ, "one plays with dice." In the sense of kudālenkhanati: kaudālikaḥ. In the sense of śastenajayati: śvastikṣaḥ. In the sense of śastrīṇajaṃtaṃ: śāstrikaḥ.

Cited in the commentary: bhābapratyayāṃnirbraṃtte iman. After what ends in a suffix of abstract sense, in the sense of "completed," iman (gloss: of kṛt and the rest; one recites and digs; dug with a hoe; the suffix proper; for kudāla, ṭhak, vṛddhi, ṭha becoming eka; conquered with a weapon, conquered with a weapon; for śastra, ṭhak, vṛddhi, ṭha becoming eka; subdued with a weapon; for śastra, ṭhak and ka, vṛddhi, ṭha becoming ika). After an ending that has an abstract sense, in the sense of "completed," iman occurs: in the sense of pākenanirbraṃtaḥ: pākimaḥ, "finished by cooking."

bakṣimatsyamṛpākahanti: in the sense "kills birds, fish and wild animals."

For "kills," said of the kinds of birds, the kinds of fish and the kinds of wild animals, ṭhak occurs after the second-case ending: in the sense of bakṣiṇihanti: bākṣi (gloss: finished cooking) kaḥ. (Gloss: paca; in the sense of the thing, bhañ, pāka; to that iman; the vowel sense.) Likewise, killing birds: śākunikaḥ; taittirikaḥ. Killing wild animals: mārgikaḥ; hāriṇikaḥ. (Gloss: śāradgikaḥ, ṭhak to śāradga; mātsyikaḥpa, killing fish; ṭhak to mina; mainikaḥ, killing birds; to dakṣin, ṭhak and vṛddhi, and also on account of the taddhita the ṭi removed, tha becoming ika.) Killing birds.

sasakṛtaṃ: in the sense "properly made." Properly. To kuni, thak. Killing partridges. (Gloss: to tittira, ṭhak and vṛddhi; to mṛga, ṭhak, killing deer; to hariṇa, ṭhak; killing; to mārga, ṭhak, vṛddhi, ṭha becoming eka; formed by sūrya, tiṣya and the rest.) Killing great fish. In the sense "it is made," ṭhak occurs after the third-case ending: ṭhak, dādhikaṃ.

śabdadarduraṃkaroti: for "makes" a sound or a dardura. For "makes," said of a sound or a dardura, ṭhak occurs after the second-case ending: in the sense of śabdaṃ karoti: ṭhak, śābdikaḥ. Likewise ṭhak, dārdurikaḥ, dārdurikaḥ.

dharmaṃcarati: for "practices the Dharma." For "practices the Dharma" (gloss: curd is mixed), ṭhak occurs after the second-case ending: in the sense of dharmaṃcarati, "acts in accord with the Dharma": ṭhak, dhārmikaḥ, one who practices the Dharma. In the commentary: "makes a sound." Cited there: adharmācca. "Makes a sound." From adharma also (gloss: makes a frog). From adharma also, for "practices," ṭhak occurs after the second-case ending: adharmaṃkaḥ.

astiṇāstaṃdiṣṭaṃmati: for asti, nāsti and diṣṭa, in the sense of a view. For asti, nāsti and diṣṭa, when a view is expressed, ṭhak occurs after the first-case ending: also āstikaḥ, nāstikaḥ, daiṣṭikaḥ.

pragtitābyata: yat, before "beneficial." By "beneficial for that" (gloss: practicing a Dharma that is divine), in whatever senses come before "beneficial," where there is no special exception of suffix, yat occurs: this is the general rule.

tadvahatirathayugaprāsogaṃ (gloss: without ratha and yuga; the Teacher): for "conveys that," said of ratha, yuga and prāsaṅga. For these, ratha and the rest, in "conveys that," yat occurs after the second-case ending: in the sense of rathaṃvahati: yat, rathyaḥ, drawing a chariot. Likewise yat, yugyaḥ, drawing the yoke; yat, brāsogyaḥ, drawn by six oxen.

dhuroyatḍhakau: from dhur, yat and ḍhak. From dhur, in "conveys that," yat and ḍhak occur: yat, dhuryaḥ; dhaurayaḥ (gloss: ḍhak, vṛddhi, ḍha becoming eya).

halica: also before hal. When the penultimate ik of a stem with a vowelless letter ra or va has a letter combined with it separately, it becomes long before a hal.

nabhakurchurāṃ: not of bha, kur and chur. (Gloss: those named bha, and the two wheels of a chariot drawing the plough here.) For kur and chur, the letters in which the penultimate ik is combined separately do not become long before a hal.

khaḥsarbadhurāta: kha from satradhura. From dhura preceded by sarva, in "conveys that," kha occurs: sarbadhurīṇaḥ.

ekadhurālkuka bā: from ekadhura, optionally elision. From ekadhura, kha is also optionally elided: ekabhuraḥ, ekadhurīṇaḥ.

śakaṭādaṇ: from śakata, aṇ. From śakaṭa, in "conveys that," aṇ occurs: śākaṭaḥ.

halasāṃrātaṭhak (gloss: drawing every plough; kha of kha ripened): from hala and sera, ṭhak. From hala and sīra, in "conveys that," ṭhak occurs. Kha removed; drawing a single plough (gloss: kha a es; ṭhak, hālikaḥ). Drawing a plough (gloss: from skera, ṭhak, vṛddhi, ṭha becoming eka): sairikaḥ, drawing a plough. Tatra (gloss: ṭhak) vṛddhi; drawing a chariot.

sātyuḥ: in "good at that." In "good at that," yat occurs after the seventh-case ending: in the sense of sāmasusādhuḥ: sāmanyaṃ, sāmanyaṃ. Likewise karmaḍyaḥ: yat to karman.

sabhāyāya: from sabhā, ya. For sabhā, in "good at that," ya occurs: sabhyaḥ, good in the assembly hall or meeting hall.

samānatīrbebāmi: for "dwelling" in samānatīrtha. From samānatīrtha. (Gloss: good at poetic phrases; the seventh-case sup; good at poetic phrases; sāmanbataya; good at action, or fit for action.) In "dwelling there," ya occurs after the seventh-case ending: in the sense of samānatīrthebāsi (gloss: sabhālayaḥ): satīrthyaḥ.

samānodareśayitaḥ: for "lying" in samāna udara. In the sense of lying in the same womb, ya occurs: in the sense of samānodareśayite: samānodaryaḥ.

sodarādyaḥ: from sodara (gloss: dwelling alike in a place of study; ya to samānatīrtha, the sa of samāna becoming sa; dwelling alike in a place of study), ya. Because samāna becomes sa, from sodara also, in the sense of "lying," ya occurs. (Gloss: ya, sodaryaḥ; lying in the same womb; lying in the same womb, that is, a full brother.)

agrādyata: from agra, yat. From agra, when being is expressed, yat occurs: in the sense of agrebhabaḥ: yat, agryaḥ.

ghachauca: also gha and cha. From agra, when being is expressed, gha and cha (gloss: lying in the same womb) also occur: agriyaḥ, agrīyaḥ.

tasmohitaṃ: for "beneficial for its sake." In the sense "beneficial for its sake," cha (gloss: the tip itself) occurs after the fourth-case ending: in the sense of sburyāyahitaṃ (gloss: tip): sūrīyaḥ.

śarīrāpayabādyata: yat for a part of the body. In the sense "beneficial for a part of the body" (gloss: gha becoming iya; the tip itself; cha becoming īya), yat occurs after the fourth-case ending: in the sense of dantāyahitaṃ: yat, dantyaṃ. Likewise yat, oṣṭhyaṃ (gloss: beneficial for the sake of the sun). Yat, nābyaṃ, beneficial for the śima. (Gloss: to sgurya, cha, cha becoming sīya; formed by sūrya, tiṣya and the rest.)

ādmanbiśvajanbhogottarabadātkhaḥ: kha from what has bhoga as its final member, and from ātman and viśvajana. For any stem that has bhoga as its final member (gloss: beneficial for the sake of the teeth; beneficial for the teeth), and for ātman, viśvajana (gloss: beneficial for the lips; beneficial for the navel), in the sense "beneficial," kha occurs after the fourth-case ending. (Gloss: mātṛbhogthinasaḥ; pitṛbhogīṇaḥ; kha, kha becoming ïna; banhubhogṣinaḥ; biśvajaniñaḥ; kha becoming īna; to ātman, kha.)

ādmādhānaikhe: for ātman and adhvan before kha. For ātman and adhvan, the ṭi is not elided before kha: ātmanīnaḥ.

tenakrītaṃ: for "bought with that."

(Gloss: beneficial for the mother's wealth; kha, kha becoming īna; beneficial for the father's wealth; beneficial for the wealth of kinsmen; beneficial for all kinds of people.) In the sense "bought with that," ṭhak occurs after the third-case ending: in the sense of sabtatyāgritaḥ: sābhatikaḥ. (Gloss: to ātman, kha, kha becoming īn, the ṭi not elided; beneficial for oneself.)

sakhyāyāyatiśadantāyāḥkan: kan, from a numeral that does not end in ti or śat. From a numeral that does not end in ti, as in saptati and catvāriṃśat, or in śat, in the senses "bought" and the rest (gloss: bought with seventy; to abtat, ṭhak, vṛddhi, ṭha becoming ika; bought with seventy), kan occurs: in the sense of bañcabhiḥ krītaḥ: bañcakaḥ, bought with five, or fivefold. For those ending in ti and śat: āśītikaḥ; cātvāriṃśatkaḥ, bought with forty, or fortyfold.

batoriḍā: optionally iṭ for vatu. From what ends in the suffix vatu also, kan arises in the senses "bought" and the rest, and optionally iṭ (gloss: bought with five; to bañcan, kan, the final n of the noun removed): tābatikaḥ, so much; tābatgaḥ. (Gloss: to aśīti, by "bought with that," ṭhak, vṛddhi, ṭha becoming ika; bought for eighty, or eightyfold; to catvāriṃśat, by "bought with that," ṭhak and ka, vṛddhi, ṭhak by the sūtra on is, us and the rest.)

biṃśatriṃśadśḍyvaṭṣunasaṃrdñāyāṃ: ḍvun from viṃśati and triṃśat when it is not a name. (Gloss: to ñat, vatu, tāvat, kan and ik; sarva and the rest, ā; to tāvat, kan; that much.) From viṃśati and triṃśat, when it is not a name, ḍvun occurs in the senses "bought" and the rest: biṃśakaḥ, twentyfold; triṅśakaḥ.

śatāccaṭhanyatābaśate: from śata also, ṭhan and yat, but not for śata. From a śata that expresses only the sense "bought," and not another hundred, ṭhan and yat also occur (gloss: for viṃśati, in "bought," ḍvun, the ḍa as indicator; the ti of viṃśa, which is to be elided, removed; ḍa, its sense; the a of whatever ka removed, and also of iñ; thirtyfold; to triṃśat, ḍvun with ḍa as indicator, the ṭi removed, vu becoming aka): in the sense of śatenakrṝtaḥ (gloss: bought with a hundred): yat, śatyaḥ; than, śatikaḥ. If the sense is not "bought," they do not occur: in the sense of śataṃbarimāṇaṃ: śatakaḥ.

tasyeṃśvaraḥ: in the sense "lord of that." From sarvabhūmi and pṛthivī, in the sense of lordship, aṇ and an occur after the sixth-case ending: in the sense of sarvabhumerīśvaraḥ: svarba (gloss: lying with a hundred) bhūmaḥ. Likewise bārthibaḥ (gloss: lord of the whole; aṇ or añ; lord of the whole earth; lord of the earth's kinds; to pṛthivī, aṇ or añ, vṛddhi).

tenatulyaṃ (gloss: broken by a hundred) kṛyācedvati: in the sense "to be made equal by that" (gloss: kan, vowel sense), vati. In the sense of being made equal by that, as in "that is like that," vati occurs: in the sense of brāhmaṇetulyaṃ: sahmaṇabata. Likewise kṣatriyabat.

tatratasyeba: in the sense "like that, in that." In the sense of "like," "as" or "in the manner of," vati occurs after the sixth- and seventh-case endings (gloss: equal to a brahmin): in the sense of debasyaiba, debaiba: vati, debabat. Likewise, equal to or like a brahmin (gloss: vati, the sense of saying iva); equal to, like or the same as a kṣatriya: vati, barbatabat; vati, rājabat (gloss: like a mountain; like a king of things).

tadartaṃ: in the sense "worthy of that." In the sense "worthy of that," ti occurs after the second-case ending: in the sense of tebidhiṃardhaḥ: bidhibata (gloss: like a god, or as a god; worthy of the offering to the assembly).

tasyabhābastvatalau: tva and tal, in the sense of its state. In the sense of its nature or state, tva and tal occur after the sixth-case ending; when tva is given the word is neuter, and when tal is given it is of feminine gender. (Gloss: the offering to the assembly, by me; sādhoḥ chṣaba; the offering to the assembly; the vati, the sense of saying iva.) In the sense: sādhusutāṃ, goodness itself; sādhudhā.

hasvātḍādautaddhīte: after a short vowel, before a taddhita beginning with t and the rest. Where the penultimate of a stem is a short vowel, the s that follows it, when a taddhita suffix such as ta, te or tva is given, becomes ṣ: goodness itself; jayuṣṭaṃ (gloss: for jayus, tā, "the short"; or s becoming ṣ, and by the ṣṭu rule t becoming ṭ, su becoming am); goodness itself (gloss: tva, su, for a neuter su becoming am; for tal, the vowel sense, ṭāp by aja and the rest). By saying "short," a long one is excluded and does not become ṣ: ṅagnid gīstāṃ (gloss: for gīr, tva; ra, the visarga); the s of visarga.

prithvadibhyaimanijḍā: optionally iman and ic from pṛthu and the rest. From pṛthu and the rest, in the sense of the state, not only do tva and tal occur, but iman and ic also optionally occur.

ṭiḥ: of the ṭi. The ṭi of pṛthu and the rest is elided before iman, ic and iyas.

ṛtoḥhalāderlaghoḥ: of a light ṛ with an initial consonant. A light ṛ that has a consonant at the beginning becomes ra before the suffixes iman, ic and eyas: prathimā, prathiḥ (gloss: tva, pṛthutvatvaṃ; the supreme; for tal, pṛthutā). By saying "with an initial consonant," where there is no initial consonant, even though the ṛ is short it does not become ra: rajimā. By saying "light," it is excluded (gloss: for prathu, iman, the ṭi elided, ṭe removed; by "with an initial consonant," ra: prathiman, su, the penultimate n lengthened, the final n of the noun removed, and by hal and the rest the su elided; breadth itself). Breadth. (Gloss: to thathu, ic, ca, vowel sense.) A heavy one does not become ra: iman, kṛṣṇaṃ ṭṣa. Pṛthu and the rest are: phṛthu, mṛdu, ṛju, softness or ease (gloss: to riju, iman), dṛḍha, bhraṃśa, kṛśa, bṛḍha and kṛṣṇa.

barṇadṛḍhādibhyaḥṣyañca: from colors and from dṛḍha and the rest, ṣyañ also. When a particular color is expressed, and for dṛḍha and the rest, ṣyañ occurs in the sense of the state (gloss: sickness itself; breadth; softness or ease; iman also): śauklyaṃ, whiteness; steadfast; very; sickness; growth; black; śukrimā (gloss: ṣyak, dābḍhyaṃ, draḍḍhimā; ṣya, hla, bāṇḍyaṃ); labaṇimā.

guṇabacanbrābmaṇādibhyaḥkarmaṇica: from words expressing qualities and from brāhmaṇa and the rest, in the sense of an action also. From words expressing qualities and from brāhmaṇa and the rest (gloss: ṣañ, ña, the sense of vṛddhi; for ṣita, the sense of dīpa; iyan; whiteness; steadfastness; iman; ja itself; iman; ba itself), ṣyañ occurs both in the sense of the state and in the sense of the action: in the sense of jaḍasyabhaba and jaḍasyakarma: ṣyañ, jāḍyaṃ. Likewise ṣyañ, brāhlaṭyaṃ (gloss: the state of being a brahmin, or a brahmin's action). Ṣyañ, caurmaṃ: thievery and the act of a thief (gloss: the root).

Cited in the commentary: caturbarṇāīnīsvārtheṣyañ. For catuvarṇa and the rest, ṣyañ in their own sense.

For caturvarṇa and the rest, in their own sense, ṣyañ occurs (gloss: foolishness itself; the act of a fool; foolishness itself, or the act of a fool): ṣyañ, cāturbaṇyi; ṣyañ, cāturbaṇyi; ṣyañ, cāturāśrāmaṃ (gloss: ṣañ, tilokyi). In the commentary it is explained that from caturveda also ṣyañ occurs in its own sense, and that vṛddhi applies to both the former and the latter members: ṣyañ, cāturbaidyaṃ (gloss: the four classes; the four freedoms; the three worlds).

stenādyanlopaśu: from sten, yat, and also elision of sten. From stena, in the sense of the state and of the action, not only does ṣyañ occur but yat also, and before yat the na is also elided: stainyaṃ, steyaṃ.

sakhyurbaḥ: ya from sakhi. For sakhi, in the sense of the state (gloss: the four Vedas) and of the action, ya occurs: sakhyaṃ.

dūtapaṇigbhyaṃca: also from dūta and paṇija. From dūta and paṇija also it occurs in the sense of the state and of the action: dūtyaṃ (gloss: thievery itself, or the act of a thief; to sten, ṣyañ; to stena, la; ta; the it of whatever, and also by the sūtra of the vowel a of na, na removed); praṇijyaṃ (gloss: friendship itself, or the act of a friend; to sakhi, ya).

kapijvādoḍhaṃk: ḍhak from kapi and jñāti. From kapi and jñāti, in the sense of the state and of the action, ḍhak occurs: ḍhak, kāpeyaṃ; ḍhak, jñāteyaṃ (gloss: the state of a messenger or a messenger's action; monkeyhood or a monkey's action; kinship itself or the act of a kinsman).

patyantapurohitādibhyolak: from what ends in pati, and from purohita and the rest, yak. From a word that has pati as its final member, and from purohita and the rest, in the sense of the state and of the action, yak occurs (gloss: the state of a merchant, or as a merchant): sanāpadyaṃ (gloss: the state of a commander or a commander's act; to senāpati, yak); baurohityaṃ (gloss: the state of a king's chaplain, or his act; to purohita, yak); rārajyaṃ, kingship itself, or the king, or the act of a king (gloss: to rājan, yak, and also on account of the taddhita the ṭi removed).

prāṇajātibayobacanodgātrādibhyoñaña: from words for kinds of living beings, words expressing age, and udgātṛ and the rest, añ. From words for kinds of living beings, words expressing age, and udvātra and the rest, in the sense of the state and of the action, añ occurs: aṇ, āśvaṃ, horseness; to kumāra, aṇ, kombaraṃ, youth (gloss: the state of being well trained); odgātraṃ (gloss: to urṇāṇra, aṇ); to hotṛ, aṇ (gloss: for ik, ab la, yan): hautraṃ, the office of fire offering.

hālanāntayupādhyoñaṇ: from what ends in hāyana, and from yuva and the rest, añ. From what has hāyana as its final member, and from yuva and the rest, in the sense of the state and of the action, an occurs: aṇ, dvehāyanaṃ (gloss: two years old); aṇ, yaubanaṃ; śaubanaṃ (gloss: the state of a dog); sotārdaṃ (gloss: the state of a ...; or the state of ...).

iganhraccalaglupūrbāta: also from what ends in ik, preceded by a light syllable. Even where the preceding letter of the stem is light and the following final is ik, a letter combined separately, aṇ occurs in the sense of the state and of the action (gloss: the state of a sage; the state of a guru; to zhuru, aṇ, vṛddhi, guṇa of u; to lagha, aṇ; and again, the state of Dharma; śat, an; aic by hūr and the rest; to satrada, aṇ, by the sūtra on sudraṃ bhaga and the rest, vṛddhi in both the former and latter members): maunai; munai aṇ; gaurapaṃ; lightness itself, lāghabaṃ. By saying "light," a heavy one is excluded: kāṇḍātvaṃ.

yopadhdhadhurūpothamādvuñ: from what has ya as penultimate and a heavy syllable next before it, vuñ. From any stem whose penultimate is the letter ya and whose letter nearest before that is heavy, in the sense of the state and of the action, vuña occurs: rāmaṇīyaka, beauty itself (gloss: the state of being one who is to be delighted; to ramaṇīya, vuña, ña for the sake of vṛddhi, ak).

Cited in the commentary: sahāyādvā: optionally from sahāya. Even when the conditions of the preceding sūtra are all met, from sahāya, in the sense of the state and of the action, vuña is optional: vuñ, sāhāyaka; sāhāyyaṃ.

dhānyānāṃbhaṅanikṣetekhañ: for grains, khañ in the sense of a field where they grow. For words denoting grains, when a field where they grow is expressed, khaña occurs: in the sense of mudgānāṃbhabanekṣetre (gloss: a field where beans, mudga, grow): maudgīnaḥ (gloss: a mudga field; to mudga, khaña, vṛddhi, iṇ).

phrīhiśālyorḍhak: ḍhak from vrīhi and śāli. From vrīhi and śāli, when a field where they grow is expressed, ḍhak occurs (gloss: to sahāya, khati; ending and du; by the sūtra on hita and the rest, yak, vṛddhi): prehayaṃ (gloss: to hāya, ḍhak; to vrīhi, ḍhak; a rice field); śāleyaṃ.

yabayabakaṣaṣṭhi kādyata: yat from yava, yavaka and ṣaṣṭhika. From yava, yavaka and ṣaṣṭhika, when a field where they grow is expressed, yat occurs: yat, yabyi, a barley field; yat, yaba..., a grain field ...kyiṃ; yat, ṣiṣṭhakyaṃ, a sixty-day field, that is, a field where the grain ripens in sixty days.

pibhāṣātilamaṣomādgāṇābhyaḥ: optionally for tila, māṣa, umā, bhaṅgā and aṇu. From these, tila and the rest, when a field where they grow is expressed, yat optionally occurs: yat, tilyaṃ; khañ, tailīnaṃ; yat, māṣyaṃ; khañ, māṣīnaṃ; yat, umyaṃ; khañ, aumīnaṃ; yat, bhādgyaṃ; yañ, bhādgīnaṃ; aṇabyaṃ; khañ, āṇabīnaṃ (gloss: a sesame field; a bean field; a field of liberation; a flax field; a field of fine grain).

tatsarbādeḥbṛthyagakarmabatrabātraṃbyābnoti: for "pervades it," said of pathi, aṅga, karma, patra and pātra preceded by sarva. For pathi and the rest preceded by sarva, in the sense "pervades it," kha occurs: in the sense of śasa sarbapathānabyabhoti: sarbapathīnaḥ. Likewise kha, sarbacādhīṇaḥ; kha, sarbakarmīṇaḥ; kha, sarbapatrīṇaḥ; kha, sarbapātrīṇaḥ (gloss: pervading every path; kha, kha becoming īna; pervading every path; pervading the whole body; pervading every action; pervading every leaf; pervading every vessel).

adhanoyatau: yat and kha from adhvan. From adhvan, in the sense of traveling swiftly, yat and kha occur (gloss: travels the road swiftly): in the sense of adhvanamaladgacchati: yat, adhānyaḥ; kha, adhānīnaḥ.

tasyapākamūlepīlvādikarṇādibhyaḥkuṇabjāhacau: from pīlu and the rest and from karṇa and the rest, kuṇap and jāhac, for its ripening and its root.

For pīlu and the rest, when their ripening is expressed, kuṇap occurs, and for karṇa (gloss: travels the road swiftly) and the rest, when their root is expressed, jāhac occurs: in the sense of pīlūnāṃpākaḥ: pīlukuṇaḥ. Likewise aśvatthakuṇaḥ (gloss: kuṇap; karkandhukuṇaḥ). In the sense of karṇasyamūlaṃ: karṇajāhaḥ. Likewise (gloss: jāhac, akṣijāhaṃ; jāhac, puṣbajāhaṃ; jāhac, bṛkṣāhaṃ).

tenabittaścucubcaṇapau: for "known by that," cuñcup and caṇap. (Gloss: the ripening of the se'u fruit; to pīlu, kuṇap, the vowel sense; the ripening of the se'u fruit; the particular ripening; kuṇap; ripened large; the root of the ear; the root of the ear; jāhac, the c a vowel sense; the root of the eye; the root of a flower; the root of a tree.) When "known by that" is expressed, cuñcup and caṇap occur after the third-case ending; in this context the ca's are not of the kind named gati. In the sense of śebdenabittaṃ: śabhacuñcurma, one who knows sound; śabhacaṇaḥ.

saṃprodaścakaṭacasvārthe: from saṃ, pra and ut, kaṭac in their own sense. From saṃ, pra and ut, and by the word "also," from vi too, kaṭa occurs in their own sense: kaṭac, saṃkaṭaḥ (gloss: extremely afflicted); kaṭac, prakaṭaṃ, known or understood (gloss: violently moving); kaṭac, baṃkaṭaḥ (gloss: built up high).

Cited in the commentary: alābūtilomābhaṃgābhyorajasikaṭajvācyaḥ: from alābū, tila, umā and bhaṅgā, kaṭac for dust. For these, alābū and the rest, when dust is expressed, kaṭac occurs (gloss: kaṭa, a soma, cut): lābūkaṭaḥ, tilkaṭaḥ, umākaṭaḥ, bhadgākaṭaḥ (gloss: the dust of flax; the dust of sesame; the dust of mustard; the dust of flax).

goṣṭhājādayaḥyṭhānādiṣubaṣunābhyaḥ: for aja and the other names of livestock, goṣṭha in the senses of a station and the rest. From aja and the other names of livestock, in the senses of a station and the rest, goṣṭha occurs after the sixth-case ending: in the sense of gabāṃsthānaṃ: gogoṣṭha. Likewise mahiṣīgoṣṭhaṃ, ajagoṣṭhaṃ.

saṃghaṃtekaṭaca: kaṭac for a gathering. When a gathering is expressed, kaṭac occurs: in the sense of abīnāṃsaṃgṭhātaḥ: abikaṭaḥ.

pisṭhareyaṭaca: yaṭac for spreading. In the sense of the spreading of them, yaṭac occurs (gloss: a station of cattle; a station of buffalo; a station of goats): in the sense of abīnāṃbistāraṃ: apiyaṭaḥ, apiyaṭaḥ (gloss: a flock of sheep; a flock of sheep).

dvidveyugaca: for twoness, goyugac. In the sense of the number two, goyugac occurs: in the sense of uṣṭādvau: aṣṭagogaṃ.

ṣaṭedveṣaṭābaca: for sixness, ṣaḍgavac (gloss: the spread of sheep; the sheep increasing, that is, in the sense of many; yaṭac, the c a root sense). In the sense of the number six, ṣaḍgavac occurs: in the sense of aśvaḥṣaṭ, "horses, six of them": six horses, aśāṣaḍgabaṃ (gloss: female pair, two; two she-camels; two she-camels).

snahatelaca: tailac for oil. In the sense of oil, tailac occurs: in the sense of tilānāṃsnehaṃ: tilatilaṃ. Likewise ghṛtatailaṃ (gloss: the oil of sesame; sesame oil; the oil of butter).

bhabanekṣetreśākaṭaśākinau: śākaṭa and śākin, for a field where it grows. When a field where it grows is expressed, śākaṭa and śākina occur: in the sense of ikṣūnāṃbhabanekṣetre: ikṣaśākaṭaṃ; ikṣuśvakinaṃ (gloss: a field where sugarcane grows; a sugarcane field).

tadsyasaṃjātaṃtārakādibhyaitaca: for "this has had it fully arise," itac from tāraka and the rest. For "this has had it fully arise," itac occurs for tāraka and the rest, ending in the first-case ending and having the sense of the sixth: in the sense of tārakāḥsaṃjātāḥasya: tārakitaṃ, the sky, that is, the one in which stars have fully arisen, starry. Likewise buṣṭhitaṃḥ, a tree, that is, flowering.

pramaṇedvalasjdaghṇañmātracaḥ: for a measure, dvayasac, dghnañ and mātrac. For a measure, ending in the first-case ending and having the sense of the sixth, dvayasac, dghnañ and mātrac occur: in the sense of hastaḥbramāṇaḥasya: hastadvayasaṃ, this much as a cubit. Likewise jānudghṇaṃ, knee-deep; nabhimātraṃ, navel-deep (gloss: dayas, ca, the vowel sense; about a cubit; dghñ, ña, the sense of vṛddhi; mātrac, ca, the vowel sense).

bramāṇelaḥ: elision for a measure. When there is a purpose such as meter, the suffixes given in the sense of a measure are elided.

dvigoḥnaṃtyaṃ: always after a dvigu. At the end of a dvigu compound, the suffixes in the sense of a measure are always elided: dvibisteḥ, tribisti, dvaḍhakī.

buruṣahastibhyāmaṇaca: from puruṣa and hastin, aṇ also. From puruṣa and hastin, for a measure, not only do dvayasac and the rest occur, but aṇ also: aṇ, bauruṣaḥ, as tall as a man; puruṣadvayasaṃ, dayasac; bauruṣa, dghnañ, as tall as a man; mātrac, buruṣamātraḥ, as tall as a man. (Gloss: it is seen; dvayasac removed; three spans; two measures; mātrac removed; dghnaḥ.) For hastin, aṇ.

inaṇyanapatye: in before aṇ, where it is not offspring. Before an aṇ that does not express offspring, the ṭi of a stem ending in in is not elided: aṇ, hāstinaṃ; hastidāyasaṃ; dghnañ, hāstidghāḥ; mātrac, hastamātraḥ (gloss: as large as an elephant; for hastin, dvayasac, the c a vowel sense, the final n of the noun removed; as large as an elephant).

yattadetebhyaḥparolmāṇabatupa: from yat, tat and etat, vatup for a quantity. For these, yat and the rest, vatup occurs for a quantity: lābata; vatup, tābata, that much; vatup, etabate, this much.

kimidaṃbhyaṃboghaḥ: from kim and idam, gha for the v.

From kim and idam, vatup occurs for a quantity (gloss: vatup), and the v of vatup also becomes gh: how much, kiyān; how much. (Gloss on yat: vatup, the vowel sense, the sense of the augment num; the a of those named pronouns is the ṭi, a.) This much: iyān. (Gloss: for idam, vatup; the vowel sense; the sense of u; īś for idam and kim.) By the sūtra "ś goes," the v becomes gh (gloss: iya; the it of which is removed), and so on.

kimaḥsaṃkhyāparimāṇiḍetica: from kim, ḍati also, for a measure of number. (Gloss: for kim, vatup; the vowel sense; īś and kīś for idam and kim, so kim becomes kīś.) The ś goes by the sūtra (gloss: the v of vatup becomes gh; iya; the it of which is removed; by "uk goes," the u of num), and the final of the long reduplicated form, which is to be elided, the t, is removed. From kim, for a measure of number, ḍati also occurs: how many, katiḥ.

kṣepena: not in a word of contempt. Kim expressing contempt does not take the suffixes of measure: kā saṃkhyā eṣāṃ deśānām, "what count are these regions?"

Quoted in the commentary: yattatbhyamiḍatiṅitikecita: "from yat and tat also, ḍati." (Gloss: for kim, ḍati; by "ḍ goes," the ṭi, which is to be elided, is removed; the sense of ḍ.) "Sometimes." Sometimes ḍati also occurs for a measure from yat and tat: as many, yatiḥ; so many, tati.

saṃkhyāyāavayavetayap: (gloss: yu bde) for these, a number, yap. From a number, tayap for a part. For expressing a part from a number, tayap occurs: in the sense of pañcāvayavāyasya, "whose parts are five," fivefold, pañcatayam. (Gloss: for pañcan, tayap; the vowel sense; the final n of the noun) is removed. (Gloss: for yat and so on, by "ḍ goes," ḍe is removed.)

dvitribhyātayasyāyajvā: from dvi and tri, ayac optionally for tayap. From dvi and tri, the suffix tayap expressing a part optionally becomes ayac. (Gloss: "of which, five parts"; tayap is given and) becomes ayac; c is for the vowel sense; by "of which," the i is removed. Twofold: dvayam, dvitayam; threefold: trayam, tritayam.

ubhātitam: from ubha, always. From ubha, the suffix tayap expressing a part always becomes ayac: ubhayaḥ.

tadasmindhikamitidaśāntataḍa: from what ends in daśa, ḍa, in the sense "that is in excess in this." In the sense "that is in excess in this" (gloss: three more, three more), ḍa occurs for what ends in daśa: ekādaśaṃ śatram, a hundred with eleven over.

śadantavidṣateśca: from what ends in śat and from viṃśati also (gloss: two parts; tal pa becomes ac). From what ends in śat and from viṃśati also, ḍa occurs in the sense of excess: tiṃśaṃ śatam, a hundred and twenty; biṃśiśatram, a hundred with eleven over, that is, a hundred and eleven. (Gloss: for ekādaśan, ḍa; the ṭi) is removed.

Quoted in the commentary: saṃkhyābūrbādabīṣyate: "it is also wanted when a number comes first." From what ends in śat and from viṃśati with a number word before them, too: a hundred and thirty (gloss: for triśat, ḍa, the ṭi removed); for birśatam, ḍa, the ṭi removed. It is held that ḍa applies for excess: ḍa, ekatriṃśaṃ śatam; ḍa, ekaviṃśaṃ śatam.

tasyabūrṇeḍaṭa: ḍaṭ for its completion. For the completion of that number, ḍaṭ occurs: in the sense of ekādaśānāṃ pūraṇam, ekādaśaḥ, śī (gloss: ṅīp); likewise dvādaśaḥ, śī, ṅīp.

nāntādasaṃkhyādeḥmaṭa (gloss: a hundred and thirty-one; a hundred and twenty-one): maṭ from what ends in n and does not have a number at its beginning. For the completion of number words ending in the letter n that do not have a number at their beginning (gloss: the completion of eleven and the rest; for ekādaśan, the sense of ḍaṭ, ṭa, ṭi, tha, ḍha and so on is ḍit, so the ṭi is removed; eleven; twelve), the completion suffix ḍaṭ is given the augment maṭ: fifth, pañcamaḥ, mī, ṅīp; saptamaḥ, mī, ṅīp; aṣṭamaḥ, mī, ṅīp; navamaḥ, mī, ṅīp; daśamaḥ, mī, ṅīp. By "ending in n," maṭ does not occur where the word does not end in the letter n. (Gloss: for pañcan, its completion ḍaṭ; by this sūtra the augment maṭ, with ṭ indicating position; the n of the noun, which is to be elided, is removed.) (Gloss: for saptan, ḍaṭ, the augment maṭ) and so on. Seventh; eighth (gloss: for aṣṭan, ḍaṭ, maṭ, the augment) and so on. (Gloss: ninth: for navan, ḍaṭ, the augment maṭ and so on; tenth: for daśan, ḍaṭ, the augment maṭ) and so on. Twentieth: viṃśaḥ, śī, ṅīp. By "not having a number at its beginning," for one that has a number at its beginning: ḍaṭ, ekādaśaḥ, śī, ṅīp.

ṣaṭkatikatepayacaturāṃthuka: thuk for ṣaṣ, kati, katipaya and catur. For these, ṣaṣ and the rest, the augment thuk occurs when the completion suffix ḍaṭ follows (gloss: for viṃśati, ṭu, te): ṣaṣṭhaḥ, sixth (gloss: ṅīp; ṣaṣṭhī). For yati, ḍaṭ, the augment thuk: katithaḥ, thī (gloss: a little; ṅīp); twelfth. Katipayathaḥ, thī (gloss: ṅīp); caturthaḥ, rthī, ṅīp.

caturaśchayatauc alopaśca: from catur, cha and yat, and also elision of c. From catur, cha and yat occur for completion, and the letter c of catur is elided. (Gloss: for ṣaṣ, ḍaṭ is given; by this sūtra thuk for ṣaṣ, with k indicating position; the sense of ṭit, so the ṭi, which is to be elided, goes by u; ṣaṭ, tha becomes ṭha.) (Gloss: for katipaya, ḍaṭ, the augment thuk:) one who has obtained a little. Fourth: for catur, ḍaṭ, the augment thu(k). Turīyaḥ, fourth; turyaḥ, fourth.

batupūgagaṇasaṃghasyatithuk: tithuk for bahu, pūga, gaṇa and saṃgha. For these, bahu and the rest, the augment tithuk occurs when the completion suffix ḍaṭ follows: bahutithaḥ, thī (gloss: ṅīp; the many-eth); for pūga, ḍaṭ, the augment tithuk: pūgatithaḥ, thī (gloss: ṅīp), the areca-nut tree. (Gloss: for catur, the c of the īyac of cha is removed; for catur, yat, its time sense, the c is removed.) Gaṇatithaḥ, thī, ṅīp; saṃghatithaḥ, thī, ṅīp.

Quoted in the commentary: pūgasaṃghābhvāṃḍaṭeṣṭa: "ḍaṭ is wanted also from pūga and saṃgha." (Gloss: the number is vatup; by "its completion," ḍaṭ, as ḍaṭ, ḍaṭi and so on have the sense ḍ and ḍiṭ, the sense of ṭi; by this sūtra tithuk, with k indicating position; the ṭe is removed.) Even though they are not numbers, pūga and saṃgha (gloss: for gaṇa, ḍaṭ, the augment tithuk: group, assembly; for saṃgha, ḍaṭ, the augment tithuk) are also held to take ḍaṭ for completion, as has already been shown in the examples.

patoritthuk: ithuk from vatu. For a stem ending in the suffix vatu, ḍaṭ occurs for completion, and when ḍaṭ follows the augment ithuk is to be given: the as-many-eth, yāvatithaḥ; the that-many-eth, tāvatithaḥ.

desteyaḥ: tīya from dvi. From dvi, tīya occurs for completion: dvitīyaḥ, second.

treḥsaṃprasāraṇaṃca: and saṃprasāraṇa of tri. From tri, tīya occurs for completion, and saṃprasāraṇa is also to be done.

(Gloss: for yāvat and tāvat, by this sūtra ḍaṭ) and the augment ithuk, with k indicating position; for the sense of ḍit, the ṭi is removed. Third: tṛtīyaḥ.

(bidśatyādibhyastamaḍanyatarasyām): from viṃśati and the rest, tamaṭ optionally. From viṃśati and the rest, the augment tamaṭ optionally occurs for the completion suffix ḍaṭ that follows: piṃśaḥ, twentieth (gloss: for piṃśati, ḍaṭ, the te removed); (biṃśa)titamaḥ, twentieth; tiṃśaḥ, thirtieth; triṃ..., third(?); śattamaḥ.

nityaṃśatādīmāsāṇhaṃmāsasaṃbatsarācca: and always from śata and the rest, and from māsa, ardhamāsa and saṃvatsara. From śata and the rest, and from māsa (gloss: from ardhamāsa and saṃvatsara; for viṃśati, its completion, ḍaṭ is wanted; for ḍaṭ, the augment tamaṭ, with ṭ indicating position, and the sense of...), from saṃvatsara as well (gloss: for triṃśat, ḍaṭ; for triṃśat, ḍaṭ, the augment tathaṭ and so on), ḍaṭ occurs for completion, and for ḍaṭ the augment tamaṭ is always to be given: hundredth, śatatamaḥ; thousandth, sahasratramaḥ; hundred-thousandth, lakṣatamaḥ; the one of the month, māsatamaḥ; the one of the half-month, ardhamāstamaḥ; the one of the year, saṃbarśarratamaḥ.

(ṣaṣṭhyādeścāsikhyādeḥ): and from ṣaṣṭi and the rest, when they do not have a number at their beginning. For ṣaṣṭi and the rest which do not have another number word before them (gloss: for śata, ḍaṭ; the sense of ṭit, ḍha and so on; for ṣaṣṭi, ḍaṭ, the augment tamaṭ), the augment tamaṭ always occurs for the completion suffix ḍaṭ: ṣaṣṭitamaḥ, sixtieth (gloss: ḍaṭ, the augment tamaṭ); sabhatitamaḥ, seventieth; aśītitamaḥ, eightieth (gloss: ḍaṭ, the augment tamaṭ); navatitamaḥ, ninetieth. Where a number comes first: ekāmaṣṭhi, sixty-one, and so on.

mataichasūkhasāmnoḥ: cha for matup, in the case of a well-spoken hymn and a melodious chant. In expressing a well-spoken hymn and a melodious chant, cha occurs in the sense of matup: in the sense of (acgāṃbāgasmin) siti, acchābākīyam; in the sense of bārabantaṃsāmaḥ, bārabantīyam (gloss: cha becomes īya; having a well-spoken hymn; having a melodious line of verse, having a melodious line of verse).

būrbādini: ini from pūrva. From pūrva, ini occurs in the sense of "by this one it was fled from, or drunk, or done": "this one ate before." In the sense of pūrvamanenabhuktam, "this one has eaten before" (gloss: cha, maga; eaten beforehand: pūcchī; for tha cha, eni, the i of ta; the sense of the expressed meaning mu), by "ehana" the n at the end of the long noun, which is to be elided, is removed, and by "ta" and the rest the su is destroyed. Likewise in the sense of būrbamanenapītam, būrbī, "drank before."

sabūrbācca: and from one with a preceding word. From pūrva together with another preceding word, ini also occurs in the sense of "eaten by this one" and so on: in the sense of bhaktapūrbamanenabhuktam, bhaktapūrbī, "one who has eaten food before." (Gloss: "this one drank before"; for durba, ini, the i of ina, the sense of the expressed meaning; by "su inhana," the n at the end of the long noun, which is to be elided, is removed, and by ha and the rest the su is destroyed.)

iṣṭadibahyaśca: and from iṣṭa and the rest. From iṣṭa and the rest also, ini occurs in the sense of "by this one it was desired" and so on (gloss: "this one heard first of food"; one who ate food before): in the sense of iṣṭamanenayajā, (iniiṣṭiyajño). Likewise adhitībyākaraṇe, "one who wishes to read grammar."

(tadasyastyasminniti) matup: matup in the sense "that belongs to this, it is in this." In the sense of possession, "that belongs to this, it is in this," matup occurs: in the sense of (śrīrasti), "this one has glory": śrīmān, glorious; śrīmatī, the glorious woman. (Gloss: "Śrī wants a sacrifice"; "Śrī wants a sacrifice"; the man; for the fifth and the rest, dni.)

tasaumatvarthe: s and t in the sense of matup. A stem ending in the letter s or the letter t (gloss: having glory or being glorious; for śrī, matup; the vowel sense u; uk goes; the sense of num; the upadhā of num removed by su long; the final of the reduplicated removed), when the suffixes in the sense of matup follow, is given the name "called bha," and the sense is that before what is called bha, saṃprasāraṇa occurs: for pidvas, matup; by "the saṃprasāraṇa of vas," the v becomes u, and by "everywhere" and the rest, ṣ: (biduṣmān), "one who has knowledge." Likewise (dhanvān?), domṣmān, "one who has arms."

mādupadhāyāścamator(boñ)yabādibhyaḥ: and from what has m or a as penultimate, the m of matup becomes v, except from yava and the rest. From what is not yava and the rest, for a stem with the letter m or the letter a as its penultimate, and by the word "and" also with the letter m (gloss: "one who is wise"), and from what ends in the letter a also (gloss: for droṇa, matup, su, num and so on), the letter m of matup becomes the letter v: "how much," (kimbā)n (gloss: for matup, num and so on); (matubadhā)n; bān, matup; vidyābān, one who has learning; matup, lakṣibānra, one who has marks; yaśasbānra, matup; bhāsvānra, "one who has radiance." For yava and the rest, the m does not become v: matup, yavamānra; matup, (bhūmimān).

jhayaḥ: from jhay. When the end of a stem is jhay, which collects letters one by one (gloss: "one who has wisdom"; for jñāna(?), matup), the letter m of matup (gloss: glorious, or endowed with excellence; for a as upadhā, num and so on; the shining one, that is, the sun) becomes the letter v: matup, (bidyudbān), "one who has lightning"; "one who has the sky"; "one who has the earth (that is, a king)."

prāṇi(skadvataḥlbajanyatarahyāṃk): from what ends in ā, for a limb of a living being, lac optionally.

In expressing a limb of a living being, from a stem ending in ā, lac optionally occurs in the sense of matup: cūḍālaḥ; matup, cūḍābān.

sidhmādibhyaśca: (gloss: sidhma, "having a thick one") and from sidhma and the rest also. From sidhma and the rest also, lac optionally occurs in the sense of matup: lac, sidhmalaḥ, "having wood"; matup, sidhmabān, "having wood"; lac, māṃsalaḥ, "having flesh"; (matup, māṃsabān); lac, maṇilaḥ (gloss: matup, ma...; lac, the c for the vowel sense); "having a crest"; ...ṇibān.

phenādilacca: and ilac from phena. For phena, in the sense of matup, lac and also ilac occur: (ilac, phenilaḥ); lac (gloss: "sidhma" is applied to treatises, auspicious things, beings, accomplished things and trees), phenalaḥ; (matup) phenabān. (Gloss: having accomplishment; having jewels; having flesh; one having jewels, endowed with jewels.)

(lomādibāmādipicchādibhyaḥśanelacaḥ: from loman and the rest, from bāman and the rest, and from piccha and the rest, śa, na and ilac.) For loman and the rest, pāman and the rest, and piccha and the rest, in the sense of matup, śa, na and ilac also occur, in that order (gloss: having accomplishment): lomaśaḥ, "having hair"; śa, romaśaḥ (gloss: matup, romabān; bāmanaḥ; matup, bāmabān; na, adganaḥ; matup, adgabān; ilac, bicchilaḥ; "having caution"; matup, picchabān; ilac, urasilaḥ, broad-chested or big-bellied); (gloss: matup, uraswān).

prajñāśrāddhārcābṛttibhyoṇaḥ (gloss: for loman, śa, the n at the end of the noun removed; having a body; having ...; matup, the n at the end of the noun removed; for bāman, ...; having purity; arcāvṛtti, having limbs): ṇa from these. From prajñā and the rest, ṇa also occurs in the sense of matup: ṇa, prājñaḥ; matup, prajñābān; ṇa, śrāddhaḥ; śraddhābān; ṇa, ārcaḥ; matup, ārcābān; ṇa, vārttaḥ; matup, brirattimān.

dantaunnataurac: urac for danta in the sense of protruding. From danta, in the sense of matup connected with expressing protrusion, urac occurs: urac, danturaḥ, "having protruding teeth."

ūṣaśuṣimuṣkamadhoraḥ (gloss: having wisdom; having faith; having offerings; having history, having history): ra from ūṣa, śuṣi, muṣka and madhu. From ūṣa and the rest, ra also occurs in the sense of matup: ūśaraḥ, ūṣabān; śuṣiraḥ, śuṣimān; muṣkaraḥ, muṣkabān; madhuraḥ, madhumān.

khamukhakuñjebhyaśca: and from kha, mukha and kuñja. From kha, mukha and kuñja also, ra occurs in the sense of matup: kharaḥ, mukharaḥ, kuñjaraḥ.

Quoted in the commentary: nagapṅaṃśupñcaṇabhyaśca: "and from naga, pāṃśu and pāṇḍu" (gloss: having form; having dryness; having thieves; having fame, or having faith; having fame). From naga, pāṃśu and pāṇḍu also, ra occurs in the sense of matup: nagaraḥ (gloss: having a donkey; insolent, or bold; having an elephant); pāṃrśuraḥ; pānūraḥ.

Also quoted in the commentary: kacchāhrasvatāṃca: "and with shortness of kacchū." Since the u is not long like ū, kacchu with shortness takes ra in the sense of matup: kacchuraḥ.

keśādonyatarasyaṃ (gloss: having a city): from keśa, va optionally. From keśa, va optionally occurs in the sense of matup (gloss: having dust; having people): keśabaḥ; and ini, keśī; ṭhan, keśikaḥ; matup, keśabān.

Quoted in the commentary: anyabhyoñapi: "from others also" (gloss: having a frog). Not only keśa, but others also take va in the sense of matup: barmaṇibaḥ; lanmaṇilaḥ.

arṇasaḥsalopaśca: and elision of the s of arṇas (gloss: having hair; having hair; adśas, having hair; having hair). For arṇas, va occurs in the sense of matup, and when va follows, the d of arṇas is also elided: va, arṇabaḥ, "having wilderness"; matup, arṇaswān.

medhārathābhrāṃmiranniracauca (gloss: having jewels): and from medhā and ratha, iran and irac. From medhā and ratha, iran and iras also occur in the sense of matup, in that order: iran, medhiraḥ; matup, medhābān; irac, rathiraḥ; matup, rathapān.

kāṇḍāṇḍādībannīracau: īran and īrac from kāṇḍa and āṇḍa. From kāṇḍa and āṇḍa, īran and īrac occur, in that order: īran, kāṇḍīraḥ; matup, gāṇḍibān; īrac, āṇḍīraḥ; matup, āṇḍabān. (Gloss: having intelligence, or having a steady mind; having chariots; having chariots.)

dyudrubhyāṃmaka: ma from dyu and dru. From dyu and dru, ma occurs in the sense of matup: dyumaḥ; drumaḥ.

ataḥiniṭhanau: ini and ṭhan from a. From a stem ending in a (gloss: having thorns; having eggs; having eggs), ini and ṭhan occur in the sense of matup: ini, daddī; ṭhan, daṇḍikaḥ; matup, daṇḍabān; ini, keśī; ṭhan, keśikaḥ; matup, keśabān; va, keśapaḥ. (Gloss: having light; having trees, or a tree.)

brīhyādibhyaśca: and from brīhi and the rest. From brīhi and the rest also, ini and ṭhan optionally occur in the sense of matup: ini, brīhī; ṭhan, brihīkaḥ (gloss: having a staff); matup, brīhimān (gloss: having hair, having hair, having hair, having hair, having hair); ini, godyumi; ṭhan, godyumikaḥ; matup, godyumabān.

śikhādeḥnaṭhan: not ṭhan from śikhā and the rest. From śikhā and the rest, ini occurs in the sense of matup, but ṭhan does not (gloss: having fruit, having fruit): "having fruit"; ini, śikhī; matup, śikhābān.

Quoted in the commentary, quoted in the commentary: sabhamyaṃ: "in the seventh" (gloss: having a mark). From a stem with one vowel and expressing a class, ini and ṭhan do not occur in the sense of the seventh: matup, swabān; matup, sidhabān.

tundādibhyaḥilacca: and ilac from tunda and the rest (gloss: having a crest). From tunda and the rest, ilac occurs in the sense of matup: ilac, tundilaḥ; matup, tundabān; ini, tundī, "having a fat belly"; ṭhan, tundikaḥ.

asmāyāmodhāsrajoboniḥ (gloss: having a self; having a lion): vini from as, māyā, medhā and sraja. For those ending in as, and for māyā, medhā and sraja, vini occurs in the sense of matup (gloss: in vini, the i is for the expressed sense; the upadhā of the num of su is lengthened; the n at the end of the noun is removed; having a fat belly; giving flesh; ...swī; if phāsi is forgotten): matup, tapaswān; vini, tapaswī; matup, tabaswān; vini, māyābī; matup, māyābān; vini, medhnabī; matup, midhābān; vini, sraghri; matup, srakrān.

śridgabṛndnabmyamārakaca: ārakac from śṛṅga and vṛnda.

From śridga and bṛnda, ārakaca occurs in the sense of matub: śridhabā kaḥ (glosses: majestic; ascetic; ascetic; having illusion or having wealth; having illusion); with matub, śridhabāna (gloss: she who is intelligent); with āragaca, brandarakaḥ (gloss: garlanded); with matupa, bṛndapāna.

phelebarhābhyaminan: from phala and barta, inana. From phala and barha, inana occurs in the sense of matub: āragaca; with inan, palitaḥ (gloss: horned); with matub, phalabān; with inan, barhaṇaḥ; with matub, barhibān.

rathācca: also from ratha (gloss: having a multitude). From ratha, inan occurs in the sense of matub (gloss: having a multitude): with inan, rathina; with matub, rathabān.

śītoṣṇatriṣābhya ścālucatadsahana: also from śīta, uṣṇa and tṛṣa, āluca, in the sense of "cannot bear it" (glosses: possessing; having fruit). From śīta, uṣṇa and tṛṣa (gloss: having peacocks or having forests), āluca occurs in the sense of "cannot bear it." In the sense of "śītaṃ na sahate," with āluca: śī tāluḥ (gloss: or one with a chariot). Likewise, with āyuca, uṣṇaluḥ; with āluca, traṃṣāluḥ.

himācca: also from hīmā. From hima too, āluca occurs in the sense of "cannot bear it": with āluca, hīmāluḥ.

balādūlaḥ: from bala, ūla. From bala (gloss: cannot bear the cold), ūla occurs in the sense of "cannot bear it": ba lūyaḥ (gloss: extremely cold).

batācca (glosses: extremely hot; extremely thirsty): also from bata. From bata too, ūla occurs in the sense of "cannot bear it": batūlaḥ.

taḥparbamarudbhyaṃ (gloss: cannot bear snow): from parba and maruta, ta. From parba and maruta, ta occurs in the sense of "cannot bear it": sarbataḥ; maru taḥ (glosses: cannot bear strength; cannot bear the wind).

ūrṇayāḥyus: from ūrṇā, yus. From ūrṇā, yus occurs in the sense of "cannot bear it" (gloss: cannot bear the wind). In the sense of "ūrṇā nashate," that is, "cannot bear wool," in the sense of many: ūrṇāyuḥ (gloss: cannot bear wool).
