bācogminiḥ: from bācā, gmi ni (glosses: mountain; to maruta, ta, and by the rule "of the jhar bajhar," the first ta is elided). To bācā, gmini, in the sense of "cannot bear it": bāgmi (gloss: one who cannot bear speech, or one who has speech, or one skilled in speaking).

ālajāṭcaubahubhāṣiṇi: in censure, ālaca and āṭaca. From bācā, when censure is to be conveyed, ālaca and āṭaca occur: with ālac, bācāṭaḥ; with āṭaca, bācāṭaḥ.

svāminnai śvarye (gloss: bacal gmini: ga, when it bears the name kroba; in ri, the i is for the sake of utterance; by the rules "of cu, ku" and "of the jhal," ka becomes ga; with su, by these and other rules, the vowel is long): in lordship, mina to svā. When lordship is expressed, min occurs from svā: svāmī.

dśādibhyoñāca: from arśas and the rest, ac (gloss: dan chok). From arśas and the rest, ac occurs in the sense of matub: with ac, larśasaḥ; with ac, baijayantaḥ; with ac, caturaḥ; with aca, palitaḥ; with ac, palitaḥ; with ac, pāṭaḥ; with ac, abhāḥ (gloss: lord); with ac, acaḥ.

bātātāṃsārābhyāṃkukca: from bāt and atīsāra, also kuka. From bata and atīsāra, ini occurs in the sense of matub, and kukāgama as well (glosses: having hemorrhoids; having a long narrow passage; having a chest; clever; grey-haired): batakī (glosses: having matted locks; having a banner; cloudy); atīsāra kī (gloss: having offerings), as quoted in the commentary.

biśācācca: also from piśāca. From piśāca too, ini occurs in the sense of matub, and kukāgama as well: piśā cakrī (glosses: to bata, ini and kukāgama; the ka is for the sake of position, the u for the sake of utterance; su and the rest; having a wind disorder).

hastājjātau: from hasta, in the sense of a species (glosses: ini and kukāgama; suffering from dysentery). From hasta, ini occurs in the sense of matub when a species is expressed: with ini, hasti.

kaṃśaṃbhyaṃbabhalustitutayasaḥ: from kaṃ and śaṃ, ba, bha, yus, ti, tu, ta and yas (gloss: having a piśāca). From kaṃ and śi, in the sense of matub (gloss: ini and kukāgama), ba, bha, yus, ti, tu, ta and yas occur: kamāḥ, śambaḥ, kambhaḥ, śambhaḥ (gloss: having an elephant); with lus, kiyuḥ, having water; with yus, śaṃyuḥ, having happiness; kantiḥ, having water; śantiḥ, having happiness; kantuḥ, having water; śantuḥ, having happiness; kantaḥ, having water; śantaḥ, having happiness; with yas, kaṃyaḥ, having water; with yas, śaṃyaḥ, having happiness.

tundibalibaḍerbhaḥ: from tundi, bali and baṭi (glosses: having water; having happiness; having water; having happiness), bha. From these, tundi and the rest, bha occurs in the sense of matub: tundibhaḥ, balibhaḥ, maṭibhaḥ.

ahiśubhamoryus: from ahaṃ and śubhaṃ, yus. From ahaṃ and śubhaṃ, yus occurs in the sense of matub: ahaṃyuḥ, śubhaṃyuḥ.

rajaḥkṛṣcasutibariṣado balaca: from rajas, kṛṣi, āsutī and brariṣad, balaca. From these, rajas and the rest (glosses: having strength and begging; having strength; a beggar), balac occurs in the sense of matub.

bale: before bala. When the suffix palaca follows, if there is at the end of the stem a letter of the abbreviation (pratyāhāra) aṇ, that letter becomes long (glosses: having a self; having virtue): rajasvalaḥp (gloss: having dust), kṛṣībalaḥ, āsutībalaḥ, bariṣadvalaḥ.

prāgniśoḥbibhaktiḥ: before "direction," case endings (vibhakti). From here up to the rule "From words of direction, the seventh, the fifth and the first," whatever suffixes there are function in the sense of case endings, and they are given the name "suffixes called case endings" (glosses: one who works the fields; one of careful conduct; one who destroys utterly).

kiṃsarbanābatudhyoñdvyādaṃbhyaḥ: from the sarbanāma words other than dvi and the rest, and from kiṃ and bahu. From the sarbanāma words that are not dvi and the rest, that is, with those excluded, and from kiṃ and bahu, the suffixes to be explained below, tasil and the rest, occur: this is the general rule.

pañcamyāstasi: from the fifth, tasil. From the sarbanāma words other than dvi and the rest, mentioned above, and from bahu and kim, tasil occurs in the sense of the fifth case ending: sarbataḥ, sarbasmat. To kim, tasil.

kutitoḥ: from ta and ha, ku.

When a suffix designated a case ending, beginning with the letter ta or beginning with the letter ha, follows, kim becomes ku: kutaḥ, kasmāta; tataḥ (gloss: from that), tasmāta; lataḥ (glosses: to yad, tasel; from which; in tasil, for the sake of accent, and the i for the sake of utterance; from all), yasmāta (gloss: from which); bahutaḥ (gloss: from many), bahoḥ (gloss: from many), as quoted in the commentary.

sarbabrātibadikāttasilca: from all stems, tasil. Not only from the sarbanāma words and the rest mentioned above, but from all stems as well, tasil occurs in the sense of the fifth (glosses: from what; to tat, tasil; for tyad and the rest, a before a case ending; for rgyad and the rest, a before a case ending): buddhataḥ, buddhāta; debataḥ, debāta; and so on.

idamiśa: for idam, iśa. When a suffix designated a case ending follows, idam becomes iśa: itaḥ (gloss: from this); ataḥ (gloss: from this); asmāta (gloss: from this).

etado'śa: for etat, aśa. When a suffix designated a case ending follows, etat becomes aśa (glosses: from the Buddha; from a god; from a god): ataḥ (gloss: from this), etasmāta.

paryabhibhyāṃca: also from mari and abhi (glosses: to dam, tasel; idam, eśa, the śa bearing the name broba; to yidampa, tasil; by the rule on byad and the rest, the la of ṭit is elided; of i and ra). From the preverbs (upasarga) bari and abhi too, tasil occurs in the sense of the fifth: baritaḥ, abhitaḥ (glosses: to etat, tasil; etat, aśa; from this).

sabtamyāstāla: for the seventh, tala (gloss: path). From the sarbanāma words other than dvi and the rest, and from bahu and kim, hral optionally occurs in the sense of the seventh: katra (gloss: in what), kasmin; sarbathā, sarbasmin; tahra (glosses: from all around; from in front), tasmin; yatra, yasmin; atra (gloss: in this), atasmin; bahutra, debaho.

idmohaḥ: from idam, ha. From idam, ha occurs in the sense of the seventh: iha, asmin.

kimo'ta (glosses: to kima, tras; the la for the sake of accent; before ta and ta, ku, hence ku; in all): from kim, ate (gloss: in that). To kima, in the sense of the seventh, at optionally occurs (glosses: in which; to etta, tral, and by the rule "aśa for etat," etat, yaśa; in many): kim, at.

kvāti: at (glosses: to idam, ha; midam, iśa; mā; idam becomes iśat; in this): before that, kva. When the suffix at, which has the sense of the seventh, follows, kima becomes kva: kva, as quoted in the commentary.

tralpi: before tral too. When tral follows too, kim optionally becomes kā: kvatra, gutra, gasmin (gloss: in what, or in which).

bāhacacchandasi: in verse (chandas), ha optionally. When there is a need, for verse and the like, ha optionally occurs from kim in the sense of the seventh (glosses: kim, at; kim, kva; the sense of time of tata; whose it also; the a of the stem is removed): kuha.

sarbikā rgyakimyattadaḥkāledā: from sarba, eka, anya, kim, yad and tat, dā in the sense of time. From these, sarba and the rest, when, ending in the seventh, they apply to time, dā occurs: ekadā, anyadā, kadā, yadā, tadā; to sarba, dā (glosses: in what, or in which; to kim, ta; from ta and ha, ku).

sarbasyaso'nyatarasyaṃdi: of sarba, with dā, optionally. When the suffix dā follows, sarba optionally becomes sa: sadā (gloss: always), or sarbadā (glosses: sarbasmin kale and so on; at one time; at another time; at what time; at which time; at that time).

idmorhil: from idi, rhil. From idam, when, ending in the seventh, it applies to time, rhil optionally occurs: to idam, rhil.

etaurathoḥ (gloss: to sarba, dā; by this sūtra sarba is altered): from ra and tha, eta and ita. When a suffix designated a case ending, beginning with the letter ra or the letter tha, follows, idam becomes eta and ita respectively: etarhi.

adhunā: adhunā. idam becomes adhunā; it is a particle in the sense of the seventh connected with time.

dānīṃca: dānīṃ too. To idam, when, ending in the seventh, it applies to time, dāniṃ also comes (gloss: at this time): idānīṃ.

tadodāca: from tad, dā too (gloss: at this time). From tad, when, ending in the seventh, it applies to time (gloss: in this), dānīṃ and dā also occur: tadānīṃ, tadā, as quoted in the commentary.

punarodā: from punar, dā. From bunar, when, ending in the seventh, it applies to time, dā optionally occurs (gloss: to idam, dānī; by idam to ita, yidam becomes iśa): phunardā.

anadya tanirtilargyatarasyāṃ: for a time not of today, rtil optionally (gloss: at that time). From the sarbanāma words, excluding dvi and the rest, and from kim and bahu, when, ending in the seventh, they apply to a time not of today, rtil optionally occurs: karti, from kim with rtil (gloss: at which time); from tata with rtil, tarti (glosses: at that time; at a later time; at which time); yarti, also with rtil.

sadyaḥ brutbarāryi ṣamaḥ pradya byadya pūrbedyur nyedyur nyataredyur itarergyur paredyur adharedyur ubhayedyur uttaredyuḥ (gloss: at once, or in succession): sadyaḥ (glosses: to samāna, dyas; to bar, ut); baruta (gloss: the farther time); parvari (gloss: to bara, āri); aiṣamaḥ; paredyabiḥ (gloss: the time of tomorrow); adya (gloss: this time); pūrbedyuḥ (gloss: the earlier time); anyedyuḥ (gloss: another time); anyataredyaḥ (gloss: a different time); itaredyuḥ (gloss: to itasa, edyus); aparedyuḥ (gloss: to apaba, etul); adharedyuḥ (gloss: to adhara, edyus); ubhayedyuḥ; udharedyuḥ (glosses: to idam, maca, and idam becomes eṣa; this time; to bar, ebyabisa; to idam, dya, and dam, a; to bhuca, awdyus). Such are these. These, sadal and the rest, are particles ending in the seventh, used in expressing time (glosses: ebasdyuḥ; to sanyatara, esmus; the remaining words; time; another time; the first time; the time of both, or both days; to ubhasa, edyul; to dya, edyus; the later time, or the following day).

prakārabacanithāla: in expressing manner, thāla. From the sarbanāma words other than dri and the rest, and from kim and bahu, thāl occurs in expressing manner. In the sense of "kena prakāreṇa": kathā; in that way, tathā; in that way, tathā; yathā; sarbathā.

idamsthamuḥ: from idam, thamu. From idam, thamu occurs in expressing manner: itthaṃ.

kimśca: also from kim. From kim too, thamu occurs in expressing manner: kathaṃ.

dik śabdebhyaḥ sabhamīpañcamī prathamābhyo digdeśakāleṣvastātiḥ (glosses: in what manner; in what manner; thus; thus; in every manner): from words of direction, from the seventh, the fifth and the first, in the senses of direction, time and place, astāti (gloss: to idam, thamu, the u being for the sake of utterance; by the rule "before ta and tha, eta and ita," it becomes ita; many).

As for the manner: from those known as words of direction, ending in the seventh, the fifth and the first, when they apply in the senses of direction, place and time, astāti occurs: barastāta, abarastāta.

pūrbhadharābarāṇāmasiburadhaybaścaiṣāṃ: of būrba, adhara and abara, asil; and these, pur, adha and aba, as well. When the suffix asi follows, these, būrba and the rest, become respectively these, phur and the rest (glosses: beyond, or from beyond, or to the beyond; to bar, astāti, the i for the sake of utterance; on this side, or from this side, or to this side).

astātica: also with astāti. When the suffix astāti follows, too, pūrba and the rest become respectively phur and the rest: rastāta (glosses: in the east, or to the east, or from; from which); adhastata (gloss: to adhara, astati); abarastāta (gloss: to abara, astāti); puraḥ (gloss: to pūṇa, asi, the i for the sake of utterance); adhaḥ (gloss: to adhara, asaṃ); abaḥ (gloss: to abara, asi).

abibhāṣābarasya: optional for abara. When the suffix astāti follows, abara becoming aba and not becoming so are to be made optional (glosses: to būrba, astāti, with the i for utterance, and būrba becomes pūra; below, or from below, or to below; another, or from another, or to another; in the east, or from the east, or to the east; below, or from below, or downward; another direction, or from another direction, or to another direction): abarastāta, abarastāta.

dakṣiṇittarābhyāmatasuca: from dakṣiṇa and uttara, atsuca. From dakṣiṇal and uttara, atasuca occurs in those senses mentioned above, the seventh and so on: dakṣiṇāta (gloss: in the south); uttarataḥ (glosses: in the north; another direction, or from another direction, or to another direction).

bibhāṣābarāparābhyaṃ: from bir and abar, optionally. In the senses of the seventh and so on, atasuca optionally comes to para and abara: bartaḥ, abarataḥ (glosses: to dakṣiṇa, atasuca, for the sake of accent, and the u for the sake of utterance; to uttarā, atasuca).

añceluka: from añca, elision. From a word of direction ending in añcati, astāti disappears: prāgbapati (gloss: dwells in the east); prāgāgataḥ.

uparyubariṣṭāta: upariṣṭāta. To the word ārdha, in the sense of astāti, aril and ariṣṭātil come, and ūrdha becomes upa; thus ubari and upariṣṭāta are particles (glosses: atasuca; to the far side; atasuca; in the western direction).

paścāta: paścāta. Of bra sdordatha, to atu, astāti is removed (gloss: comes from the east). abara becomes pāśa, and in the sense of astāti, āti is given (gloss: upari); thus paścāta is a particle.

uttararādakṣiṇādāti: from uttarā, adhara and dakṣiṇa, āti (gloss: in the upper direction). From uttarā, adhara and dakṣiṇa, āti occurs in the sense of astāti: uttarāba (glosses: in the north; āti, for the sake of utterance); adharāta (gloss: in the lower direction); dakṣiṇāta (glosses: in the south; in the west).

enapanyatarasyāmadure'bañcambāḥ: for what is not far, from what is not a fifth, enas, optionally. From words ending not in the fifth but in the seventh and the first, from adhara, dakṣiṇa and uttarā, enas optionally occurs when the distance is not far: adhareṇabsati, dakṣiṇenabasti, uttareṇabasti. Because of "not a fifth," it does not occur with one ending in the fifth: with ṅasi, uttarādāgataḥ. If it is far, enas does not occur: with ñasil, uttadatohimabāna, as quoted in the commentary.

dikṣabdamātrāta: also from direction alone (glosses: dwells near, below; dwells near the south; dwells near the north). When direction alone is expressed, too, enas occurs: būrbeṇa, dakṣiṇena (gloss: came from the north), abarṇa, uttareṇa.

dakṣiṇādāca (gloss: Himavat, far to the north): from dakṣiṇa, āca. From dakṣiṇa ending in the seventh and the first, the fifth being excluded, āca occurs: dakṣiṇābasati; with ac, dakṣiṇāramaṇīyaṃ. Because of "not a fifth," with the fifth (glosses: the east; the south; the west; the north): dakṣiṇādāgataḥ.

āhicadūre: in the far, āhi too. To dakṣiṇa, connected with an expression of distance and ending in the seventh and the first, āha comes; and by the word "too," ac as well (glosses: aca, the ca for the sake of accent; dwells in the south; plays in the south): with āñi, dakṣiṇāhibasati; with ac, dakṣiṇābasati.

uttarācca (gloss: came from the south): also from uttarā. From uttarā too, āca and āhi occur: with ac, uttarābasati; with āhi, uttarāhibasati.

saṃkhyāyābidhāḍredhā: from a numeral, in the sense of manner, dha. From numeral words, in the sense of manner, dhā occurs (gloss: dwells in the far south). In the sense of "catuḥprakāraṃ": catudhā. Likewise ekadhā, dvidhā, ṣoḍha (glosses: sixfold; dwells far, or in the south), ṣaḍḍhā, pañcadhā, and so on.

ikārdhodhyamuñnyatarasyaṃ: from aka, for dha, dhyamuña optionally. From eka, the suffix dhā in the sense of manner optionally becomes dhāmuña (glosses: fourfold; fourfold; onefold; twofold; to ṣaṣa, dhā, and by "the u of ṣa and the ḍha of dha" and "the jaśa of the jhala," ṣaḍ; fivefold; to eka, dhā, and dhā to dhyanuña, for the sake of increase (vṛddhi), the u for the sake of utterance): aikadhyama (gloss: onefold), ekadhā.

edhācca: edhā too. From dvi and tri, the suffix dhā in the sense of manner optionally becomes edhā: dvedhā, dvidhā; tredhā, triṅhi.

yāsyepāśapa: in censure, pāśapa. When censure is expressed, in the sense of the word itself, pṣaśaba occurs. In the sense of "kutsitobhaṃṣaba": bhiṣakpāśaḥ, as quoted in the commentary.

bāśakalbakamye: in desire, pāśapa and kalba (glosses: twofold; threefold). In the sense of desire, too, pāśapa and kamya occur. In the sense of "payaḥkmye": with pāśaba, payasbā śaṃ (gloss: a bad physician); with kalba, pa yaskalpaṃ (glosses: a bad physician; in bāśaba, the pa is for the sake of accent).

iṇaḥṣaḥ: from iṇa, ṣa. The visarga after a stem ending in the abbreviation iṇa becomes the letter sa when a suffix beginning with the pa class or the ka class follows: rbiṣbāśaṃ (gloss: desiring milk, or desiring water).

pūraṇadbhāgeyādana (gloss: desiring milk, or desiring water): from an ordinal (pūraṇa), from tīya, ana in the sense of a share.

From a word ending in the ordinal suffix ṭiyā, aṇ occurs in the sense of a part or share: in the sense of "dītīyobhāgaḥ," dvitāyaḥ; likewise, with an, tritīyaḥ (glosses: to sarbe, bāśaba; desiring milk).

prāgekādaśabhyoñcchandasi: when not in verse, from those before eleven. When it is not in the sense of the verse that expresses the Veda, from those before eleven, that is, to words that have an ordinal suffix, from one to ten, an occurs in the sense of a part (glosses: a numeral, a second part or a second share; half; anan, for the sake of accent; the third part of an ordinal): with an, catunraḥ; with an, daśamaḥ; and so on.

ṣaṣṣāṣṭamābhyāṃñaca: from ṣaṣṭha and aṣṭama, ña too. To ṣaṣṭha and aṣṭama, ña also occurs in the sense of a part: ṣāṣṭhaḥ; with an, ṣaṣṭhaḥ; with ña, aṣṭamaḥ; with an, aṣṭamaḥ.

bhūrarūrbecaraṭa: in the sense of what was before, caraṭa. In the sense of what came about at a former time, caraṭa occurs (glosses: a fourth part; a tenth part). In the sense of "bhūtapūrbodriṣṭaḥ" (gloss: was formerly seen), with caraṭa (gloss: the ṭa is for the sake of ṭita and so on): dṛṣṭacaraḥ (glosses: was formerly seen; ña: when ña goes, dhā, increase; sixth). Likewise (gloss: in a row) ā (gloss: eighth) ḍhyacaraḥ (glosses: was formerly rich; was formerly young); kumāracaraḥ (gloss: carṭa).

ṣaṣṭhyarūpyaca: from the sixth, rūbya too. From a word ending in the sixth, when something that came about at a former time is expressed, rūpya occurs, and caraṭ too. In the sense of "kriṣṇasyabhātapūrbogau": kṛṣṇarūpyaḥgau, or, by adding caraṭ, kṛṣṇacaraḥgau. Likewise, in the sense of "bhūtapūrbāyāśubhrā": śubhārūpyaḥ, śubhrācaraḥ.

atiśāyanetamabiṣṣano: in excellence, tamapa and iṣṭhana. When one that excels, one from among many, is expressed, tamapa and iṣṣana occur (glosses: a cow that was formerly black; a cow that was formerly black; a cow that was formerly black; was formerly white; rūpya; was formerly white; carṭa). In the sense of "ayimeṣamatiśayenalagtuḥ": laghutamaḥ, laghiṣṭhana (gloss: to laghu).

tiraśca: also from tiṅ. From a word ending in tiṅ, such as pacati, too, when excellence is expressed, tamapa occurs. In the sense of "atiśayenapacati": pacatitamāṃ (glosses: supreme, tāla and the rest; among these, the very short one; likewise; in tampa, the pa for the sake of accent; very short; in yiṣṭhana, the na for the sake of accent, and by the rule on ṭi, the ṭi is removed); bhabatitamāṃ.

dvibacanabibhajyopapadetarabīyasunau: when one is singled out from two expressed, and with a nearby word, in excellence, tarpa and īyasuna (glosses: cooks; to pacati, tamapa, and by the rule on kim, tir and indeclinables, āmu).

When one is singled out from two expressed and its excellence is expressed, and also from a nearby word, that is, when another word stands before it, when excellence is expressed, tarba and laīyasun occur (glosses: to bhabate, tanapa and āsu; exists supremely). In the sense of "ayam nayoratiśayenalaghuḥ": laghutaraḥ (gloss: very short), laghīyāna (gloss: very short).

Likewise, with a nearby word: in the sense of "udhīcyāḥ atiśayenapaṭabaḥ" (glosses: the northerners are the more clever; the northerners are the more clever), udīcīpaṭu (gloss: of these two, the one that excels in shortness) taraḥ (glosses: tarabajas; likewise, to laghu, tarpa, the pa for the sake of accent; to laghu, īyaspun, and by the rule on ṭi the ṭi is removed; the na for the sake of accent; the u after śa is an uk, and when it follows, num, for the sake of num; the ubadhā of na is long; su is removed; the end of the cluster is removed); pācyāpaṭiyānas (gloss: īyasun, the ṭi removed; jas; num; the upadhā long).

ajādiguṇabacanādeba: from aja and the rest, when a quality is expressed, these. From aja and the rest, when a quality that applies to excellence is expressed, these, that is, iṣṭhana and īyasun, occur. In the sense of "atiśayenapṛthuḥ": prathiṣthaḥ (gloss: excelling in breadth), bathīyāna (gloss: to pṛthu, āyasu).

taraptamabaughaḥ: tarapa and tamapa are gha. The suffixes taraba and tamapa, which express excellence and so on, are given the technical designation "bearing the name gha."

kimatidabyayaghādāmvadrabyaprakarṣe (glosses: excelled in breadth; to prithu, iṣṭhana, and by the rule "the ta of the first tala," ṛ becomes ra; by the rule on ṭi, the u is removed; excelling in breadth): in the excellence of what is not a substance, from gha added to kima, to e, to tiṅ and to indeclinables, āmu.

When the excellence of what is not a substance is expressed, after a suffix bearing the name gha that follows kim, words ending in the letter e, words ending in tiṅ, and indeclinables, āmu occurs. In the sense of "atiśayenakima": kiṃtarāṃ (gloss: which is supreme?), kitamāṃ; likewise prāhnatarāṃ, grāhnatamāṃ; pacatitārāṃ (gloss: cooks supremely), pacatitamāṃ; uccetarāṃ, uccaistamā, and so on; and words ending in āmu are also indeclinables.

Because of "not a substance," by way of exclusion (glosses: which is supreme?; to kima, tarab and āmu, the u for the sake of utterance; to kim, tamapa and āmu; which is supreme?; to prahṇe, tarapa, āmu; the earlier part of the day is best; to drāhne, tamapa, āmu; tarapa, āmu; tamapa, āmu; to uccau, tarapa, āmu; higher; tamapa, āsu): if it is a substance, āmu does not occur: with taraba, uccaitaraḥtruḥ, and the like.

tuśchandasi: from tṛ, in verse. From words ending in tṛn and tṛca, suffixes of the kṛta class and so on, in the verse of the Veda too, iṣṭhana and īyasun occur in the sense of excellence.

turiṣṭhameyasssu: of tra, before iṣṭhana, iman and īyasun (gloss: the tallest tree). The suffixes tṛn and tṛca (gloss: from that onward) are elided when the suffixes iṣṣana, iman and īyasun follow (gloss: to tri, iṣṣana, the tṛ removed): kariṣṭhaḥ (gloss: does it supremely); karimaḥ (glosses: to kartraṃ, iman; to kartri, īyasun); karīyāna (glosses: does it supremely; to dohitre, iṣṭhana: by this sūtra the tṛ is removed, and by the rule on ṭi, the ī is removed); dohiṣṭhaḥ (glosses: milks supremely; to dohitṛ, iman); dohimaḥ (gloss: milks supremely); dohviyāna.

praśasyasyaśraḥ: the stem praśasya becomes śra when iṣṭhana and īyasun follow.

prakrityaikāca: for one with a single aca, it remains in its natural form. When the three, iṣṭhana and the rest, follow a stem with a single aca, the elision of ṭi does not take place (gloss: dete, tral, īyasun): śreṣṭhaḥ, śreyānā.

jyaca: jya too. When eṣṭhana and īyasun follow, praśasya becomes jya: with iṣṭhana, jeṣṭhaḥ; to jya, īyasun.

jyādādīyasaḥ: after jya, āta in place of īyas.

Glosses: praśasya and bṛddha become jya; to braśasya, iṣṭhana, prasya becomes śra, the ṭi is not elided, strengthening (guṇa); supreme, or chief; to praśasya, īyasuna. The ī of the īyas that follows jya becomes āta: jyāyān.

dṛddhasyaca: of bṛddha too (gloss: welcoming). When iṣṭhana and īyasun follow, bṛddha too becomes jya. In the sense of "atiśayenabriddhaḥp": jyeṣṭhaḥ, jyāyān.

antikabāḍhayorṇadasādhau: of antika and bāḍha, neda and sādha (glosses: mighty, or chief; to braśasya, īyasun, praśasya becomes jya, the ī of īyas becomes a, by the rule on ak before a similar vowel it is long, num and so on). When the suffixes iṣṭhana and īyasun follow, antika becomes ne and bāḍha becomes sādha (glosses: the very old, or excelling in age; to bṛddha, iṣṭhana, the very old; to bṛddha, īyasun, the very old): nediṣṭhaḥ, nedīyāna; sādhiṣṭhaḥ, sādhiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: the greatest), sādhiyāna.

sthuladūrayubahrasvakṣiprakṣudrāṇāṃyaṇādiparaṃpūrbasyacaguṇa: of sthūla, dūra, yubā, hrasva, kṣipra and kṣudra, the following part beginning with yaṇ, and the preceding vowel also takes strengthening. Of these, sthula and the rest, when the suffixes iṣṭhan, īyasun and iman follow, if at the end of the stem there is a following part whose first letter belongs to the abbreviation yaṇ, it is elided, and the first ac of the stem also takes strengthening (glosses: to antika, iṣṭhaka, it becomes neda, the ṭi removed; smallest; to antika, īyasun; to sārta, iṣṭhana and īyasun, bāḍha becomes sāre dhare, the ṭa removed): sthabiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: stoutest), lbabīyāna (gloss: to sūla, iṣṭha and īyasun, the ṭi removed, by this sūtra the letter of aṇa removed, then strengthening, icalibāya and so on); dabiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: farthest), drabīlāna (glosses: to dlura, iṣṭhan and īlasun, the ṭi removed, by this sūtra the letter of yāna removed, dūyaṃ, the u strengthened, aya for eca; most youthful); yabiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: to yuba, iṣṭhan and īyasun, the ṭi removed, by this sūtra the letter of yāna, lba, removed, the u strengthened, yaya for eca and so on), yabīyāna (gloss: most youthful); hrasiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: shortest), hrasīyāna; kṣepiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: swiftest), kṣepīyāna; kṣidiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: pettiest), kṣodeyāna.

iman applies only to the three included in the "and the rest" of prithu and the rest, namely hrasva, kṣibra and kṣudra; it does not apply to all of these, sthula and the rest (glosses: to hvasva, ittana and īyasun, the ṭi removed, by this sūtra the letter of yāna, lba, removed; to kṣiza, aṣṭhan and īyasun, the ṭi removed, by this sūtra the letter of yaṇa removed, the i strengthened; to kṣudra, iṣṭhan and īyasun, the ṭi removed, by this sūtra the letter of yaṇa removed, the u strengthened): hrasimaḥ (gloss: shortness), kṣepimaḥ, kṣodimaḥ.

priyasthirsbirubahulagurubṛddhatṛptadīrgyadṛnbarakāṇāṃprasthasbabarbaṃhigarbarṣihrapadrāghipṛndāḥ: of priya, sthira, sthira, uru, bahula, guru, bṛddha, tṛpta, dīrgha and bṛndāraka: pra, sba, spha, bara, baṃhi, gara, barṣi, trapa, drāghi and bṛnha (glosses: to hrasva, iman, the ṭi removed, by this sūtra the letter of yāna, lba, removed; to kṣipra, iman; swiftness; pettiness; to kṣudra, iman).

When iṣṭhan, īyasun and iman follow, these, priya and the rest, become respectively these, pra and the rest: breṣṭhaḥ (gloss: supremely dear), preyān; stheṣṭhaḥ (gloss: most firm), stheyān (gloss: most increased); spheṣṭhaḥ, sbeyān (gloss: most increased); bariṣṭhaḥ (gloss: most excellent, or supreme), barīyān; baṃhitṭhaḥ (gloss: most numerous), baṃhīyān; gariṣṭhaḥ (gloss: heaviest), garīyāna (glosses: to priya, iṣṭhan and īyasun, by this sūtra priya becomes bra, with strengthening; to sthir, iṣṭhin and īasun, by this sūtra sthir becomes stha, with strengthening; to sthir, iṣṭhan and īyasun, sbir becomes spha, with strengthening; to uru, iṣṭha yasun, by this sūtra uru becomes bara, the ṭi removed; to batu, iṣṭhan and ailasun, by this sūtra bahula becomes baṃhi, the ṭi removed; to yuru, iṣṭhan and īyasun, by this sūtra suru becomes gara, the ṭi removed); barṣiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: oldest), barṣīyāna (gloss: to bṛddha, iṣṭhan and īyasun, by this sūtra baṃddha becomes barṣi, the ṭi removed); hrapiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: most satisfied), tabīyāna (gloss: to tṛbta, iṣṭhan and īlasun, by this sūtra hrabha becomes trapa, the ṭi removed); drāghiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: longest), drāghiyān (gloss: dridhaba, iṣṭhan and aiyasun, by this sūtra dīrdha becomes chāghi, the ṭi removed); bṛnṅiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: most numerous), bṛndīyān.

Among these, priya, aru, aru, bahula, guru and dīrgha, since they are included among pṛthu and the rest, take iman: premaḥ (gloss: joyfulness), barimaḥ (glosses: breadth; abundance), baṃñimaḥ (gloss: bahula; with iman, bahula becomes baṃhi, removed), garimaḥ (gloss: to bṛndāṅaka, iṣṭhan and īyasun, by this sūtra bṛndāraka becomes branda, the ṭi removed), drāghimaḥ.

bahormopobhūcabahaḥ: after bahu, elision, and for bahu, bhū. When īyasun, iṣṭhana and iman come after bahu, the initial letter of those suffixes is elided, and bahu too becomes bhū (glosses: to thiya, iman, thiya becomes thu, with strengthening; to uru, iman, uru becomes bara, the ṭi removed; bho-ness; to tharu, iman, guru becomes gara, the ṭi removed; to dīrdha, iman, dīrgha becomes drābhi, the ṭi removed; much longer): bhūyān (gloss: more numerous), bhāmaḥ (gloss: abundance).

iṣṭhasyayiṭca: for iṣṭhan, yiṭ too. When iṣṭhan is given to bahu, the ī of iṣṭhan is elided, bahu becomes bhū, and iṣṭhan also receives yiṭāgama: bhūyiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: most numerous).

yubālbayoḥknānyatarasyāṃ (glosses: to bahu, īyasun, by this sūtra the ī removed and bahu becomes bhū; to bahu, iman, by this sūtra the i removed and batu becomes bhū): for yuba and alba, kana optionally. When iṣṭhan and aiyasun follow, yuba and alba optionally become kana: kañiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: most youthful, or very short), kanīyāna (gloss: most youthful, or smallest); or else yabiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: most youthful), yabīyāna (gloss: fewest); albiṣṭhaḥ, albiṣṭhaḥ (glosses: iṣṭhan; īyasun), albīyāna (gloss: fewest).

binmatotluka: by bin and matupa, it disappears.

(Glosses: to the stem yuba or alba, iṣṭhan; tuba or alba becomes kana, and the ṭi is removed. To yuba or alba, īyasun; the stem becomes kana, and the ṭi is removed. To yuba, iṣṭhan and īyaun; ṭi; by the sūtra sthula blu and the rest, the letter ba of the yaṇ is removed, u takes guṇa, and the eca becomes aya and so on.) That is, when a word ends in bin and matupa, and the suffixes iṣṭhan and aiyasun follow, bin and matupa disappear: srajiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: most possessed of making), srardaiyān (gloss: to srasbin, which ends in bin, iṣṭan and īyasun; by this sūtra bin is removed); tvajiṣṭhaḥ (gloss: most possessed of skin), tvajīyāna (gloss: to tvabātu, which ends in manum, iṣṭhan and īyasun; by this sūtra matuba is removed).

praśaṃsāyāṃ tūbayaḥ: For disguise, rūpaya. In a sense such as passing off one who is not learned as learned, rūpaya comes after stems and also after forms ending in tiṅ: in the sense of braśastaḥ paṭuḥ, baṭudūbaḥ. Likewise, pacatirūpaṃ.

īṣadparismāptau kalbapa deśīyaraḥ: For what is slightly short of fully complete, kalbapa, deśya and deśīyaraḥ. (Glosses: whatever the action is, it is mostly complete; of the counterfeit kind; the form of a scholar, or a counterfeit scholar; to baṭu, ya, and the ya is for the accent; pretending to cook.) In the sense of something done yet only slightly short of fully complete, kalbapa, deśya and deśīyar come after forms ending in tiṅ and after stems: in the sense of īṣā dūno bidvāna, bidvatkalbaḥ (gloss: a slightly inferior scholar). Likewise, yaśaskalbaḥ (gloss: one of slightly lesser fame), bidvaddeśyaḥ (gloss: a slightly inferior scholar), bidvaddeśīyaḥ, bacatikalbaṃ, bacatideśyaḥ, pacatideśīyaḥ.

bibhāṣā (gloss: a slightly inferior scholar) subobahucmurastāta (glosses: to bitrasa, kasma, the ba being for the accent; by the sūtra basu srasu dhāṃsu aṇṭuha and the rest, s becomes d; before khar, car is due, and d becomes t). After suba, bahuca, optionally; but (glosses: and after bidvisa, deśya and deśīyar, for the accent; by the sūtra basu and the rest, s becomes d) it is placed before. Sub (glosses: slightly cooked; slightly uncooked) means this: after the stems that are the bases to which su and the rest are attached, bahuca comes optionally in the sense of slightly incomplete, and the suffix bahuca is to be placed before that stem: in the sense of īṣadūno paṭuḥ, bahupaṭuḥ, paṭukalbaḥ.

prakārabacane jātīyar: For expressing a kind, jātīyar. In the sense of expressing a kind, jātīyar comes: in the sense of maṭubrakāraḥ, paṭujātīyaḥ.

gharūbakalbacelaṭbrubgo (glosses: a slightly inferior scholar; to baṭu the suffix bahuca is placed before, and the ca is for the accent; a slightly inferior scholar) tramatahateṣu dyene'kāco hvasvaḥ. Before gharūpa, kalba, celaṭ, bruba, gotra, mata and hata (glosses: the kind of scholar, or the nature), the ac of dī (glosses: the nature of a scholar; in bātaiyara, for the accent), after what is not single, becomes short. When the suffixes called gha, and these, rūpa and the rest, follow, the suffixes dība and dīṣ, which express the feminine at the end of a stem with more than one aca, become short. By joining tar and the rest to brāhmaṇī: brāhmaṇitarā, brāhmatamā, brāhmaṇirūpāṃ (rūpa, ṭāba), brāhmaṇikalbā (kalba, ṭāba), brāhmaṇicolī (thelaṭ, dība), brāhmaṇibrubā (thuba, ṭāba), brāhmaṇigotrā (potra, ṭraba), brāhmaṇimatā (pata, ṭāpa), brāhmaṇihatā (haha, ṭāpa), and so on; by this sūtra the final dī is changed to short.

nadyāḥ anyatarasyaṃ. Of the nadī (glosses: the most excellent brahmin woman, tarba, ṭāba; a sham brahmin woman, or; a slightly inferior brahmin woman; a slightly inferior brahmin woman; a slightly inferior brahmin woman), optionally. (Gloss: the kind of brahmin woman.) Although they do not end in dī (gloss: a slightly inferior brahmin woman), those called nadī also optionally become short when the suffixes just explained follow: bamorutarā, bamorūtarā, stitarā, stītarā, and so on. That is, making the stem-final short or not making it short is optional, and the same is to be applied to the other suffixes as well. Although they are called nadī, lakṣi, tarī and tantī do not become short: lakṣmitarā, tarītarā, tantītarā (glosses: the woman with the most beautiful thighs; the most excellent woman), and so on.

ugitaśca: Also after what has uka as its dropped marker. When dī has been added to a stem whose dropped marker is a letter of the abbreviation uka, its final too optionally becomes short when the suffixes called gha (glosses: the most excellent heroine, or the supremely accomplished woman) and the rest follow (glosses: the mightiest woman; the woman of sweetest voice): biduṣatarā (gloss: the most learned woman), biduṣītarā, satitarā (gloss: the woman of most excellent conduct), satītamā.

prāgibātkaḥ: Before this, ka. "Before this" means: before the rule that says, "Akaca before the ṭi of the numberless (glosses: to thidāsu, ṣa arises; by gaura and the rest, rī; s and u arise; by the rule that basu again undergoes samprasāraṇa, pa becomes u; by this sūtra it optionally becomes short or does not, so it is optional. To satṛ, ṣita; by gaura and the rest, dī, the ba not being a dropped marker; by this sūtra it becomes short or does not, so it is optional) and of the sathanāmas," ka comes in whatever sense is meant; thus it is set running as a governing rule.

ajhāti: For the unknown. When the sense of the unknown is expressed, ka comes: in the sense of kasya ayi aśaḥ, "Whose horse is this?", aśākaḥ (gloss: whose horse?). Likewise, payaskaṃ (gloss: whose water, or whose milk?).

kutsite: For the contemptible. In the sense of the contemptible too, ka comes: in the sense of kutsitoñ śva, aśvakaḥ. The commentary explains, "When two stems of two syllables each, like debartta, are joined, the latter stem is optionally dropped when ka follows"; hence debadāttakaḥde, debakaḥ.

apyayasarbanāmnāmakacprakaṭeḥ: Before the ṭi of the indeclinables and the sarbanāpas (gloss: a bad horse), akaca.

(Gloss: a bad horse.) After the indeclinables and the sarbanāmas, akaca comes in the sense of the unknown and so on, and it is to be added before the ṭi of the stem: ucca (glosses: a bad Devadatta, or whose Devadatta?; the datta is removed) kaiḥ (gloss: high, whose?), nīcakaiḥ (gloss: low, whose?); (gloss: all of whom, or all the contemptible ones) sarbake (jas, śi; jas, śe), ubhake (gloss: batis, whose, or contemptible).

In the commentary it is explained: "From stems ending in suba, and from roots ending in tiṅ as well, in the sense of the unknown and so on (glosses: to uccus, akaca before the ṭi, the ca being for the accent and the a for pronunciation; to nicisa, akaca before the ti, it being a sub-ending; to sarba, kaca before the ṭi; to ubha, akaca before the ṭi), if it is a stem or a tiṅ-ending, akaca comes before the ṭi of ti and the rest." Thus: yuṣmakābhiḥ (gloss: not known by you all), asmakābhiḥ; yubakayoḥ (gloss: not known by you two), ābakayoḥ (glosses: not known by the two of us; not known among you all); yuṣmakāsu, asmakāsu (gloss: not known among us); tāyakā (gloss: not known by you), mayakī (gloss: not known by me); tvayaki, mayakyi (gloss: not known in me). (Glosses: to yāṣmābhoḥdaṅ and asmābhaḥ, akaca is added before the ṭi of the stem; not known by us; before the ṭi of yubakayoḥ and ābayoḥ, kaca.) pacataki (glosses: cooks badly, or is not known; for yusmāsu and smāsu, akaca before the ṭi of the stem; for tāyā and mayā, akaca before the ṭi of the stem), paṭhataki (glosses: not known in you; for tāyi and mayi, akaca before the stem).

kasyacadaḥ: Of ka, also da. If there is a letter ka at the end of the indeclinables, akaca comes before its ṭi (gloss: to pacati, akaca before the ṭi), and when it is added, the ka, being without its vowel, becomes da without a vowel: (gloss: whose? contemptible) bhakit, dhaki and heru (glosses: to baṭhate, akaca before the ṭi; whose reading?; from ka and bṛthag, akaca before the ṭi; by this sūtra, from the kas, the vowelless and so on removed; d) bāhira kuta (gloss: whose illness?), prithakata (gloss: separately, whose?).

kutāe śamī śuṇḍābhyoḥ raḥ: After kuṭī, śamī and śuṇḍā, ra. After these, kuṭi and the rest, ra comes in the sense of small: in the sense of hrasrakuṭī, kuṭīraḥ. Likewise, śamīraḥ, śuṇḍaraḥ.

batsokṣa śvarṣabheśca tanutve: After batsa, ukṣa and aśva, in the sense of bodiliness. After these, betsa and the rest, ṣṭaraca comes in expressing the bodiliness of the base. It has a ṣa as its dropped marker (glosses: a small cave; a small cave), that is, it is ṣita; the purpose of ṣita is dīṣa; and by the principle, "If the cause (glosses: a short śamī tree; a short elephant's trunk) is absent, what has the cause is absent too," the ṭa also reverts to ta. In the sense of tanubatsaḥ, batsataraḥ (rī; feminine dīg); likewise ukṣataraḥ (rī; feminine dīṣ), aśātaraḥ (rī; feminine dīṣ), ṛṣaghataraḥ (rī; feminine dīṣ).

kimyattado nirddhārdvayo kasyataraza: From kim, yat and tad, in singling out one of two, ṭaraca. After kim, yad (gloss: the body of a calf, or the body of a child) and tad (glosses: the body of a calf, or the body of a child; the body of a youth, or the body of a bull), (gloss: the body of a horse), in the sense of singling out one from among the two (gloss: a bull's offspring), ḍataraca comes: anayokataropaṭuḥ, anayoyataropaṭuḥ, anayotataropaṭurāgacchatu.

bā bahūnāṃ jātibaripraśne ḍatamaca: In asking about the class among many, ḍatamaca, optionally. In the sense of singling out one from among many and asking about its class, ḍata (glosses: to kim, ḍataraca, the ca being for the accent; ḍi, hala, the ṭi removed, that is its purpose; which of these two is learned?; to yad, ḍataraca; whichever of these two is learned; let the learned one of these two come here) maca optionally comes: eṣāṃ katamo brāhmaṇaḥ, eṣāṃ yatamo brāhmaṇaḥ, eṣāṃ tatamo brāhmaṇaḥ. Or, by adding akaca: eṣāṃ kakaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ, eṣāṃ yakaḥ brāgmaṇaḥ (gloss: which brahmin among these?), eṣāṃ sakaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ.

ekāccabācāṃ: Also from eka, according to the easterners. (Glosses: which brahmin among these?; to kim, ḍatamaca; whichever brahmin among these; to yad, ḍatamaca; that brahmin among these; to tata, ḍatamaca; which brahmin among these?; to kaḥ, akaca before the ṭi; to yara, akaca before the ṭi; to saca, akaca before the ṭi; that brahmin among these.) In those senses just explained, ṭataraca and ḍatamaca also come after eka, according to the view of the former eastern teachers: etayorekatarobipraḥ, eṣāmekatamobipraḥ, eṣṭhamekakaḥbipraḥ.

Quoted in the commentary: anyaśabhātaḍtanacca: From the word anya, ḍatamaca too. Ḍatamaca also comes after the word anya: eśāmyanyatamaḥ.

sarbaśabdebhyaḥsvārthekana: After all words, in their own sense, kana. (Glosses: one brahmin of these two; eka, ḍataraca; one brahmin among these; to eka, ḍataraca; to ekata, agaca before the ṭi; one brahmin among these.) All words means any whatsoever; after it, kana comes in expressing its own sense: bahutaraka (glosses: to anya, ḍatamaca; there is another among these; to kanyā, kaḥ).

keñaṇaḥ: Before ka, of aṇ. When the suffix kan follows, if the stem-final is a long letter of the abbreviation aṇ, it becomes short: ganyakā; if it is not of the abbreviation aṇ, it does not become short: naukaḥ.

Quoted in the commentary: tīyā (glosses: in kana, the na is for the accent; the very many) dīkakasvānre: After tīya, in its own sense, īkaka. After what ends in the suffix tīya, īkaka comes in its own sense: dāitīyīkaḥ (glosses: the second itself; a young woman), tārtīyīkaḥ.

prajñādibhyaśca: Also after prajñā and the rest (gloss: being a boat). After prajñā and the rest too, aṇ comes in their own sense: prājñaḥ (with dīpa, drājñī), cauraḥ (with dība, caurīḥ).

saṃkhyāyāḥ kṛyābhyāṃbṛttigaṇanekyitvasuca (glosses: to hvitīya, īkaka, the ka being the dropped marker, with vṛddhi; the third itself; to tṛtīya, īkaka): From a number, for counting the times of an action, tṛtvasuca.

After a number, in expressing the number of times connected with an action, kṛtvasuca comes (glosses: to prajñā, aṇ, with vṛddhi; wisdom; a woman of wisdom; to caura, aṇ; a thief; a female thief): in the sense of pañcabārānabhuṃkta, pañcakṛtvaḥbhuṃkte. Likewise, katikṛtvaḥbhuṃkte.

dvitraṃcaturbhyaḥsuca: After dvi, tṛ and catura, suca. After dvi, tṛ and catura, in expressing the number of times connected with an action, suca comes (glosses: eats five times; eats five times; how many times does he eat?; for dvi, suca, the ca being for the accent and the u for pronunciation, s by sasaju and the rest): drirbhuṃkte (gloss: eats twice) (gloss: for tri, suca, the ca being for the accent and the u for pronunciation, by sasaju and the rest), tṛkbaṭhati (gloss: reads three times), catudraṭhati (gloss: reads four times).

ekasyasakṛcca: Of eka, kṛta too. After eka, in expressing the number of times connected with an action, suca comes, and when suca follows, eka together with suca becomes what is called kṛta: sakṛte.

bahvalbyārthāccha skārakādanyatarasyī (gloss: to batura, suca, the ca being for the accent and the u for pronunciation; after ra the sa is due, and that sa too is removed): From what has the sense of much or little, from a doer (kāraka), śas, optionally. After what expresses the sense of much or little, when it is a doer, that is, in the sense of those whose case-endings are doers, śas optionally comes: phabuhūni (glosses: the suffix śas; once), behuśaḥ; with bhil, bahubhiḥ, with śas, bahuśaḥ; with bhyas, bahubhyāḥ, with śas, bahuśaḥ; with sub, bahuṣuḥ, with śas, bahuśaḥ. Likewise, bhurīśaḥ (bhurīn and the rest), and albyaśaḥ (albyaṃ), stakaśaḥ (stakaṃ), and so on.

"Having a doer" means that if it does not have a case-ending of a doer (glosses: many; by the many; by the many; from the many; to the many; from the many; to the many), it does not come: (gloss: to the many) bahūnāṃsvāmī.

saṃ (glosses: to the small; to the small) khyaikabaca (gloss: to the few) nāccapipmāyāṃ: Also after a number in the singular, for wishing to obtain. When a number word is expressed in the singular, śas also comes in the sense of wishing to obtain: in the sense of dvaudvaudehi, with śas, dviśaḥdehi. Likewise (gloss: the chief of the many), with śas, triśaḥdehi.

pratiyogedañcamyāstasi: In construction with prati, after the fifth, tasi. From a construction with brati, tasi comes in the sense of the fifth case-ending: in the sense of bāsudebātbrati, bāsudebataḥ (glosses: give two each!; prati). ādimadhyātta (gloss: give two!) pṛṣṭhapārśādeśca: After ādi and madhya, ta (gloss: give three!); and also after pṛṣṭha, pārśā, pārśā and the rest. After ādi and madhya, ta comes in the sense of the fifth, and it also comes after priṣṭhabārśā (gloss: separately from the son of Vasudeva) and the rest (glosses: in tasi, the i is for pronunciation; separately from the son of Vasudeva): ādita (gloss: from the first), madhyata (gloss: from the middle), bṛśṭhata (gloss: from the rear), bṛṣṭhata (gloss: from the rear), pārṣata.

apādānacāhīyaruhoḥ: And in the source, from what is not hīya or ruha. In the sense of the fifth that expresses a source not construed with hīya, that is, the root ohāka, or with ruha, tasi also comes: with ṅas, grāmādāyati, grāmātaḥāyati; with spyas, caurebhyobaṃbheti, with tasi, caurataḥbibheti, with tasi, caurataḥbibhete. Examples in which tasi does not come in construction with hāka and ruha are these: with ṅasi, sārthātahite; with ṅasi, parbatādabarohahi.

abhutatabbhabe kṛbhvastiyoge saṃpadyakarttari cviḥ: When what has not come to be comes to be, in construction with kṛ, bhū and asti (glosses: came from the village; in tasaṃ, the i is for pronunciation), for the agent of being accomplished (gloss: is afraid of the thieves), cvi. When the agent of being accomplished is expressed (glosses: connected with time; excels in that aim; descends from it), in the sense of making what has not come to be come to be, cī comes in construction with kṛ, bhū and asti.

asyacvau: Of a, before cvi. When the suffix cvi follows, a stem ending in the letter a has it become ī. berlopaḥ: Elision of bi. Of the suffix ci: after the ca has been removed by the rule "cuṭu of the nature of a suffix," the remaining pi is also elided: in the sense of akṛṣṇaḥkṛṣṇaḥ saṃpadyate garoti, kṛṣṇī karoti (gloss: makes white what is not white). In the sense of abrahmabrahdmasaṃpadyatebhabati, with ci, brahmābhabati. Making the phrasing like that: matrikaroti. In the sense of agadgāgadgāsaṃpadyatesya, gadgīkaroti (glosses: the black that was not black; makes it accomplished; to kṛḍṇā, cī, the ca removed, the baṃ elided, the sa removed, and by "of a, before cī," a becomes ī). agāḥgārgyaḥsaṃbadyakaroti (gloss: what was not Brahmā became Brahmā in full): in the sense of that, (gloss: to gārgya, cvi) karoti (gloss: became Brahmā).

kyacvauca (glosses: to matri, cvi, that is, khyi, rī is due, ṛ dī nī removed; makes into a mother; what was not so before became the Gaṅgā in full; became gadgā): Also before kya and cvi. When the suffixes kya and cvi follow (gloss: makes one who is not the son of the sage Garga into the son of Garga), the letter ya stacked with a hal at the end of a stem or root is elided: gārgīkaroti.

cvauca: Also before cvi. When cvi follows, if the stem-final is a letter of the abbreviation ik, it becomes long: to śuci, ci, śucībhabati (glosses: became pure; became pure); to baṭu, cī, baṭūsyāta (gloss: will become learned).

Quoted in the commentary: abyayasyetvadīrghaunetikecita: For the indeclinables (gloss: is to be made the son of Garga), the i and the long do not occur, according to some. If it belongs to the class of indeclinables, then when cvi follows, some do not make the a into ī, the ik long, and so on: with cvi, dibāsyātya; with cvi, svastisyāta.

arutmanaścakcaścetorahorjasvaṃlopaśca: The elision of arus, manas, cakṣus, cetas, rahas and rajas. The final letter sa of these, arus and the rest, is elided when cvi follows: arūkaroti (gloss: a wound came about), arūbhabati (glosses: makes a wound; became day; may it be well!), arūshata (gloss: became a wound). Likewise unmanī, uccakṣū, bicitī, barahī, mirajī, and so on; to these, the joining of akaroti, bhabati, syāt and the rest is to be applied by analogy.

bibhāṣā sātikā kṣsva (glosses: cvi removed, ik long; cvi removed, ik long): For completeness, sāti, optionally. In the domain of cvi connected with the sense of completeness (glosses: cvi removed, ik long; sorrowful; eyes turned up; perverted mind; desirous of attachment; dustless), sāti optionally comes.

sātba dādyoḥ: Of sāta, and of the beginning of a word. Even if a letter that is a cause of sa becoming ṣa is present before it, the letter sa at the beginning of another word, which is no part of the word itself, and the sa of the suffix sāti, do not become ṣa. An example of its not occurring at the beginning of another word: dadhisañcatvi. In the sense of kṛtknaṃ śastraṃ agniḥ saṃbatyate karota, agnisātaṃkaroti, or agnikaroti.

abhibidhausaṃpadāca: In complete pervasion, also with saṃbada. In the sense of complete pervasion, sāti also comes in construction with kṛ, bhū, asti and saṃpada (glosses: pours out curd; the weapon is made completely and fully of fire): with sāti, agnisātsaṃpadyati (glosses: completes it with fire; completes it with fire); with sāti, agnisātkaroti; with sāti, abnisātabhabati; with sārti, agnisātsyata.

tadadhinabacane: In expressing its servants. In the sense of expressing its servants, sāti comes in construction with kraṃ, bhū, asti and saṃbada (gloss: pervades it fully with fire): rājñaḥadhinakaroti (glosses: makes it the king's servants; pervades it with fire; came to be pervaded by fire; became pervaded by fire); in that sense, with sāti, rājasātkaroti (gloss: makes it the king's servants). Likewise, with sāti, rājasātabhabati (gloss: became the king's servant); with sāti, rājasātsyata; with sāti, rātsaṃpadyati.

deyitrāca: For what is to be given, trā too. In the sense of explicitly stating the master of what is to be given to someone for his sake, trā comes in construction with kṛ, bhū, asti and saṃpada, and by the word "too," sāti also comes: in the sense of bibrādhināṃdekaroti (glosses: became the king's servant; makes it fully the king's servants), with trā, bipratrākaroti; with sāti, piprasātkaroti. Likewise, with trā, bipratrābhabati; with sāti, bibrasātabhabati; with trā, bibrasātabhabati; with trā, bibratrāsyāta; with sāti, biprasātsyata; bipratrāsaṃpabyati, bibratrāsaṃpabyati, bibra (gloss: makes it a gift that depends on the brahmins) sātsaṃpadyati.

debamanubyapuruṣapurumartyebhyodvitīyāsabhamyorbahulaṃ: From deba, manuṣya (gloss: makes it a gift that depends on the brahmins), puruṣa, puru and martya (glosses: a gift that depends on the brahmins came about; it became a gift that depends on the brahmins; it became a gift that depends on the brahmins; a gift that depends on the brahmins is accomplished), in the second and the seventh, variously. After these, deba and the rest, in the sense of the second and seventh case-endings, variously, that is, in construction with kṛ, bhā, asti and saṃda, and also in construction with others that are not these, trā comes: debānagacchati, debatrāgacchati; debeṣugacchati, debatrāgacchati. Likewise, manuṣyatrā, buruṣatrā, purutrā, martyatrā.

abyaktānukaraṇādnekāco nitaunartraca: From the imitation of what is indistinct, from what is not of a single ac, when there is no iti, ḍāca. From a stem imitating an indistinct sound (gloss: goes to the gods) that is not of a single aca (gloss: goes to the gods), in construction with kṛ, bhū (glosses: to humans; to men; to the ancient ones) and asti, when there is no iti, ḍāca comes: baṭatbaṭat (glosses: ṭāca; the ca for the purpose of blocking the accent; with ḍita, the ṭi removed). For what is called paṭatpaṭā: tasyaparamāmraiḍitaṃ: Of that, the latter in repetition. When a single stem is set down repeated twice or more, as in paṭatpaṭat, the end of the former stem also takes the form of the latter.

nityaṃāmreḍetiḍāci: In repetition, always, before ḍāca. When, as just explained, a single stem is repeated twice and ḍāca follows, it always takes the form of what follows: the vowelless ta and the following ba merge and become a single ba, giving baṭpaṭākaroti. By "not of a single aca," the counter-example is śratkati; by "when there is no iti," baṭitikaroti (gloss: makes this cloth).

kṛño dvitīyatritīyaśambābījā tkiṣau: Of kṛña, from dītīya, tṛtīya, śasba and bīja, for digging. In construction with kṛña, after these, dītīya and the rest (gloss: makes it into cloth), in the sense of digging, that is, ploughing a field, ḍāca (glosses: to have faith; to baṭat, iti, and the at of the imitation of the indistinct has become i) comes: in the sense of, with ḍāca, dvitīyaṃkarṣaṇaṃkaroti, with ḍāca, dvitīyākaroti. Likewise, with ḍāca, tṛtāṃyā (gloss: ploughs three times); śasmā; with ḍāca, bījā (gloss: ploughs in the seed).

saṃkhyāyāścaguṇāntāyāḥ: Also from a number ending in guṇa. After what has a number word first and guṇa at the end (gloss: digs twice, or ploughs twice), too, in construction with kṛña (glosses: ploughs twice; the sense of first ploughing once lengthwise and then ploughing again crosswise; the sense of first sowing the seed and then ploughing again), in the sense of ploughing a field, ḍāca comes: in the sense of dviguṇaṃkarṣaṇaṃkaroti, with ḍāca, dīguṇākaroti.

samayācca yāpanāyāṃ: From samaya too, for causing to reach. From samaya too, in the sense of causing to reach, in construction with kṛña, ḍāca comes: in the sense of samayaṃyāpanākaroti (gloss: ploughs twofold), with ḍāca, samayākaroti (gloss: ploughs twofold).

sapatraniṣpatrātibyathane: From sapatra and niṣpatra, for great agitation. From sapatra and niṣpatra, in the sense of great agitation, in construction with kṛña (gloss: makes it reach its time), ḍāca comes: in the sense of sapatraṃ jaraṃ mṛgakāye brabeśayati (gloss: makes it reach its time), with ḍāca, sabatrākaroti mṛgaṃ. Likewise (gloss: the arrow's feathers did not go through, because of the armor), in the sense of niṣpatraṃśaraṃmaparaṃnirgamayatikabacena, with ḍāca, niṣpatrākarotikabacena (glosses: the armor keeps the feathers from going through; with an arrow, feathers and all, pierces the body of the deer).

niṣkulānnikoṣaṇe: From niṣku (gloss: pierces the deer, feathers and all) la, for being without a sheath. From niṣkula, in the sense of being without the sheath that lies inside, ḍāca comes in construction with kṛña: in the sense of niṣāśayatidāḍimaṃ, niṣkulākarotidāḍimaṃ.

sukhabriyādānulomye: From sukha and briya, for conformity.

After sukha and briya, in expressing conformity, ḍāca comes in construction with kṛña: with ḍāca, sukhākaroti; with ḍāca, priyākaroti.

duḥkhātbratilomye (gloss: strips the husk from the pomegranate): From duḥkha (gloss: strips the husk from the pomegranate), for non-conformity. After duḥkha, in expressing non-conformity, ḍāca comes in construction with kṛña: with ḍāca, duḥkhākaroti.

śulātbāke: From śūl, for (glosses: makes it agreeable; makes it pleasing) cooking. After śūla, in expressing cooking, ḍāca comes in construction with kṛña: in the sense of śūlenpacati, śūlākaroti.

satyādaśapathe: From satya, for what is not (gloss: makes it disagreeable and makes it painful) an oath. After satya, in another sense that is not an oath, ḍāca comes in construction with kṛña: in the sense of satyenakretabyaṃ, with ḍāca, batyākaroti.

madrātba (gloss: cooks it on an iron spit) ribābaṇi: From madrag (gloss: cooks it on an iron spit), for shaving the hair. After mahra, in expressing shaving the hair, ḍāca comes in construction with kṛña: in the sense of matraṃparibāpanaṃkaroti, with ḍāca, matrākaroti.

bhadrācca (gloss: makes a bargain by truth): From bhada too. (Gloss: makes a bargain by truth.) After bhadra too, in expressing shaving the hair, ḍāca comes in construction with kṛña: bhadrākaroti. Words ending in the suffixes ci, bati and ḍāca are also indeclinables.

atipāṇinibyākaraṇa (gloss: having shaved the hair, makes it good, that is, the sense of practicing the Dharma) syasūtrāttatthitapratyā (gloss: makes it good) yāsāmāptaḥ. So it says: from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the taddhita suffixes are complete.

Thus (gloss: makes it good), from the work called The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, in which the meaning, procedures, examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, are set down as notes, the rough identification of the taddhita suffixes, together with their domains of application, is for the time being complete.

Now I shall explain a few miscellaneous points of usage.

nityabipsayoḥ: In the wish to pervade, always. When it applies to the wish to pervade, whatever word is spoken always takes a double form: bacatipacatibhuktāṃ, uccaisuccaistiṣṭhati, bṛkṣaṃ bṛkṣaṃ sañcati, grāmogrāmormaṇīyaḥ.

barerbarjane: Of bari, for exclusion. In construction with a word that applies to exclusion, the word bari is doubled: pariparipaṃgebhyoḥbṛṣṭo bṛṣṭo debaḥ.

ubaryadtyadhasaḥ sāmībye: Of ubari (glosses: having cooked and cooked, eats; stays higher and higher; sprinkles tree after tree; plays from village to village), adgi and adhas, in proximity. When these, ubari and the rest, apply to proximity in village and in time, they take a double form (gloss: the god rained, except on those that are not the sky): upariuparigrāma, adhiarhisukhaṃ, adhoñdhobarbataṃ.

bākyāderāmaṃtritasyāsūyā saṃmatikopakutsanabhartsanaṣu: In anger, contempt and ugliness, and in not bearing to understand and in approval, the first word addressed in calling out. When anger, contempt and ugliness (glosses: the village above and above; more and more happiness; the mountain below and below) are expressed, and in not bearing to understand, that is, being unable to understand unless it is said twice or more, and in approval, the first word addressed in calling out takes a double form: hesundarahasundara tepṛthāsaundaryaṃ, which is harsh speech; hedepahedebatvāṃ bandāosi, which is approval; durbinītadurbinīte dānāṃjñabi, which is anger; hedhūnuṣgahedhūnuṣkabyarthaṃtedhanuḥ, which is contempt; and hecaurahecorabhā tayiṣyamitvāṃ (gloss: O handsome one, O handsome one, what use is your handsomeness?), which is ugliness (gloss: O god, O god, I praise you, bowing to you). So it is with these.

ekaṃpahubrīhibata (glosses: O ill-behaved one, O ill-behaved one, that has been found out; O archer, O archer, your bow is useless): Eka is like a much-grain (bahuvrīhi) compound. (Gloss: O thief, O thief, go away!) When eka is doubled in the wish to pervade, it is like a bahuvrīhi compound, that is, the case-ending of the first eka is elided: ekaikaṃkṣaraṃ.

ābādheca: In complete harm, too. In construction with complete harm, that is, harm that has become an enemy of the mind, a double form arises: gatagataḥ.

prakāreguṇabacanasya: For a kind, of a quality word. In making a kind understood, a quality word (gloss: one letter each, or one by one) takes a double form: paṭupaṭuḥ, mūlemūlesthūla.

Quoted in the commentary: krimāsamabhihareca: For the complete carrying-off (gloss: gone, gone) of an action. In expressing the complete carrying-off of a verb, it takes a double form: lunīdilunīhi.

Again, quoted in the commentary (glosses: learned, learned; thick at the root, at the root): karmabyatihāresrbanamnodvestaḥ: When an action is done reciprocally, a doubling of the rbanāmas. In making understood that an action is done reciprocally, the rbanāmas take a double form.

samā (gloss: cuts, cuts) sabacca bahulaṃ: Variously, like a compound. For what is expressed in double form, variously, as with a compound, the elision or non-elision of the case-ending of the first member, the shortening of feminine suffixes, and so on, are also to be done: with su, anyoñnyaṃbipānamanti; with su, anyoñnyebhajayanti.

Quoted in the commentary: itaraśabdasyanityaṃsamābata: The word itara is always like a compound. When the word itara is made into a double form, it is always to be treated like a compound: itaretaraṃ.

Again quoted in the commentary (glosses: the brahmins pay homage to one another; they feed one another): strīnbuṃskayorupadasyabāāmabhābobācyaḥ: After the feminine and the neuter, the latter word is optionally stated as having the nature of āma. When a feminine or neuter gender, not a masculine one, follows (gloss: the other and the other), the end of the latter part of the preceding word that has become doubled optionally becomes ām: anyoñnyāṃstrī (gloss: women, one another), barsbarīnabuṃsakaṃ (gloss: neuter, each beyond the other), anyoñnyāmimeprāhmaṇaubhojayataḥ (gloss: these two brahmin women feed one another); or (gloss: one another, or the other and the other) anyoñnyaṃ, and so on.

iti pāṇinivyākaraṇasya sūtrābhvo ruktāssamābtāḥ. That is: from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the rules on stating twice are complete.

With these, the broad sections explaining the ancillary topic of words stated twice, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, notes that set down the meaning of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, its procedures, its illustrative examples and so on, are complete for the time being.

Homage to the guru and to the glorious Lord of Secrets, Vajrapāṇi.

Having thus finished explaining all the operations of sup, namely the forming of the six genders into words, the class of indeclinables taught in broad outline, the suffixes that form the feminine, the chapter on kāraka, the four compounds, and the taddhita suffixes, together with incidental and ancillary topics, I shall now explain the second section of endings, the operations of tiṅ, by which words are formed from roots. As it says at the beginning of the commentary:

bṛkratiḥ sājalatyādyā yayā dhātvādirūbayā
vyajyaṃte śabdarūpāṇi parabatyayasaṃnidheḥ

In Tibetan this is:

Of that first, the sovereign, intrinsic nature,
Whatever forms there are, the roots and the rest,
The forms of words that make them clear
Are joined with the suffixes that follow.

So it appears, and it means this: in the beginning, through the power of the compassion and aspirations of the victors by intrinsic nature, the Buddha and others, words and so on joined with following suffixes came about, in order to form whatever bases are to be expressed, the roots and the rest, into forms that make that sound clear and show the meaning of what is expressed.

dhātoḥ: from a root. When a root stands before, then in order to form that root into a word, the endings laṭ and the rest are applied after it. This shows the domain of application of the endings ti and the rest.

If one asks what laṭ and the rest are, they are laṭ, liṭ, luṭ, lṛṭ, loṭ, laṅ, liṅ, luṅ, the benedictive liṅ, and lṛṅ. Of these, the five from laṭ to loṭ are called ṭ-marked, and the five from laṅ to lṛṅ are called ṅ-marked.

vartamāne laṭ: laṭ for the present. Of those ten l's, laṭ comes after a root to express a present action.

aṭāvitau: a and ṭ are markers. The letter ṭ of laṭ and the letter a, the vowel of la, are called markers (it), that is, they are dropped.

tibtastīsipthasthamibbasmastātāṃjhalṅāsāthāṃdhvamiṭbahimahiṅ: tiba tas jhi sib thas tha mib bas mas ta ātāṃ jhaṃ thās āthāṃ dhvaṃ aṭi bahi mahiṅ. Just as the ṭ and the a of laṭ are removed, once the markers of all ten l's have been removed, the vowelless l's become these eighteen, tip and the rest.

laḥ barasmaipadaṃ: the l's are parasmaipada. The first nine replacements of the letter l, tip and the rest, are parasmaipada, that is, they are called words for an action done for the sake of another.

tadānābātmanebadaṃ: taṅ and āna are ātmanepada. As for taṅ, the nine replacements of the vowelless l, from ta up to ṅ, and āna, that is, the suffixes of the kṛt class and so on, śānac and kānac, are ātmanepada, that is, they are called words for an action done for the sake of the self.

śeṣātgartare barasmaibadaṃ: from the remainder, parasmaipada for the agent. The remainder, those that are not words for the sake of the self, namely the nine, tip and the rest, are called parasmaipada, that is, words for an action done for the sake of someone other than the agent.

anudāttadi ātmanebadaṃ: ātmanepada for those with anudātta and those that are ṅit. Whatever roots have anudātta, that is, a vowel of low pitch as a marker, and whatever roots are ṅit, that is, have ṅ as a marker, take ātmanepada, that is, the endings of words for the sake of the self; they are called roots for one's own benefit.

svaritañicca ubhe: for those with svarita and those that are ñit, both. Roots that have svarita, that is, sounds of middle pitch as markers, and those that are ñit, that is, have the letter ñ as a marker, apply both to one's own benefit and to the benefit of others, and so they are called roots of both.

śeṣe barsmaibadaṃ: the remainder are parasmaipada. Those that are not the roots with anudātta, with ṅ as a marker, with svarita, or with ñ as a marker explained above, that is, the remaining ones once those are set aside, are called roots for the benefit of others.

tiṅ strīṇi triṇi prathamamḍbyamottamā: the triads of tiṅ are the first, the middle, and the last. Tiṅ is an abbreviation (pratyāhāra) running from ti up to ṅ. Of those eighteen, the nine ātmanepada and the nine parasmaipada each stand in groups of three: the first three are the first person, the middle three the middle person, and the last three the last person.

tānyekavacan dvivacan bahuvacanānyekaśaḥ: each of these is singular, dual, and plural. Each of those groups of three, tip and the rest, also has a singular, a dual, and a plural.

śiṣe pramaḥ: for the remainder, the first. Of the three persons of tip and the rest, first, middle, and last: when the accompanying word (upapada), that is, the word placed first, is neither yuṣmad nor asmad, then whatever remaining word, these two excluded, the root is joined with, the three of the first person apply. This is the general rule.

yuṣmadyupades mādhikaraṇe sthāninyapi madhyamaḥ: when yuṣmad is the accompanying word and has the same substratum, even when it is merely present, the middle. When yuṣmad stands as the accompanying word and has the same substratum, the three of the middle person apply to the root joined with it.

asmadyuttama: with asmad, the last. If the accompanying word is asmad, the last persons apply to the root joined with it.

Having thus explained their domain of application, I shall now explain their procedures. To the root bhū, "in the sense of being," laṭ is added by the rule "laṭ for the present."

tiṅśitsārvadhātukaṃ: tiṅ and the ś-marked are "pertaining to all roots" (sārvadhātuka). To ti and the rest, and to the intermediate suffixes that have ś as a marker and are applied, the technical name "endings pertaining to all roots" is given.

kartari śab: śap for the agent.

When the endings designated "pertaining to all roots" follow, śap comes after the root in the sense of the agent. Śap is given. As for laṭ, its a and ṭ are markers, so they are removed, and the l is changed to tip. By the rule "the final consonant," the p is removed. The letters ś and p are called markers, so they are removed: bhū a ti.

sārvabhatukārdhādhātukayoḥ: before those pertaining to all roots and those pertaining to half the roots. When the suffixes called "pertaining to all roots," or those called "pertaining to half the roots" (ārdhadhātuka), which will come below, follow, then if the root that is the domain of those endings has at its end a letter of the abbreviation ik, it changes to guṇa: bhavati, "exists." This is the singular of the first person.

For the dual: "the two exist," bhavataḥ. For the plural, the l is changed to jhi: bhū a jhi. ttoñntaḥ: anta in place of jha. The vowelless letter jh at the beginning of the endings ti and the rest becomes anta: bhavanti, "they exist."

For the middle persons too, forming them as above: bhavasi, "exists"; "the two exist," bhavathaḥ; "they exist." To bhū, laṭ; l into tas; śap; guṇa; s into ru; visarga. patha.

For the last persons too, up to the point where bhū becomes bhava, it is the same as the previous ones. To bhū, laṭ; l into jhi; from jha the i is taken out; jha is drawn into anta; guṇa; by "ay and av for ec" and so on; guṇa of a; of both, it went into the form of the former. bhava, mip. To bhū, laṭ, śap, guṇa; the l becomes sip and thas.

atodārghoyañi: lengthening of a before yañ. When a suffix or an ending called "pertaining to all roots" that begins with a letter of the abbreviation yañ follows, the final letter a becomes long: bhavāmi, "exists." Forming the dual and the plural in the same way: bhavāvaḥ, "the two exist"; bhavāmaḥ, "they exist."

Joined with their companion words, these are: with su, saḥ bhavati; with au, tau bhavataḥ; with jas, te bhavanti: the first person. And with su, tvaṃ bhavasi. To bhū, laṭ, śap; l into mip, the p a marker; guṇa and so on: bhava; by this sūtra, lengthening. To bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes vas and mas; guṇa and so on; by this sūtra, lengthening. With au, yuvāṃ bhavathaḥ; with jas, yūyaṃ bhavatha: the middle person. And with su, ā "he exists" haṃ bhavāmi; "those two exist"; "they exist"; with au, vā bhavāvaḥ; with jas, vayaṃ bha "you exist" vāma. These are the last persons, and they are the words for the sake of another.

Cited in the commentary: bhū prābtāvātmanepadi ("you two exist," "you all exist"): bhū in the sense of obtaining is ātmanepada. The root bhū also applies in the sense of obtaining ("I exist"), and in that case the endings ("we two exist," "we all exist") of the ātmanepada apply. To bhū, laṭ; l becomes ta; śap: bhapata.

ṭitaḥ vatmanepadānīṭiri: e in place of the ṭi of the ātmanepada of the ṭ-marked. The final ṭi of the ātmanepada of the ṭ-marked l's, laṭ and the rest, becomes the letter e: bhavate. For the dual: to bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes ātām; ṭi becomes e: bhava āte.

sārvadhātukamapat: what pertains to all roots and is not p-marked. Among those called "pertaining to all roots," the other endings, those that are not p-marked, that is, the ones left once those are set aside, are, as the need requires, given the technical name "ṅ-marked."

āto ṅitaḥ: of the ā of the ṅ-marked. If the first letter of the endings called ṅ-marked that follow something ending in the letter a, such as bhava before them, is the letter ā, that letter becomes iy: "the two obtain," bhavete. For the plural, a does not become i either, and forming the rest as above: bhrabante, "they obtain." These are the first persons of the ātmanepada.

For the middle persons: to bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes thās: bhava thās. thāsaḥseḥ. To bhū, laṭ, śap; after the markers are removed, l becomes ātām; by the rule "of the ṭ-marked," ṭi becomes e; by "of the ā of the ṅ-marked," ā becomes iy; by "elision of v and y before val," the y is removed; guṇa. To bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes jha; from jha the a is taken out, and jha becomes anta; by the rule "of the ṭ-marked," the ṭi; by "guṇa after a" and "for both, the form of the former." Se in place of thās: the thās that replaces a ṭ-marked l becomes se. To bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes thās; by "se in place of thās," thās becomes se: bhavase, "obtains." For the dual: bhavethe, "the two obtain." For the plural: "they obtain," bhavadhe.

For the singular of the last person: bhave, "obtains." For the dual: bhavāhe, "the two obtain." To bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes vahi; by "lengthening of a before yañ," the a is lengthened; by "ṭ-marked" and so on, the ṭi becomes e. To bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes āthām; by the rule "the ātmanepada of the ṭ-marked," ṭi becomes e; by "of the ā of the ṅ-marked," ā becomes iy; by "elision of v and y before val," it is removed; guṇa. To bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes dhvam; by the rule "the ātmanepada of the ṭ-marked," ṭi becomes e. To bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes iṭ, which is called ṭ-marked; by the rule "ṭ-marked," ṭi becomes e; by "guṇa after a" and "for both, the form of the latter." For the plural: "they obtain," bhavāmahe. To bhū, laṭ, śap; l becomes mahiṅ, the ṅ serving the abbreviation; by "before yañ," lengthening; by "ṭ-marked" and so on, ṭi becomes e.

vidhinimaṃtraṇāmantraṇādhīṣṭasaṃpraśnaprārthaneṣu liṅ: liṅ for enjoining a procedure, binding invitation, general invitation, entreaty, courteous inquiry, and request. In these cases, enjoining a procedure and the rest, liṅ comes after a root in the sense of the action. To bhū, liṅ; śap; the purpose of ṅit; the i is for the sake of pronunciation; by "tip, tas" and so on, the l becomes tip: bhava tip.

yāsuṭ parasmaivadeṣūdātto ṅicca: for the parasmaipada, yāsuṭ, which is also an udātta marked with ṅ. To the parasmaipada endings that replace liṅ the augment (āgama) yāsuṭ is given, and that yāsuṭ is named "a ṅ-marked udātta."

na ṅicca: nor is it ṅ-marked. The yāsuṭ that was named above "a ṅ-marked udātta" is called ṅ-marked while it remains yāsuṭ itself, but when that yāsuṭ changes into another form, such as iy, it is not called ṅ-marked.

bhava; to tip, yāsuṭ; the ṭ serves to fix its position, and the u is for the sake of pronunciation: bhapa yās ti.

liṅaḥ slopoñntasya: elision of an s of liṅ that is not final. The letter s that is not final in the endings called "pertaining to all roots" that replace liṅ is elided.

bhava yā ti.

itaśca: of the i as well. The i of the parasmaipada replacements of the ṅ-marked l's is also elided: the i of ti is removed.

atoyeyaḥ: after a, iy in place of yā. The initial letter yā of the endings called "pertaining to all roots" that follow something ending in a, such as bhava, becomes iy. By "elision of v and y before val," the y too is removed: bhavet.

For the dual: to bhū, liṅ, śap; l becomes tas; yāsuṭ: bhab yā tsa. tasthasthamephāṃtāṃtaṃtāmaḥ: for tas, thas, tha, and mip, tām, tam, ta, and am. The tas, thas, tha, and mip that replace the l of the four called ṅ-marked, liṅ and the rest, become tām, tam, ta, and am respectively. Tas becomes tām: bhava yātā. Yā becomes iy: bhavetāṃ. By "of v and y," the y is removed; guṇa.

For the plural: bhū, śap, yā, jhi. jhirjus: jus in place of jhi. The jhi that replaces liṅ becomes jus: bhaveyuḥ. To bhū, liṅ, śap; l becomes jhi; yāsuṭ, the ṭ serving to fix its position and the u for the sake of pronunciation; by "a non-final s of liṅ," the s is removed. By "after a, iy in place of yā"; by this sūtra, jha becomes jus; by "cu and ṭu" and so on, the j is removed; the y is drawn in; s becomes ru; r becomes visarga; sandhi.

For the singular of the middle person of liṅ: bhaveḥ. For the dual of the middle person of liṅ: mabhavetaṃ. For the plural of the middle person of liṅ: bhave. To bhū, liṅ, śap; l becomes sip, the p serving to make it p-marked; yāsuṭ; ṭ and u are removed; by "after a, iy in place of yā"; by "elision of v and y before val," s and y are removed; guṇa; by "of the i as well," the i, the vowel of s, is removed; s becomes ru, its u for the sake of pronunciation; r becomes visarga. To bhū, śap, liṅ; l becomes thas; yāsuṭ; both letters of suṭ are removed; after a, yā becomes iy; by "v and y" and so on, it is removed; sandhi; by "for tas, thas, tha, and mip," thas becomes tam. ta.

For the singular of the last person of liṅ: bhaveyaṃ. To bhū, śap; liṅ, its l becoming mip; yāsuṭ; suṭ removed; after a, yā becomes iy; guṇa; by "for tas, thas, tha, and mip, tām, tam, ta, and am," mip becomes am; the y is drawn in.

For the dual of the last person of liṅ: bhū, śap, yāsuṭ; liṅ, its l becoming vas. Yā. To bhū, śap, liṅ, its l becoming tha; yāsuṭ; suṭ removed; yā becomes iy; by "v and y" and so on, the y is removed; sandhi; by "for tas, thas, tha, and mip, tām, tam, ta, and am," tha becomes ta; iy; by "v and y" and so on, the y is removed. bhavebas.

nityaṃ ṅitaḥ: always, for the ṅ-marked. The final vowelless letter s of the replacements of the ṅ-marked, liṅ and the rest, is always elided: the s of vas is removed: bhaveva.

For the plural of the last person of liṅ: bhavema. To bhū, śap, liṅ; l becomes mas; by "always, for the ṅ-marked," the s is removed; yāsuṭ; suṭ removed; after a, yā becomes iy; by "elision of v and y before val," the y is removed; sandhi. These are the parasmaipada.

For "bhū in the sense of obtaining," the ātmanepada apply. Here too the procedure, such as bhū becoming bhava once śap is given to it, is like the previous ones. As for the replacement of the endings and so on: for the singular of the first person, to bhava, liṅ; l becomes ta: bhava ta. liṅaḥ sīyuṭ: sīyuṭ for liṅ. To the endings that replace liṅ in the ātmanepada the augment sīyuṭ is given: bhaveta. To bhava, liṅ; its markers removed; l becomes ta; by this sūtra, the augment sīyuṭ, the ṭ serving to fix its position and the u for the sake of pronunciation; by "elision of a non-final s of liṅ," the s is removed; by "elision of v and y before val," the y is removed; sandhi.

For the dual of the first person of the ātmanepada of liṅ: bhaveyātāṃ. To bhava, liṅ; l becomes ātām; sīyuṭ; ṭ and u removed; s also removed; sandhi, and the y drawn in.

For the plural of the first person of the ātmanepada of liṅ: jhasyaran: ran in place of jha. The ātmanepada jha that replaces liṅ becomes ran: bhaveran. To bhava, liṅ; l becomes jha; by this sūtra jha becomes ran; sīyuṭ; ṭ and u removed; by "elision of v and y before val," the y is removed; sandhi.

For the three middle persons of the ātmanepada of liṅ: bhavathāḥ. To bhava, liṅ; l becomes thās; the augment sīyuṭ; ṭ and u removed; by "elision before val," the y too is removed; by "a non-final s of liṅ," the s too is removed; sandhi. bhaveyāthāṃ. To bhava, liṅ; l becomes āthām; sīyuṭ; ṭ and u removed; by "a non-final s of liṅ," the s is removed; sandhi; the y drawn in. bhavadhāṃ. To bhava, liṅ; l becomes dhvam; the augment sīyuṭ; ṭ and u removed; by "elision before val," the y too is removed; by "a non-final s of liṅ," the s too is removed; sandhi.

For the singular of the last person of liṅ: iṭotra: at in place of iṭ. The iṭ that replaces liṅ becomes at; the letter t serves the purpose of "a vowel marked with t denotes its own duration": bhavaya. To bhava, liṅ; l becomes iṭ; by this sūtra iṭ becomes at; sīyuṭ; ṭ and u removed; by "a non-final s of liṅ," the s is removed; sandhi; the y drawn in.

For the dual and the plural of the last person of liṅ: bhavera hi. To bhava, liṅ; l becomes vahi; sīyuṭ; ṭ and u removed; by "elision before val," the y too is removed; by "a non-final s of liṅ," the s is removed; sandhi. bhavemahi. To bhava, liṅ; l becomes mahiṅ, the ṅ serving the abbreviation; sīyuṭ; ṭ and u removed; by "elision before val," the y too is removed; by "a non-final s of liṅ," the s is removed; sandhi.

These, together with their domains of application and their changes, are what the Kalāpa calls saptamī.

loṭca: loṭ as well. For enjoining a procedure, binding invitation, general invitation, entreaty, courteous inquiry, and request, not only does liṅ come after a root in the sense of the action, but loṭ comes as well.

āśṣiliṅloṭau: for a wish, liṅ and loṭ. In the sense of an action of wishing or of blessing, too, loṭ and the benedictive liṅ, which will come below, come after a root.

eruḥ: u in place of i. The letters i of the endings that replace loṭ become the letter u. Bhū becoming bhava once śap is given to bhū in the sense of the agent, and the rest, are like the previous ones: bhabtu. To bhava, loṭ; the ṭ is a marker; the o is for the sake of pronunciation; l becomes tip; the purpose of the p; by this sūtra, i becomes u.

tuhyostātadāśiṣyanyatarasyāṃ: for tu and hi, in a blessing, tātaṅ optionally.

When the tu and hi that replace loṭ are given not in the sense of enjoining a procedure and the rest, but in the sense of blessing or wishing, they optionally become tātaṅ: bhavatāta. To bhava, by "for a wish, liṅ and loṭ," loṭ; after its markers are removed, l becomes tip, the p serving to make it p-marked; by "u in place of i," tu; by this sūtra, tu becomes tātaṅ; the ṅ serves to make it ṅ-marked, and the a of ta is for the sake of pronunciation. bhavatu. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes tip; by "u in place of i," tu.

For the dual of the first person of the parasmaipada of loṭ: loṭ larabata: loṭ is like laṅ. In some cases among the operations of loṭ, forms are made just as with laṅ.
