For example, take a tas that replaces loṭ: the rule "for tas, thas, tha, and mip, tām, tam, ta, and am" speaks in the commentary of the ṅ-marked, so although loṭ is not ṅ-marked, by this sūtra, "like laṅ," tas becomes tām. bhavatāṃ. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes tas; by "loṭ is like laṅ," tas becomes tām.

For the plural of the first person of the parasmaipada of loṭ: bhavantu. Bhava; loṭ; l becomes jhi; from jha the i is taken out; by "anta in place of jha," it becomes anta; by "u in place of i," the i becomes u; by "guṇa after a" and "for both, one, the form of the former," it took that form; anta is drawn to the u.

For the singular of the middle person of the parasmaipada of loṭ: serhyalicca: hi in place of si, and it is not p-marked. The sip that replaces loṭ becomes hi, and it is moreover given the technical designation "not p-marked." atoheḥ: after a, the elision of hi. The letter hi that replaces loṭ, following the letter a as in bhava, is elided: bhava. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes sip; by "hi in place of si, and it is not p-marked," si becomes hi; by this sūtra, hi is removed. Or else: bhavatāta. To bhava, loṭ; sip; by "hi in place of si, and it is not p-marked," si becomes hi; by "for tu and hi, in a blessing, tātaṅ optionally," hi becomes tātaṅ; here the ṅ serves to prevent guṇa, and the a of ta is for the sake of pronunciation.

For the dual and the plural of the middle person of the parasmaipada of loṭ: bhavataṃ. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes thas; by "loṭ is like laṅ," thas becomes tam. bhavata. Bhava; loṭ; l becomes tha; by "loṭ is like laṅ," tha becomes ta.

For the singular of the last person of the parasmaipada of loṭ: methniḥ: ni in place of mi. The mi that replaces loṭ, that is, mip, becomes ni. āḍuttamasyabicca: āṭ for the last, and it is p-marked. To the last persons that replace loṭ the augment āṭ is to be given: bhavāni. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes mip; by "ni in place of mi," it becomes ni; by this sūtra, the augment āṭ, the ṭ serving to fix its position; by "for ak before a like vowel, lengthening," it is lengthened.

For the dual and the plural of the last person of the parasmaipada of loṭ: bhavāva. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes vas; by "āṭ for the last, and it is p-marked," the augment āṭ, the ṭ serving to fix its position; by "for ak before a like vowel, lengthening"; by "loṭ is like laṅ," the s is removed. bhavāma.

tebrābdhatoḥ: they come at the beginning of the root. "They," that is, the preverbs (upasarga): when preverbs are joined with a root, they are placed at the beginning of the root. This is the general rule. prabhavāni. āniloṭaḥ: of the āni of loṭ. When a preverb such as pra stands at the beginning of the root, the letter n becomes ṇ. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes mas; by "āṭ for the last, and it is p-marked," āṭ, the ṭ serving to fix its position; by "like vowels of ak," it is lengthened; by "loṭ is like laṅ," the s is removed. When a cause for it is present, the letter n of āni, the replacement of loṭ's mip together with āṭ ("may I become supreme"), becomes the letter ṇ: prabhavāṇi.

Cited in the commentary: sradantaraḥ ubasargabat: srat and antar are like preverbs. Srat and antar are like preverbs: so it says, and the purpose is that they are placed at the beginning of the root, and so on. "The path exists": sradbhavāni. "May I become other": antarbhavāṇi. By "of the āni of loṭ," n becomes ṇ.

Also cited in the commentary: duraḥparsyaṇatvanakecita: after dur, the change to ṇ does not occur, according to some. The āni of loṭ after the preverb dur in some cases does not become ṇ: dirbhavāni.

For "bhū in the sense of obtaining," once śap has been given, guṇa and the rest applied, and bhava formed as before, then for the singular of the first person of the ātmanepada of loṭ: āmetaḥ: ām in place of e. The final letters e of the endings that replace loṭ become ām ("may I become bad"). "May he obtain": bhavatāṃ. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes ta; by "ṭ-marked," the vowel a of ta becomes e; by this sūtra, e becomes ām.

For the dual and the plural of the first person of the ātmanepada of loṭ: "may the two obtain," bhapetāṃ. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes ātām; by "of the ā of the ṅ-marked," ā becomes e: although this itself is not ṅ-marked, by "loṭ is like laṅ"; by "before val" and so on, the s is removed; by "ṭ-marked" and so on, it becomes e; by "ām in place of e," it turns back into ām. bhavantaṃ.

For the singular of the middle person of the ātmanepada of loṭ: sabābhāṃbāmau: after s and v, va and am. The vowel e of the letters s and v that replace loṭ becomes va and am respectively: bhavasva. For the dual of the middle person of the ātmanepada of loṭ, and: bhavama. To loṭ, l becomes jha, and by the jha rules and so on, e; by "ām in place of e," ām; by "guṇa after a" and "for both, one, the form of the former," it took that form. For the plural: to bhava, loṭ; l becomes thās; by "se in place of thās," thās becomes se; by this sūtra, e becomes va with its vowel; the s is drawn in. "May the two obtain": bhavethāṃ. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes āthām; by "of the ā of the ṅ-marked" and "loṭ is like laṅ," ā becomes iy; by "v and y" and so on, the y is removed; sandhi; by "ṭ-marked" and so on, it becomes e; by "ām in place of e," it turns back into ām. bhavadhvaṃ. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes dhvam; by "ṭ-marked" and so on, the final ṭi becomes e; by "after s and v, va and am," the e turns back again into am.

For the singular of the last person of the ātmanepada of loṭ: etaḥai: ai in place of e.

The letters e of the endings of the last person that replace loṭ become ai. "May I obtain": bhabi. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes iṭ; by "āṭ for the last," the augment āṭ, the ṭ serving to fix its position; by "like vowels of ak," it is lengthened; by this sūtra, e becomes ai.

For the dual and the plural of the last person of the ātmanepada of loṭ: bhavāvahai, bhavamahai. To bhava, loṭ; l becomes mahi; by "āṭ for the last" and so on, āṭ is added; by "like vowels of ak," lengthening; by "ṭ-marked" and so on, i becomes e; by "ai in place of e," it becomes ai. These are loṭ, which the Kalāpa calls pañcamī, and which the Sarasvatī grammar designates "the suffix of blessing." To bhava, loṭ; l becomes vahi; by "āṭ for the last," āṭ is added; by "like vowels of ak," lengthening; by "ṭ-marked" and so on, i becomes e; by "ai in place of e," it becomes ai.

anadyataneyaṅ: laṅ for what is not of today. "Not of today" means not existing today: in the sense of an action referring to something that happened not long ago, such as yesterday, laṅ comes after a root. The way bhava is formed, by applying śap in the sense of the agent, guṇa and so on to "bhū in the sense of being," is like the previous ones. To bhava, laṅ; the letter ṅ, as a marker, serves to prevent guṇa, and the a is for the sake of pronunciation. The l becomes tip.

luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣu aḍudattaḥ: before luṅ, laṅ, and lṛṅ, aṭ, and it is udātta. When luṅ, laṅ, or lṛṅ follows, the augment aṭ is given to the root, and it is designated udātta. abhavata. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; the letter ṅ of laṅ, as a marker, serves to prevent guṇa, and the a is for the sake of pronunciation; l becomes tip, the letter p serving to make it p-marked; by "of the i as well," the i is removed.

For the dual and the plural of the first person of the parasmaipada of laṅ: abhavatāṃ. Bhava, laṅ; l becomes tas; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ, the ṭ serving to fix its position; by "for tas, thas, tha, and mip, tām, tam, ta, and am," tas becomes tām. abhavana. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root; l becomes jhi; from jha the i is changed; by "anta in place of jha," jha becomes anta; by "of the i as well," the i is removed; by "elision of the final of a conjunct," the t is removed; by "guṇa after a" and "for both, one, the form of the former," it took that form.

For the three middle persons of the parasmaipada of laṅ: abhavaḥ. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes sip, the p serving to make it p-marked; by "of the i as well," the i is removed; by the rule on s and sajuṣ and so on, s becomes ru; the u is removed; r becomes visarga. abhavahaṃ. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes thas; by "for tas, thas, tha, and mip, tām, tam, ta, and am," thas becomes tam. abhavata. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes tha; by "for tas, thas, tha, and mip, tām, tam, ta, and am," tha becomes ta.

For the three last persons of the parasmaipada of laṅ: abhavaṃ. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes mip; by "for tas, thas, tha, and mip, tām, tam, ta, and am," mip becomes am; by "guṇa after a" and "for both, one, the form of the former." abhavāva. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes vas; by "lengthening of a before yañ," it is lengthened; by "always, for the ṅ-marked," the s is removed. abhavāma. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes mas; by "lengthening of a before yañ," it is lengthened; by "always, for the ṅ-marked," the s is removed. These are the parasmaipada.

The way bhava is formed, by giving śap to "bhū in the sense of obtaining" and applying guṇa and so on, is as above. For the three first persons of the ātmanepada: abhavata. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes ta. abhavetāṃ. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes ātām; by "of the ā of the ṅ-marked," ā becomes iy; by "elision of v and y before val," the y is removed; sandhi. abhavanta. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes jha; from jha the a is taken out; by "anta in place of jha," jha becomes anta; by "guṇa after a" and "for both, one, the form of the former," it took that form.

For the three middle persons of the ātmanepada of laṅ: abhavathāḥ. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes thās; by "ru for s and sajuṣ," the u is removed, and r becomes visarga. abhavethāṃ. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes āthām; by "of the ā of the ṅ-marked," ā becomes iy; by "of v and y before val," the y is removed; sandhi. abhavadhāṃ. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes dhvam.

For the three last persons of the ātmanepada of laṅ: abhave. abhavaḥ. By "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ to the root, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes iṭ; joined in sandhi. abhavāvahi. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes vahi; by "lengthening of a before yañ," it is lengthened. abhavāmahi. To bhava, laṅ; by "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, the augment aṭ, the ṭ serving to fix its position; l becomes mahiṅ, the ṅ serving the abbreviation; by "lengthening of a before yañ," it is lengthened.

These are the procedures in which laṅ meets the root. In this grammar and in the Cāndra it is called laṅ; the Kalāpa calls it hyastanī; and the Sarasvatī grammar gives it the designation "not of today."

luṅ: luṅ. In the sense of an action referring to what has happened, that is, to the past, luṅ comes after a root. Moreover, it mostly applies in the sense of an action from which a long time has passed since it went by.

māṅalluṅ: luṅ with māṅ. To a root joined with māṅ, luṅ also comes when it applies in the sense of the future. That is, although the ending luṅ itself is a suffix that shows the past, because it is negated by māṅ it shows the future.

smottarelaṅca: when sma follows, laṅ too. When māṅ is joined and followed by sma, laṅ comes after the root in the sense of the future, and by the word "too," luṅ also comes.

cliluṅi: cli before luṅ. When luṅ follows, cli is given to the root as an intermediate suffix.

cliḥsic: sic in place of cli. The suffix cli before luṅ becomes sic.

gātisgrāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥprasmepadeṣca: after gāti, sthā, ghu, pā, and bhū, before the parasmaipada endings, of sic. Gāti and sthā: that is, the root gai, "in the sense of sound."

Pā: to drink. After iṇ, "to go," the roots that bear the name ghu, pā, "to protect," and bhū, "to be," the sic into which the suffix cli has changed is elided when the parasmaipada endings of luṅ follow.

bhūsuvostiṅi: after bhū and ṣū, before tiṅ. The ti endings of the luṅ parasmaipada that come after the roots bhū and ṣūñ, that is, the nine beginning with ti, are given the name sārvadhātuka, and when those endings follow, guṇa, vṛddhi, and the like are not applied to bhū and ṣūñ.

Abhūt. Bhū, "to be." By the rule "luṅ," luṅ is given; its ṅ serves to make it ṅit, and its u marks its kind. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given as an intermediate suffix; by the rule "sic in place of cli," cli becomes sic; and by the rule beginning "gāti," sic is elided. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. La becomes tip. Although the p is there for the sake of guṇa, in this case, after bhū and ṣū, guṇa is not applied. By the rule "of i also," the vowel i of ti is dropped.

kṅitica: also before what has k or ṅ as its marker. When something that has the letter k as its marker, or the letter ṅ as its marker, follows a root, guṇa, vṛddhi, and the like are not applied.

In the dual of the first person of the luṅ parasmaipada: abhūtām. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," cli becomes sic; and by the rule beginning "gāti," sic is elided. La becomes tas. By the rule "tām, tam, ta, and am in place of tas, thas, tha, and mip," tas becomes tām. By the rule that says "a sārvadhātuka that does not have p as its marker," tas here bears the name "having ṅ as its marker," and by the rule "also before what has k or ṅ as its marker," guṇa is not applied.

In the plural of the first person of the luṅ parasmaipada, bhuvovukaluṅliṭoḥ: in luṅ and liṭ, vuk for bhū. When the endings that replace luṅ and liṭ and that begin with a vowel (ac) follow, the augment vuk is given to the root bhū.

Abhūvan. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic; and by the rule beginning "gāti," sic is elided. La becomes jhi; the i is separated from the jh, and jh becomes ant. By the rule "of i also," the i is dropped, and by the rule "deletion of the final of a conjunct," the t is dropped. By this sūtra comes the augment vuk: its k shows its position and its u is for pronunciation, and v is brought in.

For the three forms of the middle person of the luṅ parasmaipada: abhūḥ. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic; and by the rule beginning "gāti," sic is elided. La becomes sip. By the rule "of i also," the i is dropped, and s becomes ru and then visarga. By the rule that says "bhū and ṣū," guṇa is not applied.

Abhūtam. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic; and by the rule beginning "gāti," sic is elided. La becomes thas. By the rule "tām, tam, ta, and am in place of tas, thas, tha, and mip," thas becomes tam.

Abhūta. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic; and by the rule beginning "gāti," sic is elided. La becomes tha. By the rule "tām, tam, ta, and am in place of tas, thas, tha, and mip," tha becomes ta.

For the three forms of the last person of the luṅ parasmaipada: abhūvam. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic; and by the rule beginning "gāti," sic is elided. La becomes mip. By the rule "tām, tam, ta, and am in place of tas, thas, tha, and mip," mip becomes am. By the rule "in luṅ and liṭ, vuk for bhū," comes the augment vuk: its k shows its position and its u is for pronunciation, and v is brought in.

Abhūva. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic; and by the rule beginning "gāti," sic is elided. La becomes vas. By the rule "always for ṅit," the s is dropped.

Abhūma. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic; and by the rule beginning "gāti," sic is elided. La becomes mas. By the rule "always for what has ṅ as its marker," the s is dropped.

The ātmanepada endings of luṅ apply to the root called "bhū, in the sense of obtaining," as follows.

ārdhadhātukaṃśeṣe: the rest is ārdhadhātuka. Apart from laṭ, liṅ, loṭ, and laṅ, which have already been explained, and the parasmaipada endings of luṅ given to the roots bhū and ṣūñ, the rest, that is, the ātmanepada endings and so on, the other lakāras that will come below, and the suffixes such as the kṛt suffixes for which there is no special exception, are also given the technical designation ārdhadhātuka.

vardhadhātukasyeḍālādeḥ: to the initial val of an ārdhadhātuka, iṭ. If, at the beginning of the endings and suffixes that bear the name ārdhadhātuka, there is a letter belonging to the pratyāhāra val, the augment iṭ is given to that val letter.

Abhaviṣṭa. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. Since c and i bear the name "marker," they are dropped. La becomes ta. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra "ay, av, and so on, in place of ec," o becomes av, and the v is drawn onto the i. By the rule beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ, and by the rule "ṣṭu by ṣṭu," ṭ is brought in for t.

In the dual of the first person of the luṅ ātmanepada: abhaviṣātām. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. C and i are dropped. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the rule "ay and so on, in place of ec," o becomes av. By the rule beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ. La becomes ātām, and ṭ is brought in.

In the plural, ātmanepadeṣānataḥ: before the ātmanepada endings, after what is not short a.

The jh of an ātmanepada ending that does not come after something ending in short a, such as bhava, becomes "at": abhaviṣata. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. C and i are dropped. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning with ec, o becomes av and is drawn on. La becomes jha; the a is separated from the jh, and by this sūtra jh becomes at. The t is drawn onto the a. By the rule beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ, and the ṣ is drawn onto the a.

In the singular of the middle person of the luṅ ātmanepada: abhaviṣṭhāḥ. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. C and i are dropped. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning with ec, o becomes av. La becomes thās. By the rule beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ; by the rule "ṣṭu by ṣṭu," thā becomes ṭhā. S becomes ru, the u is dropped, and it then becomes visarga.

In the dual of the middle person of the luṅ ātmanepada: abhaviṣāthām. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. C and i are dropped. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning with ec, o becomes av. La becomes āthām. By the rule beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ, and the ṣ is drawn onto the ā.

In the plural of the middle person of the luṅ ātmanepada, dhīca: also before dh. When an ending beginning with the letter dh follows, a vowelless s is elided.

vibhāṣeḍaḥ: optionally, after iṭ. Where a root ends in a letter of the pratyāhāra iṇ and the augment iṭ has been given to it, the letter dh of the endings that replace luṅ and liṭ, and that of sīdhvam in the benedictive liṅ, coming after that iṭ, optionally become the letter ḍh: it is optional. Abhaviḍhvam, abhavidhvam.

Quoted in the commentary: dhaslopovāsasyadkecita: in the case of dhvam, the elision of s is optional, according to some. As explained above, when an ending with the letter dh follows, s is elided in some cases. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," the augment aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. C and i are dropped. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning with ec, o becomes av. La becomes dhvam. By the rule "also before dh," s is dropped. By this sūtra, whether dh becomes ḍh or not is made optional. Or else, without eliding it, that very s may also be made into the letter d: abhaviddtāṃ, adhadidhaṃ.

For the three forms of the last person of the luṅ ātmanepada: luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. C and i are dropped. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning with ec, o becomes av. La becomes dhvam. Whether its s is elided or becomes d is made optional.

Abhaviṣi. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. C and i are dropped. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning with ec, o becomes av. La becomes iṭ. By the rule beginning "substitute," ṣ is brought in for s.

Abhaviṣvahi. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. C and i are dropped. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning with ec, o becomes av. La becomes vahi. By the rule beginning "substitute," ṣ is brought in for s.

Abhaviṣmahi. Luṅ is given to bhū. By the rule beginning "luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ," aṭ is given to the root, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule "cli before luṅ," cli is given; by the rule "sic in place of cli," it becomes sic. C and i are dropped. By the rule "iṭ to the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is given, and the ṭ shows its position. By the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning with ec, o becomes av. La becomes mahiṅ; the ṅ is for the sake of the pratyāhāra. By the rule beginning "substitute," ṣ is brought in for s.

namāṅyoge: not when māṅ is joined. Although it was explained above that the augment aṭ is given to the root when luṅ, laṅ, and lṛṅ follow, as an exception to that, aṭ does not come to the root when māṅ is joined, even when luṅ, laṅ, and lṛṅ follow. "You did not become": mā bhavān bhūt. Luṅ is given to bhū, la becomes tip, and aṭ is not given. Laṅ is given to bhū, then śap, and la becomes tip: mā sma bhavat, "did not become." Luṅ is given to bhū, and la becomes tip: mā sma bhūt, "did not become."

These are given the technical name luṅ here and in the Cāndra; in the Kalāpa they speak of "di and the rest, together with si," and in the Sārasvata grammar they speak of "the past endings."

parokṣeliṭ: liṭ for what is out of sight. "Out of sight" means a time that is out of sight. It is of two kinds, past and future, and of these, liṭ comes to the root in expressing a past event. Moreover, it is mostly used of what is long past.

liḍca: liṭ too. The endings that replace liṭ are also given the technical designation ārdhadhātuka.

parasmaibadānāṃṇalatususthalathusaṇlvamāḥ: in place of the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, a, ṇal, va, and ma. The nine parasmaipada endings that replace liṭ, tip and the rest, become in order these nine, beginning with ṇal.

indhibhavatibhyāṃca: also for indhi and bhavati. The endings that replace liṭ after the roots indhi, "to shine," and bhavati, that is, the root bhū, are given the name "having k as marker"; the purpose is to prevent guṇa.

liṭibhātoranabhyāsasya: before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa. When a root is pronounced twice, the first is given the name abhyāsa. "Having no abhyāsa" means this: if a root has already been doubled, it is not doubled again; so a root that has not been doubled before, one without an abhyāsa, is doubled when liṭ follows.

ekācodveprathamasya: two of the first, which has a single ac. If a root that, as explained before, has no abhyāsa is moreover a root with a single ac, then even if there is a hal at its end, that first part is doubled when liṭ follows.

pūrvoñbhyasaḥ: the former is the abhyāsa. As explained above, when a root is pronounced twice, the former is given the name abhyāsa.

hrasvarcaḥ: short. When a root is pronounced twice, the former, which bears the name abhyāsa, becomes short if it is a long ac.

abhyāsecarcca: in the abhyāsa, car also. If what bears the name abhyāsa is a letter of the pratyāhāra jhal, it becomes a letter of the pratyāhāra car, and, by the word "also," a letter of the pratyāhāra jaś. That is to say, among the letters of the pratyāhāra jhal, those of the pratyāhāra khay become the letters of the pratyāhāra car that agree with them in class and in place of articulation, and the remaining jhal letters become the letters of the pratyāhāra jaś that are of the same class and agree in place of articulation.

bhavateraḥ: for bhavati, a. When bhavati, that is, the root bhū, is pronounced twice, the u of the former, which bears the name abhyāsa, becomes the letter a when liṭ follows.

As examples of these, for bhū in the sense of existence, in the first person singular of the parasmaipada of liṭ: babhūva. To bhū, the rule "for what is out of sight, liṭ" gives liṭ. In liṭ the ṭ is for the purpose of ṭi and the i is for distinction. The la becomes tip, and by the rule "for the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, and the rest," tip becomes ṇal. Although the letter ṇ serves to bring about vṛddhi before what has ṇ as marker, here, by the rule "also for indhi and bhavati," it does not cause vṛddhi. The i is for distinction. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū becomes short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u becomes a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car also," bha becomes ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement, the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the a.

In the first person dual of the parasmaipada of liṭ: babhūvataḥ. To bhū comes liṭ, and the la becomes tas. By the rule "for the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, and the rest," tas becomes atus. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," the letter ū becomes u. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u becomes the letter a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car also," the letter bha becomes ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement, the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the a.

In the first person plural of the parasmaipada of liṭ: thabhūvuḥ. To bhū comes liṭ, and the la is changed to jhi. By the rule "for the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us, and the rest," jhi becomes us. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū becomes short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u turns into a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car," bha becomes ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement, the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to us.

For the three forms of the middle person of the parasmaipada of liṭ: babhūvitha. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to sip. By the rule "for the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us, thal, and the rest," sip becomes thal; the l is for distinction. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," it becomes short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u becomes a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car also," bha becomes ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val," the augment iṭ is given: the ṭ is for its placement, and the v is joined to the i.

thabhūpathuḥ. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la becomes thas. By the rule "for the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, and the rest," thas is changed to athus. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," it becomes short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u turns into a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car also," bha becomes ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement, the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the a.

babhūva. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to tha. By the rule "for the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, a, and the rest," tha becomes a. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū becomes short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u turns into a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car," bha becomes ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement, and the u, being for pronunciation, is dropped; the v is joined to the a.

For the three forms of the last person of the parasmaipada of liṭ: babhūva. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to mip. By the rule "for the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, a, ṇal, and the rest," mip is changed to ṇal. The l is for distinction, and the letter ṇ, though it does not cause vṛddhi here, serves elsewhere to bring about vṛddhi. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u is changed to a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car," bha turns into ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement, the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the a.

babhūviva. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to vas. By the rule "for the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, a, ṇal, va, and the rest," vas is changed to va. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u comes to be a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car," bha becomes ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes the augment iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement, and the v is joined to the i.

babhūvima. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to mas. By the rule "for the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, a, ṇal, va, ma," mas is changed to ma. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u turns into a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car," bha is changed to ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū," the augment vuk is given: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement, and the v is joined to the i.

These are the parasmaipada forms of liṭ.

As examples in which the ātmanepada endings are given to "bhū, in the sense of obtaining," in the first person singular of the ātmanepada of liṭ:

liṭstajhayoreśireca: for the ta and jha of liṭ, eś and irec.

The letter ta of the ātmanepada endings that replace liṭ becomes eś, and the letter jha becomes irec: babhūve. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to ta. By this sūtra, ta is changed to eś. By the rule "the final hal," the ś is dropped. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u turns into a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car," bha is changed to ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū," the augment vuk is given: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the e.

In the first person dual of the ātmanepada of liṭ: babhūvāte. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to ātām. By the rule beginning "of what has ṭ as marker," the end becomes e. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u is changed to a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car," bha is changed to ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū," the augment vuk is given: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the ā.

In the first person plural of the ātmanepada of liṭ: babhūvire. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to jha. By the rule "for the ta and jha of liṭ, eś and irec," jha is changed to irec. By the rule "the final hal," the c is dropped. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u is changed to a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car," bha becomes ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement, and the u, being for pronunciation, is dropped; the v is joined to the i.

For the three forms of the middle person of the ātmanepada of liṭ: babhūviṣe. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to thās. By the rule "se for thās," thās is changed to se. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u turns into a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car," bha is changed to ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement, and the v is joined to the i. By the rule beginning "of a substitute," the s becomes ṣ.

babhūvātha. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to āthām. By the rule beginning "of what has ṭ as marker," the end becomes e. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u becomes a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car also," bha is changed to ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū," the augment vuk is given: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the ā.

babhāvidhe. babhāviḍhe. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to dhvam. By the rule beginning "of what has ṭ as marker," the end becomes e. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū becomes short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u is changed to a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car also," bha is changed to ba. By the rule "vuk for bhū," the augment vuk is given: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "the option after iṭ," whether dha becomes ḍha or not is made optional.

For the three forms of the last person of the ātmanepada of liṭ: badhūve. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to iṭ; the ṭ is for distinction. By the rule beginning "of what has ṭ as marker," i becomes e. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u becomes a. By the rule "vuk for bhū," the augment vuk is given: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the e.

babhūvivahe. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to vahi. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u is changed to a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car also," bha is changed to ba. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val," iṭ is given: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "vuk for bhū," the augment vuk is given: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the i.

babhūvimahe. To bhū comes liṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to mahiṅ; the ṅ is for the sake of the pratyāhāra. By the rule "before liṭ, of a root that has no abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the rule "short," ū is made short. By the rule "for bhavati, a," u is changed to a. By the rule "in the abhyāsa, car also," bha is changed to ba. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "vuk for bhū" comes the augment vuk: the k is for its placement and the u is for pronunciation, and the v is joined to the i.

These are the forms of liṭ. Here and in the Cāndra grammar this is called liṭ, while in both the Kalāpa and the Sārasvata grammar it is called the inflection for what is out of sight (parokṣā).

anadyataniluṭ: for what is not today, luṭ. When an action refers to the future, but not to today, luṭ is applied to the root; moreover, it is mostly applied to a future that is not very far off in time.

syatāsīlṛluṭoḥ: sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ. The "lṛ" here is to be taken as both lṛṅ and lṛṭ: when lṛṅ or lṛṭ follows, sya is given to the root, and when luṭ follows, tās is to be attached.

luṭaḥprathamasyaḍāraurasaḥ: for the first endings of luṭ, ḍā, rau, and ras. The first person endings of the parasmaipada that replace luṭ, and the first person endings of the ātmanepada, become ḍā, rau, and ras respectively.

Examples of these, in order: in the first person singular of the parasmaipada, bhavitā. To bhū, by the rule "for what is not today, luṭ," comes luṭ; its ṭ is for the purpose of ṭit, and the u is for distinction, as in "for the first endings of luṭ" and so on. The la becomes tip. By the rule "for the first endings of luṭ, ḍā, rau, and ras," tip is changed to ḍā; the ḍ is for deleting the ṭi before a ḍit. By the rule "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," tās is given. By the rule "of the ṭi," the ṭi is removed, and the t is joined to the ā. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val," iṭ is given. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i.

In the first person dual of the parasmaipada of luṭ:

rica: also before r. When the letter r follows, the vowelless s of tās and of the root as, "to exist," is deleted: bhavitārau. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to tas. By the rule "for the first endings of luṭ," tas is changed to rau. By the rule "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," tās is given, and by this sūtra the s is removed. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes the augment iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," the o becomes av, and the v is joined on.

In the first person plural of the parasmaipada of luṭ: bhavitāraḥ. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to jhi. By the rule beginning "for the first endings of luṭ," jhi is changed to ras. By the rule "sya and tās," tās is given. By the rule "also before r," the s is removed. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes the augment iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined on.

In the middle person singular of the parasmaipada of luṭ:

tāsastyormopaḥ: deletion for tās and asti.

The letter s of tās and of asti, that is, of the root as, is deleted when an affix that has the letter s first follows: bhavitāsi. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to sip; the p is for the purpose of pit. By the rule "sya and tās," tās is given, and by this sūtra the s is removed. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val," iṭ is given: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined on.

In the middle person dual of the parasmaipada of luṭ: bhavitāsbraḥ. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to thas. By the rule "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," tās is given, and the s is joined to the tha. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined on.

In the middle person plural of the parasmaipada of luṭ: bhavitāstha. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to tha. By the rule "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," tās is given, and the s is joined to the tha. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val," iṭ is given: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined on.

For the three forms of the last person of the parasmaipada of luṭ: bhavitāsmi. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to mip; the p is for the purpose of pit. By the rule "sya and tās," tās is given. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined on.

bhavitālbaḥ. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to vas. By the rule "sya and tās," tās is attached. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," guṇa is applied; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av.

bhavitāsmaḥ. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to mas. By the rule "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," tās is attached. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined on. These are the parasmaipada forms.

Now, when the ātmanepada endings are attached to bhū in the sense of obtaining, the three forms of the first person are the same as the three of the first person of the parasmaipada. bhavitā: to bhū comes luṭ; the la becomes ta, and ta becomes ḍā; then tās, iṭ, and so on. bhavitārau: the la becomes ātām, and ātām is changed to rau; then tās, iṭ, and so on. The la becomes jha, and jha becomes ras; by tās, iṭ, and so on, o becomes av: bhavitāraḥ.

In the middle person singular of the ātmanepada of luṭ: bhaṅitāse. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to thās. By the rule "se for thās," thās becomes se. By the rule "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," tās is given. By the rule "deletion for tās and asti," the s is removed. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av.

In the middle person dual of the ātmanepada of luṭ: bhavitāsātha. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to āthām. By the rule beginning "of what has ṭ as marker," the end becomes e. By the rule "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," tās is attached. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined on.

In the middle person plural of the ātmanepada of luṭ: bhavitādhā. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to dhvam. By the rule beginning "of what has ṭ as marker," the end becomes e. By the rule "sya and tās," tās is attached. By the rule "also before dh," the s is removed. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined on.

In the last person singular of the ātmanepada of luṭ:

haeti: before e, h. The letter s of tās and of the root as becomes the letter h when the affix e follows: bhavitāhe. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la becomes iṭ; the ṭ is for distinction. By the rule beginning "of what has ṭ as marker," i becomes e. By the rule "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," tās is given. By this sūtra the s becomes h. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of ārdhadhātuka and sārvadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av.

In the last person dual of the ātmanepada of luṭ: bhavitāsāhe. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la becomes vahi. By the rule beginning "of what has ṭ as marker," the end becomes e. By the rule "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," tās is attached. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ; guṇa is applied, and by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av.

In the last person plural of the ātmanepada of luṭ: bhavitāsmahe. To bhū comes luṭ; its markers are removed, and the la is changed to mahiṅ; the ṅ is for the sake of the pratyāhāra. By the rule beginning "of what has ṭ as marker," i turns into e. By the rule "iṭ for an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val" comes iṭ: the ṭ is for its placement. By the rule "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined on.

These are luṭ. In both this system and the Cāndra it is called luṭ, while in the two, the Kalāpa and the Sārasvata grammar, it is called śvastani.

lidāśiṣi: for a wish, liṅ. Liṅ is used for the sense of an action that expresses a wish, and it is given the technical name "the liṅ of wishing" (āśīrliṅ). This second liṅ, technically named "the liṅ of wishing," also bears the name ārdhadhātuka.

kidāśiṣi: for a wish, kit. The augment yāsuṭ is also added to the parasmaipada endings that replace liṅ in the sense of a wish, and here, in the context of the liṅ of wishing, yāsuṭ is given the technical name "having k as marker."

The examples of the liṅ of wishing applied to a root are as follows.

For the singular of the first person of the parasmaipada of the liṅ of wishing: bhūlāta. bhū la. In the liṅ of wishing, the ṅ serves to make it ṅit, and the i serves to distinguish it. La is replaced by tip, and the p serves to make it pit. By the sūtra "and of i," the i is dropped. By the sūtra "yāsuṭ for the parasmaipada endings, and it is udātta, the raised tone," yāsuṭ is added. By the sūtra "for a wish, kit," it bears the name kit; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "of s and k at the beginning of a conjunct," the s is dropped.

For the dual of the first person of the parasmaipada of the liṅ in the sense of wishing: bhūyāstāṃ. dhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by tas. By the sūtra "for tas, thas, tha and mip, tām, tam, ta and am," tas is replaced by tām. By the sūtra "parasmaipada," yāsuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. The s is joined.

For the plural of the first person of the parasmaipada of the liṅ of wishing: bhūyāsuḥ. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by jhi. By the sūtra "jus for jhi," jhi is replaced by jus. By the sūtra beginning "cu, ṭu," the j is dropped. By the sūtra "parasmaipada," yāsuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. The s is joined to the u.

For the three numbers of the middle person of the parasmaipada of the liṅ of wishing: bhūyāḥ. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by sip; the p serves to make it pit. By the sūtra "and of i," the i is dropped. By the sūtra beginning "parasmaipada," yāsuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "of s and k at the beginning of a conjunct," the s of yāsuṭ is dropped. The s of sip becomes ru, the u is dropped, and the r becomes visarga.

bhūyāstaṃ. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by thas. By the sūtra beginning "tas, thas," thas is replaced by tam. By the sūtra beginning "parasmaipada," yāsuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. The s is joined to tam.

bhūyāsta. dhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by tha. By the sūtra beginning "tas, thas, tha, mip," tha becomes ta. By the sūtra beginning "parasmai," yāsuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. The s is joined to ta.

For the three numbers of the last person of the parasmaipada of the liṅ of wishing: bhūyāsaṃ. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by mip. By the sūtra beginning "tas, thas, tha, mip," mip is replaced by am. By the sūtra beginning "parasmaipada," yāsuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. The s is joined to am.

bhūyāsā. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by vas. By the sūtra "always for ṅit," the s is dropped. By the sūtra beginning "parasmaipada," yāsuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. The s is joined to va.

bhāyāsma. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by mas. By the sūtra "always for ṅit," the s is dropped. By the sūtra beginning "parasmaipada," yāsuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. The s is joined to ma.

The examples of the ātmanepada endings applied to bhū in the sense of obtaining are as follows.

For the singular of the first person of the ātmanepada of the liṅ of wishing: suṭ tithoḥ. For t and th, suṭ. The augment suṭ is given to the letters t and th of the ātmanepada endings that replace the liṅ of wishing: bhaviṣīṣṭa. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by ta. By the sūtra "sīyuṭ for liṅ," sīyuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is given; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped. By this sūtra the augment suṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ and is joined. By the sūtra "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," t becomes ṭ, and the ṣ is joined to ṭa.

For the dual of the first person of the ātmanepada of the liṅ of wishing: bhaviṣīyāstūṃ. bhūs. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by ātām. By the sūtra "sīyuṭ for liṅ," sīyuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," the augment iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra beginning "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" comes guṇa, and then "ec"; by the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ, and the y is joined to the ā. By the sūtra "suṭ for t and th," suṭ is inserted between the ā and tām; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. The s is joined to tām.

For the plural of the first person of the ātmanepada of the liṅ of wishing: bhaviṣīran. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by jha. By the sūtra "ran for jha," jha is replaced by ran. By the sūtra "sīyuṭ for liṅ," sīyuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped.

For the three numbers of the middle person of the ātmanepada of the liṅ of wishing: bhaviṣīṣṭaḥ. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by thās. The suṭ for t and th is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. The sīyuṭ for liṅ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," both instances of s become ṣ. By the sūtra "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," thā becomes ṭhā, and the ṣ is joined to ṭhā. The s becomes ru, and the r becomes visarga.

bhaviṣīyāsthāṃ. bhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by āthām. By the sūtra "suṭ for t and th," suṭ is inserted between the ā and thām; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation; the s is joined to thām. By the sūtra "sīyuṭ for liṅ," sīyuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ, and it is joined.

bhaviṣīdgāṃ, bhaviṣīdhaṃ. dhū la. The markers of the liṅ of wishing are dropped, and la is replaced by dhvam. By the sūtra "sīyuṭ for liṅ," sīyuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ. By the sūtra "option after iṭ," the change of dh into ḍh is made optional, so that it either changes or does not.

For the three forms of the last person in the ātmanepada of the benedictive liṅ:

Bhaviṣīya. To bhū, the benedictive liṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is replaced by iṭ. By the sūtra "at for the a of iṭ," iṭ becomes at; the letter t means "of that same duration." By the sūtra "sīyuṭ for liṅ," sīyuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ. The y is joined to the a.

Bhaviṣīvahi. To bhū, the benedictive liṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is replaced by vahi. By the sūtra "sīyuṭ for liṅ," sīyuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s is changed to ṣ.

Bhaviṣīmahi. To bhū, the benedictive liṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is replaced by mahiṅ; the ṅ serves for the pratyāhāra. By the sūtra "sīyuṭ for liṅ," sīyuṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position, and the u is for pronunciation. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

These are the liṅ in the sense of wishing. In this system and in the Cāndra it is called the benedictive liṅ, while in the Kalāpa and the Sārasvata grammar it is called the benedictive yāt and so forth.

Bhaviṣyati: lṛṭ. Lṛṭ is used for what will come about. For the sense of an action in a future that is not today, luṭ is applied to the root, and that future is used mostly in the sense of the distant time to come.

The examples of joining these future endings to the root are as follows. For the three forms of the first person of the parasmaipada:

Bhaviṣyati. To bhū, lṛṭ is added. The ṭ serves for the rule on ṭ, and the ṛ serves to distinguish it; la is changed to tip, and the p serves to make it pit. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Bhaviṣyataḥ. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to tas. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Bhaviṣyanti. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to jhi. By the sūtra "ant for jh," jh becomes ant. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "a before guṇa," of the two vowels a single one takes the form of the former. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

For the three forms of the middle person of the parasmaipada of lṛṭ:

Bhaviṣyasi. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La becomes sip; the p serves to make it pit. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra "ec becomes ay, av, āy and āv," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra "of a substitute and a suffix," s becomes ṣ.

Bhaviṣyathaḥ. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to thas. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Bhaviṣyatha. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to tha. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

For the three forms of the last person of the parasmaipada of lṛṭ:

Bhaviṣyāmi. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to mip; the p serves to make it pit. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "lengthening of a before yañ," sya becomes long. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Bhaviṣyāvaḥ. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to vas and to mas. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "lengthening of a before yañ," sya becomes long. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av, and the v is joined to the i. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Bhaviṣyāmaḥ. Bhaviṣyāmaḥ.

These are bhū joined with the parasmaipada endings of lṛṭ.

The examples of joining the ātmanepada endings to the root bhū, "in the sense of attaining," are as follows. For the three forms of the first person of the ātmanepada of lṛṭ:

Bhaviṣyate. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to ta. By the sūtra beginning "ṭit," the end becomes e. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Bhaviṣyete. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to ātām. By the sūtra beginning "ṭit," the end becomes e. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ. By the sūtra "of ā after a ṅit," the ā of ātām becomes iy. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped. By the sūtra "guṇa from a," the vowels become e.

Bhaviṣyante. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to jha. By the sūtra "ant for jh," jh is changed to ant. By the sūtra beginning "ṭit," the end becomes e. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "a before guṇa," of the two vowels a single one takes the form of the former. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

For the three forms of the middle person of the ātmanepada of lṛṭ:

Bhaviṣyase. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to thās. By the sūtra "of thās," thās is changed to se. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra "of a substitute and a suffix," s becomes ṣ.

Bhaviṣyethe. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to āthām. By the sūtra beginning "ṭit," the end becomes e. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "of ā after a ṅit," the ā of āthām becomes iy. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped. By the sūtra "guṇa from a," the vowels are joined. Before the val of an ārdhadhātuka, iṭ is added, then guṇa, and so forth.

Bhaviṣyadhve. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to dhvam. By the sūtra beginning "ṭit," the end becomes e. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

For the three forms of the last person of the ātmanepada of lṛṭ:

Bhaviṣye. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to iṭ. By the sūtra beginning "ṭit," it becomes e. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "a before guṇa," of the two vowels a single one takes the form of the latter. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Bhaviṣyāvahe. Bhaviṣyāmahe. To bhū, lṛṭ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to vahi and to mahiṅ. By the sūtra beginning "ṭit," the end becomes e. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "lengthening of a before yañ," sya becomes long. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

These are lṛṭ. In this system and in the Cāndra they are called lṛṭ, while in the Kalāpa and the Sārasvata grammar they are called "ti and so forth together with sya," or bhaviṣyanti.

"Liṅnimitte lṛṅ kriyātipattau": when there is occasion for liṅ, lṛṅ is used for the failure of an action. Failure of the action means that, in the domain of liṅ, lṛṅ applies when the time has passed, or in the sense that the collection of causes has not come together. It is also explained that in some cases it applies in the sense of an action left unfinished and incomplete, and also to a fresh accomplishment of an action that has just been completed.

The examples of joining lṛṅ to the root are as follows. For the three forms of the first person of the parasmaipada of lṛṅ:

Abhaviṣyat. To bhū, lṛṅ is added. The ṅ serves to make it ṅit, and the ṛ serves for sya. La is changed to tip; the p serves to make it pit. By the sūtra "and of i," the i is dropped. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. Before the val of an ārdhadhātuka, iṭ is added. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra "of a substitute and a suffix," s becomes ṣ.

Abhaviṣyatām. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to tas. By the sūtra beginning "tas, thas, tha, mip," tas is changed to tām. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. Before the val of an ārdhadhātuka, iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Abhaviṣyan. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to jhi. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "ant for jh," jh becomes ant. By the sūtra "and of i," the i is dropped. By the sūtra "elision of the final of a conjunct," the t is dropped. By the sūtra "a before guṇa," of the two vowels a single one takes the form of the former. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," with the sūtra beginning "ec" and the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

For the three forms of the middle person of the parasmaipada of lṛṅ:

Abhaviṣyaḥ. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to sip; the p serves to make it pit. By the sūtra "and of i," the i is dropped. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra beginning "s and sajuṣ," s becomes ru; the u is dropped, and the r becomes visarga. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Abhaviṣyatam. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to thas. By the sūtra beginning "tas, thas, tha, mip," thas is changed to tam. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Abhaviṣyata. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to tha. By the sūtra beginning "tas, thas, tha, mip," tha is changed to ta. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

For the three forms of the last person of the parasmaipada of lṛṅ, in order:

Abhaviṣyam. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to mip. By the sūtra beginning "tas, thas, tha, mip," mip is changed to am. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "a before guṇa," of the two vowels a single one takes the form of the latter. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Abhaviṣyāva. Abhaviṣyāma.

The examples of joining the ātmanepada endings of lṛṅ to the root bhū, "in the sense of attaining," are as follows. For the three forms of the first person of the ātmanepada of lṛṅ:

To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to vas and to mas. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "lengthening of a before yañ," sya becomes long. By the sūtra "always of a ṅit," the s is dropped. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Abhaviṣyata. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to ta. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra "of a substitute and a suffix," s becomes ṣ.

Abhaviṣyetām. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to ātām. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "of ā after a ṅit," the ā of ātām becomes iy. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped. By the sūtra "guṇa from a," the vowels become e. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. Before the val of an ārdhadhātuka, iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Abhaviṣyanta. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to jha. By the sūtra "ant for jh," jh is changed to ant. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "a before guṇa," of the two vowels a single one takes the form of the former. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

For the three forms of the middle person of the ātmanepada of lṛṅ:

Abhaviṣyathāḥ. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to thās. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," it becomes av. By the sūtra "of a substitute and a suffix," s becomes ṣ. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position.

Abhaviṣyethām. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to āthām. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "of ā after a ṅit," the ā of āthām becomes iy. By the sūtra "elision of v and y before val," the y is dropped. By the sūtra "guṇa from a," the vowels become e. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

Abhaviṣyadhvam. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to dhvam. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added.

By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

For the three forms of the last person of the ātmanepada of lṛṅ:

Abhaviṣye. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to iṭ. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "guṇa from a," the vowels become e. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root.
