Abhaviṣyāvahi. Abhaviṣyāmahi. To bhū, lṛṅ is added, and its indicatory letters are removed. La is changed to vahi and to mahiṅ. By the sūtra "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ," sya is added. By the sūtra "lengthening of a before yañ," sya becomes long. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "of sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka," the root takes guṇa; by the sūtra beginning "ec," o becomes av. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ.

An instance of its use is this: "Yadā vṛṣṭiḥ surājyaṃ cābhaviṣyat," "When rain had fallen and the king had come to be at ease," "tadā subhikṣam abhaviṣyat," "then there would have been plentiful alms." Here the falling of rain and the king's ease are a fresh accomplishment, already completed, while "alms would be obtained" is an example of an action not yet complete, since they have not yet been obtained.

These are lṛṅ. In this system and in the Cāndra grammar they are called lṛṅ, while in the Kalāpa they are called the endings for the failure of an action. Then good alms would be obtained. In the Sārasvata grammar they are called the endings of the action left over.

Thus the ten, beginning with laṭ, have been identified, and something of their substitutions and so on has been explained. Now I shall explain the procedure for joining them to roots, the general rule together with its exceptions.

"Akakhādāv aṣānte pāṭhe vā": optionally, in the recitation, for what has no k or kh at the beginning and no ṣ at the end. In the teaching, or recitation, of the roots, with roots such as nad and gad, and with any root that has no letter k or kh at its beginning and no ṣ at its end following it, the n of the preverb ni optionally changes to ṇ after a preceding preverb such as pra that contains the cause for the change of n to ṇ. Thus praṇibhavati, "it certainly exists," or pranibhavati.

"Pugantalaghūpadhasya ca": and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate. Stems ending in the augment puk, and roots whose penultimate is a short letter of the pratyāhāra ik, take guṇa when there follows a sārvadhātuka or ārdhadhātuka ending that is a cause of guṇa, as with bhū, laṭ, śap, and la becoming tip.

Cetati. To citī, "to know correctly," laṭ and śap are added, and la becomes tip; by this sūtra the root takes guṇa. Cetet. Cetatu. Acetat. When śap is added to citī in the sense of the agent, the four called sārvadhātuka, beginning with laṭ, follow in every procedure the case of bhū; the parasmaipada endings apply, but the ātmanepada endings do not.

The examples of joining luṅ to citī: cit with liṅ, śap, yāsuṭ, and la becoming tip; cit with loṭ, śap, and la becoming tip; cit with laṅ, śap, and la becoming tip. This differs somewhat from the case of bhū.

"Vadavrajahalantasyācaḥ": of the ac of vad, vraj, and what ends in a consonant. The first ac of the root vad, of vraj, and of roots ending in a consonant takes vṛddhi before sic, the substitute for cli, when parasmaipada endings follow.

"Neṭi": not where there is iṭ. Although it was said above that the first ac of roots ending in a consonant and so on takes vṛddhi before sic, the substitute for cli, when parasmaipada endings follow, as an exception to that, even when those causes are present, that ac does not take vṛddhi when an iṭ, such as that given by "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," stands in between.

"Astisico 'pṛkte": of as and of sic before an apṛkta. When, after the root as or after sic, the substitute for cli, there comes an ending called apṛkta, that is, an ending that is a single consonant without a vowel, of the kind that occurs as an ending substituted for luṅ, the augment īṭ is given to that consonant ending.

"Dīdhīvevīṭām": of dīdhī, vevī, and iṭ. The roots dīdhī and vevī and the intermediate suffix iṭ do not undergo vṛddhi, guṇa, and the like.

"Iṭa īṭi": after iṭ, before īṭ. The sic that follows iṭ is elided when the augment īṭ follows.

Since the commentary explains that it is not the case that, once sic has been elided, sandhi is not applied again, the vowel becomes long by the sūtra "long for ak before a similar vowel."

Acetīt. To cit, luṅ is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. The indicatory letters are removed, and la is changed to tip. By the sūtra "cli for luṅ," cli is added. By the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic, and the c and the i are dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate," the root takes guṇa. By the sūtra "and of i," the i of ti is dropped. By the sūtra "of as and of sic before an apṛkta," the augment īṭ is given; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "after iṭ, before īṭ," sic is elided. By the sūtra "long for ak before a similar vowel," it becomes long.

Acetiṣṭām. To cit, by the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. La is changed to tas. By the sūtra "cli for luṅ," cli is added. By the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic, and the c and the i are dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate," the root takes guṇa. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ. By the sūtra beginning "tas, thas, tha, mip," tas is changed to tām. By the sūtra "ṣṭu by contact with ṣṭu," the t becomes ṭ and is joined to the ṣ.

For the plural of the first person of the parasmaipada of luṅ:

"Sijabhyastavidibhyaś ca": and after sic, an abhyasta, and vid. After the suffix sic, after what is called abhyasta, and after roots such as vid, jhi becomes jus.

Acetiṣuḥ. To cit, luṅ is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "cli for luṅ," cli is added. By the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic, and the c and the i are dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate," the root takes guṇa. La becomes jhi, and by this sūtra jhi is changed to jus. By the sūtra beginning "cu and ṭu," the j is dropped. By the sūtra "of a substitute and a suffix," s becomes ṣ.

For the singular of the middle person of the parasmaipada of luṅ:

Acetīḥ. To cit, luṅ is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. La is changed to sip. By the sūtra "and of i," the i is dropped. By the sūtra "cli for luṅ," cli is added. By the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic, and the i and the c are dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate," the root takes guṇa. By the sūtra "of as and of sic before an apṛkta," the augment īṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "after iṭ, before īṭ," sic is elided. By the sūtra "long for ak before a similar vowel," it becomes long. By the sūtra beginning "s and sajuṣ," s becomes ru; the u is dropped, and the r becomes visarga.

For the dual and plural of the middle person of the parasmaipada of luṅ: acetiṣṭam, acetiṣṭa.

For the three forms of the last person of the parasmaipada of luṅ: to cit, luṅ is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. La is changed to thas and to tha, and these in turn, by the sūtra beginning "tas, thas, tha, mip," are changed to tam and ta. By the sūtra "cli for luṅ," cli is added. By the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic, and the i and the c are dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate," the root takes guṇa. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ. By the sūtra "ṣṭu by contact with ṣṭu," both t become ṭ and are joined to the ṣ.

Acetiṣam. To cit, luṅ is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added to the root; the ṭ indicates its position. La is changed to mip, and by the sūtra beginning "tas, thas, tha, mip," mip is changed to am. By the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic, and the c and the i are dropped. By the sūtra "iṭ before the val of an ārdhadhātuka," iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate" and so on, the root takes guṇa. By the sūtra "of a substitute and a suffix," s becomes ṣ.

Acetiṣva. Acetiṣma. To cit, luṅ is added. By the sūtra "for luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ" and so on, aṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. La is changed to vas and to mas. By the sūtra "always of a ṅit," both s are dropped. By the sūtra "cli for luṅ," cli is added. By the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic, and the c and the i are dropped. By the sūtra on iṭ before val, iṭ is added; the ṭ indicates its position. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate," the root takes guṇa. By the sūtra beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ and is joined to va and ma.

The examples of joining liṭ to cit are as follows. For the singular of the first person of the parasmaipada:

Ciceta, "he knew."

"Asaṃyogāl liṭ kit": after what is not a conjunct, liṭ is kit. To cit, a root whose letters are not a conjunct, liṭ is added. By the sūtra "before liṭ, of a root without an abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the sūtra "the first consonant remains," the t is dropped. La is changed to tip, and by the sūtra beginning "of the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us," tip is changed to ṇal. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate," the root takes guṇa, and the t is joined to the a. The endings that follow, substituted for liṭ, which are not called pit, are given the technical name kit. The purpose of this is that the root does not take guṇa.

For the dual and plural of the first person of the parasmaipada of liṭ:

Cicitatuḥ. To cit, liṭ is added. By the sūtra "before liṭ, of a root without an abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the sūtra "the first consonant remains," the t is dropped. La is changed to tas and to jhi. By the sūtra "of the parasmaipada endings, ṇal, atus, us," tas is changed to atus and jhi to us. Both t are joined. By the sūtra beginning "s and sajuṣ," both s are changed to ru; both u are dropped, and both r become visarga. Cicituḥ.

For the three forms of the middle person of the parasmaipada of liṭ:

Ciceti tha. To cit, liṭ is added. By the sūtra "before liṭ, of a root without an abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the sūtra "the first consonant remains," the t is dropped. La is changed to sip, and by the sūtra "of the parasmaipada endings," sip is changed to thal. By the sūtra beginning "final consonant," the l is dropped. Before the val of an ārdhadhātuka, iṭ is added. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate" and so on, the root takes guṇa.

Cicitathuḥ. Cicita. To cit, liṭ is added. By the sūtra "before liṭ, of a root without an abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the sūtra "the first consonant remains," the t is dropped. La is changed to thas and to tha. By the sūtra "of the parasmaipada endings," thas is changed to athus and tha to a.

For the three forms of the last person of the parasmaipada of liṭ:

Ciceta. To cit, liṭ is added. By the sūtra "before liṭ, of a root without an abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the sūtra "the first consonant remains," la is changed to mip, and by the sūtra "of the parasmaipada endings," mip is changed to ṇal. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate" and so on, the root takes guṇa.

Cicitiva. Cicitima.

When luṭ is joined to cit, there are cetitā, cetitārau, cetitāraḥ, and so on; the whole procedure is like the case of joining luṭ to bhū.

When the benedictive liṅ is joined to cit: to cit, by the sūtra "before liṭ, the root is pronounced twice," and by "the first consonant remains," la is changed to vas and mas. By the sūtra "of the parasmaipada endings" and so on, vas is changed to va and mas to ma. Iṭ is added before the val of an ārdhadhātuka affix. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate" and so on, the root takes guṇa.

For the first three persons of the parasmaipada: cityāstāṃ, cityāsuḥ. For the three middle persons: cityāḥ, cityāstaṃ, cityāsta. For the three last persons: cityāsaṃ, cityāsva, cityāsma.

When the parasmaipada endings of lṛṭ are joined to cit, for the first three persons: cetiṣyata, citiṣyatāṃ, cetiṣyanti. For the three middle persons: cetiṣyasi, cetiṣyataṃ, cetiṣyath. For the three last persons: cetiṣyāmi, cetiṣyāvaḥ, cetiṣyāmaḥ.

When the parasmaipada endings of lṛṅ are joined to cit, for the first three persons: acetiṣyata, acetiṣyatāṃ, acetiṣyan. For the three middle persons: acetiṣyaḥ, acetiṣyataṃ, acetiṣyata. For the three last persons: acetiṣyaṃ, acetiṣyāva, acetiṣyāma.

Next, the examples of joining the parasmaipada endings of the ten la affixes, laṭ and the rest, to the root cyutir, "in sprinkling all over." These are for the most part like the case of citī, "in knowing correctly," just explained. The ir of the root is an indicatory letter (anubandha). When śap and so on are added for the agent, for the first three persons of laṭ: cyotti, cyottaḥ, cyotanti. For the three middle persons: cyautasi, cyautathaḥ, cyauttha. For the three last persons: cyotāmi, cyautāvaḥ, cyautāmaḥ.

When liṅ is joined to cyutir, for the first three persons: cyitita, cyotitāṃ, cyoteyuḥ. For the three middle persons: cyoteḥ, cyotetaṃ, cyoteta. For the three last persons: cyoteyaṃ, cyotev, cyotem.

When the parasmaipada endings of loṭ are joined to cyut, for the first three persons: cyotatu, cyotatāta, cyotatāṃ, cyotantu. For the three middle persons: cyota, cyatotāta, cyotataṃ, cyotata. For the three last persons: cyotāni, cyotāva, cyotāma.

When the parasmaipada endings of laṅ are joined to cyut, for the first three persons: acyotata, acyotatāṃ, acyotana. For the three middle persons: acyotaḥ, acyotaṃ, acyotat. For the three last persons: acyotaṃ, acyotāva, acyotāma.

The case of joining luṅ to cyut differs a little from that of citī. The sūtra irito vā means "optionally, after what has ir." By this sūtra, which says that before luṅ following a root that has ir there is cli, the cli in the parasmaipada optionally becomes aṅ. In the option where cli is changed to aṅ, for the first three persons: acyutata, acyutatāṃ, acyutana. For the three middle persons: acyutaḥ, acyutatāṃ, acyutata. For the three last persons: acyutā, acyutāva, acyutāma.

Alternatively, cli is changed to sic, and the whole procedure is like the case of citī. For the first three persons: acyotāṃti, acyotaṃṣṭāṃ, acyotiṣāṃḥ. For the three middle persons: acyotīḥ, acyotiṣṭaṃ, acyotiṣṭa. For the three last persons: acyotiṣaṃ, acyotiṣva, acyotiṣma.

When liṭ is joined to cyut, for the first three persons: by the sūtra halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, "the first consonant remains." Of the root pronounced twice, the first is called the abhyāsa. In it, the initial consonant, such as the letter ca of cyut, remains, that is, it stays without being elided, while the other consonants, the lower member of a consonant cluster and any final consonant without a vowel, are elided. cucyoto, cucyotatuḥ, cucyotuḥ. For the three middle persons: cucyotitha, cucyotithaḥ, cucyota. For the three last persons: cucyota, cucyotiva, cucyotima.

When the parasmaipada endings of luṭ are joined to cyut, the whole procedure is like the case of citī. For the first three persons: cyotitā, cyotitārau, cyotitāraḥ. For the three middle persons: cyotitāsi, cyotitāsthaḥ, cyatitāsṭa. For the three last persons: cyotitāsmi, cyotitāspaḥ, cyotitāsmaḥ.

When the parasmaipada endings of the benedictive liṅ are joined to cyut, the procedures too are like the case of citī. For the first three persons: cyutyāta, cyuṃtyāstāṃ, cyudyāsuḥ. For the three middle persons: cyutyāḥ, cyutyāstāṃ, cyutyāsta. For the three last persons: cyutyāsa, cyutyāsā, cyutyāsma.

When the parasmaipada endings of lṛṭ are joined to cyut, the whole procedure too is like the case of citī. For the first three persons: cyautiṣyati, cyotiṣyataḥ, cyitiṣyanti. For the three middle persons: cyotiṣyasi, cyotiṣyathaḥ, cyotiṣyatha. For the three last persons: cyotiṣyāmi, cyotiṣyāvaḥ, cyotiṣyāmaḥ.

When the parasmaipada endings of lṛṅ are joined to cyut, the operations too are like the case of citī. For the first three persons: acyotiṣyata, acyotiṣyatāṃ, acyautiṣyana. For the three middle persons: acyotiṣyaḥ, acyotiṣyataṃ, acyotimyata. For the three last persons: acyotiṣyaṃ, acyotiṣyāva, acyotiṣyāma.

To the root ścyutir, "in causing change," when the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are joined, the procedures are for the most part like the case of cyutir just explained. For the first three persons of laṭ: ścyotati, ścyotataḥ, ścyotanti. For the three middle persons: ścyotasi, ścyotathaḥ, ścyotatha. For the three last persons: ścyoḍāmi, ścyotāvaḥ, ścyotāmaḥ.

When the parasmaipada endings of liṅ are joined to ścyutir, the procedure is like that of cyut. For the first three persons: ścyotita, ścyotetāṃ, ścyoteyuḥ. For the three middle persons: ścyoteḥ, ścyotetaṃ, ścyoteta. For the three last persons: ścyotayāṃ, ścyoteva, ścyatema.

When the parasmaipada endings of loṭ are joined to ścyutir, the procedures too are like those of cyutir. For the first three persons: ścyotatu, ścyotatātāṃ, ścyotatāṃ, ścyotantu. For the three middle persons: ścyoto, ścyotatāta, ścyotataṃ, ścyotata. For the three last persons: ścyotāni, ścyotāva, ścyotāma.

When the parasmaipada endings of laṅ are joined to ścyutir, the procedures too are like those of cyutir. For the first three persons: aścyotata, aścyotatī, aścyotana. For the three middle persons: aścyotaḥ, aścyotetaṃ, aścyotata. For the three last persons: aścyoti, aścyotāva, aścyotāma.

When the parasmaipada endings of luṅ are joined to ścyutir, the procedures too are like the case of cyutir:

the change of cli to aṅ and the change to sic are made optional. So in the aṅ option, for the first three persons: aścyutata, aścyutatā, aścyutana. For the three middle persons: aścyutaḥ, aścyutata, aścyuhata. For the three last persons: aścyutaṃ, aścyutāpa, aścyutāma.

In the option where cli is changed to sic, for the first three persons: aścyotīta, aścyotiṣṭāṃ, aścyoṣaḥ. For the three middle persons: aścyitīḥ, aścyotiṣṭaṃ, aścyotiṣṭa. For the three last persons: aścyotoṣaṃ, aścyotiṣva, aścyotiṣma.

When the parasmaipada endings of liṭ are joined to ścyutir, the procedures too are like the case of cyutir, except that the elision in the abhyāsa differs a little. The sūtra śarpūrvāḥ khyaḥ means "the khay letters preceded by śar." Of the root pronounced twice, in the part called the abhyāsa, if the earlier letter is a letter of the śar group and the one after it is a letter of the khay group, that khay remains and the other consonants are elided. For the first three persons: cuścyuta, cuścyatatuḥ, cuścyotuḥ. For the three middle persons: cuścyotitha, cuścyotathuḥ, cuścyota. For the three last persons: cuścyota, cuścyotiva, cuścyotima.

When the parasmaipada endings of luṭ are joined to ścyutir, the whole procedure is like the case of cyutir. For the first three persons: ścyotitā, ścyotitāro, acyotitāraḥ. For the three middle persons: ścyotitāsi, ścyotitāsthaḥ, ścyotitāstha. For the three last persons: ścyititāsmi, ścyotitāspaḥ, ścyotitāsmaḥ.

When the parasmaipada endings of the benedictive liṅ are joined to ścyutir, the whole procedure is like the case of cyutir. For the first three persons: ścyutyāta, ścyutyāstāṃ, ścyutyasuḥ. For the three middle persons: ścyutyāḥ, ścyutyāstaṃ, ścyutyāsta. For the three last persons: ścyutyūsaṃ, ścyutyāsva, ścyutyāsma.

When the parasmaipada endings of lṛṭ are joined to ścyutir, the procedures too are like the case of cyutir. For the first three persons: ścyotiṣyate, ścyotiṣyataḥścyo, taḥścyotiḍyanti. For the three middle persons: ścyotiṣyasi, ścyotiṣyathaḥ, ścyotiṣcyatha. For the three last persons: ścyotiścyāmi, ścyotiṣcyāvaḥ, ścyotiṣcyāmaḥ.

When the parasmaipada endings of lṛṅ are joined to ścyutir, the procedures too are like the case of cyutir. For the first three persons: aścyotiṣyata, aścyotiṭyatāṃ, aścyotiṣyana. For the three middle persons: aścyotiṣyaḥ, aścyotiṣyataṃ, aścyotiṣyata. For the three last persons: aścyotiṣyaṃ, aścyotiṣyāva, aścyotiṣyāma.

To the root mantha, "in churning," the whole procedure of joining the parasmaipada endings of the ten la affixes, laṭ and the rest, is like the one just explained. However, in the benedictive liṅ, by the sūtra "of those that do not have i as indicatory letter, of the penultimate of a root ending in a consonant, before what has k or ṅ as indicatory letter," the elision of na applies. In laṭ: manthati and so on. In liṅ: manthit and so on. In loṭ: manthatu and so on. In laṅ: amanthat and so on. In luṅ: amanthāti and so on. In liṭ: mamantha, manthatuḥ, and so on. In luṭ: manthatī and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, since by the sūtra "in the benedictive, kit" the na is dropped: mathyāt and so on. In lṛṭ: manthiṣyati and so on. In lṛṅ: amanthiṣyata and so on. There is no operation at all that differs from the others.

idito num dhāto. Since the sūtra "after what is not a conjunct, liṭ is kit" applies, and here there is a conjunct, liṭ is not kit, and so the na is not elided. The sūtra means "num for a root that has i as indicatory letter." After roots that have i as indicatory letter, such as kuthi, whatever affix arises, whether an affix forming a noun or an affix forming a verb, the augment num is given to that root. The m serves to fix its position and the u serves for pronunciation.

To the root kuti, "in harming and afflicting," the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are joined. In laṭ: kunthati and so on. In liṅ: kunthita and so on. In loṭ: akundratu and so on. In laṅ: akunthata and so on. In luṅ: akanthīta and so on. In liṭ: the sūtra kuhoścuḥ means "of ku and h, cu." If the part called the abhyāsa of the root pronounced twice is ku, that is, the velar class, it changes to the corresponding palatal of the c class; and h changes to jh, and then, by the sūtra "and car in the abhyāsa," it changes to j. cukuntha, cukunthatuḥ, cukunthuḥ, and so on. In luṭ: kunthatī and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, since here the num is that of a root with i as indicatory letter, the na is not elided: kuṣṭhya and so on. In lṛṭ: kunthiṣyati and so on. In lṛṅ: akunthiṣyata and so on; the rest should be applied in the same way.

The sūtra dhādādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ means "of the initial ṣa of a root, sa." The initial letter ṣa of a root such as ṣidhu changes to the letter sa. To the root ṣidhu, "in going," the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are joined; for the first person singular of laṭ: sedhati.

The sūtra upasargādsunotisuvatisyatistautistaudhatisthāsenayasebhasicasañjasvañjāṃ means "after an upasarga, of suniti, suvti, syati, stauti, stobhati, sthā, senaya, sedha, sica, sañja and sāñja." After a preceding upasarga that is a cause for the letter sa to change into the letter ṣa, the roots sunitaṃ and the rest, that is, ṣūta, "generating"; ṣūña, "driving"; ṣo, "the act of ending"; ṣṭuña, "praising"; ṣṭubha, "stiffening"; ṣṭhā, "standing"; ṣiña, "binding"; ṣibhu, "going"; ṣica, "dripping"; ṣañja, "clinging"; and ṣañja, "embracing": their initial letter ṣa, which by the sūtra "of the initial ṣa of a root, sa" had been changed from ṣa to sa, changes back into the letter ṣa.

The sūtra sadirprateḥ means "of sadi, when not after prati." Leaving aside prati, after an upasarga that is a cause for the change into ṣa, of sadi, that is, of the root ṣadli, "going," the sa that came from ṣa also changes back into ṣa.

The sūtra staṃbheḥ means "of stambhi." After a preceding upasarga that is such a cause, the letter sa of the root ṣṭabhi, "binding separately," also changes back into the letter ṣa.

The sūtra abāccālambanābidūryayoḥ means "also after ava, in the senses of support and nearness." After a preceding ava as well, when the letters of stambhi are used in the sense of support or of nearness, sa becomes the letter ṣa.

The sūtra peścasbanobhojane means "also after vi, of svana in the sense of food." By vi, and by the word "also," after a preceding ava too, when svanati is used in the sense of food, sa becomes the letter ṣa.

The sūtra parinibibhyaḥsebasitasyasibasahasuṭstuṣvañjuṃ means "after pari, ni and vi, of seba, sita, saya, siba, saha, stu, ṣvañja and suṭ."

After the preceding upasargas pari, ni and vi, the roots seva and the rest, that is, ṣebṛ, "seeing"; sitā and ṣiña, "binding"; ṣibu, "weaving cloth"; khaha, "enduring"; ṣṭuña, "praising"; and ṣvañja, "embracing": these, and the sa letters connected with suṭ, change into the letter ṣa.

When laṭ and the rest are joined to ṣidhu preceded by ni: in laṭ, niṣedhati and so on. In liṅ, nisedheta and so on. In loṭ, nisedhatu and so on.

The sūtra brakasitādaṭyabayoñbi means "before sita, even with aṭ intervening." After a preceding upasarga that is such a cause, the letter sa of sita, that is, of sunoti and the rest, becomes the letter ṣa even when the augment aṭ stands between. In laṅ, nyaṣedhata and so on. In luṅ, nyaṣedhita and so on.

The sūtra sthādiṣvabhyāsenacābhyāsasya means "for sthā and the rest, also of the abhyāsa, by the abhyāsa." After a preceding upasarga that is such a cause, when sthā and the rest have a doubled root with the part called the abhyāsa, that abhyāsa itself becomes the letter ṣa. In liṭ, niṣiṣedha: by this sūtra the first sa becomes ṣa, and by the rule of change throughout and so on the second sa becomes ṣa. niṣiṣidhituḥ, niṣiṣidhuḥ: by the sūtra "after what is not a conjunct," liṭ here is kit, and so there is no guṇa; and so on. In luṭ, niṣedhitā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, niṣidhyāta and so on. In lṛṭ, niṣedhiṣyati and so on; and in lṛṅ, nyaṣedhiṣyata and so on.

The sūtra sedhatergatau means "of sedhati, in the sense of going." Even when a preceding upasarga that is such a cause is present, the letter sa of the root ṣidha does not change into ṣa when the sense of going is expressed. When the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are joined to ṣidha, "going," preceded by ni: in laṭ, nisedhati and so on; when put into a phrase, nisedhatipāṃ. In liṅ, nisedheta and so on. In loṭ, nisedhatu and so on. In laṅ, nyasedhata and so on. In luṅ, nyasedhita and so on. In liṭ, nisisedha, nisisidhatuḥ, and so on. In luṭ, nisedhitā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, nisidhyāta and so on. In lṛṭ, "he makes the cattle go out definitely": nisedhiṣyati and so on. In lṛṅ, nyasidhiṣyata and so on.

The root ṣidhū, "in teaching" (by the sūtra "after what is not a conjunct," liṭ here is kit, and so the penultimate does not take guṇa) "and also in auspiciousness": the procedures for joining laṭ and the rest to this root (by the sūtra "in the benedictive, kit," the penultimate does not take guṇa) are likewise like those just explained, except that from luṅ onward, in the cases called ārdhadhātuka, they differ a little. In laṭ, sedhati and so on; in liṅ, sedheta and so on; in loṭ, sedhatu and so on; in laṅ, asedhata and so on.

In luṅ: the sūtra svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūditobā means "of svarati, sūyati, dhūñ and what has ū as indicatory letter, optionally." For the roots sbṛ, "in sound"; ṣūña and ṣūṅa, "giving birth"; bhū, "shaking"; and the roots with ū as indicatory letter, iṭ is optional before an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val. In the option where iṭ is given, for the first three persons: asedhīta, asedhīṣṭāṃ, asedhiṣāḥ. For the three middle persons: asedhiḥ, asedhiṣṭaṃ, asidhiṣṭa. For the three last persons: asedhiṣaṃ, asedhiṣva, asedhiṣma, and so on, like the earlier ones.

In the option where iṭ is not given, for the first person singular of luṅ: asaitsīta. Luṅ is added to ṣidhū; this is the sense of iṭ being optional for what has ū. By the sūtra "of the initial ṣa of a root, sa," ṣa becomes sa. By the sūtra on luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ and so on, aṭ is added to the root; its ṭa serves to fix the position and is an indicatory letter. La is changed to tip. By the sūtra "and of it," the i is dropped. In luṅ, by the sūtra on cli, cli is given; by the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic; c and i are dropped. By the sūtra on what ends in vad, vraj and a consonant, of the vowel, the penultimate of the root takes vṛddhi. By the sūtra of asti and sic before a single-letter affix, īṭ is added, its ṭ serving to fix the position. By the sūtra "car before khar," dh becomes t.

The sūtra jhalojhali means "of what follows jhal, before jhal." The sic that replaces cli after a root ending in a letter of the jhal group is elided before a following case ending that begins with a letter of the jhal group.

The sūtra jhaṣastathojhoñdhaḥ means "after a jhaṣ other than that of dhā, ta and tha become dha." After a root ending in a letter of the jhaṣ group, other than the root ḍujhāñ, the letters ta and tha change into the letter dha.

For the first person dual of luṅ: asaidhūṃ. Luṅ is added to ṣidhū. By the sūtra "of the initial ṣa of a root, sa," ṣa becomes sa. By the sūtra on luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ and so on, aṭ is added to the root. In luṅ, by the sūtra on cli, cli is given; by the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic. By the sūtra on what ends in vad, vraj and a consonant, of the vowel, the root takes vṛddhi; the indicatory letters are dropped, and la is changed to tas. By the sūtra on tas, thas, tha, mip and so on, tas is changed to tāṃ. By the sūtra "of what follows jhal, before jhal," sic is elided. By this sūtra, ta is changed to dha. By the sūtra on jaś for jhaś, the upper dha is changed to da.

For the first person plural: asisatsuḥ. For ṣidhū: by the sūtra "of the initial ṣa of a root, sa," ṣa becomes sa; by the sūtra on luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ and so on, aṭ is added to the root. In luṅ, by the sūtra on cli, cli is given; by the sūtra "sic for cli," it is changed to sic; a and c are dropped, and when the indicatory letters are dropped, la is changed to jhi. By the sūtra "also after sic, a reduplicated root and vid," jhi is changed to jus. By the sūtra on cu and ṭu and so on, the j is dropped. By the sūtra on what ends in vad, vraj and a consonant, of the vowel, the root takes vṛddhi. By the sūtra "car before khar," dh becomes t, derived as before.

For the three middle persons: asaitsī, asaiddhaṃ, asaiddha. For the three last persons: asaitsaṃ, asaitsma, asaitsma.

When the parasmaipada endings of liṭ are joined to ṣidhū, for the first three persons: sisedha, sisedha, sisetuḥ, sisedhuḥ. For the middle person singular, since iṭ is made optional: sisedhitha, sisidṅha. For the middle person dual and plural: sisedhathuḥ, sisedha. For the three last persons: sisedha, sisedhā: la becomes vas, vas is changed to va, and dh is brought in. sisedhma: la becomes mas, mas is changed to ma, and dh is brought in before ma.

When the parasmaipada endings of luṭ are joined to ṣidhū, iṭ being made optional, in the option where iṭ is given, for the first three persons: sedhitā, sedhitārau, sedhitāraḥ. For the three middle persons: sedhitāsi, sedhitāsthaḥ, sedhatāstha. For the three last persons: sedhitāmi, sedhitāsāḥ, sedhitāsmaḥ, and so on.

In the option where iṭ is not given, for the first three persons: seddhā, sedthārau, sadthāraḥ. For the three middle persons: sedthāsi, sedthāsthaḥ, sedthāstha. For the three last persons: sedthāmi, sedthāsvaḥ, sedthāsvaḥ, sedthāsmaḥ.

When the parasmaipada endings of the benedictive liṅ are joined to ṣidhū, for the first three persons: sidhyāta, sidhyāstaṃ, sidhyāsu. For the three middle persons: sidhyāḥ, sidhyastaṃ, sidhyasta. For the three last persons: sidhyāsaṃ, sidhyāsma, sidhyāsma.

When the parasmaipada endings of lṛṭ are joined to ṣidhū, giving iṭ and not giving it being made optional, in the option where iṭ is added, for the first three persons: sedhiṣyati, sedhiṣyataḥ, sidhiṣyanti. For the three middle persons: sedhiṣyasi, sedhiṣyathaḥ, sedhiṣyatha. For the three last persons: sedhiṣyāmi, sadhiṣyāmaḥ. In the option where iṭ is not given, for the first three persons: asetsyati, setsyataḥ, setsyanti, setsyanti. For the three middle persons: etmyasi, setsyathaḥ, setsyatha. For the three last persons: setsyāmi, setsyāvaḥ, setsyāmaḥ.

When the parasmaipada endings of lṛṅ are joined to ṣidhū, iṭ being made optional, in the option where iṭ is given, for the first three persons: asedhiṣyata, asedhiṣyatāṃ, asedhiṣyana. For the three middle persons: asedhiṣyataṃ, asedhiṣyata. For the three last persons: asedhiṣyaṃ, asedhiṣyāva, asedhaṣyāma. In the option where iṭ is not given, for the first three persons: asetsyata, asetsyatāṃ, asetsyana. For the three middle persons: asetsyaḥ, asetsyataṃ, asetsyata. For the three last persons: asetsyāṃ, asetsyāva, asetsyāma.

To the root khad, "in being firm, and also in harming," the procedures of joining the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are likewise like the earlier ones, except that the case of luṅ differs a little. Thus in laṭ, khadati and so on; in liṅ, khadeta and so on; in loṭ, khadtu and so on; in laṅ, akhadata and so on.

The sūtra atohalāderāghoḥ means "of the short a of what begins with a consonant." Before a sic that replaces cli and is followed by a parasmaipada ending, the short letter a that has entered as the vowel of a consonant, in a root that begins with a consonant, that is, one that is not a single vowel alone, optionally takes vṛddhi or does not. For the first person singular of luṅ: akhadīta, akhādīt. For the dual: akhadiṣṭāṃ, akhādiṣṭāṃ. For the plural: akhadiṣuḥ, akhādiṣuḥ, and so on.

The sūtra ataupadhāyāḥ means "of the penultimate a." Before an affix that has ñ or ṇ as indicatory letter, the penultimate letter a of the root takes vṛddhi. For the first person singular of liṭ: cakhāda. Liṭ is added to khad. By the sūtra "before liṭ, of a root without an abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the sūtra "the first consonant remains," the lower d is dropped. By the sūtra "of ku and h, cu," the upper kh becomes ch, and by the sūtra "and car in the abhyāsa," ch is changed to c. When the indicatory letters have been dropped, la is changed to tip. By the sūtra on ṇal and the rest for the parasmaipada endings, tip is changed to ṇal; and, as the special point, by this sūtra the penultimate a takes vṛddhi and so on, which is the purpose of the ṇ; the a is joined to d. For the dual and plural: cakhadatuḥ, cakhaduḥ. For the three middle persons: cakhaditha, cakhadathuḥ, cakhada.

The sūtra ṇaludhamobā means "optionally for the ṇal of the last person." Before the ṇal of the last person of liṭ, the penultimate a optionally takes vṛddhi or does not. For the last person singular: cakhāda, cakhada. For the dual and plural: cakhadiva, cakhadima. In luṭ, khaditā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, khadyāta and so on. In lṛṭ, khadiṣyati and so on. In lṛṅ, akhadiṣyata and so on.

To the root gad, "in speaking clearly," the procedures of joining the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are likewise like the earlier ones. In laṭ, gadati and so on. In liṅ, gadeta and so on. In loṭ, gadatu and so on. In laṅ, agadata and so on. In luṅ, since vṛddhi of the penultimate is made optional: aradīta, agādīta, and so on. In liṭ: jagāda, jagadatuḥ, jagaduḥ. For the three middle persons: jagaditha, jagadathuḥ, jagada. For the three last persons: jagāda, jagada, made with and without vṛddhi by the sūtra "optionally for the ṇal of the last person"; jagadima, jagadima. In luṭ, gaditā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, gadyāta (when the root has been pronounced twice, by the sūtra "of ku and h, cu," g is changed to j) and so on. In lṛṭ, gadiṣyataṃ and so on. In lṛṅ, agadiṣyata and so on.

The way the change occurs in the upasarga ni when the roots gad and the rest follow is this. The sūtra nergadandabatapadastumāsyatihantiyātipātidrātibsātibyatibahatiśāmyaticinotidegghīṣuca means: "of ni, before gad," "speaking clearly"; nad, "unclear sound"; pat, "in falling"; vad, "in going"; ghu, the roots called ghu, namely ḍudhāñ, "holding," and ḍudāñ, "giving"; mā, "in not being cut off"; syati, from ṣo, "in the act of ending"; hanti, from han, "in harming, and also in going"; yāti, "in causing to attain"; pāti, from vā, "in going, and also in smell"; drāti, from drā, "in censure"; psāti, from psā; vayati, from veñ, "in weaving"; vahati, from vaha, "in obtaining"; śāmyati, from śamu, "in calming"; cinoti, from ciñ, "in accumulating"; and deha, from deha, "in coating": "and these as well." When these roots, gad and the rest, follow, the letter na of the upasarga ni that comes after those upasargas that are causes for change into ṇa changes into ṇa. So when laṭ and the rest are joined to gad preceded by pra and ni, and the na of ni is changed to ṇa: praṇigadati and so on.

To the root rad, "in digging apart," the joining of the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest is like the earlier ones, except for a little in the case of liṭ. In laṭ, radita and so on. In liṅ, radeta and so on. In loṭ, radatu and so on; "he recites definitely and thoroughly." In laṅ, aradata and so on. In luṅ, since vṛddhi is made optional: arārīta, aradīta, and so on. For the first person singular of liṭ: rarāda.

The sūtra ataekahalmadhyeñnādeśādermiṭi means "in liṭ, of the a standing in the middle between single consonants, where the first is not a substitute."

Before a liṭ that has k as indicatory letter, when the first part of the root pronounced twice, the one called the abhyāsa, is not a substitute produced by a sūtra such as "and car in the abhyāsa" or "of ku and h, cu," then the middle, if the letter after it is not a conjunct but a single consonant, has its vowel a changed into the letter e, and the part called the abhyāsa is elided. For the first person dual and plural of liṭ: redtuḥ, reduḥ.

The sūtra thalicaseṭi means "and also before thal with iṭ." For the middle person singular of liṭ, red: liṭ is added to rad. By the sūtra "before liṭ, of a root without an abhyāsa," the root is pronounced twice. By the sūtra "the first consonant remains," the upper d is dropped. When the indicatory letters have been dropped, la is changed to tas and jhi; by the sūtra "of the parasmaipada endings," tas is changed to atus and jhi to us. By this sūtra the vowel of the latter becomes e and the abhyāsa is dropped, and d is joined to a and to us. Before thal accompanied by iṭ, too, it changes just as explained: raditha. For the middle and last persons: redthuḥ, red. For the last person singular, since vṛddhi is made optional: rarāda, rarada. For the dual and plural: rediva, redima. Luṭ and the rest are like the earlier ones. In luṭ, raditā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ (liṭ added to rad), radyāta and so on. In lṛṭ, radiṣyati and so on. In lṛṅ, aradiṣyata and so on.

The sūtra ṇinaḥ means "of ṇa, na." The initial letter ṇa of a root changes into the letter na. To the root ṇad, "in unclear sound," laṭ and the rest are joined, and by this sūtra ṇa is changed to na. All the other procedures are like the ones just explained. In laṭ, nadti and so on. In liṅ, nadata and so on. In loṭ, nadtu and so on. In laṅ, anadata and so on. In laṅ, anadata and so on. In luṅ, since vṛddhi is made optional: anādīta, anadīta, and so on. In liṭ: nanāda, medtuḥ, neduḥ, and so on. In luṭ, naditā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, nadyāta and so on. In lṛṭ, nadiṣyati and so on. In lṛṅ, anadiṣyata and so on; there is no differing procedure at all.

The sūtra upasrgādsamāse'pinopadeśasya means "after an upasarga, even when not in a compound, of what is taught with ṇa." What is taught with ṇa, that is, the letter na that was changed from ṇa by the sūtra "of ṇa, na" for the initial ṇa of a root, changes into ṇa after a preceding upasarga that is a cause for change into ṇa, whether in a compound or not in a compound. Laṭ is added to ṇad preceded by pra; by the sūtra "of ṇa, na," ṇa is changed to na; by this sūtra it is changed back to ṇa: praṇadati and so on.

To the root ard, "in going, and also in asking," the procedures of joining laṭ and the rest are likewise like those just explained, except for a little in the case of liṭ. In laṭ, ardati and so on. In liṅ, ardeta and so on. In loṭ, ardatu and so on; "a thoroughly unclear sound." In laṅ: ārdata. Laṅ is added to ard. By the sūtra "śap for the agent," śap is given and ś is dropped. When the indicatory letters have been dropped, la is changed to tip. By the sūtra "and of it," i is dropped. By the sūtra on luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ and so on, aṭ is added to the root, its ṭ serving to fix the position. By the sūtra "āṭ for those beginning with a vowel," āṭ too is given to the root, its ṭ serving to fix the position. By the sūtra "a long vowel for similar ak," the three, a, ā and a, become a single long vowel; and so on. In luṅ, ārditā and so on.

The sūtra ataādeḥ means "of an initial a." If the first part of the root pronounced twice, the one called the abhyāsa, is only the letter a, not one that has entered as the vowel of a consonant, that a becomes long.

The sūtra smānnuṭadvihalaḥ means "after that, nuṭ, for what has two consonants." (By the sūtra "āṭ for those beginning with a vowel," āṭ, its ṭ serving to fix the position, as explained above.) After the a that has become long, the augment nuṭ is given to the following letter a; and for this a doubled cluster of consonants must stand after that a. In liṭ: ānarda, ānardatuḥ, ānarduḥ. For the three middle persons: ānerditha, ānardathuḥ, ānarda. For the three last persons: ānārda, ānardiva, ānardima. In luṭ, ārditā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, ārdyāta. For ard: by the sūtra "of what has a single vowel, the second," a is pronounced twice; by the sūtra "of an initial a," the upper a becomes long; by this sūtra the augment nuṭ is given to the latter a, its ṭ serving to fix the position and its u for pronunciation; when the indicatory letters have been dropped, la is changed to tip, tas and jhi, and by the sūtra "of the parasmaipada endings," tip and the rest in order to ṇal, atus and us; and so on. In lṛṭ, ardiṣyati and so on. In lṛṅ, ārdiṣyat and so on.

To the root idi, "in supreme lordship," the procedures of joining the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are likewise for the most part the same. For the first three persons of laṭ: indati, indataḥ, intanti. (By the sūtra "āṭ for those beginning with a vowel," āṭ and the a of the root are joined in sandhi and become a single long a.) For the three middle persons: indasi, indathaḥ, indatha. For the three last persons: inbāmi, indāvaḥ, indāmaḥ. In liṅ (by the sūtra "num for what has i as indicatory letter," num is added to the root, its m serving to fix the position and its u for pronunciation), for the first three persons: indeta, indetāṃ, indeyuḥ. For the three middle persons of liṅ: inreḥ, indetaṃ, indetaṃ. For the three last persons: indayaṃ, indepa, indema. For the first three persons of loṭ: indatu, indatāt, indatāṃ, indantu. For the three middle persons: inda, indatāt, indataṃ, indata. For the three last persons: indāni, indāni, indāva, indāma.

The sūtra āḍajāṅīnāṃ means "āṭ for those beginning with a vowel." For roots beginning with a vowel, before luṅ, laṅ and lṛṅ, aṭ is not given; āṭ is given instead. For the first three persons of laṅ: aindata, endatāṃ, indana. For the three middle persons: ainṅaḥ, aindate, aindata. For the three last persons: aindaṃ, aindāva, ainrāma. For the first three persons of luṅ: aindīta, indiṣvaṃ, endeṣvaḥ. For the three middle persons: aindīḥ, endiṣṭaṃ, indiṣma. To idi, laṅ is added, with śap. By the sūtra "num for what has i as indicatory letter," num is added; that is the purpose of the i, while the m serves to fix the position and the u is for pronunciation. By this sūtra āṭ is added to the root, its ṭ serving to fix the position. By the sūtra "and after āṭ," vṛddhi. La becomes tip, and by the sūtra "and of it," the i is dropped. For the three last persons: indiṣvaṃ, indiṣma, indiṣma.

The sūtra ijādeścagurumatoñncchaḥ means "and also after what begins with ic and has a heavy vowel, other than ṛcch."

That is: if, after a root other than ṛccha "to go", that root being set aside, whose first letter is a letter of the abbreviation ic, and that ic letter moreover has a heavy syllable, there follow the endings that replace liṭ, then ām is given as a suffix at the end of that root. The m here does not serve to fix the position, so it is not dropped.

The sūtra āmaḥ means "after ām." After ām has been added to the root, all the endings that replace liṭ that follow it are elided.

The sūtra kṛñcānuprayujyate liṭi means "and kṛñ is employed after it, with liṭ." After a root to which ām has been added, kṛñ, an abbreviation, that is, kṛ, bhū and asti, is to be employed afterward, and liṭ is to be added to them.

The sūtra urat means "of ṛ, at." The first part of a reduplicated root, which has the name abhyāsa, if it is ṛ, becomes at, with r following.

For the first person singular of the parasmaipada of liṭ: indāṃ cakāra. For the dual and plural, by the sūtra "of ik, yaṇ before ac," ṛ is changed to r: indāṃ cakratuḥ, indāṃ cakruḥ.

The sūtra kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi means "with liṭ, after kṛ, sṛ, bhṛ, vṛ, stu, dru, sru and śru."

To the root idi, liṭ. By the sūtra "num for what has i as indicatory letter," num is added to the root, and the m and the u are dropped. By the sūtra "and also after what begins with ic and has a heavy vowel, other than ṛcch," ām is added to the root. By the sūtra "after ām," liṭ is elided. Thus indāṃ is formed. By the sūtra "and kṛñ is employed after it, with liṭ," kṛ is added, and by the sūtra on liṭ, liṭ is added to kṛ. By the sūtra "with liṭ, of a root without abhyāsa," the root is reduplicated. By this sūtra, ṛ becomes ar, with r following. By the sūtra "the first consonant remains," the r is also dropped. By the sūtra "of ku and h, cu," k becomes c. The indicatory letters are dropped, and la is changed to tip. By the sūtra "of the parasmaipada endings," tip is changed to ṇal. By the sūtra "of ac, before what has ñ or ṇ as indicatory letter," vṛddhi: ṛ becomes ār, with r following, and the r is joined to the a.

After kṛ "to do," sṛ "to go," bhṛñ "to bear," vṛñ "to cover," ṣṭuñ "to praise," dru and sru "to go," and śru "to hear," iṭ is not inserted in the liṭ that follows. For the middle person singular of liṭ: indāṃ cakartha. For the dual and plural: indāṃ cakrathuḥ, indāṃ cakra. For the last person singular, vṛddhi being made optional: indāṃ cakāra, indāṃ cakara. For the dual and plural: indāṃ cakṛma.

To indāṃ, once it has been formed, bhū and asti together with liṭ are also to be added. In adding liṭ to these two there is no further procedure beyond what has been explained in their respective places. With bhū: indāṃ babhūva, indāṃ babhūvatuḥ, indāṃ babhūvuḥ, and so on. Adding asti: indāmāsa, indāmāsuḥ, and so on.

For the three first persons of luṭ: inditā, inditārau, inditāraḥ. For the three middle persons: inditāsi, inditāsthaḥ, inditāstha. For the three last persons: inditāsmi, inditāsvaḥ, inditāsmaḥ.

For the three first persons of the benedictive liṅ: indyāt, indyāstām, indyāsuḥ. For the three middle persons: indyāḥ, indyāstam, indyāsta. For the three last persons: indyāsam, indyāsva, indyāsma.

For the three first persons of lṛṭ: indiṣyati, indiṣyataḥ, indiṣyanti. For the three middle persons: indiṣyasi, indiṣyathaḥ, indiṣyatha. For the three last persons: indiṣyāmi, indiṣyāvaḥ, indiṣyāmaḥ.

For the three first persons of lṛṅ: aindiṣyat, aindiṣyatām, aindiṣyan. For the three middle persons: aindiṣyaḥ, aindiṣyatam, aindiṣyata. For the three last persons: aindiṣyam, aindiṣyāva, aindiṣyāma.

For the root ṇidi, "in the sense of censure (kutsā)": the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest, including āṭ for roots beginning with ac by the sūtra "of those beginning with ac, āṭ," which is added to the root, and vṛddhi by the sūtra "and after āṭ," are to be applied by analogy with what was just explained. With laṭ: nindati and so on. With liṅ: nindet and so on. With loṭ: nindatu and so on. With laṅ: anindat and so on. With luṅ: anindīt and so on. With liṭ: nininda and so on. With luṭ: ninditā and so on, and with the benedictive liṅ: nindyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: nindiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: anindiṣyat and so on.

The sūtra vā niṃsanikṣanindām means "optionally, of niṃs, nikṣ and nind." After a preceding element that is the cause for the substitution of ṇ for n, the ṇ of these three, namely the two roots ṇisi and ṇikṣa, "in the sense of kissing," and ṇidi "in the sense of censure," just explained, which had become n, optionally becomes ṇ again or remains the letter n: praṇindati, "censures greatly"; pranindati, "censures greatly"; as in pranindati.

For the root ukha, "in the sense of going": the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are like the preceding ones, except for a slight difference in the case of liṭ. With laṭ: okhati and so on. With liṅ: okhet and so on. With loṭ: okhatu and so on. With laṅ: aukhat and so on. With luṅ: aukhīt and so on.

The sūtra abhyāsasyāsavarṇe means "of the abhyāsa, before a dissimilar vowel." When the first part of a reduplicated root, which has the name abhyāsa, is either u or i not joined as the vowel of a consonant, and a dissimilar ac follows it, u becomes uv and i becomes iy. By the sūtra "of those beginning with ac, āṭ," āṭ is added to the root, its ṭ serving to fix the position, and by the sūtra "and after āṭ," vṛddhi by the rule for ac.

For the first person singular of liṭ: uvokha. For the dual and plural: ūkhatuḥ, ūkhuḥ. To ukha, liṭ. By the sūtra "of the first part having a single ac, twice," u is reduplicated. The indicatory letters are dropped, and la is changed to tip. By the sūtra "of the parasmaipada endings," tip is changed to ṇal. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate," guṇa; by this sūtra u is changed to uv, and the rest is joined as before. For the three middle persons: uvokhitha, ūkhathuḥ, ūkha. For the three last persons: uvokha, ūkhiva, ūkhima. With luṭ: okhitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: ukhyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: okhiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: aukhiṣyat and so on.

For the root añcu, "in the sense of going and of honoring": the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are like the preceding ones, except for a small point of procedure, the eliding or not eliding of n in the case of the benedictive liṅ. With laṭ: añcati and so on. With loṭ: añcatu and so on. With laṅ: āñcat and so on. With luṅ: āñcīt and so on. With liṭ: ānañca. By the sūtra "of the initial a," the a is lengthened, and by the sūtra "after that, nuṭ, for what has two consonants," nuṭ is added as an augment, and so on. With luṭ: añcitā and so on.

With the benedictive liṅ: by the sūtra "kit in the benedictive," the endings are kit. When añc is used in the sense of going, the n is elided; but by the sūtra "not of añc in the sense of honoring," the n is not elided there. In the sense of going: acyāt and so on; in the sense of honoring: añcyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: añciṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: āñciṣyat and so on.

For the root mrucu, "in the sense of going": the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are like the preceding ones, except merely for the change of cli to aṅ or its change to sic, optionally, in the case of luṅ. With laṭ: mrocati and so on. With liṅ: mrocet and so on. With loṭ: mrocatu and so on. With laṅ: amrocat and so on.

The sūtra jṝstambhumrucumlucugrucuglucugluñcuśvibhyaśca means "and also after jṝ, stambhu, mrucu, mlucu, grucu, glucu, gluñcu and śvi." After the root jṝ "to grow old," stambhu, a root found only in the sūtras, mrucu, grucu and gluñcu "to go," mlucu and glucu "to steal," and ṭuośvi "in the sense of going and of growing," cli also optionally becomes aṅ. For the three first persons of the parasmaipada of luṅ, on the side where it is changed to aṅ: amrucat, amrucatām, amrucan, and so on. On the side where it is changed to sic: amrocīt, amrociṣṭām, amrociṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: mumroca, mumrocatuḥ, mumrocuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: mrocitā, mrocitārau, mrocitāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: mrucyāt, mrucyāstām, mrucyāsuḥ, and so on. With lṛṭ: mrociṣyati, mrociṣyataḥ, mrociṣyanti, and so on. With lṛṅ: amrociṣyat, amrociṣyatām, amrociṣyan, and so on. Likewise for mlucu, grucu, glucu and gluñcu, all the procedures are the same as those just explained, and in the case of the benedictive liṅ the nasal of gluñcu is elided.

For the root āchi, "in the sense of lengthening": the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are, by analogy, like the preceding ones, except for a slight difference in the case of liṭ. With laṭ: āñchati, num having been given by the sūtra "num for what has i as indicatory letter," and so on. With liṅ: āñchet and so on. With loṭ: āñchatu and so on. With laṅ: āñchat and so on. With luṅ: āñchīt and so on.

Cited in the commentary: āñchater dvihalo nuḍ vā, "for āñchati, which has two consonants, nuṭ optionally." When āchi is reduplicated, the nuṭ augment is optionally given to the former of the two stacked consonants. For the three first persons of liṭ, on the side where the nuṭ augment is given to the reduplicated root: ānāñcha, ānāñchatuḥ, ānāñchuḥ, and so on. On the side where nuṭ is not given: āñcha, āñchatuḥ, āñchuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: āñchitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: āñchyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: āñchiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: āñchiṣyat and so on.

The sūtra upadhāyāṃ ca means "and also of the penultimate." When the letter r or the letter v follows in a root, and its penultimate is a short letter of the abbreviation ik, it becomes long. To the root hurchā, "in the sense of being crooked," the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added, and by this sūtra the vowel is made long. With laṭ: hūrchati and so on. With liṅ: hūrchet and so on. With loṭ: ahūrchat and so on. With luṅ: ahūrchīt and so on. With liṭ: juhūrcha and so on. With luṭ: hūrchitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: hūrchyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: hūrchiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: ahūrchiṣyat and so on.

For the root vaja, "in the sense of going," too, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest follow by analogy the preceding ones, except in the case of liṭ. With laṭ: vajati and so on. With liṅ: vajet and so on. With loṭ: vajatu and so on. With laṅ: avajat and so on. With luṅ, vṛddhi being made optional: avajīt and so on, or else avājīt and so on.

The sūtra na śaśadadavādiguṇānām means "not of śaśa, dada, and what begins with v." When the root śaśa "to go far," dada "to give," and roots beginning with the letter v are reduplicated, the elision of the abhyāsa and the change of the following a to e and so on are not done. For the three first persons of liṭ: vavāja, vavajatuḥ, vavajuḥ. For the three middle persons: vavajitha, vavajathuḥ, vavaja. For the last person singular, vṛddhi being made optional: vavāja, vavaja. For the dual and plural: vavajiva, vavajima. With luṭ: vajitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: vajyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: vajiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: avajiṣyat and so on.

For the root vraja, "in the sense of going," the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are also like the preceding ones. With laṭ: vrajati and so on. With liṅ: vrajet and so on. With loṭ: vrajatu and so on. With laṅ: avrajat and so on. With luṅ: avrājīt, avrājiṣṭām, avrājiṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: vavrāja, vavrajatuḥ, vavrajuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: vrajitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: vrajyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: vrajiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: avrajiṣyat and so on. The sūtra vadavrajahalantasyācaḥ: vṛddhi of the vowel of vada, vraja and what ends in a consonant.

For the root aja, "in the sense of going and of throwing," too, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest in the four that are called sārvadhātuka are like the preceding ones. With laṭ: ajati and so on. With liṅ: ajet and so on. With loṭ: ajatu and so on. With laṅ: ājat and so on. Beginning from luṅ, the ones called ārdhadhātuka are slightly different.

The sūtra ajer vy aghañapoḥ means "of aja, vī, when it is not ghañ or ap." The root aja becomes vī when there follow suffixes such as the kṛt suffixes, other than ghañ and those beginning with a, that are called ārdhadhātuka. Cited in the commentary: valādāv ārdhadhātuke veṣyate, "it is held to be optional before an ārdhadhātuka beginning with val." Although it was explained above that the root aja becomes vī when what is called ārdhadhātuka follows, within that, when what follows is an ārdhadhātuka having at its beginning a letter of the abbreviation val, aja optionally becomes vī or does not.

The sūtra ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt means "not iṭ after what has a single ac in the instruction."

Setting aside roots ending in ū and roots ending in ṝ, and hu, ṣṇu, kṣṇu, śīṅ, yu, ṇu, kṣu, śvi, ḍī, śṛ, ḍī, śri, vṛṅ and vṛñ, after the roots that have a single ac and have no consonant at their end, iṭ does not come before what begins with val. And although they are not roots with a single ac and no final consonant, after these roots too iṭ does not come before what begins with val: śakḷ, ghasḷ, rabha, yabha, labha, labha, yamu, ramu, mana, ṇama, hana, gamḷ, diha, duha, miha, ṇaha, vaha, liha, ruha, daha, diśa, dṛśa, daṃśa, spṛśa, mṛśa, viśa, ruśa, kruśa, liśa, riśa, ṣidha, rudhir, rādha, sādha, yudha, śudha, budha, krudha, kṣudha, vyadha, bandha, śuṣa, puṣa, śliṣa, duṣa, dviṣa, piṣḷ, piṣḷ, tviṣa, ruṣa, śekṛ, the two kṛṣa, "in the sense of harming" and kṛṣa "in the sense of ploughing," tapa, opyāyī, ṭuvapa, ñiṣvapa, lipa, lapa, stṛpa, dṛpa, sṛpa, śapa, chupa, kṣipa, skandir, hada, chidir, bhidir, kṣudir, ada, śadḷ, ṣadḷ, khida, nuda, tuda, ñiṣvidā, pada, vanu, vida, vidḷ, ḍupacaṣ, vaca, vica, rica, pracha, rañja, ṇijir, ṣica, mucḷ, bhaja, bhañju, bhrasja, yaja, tyaja, yujir, ṣañja, ruja, ṣvañja, sṛja, maja, bhuja, mijir, and so on.

For the three first persons of luṅ, on the side where aja does not become vī: ājīt, ājiṣṭām, ājiṣuḥ. For the three middle persons: ājīḥ, ājiṣṭam, ājiṣṭa. For the three last persons: ājiṣam, ājiṣva, ājiṣma.

On the side where aja becomes vī: the sūtra sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu means "vṛddhi with sic, in the parasmaipada." If the root ends in a letter of the abbreviation ik, vṛddhi takes place when sic follows together with the parasmaipada endings. For the three first persons of luṅ: avaiṣīt, avaiṣṭām, avaiṣuḥ. For the three middle persons: avaiṣīḥ, avaiṣṭam, avaiṣṭa. For the three last persons: avaiṣam, avaiṣma.

For the three first persons of liṭ: vivāya, vivyatuḥ, vivyuḥ.

The sūtra acas tāsvat thaly aniṭo nityam means "after ac, for thal, as with tās, iṭ never." After a root that has a single ac and no final consonant, iṭ never comes for thal, just as with tās.

The sūtra ṛto bhāradvājasya means "after ṛt, in the view of Bhāradvāja." Although it was said above that for tās and thal iṭ never comes after a root having a single ac and no final consonant, as an exception to that, the ancient sage Bhāradvāja holds that iṭ is inserted after roots ending in ṛt, and after those having a single ac and no final consonant, also for thal, tās, and what begins with val. Therefore in the case of thal three forms arise here. By the statement "it is held to be optional before an ārdhadhātuka beginning with val," aja optionally becomes vī or does not, and on the side where it becomes vī, iṭ is made optional by these two sūtras: ājitha, vivayitha, viveta. For the dual and plural of the middle person: vivyathuḥ, vivya. For the last person singular, vṛddhi and guṇa being made optional: vivāya, vivaya. For the dual and plural, becoming vī or remaining as aja being made optional: ājiva, ājima. On the side where it becomes vī, iṭ being made optional: viviyiva, viviyima. On the side without iṭ: vivīva, vivīma.

For the three first persons of luṭ, on the side where aja is not changed to vī: ajitā, ajitārau, ajitāraḥ. For the three middle persons: ajitāsi, ajitāsthaḥ, ajitāstha. For the three last persons: ajitāsmi, ajitāsvaḥ, ajitāsmaḥ. For the three first persons, on the side where aja is changed to vī: vetā, vetārau, vetāraḥ. For the three middle persons: vetāsi, vetāsthaḥ, vetāstha. For the three last persons: vetāsmi, vetāsvaḥ, vetāsmaḥ. If iṭ is added as the sage Bhāradvāja holds: vayitā, vayitārau, vayitāraḥ, and so on.

With the benedictive liṅ there is no further procedure. For the three first persons: vīyāt, vīyāstām, vīyāsuḥ. For the three middle persons: vīyāḥ, vīyāstam, vīyāsta. For the three last persons: vīyāsam, vīyāsva, vīyāsma.

For the three first persons of lṛṭ, on the side where aja is not changed to vī: ajiṣyati, ajiṣyataḥ, ajiṣyanti. For the three middle persons: ajiṣyasi, ajiṣyathaḥ, ajiṣyatha. For the three last persons: ajiṣyāmi, ajiṣyāvaḥ, ajiṣyāmaḥ. For the three first persons, on the side where aja is changed to vī: veṣyati, veṣyataḥ, veṣyanti. For the three middle persons: veṣyasi, veṣyathaḥ, veṣyatha. For the three last persons: veṣyāmi, veṣyāvaḥ, veṣyāmaḥ. If iṭ is added as Bhāradvāja holds: vayiṣyati, vayiṣyataḥ, vayiṣyanti, and so on.

For the three first persons of lṛṅ, on the side where aja is not changed to vī: ājiṣyat, ājiṣyatām, ājiṣyan. For the three middle persons: ājiṣyaḥ, ājiṣyatam, ājiṣyata. For the three last persons: ājiṣyam, ājiṣyāva, ājiṣyāma. For the three first persons, on the side where aja is changed to vī: aveṣyat, aveṣyatām, aveṣyan. For the three middle persons: aveṣyaḥ, aveṣyatam, aveṣyata. For the three last persons: aveṣyam, aveṣyāva, aveṣyāma. If iṭ is given as the sage Bhāradvāja holds: avayiṣyat, avayiṣyatām, avayiṣyan, and so on; the rest follows by analogy.

For the root kṣi, "in the sense of wasting away," too, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are for the most part like those just explained. With laṭ: kṣayati and so on. With liṅ: kṣayet and so on. With loṭ: kṣayatu and so on. With laṅ: akṣayat and so on. With luṅ: akṣaiṣīt, akṣaiṣṭām, akṣaiṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: cikṣāya, cikṣiyatuḥ, cikṣiyuḥ. For the three middle persons: cikṣayitha, cikṣetha, cikṣiyathuḥ, cikṣiya. For the last person singular: cikṣāya, cikṣaya. For the dual: cikṣiyiva, cikṣiva. For the plural: cikṣiyima, cikṣima. With luṭ, iṭ being made optional: kṣetā or kṣayitā, and so on.

The sūtra akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ means "long, before what is neither kṛt nor sārvadhātuka."

When there follow suffixes beginning with the letter y and called kit or ṅit, which are endings, ārdhadhātuka or sārvadhātuka, not belonging to the kṛt suffixes and the rest, the ac at the end of the root becomes long. With the benedictive liṅ: kṣīyāt, kṣīyāstām, kṣīyāsuḥ, and so on. With lṛṭ, iṭ being made optional: kṣeṣyati or kṣayiṣyati, and so on. With lṛṅ too: akṣeṣyat or akṣayiṣyat, and so on.

For the root kaṭe, "in the sense of raining and of covering," the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are also like the preceding ones, except for the single difference that vṛddhi is not done in the case of luṅ. With laṭ: kaṭati and so on. With liṅ: kaṭet and so on. With loṭ: kaṭatu and so on. With laṅ: akaṭat and so on.

The sūtra hmyantakṣaṇaśvasajāgṛṇiśvyeditām means "of what ends in h, m and y, of kṣaṇa, śvasa, jāgṛ, ṇi and śvi, and of what has e as indicatory letter." When the replacement of cli, sic, beginning with iṭ, follows, vṛddhi does not take place for roots ending in the letter h, the letter m or the letter y; for kṣaṇu "to harm," śvasa "to breathe," jāgṛ "to wake," and ṭuośvi "to go and to grow"; for any root to which the suffix ṇi has been added; and for roots with e as indicatory letter. Here, since kaṭe has e as indicatory letter, vṛddhi is not done in luṅ: akaṭīt, akaṭiṣṭām, akaṭiṣuḥ, and so on.

For the three first persons of liṭ: cakāṭa, cakaṭatuḥ, cakaṭuḥ. For the three middle persons: cakaṭitha, cakaṭathuḥ, cakaṭa. For the three last persons: cakāṭa, cakaṭa, cakaṭiva, cakaṭima. With luṭ: kaṭitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: kaṭyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: kaṭiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: akaṭiṣyat and so on.

The sūtra gupūdhūpavicchipaṇipanibhya āyaḥ means "āya after gupū, dhūpa, vicchi, paṇi and pani." After these roots, gupū "to protect," dhūpa "to heat," viccha "to go," and paṇa and pana, "in the sense of transaction," āya comes in their own meaning. It is a suffix that makes a root into a further root.

The sūtra sanādyantā dhātavaḥ means "what ends in san and the rest are roots." What ends in the suffixes san and the rest when they have been added, and what ends in kamu with ṇiṅ added, also remain roots. These are called suffixes that form a root from a root, and suffixes that form a root from a noun.

To gupū "to protect," āya is added. The letter ū has the purpose of being ūdit. By the sūtra "and of what ends in puk and has a short penultimate," guṇa. Having made the root into a root, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added, and the procedures are like the preceding ones. With laṭ: gopāyati and so on. With liṅ: gopāyet and so on. With loṭ: gopāyatu and so on. With laṅ: agopāyat and so on.

For the ārdhadhātuka endings it is made optional. The sūtra āyādaya ārdhadhātuke vā means "āya and the rest, optionally, before an ārdhadhātuka." The suffixes āya and the rest come optionally when what is called ārdhadhātuka follows. The sūtra ato lopaḥ means "elision of a." The a at the end of a suffix is elided when what is called ārdhadhātuka follows.

For the three first persons of luṅ, on the side where āya is added to gupū: agopāyīt, agopāyiṣṭām, agopāyiṣuḥ. For the three middle persons: agopāyīḥ, agopāyiṣṭam, agopāyiṣṭa. For the three last persons: agopāyiṣam, agopāyiṣva, agopāyiṣma. On the side where āya is not given, iṭ is made optional by the sūtra on roots with ū as indicatory letter and the rest. On the side where iṭ is added: agopīt, agopiṣṭām, agopiṣuḥ, and so on. For the three first persons, on the side where iṭ is not given: agaupsīt, agauptām, agaupsuḥ. For the three middle persons: agaupsīḥ, agauptam, agaupta. For the three last persons: agaupsam, agaupsva, agaupsma.

For liṭ: the sūtra kāspratyayād ām amantre liṭi means "ām with liṭ, after kās and after a suffix, when not in a mantra." By the sūtra "of jhal, before jhal," the s is dropped. Kāsṛ is "in the sense of a bad sound," and "mantra" expresses the sense of invocation. After kās, from which the s has not been dropped by the sūtra "of jhal, before jhal," and after what ends in the suffixes san and the rest, when liṭ follows, ām is to be added at the end of the root. To gopāya, liṭ. By this sūtra ām is added. By the sūtra "after ām," liṭ too is elided. By adding afterward kṛñ, bhū, as and the rest together with liṭ: gopāyāmāsa, gopāyāṃ babhūva, and so on.

Or else āya is not added. For the three first persons: jugopa, jugupatuḥ, jugupuḥ. For the three middle persons: jugopitha, jugoptha, jugupathuḥ, jugupa. For the last person singular: jugopa. For the dual, iṭ being made optional by the sūtra on roots with ū as indicatory letter and the rest: jugupiva, jugupva. For the plural too: jugupima, jugupma.

With luṭ, on the side where āya is added to gupū: gopāyitā and so on. On the side where āya is not added, iṭ being made optional: gopitā or goptā, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, on the side where āya is added to gup, by the sūtra "elision of a" the a at the end of the root is dropped and the rest is joined: gopāyyāt and so on; or else, not adding āya: gupyāt and so on. With lṛṭ, on the side where āya is added to gupū: gopāyiṣyati and so on. On the side where āya is not added, iṭ being made optional: gopiṣyati or gopsyati, and so on. Likewise with lṛṅ: agopāyiṣyat and so on, or agopiṣyat and so on, or agopsyat and so on.

For the root dhūpa, "in the sense of heating," too, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are like those just explained. With laṭ: dhūpāyati and so on. With liṅ: dhūpāyet and so on. With loṭ: dhūpāyatu and so on. With laṅ: adhūpāyat and so on. With luṅ: adhūpāyīt or adhūpīt, and so on. With liṭ: dhūpāyāmāsa and so on, or else dudhūpa, dudhūpatuḥ, dudhūpuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: dhūpāyitā and so on, or else dhūpitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: dhūpāyyāt and so on, or else dhūpyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: dhūpāyiṣyati and so on, or else dhūpiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: adhūpāyiṣyat and so on, or else adhūpiṣyat and so on.

For the root tapa, "in the sense of heating," the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are for the most part like the preceding ones. However, although the root tapa belongs to the class that does not take iṭ, the commentary explains that for tapa iṭ comes in the three, thal, va and ma, of liṭ. With laṭ: tapati and so on. With liṅ: tapet and so on. With loṭ: tapatu and so on. With laṅ: atapat and so on.

For the three first persons of luṅ: atāpsīt, atāptām, atāpsuḥ. For the three middle persons: atāpsīḥ, atāptam, atāpta. For the three last persons: atāpsam, atāpsva, atāpsma. By the sūtra "after jhal, before jhal," sic is dropped.

For the three first persons of liṭ: tatāpa, tepatuḥ, tepuḥ. For the three middle persons: tepitha, tepathuḥ, tepa. For the three last persons: tatāpa, tatapa, tepiva, tepima. With luṭ: taptā, taptārau, taptāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: tapyāt, tapyāstām, tapyāsuḥ, and so on. With lṛṭ: tapsyati, tapsyataḥ, tapsyanti, and so on. With lṛṅ: atapsyat, atapsyatām, atapsyan, and so on.

The sūtra ṣṭhivuklamvācamāṃ śiti means "of ṣṭhivu, klamu and ācamu, before what has ś as indicatory letter." The ac of the roots ṣṭhivu "to spit out," klamu "to be weary," and camu "to eat" preceded by the prefix āṅ, becomes long when a suffix having ś as indicatory letter follows.

When the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added to the root camu, "in the sense of eating," preceded by the prefix āṅ: ācāmati and so on. When the prefix āṅ does not precede, it does not become long. With laṭ: camati and so on. With liṅ: camet and so on. With loṭ: camatu and so on. With laṅ: acamat and so on. With luṅ: acamīt, acamiṣṭām, acamiṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: cacāma, cematuḥ, cemuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: camitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: camyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: camiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: acamiṣyat, acamiṣyatām, acamiṣyan, and so on.

The sūtra vā bhrāśabhlāśabhramukramuklamutrasitruṭilaṣaḥ means "optionally after bhrāśa, bhlāśa, bhramu, kramu, klamu, trasī, truṭi and laṣa." After the roots bhrāśṛ and ṭubhlāśṛ "to blaze," bhramu "to move about," kramu "to step," klamu "to be weary," trasī "to be distressed," truṭi "to cut," and laṣa "to be beautiful," in the domain of śap, given by the sūtra "śap for the agent," śyan optionally comes.

For the root kramu, "in the sense of stepping," on the side where śyan is given in adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest: with laṭ, kramyati and so on. With liṅ: kramyet and so on. With loṭ: kramyatu and so on. With laṅ: akramyat and so on.

On the side where śap is given: the sūtra kramaḥ parasmaipadeṣu means "of kram, before the parasmaipada endings." The letter a, the penultimate of the root kram, becomes long when the parasmaipada endings follow together with śap. With laṭ: krāmati and so on. With liṅ: krāmet and so on. With loṭ: krāmatu and so on. With laṅ: akrāmat and so on.

The sūtra snukramor anātmanepadanimitte means "after snu and kram, when it is not a cause of the ātmanepada." After the roots snu and kram, iṭ comes when what begins with val follows, setting aside the ātmanepada endings that have a cause for the ātmanepada. With luṅ: akramīt, akramiṣṭām, akramiṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: cakrāma, cakramatuḥ, cakramuḥ, cakramitha, cakramathuḥ, cakrama, and so on. With luṭ: kramitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: kramyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: kramiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: akramiṣyat and so on.

The sūtra iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ means "ch of iṣu, gam and yam." When a suffix having ś as indicatory letter follows, the final letters of the roots iṣu "to desire," gamḷ "to go," and yamu "to restrain," that is, the two m's and the ṣ, become the letter ch.

To the root yamu, "in the sense of restraining," the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added. By the sūtra "śap for the agent," śap; by this sūtra, m becomes ch. With laṭ: yacchati and so on. With liṅ: yacchet and so on. With loṭ: yacchatu and so on. With laṅ: ayacchat and so on.

The sūtra yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca means "and sak, of yam, ram, nam and what ends in ā." For the three roots yamu "to restrain," ramu "to play," and ṇamu "to bow," and for those ending in ā, such as yā "to obtain," when sic, the replacement of cli, follows, the augment sak comes, and iṭ also comes to sic. To yamu, luṅ, sic; by this sūtra sak, the k serving to fix the position and the a for pronunciation. For the three first persons: ayaṃsīt, ayaṃsiṣṭām, ayaṃsiṣuḥ. For the three middle persons: ayaṃsīḥ, ayaṃsiṣṭam, ayaṃsiṣṭa. For the three last persons: ayaṃsiṣam, ayaṃsiṣva, ayaṃsiṣma.

For the three first persons when liṭ is added to yamu: yayāma, yematuḥ, yemuḥ. For the three middle persons: yemitha, yayantha, yemathuḥ, yema. For the three last persons: yayāma, yayama, yemiva, yemima. With luṭ: yantā, yantārau, yantāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: yamyāt, yamyāstām, yamyāsuḥ, and so on. With lṛṭ: yaṃsyati, yaṃsyataḥ, yaṃsyanti, and so on. With lṛṅ: ayaṃsyat, ayaṃsyatām, ayaṃsyan, and so on.

For the root ṇamu, "in the sense of bowing deeply and of sound," the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are also like those just explained. With laṭ: namati and so on. With liṅ: namet and so on. With loṭ: namatu and so on. With laṅ: anamat and so on. With luṅ: anaṃsīt and so on. With liṭ: nanāma, nematuḥ, nemuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: nantā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: namyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: naṃsyati and so on. With lṛṅ: anaṃsyat and so on.

For the root haya, "in the sense of going," the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest also follow by analogy the preceding ones. With laṭ: hayati and so on. With liṅ: hayet and so on. With loṭ: hayatu and so on. With laṅ: ahayat and so on. With luṅ: ahayīt and so on. With liṭ: jahāya, jahayatuḥ, jahayuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: hayitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: hayyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: hayiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: ahayiṣyat and so on.

For the root dala, "in the sense of splitting apart," too, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are like the preceding ones, except merely for the difference that vṛddhi is done in luṅ. With laṭ: dalati and so on. With liṅ: dalet and so on. With loṭ: dalatu and so on. With laṅ: adalat and so on.

The sūtra ato lrāntasya means "of the a of what ends in l or r." The a of the penultimate of a root that has the letter l or the letter r at its end takes vṛddhi when sic followed by the parasmaipada endings comes after it: adālīt, adāliṣṭām, adāliṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: dadāla, delatuḥ, deluḥ, and so on. With luṭ: dalitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: dalyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: daliṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: adaliṣyat and so on.

The sūtra ādir ñiṭuḍavaḥ means "initial ñi, ṭu and ḍu."

The initial ñi, ṭu and ḍu of a root are termed "it" and are to be elided.

For the root ñiphalā, in the sense of dispersing: by this sūtra the ñi is dropped, and the procedure for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest is like the previous ones. With laṭ: phalati and so on. With liṅ: phalata and so on. With liṅ: phalet and so on. With loṭ: phalatu and so on. With laṅ: aphalat and so on. With luṅ: aphālīt, aphāliṣṭām, aphāliṣuḥ, and so on. In the first person singular of liṭ: paphāla.

The sūtra tṝphalabhajatrapaś ca means "and of tṝ, phal, bhaj and trap as well." When liṭ endings termed "it" with k or ṅ follow, and when thal with iṭ follows, the reduplicated syllable of the roots tṝ, in the sense of swimming across, ñiphalā, in the sense of dispersing, bhaja, in the sense of serving, and trapūṣ, in the sense of being ashamed, is elided, and the vowel also becomes e. In the first person dual: phelatuḥ; plural: pheluḥ. In the three of the middle person: phelitha, phelathuḥ, phela. In the three of the last person: paphāla or paphala, pheliva, phelima. With luṭ: phalitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: phalyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: phaliṣyati. With lṛṅ: aphaliṣyat and so on.

For the root ṇikṣa, in the sense of kissing, the forms made by adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest likewise follow the pattern of the previous ones. With laṭ: nikṣati and so on. With liṅ: nikṣet and so on. With loṭ: nikṣatu and so on. With laṅ: anikṣat and so on. With luṅ: anikṣīt and so on. With liṭ: ninikṣa and so on. With luṭ: nikṣitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: nikṣyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: nikṣiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: anikṣiṣyat and so on.

For the root tsara, in the sense of going in disguise, the procedure for adding the parasmaipada endings is like the previous ones. With laṭ: tsarati and so on. With liṅ: tsaret and so on. With loṭ: tsaratu and so on. With laṅ: atsarat and so on. With luṅ: atsārīt and so on. With liṭ: tatsāra, tatsaratuḥ, tatsaruḥ, and so on. With luṭ: tsaritā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: tsaryāt and so on. With lṛṭ: tsariṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: atsariṣyat and so on.

Cited in the commentary: subhūtuṣyai. The rule "of the a of what ends in l or r" applies. The penultimate: long. The sūtra subdhātuṣṭhivuṣvaṣkatīnāṃ satvapratiṣedhaḥ means "not so for nominal roots, ṣṭyai, ṣvaṣk and ṣṭhiv." For nominal roots, for the root ṣṭyai, in the sense of sound and of massing together, for ṣvaṣka, in the sense of going, and for ṣṭhivu, in the sense of spitting, the initial letter ṣ does not become the letter s.

For the root ṣṭhivu, in the sense of spitting, laṭ and the rest are added; by this rule ṣ does not become s, and the rest of the procedure is like the previous ones. With laṭ: ṣṭhīvati and so on. With liṅ: ṣṭhīvet and so on. With loṭ: ṣṭhīvatu and so on. With laṅ: aṣṭhīvat and so on. With luṅ: aṣṭhevīt and so on.

Cited in the commentary: ṣṭhiveḥ abhyāsasya ṭhakāraḥ thakāro vā, that is, "of the reduplicated syllable of ṣṭhivu, the letter ṭha or the letter tha." The rule "of ṣṭhivu, klamu and the rest, long before an affix with ś as its it" applies, and optionally. When ṣṭhivu is reduplicated, in the part termed the reduplicated syllable, the rule "the khay consonants preceded by a śar" applies: the letter ṭha left after ṣ is dropped becomes the letter ṭha itself, or else tha. In the first person singular of liṭ: ṭiṣṭheva or tiṣṭheva. In the dual: ṭiṣṭhevatuḥ or tiṣṭhevatuḥ. In the plural: ṭiṣṭhevuḥ or tiṣṭhevuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: ṣṭhevitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: ṣṭhīvyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: ṣṭheviṣyati and so on, and with lṛṅ: aṣṭheviṣyat and so on.

The rule "in the reduplicated syllable, car as well" applies: in the option where it is changed to ṭha, it becomes ṭa, and in the option where it is changed to tha, it is changed to ta. Ṭa is an it, and so on: ṭi, e.
