For the root ji, in the sense of conquering, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added, and apart from a little in the case of liṭ, the procedure follows the pattern of the previous ones. With laṭ: jayati and so on. With liṅ: jayet and so on. With loṭ: jayatu and so on. With laṅ: ajayat and so on. With luṅ: ajaiṣīt, ajaiṣṭām, ajaiṣuḥ, and so on.

The sūtra sanliṭor jeḥ means "of ji, before san and liṭ." When san or liṭ follows, the latter consonant of the reduplicated root ji becomes the corresponding member of the ka series. In the three of the first person of liṭ: jigāya, jigyatuḥ, jigyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jigayitha or jigetha, jigyathuḥ, jigya. In the three of the last person: jigāya or jigaya, jigyiva, jigyima. With luṭ: jetā, jetāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: jīyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: jeṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: ajeṣyat and so on.

For the root turvī, in the sense of harming, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are likewise like the previous ones. With laṭ: tūrvati and so on. With liṅ: tūrvet and so on. The rule of lengthening applies for those that are not kṛt and sārvadhātuka affixes: long. With loṭ: tūrvatu and so on. With laṅ: atūrvat and so on. With luṅ: atūrvīt and so on. With liṭ: tutūrva and so on. With luṭ: tūrvitā and so on. The rule "of the penultimate as well" applies: long. With the benedictive liṅ: tūrvyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: tūrviṣyati and so on, and with lṛṅ: atūrviṣyat and so on.

For the root rakṣa, in the sense of protecting, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added, and the procedure is like the previous ones. With laṭ: rakṣati and so on, and with liṅ: rakṣet and so on. With liṭ: rakṣatu and so on. With laṅ: arakṣat and so on. With luṅ: rarakṣuḥ and so on. With luṭ: rakṣitā and so on. With liṭ: rarakṣa, rarakṣatuḥ, rarakṣuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: rakṣitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: rakṣyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: rakṣiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: arakṣiṣyat and so on.

The sūtra akṣo 'nyatarasyām means "from akṣa, optionally." For the root akṣū, in the sense of pervading and also of massing together, when the affixes termed sārvadhātuka follow, then in the domain of śap, prescribed by the rule "śap in the active," śnu optionally occurs. In the option where śap is added to akṣa, with laṭ: akṣati and so on. With liṅ: akṣet and so on. With loṭ: akṣatu and so on. With laṅ: ākṣat and so on. In the option where śnu is added, in the three of the first person of laṭ: akṣṇoti, akṣṇutaḥ, akṣṇuvanti. In the three of the middle person: akṣṇoṣi, akṣṇuthaḥ, akṣṇutha. In the three of the last person: akṣṇomi, akṣṇuvaḥ, akṣṇumaḥ. In the first person singular and dual of liṅ: akṣṇuyāt, akṣṇuyātām. For the plural, the sūtra usy apadāntāt means "when us follows, from what is not word-final."

Jhi is changed to jus, and the j is dropped, leaving us. When us follows, a non-final ā, for the two together, becomes the single form of the following vowel: akṣṇuyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: akṣṇuyāḥ, akṣṇuyātam, akṣṇuyāta. In the three of the last person: akṣṇuyām, akṣṇuyāva, akṣṇuyāma.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: akṣṇotu or akṣṇutāt, akṣṇutām, akṣṇuvantu. In the three of the middle person: akṣṇuhi or akṣṇutāt, akṣṇutam, akṣṇuta. In the three of the last person: akṣṇavāni, akṣṇavāva, akṣṇavāma.

In the three of the first person of laṅ: ākṣṇot, ākṣṇutām, ākṣṇuvan. In the three of the middle person: ākṣṇoḥ, ākṣṇutam, ākṣṇuta. In the three of the last person: ākṣṇavam, ākṣṇuva, ākṣṇuma.

With luṅ, by the rule "ū as it" and the rest, iṭ is made optional. In the option where iṭ is added: ākṣīt, ākṣiṣṭām, ākṣiṣuḥ, and so on, which are easy to understand. In the option without iṭ, in the first person singular: the sūtra ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si means "before s, k for ṣ and ḍh." When the letter s follows, the letters ṣ and ḍh become the letter k: ākṣīt.

The derivation: to akṣa, luṅ. With luṅ, the rule for cli applies, and cli is given. The rule "sic for cli" applies, and it is changed to sic. The c and the i are dropped. The rule "āṭ of those beginning with a vowel" applies: āṭ is written at the beginning of the root and the sandhi is made. The l is changed to tip. For the purpose of itaś ca, the rule "and of it" applies, and the i is dropped. The rule astisico 'pṛkte gives īṭ; the ṭ serves to mark its position. The rule "of s and k at the beginning of a cluster" applies, and the k sound is dropped. The rule "before s, k for ṣ and ḍh" applies, and ṣ is changed to k. By the rule of substitution and the rest, s becomes ṣ; k and ṣ are joined as kṣ, and īt is drawn in.

In the dual: āṣṭām. The derivation: to akṣa, luṅ. With luṅ, the rule for cli applies, and cli is given. The rule "sic for cli" applies, and it is changed to sic. The rule "āṭ of those beginning with a vowel" applies: āṭ to the root. By "of s and k at the beginning of a cluster" and the rest, the k is dropped. It is changed to tas. By "tas, thas" and the rest, tas is changed to tām. The rule "of s after a jhal before a jhal" applies, and the sic disappears. The rule ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ applies, and ṭ is drawn in after ṣ.

In the first person plural: ākṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ākṣīḥ, āṣṭam, āṣṭa. In the last person singular: ākṣam. In the dual and plural: ākṣva, ākṣma.

The derivation: to akṣa, luṅ. With luṅ, the rule for cli applies, and cli is given. Cli becomes si; the rule for c applies, and it is changed to sic. The l is changed to jhi. The rule "jus for jhi" applies: jus. By cuṭū and the rest, the j is dropped. By "āṭ of those beginning with a vowel," āṭ. By "at the beginning of a cluster" and the rest, the k is dropped. By the rule called "of ṣ and ḍh before s," ṣ becomes k. By the rule of substitution and the rest, s becomes ṣ. K and ṣ are joined as kṣ, and us is drawn in: ākṣuḥ.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: ānakṣa, ānakṣatuḥ, ānakṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ānakṣitha, ānakṣathuḥ, ānakṣa. In the three of the last person: ānakṣa, ānakṣima.

With luṭ, since iṭ has been made optional, in the option where iṭ is added: akṣitā, akṣitārau, akṣitāraḥ, and so on. In the option without iṭ: by "at the beginning of a cluster," the rule for k applies and the k is dropped; the rule ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ applies and ṭā is drawn in, giving aṣṭā, aṣṭārau, aṣṭāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: akṣyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: akṣiṣyati, akṣiṣyataḥ, akṣiṣyanti, and so on; or akṣyati, akṣyataḥ, akṣyanti, and so on. With lṛṅ: ākṣiṣyat, ākṣiṣyatām, ākṣiṣyan, and so on; or else ākṣyat, ākṣyatām, ākṣyan, and so on.

The sūtra tanūkaraṇe takṣaḥ means "of takṣū, in the sense of making thin." When the root takṣū is used in the sense of making thin, śnu optionally occurs in the domain of śap. With laṭ: takṣati and so on, or takṣṇoti and so on. With liṅ: takṣet and so on, or takṣṇuyāt and so on. With loṭ: takṣatu and so on, or takṣṇotu and so on. With laṅ: atakṣat and so on, or atakṣṇot and so on. With luṅ, since iṭ has been made optional, in the option where iṭ is given: atakṣīt, atakṣiṣṭām, atakṣiṣuḥ, and so on. In the option without iṭ: atākṣīt, atāṣṭām, atākṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: tatakṣa, tatakṣatuḥ, tatakṣuḥ, and so on. With luṭ too, since iṭ has been made optional, in the option where iṭ is added: takṣitā, takṣitārau, takṣitāraḥ, and so on. In the option where iṭ is not given: taṣṭā, taṣṭārau, taṣṭāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: takṣyāt, takṣyāstām, takṣyāsuḥ, and so on. With lṛṭ too, since iṭ has been made optional, in the option where iṭ is given: takṣiṣyati, takṣiṣyataḥ, takṣiṣyanti, and so on. In the option without iṭ: takṣyati, takṣyataḥ, takṣyanti, and so on. With lṛṅ too, since iṭ has been made optional, in the option where iṭ is added: atakṣiṣyat, atakṣiṣyatām, atakṣiṣyan, and so on. In the option where iṭ is not given: atakṣyat, atakṣyatām, atakṣyan, and so on. The whole procedure is like what was explained in the section on akṣū.

For the root kṛṣa, in the sense of ploughing, the procedure for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest is also like the previous ones, except in the case of luṅ. With laṭ: karṣati and so on. With liṅ: karṣet and so on. With loṭ: karṣatu and so on. With luṅ it is a little different. The sūtra on kṛṣ, mṛṣ, spṛś, tṛp, dṛp and sṛp means "from kṛṣ, mṛṣ, spṛś, tṛp, dṛp and sṛp, the sic of cli is optional." From the roots kṛṣ, in the sense of ploughing, mṛṣa, in the sense of forbearance, spṛśa, in the sense of touching, tṛpa, in the sense of being satisfied, dṛpa, in the sense of joy, and sṛplṛ, in the sense of going, in luṅ, by the rule "cli," cli optionally becomes sic.

The sūtra anudāttasya car dupadhasyānyatarasyām means "and of an anudātta root with ṛ as its penultimate, optionally." For a root that is anudātta, that is, whose vowel is of low pitch, and that has ṛ as its penultimate, when a letter of the jhal group that is not termed "it" with k follows, the augment am is optionally inserted. In the option where cli is changed to sic and am is not given, in the three of the first person: akārkṣīt. By "of vad, vraj and what ends in a consonant" and the rest, there is vṛddhi; by the rule called "of ṣ and ḍh before s," ṣ becomes k; by the rule of substitution and the rest, s becomes ṣ; k and ṣ are joined as kṣ, and īṭ is drawn in. Akārṣṭām: the l becomes tas; by "tas, thas" and the rest, it is changed to tām; the rule "of s after a jhal before a jhal" applies, and the sic disappears; the rule ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ applies, and tām becomes ṭām. Akārkṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: akārkṣīḥ, akārṣṭam, akārṣṭa. In the three of the last person: akārkṣam, akārkṣva, akārkṣma.

In the option where am is added, the r takes its place and yaṇ is made by the rule iko yaṇ aci. In the three of the first person: akrākṣīt, akrāṣṭām, akrākṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: akrākṣīḥ, akrāṣṭam, akrāṣṭa. In the three of the last person: akrākṣam, akrākṣva, akrākṣma.

The sūtra śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ means "ksa, from a root without iṭ that ends in śal and has ik as its penultimate." For the root ending in a letter of the śal group, by vad, vraj and the rest, long. From a root ending in a letter of the śal group, with a letter of the ik group as its penultimate, and taking no iṭ, cli becomes ksa. The letter k is elided, since its purpose is that am is not given when an affix has k as its it.

To kṛṣ, luṅ. With luṅ, the rule for cli applies, and cli is given. By this sūtra cli is changed to ksa. Since the k is dropped, in the three of the first person: akṛkṣat, akṛkṣatām, akṛkṣan. In the three of the middle person: akṛkṣaḥ, akṛkṣatam, akṛkṣata. In the three of the last person: akṛkṣam, akṛkṣāva, akṛkṣāma.

In the three of the first person with liṭ added to kṛṣ: cakarṣa, cakṛṣatuḥ, cakṛṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cakarṣitha or cakarṣa, cakṛṣathuḥ, cakṛṣa. In the three of the last person: cakarṣa, cakṛṣiva, cakṛṣima.

Luṭ is added to kṛṣ. Since the augment am has been made optional by the rule "and of an anudātta root with ṛ as its penultimate, optionally," in the option where am is given: kraṣṭā, kraṣṭārau, kraṣṭāraḥ, and so on. In the option where am is not given, guṇa is made by the rule "of a penultimate short vowel and of what ends in puk" and the rest: karṣṭā, karṣṭārau, karṣṭāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: kṛṣyāt and so on. With lṛṭ, since the augment am has been made optional, in the option where am is given: krakṣyati, krakṣyataḥ, krakṣyanti, and so on. In the option where am is not given: karkṣyati, karkṣyataḥ, karkṣyanti, and so on. Likewise with lṛṅ too, since am has been made optional, in the option where am is given: akrakṣyat, akrakṣyatām, akrakṣyan, and so on. In the option where am is not given: akarkṣyat, akarkṣyatām, akarkṣyan, and so on.

For the root ruṣa, in the sense of harming, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest also follow the pattern of the previous ones, except in the case of luṭ. With laṭ: roṣati and so on. With liṅ: roṣet and so on. With loṭ: roṣatu and so on. With laṅ: aroṣat and so on. With laṅ: aroṣat and so on. With luṅ, the rule "ksa, from a root without iṭ that ends in śal and has ik as its penultimate" applies; since cli is changed to ksa: arukṣat, arukṣatām, arukṣan, and so on. With liṭ: ruroṣa, ruruṣatuḥ, ruruṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ruroṣitha or ruroṣṭha, ruruṣathuḥ, ruruṣa. In the three of the last person: ruroṣa, ruruṣiva, ruruṣima.

The sūtra iṣusahalubharuṣariṣaḥ means "from iṣu, saha, lubha, ruṣa and riṣa." From the roots iṣu, in the sense of desiring, ṣaha, in the sense of forbearance, lubha, in the sense of being attached, and ruṣa and riṣa, in the sense of harming, iṭ is optional before an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with the letter t. To ruṣa, luṭ. In the option where iṭ is given: roṣitā, roṣitārau, roṣitāraḥ, and so on. In the option without iṭ: roṣṭā, roṣṭārau, roṣṭāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: ruṣyāt, ruṣyāstām, ruṣyāsuḥ, and so on. With lṛṭ: rokṣyati, rokṣyataḥ, rokṣyanti, and so on. With lṛṅ: arokṣyat, arokṣyatām, arokṣyan, and so on.

For the root riṣa, in the sense of harming, the whole procedure for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest is like the one just explained. However, in luṭ iṭ is made optional, while for the other ārdhadhātuka affixes iṭ is always added. With laṭ: reṣati and so on. With liṅ: reṣet and so on. With loṭ: reṣatu and so on. With laṅ: areṣat and so on. With luṅ: areṣīt, areṣiṣṭām, areṣiṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: rireṣa, ririṣatuḥ, ririṣuḥ, rireṣitha, and so on. With luṭ, since iṭ has been made optional: reṣitā and so on, or reṣṭā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: riṣyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: reṣiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: areṣiṣyat and so on.

For the root uṣa, in the sense of burning, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are also like the previous ones, except in the case of liṭ. With laṭ: oṣati and so on. With liṅ: oṣet and so on. With loṭ: oṣatu and so on. With laṅ: auṣat and so on. With luṅ: auṣīt and so on.

The sūtra uṣavidajāgṛbhyo 'nyatarasyām means "from uṣ, vid and jāgṛ, optionally." From the roots uṣ, in the sense of burning, vid, in the sense of knowing, and jāgṛ, in the sense of waking from sleep, ām optionally occurs when liṭ follows. To uṣa, liṭ. In the option where ām is added: o; the rule "āṭ of those beginning with a vowel" applies, and āṭ is given; by "and from āṭ," vṛddhi: oṣāṃ babhūva, oṣāṃ cakāra, oṣām āsa, and so on. In the option where ām is not added, in the three of the first person: uvoṣa, ūṣatuḥ, ūṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: uvoṣitha, ūṣathuḥ, ūṣa. In the three of the last person: uvoṣa, ūṣiva, ūṣima. With luṭ: oṣitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: uṣyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: oṣiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: auṣiṣyat and so on.

For the root śaśa, in the sense of going far by leaps, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest also follow the pattern of the previous ones. With laṭ: śaśati and so on. With liṅ: śaśet and so on. With loṭ: śaśatu and so on. With laṅ: aśaśat and so on. With luṅ: aśaśīt and so on. With liṭ: śaśāśa, śaśaśatuḥ, śaśaśuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: śaśitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: śaśyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: śaśiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: aśaśiṣyat and so on.

For the root miha, in the sense of voiding urine, the forms made by adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are also mostly like the previous ones. With laṭ: mehati and so on. With liṅ: mehet and so on. With loṭ: mehatu and so on. With laṅ: amehat and so on. With luṅ: amikṣat, amikṣatām, amikṣan, and so on.

The derivation: to miha, luṅ. By "luṅ" and the rest, aṭ. With luṅ, the rule for cli applies, and cli is given. By the rule called "from a root that ends in śal and has ik as its penultimate," cli is changed to ksa. The k is dropped. The rule "ḍh for h" applies: h becomes ḍh. The rule "k for ṣ and ḍh" applies: ḍh becomes k. By the rule of substitution and the rest, s becomes ṣ. K and ṣ are joined as kṣ. The l becomes tip, and is changed to the forms of the endings.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: mimeha, mimihatuḥ, mimihuḥ. In the three of the middle person: mimehitha or mimeḍha, mimihathuḥ, mimiha. In the three of the last person: mimeha, mimihiva, mimihima.

The sūtra ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ means "elision of ḍh before ḍh." A final ḍh without a vowel is to be elided when ḍh follows. With luṭ: meḍhā, meḍhārau, meḍhāraḥ, and so on.

With the benedictive liṅ, to miha: in liṭ, the root is reduplicated; for the h, by the rule "sip of the parasmaipada," sip is changed to thal; the rule "ḍh for h" applies: h becomes ḍh; by "after jhaṣ, dh for t and th," th becomes dh; the rule ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ applies, and dh becomes ḍh; the rule "elision of ḍh before ḍh" applies, and the former ḍh is dropped. With the benedictive liṅ: mihyāt and so on.

To miha, luṭ, tā. Since the ḍ and ṭ of ḍā are dropped, tā. The rule "ḍh for h" applies: h becomes ḍh. By "after jhaṣ, dh for t and th" and the rest, t becomes dh, and the rule ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ applies, making ḍh. By this sūtra the former ḍh is dropped. With lṛṭ: mekṣyati. The rule "ḍh for h" applies: h becomes ḍh. The rule "before s, k for ṣ and ḍh" applies: ḍh becomes k. By the rule of substitution and the rest, s becomes ṣ, and k and ṣ are joined as kṣ, and so on.

With lṛṅ: amekṣyat and so on.

For the root daha, in the sense of reducing to ashes, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added, and the procedure is mostly like the one just explained. With laṭ: dahati and so on. With liṅ: dahet and so on. With loṭ: dahatu and so on. With laṅ: adahat and so on. In the first person singular of luṅ: adhākṣīt.

The derivation: to daha, luṅ. Cli is changed to sic, and the i and the c are dropped. The l is changed to tip; the rule for iṭ applies, and the i is dropped. By the rule called astisicaḥ, īṭ. By "of daha and the rest," gh for h. By "bhaṣ for the baś of a monosyllabic root" and the rest, d becomes dh. By "of vad, vraj" and the rest, vṛddhi. The rule "car before khar" applies, and gh becomes k. By the rule of substitution and the rest, s becomes ṣ, and k and ṣ are joined as kṣ.

In the first person dual of luṅ: adāgdhām. The derivation: to daha, luṅ, cli, and the l becomes tas. By "tas, thas" and the rest, tas becomes tām. By "of daha and the rest," gh for h. By "of vad, vraj" and the rest, vṛddhi. The rule "of s after a jhal before a jhal" applies, and the sic is dropped. By "after jhaṣ, dh for t and th" and the rest, t becomes dh. By "jaś for jhal before jhaś," g for gh, and the ending is drawn in.

In the first person plural: adhākṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: adhākṣīḥ, adāgdha. In the three of the last person: adhākṣam, adhākṣva, adhākṣma.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: dadāha, dehatuḥ, dehuḥ. In the three of the middle person: dehitha or dadagdha, dehathuḥ, deha.

The derivation of the plural of luṅ: to daha, luṅ, sic. The l becomes jhi, jhi becomes jus, and the j is dropped. By "of daha and the rest," h becomes gh. By "bhaṣ for the baś of a monosyllabic root" and the rest, d becomes dh. By "of vad, vraj" and the rest, vṛddhi. The rule "car before khar" applies, and gh becomes k. By the rule of substitution and the rest, s becomes ṣ, and k and ṣ are joined as kṣ and drawn in.

In the three of the last person: dadāha or dadaha, dehiva, dehima. With luṭ: dagdhā, dagdhārau, dagdhāraḥ. With the benedictive liṅ: dahyāt. With lṛṭ: dhakṣyati, dhakṣyataḥ, dhakṣyanti, and so on. With lṛṅ: adhakṣyat, adhakṣyatām, adhakṣyan, and so on.

For caha, in the sense of cheating, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added. Since the root has the vowel a, the procedure is easy to understand. With laṭ: cahati and so on. With liṅ: cahet and so on. With loṭ: cahatu and so on. With laṅ: acahat and so on. With luṅ: acahīt and so on. With liṭ: cacāha, cehatuḥ, cehuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: cahitā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: cahyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: cahiṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: acahiṣyat and so on.

For the root śuca, in the sense of grief, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added. With laṭ: śocati and so on. With liṅ: śocet and so on. With loṭ: śocatu and so on. With laṅ: aśocat and so on. With luṅ: aśocīt, aśociṣṭām, aśociṣuḥ, and so on. With loṭ: śuśoca, śuśucatuḥ, śuśucuḥ, and so on. With luṭ, iṭ is made optional. Cited in the commentary: "bhraṃśuśucavasāśubhyaḥ parasya tāder ārdhadhātukasya iḍ vā," which means "iṭ is optional for an ārdhadhātuka beginning with t that follows bhṛśu, śuca, vasa and aśu." After the roots bhṛśu, in the sense of falling down, śuca, in the sense of grief, vasa, in the sense of covering all over, and aśu, in the sense of eating, iṭ is made optional for a following ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with the letter t: śocitā, śocitārau, śocitāraḥ, and so on. In the option without iṭ, the rule "ku for cu" applies; since c is changed to k: śoktā, śoktārau, śoktāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: śucyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: śociṣyati and so on. With lṛṅ: aśociṣyat and so on.

For the root glai, in the sense of the waning of joy, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added. With laṭ: glāyati and so on. With liṅ: glāyet and so on. With loṭ: glāyatu and so on. With laṅ: aglāyat and so on.

The sūtra ād eca upadeśe 'śiti means "ā for ec, in the domain of what is not adjacent to an affix whose it is ś." In the domain of what is not adjacent to an affix whose it is ś, a root-final letter of the ec group (as in the ay and the rest of śap and śe) becomes ā. To glai, luṅ: aglāsīt, aglāsiṣṭām, aglāsiṣuḥ, and so on.

The sūtra āta au ṇalaḥ means "after ā, au for ṇal." The derivation: the root glai, with luṅ; aṭ to the root; with luṅ, cli; cli becomes sic; the l becomes tip; the rule "and of it" applies, and the i is dropped. By this sūtra the final ec becomes ā. By "yam, ram, nam and what ends in ā," sak as well; sak and iṭ. By astisicaḥ and the rest, īṭ. The rule "after iṭ, before īṭ" applies, and the sic is dropped. After a root ending in ā, the two ṇal endings, the singular of the first person of liṭ and the singular of the last person, are to be changed to au. In the first person singular: jaglau.

The sūtra āto lopa iṭi ca means "and before iṭ, elision of ā." Before ārdhadhātuka affixes that are termed "it" with k and begin with a vowel, and before iṭ as well, the root-final ā is to be elided. In the dual and plural: jaglatuḥ, jagluḥ. The derivation of jaglau: to glai, liṭ. By "not adjacent to an affix whose it is ś" and the rest, ec becomes ā. By "not reduplicated" and the rest, the root is reduplicated; the first consonant remains and the one after it is dropped. By the rule for ku and the rest, g becomes j. The l is changed to ṇal. By this sūtra, au, and the sandhi is made.

In the three of the middle person: jaglitha or jaglātha, jaglathuḥ, jagla. In the three of the last person: jaglau, jagliva, jaglima, and so on. With luṭ: glātā, glātārau, glātāraḥ, and so on.

With the benedictive liṅ, the sūtra vānyasya saṃyogādeḥ means "optionally, of another root beginning with a cluster as well." For the roots termed ghu, for mā, in the sense of honoring, and ṣṭhā, in the sense of ceasing from motion, and further for roots that end in ā and begin with a cluster of letters and the rest, when the benedictive liṅ termed "it" with k follows, the final optionally becomes e: glāyāt and so on, or else, being changed to e, gleyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: glāsyati and so on. With lṛṅ: aglāsyat and so on.

For the root gai, in the sense of sound, the procedures for adding the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are also mostly like the one just explained. With laṭ: gāyati and so on. With liṅ: gāyet and so on. With loṭ: gāyatu and so on. With laṅ: agāyat and so on. With luṅ: agāsīt, agāsiṣṭām, agāsiṣuḥ. With liṭ: jagau, jagatuḥ, jaguḥ, and so on.

The sūtra er liṅi means "e before liṅ." The final of the roots termed ghu, of mā, in the sense of honoring, ṣṭhā, in the sense of ceasing from motion, gai, in the sense of sound, pā, in the sense of drinking, ohāk, in the sense of abandoning, and ṣo, in the sense of ending, becomes e when the benedictive liṅ termed "it" with k follows. To gai, the benedictive liṅ. By "not adjacent to an affix whose it is ś" and the rest, ec becomes ā. By this sūtra, e: geyāt, geyāstām, geyāsuḥ, and so on. With lṛṭ: gāsyati and so on. With lṛṅ: agāsiṣyat and so on.

For the root ṣṭyai, in the sense of sound and of massing together, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added, and the procedure follows the pattern of the previous one: styāyati and so on. With liṅ: styāyet and so on.

With loṭ: ṣṭyāyatu and so on. With laṅ: aṣṭyāyat and so on. With luṅ: aṣṭyāsīt, aṣṭyāsiṣṭām, aṣṭyāsiṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: taṣṭyau, taṣṭyatuḥ, taṣṭyuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: as a nominal root, by the rule on ṣvaṣk and the rest, ṣ does not become s: ṣṭyātā, ṣṭyātārau, ṣṭyātāraḥ.

With the benedictive liṅ: to ṣṭyai, liṭ. By "not adjacent to an affix whose it is ś" and the rest, the final becomes ā. By "not reduplicated" and the rest, the root is reduplicated. The rule "the khay consonants preceded by a śar" applies, and ṣ and y are dropped. By the rule called "when the cause is absent, what depends on it is absent too," since ṣ is dropped, ṭh reverts to th. The rule "in the reduplicated syllable, car as well" applies, and th becomes t. With ṇal, the rule "after ā, au for ṇal" applies, and the sandhi is made. By the rule called "optionally, of another root beginning with a cluster as well," the final is made optionally to become e or not: ṣṭyāyāt, ṣṭyāyāstām, ṣṭyāyāsuḥ, and so on; or else ṣṭyeyāt, ṣṭyeyāstām, ṣṭyeyāsuḥ, and so on. With lṛṭ: ṣṭyāsyati and so on. With lṛṅ: aṣṭyāsyat and so on.

For the root daip, in the sense of purifying, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are also added, and the procedure is like the one just explained; since the p is a marker, it is dropped. With laṭ: dāyati and so on. With liṅ: dāyet and so on. With loṭ: dāyatu and so on. With laṅ: adāyat and so on.

The sūtra dādhā ghv adāp means "dā and dhā, other than dāp, are ghu." Roots other than dāp, in the sense of cutting, and daip, in the sense of purifying, that take the form dā or dhā, such as ḍudāñ, in the sense of giving, ḍudhāñ, in the sense of holding, do, in the sense of cutting, and deṅ, in the sense of protecting, are given the technical name "termed ghu." This has the same meaning as the Cāndra's rule "of what is not dīp" and the Kalāpa's rule "dā and dhā other than dāp are dā." In this case too, since daip is not termed ghu, the sic that cli becomes is not elided. With luṅ: adāsīt, adāsiṣṭām, adāsiṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: dadau, dadatuḥ, daduḥ, and so on. With luṭ: dātā, dātārau, dātāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, since it is not termed ghu, the final does not become e: dāyāt and so on. With lṛṭ: dāsyati and so on. With lṛṅ: adāsyat and so on.

For the root dheṭ, in the sense of drinking, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added, and the procedure is mostly like the previous ones. With laṭ: dhayati and so on. With loṭ: dhayatu and so on. With laṅ: adhayat and so on.

The sūtra vibhāṣā dheṭśvyoḥ means "optionally, for dheṭ and śvi." From the roots dheṭ and śvi, the cli of the rule "cli in luṅ" is optionally changed either to sic or to what is called caṅ.

The sūtra caṅi means "before caṅ." When caṅ follows, the root that is not reduplicated is to be reduplicated. To dheṭ, luṅ; cli is changed to caṅ. The letter ṅ of caṅ serves as the marker ṅ, and the letter c serves to reduplicate the root by the rule "before caṅ." By "not adjacent to an affix whose it is ś" and the rest, the final becomes ā. The root is reduplicated; the rule "short" applies and the vowel is shortened. The rule "in the reduplicated syllable, car as well" applies, and dh becomes d. The rule "and before iṭ, elision of ā" applies, and since the a is dropped, in the three of the first person: adadhat, adadhatām, adadhan. In the three of the middle person: adadhaḥ, adadhatam, adadhata. In the three of the last person: adadham, adadhāva, adadhāma.

In the option where cli is changed to sic: the sūtra vibhāṣā ghrādheṭśāchāsaḥ means "optionally, from ghrā, dheṭ, śā, chā and sā." From the roots ghrā, in the sense of smelling, dheṭ, in the sense of drinking, śo, in the sense of making thin, cho, in the sense of cutting, and ṣo, in the sense of ending, when the parasmaipada follows, the sic that cli becomes is optionally lost. In the option where sic is dropped, in the first person singular and dual: adhāt, adhātām.

The sūtra ātaḥ means "after ā." After a root ending in ā whose sic is lost, the jhi that l is changed to becomes jus: adhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: adhāḥ, adhātam, adhāta. In the three of the last person: the derivation of the plural is this. To dheṭ, luṅ; cli becomes sic; the l becomes jhi. By "luṅ" and the rest, aṭ to the root. By "ghrā" and the rest, the sic is lost. By this sūtra, jhi becomes jus. By cuṭū and the rest, the j is dropped. The rule "when us follows, from what is not word-final" applies: the two together take the single form of the following vowel. Adhām, adhāva, adhāma.

In the option where sic is not lost, since sak and iṭ are added by "yam, ram, nam and what ends in ā" and the rest: adhāsīt, adhāsiṣṭām, adhāsiṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: dadhau, dadhatuḥ, dadhuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: dhātā, dhātārau, dhātāraḥ, and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, the rule "e before liṅ" applies: dheyāt, dheyāstām, dheyāsuḥ, and so on. With lṛṭ: dhāsyati, dhāsyataḥ, dhāsyanti, and so on. With lṛṅ: adhāsyat, adhāsyatām, adhāsyan, and so on.

The sūtra pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyartisartiśadasadāṃ pibajighradhamatiṣṭhamanayacchapaśyarcchadhauśīyasīdāḥ means "of pā, ghrā, dhmā, sthā, mnā, dāṇ, dṛśi, arti, sarti, śad and sad: piba, jighra, dhama, tiṣṭha, mana, yaccha, paśya, ṛccha, dhau, śīya and sīda." When a condition whose it is ś follows, the roots pā, in the sense of drinking, ghrā, in the sense of smelling, dhmā, in the sense of sound and of blowing on fire, ṣṭhā, in the sense of ceasing from motion, mnā, in the sense of repeated practice, dāṇ, in the sense of giving, dṛśir, in the sense of seeing, arti, that is, ṛ, in the sense of moving, sarti, that is, sṛ, in the sense of going, and śadḷ and ṣadḷ, in the sense of going, become, in order, piba and the rest.

To pā, in the sense of drinking, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added. With laṭ: pibati and so on. With liṅ: pibet and so on. With loṭ: pibatu and so on. With laṅ: apibat and so on. With luṅ, the sic is lost by the rule called "from gā, sthā, ghu, pā and bhū": apāt, apātām, apuḥ. With liṭ: papau, papatuḥ, papuḥ, and so on. With luṭ: pātā, pātārau, pātāraḥ. With the benedictive liṅ, the rule "e before liṅ" applies and the final becomes e: peyāt, peyāstām, peyāsuḥ. With lṛṭ: pāsyati, pāsyataḥ, pāsyanti, and so on. With lṛṅ: apāsyat. For apuḥ, the rule "after ā" applies: jhi becomes jus, and by "when us follows, from what is not word-final" and the rest, the two together take the single form of the following vowel. Apāsyatām, apāsyan, and so on.

To ghrā, in the sense of smelling, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are added. With laṭ: jighrati and so on. With liṅ: jighret and so on. With loṭ: jighratu and so on. With laṅ: ajighrat and so on. With luṅ, the rule "optionally, from ghrā, dheṭ, śā, chā and sā" applies, and the sic is optionally lost. In the option where it is dropped: aghrāt, aghrātām, aghruḥ, and so on. In the option where sic is not dropped, since sak and iṭ are added by "yam, ram, nam and what ends in ā" and the rest: aghrāsīt, aghrāsiṣṭām, aghrāsiṣuḥ, and so on. With liṭ: jaghrau, jaghratuḥ, jaghruḥ, and so on.

With luṭ: ghrātā, ghrātārau, ghrātāraḥ, ghrātāraḥ. With the benedictive liṅ: by "optionally, of another beginning with a conjunct" and so on, option is due, and since the change to e is made optional, occurring or not occurring: ghreyīta, ghreyāstāṃ, ghreyāsuḥ and so on; or else: ghrāyāta, ghrāyaṅshāṃ, ghrāṃyābhuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ: ghāsyati, ghrāsyataḥ, ghrāsyanti and so on. With lṛṅ: aghrāsyata, aghrāsyataṃ, aghrāsyan and so on. Lṛṅ: aghrāsyata, aghrāsyatāṃ, aghrāsyan and so on.

To dhmā, "in the senses of sound and of applying fire throughout," laṭ and the rest of the parasmaipada endings are also attached. With laṭ: dhamati and so on. With liṅ: dhameta and so on. With loṭ: dhamatu and so on. With laṅ: adhamata and so on. With laṅ: adhamata and so on. With luṅ, sak and iṭ are given by "of yam, ram, nam and those ending in āt" and so on: adhmasīta, aṅpmāsiṣṭāṃ, adhmāsiṣuḥ and so on. With liṭ: padhmau, daṅpmatuḥ, daṅpmuḥ and so on. With luṭ: dadmmatā and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, since the change to e is made optional, occurring or not occurring: dhmeyāta, dhmeyāste, dhmeyāsuḥ and so on; or else: rdmāyāṭa, thmāyāstāṃ, dhmāyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ: ṅpmāsyati, dhmāsyataḥ, dhmāsyanhi and so on. With lṛṅ: yadhmāsyata, aṅśmasyatāṃ, aṅpmāsyan and so on.

To ṣṭhā, "in the sense of ceasing from going," laṭ and the rest of the parasmaipada endings are attached. With laṭ: tiṣṭhati and so on. With liṅ: tiṣṭhata and so on. With loṭ: tiṣṭhatu and so on. With laṅ: atiṣṭhata and so on. With luṅ: by "for ṣ at the beginning of the root," s is due, and ṣ becomes s. By what is called "when the cause is absent, what has that cause is also absent," the ṭh also reverts to th. By "gāti, sthā" and so on, the sic is dropped: asthāta, asthātāṃ, asthuḥ and so on. With liṭ: by "preceded by śar": tasthau, tasthatuḥ. The la and ya are dropped; by "the car of the reduplicate," it is also identified, and th becomes t: tasthuḥ and so on. With luṭ: sthādā, sthātārau, sthātāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: by "e before liṅ," e is due, and the final becomes e: stheyāta, stheyāstāṃ, stheyāuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ: sthāsyati, sthāsyataḥ, sthāsyantri and so on. With lṛṅ: asthāsyata, asbāsyatāṃ, asbāsyan and so on.

To mnā, "in the sense of practicing," laṭ and the rest of the parasmaipada endings are attached. With laṭ: manati and so on. With liṅ: mane and so on. With loṭ: manatu and so on. With laṅ: amanata and so on. With luṅ, sak and iṭ are attached by "yam, ram, nam and those ending in āt" and so on: amnāsīha, amnāsiṣṭāṃ, amnāsiṣuḥ and so on. With liṭ: mamnau, mamnatuḥ, mamnuḥ and so on. With luṭ: mnātā, mnātāṅau, mnātāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, by "optionally, of another beginning with a conjunct" and so on, option is due: mneyāta, mnayāstāṃ, mneyāsuḥ and so on; or else: mnāyāta, mnāyāstāṃ, mnāyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ: mnāyāti, mnāyāstāṃ, mnāyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ: aṭnāsyata, amnāsyataṃ, asnāsyanti and so on.

Dāṇ, "to give," with ṇ as an indicatory marker: laṭ and the rest of the parasmaipada endings are attached. With laṭ: yacchati and so on. With liṅ: yacchata and so on. With loṭ: yacchatu and so on. With laṅ: ayacchata and so on. With luṅ: by "gāti, sthā, ghu" and so on, the sic is destroyed: adāda, aṅātāṃ, aduḥ and so on. With liṭ: dadau, dadatuḥ, daduḥ and so on. With luṭ: dātā, dātārau, dātāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: by "e before liṅ," e is due: deyāta, deyāsthāṃ, deyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ: dāsyataḥ, dāsyanti and so on. With lṛṅ: adāsyata, adāsyatāṃ, adāsyan and so on.

To the root hvṛ, "in the sense of crookedness," laṭ and the rest of the parasmaipada endings are attached. With laṭ: hārati; and with liṅ: hrareta and so on. With loṭ: hāratu and so on. With laṅ: ahvarta and so on. With luṅ: by "vṛddhi before sic, in the parasmaipada endings," vṛddhi is due; vṛddhi being made, for the three forms of the first person: ahvārṣīta, ahnārṣḍāṃ, agmyarṅaḥ. For the three forms of the middle person: ahmārṣīḥ, ahvāḍaṃṣṭa, ahvārṣṭa. For the three forms of the last person: ahvārṣṭi, ahvārṣma, ahvarṣṭa.

For the singular of the first person of liṭ: the root. Here, although two jhal follow, the sic is not elided. For the commentary gives an example: just as a son who has grown to maturity does no harm to his father, so, since the cause by which the earlier jhal letter came about is the sic, it is not to be elided; so it says. It is pronounced twice. The first consonant remains. The at of ṛt. Cu for ku and h. By "the car of the reduplicate is also identified" and so on, and by making vṛddhi: jaśvāra.

Ṛtaśca saṃyogādergūṇaḥ, "Guṇa also for ṛt beginning with a conjunct." For a root ending in ṛ and having a conjunct letter at its beginning, guṇa occurs before a liṭ that is not a cause of vṛddhi. For the dual and plural of the first person: jahvaratuḥ, jahvaraḥ. For the three forms of the middle person: jahvartha, jahvarathuḥ, jahāra. For the three forms of the last person: jahvāra, jahvara, jahvariva, jahvarima. With luṭ: hvartā, hvartārau, hvartātaḥ and so on.

Guṇo 'rtisaṃlogābyoḥ, "Guṇa for arti and for those beginning with a conjunct." Since the commentary explains, "iṭ does not apply to val following one ending in ṛt," iṭ is not given. Arti is the root ṛ, to go. By "kṛ, sṛ" and so on, with regard to iṭ; "and also in the sense of obtaining." For arti and for roots ending in ṛ that have a conjunct letter at their beginning, guṇa occurs before a benedictive liṅ with its initial and before the suffix yak. With the benedictive liṅ: hvaryāta, hvaryāsuḥ.

Ṛṅdhanossye, "From ṛt and han, before sya." From roots ending in ṛt and from han, "in the senses of harming and going," iṭ occurs for the sya of "sya and tās before lṛ and luṭ" that follows them. With lṛṭ: hāriṣyati, hāreṣyataḥ, hvariṣyanti and so on. With lṛṅ: ahāriṣyata, ahvariṣyatāṃ, ahvariṣyan and so on.

For the root svṛ, "in the senses of sound and of affliction," the procedure of attaching laṭ and the rest of the parasmaipada endings is mostly the same as the one just explained. With laṭ: svarati and so on. With liṅ: svareta and so on. With loṭ: svaratu and so on. With laṅ: asvarata and so on. With luṅ: by "svarati, sūti, sūyati, dhūñ, and those with ū as marker" and so on, iṭ is made optional, so in the alternative where iṭ is attached: asvārṛta, asvārṛṣṭāṃ, asvāriṣuḥ and so on; or asvārṣīta, asvārṣṭāṃ, asvārṣāḥ and so on. With liṭ: sasvāra, sasvaratuḥ, sasvaruḥ and so on. With luṭ too, iṭ being made optional by the previous sūtra: svaritā, svaritārau, svaritāraḥ and so on; or sartā, svartārau, svartāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: by "guṇa for arti and for those beginning with a conjunct": svaryāta, svarlāstāṃ, svaryasuḥ and so on.

It is quoted in the commentary: "svarateḥ syasya nityamiḍācyaḥ": from svarati, iṭ is always to be stated for sya. That is, sya following the root svṛ always takes iṭ. With lṛṭ: svariṣyati, svariṣyati, svariṣyataḥ, svariṣyanti and so on. With lṛṅ: asvariṣyata, asvariṣyatāṃ, asvariṣyan and so on.

For the root stated as "sṛ, also in the sense of going," attach the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest. By the sūtra "bāghrādhmā" and so on, sṛ is changed into dhau, and with śap for the agent: dhāvati and so on. With liṅ: dhāveta and so on. With loṭ: dhāvatu and so on. With laṅ: adhāvata and so on. Moreover, the commentary explains: "When sṛ, to go, is used in the sense of going very swiftly, it becomes dhau before an affix that has ś as its marker; but for going slowly it does not become dhau." Therefore, in the sense of going slowly: with laṭ, sarti and so on; with liṅ, sarita and so on; with loṭ, sartu and so on; with laṅ, asarta and so on.

"sartiśāsdyartibhyaśca": also from sarti, śāsti and arti. That is, from sṛ, to go, śāsu, to instruct, and ṛ, to go and also to obtain, cli too becomes aṅ, in both the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada. For sṛ, with luṅ, cli too becomes aṅ. "ṛdṛśoñadi guṇaḥ": guṇa for ṛ and dṛś before aṅ. That is, roots ending in ṛ, and dṛśir, to see, take guṇa before aṅ, the replacement of cli: asarta, asartāṃ, asaran and so on.

It is quoted in the commentary: "ṛsṛbhyāmaṅbā kecita": from ṛ and sṛ, according to some, aṅ is optional. Although it was explained above that for sṛ, śāsu and ṛ, cli becomes aṅ, in some contexts, from ṛ and sṛ, it may optionally become sic as well: asārṣīta, asārṣṭāṃ, asārṣuḥ and so on.

For sṛ, attaching liṭ: svasāra, sasratuḥ, sasruḥ; sasartha, sasrathuḥ, sasra; sasāra or sasara, sasraṃva, sasraṃma. With luṭ: sartā, sartārau, sartāraḥ and so on.

"riṅ śayakliṅṣya": riṅ before śa, yak and liṅ. That is, before the affixes śa and yak, the ya of the benedictive liṅ, and ṇal, atus, us, thal with p as its marker, athus, a and ṇal, when these do not take iṭ, the final ṛ of a root becomes what is called riṅ; the marker serves to block the vowel. For sṛ with the benedictive liṅ: sṛyāta, sriyāstāṃ, sriyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, iṭ is given by the rule "from those ending in ṛ and from han, before sya": sariṣyati, sariṣyataḥ, sariṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ, attaching iṭ: asariṣyata, asariṣyatāṃ, asariṣyan and so on.

For the root stated as "ṛ, to go and to obtain," attach the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest. By "pāghrādhmā" and so on it is changed into ṛccha. With laṭ: ṛcchati and so on. With liṅ: ṛccheta and so on. With loṭ: ṛcchatu and so on. With laṅ: ārcchata and so on. With luṅ, since changing cli into aṅ and changing it into sic are made optional, in the alternative with aṅ: ārta, āratāṃ, āran and so on; in the alternative where it is changed into sic: ārṣīta, ārṣāṃ, ārṣuḥ and so on.

For the first-person singular of liṭ, the root is stated twice; by the rule "a for ṛ" the upper ṛ is changed into ar; since the r is dropped by the rule "the first consonant remains," the lower ṛ takes vṛddhi; and by lengthening when ak meets a similar vowel: ār. "ṛcchatyāṃtāṃ": of ṛcchati and of those ending in ṝ. That is, the root ṛ, to go, and roots ending in ṝ take guṇa before liṭ endings that are not a cause of vṛddhi. In the first-person dual and plural: ārtuḥ, āruḥ. In the middle-person singular: "iṭtbyartibyayatīnāṃ": iṭ for atti, arti and vyayati. That is, thal following the roots ad, to eat, ṛ, to go, and vyañ, to cover, always takes iṭ: āretha. In the middle-person dual and plural: ārathuḥ, āruḥ. In the three of the last person: ār, āriva, ārim. With luṭ: artā, artārau, artāraḥ. With the benedictive liṅ, guṇa having been made by "arti and those beginning with a conjunct" and so on: aryāta, aryāstāṃ, aryāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, attaching iṭ by "ṛt and han" and so on: ariṣyati, ariṣyataḥ, ariṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ: āriṣyata, āriṣyatāṃ, āriṣyan and so on.

"śrubaḥ śṛca": and śṛ for śru. That is, for the root stated as "śru, to hear," before the sārvadhātuka affixes, in the agent, śnu comes in place of śap, and not only that: the root śru itself becomes śṛ. The letter ś is there so that it drops as a marker. In the first-person singular and dual of laṭ: śṛṇoti, śṛṇutaḥ.

"huśnuboḥ sārbadhātuke": of hu and śnu, before a sārvadhātuka. That is, the final u of the root hu, to give, and of the affix śnu, and moreover of roots with a single vowel that are not conjuncts, becomes yaṇ before a sārvadhātuka ending that begins with a vowel, the n having become ṇ by "r and ṣ" and so on, and with guṇa as befits the sārvadhātuka itself. In the first-person plural of laṭ: śṛṇvanti. In the three of the middle person: śṛṇoṣi, śṛṇuthaḥ, śṛṇutha. In the last-person singular: śṛṇomi.

"lopaścāsyānyatarasyāṃ bśoḥ": and before v and m its elision is optional. That is, the u of the affix is optionally elided before endings that begin with v or m and are not named as having p as marker. In the last-person dual and plural: śṛṇuvaḥ or śṛṇvaḥ, śṛṇumaḥ or śṛṇmaḥ. In the three of the first person of liṅ: śṛṇuyāta, śṛṇuyāstāṃ, śṛṇurāsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: śṛṇuyāḥ, śṛṇuyāstaṃ, śṛṇuyāsta. In the three of the last person: śṛṇuyāṃ, śṛṇuyāva, śṛṇuyāma. In the three of the first person of loṭ: śṛṇotu or śṛṇutāta, śṛṇutāṃ, śṛṇvantu. In the middle-person singular: "utaśca pratyayāta saṃyoga pūtāta": and from the affix u, when it is not preceded by a conjunct.

That is, after the final u of an affix that is not preceded by a conjunct, hi, the replacement of sip, is also elided: śṛṇu. La, sip; la, sip; si, hi. With hi dropped, by "for tu and hi, tāt too," hi is changed into tātaṅ: śṛṇutāta. In the dual and plural: śṛṇutaṃ, śṛṇuta. In the three of the last person: śṛṇavāṇi, śṛṇavāva, śṛṇavāma.

In the three of the first person of laṅ: aśiṇatāṃ, aśṛṇutrī, aśṛṇvan. In the three of the middle person: aśṛṇoḥ, aśṛṇutaṃ, aśṛṇuta. In the three of the last person: aśṛṇavaṃ, aśṛṇuva, aśṛṇma, aśṛṇuma, aśṛṇuma.

For śru, attach luṅ. By "vṛddhi in sic before the parasmaipada endings," vṛddhi being made, in the three of the first person: aśrauṣīta, aśrauṣṭāṃ, aśrauṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: aśrauṣī, aśrauṣṭa. In the three of the last person: aśrauṣa, aśrauṣva, aśrauṣma. In the three of the first person of liṭ: śuśrāva, śuśruvatuḥ, śuśruvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: śuśrotha, śuśruvathuḥ, śuśruva. In the three of the last person: śuśrāva, śaśruva, śuśruma. With luṭ: śrotā, śrotārau, śrautāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, lengthening by "not kṛt" and so on; before a vowel, uv is made by "śnu, root, śru" and so on. Having done this: śūyāta, śrūyāstāṃ, śrūyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, the vṛddhi of the root before ṇal having been made optional, and guṇa being made by "ārdhadhātuka and sārvadhātuka" and so on: śroṣyati, śroṣyataḥ, śroṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ: aśroṣyata, aśroṣyatāṃ, aśroṣyana and so on.

For the root stated as "ṣu, to bring forth," attach the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest. By "the initial ṣ of a root becomes s," and by giving śap for the agent: with laṭ, savati and so on; with liṅ, saveta and so on; with loṭ, savatu and so on; with laṅ, asavata and so on.

"stusudhūñbhyaḥ parasmaipadeṣu": from stu, su and dhūñ, before the parasmaipada endings. That is, from the roots ṣṭuñ, to praise, and ṣu, to bring forth, which become stu and su when the initial ṣ of the root is made s, and from dhūñ, to shake, sic takes iṭ before the parasmaipada endings. For su, with luṅ: asāvīta, asāviṣṭāṃ, asāviṣuḥ and so on.

It is quoted in the commentary: "rudusunudhātūnāṃ liṭaṃpinā iḍā": for the roots ru, du, su and nu, iṭ is optional before what is not liṭ. That is, from the roots ru, to sound, du, to go, ṣu, to bring forth, and ṇu, to praise, iṭ always comes before liṭ endings beginning with val, while before other endings beginning with val that are not liṭ, iṭ comes optionally. For su with luṅ, the examples with iṭ attached are the ones just given, asāvīta and so on; in the alternative without iṭ, vṛddhi being made: asauṣīta, asauṣṭāṃ, asauṣuḥ and so on.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: suṣāva, suṣuvatuḥ, suṣuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: suṣotha, suṣuvathuḥ, suṣuva, sudaṣuva. In the three of the last person: suṣāva, suṣava, suṣuviva, suṣuvima. With luṭ, iṭ being made optional: savitā, savitārau, savitāraḥ and so on; or else sotā, sotārau, sotāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, lengthening being made by "not kṛt" and so on: sūyāta, sūyāstāṃ, sūyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, iṭ being made optional: saviṣyati, saviṣyataḥ, saviṣyanti and so on; or else soṣyati, soṣyataḥ, soṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ: asaviṣyata, asaviṣyatāṃ, asaviṣyan and so on; or else asoṣyata, asoṣyatāṃ, asoṣyan and so on.

For the root stated as "sru, to go," attaching the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest: with laṭ, sravati and so on; with liṅ, sraveta and so on; with loṭ, sravatu and so on; with laṅ, asravata and so on.

"ṇiśridrusrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ": caṅ for ṇi, śri, dru and sru, in the agent. That is, from those ending in the affix ṇi, and from śriñ, to resort to, dru, and sru, to go, cli becomes caṅ in the agent. The ṅ is for the purpose of ṅit, and the c is for the purpose of stating the root twice, by the rule "before caṅ." For sru, with luṅ, cli is changed into caṅ, and before a vowel uv is made by "śnu" and so on. In the three of the first person: asusruvata, asusruvatāṃ, asusruvan. In the three of the middle person: asusruvaḥ, asusruvataṃ, asusruvata. In the three of the last person: asusruvaṃ, asusruvāva, asusruvāma.

With liṭ, in the three of the first person: susrāva, susruvatuḥ, susruvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: susrotha, susruvathuḥ, susruva. In the three of the last person: susrāva with ṇal, or susrava, susruva, susruma. Here the second s does not become ṣ, because this root has the letter s from the start. With luṭ: srotā, srotārau, srotāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, lengthening being made by "not kṛt" and so on: srūyāta, srūyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ: sroṣyati, sroṣyataḥ, sroṣyanti and so on. With lṛṅ: asroṣyata, asroṣyatāṃ, asroṣyan and so on.

For the root stated as "du, to go," attaching the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest: with laṭ, davati and so on; with liṅ, davati and so on; with loṭ, davatu and so on; with laṅ, adavata and so on. With luṅ, iṭ being made optional by "the roots ru, du, su" and so on: adāvīta, adāviṣṭāṃ, adāviṣuḥ and so on; or else adauṣīta, adauṣuḥ and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: dudāva, duduvatuḥ, duduvuḥ. Since the commentary explains that "the forms of liṭ with iṭ are in some cases to be treated as having k as marker, and in some cases also as having p as marker," in the three of the middle person: dudavitha, duduvitha, duduvathuḥ, duduva. In the three of the last person: dudāva, dudava, duduviva, dudaviva, duduvima, dudavima. With luṭ, iṭ being made optional by "the roots ru, du, su" and so on, in the alternative with iṭ: davitā, davitārau, davitāraḥ and so on; and in the alternative without iṭ: dotā, dotārau, dotāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, lengthening being made by "not kṛt" and so on: dūyāta, dūyāstāṃ, dūyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, iṭ being made optional by "the roots ru, du, su" and so on: daviṣyati, daviṣyataḥ, daviṣyanti and so on; or else doṣyati, doṣyataḥ, doṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ as well: adaviṣyata, adaviṣyatāṃ, adaviṣyan and so on; or else adoṣyata, adoṣyan and so on.

For the root stated as "dru, to go," attaching the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest: with laṭ, dravati and so on.

With liṅ: draveta and so on. With loṭ: dravatu and so on. With laṅ: adravata and so on. With luṅ, cli is changed into caṅ by the rule "ṇiśridru," and by "before caṅ" the root is stated twice: adudruvata, adudruvatāṃ, adudruvan and so on. In the first person of liṭ: dudrāva, dudruvatuḥ, dudruvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: dudrotha, dudruvathuḥ, dudruva. In the three of the last person: dudrāva, dudrava, dudruma; by "kṛ, kṛ" and so on, iṭ does not apply. With luṭ: drotā, drotārau, drotāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, lengthening being made by "not kṛt" and so on: drūyāta, drūyāstāṃ, drūyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ: droṣyati, droṣyataḥ, droṣyanti and so on. With lṛṅ: adroṣyata, adroṣyatāṃ, adroṣyan and so on.

For the root stated as "gamḷ, to go," attach the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest. By "cha for iṣu, gam and yam," the m being changed into cha: with laṭ, gacchati and so on; with liṅ, gaccheta and so on; with loṭ, gacchatu and so on; with laṅ, agacchata and so on.

"buṣādidyuhābyāṃditaḥ parasmaipadeṣu": from puṣa and the rest, dyuta and the rest, and those with ḷ as marker, before the parasmaipada endings. That is, from the roots puṣa and the rest, dyuta and the rest, and roots with ḷ as marker, before the parasmaipada endings of luṅ, cli becomes aṅ in luṅ. The letter ṅ is there so that the penultimate is not elided by the rule "when not aṅ." For gamḷ with luṅ, cli being changed into aṅ: agamata, agamatāṃ, agaman and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: jagāma, jagmatuḥ, jagmuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jagmitha, jagmathuḥ. In the three of the last person: jagāma, jagama, jagmiva, jagmima. With luṭ: gantā, gantārau, gantāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: gamyāstāṃ, gamyāsuḥ and so on.

"gameriṭ parasmaipadeṣa": for gam, before the parasmaipada endings, iṭ; by "gam, han, jan, khan" and so on, the penultimate is elided. That is, from gam, iṭ comes before ārdhadhātuka parasmaipada endings beginning with s, and in some contexts before ātmanepada endings as well. For gam with lṛṭ, iṭ being attached by this sūtra: gamiṣyati, gamiṣyataḥ, gamiṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ: agamiṣyata, agamiṣyatāṃ, agamiṣyan and so on.

For the root stated as "sṛpḷ, to go," attaching the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest: with laṭ, sarpati and so on; with liṅ, sarpeta and so on; with loṭ, sarpatu and so on; with laṅ, asarpata and so on. With luṅ, cli is changed into aṅ by "puṣa and the rest, dyuta and the rest, and those with ḷ as marker" and so on, and it is optionally changed into sic by "kṛṣa, mṛśa, tṛpa, dṛpa, sṛpa" and so on; and in the alternative where it is changed into sic, the augment am optionally applies by "of an anudātta root with ṛ as penultimate" and so on. So three ways of deriving it arise. In the alternative where cli is changed into aṅ: asṛpata, asṛpatāṃ, asṛpan and so on. In the alternative where cli is changed into sic and the augment am is given: asrapsīta, asrāptāṃ, sic being dropped by "jhal after jhal," asrapsuḥ and so on. In the alternative where the augment am is not given, vṛddhi being made: asārpsīta, asārptāṃ, sic being dropped by "jhal after jhal," asārpsuḥ and so on.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: sasārpa, sasṛpatuḥ, sasṛpuḥ. In the three of the middle person: sasarpitha, sasṛpathuḥ, sasṛpa. In the three of the last person: sasārpa, sasarpa, sasṛpiva, sasṛpima. With luṭ: sarptā, sarptārau, sarptāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: sṛpyāta, sṛpyāstā, sṛpyāsuḥ. With lṛṭ, guṇa being made: sarpsyati, sarpsyataḥ, sarpsyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ: asarpsyata, asarpsyatāṃ, asarpsyan and so on.

For the root stated as "skandir, to go and to dry up," attaching the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest: with laṭ, skandati and so on; with liṅ, skandeta and so on; with loṭ, skandatu and so on. With luṅ, by "optionally for those with ir as marker," cli optionally becomes aṅ. In the alternative with aṅ, the n being dropped by "not having i as marker" and so on: askadata, askadatāṃ, askadan and so on. In the alternative where cli is changed into sic, vṛddhi being made by "vada, vraja" and so on: askāntsīta, askāntāṃ, askāntsuḥ and so on.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: caskanda, caskandatuḥ, caskanduḥ. In the three of the middle person: caskanditha or caskantha, caskandathuḥ, caskanda. In the three of the last person: caskanda, caskandiva, caskandima. With luṭ, d becomes t by "car before khar," s is dropped by "jhal after jhal," and the upper t is dropped by "of jhar before a similar jhar": skantā, skantārau, skantāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, d becomes t by "car before khar," the t is dropped by "of jhar before a similar jhar," and the n is dropped by "not having i as marker" and so on: skadyāta, skadyāstāṃ, skadyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, d being changed into t by "car before khar": skantsyati, skantsyataḥ, skantsyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ: askantsyata, askantsyatāṃ, askantsyan and so on.

"beḥ skandenaniṣṭāyāṃ": of skand after vi, when not before niṣṭhā. That is, the s of skandi following the preverb vi optionally becomes the letter ṣ when it does not have an affix named niṣṭhā among the kṛt affixes and so on: viskandati, viṣkandati and so on. If the affix is named niṣṭhā, it does not change: attaching kta, which is named niṣṭhā, gives viskannaḥ and the like.

"pariśca, pareśca": also from pari. That is, the s of skandi also optionally becomes the letter ṣ after the preverb pari: pariskandati, pariṣkandati and so on. It is quoted in the commentary: "niṣṭhāyāmapi bāṣatā": before niṣṭhā too, ṣ is optional. That is, the s of skanda after the preverb pari optionally becomes ṣ even before the niṣṭhā affix. Giving kta to skandir preceded by pari: pariskannaḥ, pariṣkaṇṇaḥ and so on.

For the root stated as "tṝ, to overcome and to ferry across," attaching the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest: with laṭ, tarati and so on; with liṅ, tareta and so on; with loṭ, taratu and so on; with laṅ, atarata and so on.

"bṝto bā": optionally from vṛ and from those ending in ṝ. That is, after the two roots vṛñ, to cover, and vṛṅ, to honor, and after roots ending in ṝ, īṭ optionally comes before endings beginning with val that are not liṭ.

"sicica pasmaipadeṣa": also in sic, before the parasmaipada endings. That is, although it was explained above that after vṛñ, vṛṅ and those ending in ṝ, īṭ is optional before endings beginning with val, as an exception to that, before sic with parasmaipada endings the long īṭ does not come; only the short one is to be given. For tṝ with luṅ, iṭ and vṛddhi being made: atārīta, atāriṣṭāṃ, atāriṣuḥ and so on.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: tatāra, teratuḥ, teruḥ. In the three of the middle person: teritha, terathuḥ, tera. In the three of the last person: tatāra, tatara, teriva, terima. With luṭ, iṭ and īṭ being made optional by "optionally from vṛ and ṝ": taritā, taritārau, taritāraḥ and so on. Guṇa is by the rule "of ṛcchati and ṝ," and the elision of the reduplicated syllable and the change into e are by "tṝ, phal" and so on. Or else: tarītā, tarītārau, tarītāraḥ and so on.

"na liṅi": not before liṅ. That is, before endings beginning with val of the benedictive liṅ, such as in "sīyuṭ in liṅ," the long īṭ does not come; examples will appear in detail in the section on the ātmanepada, to be explained later.

"ṝta iṅlhātoḥ": it for the ṝ of a root. That is, roots ending in ṝ become it whenever an affix occurs that has no special provision such as guṇa or vṛddhi, and it is to be written with r following. For tṝ with the benedictive liṅ: tīryāta, tīryāstāṃ, tīryāsuḥ. With lṛṭ, iṭ and īṭ being made optional by "optionally from vṛ and ṝ": tariṣyati, tariṣyataḥ, tariṣyanti and so on; or else tarīṣyati, tarīṣyataḥ, tarīṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ: atariṣyata, atariṣyatāṃ (the a being lengthened by "of the penultimate"), atariṣyan and so on; or else atarīṣyata, atarīṣyatāṃ, atarīṣyan and so on.

"daṃśa sañḍa sāñjaṃ śapi": of daṃśa, sañja, sāñja and sāñja, before śap. That is, the letter n of the roots daṃśa, to bite, ṣañja, to cling, and ṣvañja, to embrace, is elided before the affix śap. For ṣañja with laṭ: with śap, the initial ṣ of the root becoming s, and the ñ being dropped by this sūtra: sajati and so on. Likewise, with liṅ: sajeta and so on. With loṭ: sajatu and so on. With laṅ: asajata and so on.

In the first-person singular of luṅ: vṛddhi by "vada, vraja" and so on; j becomes g by "ku for cu"; g becomes k by "car before khar"; and s being made ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: asāṃkṣīta. In the dual: j becomes g by "ku for cu," sic is dropped by "jhal after jhal," and "car before khar" being applied: asāktāṃ. In the plural, by "ku for cu," "car before khar," "ādeśa" and so on: asāṃkṣuḥ. Derived by the same procedures as these, in the three of the middle person: asaṃkṣīḥ, asāṃktaṃ, asāṃkta, asāṃkta. In the three of the last person: asāṃkṣa, asāṃkṣma.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: sasaṃja, sasaṃjatuḥ, sasaṃjaḥ. In the three of the middle person: sasaṃjitha, sasaṃktha, sasaṃjathuḥ, sasaṃja. In the three of the last person: sasaṃjiva, sasaṃjiv. With luṭ, "ku for cu" and "car before khar" being applied: saṃktā, saṃktārau, saṃktāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, the n being dropped by "not having i as marker" and so on: sajyāta, sajyāstāṃ, sajyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, by "ku for cu," "car before khar," and s being made ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: saṃkṣyati, saṃkṣyataḥ, saṃkṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ: asaṃkṣyatāṃ, asaṃkṣyan and so on.

For the root stated as "dṛśir, to see," attach the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest. By the sūtra "bābhrādhmā" and so on, dṛśir being changed into paśya: with laṭ, paśyati and so on; with liṅ, paśyata and so on; with loṭ, paśyata and so on; with loṭ, paśyatu and so on; with laṅ, apaśyata and so on.

"nadṛṃśaḥ": not for dṛś. That is, as an exception to the rule stated above, "ksa for roots ending in śal, with ik as penultimate, that are without iṭ": although dṛś ends in śal, has ik as penultimate and is without iṭ, cli after dṛś does not become ksa. For dṛś with luṅ, by "optionally for those with ir as marker," changing cli into aṅ and changing it into sic are made optional. In the alternative with aṅ, guṇa being made by "before aṅ, of those ending in ṛ and of dṛś": adarśata, adarśatāṃ, adarśan and so on.

In the alternative where cli is changed into sic: "sṛjidṛṃśojhalyamkiti": am for sṛj and dṛś before jhal not having k as marker. That is, to the two roots sṛja, to emit, and dṛśir, the augment am is attached before affixes beginning with a letter of the group jhal that are not named as having k as marker. The letter m, which drops as a marker, means "after the last vowel." Thus: adrakṣīta, adraṣṭāṃ; sic is dropped by "jhal after jhal," ś becomes ṣ by "vraśca, bhrasja" and so on, and t becomes ṭ by "ṣṭu for ṣṭu"; adrakṣuḥ and so on.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: dadarśa, dadṛśatuḥ, dadṛśuḥ. "bibhāṣā sṛjidṛśoḥ": by "vraśca, bhrasja" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; by "k for ṣ and ḍh," ṣ becomes k; by "ādeśa" and so on, s becomes ṣ; k and ṣ combined give kṣ. Optional from sṛj and dṛś. That is, after sṛja, to emit, and dṛśir, to see, the liṭ replacement thal is to be made either to take iṭ or not to take it: dadarśitha, dadraṣṭha; am by "sṛjidṛśo, jhal, k" and so on; ś becomes ṣ by "vraśca, bhrasja" and so on; and th becomes ṭh by "ṣṭu for ṣṭu." In the middle-person dual and plural: dadṛśathuḥ, dadṛśa. In the three of the last person: dadarśa, dadṛśiva, dadṛśima.

With luṭ, by "am for sṛj and dṛś before jhal not having k as marker," the augment am being given: draṣṭā, draṣṭārau, draṣṭāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ: dṛśyāta, dṛśyāstāṃ, dṛśyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, the augment am, ś becoming ṣ by "vraśca, bhrasja" and so on, "k for ṣ and ḍh," and s becoming ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on, being applied: drakṣyati, drakṣyataḥ, drakṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ, ś becoming ṣ by "vraśca, bhrasja" and so on, and t becoming ṭ by "ṣṭu for ṣṭu": adrakṣyata, adrakṣyatāṃ, adrakṣyan and so on.

For the root stated as "daṃśa, to bite," attach the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest. By "daṃśa, sañja, svañja" and so on, the n being dropped before śap: daśati and so on. With liṅ: daśeta and so on. With loṭ: daśatu and so on. With laṅ: adaśata and so on. With luṅ, ś being changed into ṣ by "vraśca, bhrasja" and so on: adaṃkṣīta, adaṃṣṭāṃ, adaṃkṣuḥ and so on.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: dadaṃśa, dadaṃśatuḥ, dadaṃśuḥ. In the three of the middle person: dadaṃśitha, dadaṃṣṭha, dadaṃśathuḥ, dadaṃśa. In the three of the last person: dadaṃśa, dadaṃśiva, dadaṃśima. With luṭ: by "vraśca," and by "jhal after jhal" sic is dropped; by "ṣṭu for ṣṭu" t becomes ṭ; by "bhrasja" and so on ś becomes ṣ; and t being made ṭ by "ṣṭu for ṣṭu": daṃṣṭā, daṃṣṭārau, daṃṣṭāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, the n being dropped by "not having i as marker" and so on: daśyāta, daśyāstāṃ, daśyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, ś becoming ṣ by "vraśca, bhrasja" and so on, "k for ṣ and ḍh before s," and s being made ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: daṃkṣyati, daṃkṣyataḥ, daṃkṣyataḥ, daṃkṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ too: adaṃkṣyata, adaṃkṣyatāṃ, adaṃkṣyan and so on.

"guptajkidbhyaḥ san": san from gupa, tija and kit. That is, after the three roots stated as "gupū, to protect and to censure," "tija, to be sharp, and also to endure," and "kit, to dwell, and also to cure disease," san comes. The letter n of san is there for the purpose of stating the root twice by "before san and yaṅ." "sanyadoḥ": before san and yaṅ. That is, before san and yaṅ, a root that has no reduplicated syllable is to be stated twice. "būrvatsanaḥ": of san, like the preceding. That is, what ends in san, when san is given to a root, is also like the preceding: since it stands as a root, san is called "the affix that makes a root into a root."

It is quoted in the commentary: "deḥ kramanindākṣamarugjayeṣu sanniṣyate": from gupa and the rest, in order, san is desired in the senses of censure, endurance and curing disease. That is, the application of san to gupa and the rest explained above is also in order: san is held to come when the root gupū is used for censure, tija for endurance, and kit for curing disease; it does not apply in other senses such as craving.

For kit: san; by "before san and yaṅ" the root is stated twice; by "the first consonant remains" the upper t is dropped; by "cu for ku and h" the upper k becomes c. To what is called cikitsa, attach the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest: śap for the agent; after the markers are dropped, by "of a, before guṇa," the two are made one in the form of the latter. With laṭ: cikitsati, cikitsataḥ, cikitsanti and so on. With liṅ: cikitseta, cikitsetāṃ, cikitseyuḥ and so on. With loṭ: cikitsatu or cikitsatāta, cikitsatāṃ, cikitsantu and so on. With laṅ: acikitsata, acikitsatāṃ, acikitsan and so on.

Before the ārdhadhātuka affixes: by iṭ before endings beginning with val, and by "elision of a," the root-final a being dropped: with luṅ, acikitsita, acikitsiṣṭāṃ, acikitsiṣuḥ and so on. With liṭ: by "ām before liṭ, after kās and after an affix, when not in a mantra," ām is attached to the root; by "after ām," liṭ too is lost; and kṛñ, bhū, as and the rest, together with liṭ, being appended after it: cikitsāmāsa, cikitsācakāra, cikitsābabhūva and so on. With luṭ: iṭ before endings beginning with val, and the a being dropped by "elision of a": cikitsitā, cikitsitārau, cikitsitāraḥ and so on. With the benedictive liṅ, the a being dropped by "elision of a": cikitsyāta, cikitsyāstāṃ, cikitsyāsuḥ and so on. With lṛṭ, iṭ before endings beginning with val, and "elision of a": cikitsiṣyati, cikitsiṣyataḥ, cikitsiṣyanti and so on. Likewise, with lṛṅ: acikitsiṣyata, acikitsiṣyatāṃ, acikitsiṣyana and so on.

"kitaḥ saṃdehec": and from kit in the sense of doubt. That is, from kit used in the sense of doubt, san also optionally comes, all the procedures being like those just explained: vicikitsati and so on.

"ṛtirī yaṅ": īyaṅ from ṛti. That is, for the root stated as "ṛta, to go, and also to rejoice," the affix i that gives the root its own form being attached, when ṛti is used in the sense of rejoicing, the affix īyaṅ comes after it, and what ends in the attached īyaṅ is also a root. The letter ṅ of īyaṅ is there so that the ātmanepada endings apply. Attaching īyaṅ, laṭ, śap and so on to ṛt gives ṛtīyate and so on; detailed examples will be explained below.

With these, the general rules together with their exceptions, in rough outline, for attaching the parasmaipada endings, the replacements of the ten l-affixes laṭ and the rest, to the roots of the class beginning with bhū that take śap in the sense of the agent and take the parasmaipada, have been explained.

Now I shall explain the procedure for attaching the ātmanepada endings to the roots of the class beginning with bhū that take the ātmanepada. To the root stated as "edha, to grow," attach the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest. Since the procedures are like those in the section on "bhū, to obtain," in the three of the first person of laṭ: edhate. For edha with laṭ, śap: after the markers are dropped, from la comes ta, and a arises; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e, and so te is drawn.

Edhete. For edha with śap and laṭ, la is replaced by ātām, and from ātām, ām is obtained. By "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final is drawn as e. By "ā of what has ṅ as marker," ā becomes iy; by "of v and y before val," which calls for deletion, y is dropped; i is joined in sandhi. Edhante. For edha with śap and laṭ, la becomes jha, and from jha, a is removed. By "jha becomes ant," and by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e. By "a before guṇa," the two become one, the form of the latter.

In the three of the middle person of laṭ: edhase. For edha with śap and laṭ, la becomes thās; by "thās becomes se," thās becomes se. Edhethe. For edha with śap and laṭ, la becomes āthām, and from āthām, ām is removed. By "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e. By "ā of what has ṅ as marker," ā becomes iy; by "of v and y before val," which calls for deletion, y is dropped; i is joined in sandhi. Edhadhve. For edha with śap and laṭ, la becomes dhvam; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e.

In the three of the last person: edhe. For edha with śap and laṭ, la becomes iṭ; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, i becomes e. By "a before guṇa," the two become one, the form of the latter. Edhāvahe. For edha with śap and laṭ, la becomes vahi and mahiṅ; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes i, that is, e. By "a is lengthened before yañ," a is made long. Edhāmahe.

Edha with liṅ, śap: for liṅ there is sīyuṭ. When sīyuṭ has been added and so on, in the three of the first person: for edha with śap and liṅ, la becomes ta, and liṅ takes sīyuṭ; ṭ is a marker and u is for the sake of pronunciation. By "of v and y before val," which calls for deletion, y is dropped. By "of liṅ, the s that is not final," which calls for deletion, s is dropped, and sandhi is applied. Edheta. For edha with śap, la becomes ātām, and the markers are dropped; by "of liṅ, the s that is not final" and so on, s is dropped, and sandhi is applied. Edheyātām. Edheran. For edha with śap and liṅ, la becomes jha, with sīyuṭ; the markers are dropped; by "of liṅ, the s that is not final" and so on, s is dropped, and sandhi is applied. By "jha becomes ran," jha becomes ran. By "of v and y before val," which calls for deletion, y is dropped.

In the three of the middle person: edhethāḥ. For edha with śap and liṅ, la becomes thās, with sīyuṭ, and the markers are dropped. By "of liṅ, the s that is not final" and so on, s is dropped; by "of v and y before val," which calls for deletion, y is dropped. Edheyāthām. For edha with śap and liṅ, la becomes āthām, with sīyuṭ; by "of liṅ, the s that is not final" and so on, s is dropped, and sandhi is applied. Edhedhvam. For edha with liṅ and śap, la becomes dhvam, with sīyuṭ; by "of liṅ, the s that is not final" and so on, s is dropped, and y is dropped before val.

In the three of the last person: edheya. For edha, la becomes iṭ, with sīyuṭ, and the markers are dropped; by "iṭ becomes at," iṭ becomes at, and sandhi is applied. Edhevahi. For edha with śap and liṅ, la is changed into vahi and mahiṅ, with sīyuṭ, and the markers are dropped. By "of v and y," y is dropped; by "of liṅ, the s that is not final" and so on, s is dropped, and sandhi is applied. Edhemahi.

In the three of the first person of edha with loṭ attached: edhatām. For edha with śap and loṭ, la becomes ta; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e; by "e becomes ām," e becomes ām. Edhetām. For edha with śap and loṭ, la becomes ātām; by "ā of what has ṅ as marker," ā becomes iy, and sandhi is applied; by "of v and y," y is dropped. By "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e, and by "e becomes ām," it turns back into ām once again. Edhantām. For edha with loṭ, la becomes jha; by "jha becomes ant," jha becomes ant. By "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e; by "e becomes ām," e becomes ām. By "a before guṇa," the two become one, the form of the latter.

In the three of the middle person: edhasva. For edha with śap and loṭ, la becomes thās; by "thās becomes se," thās becomes se; by "after s and v, va and am," e becomes va. Edhethām. For edha with śap and loṭ, la becomes āthām; by "ā of what has ṅ as marker," ā becomes iy; by "of v and y," y is dropped, and i is joined in sandhi. By "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e; by "e becomes ām," e becomes ām again. Edhadhvam. For edha with śap and loṭ, la becomes dhvam; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e; by "after s and v, va and am," e becomes am once again.

In the three of the last person: edhai. For edha with śap and loṭ, la becomes iṭ; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, i becomes e; by "e becomes ai," e is changed into ai. By "āṭ for the last person," āṭ is added; ṭ is a marker; by "a vowel of the ak class with one of the same class becomes long," and by vṛddhi of the vowel, the form is made. Edhāvahai. For edha with śap and loṭ, la is changed into vahi and mahiṅ; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e; by "e becomes ai," e becomes ai. By "āṭ for the last person," āṭ is added, ṭ being a marker, and by "a vowel of the ak class with one of the same class becomes long," it is lengthened. Edhāmahai.

In the three of the first person of edha with laṅ attached: aidhata. For edha with laṅ, la becomes ta; by "āṭ for those beginning with a vowel," āṭ is added to the root, ṭ being a marker; and by "and of āṭ," vṛddhi takes place. Aidhetām. For edha with śap and laṅ, after āṭ and vṛddhi, la becomes ātām; by "ā of what has ṅ as marker," ā becomes iy; by "of v and y," y is dropped, and sandhi is applied. Aidhanta. For edha with śap and laṅ, the root takes āṭ and vṛddhi; la becomes jha, and by "jha becomes ant," jha becomes ant. By "a before guṇa," the two become one, the form of the latter.

In the three of the middle person: aidhathāḥ. For edha with śap and laṅ, la becomes thās, and the root takes āṭ and vṛddhi. Aidhethām. For edha with śap and laṅ, the root takes āṭ and vṛddhi, and la becomes āthām; by "ā of what has ṅ as marker," ā becomes iy; by "of v and y before val," which calls for deletion, y is dropped, and sandhi is applied. Aidhadhvam. For edha with śap and laṅ, the root takes āṭ and vṛddhi, and la is changed into dhvam.

In the three of the last person: aidhe. For edha with śap and laṅ, the root takes āṭ and vṛddhi, la is changed into iṭ, and sandhi is applied. Aidhāvahi. For edha with śap and laṅ, the root takes āṭ and vṛddhi, la is changed into vahi and mahiṅ, and by "a is lengthened before yañ," it becomes long. Aidhāmahi.

Edha with luṅ. For luṅ, by "cli for luṅ," cli is put. By "sic for cli," cli is changed into s. By "āṭ for those beginning with a vowel," āṭ is added to the root, and by "and of āṭ," vṛddhi takes place. And because the suffix that is ārdhadhātuka begins with val, it takes iṭ. When iṭ has been added and so on, in the three of the first person: aidhiṣṭa. La is changed into ta; by "the substitute and the suffix" and so on, s becomes ṣ, and by "with ṣ and ṭ-class, ṣ and ṭ-class," t becomes ṭ. Aidhiṣātām. La is changed into ātām; by "the substitute and the suffix" and so on, s becomes ṣ. Aidhiṣata. La is changed into jha; from jha, a is removed, and by "in the ātmanepada, after what is not a," jha is changed into at.

In the three of the middle person: aidhiṣṭhāḥ. La becomes thās; by "the substitute and the suffix" and so on, s becomes ṣ, and by "with ṣ and ṭ-class, ṣ and ṭ-class," th becomes ṭh. Aidhiṣāthām. La becomes āthām; by "the substitute and the suffix" and so on, s becomes ṣ. Aidhidhvam. La becomes dhvam, and s is dropped; by the option allowed after iṭ, dh either stays as it is or else becomes ḍh: aidhiḍhvam.

In the three of the last person: aidhiṣi. La is changed into iṭ. Aidhiṣvahi. La is changed into vahi. Aidhiṣmahi. La is changed into mahiṅ.

Edha with liṭ. By "after a root beginning with an ic vowel and having a heavy syllable, other than ṛcch," ām is attached to the end of the root, and by "after ām," liṭ too is elided, so that edhām is formed. To it kṛñ and the rest must be added, for: "āmpratyayavat kṛño 'nuprayogasya": "of kṛñ added as an auxiliary, just as with the suffix (pratyaya) ām."

Of the three that are added after ām, kṛ, bhū and as: although ām is attached to roots that take the ātmanepada, such as edh, bhū and as are words of the parasmaipada, so only the parasmaipada suffixes of liṭ are applied to them. Kṛñ is a word of both padas, so if the root to which ām is attached takes the ātmanepada, kṛñ is applied with ātmanepada suffixes, as before; and if that root takes the parasmaipada, kṛñ too should be applied with parasmaipada suffixes. When bhū and as are attached to edhām: edhāṃ babhūva, edhām āsa.

In the three of the first person with kṛñ attached: edhāṃ cakre. Kṛ with liṭ: by "in liṭ, of a root without reduplication," the root is stated twice. By "ṛ becomes at," ṛ is changed into a. By "c for k and h," k becomes c. La is changed into ta. By "for ta and jha of liṭ, eś and irec," ta becomes eś; ś is dropped, and by "ik before a vowel becomes yaṇ," yaṇ is made. Edhāṃ cakrāte. La becomes ātām; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e. Edhāṃ cakrire. Kṛ with liṭ: the root is stated twice. By "ṛ becomes a," ṛ becomes a; by "c for k and h," ka becomes ca. La is changed into jha; by "for ta and jha of liṭ, eś and irec," jha is changed into irec, its c serving for pronunciation, and by "ik before a vowel becomes yaṇ," yaṇ is made.

In the singular and dual of the middle person: edhāṃ cakṛṣe. La is changed into thās; by "thās becomes se," thās becomes se; by "the substitute and the suffix" and so on, s becomes ṣ. Edhāṃ cakrāthe. La becomes āthām; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e; by "ik before a vowel becomes yaṇ," yaṇ is made.

In the plural of the middle person: "iṇaḥ ṣīdhvaṃluṅliṭāṃ dho 'ṅgāt": after a stem ending in iṇ, the dh of ṣīdhvam, luṅ and liṭ. That is, after the end of a root falling within the group iṇ, the letter dh of sīdhvam of the benedictive liṅ, and of luṅ and liṭ, becomes the letter ḍh. Edhāṃ cakṛḍhve. Kṛ with liṭ: the root is stated twice; by "ṛ becomes at," and by "c for k and h," ka becomes ca. La becomes dhvam; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e; by this sūtra, dh becomes ḍh.

In the three of the last person: edhāṃ cakre. La is changed into iṭ; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e. Edhāṃ cakṛvahe. La is changed into vahi and mahiṅ; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e. Edhāṃ cakṛmahe.

Edha with luṭ: since iṭ is added to a suffix beginning with val, in the three of the first person: edhitā, edhitārau, edhitāraḥ. In the three of the middle person: edhitāse. For edha with luṭ and tās, la is changed into thās; by "thās becomes se," thās becomes se; by "of tās and as," which calls for deletion, the s of tās is dropped; and iṭ is added before val. Edhitāsāthe. La is changed into āthām; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e. Edhitādhve. La becomes dhvam; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e; by "and before dh," the s of tās is dropped.

In the three of the last person: edhitāhe. For edha with luṭ and tās, la is changed into iṭ; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, i becomes e; by "h before e," s becomes h; and iṭ is added before val. Edhitāsvahe. La is changed into vahi and mahiṅ; by "having ṭ as marker" and so on, the final becomes e. Edhitāsmahe.

In the three of the first person of edha with the benedictive liṅ attached: edhiṣīṣṭa, edhiṣīyāstām, edhiṣīran. In the three of the middle person: edhiṣīṣṭhāḥ, edhiṣīyāsthām, edhiṣīdhvam, edhiṣīḍhvam. In the three of the last person: edhiṣīya, edhiṣīvahi, edhiṣīmahi.

In the three of the first person of edha with lṛṭ attached: edhiṣyate, edhiṣyante. In the three of the middle person: edhiṣyase, edhiṣyethe, edhiṣyadhve. The three of the last person: edhiṣye; la is changed into iṭ, and by "iṭ becomes at," iṭ becomes at. Edhiṣyāvahe, edhiṣyāmahe.

Edha with lṛṅ: by "āṭ for those beginning with a vowel," āṭ is added to the root, and by "and of āṭ," vṛddhi takes place.
