When sya has been added and so on, in the three of the first person: aidhiṣyata, aidhiṣyetām, aidhiṣyanta. In the three of the middle person: aidhiṣyathāḥ, aidhiṣyethām, aidhiṣyadhvam. In the three of the last person: aidhiṣye, aidhiṣyāvahi, aidhiṣyāmahi, and so on. For the most part the procedure is like that explained in the section on "bhū, to obtain."

For the root stated as "īkṣa, to see," the whole procedure for attaching the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest is like what has just been explained.

For the root stated as "dada, to give," when the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest are attached, the procedure, apart from the section on liṭ, is like the section on edha. In laṭ: dadate, dadete, dadante, and so on. In liṅ: dadeta, dadeyātām, daderan, and so on. In loṭ: dadatām, dadetām, dadantām, and so on. In laṅ: adadata, adadetām, adadanta, and so on. In luṅ: adadiṣṭa, adadiṣātām, adadiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, when the root has been stated twice and iṭ added before val and so on, in the three of the first person: dadade, dadadāte, dadadire. In the three of the middle person: dadadiṣe, dadadāthe, dadadidhve, dadadiḍhve. In the three of the last person: dadade, dadadivahe, dadadimahe, and so on. Here, by the sūtra on śas, dad, roots beginning with v and the rest, the deletion of the reduplicated syllable and the change to e are not carried out.

In luṭ, since iṭ is added to the ārdhadhātuka suffix beginning with val, when iṭ is attached: daditā, daditārau, daditāraḥ, daditāse, daditāsāthe, daditādhve, daditāhe, daditāsvahe, daditāsmahe. In the benedictive liṅ too, iṭ is attached: dadiṣīṣṭa, dadiṣīyāstām, dadiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, from iṭ before val and from sya, which is supplied by "sya and tās," come dadiṣyate, dadiṣyete, dadiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: adadiṣyata, adadiṣyetām, adadiṣyanta, and so on.

For the root stated as "ṣvaṣka, to go," the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest are attached, and the procedure is like that just explained. Here the initial ṣ of nominal roots and the like does not change into s. In laṭ: ṣvaṣkate, ṣvaṣkete, ṣvaṣkante, and so on. In liṅ: ṣvaṣketa, ṣvaṣkeyātām, ṣvaṣkeran, and so on. In loṭ: ṣvaṣkatām, ṣvaṣketām, ṣvaṣkantām, and so on. In laṅ: aṣvaṣkata, aṣvaṣketām, aṣvaṣkanta, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is attached before val: aṣvaṣkiṣṭa, aṣvaṣkiṣātām, aṣvaṣkiṣata, and so on.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: saṣvaṣke, saṣvaṣkāte, saṣvaṣkire. In the three of the middle person: saṣvaṣkiṣe, saṣvaṣkāthe, saṣvaṣkidhve, saṣvaṣkiḍhve. In the three of the last person: saṣvaṣke, saṣvaṣkivahe, saṣvaṣkimahe.

In luṭ, in the three of the first person with iṭ attached: ṣvaṣkitārau, ṣvaṣkitāraḥ. In the three of the middle person: ṣvaṣkitāse, ṣvaṣkitāsāthe, ṣvaṣkitādhve. In the three of the last person: ṣvaṣkitāhe, ṣvaṣkitāsvahe, ṣvaṣkitāsmahe.

In the three of the first person of the benedictive liṅ: ṣvaṣkiṣīṣṭa, ṣvaṣkiṣīyāstām, ṣvaṣkiṣīran. In the three of the middle person: ṣvaṣkiṣīṣṭhāḥ, ṣvaṣkiṣīyāsthām, ṣvaṣkiṣīdhvam, ṣvaṣkiṣīḍhvam. In the three of the last person: ṣvaṣkiṣīya, ṣvaṣkiṣīvahi, ṣvaṣkiṣīmahi.

In lṛṭ, since sya and iṭ before val are supplied: ṣvaṣkiṣyate, ṣvaṣkiṣyete, ṣvaṣkiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aṣvaṣkiṣyata, aṣvaṣkiṣyetām, aṣvaṣkiṣyanta, and so on.

For the root stated as "ṛja, to go, and also to stay," the procedure for attaching the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest is like the one before. In laṭ: arjate, arjete, arjante, and so on. In liṅ: arjeta, arjeyātām, arjeran, and so on. In loṭ: arjatām, arjetām, arjantām, and so on. In laṅ: ārjata, ārjetām, ārjanta, and so on. In luṅ, with iṭ before val, the change of cli into sic, and so on: ārjiṣṭa, ārjiṣātām, ārjiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, the root is stated twice; by "ṛ becomes at," ṛ becomes a; and by the lengthening of an initial a, the giving of nuṭ, and so on, the forms are produced. In the three of the first person: ānṛje, ānṛjāte, ānṛjire. In the three of the middle person: ānṛjiṣe, ānṛjāthe, ānṛjidhve, ānṛjiḍhve. In the three of the last person: ānṛje, ānṛjivahe, ānṛjimahe. In luṭ, with iṭ before val, the addition of tās, and so on: arjitā, arjitārau, arjitāraḥ, arjitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: arjiṣīṣṭa, arjiṣīyāstām, arjiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, with iṭ before val, and sya attached by "sya and tās in lṛ and luṭ": arjiṣyate, arjiṣyete, arjiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: ārjiṣyata, ārjiṣyetām, ārjiṣyanta, and so on.

For the root stated as "tija, to sharpen, and also to endure": by "after gup, tij and kit, san," san is added. By "in san and yaṅ," the root is stated twice. By "the initial consonant remains," the upper j is dropped. By "k-class for c-class," j becomes g; by "c-class before khar," g becomes k. By "the substitute and the suffix" and so on, s becomes ṣ, and k and ṣ combine as kṣ. When titikṣa has been formed in this way and laṭ and the rest are attached: in laṭ, titikṣate, titikṣete, titikṣante, and so on. In liṅ: titikṣeta, titikṣeyātām, titikṣeran, and so on. In loṭ: titikṣatām, titikṣetām, titikṣantām, and so on. In laṅ: atitikṣata, atitikṣetām, atitikṣanta, and so on. In luṅ, with the ārdhadhātuka: śap is added in the sense of the agent and its markers are dropped; by "a before guṇa," the two become one, the form of the latter. Iṭ is due before an ārdhadhātuka suffix beginning with val, and iṭ is given. By "deletion of a," the final a of the root is deleted, and so on: atitikṣiṣṭa, atitikṣiṣātām, atitikṣiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, by "after a suffixed root such as kās, ām," ām is attached to the end of the root; by "after ām," liṭ is elided; and when kṛñ and the rest are attached: titikṣāṃ cakre, titikṣāṃ babhūva, titikṣām āsa, and so on. In luṭ, with iṭ before val, the deletion of a, and so on: titikṣitā, titikṣitā, titikṣitārau, titikṣitāraḥ, titikṣitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ too: titikṣiṣīṣṭa, titikṣiṣīyāstām, titikṣiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, with iṭ before an ārdhadhātuka suffix beginning with val, and sya attached by "sya and tās": titikṣiṣyate, titikṣiṣyete, titikṣiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: atitikṣiṣyata, atitikṣiṣyetām, atitikṣiṣyanta, and so on.

For the root stated as "ṣvañja, to embrace," laṭ and the rest are attached. By "the initial ṣ of a root," ṣ becomes s, and by "of daṃś, sañj and svañj before śap," n is deleted, and so on. In laṭ: svajate, svajete, svajante, and so on. In liṅ: svajeta, svajeyātām, svajeran, and so on. In loṭ: svajatām, svajetām, svajantām, and so on; and in laṅ: asvajata, asvajetām, asvajanta, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ does not enter. Cli is changed into sic, and the forms are produced by deletion of a jhal after a jhal before a jhal, by "k-class for c-class," and so on. In the three of the first person of luṅ: asvaṅkta, asvaṅkṣātām, asvaṅkṣata. In the three of the middle person: asvaṅkthāḥ, asvaṅkṣāthām, asvaṅgdhvam. In the three of the last person: asvaṅkṣi, asvaṅkṣvahi, asvaṅkṣmahi.

In liṭ, it is quoted in the commentary: "svañjeḥ saṃyogād api liṭo vā kittvam": "After svañj, even after a conjunct, liṭ is optionally kit." That is, after svañj and after a conjunct, the following liṭ suffixes that are not causes of guṇa and vṛddhi are optionally given the designation "having k as marker." The purpose is that for a kit suffix, the deletion of n of roots not having i as marker, and guṇa and so on, should be optional. In the kit option, in the three of the first person: sasvaje, sasvajāte, sasvajire. In the three of the middle person: sasvajiṣe, sasvajāthe, sasvajidhve, sasvajiḍhve. In the three of the last person: sasvaje, sasvajivahe, sasvajimahe. In the option where the designation kit is not made, everything is the same except that n is not deleted: sasvañje, sasvañjāte, sasvañjire, and so on.

In luṭ, by "k-class for c-class," j becomes g, and by "c-class before khar," g is changed into k: svaṅktā, svaṅktāraḥ, svaṅktāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "k-class for c-class," and by "c-class before khar," g becomes k; by the change of "the substitute and the suffix" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ becomes ṣ; k and ṣ combine as kṣ, and so on: svaṅkṣīṣṭa, svaṅkṣīyāstām, svaṅkṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, the forms are produced by "k-class for c-class," "c-class before khar," "the substitute and the suffix," and so on: svaṅkṣyate, svaṅkṣyete, svaṅkṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: asvaṅkṣyata, asvaṅkṣyetām, asvaṅkṣyanta, and so on.

When an upasarga is applied before svajate, by "after pari, ni and vi" and so on, s becomes ṣ: niṣvajate, and so on.

"sivādīnāṃ vāṭ vyavāye 'pi": of siv and the rest, optionally, even when aṭ intervenes. That is, after the upasargas pari, ni and vi, siv and the rest, namely ṣivu, to weave cloth; ṣaha, to show respect; ṣṭuñ, to praise; and ṣvañja, to embrace; and the s of the augment suṭ is certainly included. These letters, even when the augment aṭ stands between, optionally become the letter ṣ: nyaṣvajata, nyasvajata, and so on. These follow laṅ.

"sadisvañjyoḥ parasya liṭi": after sad and svañj, in liṭ. When liṭ is given to "ṣadḷ, to decay, to go, and to be thoroughly pleased," and to "ṣvañja, to embrace," the root is stated twice, and the first part is called the abhyāsa. What follows it does not become ṣ, even after pari, ni and vi coming before: niṣasvaje or niṣasvañje, and so on.

For the root stated as "trapūṣ, to be ashamed," laṭ and the rest are attached. Ū and ṣ are markers. The forms are produced by attaching śap in all the sārvadhātuka endings, and by optionally attaching iṭ, through "having ū as marker" and so on, before the ārdhadhātuka suffixes beginning with val, and so on. In laṭ: trapate, trapete, trapante, and so on. In liṅ: trapeta, trapeyātām, traperan, and so on. In loṭ: trapatām, trapetām, trapantām, and so on. In laṅ: atrapata, atrapanta, and so on. In luṅ, in the option where iṭ is attached: atrapiṣṭa, atrapiṣātām, atrapiṣata, and so on. In the option where iṭ is not given: atrapta, atrapsātām, atrapsata, and so on. In liṭ, by the sūtra "and of tṝ, phala, bhaja and trapa," the deletion of the abhyāsa and the change to e and so on are carried out: trepe, trepāte, trepire, and so on. In luṭ, since iṭ before val is made optional: trapitā and so on, or traptā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ too, since iṭ is made optional: trapiṣīṣṭa, trapiṣīyāstām, trapiṣīran, and so on; or, in the option where iṭ is not given, trapsīṣṭa, trapsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, since iṭ is made optional: trapiṣyate, trapiṣyete, trapiṣyante, and so on; or trapsyate, trapsyete, trapsyete, trapsyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: atrapiṣyata, atrapiṣyetām, atrapiṣyanta, and so on; or atrapsyetām, atrapsyanta, and so on.

"radhijabhor aci": of radh and jabh before a vowel. Before a suffix beginning with a vowel, following radha, to harm, and jabha, to stretch the body, the augment num arises.

Jabha: laṭ and the rest are attached. The forms are produced by attaching śap in all the sārvadhātuka endings, and iṭ to the ārdhadhātuka suffixes beginning with val, and so on. In laṭ: jambhate, jambhete, jambhante, and so on. In liṅ: jambheta, jambheyātām, jambheran, and so on. In loṭ: jambhatām, jambhetām, jambhantām. In laṅ: ajambhata, ajambhetām, ajambhanta. In luṅ: ajambhiṣṭa, ajambhiṣātām, ajambhiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: jajambhe, jajambhāte, jajambhire, and so on. In luṭ: jambhitā, jambhitārau, jambhitāraḥ, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: jambhiṣīṣṭa, jambhiṣīyāstām, jambhiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: jambhiṣyete, jambhiṣyante, and so on. In lṛṅ: ajambhiṣyata, ajambhiṣyetām, ajambhiṣyanta, and so on.

For the root stated as "ṣṭubha, to be firm," laṭ and the rest are attached. By "for the initial ṣ of a root, s," ṣ becomes s, and by "when the cause is absent, what it causes is also absent," ṭ reverts to t. The forms are made by attaching śap in all the sārvadhātuka endings and iṭ to the ārdhadhātuka suffixes. In laṭ: stobhate, stobhete, stobhete, stobhante, and so on. In liṅ: stobheta, stobheyātām, stobheran, and so on. In loṭ: stobhatām, stobhetām, stobhantām, and so on. In laṅ: astobhata, astobhetām, astobhanta, and so on. In luṅ: astobhiṣṭa, astobhiṣātām, astobhiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, by "preceded by śar" and so on, the s of the abhyāsa is deleted, and so on: tuṣṭubhe, tuṣṭubhāte, tuṣṭubhire, and so on. In luṭ: stobhitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: stobhiṣīṣṭa, stobhiṣīyāstām, stobhiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: stobhiṣyate, stobhiṣyete, stobhiṣyante, and so on. In lṛṅ: astobhiṣyata, astobhiṣyetām, astobhiṣyanta, and so on.

For the root stated as "paṇa, to trade, and also to praise," laṭ and the rest are attached. Āya is attached to roots such as gup and dhūp, and the commentary says that for the ātmanepada endings this is to be optional. So in the option where āya is attached, in laṭ: paṇāyate, paṇāyete, paṇāyante, and so on. In liṅ: paṇāyeta, paṇāyeyātām, paṇāyeran, and so on. In loṭ: paṇāyatām, paṇāyetām, paṇāyantām, and so on. In laṅ: apaṇāyata, apaṇāyetām, apaṇāyanta, and so on. In luṅ, with iṭ before val, and the deletion due for a, the a at the end of the root being dropped: apaṇāyiṣṭa, apaṇāyiṣātām, apaṇāyiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, by the sūtra on kās and the rest, ām is attached, and so on: paṇāyāṃ cakre, paṇāyāṃ babhūva, paṇāyām āsa, and so on. In luṭ: paṇāyitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: paṇāyiṣīṣṭa, paṇāyiṣīyāstām, paṇāyiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: paṇāyiṣyate, paṇāyiṣyete, paṇāyiṣyante, and so on. In lṛṅ: apaṇāyiṣyata, apaṇāyiṣyetām, apaṇāyiṣyanta, and so on.

In the option where āya is not attached, in laṭ: paṇate, and so on. In liṅ: paṇeta, and so on. In loṭ: paṇatām, and so on. In laṅ: apaṇata, and so on. In luṅ: apaṇiṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ: peṇe, peṇāte, peṇire, and so on. In luṭ: paṇitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: paṇiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: paṇiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: apaṇiṣyata, and so on. Further, the commentary explains that although paṇ takes the ātmanepada endings, in some cases, in the option where āya is attached, the parasmaipada endings also come in; so paṇāyati and the like also occur.

"kamer ṇiṅ": after kami, ṇiṅ. For the root stated as "kamu, to be lovely," after kami, to which the suffix i in its own sense is attached, ṇiṅ comes. Its ṅ serves to bring in the ātmanepada, and its ṇ serves for vṛddhi of the root. In laṭ, with śap in the sense of the agent, guṇa, and so on: kāmayate, and so on. In liṅ: kāmayeta, and so on. In loṭ: kāmayatām, and so on. In laṅ: akāmayata, and so on.

When ṇi is attached to kamu, kāmi results. For kāmi with luṅ: luṅ, cli, ṇi; by "after ṇi, śri" and so on, cli is changed into caṅ, and la becomes ta: kāmi caṅ ta. "ṇau caṅy upadhāyā hrasvaḥ": the penultimate of ṇi before caṅ becomes short. That is, the penultimate of a stem ending in ṇi becomes short before caṅ, into which cli was changed; so kā became short. By "before caṅ," the root is stated twice. By "c-class for k and h," k becomes c: ca ka; and so cakami caṅ ta arises.

"sanval laghuni caṅpare 'nag lope": when ak is not deleted, before a light syllable with caṅ following, as with san. That is, for a stem ending in ṇi whose syllable is light, and in which no letter of the group ak at the end of the root has been dropped, the operations on the abhyāsa before caṅ are to be done as with san. "sanyataḥ": of a, before san. Before san, the a of the first part of the doubled root, called the abhyāsa, becomes i. So here, by the earlier and the later sūtras together: cikami caṅ ta. "dīrgho laghoḥ": the lengthening of a light vowel. The light vowel of the abhyāsa, before a light syllable, with ṇi and caṅ following, becomes long: ci became long, cīkami caṅ ta. "ṇer aniṭi": of ṇi, before what is not iṭ. Before an ārdhadhātuka ending that does not begin with iṭ, ṇi is to be deleted. The marker ṇ is dropped, and the markers ṅ and c of caṅ are dropped too. Since aṭ is added to the root in luṅ, laṅ and the rest: acīkamata. Produced in the same way, in the dual and plural: acīkametām, acīkamanta. In the three of the middle person of luṅ: acīkamathāḥ, acīkamethām, acīkamadhvam. In the three of the last person: acīkame, acīkamāvahi, acīkamāmahi.

By the sūtra "āya and the rest are optional before the ārdhadhātuka," in the option where ṇiṅ is not given, since the commentary explains that cli becomes caṅ even where there is no ṇi: acakamata, acakametām, acakamanta, and so on.

In liṭ, by "kās" and so on, ām is attached to kāmi: kāmi ām liṭ; by "after ām," liṭ is elided. "ayām antālv āyyetnviṣṇuṣu": ay before ām, anta, ālu, āyya, itnu and iṣṇu. Before ām, and before the kṛt and other suffixes ālu, āpya, itnu and iṣṇu, what ends in ṇi becomes ay: kāmayāṃ cakre, kāmayāṃ babhūva, kāmayāṃ babhūva, kāmayām āsa, and so on. In the option where ṇiṅ is not given: cakame, cakamāte, cakamire. In the three of the middle person: cakamiṣe, cakamāthe, cakamiḍhve. In the three of the last person: cakame, cakamivahe, cakamimahe.

In luṭ, in the option where ṇiṅ is attached: kāmayitā and so on; in the option where ṇiṅ is not attached: kamitā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, in the option where ṇiṅ is attached: kāmayiṣīṣṭa and so on; in the option where ṇiṅ is not attached: kamiṣīṣṭa and so on. In lṛṭ, in the option where ṇiṅ is attached: kāmayiṣyate and so on; in the option where ṇiṅ is not given: kamiṣyate and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, in the option where ṇiṅ is attached: akāmayiṣyata and so on; in the option where ṇiṅ is not attached: akamiṣyata and so on.

For the root stated as "aya, to go," laṭ and the rest are attached. In laṭ: ayate, and so on. In liṅ: ayeta, and so on. In loṭ: ayatām, and so on. In laṅ: āyata, and so on. In luṅ: āyiṣṭa, and so on. "dayāyāsaś ca": and also after day, ay and ās. After daya, to give; aya, to go; and ās, to sit, ām is also to be attached before liṭ. For aya, the forms are produced with liṭ, ām and so on: ayāṃ cakre, ayāṃ babhūva, ayām āsa, and so on. In luṭ, since there is iṭ before val: ayitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: ayiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: ayiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: āyiṣyata, and so on.

"upasargasyāyatau": of an upasarga, before ayati. The letter r of an upasarga becomes the letter l before ayate. Pra is placed before ayate; by this sūtra r becomes l, and by "ak with a like vowel becomes long," the vowel is lengthened: plāyate, "he makes go forth." Likewise parā with ayate: palāyate, "he makes go beyond." For pari with laṅ, by "ik before a vowel becomes yaṇ," yaṇ is made, and with sandhi: palyayate, "he makes go all around." The commentary explains that even before ayate, the letter r of prati, nir and dur does not become l: so pratyayate, "he makes go severally"; nirayate, "he makes not go"; durayate, "he makes go badly."

For the root stated as "daya, to go, to harm and to give," laṭ and the rest are attached, and every operation is like that of aya. In laṭ: dayate, and so on. In liṅ: dayeta, and so on. In loṭ: dayatām, and so on. In laṅ: adayata, and so on. In luṅ: adayiṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ, since ām is attached by "also after day, ay and ās": dayāṃ cakre, dayāṃ babhūva, dayām āsa, and so on. In luṭ: dayitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: dayiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: dayiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: adayiṣyata, and so on.

For the root stated as "sphāyī, to grow," laṭ and the rest are attached. In laṭ: sphāyate, and so on. In liṅ: sphāyeta, and so on. In loṭ: sphāyatām, and so on. In laṅ: asphāyata, and so on. In luṅ and the rest, before suffixes beginning with val, iṭ is to be optional, for it is quoted in the commentary: "cāyasphāyapyāyām iḍ vā": iṭ is optional for cāy, sphāy and pyāy. For cāyṛ, to worship, and for sphāyī and opyāyī, to grow, iṭ is to be optional before a suffix beginning with val, liṭ excepted. In luṅ, in the option where iṭ is attached: asphāyiṣṭa, asphāyiṣātām, asphāyiṣata, and so on. In the option where iṭ is not given, y is dropped by "of v and y before val," which calls for deletion. In the three of the first person: asphāsta, asphāsātām, asphāsata. In the three of the middle person: asphāsthāḥ, asphāsāthām, asphādhvam; by "and before dh," sic too is dropped. In the three of the last person: asphāsi, asphāsvahi, asphāsmahi.

In liṭ, the root is stated twice; by "short," the vowel reverts to short; by "khay preceded by śar," s is dropped; by "car in the abhyāsa," ph is changed into p, and so on. In the three of the first person: pasphāye, pasphāyāte, pasphāyire. In the three of the middle person: pasphāyiṣe, pasphāyāthe, pasphāyidhve, pasphāyiḍhve. In the three of the last person: pasphāye, pasphāyivahe, pasphāyimahe. In luṭ, in the option where iṭ is attached: sphāyitā, sphāyitārau, sphāyitāraḥ, and so on; and in the option without iṭ, y being dropped by "of v and y before val," which calls for deletion: sphātā, sphātārau, sphātāraḥ, and so on.

In the benedictive liṅ, in the option where iṭ is attached: sphāyiṣīṣṭa, and so on; and in the option without iṭ, y being dropped: sphāsīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ, in the option where iṭ is attached: sphāyiṣyate, and so on; and in the option without iṭ, y being dropped by "of v and y": sphāsyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, in the option where iṭ is attached: asphāyiṣyata, and so on; and in the option where iṭ is not given, y being dropped: asphāsyata, and so on.

For opyāyī, "to grow," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, pyāyate, and so on. In liṅ, pyāyeta, and so on. In loṭ, pyāyatām, and so on. In laṅ, apyāyata, and so on.

Dīpajanabudhapūritāyipyāyibhyo 'nyatarasyām: "From dīpa, jana, budha, pūri, tāyi and pyāyi, optionally." From dīpī, "to blaze," janī, "to be born," budha, "to understand," pūrī, "to be satisfied," tāyṛ, "to extend," and opyāyī, "to grow," before ta, the singular of the first person of luṅ, cli optionally becomes ciṇ, or else it becomes sic. By ciṇo luk, "after ciṇ it is elided," the ta that replaced la after the ciṇ that was substituted for cli is also to be elided. Thus: pyāy plus la, in luṅ; in luṅ, by "dīpa" and so on, cli is changed into ciṇ. The ṇ serves for vṛddhi; the c serves for the rule "after ciṇ it is elided." By this sūtra the ta that replaced la is dropped: apyāyi. In the option where cli is changed into sic, iṭ is made optional by "cāya" and so on. In the option where iṭ is attached: apyāyiṣṭa, apyāyiṣātām, apyāyiṣata, and so on; and in the option where iṭ is not given, y being dropped by "of v and y before val, which calls for deletion": apyāsta, apyāsātām, apyāsata, and so on.

Liḍyaṅoś ca: "Also before liṭ and yaṅ." Before liṭ and yaṅ, pyāy is to be changed into pī. Pyāy plus liṭ; by this sūtra it is changed into pī; and being formed by reduplication and so on: pipye, pipyāte, pipyire. In the three of the middle person: pipyiṣe, pipyāthe, pipyidhve, pipyiḍhve. In the three of the last person: pipye, pipyivahe, pipyimahe. In luṭ, iṭ being made optional, in the option where iṭ is given: pyāyitā, and so on; and in the option without iṭ, y being dropped by "of v and y before val, which calls for deletion": pyātā, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ, in the option where iṭ is attached: pyāyiṣīṣṭa, and so on; and in the option without iṭ: pyāsīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ, in the option where iṭ is attached: pyāyiṣyate, and so on; and in the option where iṭ is not given, y being dropped by "of v and y" and so on: pyāsyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: apyāyiṣyata, and so on, or apyāsyata, and so on.

For tāyṛ, "to extend and to protect," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, tāyate, and so on. In liṅ, tāyeta, and so on. In loṭ, tāyatām, and so on. In laṅ, atāyata, and so on. In the singular of the first person of luṅ, in the option where, by "dīpa" and so on, cli is optionally changed into ciṇ: atāyi; or else, being changed into sic: atāyiṣṭa, atāyiṣātām, atāyiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: tatāye, tatāyāte, tatāyire, tatāyiṣe, and so on. In luṭ: tāyitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: tāyiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: tāyiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: atāyiṣyata, atāyiṣyetām, atāyiṣyanta, and so on.

For śala, "to move, and also to cover," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, śalate, and so on. In liṅ, śaleta, and so on. In loṭ, śalatām, and so on. In laṅ, aśalata, and so on. In luṅ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being attached: aśaliṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ, deletion of the abhyāsa, change into e, and so on being made: śele, śelāte, śelire, and so on. In luṭ: śalitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, iṭ being attached: śaliṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: śaliṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: aśaliṣyata, and so on.

For ṣevṛ, "to wash," applying laṭ and the rest, and forming it by changing the initial ṣ of the root into s and so on: in laṭ, sevate, and so on. In liṅ, seveta, and so on. In loṭ, sevatām, and so on. In laṅ, asevata, and so on. In luṅ, the root being one that takes the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val, iṭ is given: aseviṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ, the root being reduplicated, the shortening that is due, the change of e into i, and so on being made: siṣeve, siṣevāte, siṣevire, and so on. In luṭ: sevitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: seviṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: seviṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: aseviṣyata, and so on.

For kāśṛ, "to blaze," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, kāśate, and so on. In liṅ, kāśeta, and so on. In loṭ, kāśatām, and so on. In laṅ, akāśata, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ being attached: akāśiṣṭa, and so on. Quoted in the commentary: kāśakāsor ām vā, "For kāś and kās, optionally ām." For kāśṛ, "to blaze," and kāsṛ, "to make a bad sound," before liṭ, ām is to be attached optionally. In the option where ām is attached: kāśāṃ cakre, kāśāṃ babhūva, kāśām āsa, and so on; and in the option where ām is not attached: cakāśe, cakāśāte, cakāśire, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ being attached: kāśitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: kāśiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: kāśiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: akāśiṣyata, and so on.

For kāsṛ, "to make a bad sound," all the operations of applying laṭ and the rest are just like those explained immediately above.

For īha, "to play," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, īhate, and so on. In liṅ, īheta, and so on. In loṭ, īhatām, and so on. In laṅ, aihata, and so on. In luṅ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being given: aihiṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ, ām being attached by the rule on a root beginning with ic and having a heavy syllable, and so on: īhāñcakre, īhāṃbabhūva, īhāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ being given: īhitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: īhiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ too, the root being one that takes the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val, iṭ is given: īhiṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aihiṣyata, and so on.

For gāṅ, "to go," laṭ and the rest are applied. By "śap in the agent," and after the anubandha of śap is dropped, lengthening being made by "of a like ak," in the three of the first person of laṭ: "goes," gāte. La is replaced by ātām, and by "of ṭit" and so on the final becomes e, with lengthening by "of a like ak": gāte. La is replaced by jha; by "before ātmanepada endings, not after a," jha is changed into at; by "of ṭit" and so on the final becomes e, and by "of a like ak" and so on it is lengthened: gāte. In the three of the middle person: gāse, gāthe, gādhve. In the three of the last person: ge, gāvahe, gāmahe.

The three of the first person of liṅ, "should go" and "they should go": geta, geyātām, geran. In the three of the middle person: gethāḥ, geyāthām, gedhvam. In the three of the last person: geya, gevahi, gemahi.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: la is replaced by ta, by "of ṭit" and so on it becomes e, and by "ām of et," e becomes ām: gātām. La is replaced by ātām, lengthened by "of a like ak": gātām; "they shall go": gātām. In the three of the middle person: gāsva, gāthām, gādhvam. In the three of the last person: gai, gāvahai, gāmahai.

In the three of the first person of laṅ: agāta, agātām, agāta. In the three of the middle person, "go!": agāthāḥ; "go, you two!": agāthām; and, jha being replaced by at by "before ātmanepada endings" and so on, by "of ṭit" and so on, and by "ām of et": agādhvam. In the three of the last person: age, agāvahi, agāmahi. In luṅ: agāsta, agāsātām, agāsata, and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: jage, where a is dropped by "of ā, deletion also before iṭ"; jagāte, jagire. In the three of the middle person: jagiṣe, jagāthe, jagidhve, jagiḍhve. In the three of the last person: jage, jagivahe, jagimahe. In luṭ: gātā, gātārau, gātāraḥ, gātāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: gāsīṣṭa, gāsīyāstām, gāsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: gāsyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: agāsyata, and so on.

For ruṅ, "to go, and also to speak," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, ravate, and so on. In liṅ, raveta, and so on. In loṭ, ravatām, and so on. In laṅ, aravata, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ being made optional by "ru, dru" and so on: araviṣṭa, araviṣātām, araviṣata, and so on, or aroṣṭa, aroṣātām, aroṣata, and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: ruruve, ruruvāte, ruruvire. In the three of the middle person: ruruviṣe, ruruvāthe, ruruvidhve, ruruviḍhve. In the three of the last person: ruruve, ruruvivahe, ruruvimahe. In luṭ, iṭ being made optional: ravitā, and so on, or rotā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ too, iṭ being made optional: raviṣīṣṭa, and so on, or roṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: raviṣyate, and so on, or roṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: araviṣyata, and so on, or aroṣyata, and so on.

For deṅ, "to protect," laṭ and the rest being given: in laṭ, dayate, and so on. In liṅ, dayeta, and so on. In loṭ, dayatām, and so on. In laṅ, adayata, and so on.

Sthāghvor icca: "And i for sthā and ghu." Before the ātmanepada endings of luṅ, the final of sthā and of the roots named ghu becomes i; and the sic that replaces cli after what has become i is designated as having the name kit, so that guṇa and so on are not made. Thus: deṅ, in luṅ, sic; by "when not śit, ā for ec in the original statement," e becomes ā, and by this sūtra ā is changed into i; ta, the affix due at that time, being placed after it: adi s ta. To this applies hrasvād aṅgāt, "after a short stem." The sic that replaced cli after a stem ending in a short vowel is deleted before an affix beginning with a letter of the jhal class; sic being dropped: adita. In the dual and plural: adiṣātām, adiṣata. In the three of the middle person: adithāḥ, adiṣāthām, adidhvam, adiḍhvam. In the three of the last person: adiṣi, adiṣvahi, adiṣmahi.

Dayater digi liṭi: "Digi for dayati before liṭ." Before liṭ, dayati, that is, deṅ, "to protect": the root deṅ becomes digi, and reduplication and so on are not done. In the three of the first person: digye, digyāte, digyire. In the three of the middle person: digyiṣe, digyāthe, digyidhve, digyiḍhve. In the three of the last person: digye, digyivahe, digyimahe. In luṭ, ec being changed into ā by "when not śit" and so on: dātā, dātārau, dātāraḥ, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: dāsīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: dāsyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: adāsyata, and so on.

For ḍīṅ, "to go through the sky," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, ḍayate, and so on. In liṅ, ḍayeta, and so on. In loṭ, ḍayatām, and so on. In laṅ, aḍayata, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ and guṇa of the root being made: aḍayiṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ, the root being reduplicated, shortened by "short," and ḍ being changed into ṭ by "car in the abhyāsa," and so on: ṭiḍye, ṭiḍyāte, ṭiḍyire. In the three of the middle person: ṭiḍyiṣe, ṭiḍyāthe, ṭiḍyidhve, ṭiḍyiḍhve. In the three of the last person: ṭiḍye, ṭiḍyivahe, ṭiḍyimahe. In luṭ, iṭ being attached and guṇa made: ḍayitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: ḍayiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: ḍayiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: aḍayiṣyata, and so on.

For gup, "to hide and to censure": by "san after gup, tij and kit," san is attached; by "before san and yaṅ," the root is reduplicated; by "cu for ku and h," g is changed into j; and jugupsa is thus formed. Applying laṭ and the rest to it: in laṭ, jugupsate, and so on. In liṅ, jugupseta, and so on. In loṭ, jugupsatām, and so on. In laṅ, ajugupsata, and so on. In luṅ, by the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val, and a being dropped by "deletion of a": ajugupsiṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ, ām being attached by "after kās" and so on: jugupsāñcakre, jugupsāṃbabhūva, jugupsāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ being given and a being dropped by "deletion of a": jugupsitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: jugupsiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: jugupsiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: ajugupsiṣyata, and so on.

Mānbadhadānśānbhyo dīrghaś cābhyāsasya: "From mān, badh, dān and śān; and lengthening of the abhyāsa." From mān, "to honor," badh, "to censure," dān, "to cut off completely," and śān, "to sharpen," san comes about; and the root being reduplicated by "before san and yaṅ," its first part, which has the name abhyāsa, also becomes long. Thus: mān, san; the root is reduplicated; by "short," the former part becomes short; by "i for a before san," a becomes i; and by this sūtra it is lengthened. To mīmāṃsa so formed, laṭ and the rest are applied: in laṭ, mīmāṃsate, and so on. In liṅ, mīmāṃseta, and so on; in loṭ, mīmāṃsatām, and so on; and in laṅ, amīmāṃsata, and so on. In luṅ, by the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val, and a being dropped by "deletion of a": amīmāṃsiṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ, ām being attached by "after kās" and so on: mīmāṃsāñcakre, mīmāṃsāṃbabhūva, mīmāṃsāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, by iṭ, and a being dropped by "deletion of a": mīmāṃsitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: mīmāṃsiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ, mīmāṃsiṣyate, and so on; and in lṛṅ, amīmāṃsiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise badh, "to censure," takes san; the root is reduplicated by "before san and yaṅ"; by "i for a before san," a becomes i; by this sūtra it is lengthened; by "bhaṣ for the baś of a monosyllabic root ending in jhaṣ, before s and dhv," the latter b becomes bh; and by "car before khar," dh is changed into t. To bībhatsa so formed, laṭ and the rest are applied: in laṭ, bībhatsate, and so on. In liṅ, bībhatseta, and so on. In loṭ, bībhatsatām, and so on. In luṅ, by the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val, and a being dropped by "deletion of a": abībhatsiṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ: bībhatsāñcakre, bībhatsāṃbabhūva, bībhatsāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ: bībhatsitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: bībhatsiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: bībhatsiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: abībhatsiṣyata, and so on.

For dyuta, "to shine," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, dyotate, and so on. In liṅ, dyoteta, and so on. In loṭ, dyotatām, and so on. In laṅ, adyotata, and so on.

Dyudbhyo luṅi: "From dyut and the rest, in luṅ." For dyut and the rest, in luṅ the parasmaipada endings optionally occur. In the parasmaipada option, cli being changed into aṅ by the sūtra "after puṣa and the rest, dyut and the rest": adyutat, adyutatām, adyutan, and so on. In the ātmanepada option, cli is changed into sic, and the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val is attached: adyotiṣṭa, adyotiṣata, and so on.

Dyutisvāpyoḥ saṃprasāraṇam: "Saṃprasāraṇa of dyuti and svāpi." For dyuta, "to blaze," and ñiṣvap, "to sleep," in liṭ the first part of the reduplicated root, which has the name abhyāsa, is to be changed back by saṃprasāraṇa: didyute, didyutāte, didyutire, didyutiṣe, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ being attached: dyotitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: dyotiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: dyotiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: adyotiṣyata, and so on.

For vṛtu, "to proceed," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, vartate, and so on. In liṅ, varteta, and so on. In loṭ, vartatām, and so on. In laṅ, avartata, and so on. In luṅ, the parasmaipada and ātmanepada endings being made optional by "from dyut and the rest, in luṅ": in the option where parasmaipada endings are attached, avṛtat, avṛtatām, avṛtan, and so on. In the ātmanepada option, cli is changed into sic and the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val is attached: avartiṣṭa, avartiṣātām, avartiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: vavṛte, vavṛtāte, vavṛtire, and so on. In luṭ: vartitā, vartitārau, vartitāraḥ, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: vartiṣīṣṭa, vartiṣīyāstām, vartiṣīran, and so on.

Vṛdbhyaḥ syasanoḥ: "From vṛt and the rest, before sya and san." Vṛt and the rest are vṛtu, "to proceed," vṛdhu, "to grow," śṛdhu, "to make a bad sound," syandū, "to ooze," and kṛpū, "to be able." Although these roots take the ātmanepada endings, before sya and san they optionally take the parasmaipada endings as well.

Na vṛdbhyaś caturbhyaḥ: "Not from the four, vṛt and the rest." From the four of the five, vṛt and the rest, leaving aside kṛpū, iṭ does not occur before parasmaipada endings beginning with the letter s, and in some cases it is optional before other affixes. For vṛtu, by "from vṛt and the rest," in lṛṭ, in the option where parasmaipada endings are attached: vartsyati, vartsyataḥ, vartsyanti, and so on. In the option where ātmanepada endings are attached: vartiṣyate, vartiṣyete, vartiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, in the parasmaipada option: avartsyat, avartsyatām, avartsyan, and so on. In the option where ātmanepada endings are attached: avartiṣyata, avartiṣyetām, avartiṣyanta, and so on.

For syandū, "to ooze," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, syandate, and so on. In liṅ, syandeta, and so on. In loṭ, syandatām, and so on. In laṅ, asyandata, and so on. In luṅ, the parasmaipada and ātmanepada endings being made optional by "dyut and the rest": in the option where parasmaipada endings are attached, cli is changed into aṅ by "after puṣa and the rest, dyut and the rest," and n is dropped by "of what is not idit" and so on: asyadat, asyadatām, asyadan, and so on. In the ātmanepada option, iṭ being made optional by "ūdit" and so on: in the option where iṭ is attached, asyandiṣṭa, asyandiṣātām, asyandiṣata, and so on. In the three of the first person of the option where iṭ is not attached: asyanta, asyantsātām, asyantsata. In the three of the middle person of that option: asyanthāḥ, asyantsāthām, asyandhvam. In the three of the last person: asyantsi, asyantsvahi, asyantsmahi.

In the three of the first person, liṭ being applied: sasyande, sasyandāte, sasyandire. In the middle person, for ta, sic is dropped by "after jhal, before jhal"; d is dropped by "of jhar before a like jhar"; and d is turned into t by "car before khar." In the three: sasyandiṣe or sasyantse, sasyandāthe, sasyandidhve or sasyandhve, d being dropped by "of jhar before a like jhar": sasyandhve. In the three of the last person: sasyande, sasyandivahe or sasyandvahe, sasyandimahe or sasyandmahe. In luṭ, iṭ being made optional: in the option where iṭ is given, syanditā, and so on; and in the option without iṭ, d being dropped by "of jhar before a like jhar": syantā, syantārau, syantāraḥ, and so on.

In the benedictive liṅ, in the option where iṭ is attached: syandiṣīṣṭa, syandiṣīyāstām, syandiṣīran, and so on; and in the option without iṭ, d being changed into t by "car before khar": syantsīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ, the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada endings being made optional by "from vṛt and the rest, before sya and san": in the parasmaipada option, iṭ does not occur, by "not from the four, vṛt and the rest," and d is changed into t by "car before khar": syantsyati, syantsyataḥ, syantsyanti, and so on. In the ātmanepada option, iṭ being made optional by "ūdit" and so on: in the option with iṭ, syandiṣyate, and so on; and in the option without iṭ, syantsyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, in the parasmaipada option: asyantsyat, asyantsyan, and so on; and in the option where ātmanepada endings are attached, iṭ being made optional: asyandiṣyata, and so on, or else asyantsyata, and so on.

Anuviparyabhinibhyaḥ syandater aprāṇiṣu: "For syandati after anu, vi, pari, abhi and ni, where not of living beings." When it applies to what is not a living being, after these prefixes, anu and the rest, the letter s of syandate optionally becomes the letter ṣ: anuṣyandate rathaḥ, "the chariot runs along," and so on, or anusyandate rathaḥ, and so on. Likewise vi, pari, abhi and ni are to be applied. Since "not of living beings" excludes them, when it applies to a living being it does not become ṣ: nisyandate hastī, "the elephant oozes."

For kṛpū, "to be able," laṭ, "the chariot runs along," and the rest, "the chariot runs along," are applied. Kṛpo ro laḥ: "L for the r of kṛp." The letter r of kṛpū is to be changed into the letter l before an affix; and since this is not absolutely fixed, in some cases it is also not changed. Kṛpū, laṭ, "the elephant surely moves," śap; by this sūtra ṛ becomes ḷ, and guṇa being made by "of a penultimate light vowel, and of what ends in puk" and so on: kalpate, and so on. In liṅ, kalpeta, and so on. In loṭ, kalpatām, and so on. In laṅ, akalpata, and so on. In luṅ, the parasmaipada and ātmanepada endings being made optional by "from dyut and the rest, in luṅ": in the parasmaipada option, cli being changed into aṅ by "after puṣa and the rest, dyut and the rest": aklṛpat, aklṛpatām, aklṛpan, and so on. In the ātmanepada option, iṭ being made optional by "ūdit" and so on: in the option with iṭ, akalpiṣṭa, akalpiṣātām, akalpiṣata, and so on; and in the option without iṭ:

Liṅsicāv ātmanepadeṣu: "Liṅ and sic before the ātmanepada endings." After a root ending in a consonant whose penultimate letter is one of the ik class, the benedictive liṅ and the sic of the ātmanepada that begin with a letter of the jhal class and are without iṭ are designated as having the name kit, so that guṇa, vṛddhi and so on are not made. In the three of the first person: aklṛpta, aklṛpsātām, aklṛpsata. In the three of the middle person: aklṛpthāḥ, aklṛbdhvam. In the three of the last person: aklṛpsi, aklṛpsvahi.

In the three of the first person, liṭ being applied: caklṛpe, caklṛpāte, caklṛpire. In the three of the middle person, sic being dropped by "after jhal, before jhal": caklṛpiṣe or caklṛpse, caklṛpāthe, caklṛpidhve, caklṛpiḍhve; and, sic being dropped by "after jhal, before jhal," and b coming about by "jaś for jhal before jhaś": caklṛbdhve. In the three of the last person: caklṛpe, caklṛpivahe or caklṛpvahe, caklṛpimahe or caklṛpmahe.

Luṭi ca klṛpaḥ: "And for klṛp in luṭ." For klṛp, in luṭ, and by the word "and" in lṛṭ and lṛṅ, the parasmaipada endings optionally occur; and after a stem ending in san too the parasmaipada endings optionally occur. Tāsi ca klṛpaḥ: "And before tās, for klṛp." After klṛp, iṭ does not occur before tās, nor before the parasmaipada affixes beginning with the letter s. By "and in luṭ," the parasmaipada and ātmanepada endings being made optional, in the parasmaipada option iṭ does not enter, by this sūtra; and guṇa being made by "of what ends in puk" and so on: kalptā, kalptārau, kalptāraḥ, kalptāsi, and so on. In the ātmanepada option, iṭ being made optional by "ūdit" and so on: in the option where iṭ is given, kalpitā, kalpitārau, kalpitāraḥ, kalpitāse, and so on; and in the option where iṭ is not given, kalptā, kalptārau, kalptāraḥ, kalptāse, and so on.

In the benedictive liṅ, iṭ being made optional by "ūdit" and so on: in the option where iṭ is given, kalpiṣīṣṭa, and so on; and in the option without iṭ, since it is kit by "liṅ and sic before the ātmanepada endings," guṇa is not made: klṛpsīṣṭa, klṛpsīyāstām, klṛpsīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ, the parasmaipada and ātmanepada endings being made optional by "and for klṛp in luṭ": in the option where the parasmaipada endings are attached, iṭ does not enter, by "and before tās, for klṛp": kalpsyati, kalpsyataḥ, kalpsyanti, and so on. In the ātmanepada option, iṭ being made optional by "ūdit" and so on: in the option where iṭ is given, kalpiṣyate, and so on; and in the option without iṭ, kalpsyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, the parasmaipada and ātmanepada endings being made optional by "and for klṛp in luṭ": in the option where the parasmaipada endings are attached, iṭ does not enter, by "and before tās": akalpsyat, akalpsyatām, akalpsyan, and so on. In the ātmanepada option, iṭ being made optional: akalpiṣyata, and so on, or akalpsyata, and so on.

For vyatha, "to suffer and to tremble," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, vyathate, and so on. In liṅ, vyatheta, and so on. In loṭ, vyathatām, and so on. In laṅ, avyathata, and so on. In luṅ: avyathiṣṭa, avyathiṣātām, avyathiṣata, and so on.

Vyatho liṭi: "For vyath, in liṭ." Before liṭ, the abhyāsa of the reduplicated vyath undergoes saṃprasāraṇa: vivyathe, vivyathāte, vivyathire, vivyathiṣe, and so on. In luṭ: vyathitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: vyathiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: vyathiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: avyathiṣyata, and so on.

For ñitvarā, "to hurry," applying laṭ and the rest: in laṭ, tvarate, and so on. In liṅ, tvareta, and so on. In loṭ, tvaratām, and so on. In laṅ, atvarata, and so on. In luṅ: atvariṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ: tatvare, tatvarāte, tatvarire, tatvariṣe, and so on.

In luṭ: tvaritā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: tvariṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: tvariṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: atvariṣyata, and so on.

Thus the procedure for applying the ātmanepada case endings, laṭ and the rest, to those roots of the bhū class and the rest that take the ātmanepada, in whose domain śap enters for the agent, has been explained in its broad outlines, with the general rules and the exceptions.

Now I shall explain together whatever procedures are appropriate: applying both the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada endings, laṭ and the rest, to the roots of the bhū class and the rest that take both kinds of endings; and further, applying the ātmanepada to roots that take the ātmanepada, applying the parasmaipada endings to roots that take the parasmaipada, and so on.

For ḍupacaṣ, "to cook," the anubandhas being dropped and laṭ and the rest applied: in the parasmaipada endings of laṭ, pacati, pacataḥ, pacanti, and so on. In the ātmanepada endings, pacate, pacete, pacante, and so on. Likewise, śap being given for the agent, in the parasmaipada endings of liṅ: pacet, pacetām, paceyuḥ, and so on. In the ātmanepada endings: paceta, paceyātām, paceran, and so on. In the parasmaipada endings of loṭ: pacatu, pacatāt, pacatām, pacantu, and so on. In the ātmanepada endings: pacatām, pacetām, pacantām, and so on. In the parasmaipada endings of laṅ: apacat, apacatām, apacan, and so on. In the ātmanepada endings: apacata, apacetām, apacanta, and so on.

In luṅ, since the root is aniṭ, iṭ does not enter. By "vada, vraja" and so on the penultimate is lengthened; by "ku for cu," c becomes k; by "in a substitute" and so on s is changed into ṣ; and by the deletion of sic, due before what begins with jhal, and so on, the forms are made. In the parasmaipada endings: apākṣīt, apāktām, apākṣuḥ, and so on. Likewise in the ātmanepada endings: apakta, apakṣātām, apakṣata, and so on; for in the ātmanepada the penultimate is not lengthened.

In liṭ, the forms being made by the reduplication of the root, by the deletion of the abhyāsa and the change into e before what is kit, by the attaching of iṭ before what begins with val by the sūtra "kṛ, vṛ, sṛ" and so on: papāca, pecatuḥ, pecuḥ, pecitha, papaktha, and so on. In the ātmanepada endings: pece, pecāte, pecire, and so on. In luṭ, c being changed into k by "ku for cu": in the parasmaipada endings, paktā, paktārau, paktāraḥ, paktāsi, and so on. In the ātmanepada endings: paktā, paktārau, paktāraḥ, paktāse, and so on. In the parasmaipada endings of the benedictive liṅ: pacyāstām, pacyāsuḥ, and so on. In the ātmanepada endings, the forms being made by "ku for cu," by "in a substitute," and so on: pakṣīṣṭa, pakṣīyāstām, pakṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, by "ku for cu," "in a substitute," and so on: in the parasmaipada endings, pakṣyati, pakṣyataḥ, pakṣyanti, and so on; and in the ātmanepada, pakṣyate, pakṣyete, pakṣyante, and so on. Likewise in the parasmaipada endings of lṛṅ: apakṣyat, apakṣyatām, apakṣyan, and so on; and in the ātmanepada endings: apakṣyata, apakṣyetām, apakṣyanta, and so on.

For patḷ, "to go," since the root takes the parasmaipada, the parasmaipada endings, laṭ and the rest, are applied: in laṭ, patati, and so on. In liṅ, patet, and so on. In loṭ, patatu, and so on. In laṅ, apatat, and so on.

Pataḥ pum: "Pum for pat." Before the aṅ that replaced the cli of pat, the augment pum is to be given; the m serves for its position, and the u for its utterance. Pat, luṅ; in luṅ, cli being changed into aṅ by "after puṣa and the rest, dyut and the rest, ḷdit and the rest," and the augment pu being given by this sūtra: apaptat, apaptatām, apaptan, and so on. In liṭ, the forms being made by dropping the abhyāsa before what is kit, changing into e, and so on: papāta, petatuḥ, petuḥ, petitha, and so on. In luṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being attached: patitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: patyāt, patyāstām, patyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being attached: patiṣyati, patiṣyataḥ, patiṣyanti, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: apatiṣyat, apatiṣyatām, apatiṣyan, and so on.

For ṭuvamu, "to vomit," since it too takes the parasmaipada, the parasmaipada endings, laṭ and the rest, are applied: in laṭ, vamati, and so on. In liṅ, vamet, and so on. In loṭ, vamatu, and so on. In laṅ, avamat, and so on. In luṅ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being attached: avamīt, avamiṣṭām, avamiṣuḥ, and so on. Quoted in the commentary: vamer etvābhyāsalopau vā, "For vam, the deletion of the abhyāsa and e are optional." Although it was explained above, by "of śas, dad, and what begins with v," that the abhyāsa is not deleted, as an exception to that, before a liṭ that is kit, the deletion of the abhyāsa of vam, the change into e, and so on are optional: vavāma, vematuḥ or vavamatuḥ, vemuḥ or vavamuḥ, vemitha or vavamitha. In luṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being given: vamitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: vamyāt, vamyāstām, vamyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being given: vamiṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: avamiṣyat, and so on.

Bhramu, "to move," also takes the parasmaipada, so the parasmaipada endings, laṭ and the rest, are applied. For all the roots of the bhū class and the rest, śap comes for the agent; and śyan being made optional by the sūtra "bhrāśa, bhlāśa, bhramu" and so on: in laṭ, bhramati, and so on, or bhrāmyati, and so on. Likewise in liṅ, bhramet, and so on, or bhrāmyet, and so on. In loṭ, bhramatu, and so on, or bhrāmyatu, and so on. In laṅ, abhramat, and so on, or abhrāmyat, and so on. In luṅ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being given: abhramīt, abhramiṣṭām, abhramiṣuḥ, and so on.

Vā jṝbhramutrasām: "Optionally, of jṝ, bhramu and tras." For jṝṣ, "to lose one's youth," bhramu, "to move," and trasī, "to be distressed," before a liṭ that is kit, the deletion of the abhyāsa, the change into e, and so on are optional: babhrāma, bhrematuḥ or babhramatuḥ, bhremuḥ, bhremitha or babhramitha, and so on. In luṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being attached: bhramitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: bhramyāt, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being attached: bhramiṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: abhramiṣyat, and so on.

Ṣaha, "in the sense of enduring." Since the root is ātmanepadin, the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest are applied. By the operations that change ṣ into s, such as the rule that the initial ṣ of a root becomes s: in laṭ, sahate, and so on. In liṅ, saheta, and so on. In loṭ, sahatām, and so on. In laṅ, asahata, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ being added: asahiṣṭa, asahiṣātām, asahiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: sehe, sehāte, sehire, and so on.

In luṭ, iṭ is made optional by the sūtra "iṣu, saha," and so on. On the side with iṭ: sahitā, sahitārau, sahitāraḥ, and so on. On the side without iṭ: to saha is added luṭ; luṭ becomes tās; by "of luṭ, the first" and so on, ta becomes ḍā: saha plus tā. By the rule that h becomes ḍh: saḍh plus tā. Since dhā does not follow a jhaṣ consonant, t and th become dh: saḍh plus dhā. By the rule that before a retroflex a dental becomes retroflex, dh is changed into ḍh: saḍh plus ḍhā. Then for ḍhā there is sahivahor od avarṇasya: "the a of sahi and vahi becomes o." When ḍh has been deleted by the rule that ḍh is elided before ḍh, the letter a of ṣaha, "to endure," and of vaha, "to convey," is to be changed into o. By "ḍh before ḍh" the former ḍh is deleted, and by this sūtra a is changed into o: soḍhā. Likewise soḍhārau, soḍhāraḥ. This is sahivahor od avarṇasya.

Soḍhaḥ: "of soḍh." Although, before saha becomes soḍh, a preverb occurs that is a cause for the change into ṣ, by "soḍhaḥ" it does not become the letter ṣ: visoḍhā, parisoḍhā, and so on.

In the benedictive liṅ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added: sahiṣīṣṭa, sahiṣīyāstām, sahiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added: sahiṣyate, sahiṣyete, sahiṣyante, and so on. Likewise, in lṛṅ: asahiṣyata, asahiṣyetām, asahiṣyanta, and so on.

Ṣadḷ, "in the senses of disintegrating, going, and wearing down." Since it is parasmaipadin, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are applied. In the four sārvadhātuka tenses, it is changed into sīd by the sūtra "pā, ghrā, dhmā," and so on: in laṭ, sīdati, and so on. In liṅ, sīdet, and so on. In loṭ, sīdatu, and so on. In laṅ, asīdat, and so on. In luṅ, cli is changed into aṅ by "after puṣa and the rest, dyuta and the rest, and roots marked with ḷ": asadat, asadatām, asadan, and so on. In liṭ: sasāda, sedatuḥ, seduḥ, seditha, sasattha, and so on. In luṭ, d is changed into t by khari ca, "and before a khar consonant": sattā, sattārau, sattāraḥ, sattāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: sadyāt, sadyāstām, sadyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: satsyati, satsyataḥ, satsyanti, and so on. Likewise, in lṛṅ: asatsyat, asatsyatām, asatsyan, and so on.

Śadeḥ śitaḥ: "of śadi, before affixes marked with ś." Śadḷ, "in the sense of perishing": although the root is by nature parasmaipadin, before the affixes marked with ś the ātmanepada endings come in. So the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest, the four sārvadhātuka tenses, are applied, and by the sūtra "pā, ghrā, dhmā," and so on, śad is changed into śīya: in laṭ, śīyate, and so on. In liṅ, śīyeta, and so on. In loṭ, śīyatām, and so on. In laṅ, aśīyata, and so on. For luṅ and the rest, the ārdhadhātuka tenses, the parasmaipada endings are applied. In luṅ, cli is changed into aṅ by "puṣa" and so on: aśadat, aśadatām, aśadan, and so on. In liṭ: śaśāda, śedatuḥ, śeduḥ, śeditha, śaśattha, and so on. In luṭ, d is changed into t by khari ca: śattā, śattārau, śattāraḥ, śattāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: śadyāt, śadyāstām, śadyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, d is changed into t by khari ca and the forms are derived: śatsyati, śatsyataḥ, śatsyanti, and so on. Likewise, in lṛṅ: aśatsyat, aśatsyatām, aśatsyan, and so on.

Phaṇa, "in the sense of going." Since it is parasmaipadin, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are applied. In laṭ, phaṇati, and so on. In liṅ, phaṇet, and so on. In loṭ, phaṇatu, and so on. In laṅ, aphaṇat, and so on. In luṅ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added: aphāṇīt, aphāṇiṣṭām, aphāṇiṣuḥ, and so on.

Phaṇāṃ ca saptānām: "and of the seven, phaṇa and the rest." Among phaṇa and the rest, these seven roots are phaṇa, "to go," rājṛ, bhrājṛ, ṭubhrāśṛ, ṭubhlāśṛ, syamu, and svana, "to sound." For these seven, in liṭ before an affix marked with k, where the penultimate would otherwise be strengthened by "vada, vraja," and so on, the deletion of the abhyāsa before the following affix, the change into e, and so on are optional. Adding liṭ to phaṇa: paphāṇa, pheṇatuḥ or paphaṇatuḥ, pheṇuḥ or paphaṇuḥ, pheṇitha or paphaṇitha, and so on. In luṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added: phaṇitā, phaṇitārau, phaṇitāraḥ, phaṇitāsmi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: phaṇyāt, phaṇyāstām, phaṇyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added: phaṇiṣyati, phaṇiṣyataḥ, phaṇiṣyanti, and so on. Likewise, in lṛṅ: aphaṇiṣyat, aphaṇiṣyatām, aphaṇiṣyan, and so on.

Rājṛ, "in the sense of shining." Since the root takes both voices, both the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest come in. With the parasmaipada endings of laṭ: rājati, rājataḥ, rājanti, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: rājate, rājante, and so on. Applying the parasmaipada endings of liṅ: rājet, rājetām, rājeyuḥ, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: rājeta, rājeyātām, rājeran, and so on. Applying the parasmaipada endings of loṭ: rājatu, rājatāt, rājatām, rājantu, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: rājatām, rājetām, rājantām, and so on. Applying the parasmaipada endings of laṅ: arājat, arājatām, arājan, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: arājata, arājetām, arājanta, and so on. With the parasmaipada endings of luṅ: arājīt, arājiṣṭām, arājiṣuḥ, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: arājiṣṭa, arājiṣātām, arājiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, by "and of the seven, phaṇa and the rest," the deletion of the abhyāsa and so on are optional. With the parasmaipada endings: rarāja, rejatuḥ or rarājatuḥ, rejuḥ or rarājuḥ, and so on. Applying the ātmanepada endings: reje or rarāje, rejāte or rarājāte, rejire or rarājire, and so on. Applying the parasmaipada endings of luṭ: rājitā, rājitārau, rājitāraḥ, rājitāsi, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: rājitā, rājitārau, rājitāraḥ, rājitāse, and so on.

And so on. With the parasmaipada endings of the benedictive liṅ: rājyāt, rājyāstām, rājyāsuḥ, and so on. Applying the ātmanepada endings: rājiṣīṣṭa, rājiṣīyāstām, rājiṣīran, and so on. With the parasmaipada endings of lṛṭ: rājiṣyati, rājiṣyataḥ, rājiṣyanti, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: rājiṣyate, rājiṣyete, rājiṣyante, and so on. With the parasmaipada endings of lṛṅ: arājiṣyat, arājiṣyatām, arājiṣyan, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: arājiṣyata, arājiṣyetām, arājiṣyanta, and so on.

Ṭubhrāśṛ, "in the sense of shining." Since it is ātmanepadin, the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest come in. In the four sārvadhātuka tenses, śap and śyan are made optional in the sense of the agent by the sūtra "bhrāśa, bhlāśa, bhramu," and so on. So in laṭ: bhrāśate, and so on, or else bhrāśyate, and so on. Likewise in liṅ: bhrāśeta, and so on, or bhrāśyeta, and so on. In loṭ: bhrāśatām, and so on, or bhrāśyatām, and so on. In laṅ: abhrāśata, and so on, or abhrāśyata, and so on. In luṅ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added: abhrāśiṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ, the deletion of the abhyāsa and so on are made optional by the sūtra on phaṇa and the rest: bhreśe or babhrāśe, bhreśāte or babhrāśāte, bhreśire or babhrāśire, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ being added: bhrāśitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: bhrāśiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: bhrāśiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: abhrāśiṣyata, and so on. Likewise ṭubhlāśṛ, "to shine," is in every procedure just like what has just been explained.

Svana, "in the sense of sound." Since the root is parasmaipadin, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are applied. In laṭ: svanati, and so on. In liṅ: svanet, and so on. In loṭ: svanatu, and so on. In laṅ: asvanat, and so on. In luṅ, vṛddhi is made optional: asvanīt, asvaniṣṭām, asvaniṣuḥ, and so on, or asvānīt, and so on. In liṭ, the deletion of the abhyāsa and so on being made optional by the rule on phaṇa and the rest: sasvāna, svenatuḥ or sasvanatuḥ, svenuḥ or sasvanuḥ, and so on. In luṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being applied: svanitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: svanyāt, and so on. In lṛṭ: svaniṣyati, and so on. In lṛṅ: asvaniṣyat, and so on.

By the rule "svani, in the sense of eating," with what carries over from above: when vi or ava comes before svani and the sense of eating is expressed, the s becomes ṣ: viṣvaṇati māṃsam, "he eats meat with a noise." Where it is not eating, it does not become ṣ: visvanati vīṇā, "the lute resounds," and so on. Likewise ava is to be applied as well.

Khanu, "in the sense of digging." Since it is parasmaipadin, the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are applied. In laṭ: khanati, and so on. In liṅ: khanet, and so on. In loṭ: khanatu, and so on. In laṅ: akhanat, and so on. In luṅ, vṛddhi being made optional: akhānīt, akhāniṣṭām, akhāniṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, the forms are derived by the deletion of the penultimate a before affixes marked with k, by the sūtra "gama, hana, jana, khana," and so on: cakhāna, cakhnatuḥ, cakhnuḥ, and so on. In luṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added: khanitā, and so on.

Ye vibhāṣā: "optionally before y." For the roots khana, "to dig," jana, "to be born," and ṣaṇa, "to honor," before an affix marked with k or ṅ that begins with the letter y, the final also optionally becomes ā. In the benedictive liṅ: khanyāt, and so on, or khāyāt, and so on. In lṛṭ: khaniṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: akhaniṣyat, and so on.

Cāyṛ, "in the senses of worshipping and of perceiving," is also parasmaipadin, so the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest are applied. In laṭ: cāyati, and so on. In liṅ: cāyet, and so on. In loṭ: cāyatu, and so on. In laṅ: acāyat, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is made optional by the cited rule on cāya, spāya, pyāya, and so on. On the side where iṭ is not added, the forms are derived by the deletion of y according to the rule "v and y are deleted before val," and so on. So: acāyīt, acāyiṣṭām, acāyiṣuḥ, and so on, or acāsīt, acāstām, acāsuḥ, and so on. In liṭ: cacāya, cacāyatuḥ, cacāyuḥ, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ being made optional: cāyitā, and so on, or cātā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: cāyyāt, and so on. In lṛṭ, the adding of iṭ and the deletion of y being made optional: cāyiṣyati, and so on, or cāsyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: acāyiṣyat, and so on, or acāsyat, and so on.

Laṣa, "in the sense of loveliness," is also parasmaipadin, so the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest come in. In the four sārvadhātuka tenses, śap and śyan are made optional by the sūtra "bhrāśa, bhlāśa, bhramu," and so on. So in laṭ: laṣati, and so on, or laṣyati, and so on. Likewise in liṅ: laṣet, and so on, or laṣyet, and so on. In loṭ: laṣatu, and so on, or laṣyatu, and so on. In laṅ: alaṣat, and so on, or alaṣyat, and so on. In luṅ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added and vṛddhi being made optional: alāṣīt, alāṣiṣuḥ, and so on, or alaṣīt, and so on. In liṭ: lalāṣa, leṣatuḥ, leṣuḥ, and so on. In luṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added: laṣitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: laṣyāt, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ being applied: laṣiṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: alaṣiṣyat, and so on.

Ūd upadhāyā gohaḥ: "the penultimate of goh becomes ū." Before an affix beginning with a vowel, goha: that is, the letter u that is the penultimate of guhū, "to conceal completely," becomes ūt, that is, it becomes long ū.

Since guhū takes both voices, with the parasmaipada endings of laṭ: gūhati, and so on, and with the ātmanepada endings: gūhate, and so on. Likewise with the parasmaipada endings of liṅ: gūhet, and so on, and with the ātmanepada endings: gūheta, and so on. With the parasmaipada endings of loṭ: gūhatu, and so on, and with the ātmanepada endings: gūhatām, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is made optional by the rule on roots marked with ū and so on. On the side where iṭ is added, the penultimate is lengthened by the sūtra "of goh." On the side where iṭ is added, with the parasmaipada endings: agūhīt, agūhiṣṭām, agūhiṣuḥ, and so on; and with the ātmanepada endings: agūhiṣṭa, agūhiṣātām, agūhiṣata, and so on.

On the side without iṭ, by "after a root ending in śal with a penultimate ik, and lacking iṭ," and so on, cli is changed into ksa. By the rule that h becomes ḍh: guḍh. By the sūtra "of a single-vowel root ending in jhaṣ, a baś becomes bhaṣ before s and dhv," g becomes gh. By the rule that ṣ and ḍh become k before s: ghuk. The forms are then derived by changing s into ṣ through the rule on substitutes and affixes, and so on: aghukṣat, aghukṣatām, aghukṣan, and so on.

On the side without iṭ, for the ātmanepada endings: lug vā duhadihalihaguhām ātmanepade dantye, "for duh, dih, lih and guh, before an ātmanepada ending beginning with a dental, there is optional elision." That is: for duha, "to milk," diha, "to accumulate," liha, "to taste," and guhū, "to conceal completely," the ksa that replaces the following cli is optionally elided before an ātmanepada ending that stands among the dentals or whose first letter arises from the dentals. On the side where ksa is not elided, in the first person singular: aghukṣata. On the side where ksa is elided: by the rule that h becomes ḍh, guḍh; t becomes dh by the rule beginning "not after dhā"; by the rule that a dental after a retroflex becomes retroflex, dh becomes ḍh; by the rule that ḍh is elided before ḍh, the former ḍh is deleted; and by "when ḍh or r is deleted," with the sūtra "the preceding aṇ becomes long," u is lengthened into ū. Deriving the form in this way: agūḍha.

Ksasyāci: "of ksa, before a vowel." The final of the ksa that replaces cli after lih and the rest is deleted before ātmanepada endings beginning with a vowel. In the first person dual and plural: aghukṣātām, aghukṣata. Yet the commentary explains that, although the ending begins with a vowel, in the plural the deletion of the final of ksa is in some cases not wanted, so there is also a form like aghukṣanta.

Treating them by these same procedures, in the three middle persons: agūḍhāḥ, aghukṣathāḥ, aghukṣāthām; and agh, where g is changed into gh by the rule "of a single-vowel root, a baś," and so on: aghūḍhvam, aghukṣadhvam. In the three last persons: aghukṣi, aghukṣāvahi, aghukṣāmahi.

With the parasmaipada endings of liṭ: jugūha, jugūhatuḥ, jugūhuḥ, jugūhitha, jugūḍha, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: jugūhāte, jugūhire, jughukṣe, and so on.

In luṭ, iṭ being made optional: gūhitā, gūhitārau, gūhitāraḥ, gūhitāsi, and so on, or gūḍhā, gūḍhārau, gūḍhāraḥ, gūḍhāsi, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings too: gūhitā, gūhitārau, gūhitāraḥ, gūhitāse, and so on, or gūḍhā, gūḍhārau, gūḍhāraḥ, gūḍhāse, and so on.

With the parasmaipada endings of the benedictive liṅ: guhyāt, guhyāstām, guhyāsuḥ, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings, iṭ being made optional by the rule on roots marked with ū and so on: gūhiṣīṣṭa, gūhiṣīyāstām, gūhiṣīran, and so on, or ghukṣīṣṭa, ghukṣīyāstām, ghukṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, iṭ being made optional, with the parasmaipada endings: gūhiṣyati, gūhiṣyataḥ, gūhiṣyanti, and so on, or ghukṣyati, ghukṣyataḥ, ghukṣyanti, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: gūhiṣyate, gūhiṣyete, gūhiṣyante, and so on, or ghukṣyate, ghukṣyete, ghukṣyante, and so on. Likewise, with the parasmaipada endings of lṛṅ: agūhiṣyat, agūhiṣyatām, agūhiṣyan, and so on, or aghukṣyat, aghukṣyatām, aghukṣyan, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings: agūhiṣyata, agūhiṣyetām, agūhiṣyanta, and so on, or aghukṣyata, aghukṣyetām, aghukṣyanta, and so on.

Hṛñ, "in the sense of taking away," also takes both voices, so both the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest come in. With the parasmaipada endings of laṭ: harati, and so on; with the ātmanepada endings: harate, and so on. Likewise with the parasmaipada endings of liṅ: haret, and so on; with the ātmanepada endings: hareta, and so on. With the parasmaipada endings of loṭ: haratu, and so on; with the ātmanepada endings: haratām, and so on. With the parasmaipada endings of laṅ: aharat, and so on; with the ātmanepada endings: aharata, and so on.

With the parasmaipada endings of luṅ, vṛddhi being made by the rule "before sic, vṛddhi, in the parasmaipada": ahārṣīt, ahārṣṭām, ahārṣuḥ. In the three middle persons: ahārṣīḥ, ahārṣṭam, ahārṣṭa. In the three last persons: ahārṣam, ahārṣva, ahārṣma.

Uś ca: "and after ṛ." This sets down the convention that, after a root ending in ṛ, the sic without iṭ that replaces cli, when followed by an ātmanepada ending, and also the ātmanepada endings of the benedictive liṅ, are designated as marked with k. The purpose is that vṛddhi and guṇa are not made. Applying the ātmanepada endings of luṅ to hṛñ, in the three first persons: ahṛta, ahṛṣātām, ahṛṣata. In the three middle persons: ahṛthāḥ, ahṛṣāthām, ahṛḍhvam. In the three last persons: ahṛṣi, ahṛṣvahi, ahṛṣmahi.

In liṭ, by "lacking an abhyāsa" and so on, and by "after a short stem," sic is lost before endings beginning with jhal. The root is stated twice; by the rule that ṛ becomes a, ṛ becomes a; by the rule that a velar and h of the abhyāsa become palatal, h becomes jh; and by the rule that in the abhyāsa a jhaś becomes car, jh is changed into j. Deriving the forms in this way, in the three first persons of the parasmaipada: jahāra, jahratuḥ, jahruḥ. In the three middle persons: jahartha, jahrathuḥ, jahra. In the three last persons: jahāra or jahara, jahriva, jahrima. Likewise, in the three first persons of the ātmanepada: jahre, jahrāte, jahrire. In the three middle persons: jahriṣe, jahrāthe, jahridhve, or with ḍh, jahriḍhve. In the three last persons: jahre, jahrivahe, jahrimahe.

In luṭ, guṇa being made by the rule for sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka affixes, with the parasmaipada endings: hartā, hartārau, hartāraḥ, hartāsi, and so on. Likewise with the ātmanepada endings: hartā, hartārau, hartāraḥ, hartāse, and so on.

With the parasmaipada endings of the benedictive liṅ, ṛ is changed into ri by the rule "riṅ before śa, yak, and the liṅs": hriyāt, hriyāstām, hriyāsuḥ, and so on. With the ātmanepada endings, by "and after ṛ," being marked with k, guṇa and the rest are not made: hṛṣīṣṭa, hṛṣīyāstām, hṛṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ and lṛṅ, iṭ is applied by the sūtra "after ṛ-final roots and han, before sya." With the parasmaipada endings of lṛṭ: hariṣyati, and so on; with the ātmanepada endings: hariṣyate, and so on. Likewise, with the parasmaipada endings of lṛṅ: ahariṣyat, and so on; with the ātmanepada endings: ahariṣyata, and so on.

Bhṛñ, "in the sense of filling," also takes both voices. So with the parasmaipada endings of laṭ: bharati, and so on; and with the ātmanepada endings: bharate, and so on. Likewise with the non-taṅ endings, that is, the parasmaipada, of liṅ: bharet, and so on; and with the taṅ endings, that is, the ātmanepada: bhareta, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: bharatu, and so on; with the taṅ endings: bharatām, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: abharat, and so on; with the taṅ endings: abharata, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of luṅ, vṛddhi being made by the sūtra "before sic, vṛddhi," and so on: abhārṣīt, abhārṣṭām, abhārṣuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings of luṅ, by "and after ṛ," being marked with k, guṇa is not made; and the forms are derived by the deletion of sic before endings beginning with jhal, by the sūtra "after a short stem," and so on: abhṛta, abhṛṣātām, abhṛṣata, and so on.

In liṭ, by "kṛ, sṛ, bhṛ," and so on, iṭ does not come in before endings beginning with val. In the three first persons of the non-taṅ endings: babhāra, babhratuḥ, babhruḥ. In the three middle persons: babhartha, babhrathuḥ. In the three last persons: babhāra or babhara, babhṛva, babhṛma. In the three first persons of the taṅ endings: babhre, babhrāte, babhrire. In the three middle persons: babhṛṣe, babhrāthe, babhṛḍhve. In the three last persons: babhre, babhṛvahe, babhṛmahe.

In luṭ, since the commentary explains that iṭ is optional, with the non-taṅ endings: bharitā, bharitāsi, and so on, or bhartā, bhartāsi, and so on. Likewise with the taṅ endings: bharitā, bharitāse, and so on, or bhartāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ, ṛ is changed into ri by "riṅ before śa, yak, and the liṅs": bhriyāt, and so on. With the taṅ endings, by "and after ṛ," being marked with k, guṇa and the rest are not made: bhṛṣīṣṭa, and so on.

In lṛṭ and lṛṅ, iṭ being added by "after ṛ-final roots and han, before sya": with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṭ, bhariṣyati, and so on; with the taṅ endings, bhariṣyate, and so on. Likewise with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ, abhariṣyat, and so on; with the taṅ endings, abhariṣyata, and so on.

Dāna, "in the sense of cutting down." By "mān, badh, dān," and so on, san is added; by the rule on san, the a of the abhyāsa becomes i, and by "mān, badh, dān," and so on, it is changed into ī. Deriving it in this way, dīdāṃsa is formed, and to it the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest are applied. Although the root itself takes both voices, it is explained that after a san-final stem the taṅ endings occur. In laṭ: dīdāṃsate, and so on. In liṅ: dīdāṃseta, and so on. In loṭ: dīdāṃsatām, and so on. In laṅ: adīdāṃsata, and so on. In luṅ, with the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val, and the a being deleted by the rule on the deletion of a: adīdāṃsiṣṭa, and so on. In liṭ, ām being applied by the rule beginning "kās": dīdāṃsāṃcakre, dīdāṃsāṃbabhūva, dīdāṃsāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ too, iṭ being added: dīdāṃsitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: dīdāṃsiṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: dīdāṃsiṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ: adīdāṃsiṣyata, and so on.

Śāna, "in the sense of sharpening": here too the forms are derived by applying san and so on, giving śīśāṃsate and the rest; every procedure is like what was just explained in the section on dāna.

Bhaja, "in the sense of serving," takes both voices, so both the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest come in. With the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: bhajati, and so on; with the taṅ endings: bhajate, and so on. Likewise with the non-taṅ endings of liṅ: bhajet, and so on; with the taṅ endings: bhajeta, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: bhajatu, and so on; with the taṅ endings: bhajatām, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: abhajat, and so on; with the taṅ endings: abhajata, and so on.

In luṅ, by the rule that a palatal becomes velar, j becomes g; by the rule that before khar a car is substituted, g becomes k; by "after jhal, before jhal," sic is lost before endings beginning with jhal; and for the others, s is changed into ṣ by the rule on substitutes and so on. Deriving the forms in this way, in the three first persons of the non-taṅ endings: abhākṣīt, abhāktām, abhākṣuḥ. In the three middle persons: abhākṣīḥ, abhāktam. In the three last persons: abhākṣam, abhākṣva, abhākṣma. Likewise in the three first persons of the taṅ endings: abhakta, abhakṣātām, abhakṣata. In the three middle persons: abhakthāḥ, abhakṣāthām, and abhagdhvam. In the three last persons: abhakṣi, abhakṣvahi, abhakṣmahi.

In liṭ, the root is stated twice; before affixes marked with k, by the rule "and of tṝ, phal, bhaj and trap," the deletion of the abhyāsa and the change into e are made. Deriving the forms in this way, in the three first persons of the non-taṅ endings: babhāja, bhejatuḥ, bhejuḥ. In the three middle persons: bhejitha or babhaktha, bhejathuḥ, bheja. In the three last persons: babhāja or babhaja, bhejiva, bhejima. In the three first persons of the taṅ endings: bheje, bhejāte, bhejire. In the three middle persons: bhejiṣe, bhejāthe, bhejidhve. In the three last persons: bheje, bhejivahe, bhejimahe.

In luṭ, by the rule that a palatal becomes velar, j becomes g, and by the rule that before khar a car is substituted, g is changed into k. Deriving the forms in this way, with the non-taṅ endings: bhaktā, bhaktāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: bhaktā, bhaktāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ: bhajyāt, bhajyāstām, bhajyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, by the rule that a palatal becomes velar, j becomes g; by the rule on car before khar, g becomes k; and by the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed into ṣ: bhakṣīṣṭa, bhakṣīyāstām, bhakṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, deriving the forms in accordance with the procedure just explained, with the non-taṅ endings: bhakṣyati, and so on; with the taṅ endings: bhakṣyate, and so on. Likewise with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: abhakṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: abhakṣyata, and so on.

Śriñ, "in the sense of serving," also takes both voices, so both the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest come in. With the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: śrayati, and so on; with the taṅ endings: śrayate, and so on. Likewise with the non-taṅ endings of liṅ: śrayet, and so on; with the taṅ endings: śrayeta, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: śrayatu, and so on; with the taṅ endings: śrayatām, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: aśrayat, and so on; with the taṅ endings: aśrayata, and so on.

In luṅ, by "after ṇi, śri, dru," and so on, cli is changed into caṅ. By the rule "before caṅ," the root is stated twice; by the rule that only the first consonant of the abhyāsa remains, r is deleted; and before a vowel, iy is substituted by the rule beginning "of śnu and roots," and so on. Deriving the forms in this way, with the non-taṅ endings: aśiśriyatām, aśiśriyan, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: aśiśriyata, aśiśriyetām, aśiśriyanta, and so on.

In liṭ, for the forms that are not causes of vṛddhi, the designation "marked with k" is made optional through the citation of the rule "after svañj and the rest, in a reduplicated form, liṭ is optionally marked with k." On the side where it is marked with k, iy is substituted; on the side where it is not, guṇa is made. In the three first persons of the non-taṅ endings: śiśrāya; śiśriyatuḥ or śiśrayatuḥ; śiśrayuḥ or śiśriyuḥ. In the three middle persons: śiśrayitha; śiśrayathuḥ or śiśriyathuḥ; śiśraya or śiśriya. In the three last persons: śiśrāya or śiśraya; śiśrayiva or śiśriyiva; śiśrayima or śiśriyima. Likewise with the taṅ endings too: śiśraye or śiśriye; śiśrayāte or śiśriyāte; and so on.

In luṭ, the iṭ due before an affix beginning with val being added, and guṇa being made by the rule on sārvadhātuka and the rest, with the non-taṅ endings: śrayitā, śrayitāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: śrayitā, śrayitāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ, lengthening being made by "not before a kṛt affix," and so on: śrīyāt, śrīyāstām, śrīyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, iṭ being added: śrayiṣīṣṭa, śrayiṣīyāstām, śrayiṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, iṭ being added and guṇa made, with the non-taṅ endings: śrayiṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: śrayiṣyate, and so on. Likewise with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: aśrayiṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: aśrayiṣyata, and so on.

Rañja, "in the sense of dyeing," also takes both voices, so both the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest come in. Rañjeś ca: "and of rañji." The n of rañja is also deleted before the śap that has the sense of the agent. With the n deleted, with the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: rajati, and so on; with the taṅ endings: rajate, and so on. Likewise with the non-taṅ endings of liṅ: rajet, and so on; with the taṅ endings: rajeta, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: rajatu, and so on; with the taṅ endings: rajatām, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: arajat, and so on; with the taṅ endings: arajata, and so on.

In luṅ, by the rule that a palatal becomes velar, j becomes g; by the rule that before khar a car is substituted, g becomes k; by the rule on substitutes and so on, s becomes ṣ; and before endings beginning with jhal, sic is deleted by "after jhal, before jhal," and so on. Deriving the forms in this way, with the non-taṅ endings vṛddhi is also made by "vada, vraja," and so on. In the three first persons: arāṅkṣīt, arāṅktām, arāṅkṣuḥ. In the three middle persons: arāṅkṣīḥ, arāṅktam, arāṅkta. In the three last persons: arāṅkṣam, arāṅkṣva, arāṅkṣma. Likewise with the taṅ endings: araṅkta, araṅkṣātām, araṅkṣata, and so on.

In liṭ, for the forms that are not causes of vṛddhi, the deletion of n is made optional by "svañj" and so on.
