In the three first persons of the non-taṅ endings: rarañja; rarañjatuḥ or rarajatuḥ; rarañjuḥ or rarajuḥ. In the three middle persons: rarañjitha or raraṅktha; rarañjathuḥ or rarajathuḥ; rarañja or raraja. In the three last persons: rarañja; rarañjiva or rarajiva; rarañjima or rarajima. Likewise in the three first persons of the taṅ endings: rarañje or raraje; rarañjāte or rarajāte; rarañjire or rarajire. In the three middle persons: rarañjiṣe or rarajiṣe; rarañjāthe or rarajāthe; rarañjidhve, or rarajidhve or rarajiḍhve. In the three last persons: rarañje or raraje; rarañjivahe or rarajivahe; rarañjimahe or rarajimahe.

In luṭ, the palatal being made velar and car being substituted before khar, with the non-taṅ endings: raṅktā, raṅktāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: raṅktā, raṅktāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ, the n being deleted by the rule on roots "not marked with i," and so on: rajyāt, rajyāstām, rajyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, by the rule that a palatal becomes velar, car before khar, and the rule on substitutes and so on: raṅkṣīṣṭa, raṅkṣīyāstām, raṅkṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, deriving the forms by the rule that a palatal becomes velar and so on, with the non-taṅ endings: raṅkṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: raṅkṣyate, and so on. Likewise with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: araṅkṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: araṅkṣyata, and so on.

Tviṣa, "in the sense of shining," also takes both voices, so both the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest come in. With the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: tveṣati, and so on; with the taṅ endings: tveṣate, and so on. Likewise in liṅ: tveṣet, and so on; with the taṅ endings: tveṣeta, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: tveṣatu, and so on; with the taṅ endings: tveṣatām, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: atveṣat, and so on; with the taṅ endings: atveṣata, and so on.

In luṅ, by "after a root ending in śal with a penultimate ik, and lacking iṭ, ksa," cli is changed into ksa; the k is deleted; by the rule that ṣ and ḍh become k before s, ṣ becomes k; and by the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed into ṣ. Deriving the forms in this way, with the non-taṅ endings: atvikṣat, atvikṣatām, atvikṣan, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: atvikṣata, atvikṣātām, atvikṣata, and so on.

In liṭ, for the forms that are not causes of vṛddhi, being marked with k is made optional through the citation of "svañj" and so on. With the non-taṅ endings: titveṣa; titveṣatuḥ or titviṣatuḥ; titveṣuḥ or titviṣuḥ. In the three middle persons: titveṣitha or titviṣitha, or titvekṣa; titveṣathuḥ or titviṣathuḥ; titveṣa or titviṣa. In the three last persons: titveṣa; titveṣiva or titviṣiva; titviṣima or titveṣima. In the three first persons of the taṅ endings: titveṣe or titviṣe; titveṣāte or titviṣāte; titveṣire or titviṣire. In the three middle persons: titveṣiṣe or titviṣiṣe; titveṣāthe or titviṣāthe; titveṣidhve or titviṣidhve. In the three last persons: titveṣe or titviṣe; titveṣivahe or titviṣivahe; titveṣimahe or titviṣimahe.

In luṭ, deriving the forms by guṇa according to the rule on pu-final and the rest, and by changing t into ṭ according to the rule that a dental after a retroflex becomes retroflex, and so on, with the non-taṅ endings: tveṣṭā, tveṣṭāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: tveṣṭā, tveṣṭāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ: tviṣyāt, tviṣyāstām, tviṣyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, by the rule that ṣ and ḍh become k before s, ṣ becomes k, and by the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed into ṣ: tvikṣīṣṭa, tvikṣīyāstām, tvikṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, ṣ being changed into k and so on, with the non-taṅ endings: tvekṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: tvekṣyate, and so on. Likewise with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: atvekṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: atvekṣyata, and so on.

Yaja, "in the senses of worshipping the gods, associating, and giving," also takes both voices, so both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings come in. With the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: yajati, and so on; with the taṅ endings: yajate, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of liṅ: yajet, and so on; with the taṅ endings: yajeta, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: yajata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: yajatāṃ, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: ayajata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: ayajata, and so on.

In luṅ, for the endings that begin with a jhal consonant, sic is dropped by the rule "after a jhal, before a jhal"; by praścabhrasja and so on, j becomes ṣ; and by "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," t is changed into ṭ, and so on. For the endings that do not begin with a jhal, by "before s, ṣ and ḍh take k," ṣ becomes k. These being formed by the rule of thorough change and so on, with the non-taṅ endings the three of the first person are ayākṣīta, ayāṣṭāḥ; the three of the middle person, ayākṣīḥ, ayāṣṭaṃ, ayāṣṭa; the three of the last person, ayākṣaṃ, ayākṣva, ayākṣma. With the taṅ endings, the three of the first person are ayaṣṭa, ayakṣātāṃ, ayakṣata. The lengthening comes by vadabhaja and so on. The three of the middle person are ayaṣṭhā, ayakṣāthāṃ, and, sic being dropped by the rule "after a jhal," ṣ becoming ḍ by "final jhals take jaś," and dh becoming ṭh by "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," ayaḍḍhaṃ. The three of the last person are ayakṣi, ayakṣahi.

liṭyabhyassyobhayeṣāṃ: "In liṭ, of the abhyāsa of both." That is, when liṭ follows, the reduplicative syllable (abhyāsa) of both groups, namely vac and the rest and grah and the rest, undergoes saṃprasāraṇa. Since yaj is one of the group of vac and the rest, in the singular of the first person of liṭ with the non-taṅ endings the form is iyāja.

vacisrapiyajādīnīkiti: "Of vac, svap, yaj and the rest, before a kit." That is, when an affix bearing the name in which k drops away follows vac, "to explain," and ñiṣvap, "to sleep," these two, and yaj and the rest, the letters of yaṇ undergo saṃprasāraṇa, in both if there is an abhyāsa, and even if there is no abhyāsa. So in the dual and plural of the first person of liṭ with the non-taṅ endings: ījatunaḥ, ījuḥ. The three of the middle person: iyajitha, iyaṣṭha, ījathu, ija. The three of the last person: iyāja, iyaja, ījiva, ījima. Likewise, with the taṅ endings, the three of the first person: īje, ījāte, ījire. The three of the middle person: ījiṣi, ījāthe, ījiṅhve, and ī, where by vraścabhrasja and so on j becomes ṣ, and by "ṣṭu with ṣṭu" th becomes ṭh, jiḍhve. The three of the last person: īje, ījivahe, ījimahe.

In luṭ, j becoming ṣ by vraścabhrasja and so on, and by "ṣṭu with ṣṭu" and so on, with the non-taṅ endings: yaṣṭā, yaṣṭāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: yaṣṭa, yaṣṭāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ, the change by saṃprasāraṇa through the rule "of vac, svap, yaj and the rest, before a kit" gives ijyāta, ijyāstāṃ, ijyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, j becoming ṣ by vraścabhrasja and so on, ṣ becoming k by "before s, ṣ and ḍh take k," and by the rule of thorough change and so on: yakṣīṣṭa, yakṣīyāstāṃ, yakṣīrana, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, the forms being produced by j being changed into ṣ and so on, with the non-taṅ endings: yakṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: yakṣyate, and so on. Likewise, with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: ayakṣata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: akṣyata, and so on.

ṭuvapa, "in the sense of sowing seed," also takes both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings. With the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: vapati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: papate, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of liṅ: vapeta, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vapeta, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: papatu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: papatāṃ, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: avapata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: avapata, and so on.

In luṅ, for the endings that begin with a jhal, sic being elided by "after a jhal, before a jhal," and so on, with the non-taṅ endings the three of the first person are avavsīta, apaptāṃ, avapsuḥ; the three of the middle person, avapsīḥ, avaptaṃ, avapta; the three of the last person, avapsaṃ, avapsā, apapsa. Likewise, with the taṅ endings, the three of the first person are avavta, avavsāthāṃ, apapsata; the three of the middle person, avapthāḥ, avapsāthaṃ, avastvaṃ; the three of the last person, avapsi, avapsvahi, avapsvahi.

In liṭ, for the endings that are not kit, the abhyāsa is changed by saṃprasāraṇa through "in liṭ, of the abhyāsa of both"; and for the kit endings, both are changed by saṃprasāraṇa through the sūtra "of vac, svap, yaj and the rest." Then sic being dropped by "after a jhal, before a jhal," p becoming b by "final jhals take jaś," and lengthening and so on being applied by "before a similar ak, long," with the non-taṅ endings the three of the first person are upāpa, ūpatuḥ, ūpuḥ; the three of the middle person, uvapitha, uvapva, ūpathuḥ, ūpa; the three of the last person, uvāpa, uvapa, ūpiva, ūpima. Likewise, with the taṅ endings: ūve, ūpāte, ūpire, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of luṭ: vaptā, vaptāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vaptā, paptāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ, saṃprasāraṇa being applied by "of vac, svap, yaj and the rest": upyāta, upyāstāṃ, upyāsuḥ, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vapsīṣṭa, vapsīyāshāṃ, vapsīrana, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, apart from introducing the s, there is no other operation. With the non-taṅ endings: vapsyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vapsyate, and so on. Likewise, with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: avavsyata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: avapsyata, and so on.

vaha, "in the sense of conveying," also takes both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings. With the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: vahati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vahati, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of liṅ: vaheta, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vaheta, and so on. With loṭ: vahatu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vahatāṃ, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: avahata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: avahata, and so on.

In luṅ, for the endings that do not begin with a jhal, h becomes ḍh by the rule "h takes ḍh." By "before s, ṣ and ḍh take k," ḍh becomes k. By the rule of thorough change and so on, s is changed into ṣ, and so on. For the endings that begin with a jhal, h becomes ḍh; by "after a jhal, before a jhal," sic is dropped; by "not after dhā" and so on, t and th become dh; by "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," dh becomes ḍh; by "ḍh is elided before ḍh," the former ḍh is dropped; and by "of sah and vah, the a becomes o," a is changed into o, and so on. Formed in this way, with the non-taṅ endings the three of the first person are alṭākṣīta, avoḍhāṃ, avoḍhaṃ, avākṣuḥ; the three of the middle person, avākṣīḥ, avoḍhaṃ, avoḍha; the three of the last person, avākṣaṃ, avākṣma, avākṣma. Likewise, with the taṅ endings, the three of the first person are avoḍha, avakṣātāṃ, avakṣata. The lengthening comes by varbhraja and so on. The three of the middle person are avoḍhāḥ, avakṣāthāṃ, avoḍhaṃ; the three of the last person, avakṣi, avakṣāhi, avakṣmahi.

In liṭ, for the endings that are not kit, the abhyāsa undergoes saṃprasāraṇa through the sūtra "in liṭ, of both" and so on; and for the kit endings, both undergo saṃprasāraṇa through "vac, svap, yaj and the rest," and so on. When this has been done, with the non-taṅ endings the three of the first person are uvāha, ūhatuḥ, ūhuḥ; the three of the middle person, uvahitha, uvoḍha with the ending thal, ūhathuḥ, ūha; the three of the last person, uvāha, uvaha, ūhiva, ūhima. Likewise, with the taṅ endings: ūhe, ūhāte, ūhire, and so on.

In luṭ, h becomes ḍh; by "not after dhā" and so on, t becomes dh; by "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," dh becomes ḍh; by "ḍh is elided before ḍh," the former ḍh is dropped; and by "of sah and vah" and so on, a is changed into o, and so on. Formed in this way, with the non-taṅ endings: voḍhā, voḍhāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: voḍhā, poḍhāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ, saṃprasāraṇa being applied by "vac, svap, yaj and the rest": uhyāta, uhyāsu, and so on. With the taṅ endings, h becoming ḍh by "h takes ḍh," ḍh becoming k by "before s, ṣ and ḍh take k," and s being changed into ṣ by the rule of thorough change and so on: vakṣīṣṭa, vakṣīyāstāṃ, vakṣārana, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, the forms being produced by h being changed into ḍh and so on, with the non-taṅ endings: vakṣyati, vakṣyataḥ, vakṣyanti, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vakṣyate, vakṣyeti, vakṣyante, and so on. Likewise, with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: avakṣyuta, avakṣyatāṃ, avakṣyana, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: avakṣyata, avakṣyetāṃ, avakṣyanta, and so on.

veña, "in the sense of weaving cloth," is also a root of both voices, so in laṭ and the rest both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings come in. With the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: payati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vāya, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of liṅ: vayeta, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vayeta, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: vayatu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vayatāṃ, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: avayata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: avayata, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of luṅ, ec becomes āt by "not before what bears ś as a dropped marker" and so on; and by "of yam, ram, nam and those ending in ā, also," iṭ and sak are added. So the three of the first person are avāsīṣṭāṃ, avāsiṣuḥ; the three of the middle person, avāsīḥ, avāsiṣṭa; the three of the last person, avāsiṣaṃ, avāsiṣā, avāsiṣma. With the taṅ endings, apart from bringing them in, there is no further operation: the three of the first person are avāsta, avāsātāṃ, avāsata; the three of the middle person, avāsthraḥ, avāsāthāṃ, avāsāṅhvaṃ; the three of the last person, avvasi, avāsvahi, avāsmahi.

In liṭ there are two alternatives: veñ remaining just as it is, and its being changed into vayi. In the alternative where veñ remains as it is: veñaḥ, "of veñ." Although by the earlier rule "in liṭ, of both" and so on, veñ is included in the group of vac and the rest, and before dh too sic is dropped, this is an exception to it: when liṭ follows, veñ does not undergo saṃprasāraṇa. So when liṭ is applied to veñ, with the non-taṅ endings the three of the first person are vavau, vavatuḥ, vavuḥ; the three of the middle person, vavitha, vavātha, vavathuḥ, vava; the three of the last person, vavau, vaviva, vavima. With the taṅ endings too, ā is dropped by "after iṭ also, ā is elided," so the three of the first person are vave, vavāte, vavīre. By "after ā, ṇal takes au," ṇal becomes au; and by "after iṭ also, ā is elided," ā is dropped. The three of the middle person are vaviṣe, vavāthe, vaviṅhe, vaviḍhe; the three of the last person, vave, vavivahe, vavimahe.

Then, in the other alternative: veñovayiḥ, "of veñ, vayi." That is, when liṭ follows, veñ optionally becomes vayi. In the singular of the first person of liṭ with the non-taṅ endings, veñ is changed into vayi, and its i, being there only for the sake of pronunciation, is dropped. By "not an abhyāsa" and so on, the root is doubled; and through the sūtra "in liṭ, of both" and so on, the abhyāsa undergoes saṃprasāraṇa, giving uvāya. In the dual, the root is doubled; through the sūtra "vac, svap, yaj and the rest," both v's are changed by saṃprasāraṇa; and by "before a similar ak, long," the vowel is lengthened, giving ūy with atus.

As to that: grahijyāvayivyadhivaṣṭivicatidṛścatipṛchatipṛjjatīnīditica, that is, "of grahijyāvayivyādhi, vaṣṭipicativṛścatipṛchatibhṛjyati, also before what bears ṅ as a dropped marker." Graha means "to take up"; jyā, "to lose one's youth"; vayi is veña, "the warp of threads"; vyadha, "to pierce"; vaśa, "to be beautiful," whose form is vaṣṭi; vicir, "to become separate"; vraścu, "to cut"; praccha, "to wish to know"; bhrajja, "to harm." The letters of these roots that are gathered under the abbreviation yaṇ undergo saṃprasāraṇa when affixes that bear the name in which k drops away, or that bear the name in which ṅ drops away, follow.

liṭibyoyaḥ: "In liṭ, the y of vay." Although by the sūtra just explained, "grahi, jyā, vayi" and so on, the y of vay would also be changed into i, this is an exception to it: when a kit ending of liṭ follows, the letter y of vay does not undergo saṃprasāraṇa. vaścāsyānyatarasyaṃkita: "Before a kit, its v too, optionally."

When a kit ending of liṭ follows, its y, that is, the letter y of vay, which was said not to undergo saṃprasāraṇa, optionally becomes the letter v. When y and v have thus been made optional, the forms are uyataḥ, ūvatuḥ; likewise in the plural, ūyuḥ, ūvuḥ. The three of the middle person: uvayitha, ūyathuḥ, ūvathuḥ, ūya, ūva. The three of the last person: uvāya, uvaya, ūyiva, ūviva, ūyima. With the taṅ endings likewise, the three of the first person: ūye, ūve, ūyāte, ūvāte, ūyire. The three of the middle person: ūviṣe, ūsṅathe, ūvāthe, ūyiḍhe, ūyeḍhe, ūvidhve, ūviḍhve. The three of the last person: ūye, ūve, ūyivahi, ūvivahi, ūyimahi, ūvimahi.

In luṭ, since there is no other operation apart from ec being changed into āt by "not before what bears ś as a dropped marker" and so on, with the non-taṅ endings: vātā, vātāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vātā, vātāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ, the root is changed by saṃprasāraṇa through "vac, svap" and so on, and lengthened by "not before a kṛt" and so on, giving ūyāta, ūyāstāṃ, ūyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings there is no other operation: vāsīṣṭa, vāsīyāsdī, vāsīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, ec being changed into āt, with the non-taṅ endings: vasyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vāsyate, and so on. Likewise, with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: apasyata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: avasyata, and so on.

vyeña, "in the sense of wrapping all around," is also a root of both voices. With the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: vyayati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vyayāte, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of liṅ: vyayeta, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vyayeta, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: vyayatu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vyayatāṃ, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: avyāsyata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: avyāsyata, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of luṅ, sak and iṭ being added by "of yam, ram, nam and those ending in ā, also," the forms are avyāsīta, avyāsiṣṭāṃ, avyāsiṣuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, the three of the first person: avyāsta, ahvasātāṃ, avyāsata; the three of the middle person: avyāsthā, avyāsāthāṃ, avyādhraṃ; the three of the last person: avyāsi, avyāsvahi, avyāsmahi.

navyoliṭi: "Not of vyā in liṭ." That is, when liṭ follows, the ec of vyeñ does not become āt. Liṭ is applied to vyeñ; through the sūtra "in liṭ, of both" and so on, the abhyāsa undergoes saṃprasāraṇa; by "of ac," with sic dropped, and by "before what bears ñ or ṇ as a dropped marker," vṛddhi is applied, giving vivyāya.

Quoted in the commentary: vyeñaḥkitiiṭisaṃvrasāraṇaṃvā, "Of vyeñ, before a kit of liṭ, saṃprasāraṇa optionally." That is, not only the abhyāsa of vyeñ: when a kit ending of liṭ follows, both are optionally changed by saṃprasāraṇa. In the alternative where only the abhyāsa undergoes saṃprasāraṇa, before endings that begin with an ac, ec becomes ay, av and so on; and in the alternative where both undergo saṃprasāraṇa, ik before an ac is made yaṇ. So in the dual and plural of the first person: pivyayatuḥ, vivyatuḥ, divyayuḥ, vivyuḥ. Likewise, the three of the middle person: vivyayitha, vivyayitha, vivyayathuḥ, vivyathuḥ, vivyaya, vivya. The three of the last person: vivyāya, vivyaya, vivyaya, vivyayiva, vivyiva, vivyayim, vivyima. Likewise with the taṅ endings too: vivyaye, vivye, vivyayāte, vivyāte, vivyayire, vivyire, and so on.

In luṭ, ec being changed into āt by "not before what bears ś as a dropped marker" and so on (by "of atti, arti and vyāyati, iṭ," iṭ is not made optional before thal), with the non-taṅ endings: vyātā, vyātāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vyātāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ, ec becoming āt by "not before what bears ś as a dropped marker" and so on, saṃprasāraṇa being applied by "vac, svap" and so on, and lengthening by "not before a kṛt" and so on, the forms are vīyāta, vīyvastāṃ, viyāsuḥ, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vyāsīṣṭa, vyāsīyāstāṃ, and so on.

In lṛṭ, ec being changed into āt, with the non-taṅ endings: vyāsyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: vyāsyate, and so on. Likewise, with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: avyāsyata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: avyāsyata, and so on.

hvauña, "in the sense of rivalry, and also of sound," is also a root of both voices. With the non-taṅ endings of laṭ: hvayati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: hvayate, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of liṅ: hvayata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: hvayeta, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of loṭ: hvayatu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: hvayatāṃ, and so on. With the non-taṅ endings of laṅ: ahvayata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: ahvayata, and so on.

livisicihvaśca: "From livi, sici and hvā too." That is, from liva, "to smear," ṣica, "to drip," and hvā, "to rival," too, cli becomes aṅ. Cli being changed into aṅ, and a being dropped by "after iṭ also, ā is elided," with the non-taṅ endings: ahvatāṃ, ahvana, and so on.

With the taṅ endings it is optional: ātmanepadeṣvanyatarasyāṃ, "Before the ātmanepada endings, optionally." That is, from liva, ṣica and hvā, when ātmanepada endings follow, cli is optionally changed into aṅ or into sic. In the alternative where cli is changed into aṅ, ā being dropped, the three of the first person are ahvata, ahvetāṃ, ahvanta; the three of the middle person, ahvathāḥ, ahvethāṃ, ahvadhāṃ; the three of the last person, ahve, ahvāvahi, ahvāmahi. In the alternative where cli is changed into sic, ec is only changed into āt: āhvasta, ahvasātāṃ, ahvasata, and so on.

abhyastasyaca: "Of the reduplicated stem too." That is, when liṭ follows, the reduplicated stem (abhyasta) of hva undergoes saṃprasāraṇa. Liṭ is applied to hvā, and the abhyasta, that is, both parts, undergoes saṃprasāraṇa. For the endings that are not kit, vṛddhi and guṇa are applied; and for the kit endings, uv is applied by "before an ac, of śnu, a root" and so on. So with the non-taṅ endings the three of the first person are juhāva, juhuvatuḥ, juhuvuḥ; the three of the middle person, juhavitha, juhotha, juhuvathuḥ, juhuva; the three of the last person, juhāva, juhava, juhuviva, juhuvima. Likewise with the taṅ endings too: juhuve, juhuvāte, juhuvire.

In luṭ, ec being changed into āt by "not before what bears ś as a dropped marker" and so on, with the non-taṅ endings: hvātā, hvātāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: hvātā, hvātāse, and so on.

With the non-taṅ endings of the benedictive liṅ, moreover, by "optionally, of a root beginning with a conjunct," e is optionally changed into āt or left unchanged, giving hvāyāta, hvāyāṃstāṃ, hvāyāsuḥ, and so on; or heyāta, hveyāstāṃ, hveyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, ec being changed into āt: hvāsīyāstāṃ, hvāsirana, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, ec being changed into āt, with the non-taṅ endings: hvāsyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: hvāsyata, and so on. Likewise, with the non-taṅ endings of lṛṅ: atvāsyata, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: ahvāsyata, and so on.

vas, "in the sense of dwelling," is a parasmaipada root, so in laṭ and the rest the non-taṅ endings come in. In laṭ: vasti, and so on. In liṅ: vaseta, and so on. In loṭ: vastu, and so on. In laṅ: avasha, and so on.

sasyārṅhadhātuke: "Of s, before an ārdhadhātuka." That is, when an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with the letter s follows, the s of vas is to be changed into the letter t. So when luṅ is applied to vas, the three of the first person are avātsīta, avādtāṃ, avātsuḥ; the three of the middle person, avātsīḥ, avāttaṃ, avātta; the three of the last person, avātsaṃ, avādsā, avādsma.

śāsivasighasīnāṃca: "Of śāsi, vasi and ghasi too." That is, of śāsu, "to instruct," vas, "to dwell," and ghasḷ, "to eat" (vṛddhi coming by vaṅthra and so on, and sic being dropped by "after a jhal, before a jhal"), the letter s becomes the letter ṣ after the letters of the abbreviation iṇ and after the letter k. Liṭ is added to vas. For the endings that are not kit, the abhyāsa is changed by saṃprasāraṇa through "in liṭ, of both" and so on; for the kit endings, both undergo saṃprasāraṇa through "vac, svap" and so on; and by this sūtra s is changed into ṣ. So the three of the first person are uvāsa, ūṣatuḥ, ūṣuḥ; the three of the middle person, uvasitha, avastha, ūṣathuḥ, ūṣa; the three of the last person, uvāsa, uvas, ūṣiva, ūṣam.

In luṭ: vastā, vastarau, vastarau, vastaraḥ, vastāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, saṃprasāraṇa being applied through "vac, svap" and so on, and s being changed into ṣ through "of śāsi, vasi, ghasi" and so on: uṣyāta, uṣyāstāṃ, ūṣyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, s being changed into t through "of s, before an ārdhadhātuka": vatsyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: avatsyata, and so on.

Vad, "in the sense of speaking clearly," also takes the parasmaipada endings. In laṭ: vadti, and so on; in liṅ: vadata, and so on; in loṭ: vadtu, and so on; in laṅ: avadata, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ being added by "before what begins with val" and vṛddhi by vadabhraja and so on: avādīta, avādiṣṭāṃ, avādiṣaḥ, and so on. In liṭ, for the endings that are not kit, the abhyāsa undergoes saṃprasāraṇa through "in liṭ, of both" and so on; and for the kit endings both are changed by saṃprasāraṇa through "vac, svap" and so on. So the three of the first person are uvād, ūdatuḥ; the three of the middle person, uvaditha, ūdathunaḥ, ūda; the three of the last person, uvāda, avada, ūdīva, ūdima. In luṭ, iṭ being applied by "before what begins with val": vaditā, vaditārau, vaditāraḥ, vaditāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: udyāta, udyāstāṃ, udyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ being added: vadiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: adiṣyata, and so on.

ṭuośvi, "in the senses of going and of growing," is also a parasmaipada root, so in laṭ and the rest the non-taṅ endings come in. In laṭ: śvayati, and so on (saṃprasāraṇa being applied through "vac, svap" and so on). In liṅ: śvayatu, and so on. In loṭ: śvayatu, and so on. In laṅ: aśāyata, and so on.

In luṅ there are three ways of forming it. By jvṝstambmu, mrucu, mluci and so on, cli is optionally changed either into aṅ or into sic. In the aṅ alternative: śvayiteraḥ, "the a of śvayati." That is, when aṅ, substituted for cli, follows, the letter i of śvayati becomes the letter a; and by "a, from at, before guṇa," the two together take the form of the one that follows: aśvata, aśvatāṃ, aśvana, and so on. In the alternative where cli is changed into sic, iṭ being added by "before what begins with val": aśvayīta, aśvayiṣḍā, aśvayiṣuḥ, and so on. And by "optionally, of dheṭ and śvi," cli is changed into caṅ; by "before caṅ," the root is doubled; and by "the first hal remains" and "before an ac, of śnu, a root" and so on, it is changed into uv, giving aśiśviyata, aśiśviyataṃ, aśiśviyana, and so on.

vibhāṣāśeḥ: "Optionally, of śvi." That is, when liṭ follows, the saṃprasāraṇa of śvi is optional, either applied or not. In the alternative where it is applied, the three of the first person are śuśāva, śuśuvatuḥ, śuśuvuḥ; the three of the middle person, śuśavatha, śuśuvathuḥ, śuśuva; the three of the last person, śuśāva, śuśuviva, śuśuvima. In the alternative where it is not applied, the three of the first person are śiśvāya, śiśviyatuḥ, and śiśviyuḥ. (By this sūtra the v together with the vowel is changed into u, and then the root is doubled; for the endings that are not kit, guṇa and vṛddhi apply in the ordinary way, and for the kit endings, uv comes by "before an ac, of śnu" and so on.) The three of the middle person: śiśvayatha, śiśviyathuḥ, śiśviya. The last person: śiśāya, śiśvaya, śiśviyiv, śiśviyim.

In lṛṭ, iṭ being added by "before what begins with val": śvayitā, śvayitāsī, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, saṃprasāraṇa being applied through "vac, svap" and so on, and lengthening through "not before a kṛt" and so on: śūyāta, śūyāstāṃ, śūyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ being added by "before what begins with val": śvayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aśvayiṣyata, and so on.

itipāṇinivyākaraṇasūtraddhrādayassamāvta: that is, "Thus, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, bhū and the rest are complete."

With these, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, notes setting down the meaning, the procedures, the illustrative examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the coarse outline, general rules together with their exceptions, is for the moment complete: of the roots of the bhū class and the rest, in which śap comes in for the agent, the way of applying the parasmaipada endings to roots having the voice "for another," which take the parasmaipada; the way of applying the ātmanepada endings to roots having the voice "for oneself," which take the ātmanepada; and the way of applying both the parasmaipada and the ātmanepada endings to roots having both voices, and so on.

Now I shall present the verbs of the ad class and the rest, in which the śap that comes in for the agent is lost. adiprabhṛtibhyaḥśpaḥ: "From ad and the rest, of śap."

For the root ad, "in the sense of eating," and for adi and the rest, formed by applying the affix i that names a root in its own form, the śap that comes in for the agent is lost.

Laṭ and the other non-taṅ endings are applied to ad. By "śap for the agent," śap is given, and by this sūtra śap is dropped. So the three of the first person of laṭ are attaḥ, adanti; the three of the middle person, atsi, atthaḥ, attha; the three of the last person, admi, advaḥ, atmaḥ. The three of the first person of liṅ are adyāda, adyātāṃ, adyūnaḥ; the three of the middle person, adyāḥ, adyātāṃ, adyāta; the three of the last person, adyāṃ, adyāva (by "before khar, car," d becomes t), adyāma. The three of the first person of loṭ are attu, attāta, attāṃ, adandu.

For the singular of the middle person: hujhavhyo (by "before us, of what is not word-final," the two together take the single form of the one that follows) heṭdhiḥ, "From hu and the jhals, dhi for hi." That is, after hu, "to give," and after roots ending in the letters of the abbreviation jhal, the following hi becomes dhi: addhi. In the dual and plural: attaṃ, atta. The three of the last person: adāni, adāva, adāma.

adaḥsarveṣāṃ: "After ad, according to all." That is, after ad, according to all, to an apṛkta ending consisting of a single hal (to ad, laṭ and śap are applied, and śap is dropped by "ad and the rest"; by "of si, hi, and it does not bear p as a dropped marker," si is changed into hi, and by this sūtra hi is brought in; to that which bears that name; by "of mi in loṭ, ni," and by "for the last person, āṭ, and it bears p as a dropped marker," āṭ is given; vas and mas are changed, and by "like laṅ" and so on the s is dropped; by "for the last person, āṭ, and it bears p as a dropped marker," āṭ is brought in) the augment aṭ is given: all the ancient sages hold this. In the singular of the first person of laṅ: ādatā, with āṭ. In the dual and plural of the first person: āttāṃ, ādana. Likewise, the three of the middle person: adaḥ, āttāṃ, ātta. The three of the last person: ādaṃ, ādā, ātma.

luṅsanorghasḷ: "Before luṅ and san, ghasḷ." That is, when luṅ and san follow, ad is to be changed into ghasḷ. The ḷ is there to mark it as having ḷ as a dropped marker. So: aghasata, aghasatāṃ, aghas, and so on.

liḍyanyatarasyāṃ: "In liṭ, optionally." That is, when liṭ follows, ad optionally becomes ghasḷ. In the alternative where ad is changed into ghasḷ, the root is doubled; by "of ku and h, cu," gh becomes jh, and by "of the abhyāsa, car too," jh becomes j. For the kit endings (by "puṣ and the rest, dyut and the rest, and those with ḷ as a dropped marker," cli is changed into aṅ), the penultimate is dropped by "of gam, han, jan, khan and ghas" and so on; by "before khar, car," gh becomes k; and by "of śāsi, vasi and ghasi too," s is changed into ṣ, and so on. So the three of the first person are jaghāsa, jakṣatuḥ, jakṣuḥ; the three of the middle person, jaghasitha, jakṣathuḥ, jakṣa; the three of the last person, jaghāsa, jaghas, jakṣiva, jakṣima. In the alternative where it is not changed into ghasḷ, the three of the first person are āda, ādatuḥ, āduḥ; the three of the middle person, āditha, ādathuḥ, āda; the three of the last person, ād, ādipa, ādima.

In luṭ, d being made t by "before khar, car": attā, attārau, attāraḥ, attādi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: adyāta, adyāstāṃ, adyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, d being changed into t by "before khar, car": adsyati, adsyataḥ, adsyanti, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ātsyata, ātsyatāṃ, ādsyana, and so on.

psā, "in the sense of eating," is also a parasmaipada root, so in laṭ and the rest the non-taṅ endings come in, and by "from ad and the rest, of śap," śap is lost. The three of the first person of laṭ are psāyāṃ, psāni; the three of the middle person, bsāsi, psāthaḥ, psātha; the three of the last person, psāmi, psāvaḥ, psāmaḥ. The three of the first person of liṅ are psāyāta, psāyātāṃ, psāyuḥ; the three of the middle person, psāyāḥ, psāyātaṃ, psāyāta; the three of the last person, psāyāṃ, psāyava, psāyāma. The three of the first person of loṭ are psātu, psātāta, psātāṃ, psāntu; the three of the middle person, psāhi, psātāta, psātaṃ, psāta; the three of the last person, psāni, psāva, psāma. In the singular and dual of the first person of laṅ: absāta, absāta, apsātāṃ.

laṅśākaṭāyenasyava: "Of laṅ, necessarily, according to Śākaṭāyana." That is, after a root ending in ā, the jhi substituted for laṅ becomes jus; it is explained that according to the view of the ancient sage Śākaṭāyana it necessarily does so. For psā, laṅ is changed into jhi, and it being made optional whether it is changed into jus, according to Śākaṭāyana's view, or into ant, the forms are apsuḥ, apmana. The three of the middle person: apsāḥ, apsātaṃ, apsāta. The three of the last person: apsāṃ, apsāva, apsāma.

In luṅ, the augment sak and iṭ being added by "of yam, ram, nam and those ending in ā, also," the three of the first person are apsāsīta, apsāsiṣṭāṃ, apsāsaṃṣi; the three of the middle person, apsāsīḥ, absāsiṣṭaṃ; the three of the last person, apsāsiṣaṃ, apsāsiṣva, apsāsiṣma. The three of the first person of liṭ are papsau, papsatuḥ, bablaḥ; the three of the middle person, papsitha, papsātha, papsathuḥ, papsa; the three of the last person, papsau, papsiva, papsima. In luṭ: psātā, psātārau, psātāra, psātāsi, and so on.

In the benedictive liṅ (otherwise: by "after ā, au for ṇal," ṇal is changed into au, and by "after iṭ also, ā is elided," ā is dropped), by "optionally, of a root beginning with a conjunct," ā is optionally changed into e or left unchanged, giving psāyāta, psāyāstāṃ, psāyāḥ, and so on; or pseyāta, speyāstaṃ, speyāsu, and so on. In lṛṭ: spāsyati, spāsyataḥ, spāsyanti, and so on; and in lṛṅ: aspāsyata, aspāsyatāṃ, aspāsyana, and so on.

"Vaśa: in the sense of loveliness." For this root too the endings apply and śap is elided. Before the kit endings, saṃprasāraṇa takes place by the rule beginning "grahi," and ś is changed into ṣ by the rule beginning "vraśca bhrasja." Thus, in the three of the first person of laṭ, ś becomes ṣ by "vraśca" and so on, and t becomes ṭ by "ṣṭu": vaṣṭi, uṣṭaḥ, uśanti. In the three of the middle person: vakṣi. Here ś becomes ṣ by "vraśa" and so on; by "before s, ṣ and ḍh become k," ṣ becomes k; and by "substitution" and so on, s becomes ṣ: uṣbaḥ, udṭha. In the three of the last person: vaśmi, uśāḥ.

Saṃprasāraṇa having been made by "grahi jyā" and so on: uśyāta, uśyatāṃ, uśyatāṃ, uśyuḥ. By "vraśca" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; by "ṣṭu," t becomes ṭ; and by "grahi" and so on, prasāraṇa: it is thus changed. In the three of the middle person: uśyāḥ. By "vraśca" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; by "ṣṭu" and so on, th becomes ṭh; and saṃprasāraṇa having been made by "grahi" and so on: uśyātaṃ, uśyāta. In the three of the last person: uśyāṃ, uśyāva, aśyāma.

In loṭ too, before the kit endings, saṃprasāraṇa takes place by "grahi jyā" and so on; before endings beginning with jhal, ś becomes ṣ by "vraśca bhrasja" and so on; and ṣṭu is formed by "ṣṭu" and so on. Thus, in the three of the first person: vaṣṭu, uṣṭāta, uṣṭaṃ, uśanśa. In the three of the middle person: uḍhi, uṣḍāta, uṣṭa. In the three of the last person: vaśāni, vaśāva, vaśāma.

In the singular of the first person of laṅ: vaśal laṅ, la ti. By "of it also," i is elided; by "hal ṅyāp" and so on, t is elided: vaśa la hi. By "grahi" and so on, saṃprasāraṇa; by "vraśca" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; by "hu jhal" and so on, hi becomes dhi; by "ṣṭu," dh becomes ḍh; by "final jhal" and so on, ṣ becomes ḍ. By "vraśca" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; by "of final jhal, jaś," ṣ becomes ḍ; and by "optionally at a pause": avaṭ, avaṭ. In the dual and plural: auṣṭāṃ, auśana. Likewise, in the three of the middle person: avaḍa, avaṭa, auṣṭaṃ, auṣṭa. In the three of the last person: avaśaṃ, auśva, auśma.

In luṅ: by "of a light vowel in a root beginning with hal" and so on, vṛddhi is optional, and with iṭ added: avāśīt. By "grahi" and so on, saṃprasāraṇa; by "āṭ for those beginning with ac," āṭ is added to the root; and by "after āṭ also," vṛddhi: avāśiṣṭaṃ, vāśiṣaḥ, and so on; or else agāśit and so on.

In liṭ, before the endings that are not kit, the reduplicated syllable is formed by "two" and so on, with saṃprasāraṇa; and before the kit endings both are changed to saṃprasāraṇa by "graha" and so on. Formed further by "ak, before a like vowel, becomes long" and so on: in the three of the first person, uvāśa, ūśatuḥ. In the three of the middle person: uvaśitha, ūśathuḥ, ūśa. In the three of the last person: uvāśa, uvaśa, ūśiva, ūśima. In luṭ: vaśitā, vaśitārau, vaśitāraḥ, vaśitāraḥ, vaśitāraḥ, vaśitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, saṃprasāraṇa having been made by "graha jyā" and so on: uśyāta, uśyāstā, uśyasuḥ, uśyāḥ, uśyāstaṃ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ having been given by "for endings beginning with val": vaśiṣyati, vaśiṣyataḥ, vaśiṣyanti, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: apaśiṣyata, āvaśiṣyatāṃ, alaśiṣana, and so on.

"Hana: in the sense of harming and of going." For this root too, in laṭ and the rest, the parasmaipada endings apply and śap is elided. In the singular of the first person of laṭ: hante. Anudāthopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopa jhali kditi: "Of roots taught as anudātta, of vanoti, and of tanoti and the rest, the nasal is elided before a jhal ending marked with k or ṅ." The roots taught as anudātta are: yamu, in the sense of cessation; ramu, playing; nama, bowing down; gamḷ, going; hana, killing; and manu, knowing. Vanoti is vanu, harming. Tanoti and the rest are: tanu, extending; kṣaṇu, harming; ṛṇu, going; ghṛṇu, blazing; vanu, begging; and manu, understanding. Of these, the nasal letters are to be elided when there follows a suffix whose first letter belongs to the group jhal and which is named as marked with k or ṅ. So when the dual of the first person is added to hana: hataḥ. In the plural, the penultimate is elided by "gama hana jana" and so on, and by "the h of hanti before ñit, ṇit and n," h is changed into gh: ghānti. In the three of the middle person: hanṣi, hathaḥ, haza. In the three of the last person: hanyi, hanvaḥ, hanmaḥ. Vamorvā: optionally before v and m. When an upasarga that is a conditioning cause for n becoming ṇ precedes, the letter n of hana optionally becomes ṇ when v or m follows: prahanmi, prahaṇmi, prahanaḥ, prahaṇvaḥ, and so on.

In the three of the first person of liṅ: hanyāta, hanyātāṃ, hanyāḥ. In the three of the middle person: hanyāḥ, hanyāte, hanyāta. In the three of the last person: hanyāṃ, hanyāva, hanyāma. When an upasarga that is a conditioning cause precedes, making the sense "to harm intensely," then by "of hanti, preceded by a," n becomes ṇ: prahaṇyata, and so on.

In loṭ, before the kit endings, the nasal is elided by "taught as anudātta" and so on, and before endings beginning with ac, the penultimate is elided by "gama hana" and so on. Formed in this way, in the three of the first person: hantu, hatvāta, hatāṃ, ghnantu. In the singular of the middle person: hantirjaḥ, "of hanti, ja." By "of si, hi, and it is not pit," the si in loṭ is changed into hi, and when this hi follows, hanti is to be changed into ja: jahi, hahatāta. Asiṅdhavadatrāśrayi: here, where there is a common basis, the earlier operation counts as not accomplished. In this jahi, which stands on a common basis, the elision of hi by "after a, of hi" is not effected, because of the defining condition, the letter n, in the earlier form hana. In the dual and plural: hataṃ, hata. In the three of the last person, āṭ having been given by "āṭ for the last, and it is pit": hanāni, hanāpa, hanāma.

In laṅ, the endings consisting of a single consonant are elided by "hal ṅyāp" and so on; before kit endings beginning with jhal, n is elided by "anudātta" and so on; and before endings beginning with ac, the penultimate is elided by "gama hana" and so on. When this is done, in the three of the first person: ahana, ahatāṃ, aghnana. In the three of the middle person: ahani, ahaha. In the three of the last person: ahanaṃ, ahanva.

Luṅi ca: "also in luṅ." When luṅ follows, hana is to be changed into what is called vaṅdhan, vaṅdha. Hana with luṅ: by this sūtra hana is changed into vadha; iṭ is added by "for endings beginning with val"; and by "elision of a," a is elided: avadhīta, avadhiṣu, and so on.

In liṭ the root is said to be doubled. By "of ku and h, c," h becomes jh; by "of the reduplicated syllable, cara also," jh becomes j. Before ṇal, by "the h of hanti before ñit, ṇit and n," h becomes gh, and by "of the penultimate also," vṛddhi. Before the kit endings, the penultimate is elided by "gama hana" and so on, so that afterwards a is elided; and since from the beginning it is not hal-final, vṛddhi by "pada" and so on is not made here. Ṅdhā is elided. When h has been changed into gh by "the h of hanti" and so on, and the rest has been done: ghāna, jaghnatuḥ, jaghūḥ. In the singular of the middle person: abhyāsācca, "after the reduplicated syllable also." After the reduplicated syllable too, the following h is changed into gh: jaghanitha, jaghantha. In the dual and plural: jaghnathuḥ, jaghna. In the three of the last person: jagnana, jagnana, jagniva, jaghima. In luṭ: hantā, hantārau, hantāḥ, handāḥ, hantasi, and so on.

Hanovaṅdhalidi: "in liṅ, vaṅḍa for han." When the benedictive liṅ follows, han is to be changed into what is called vaṅdha. Han with the benedictive liṅ: by this sūtra it is changed into vaṅdha, and a being elided by "elision of a": vaṅdhyāta, saṅdhtāstaṃ, paṅdhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ having been given by "of ṛ-final roots and han, before sya": haniṣyati, haniṣyataḥ, haniṣyanti, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ahaniṣyata, ataniṣyana, and so on.

"Dyu: in the sense of approaching." For this the endings apply, and śap too is elided by "ad" and so on. Uto vṛṅdhir luki havi: "when there is elision, before hal, vṛddhi of u." When an intervening suffix is elided, as in the elision of śap, then before a following suffix that begins with hal and is named as marked with p, u undergoes vṛddhi. So when laṭ is added to dyu, in the singular of the first person: dyauti. In the dual and plural: dyutaḥ, dyuvanti. In the three of the middle person: dyauṣa, dyuthaḥ. In the three of the last person: dyaumi, dyovaḥ, dyumavaḥ. In liṅ there is no further operation: dyuyāta, dyuyāstaṃ, dyuyāḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, vṛddhi takes place before tip and before endings beginning with hal; and before endings beginning with ac, u is changed into uv by "before ac, of śnu and of a root" and so on. When this is done, in the three of the first person: dyautu, dyautāta, dyutāṃ, dyuvantu. In the three of the middle person: dyuhi, dyutāta, dyutaṃ, dyuta. In the three of the last person: dyavāni, dyavāva, dyavāma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of laṅ: adyauta, adyutāṃ, adyuvana. In the three of the middle person: adyauḥ, adyutaṃ, adyuta. In the three of the last person: adyavaṃ, with guṇa; adyuva, adyuma.

In luṅ: "vṛddhi before sic"; after āṭ has been given, guṇa is made. Vṛddhi having been made by "before the parasmaipada endings," in the three of the first person: adyauṣīda, adyauṣḍāṃ, adyauṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: adyauṣīḥ, adyauṣṭāṃ, adyauṣṭa. In the three of the last person: adyauṣaṃ, adyauṣma.

In liṭ, before the endings other than ṇal, both of them, and thal, kit is optionally made by the citation of "svañja, after a conjunct, first" and so on. In the kit alternative, uv is made by "before ac, of śnu and of a root," and in the alternative that is not kit, guṇa is made. Thus, in the three of the first person: dudyāva, durgyuvatuḥ, dudyavatuḥ, dudyuvuḥ, dudyavuḥ. In the three of the middle person: dudyotha, dudyavitha, dudyuvathuḥ, dudyavthuḥ, dudyuva, dudyava. In the three of the last person: dudyāva, dudyava, dudyuviva, dudyaviva, dudyuvima, dudyavima. In luṭ, guṇa having been made by "before sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka endings" and so on: hyotā, dyotārau, dyotāraḥ, dyotāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, lengthening having been made by "not before a kṛt suffix" and so on: dyūyāta, dyūyāstāṃ, dyuyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, guṇa having been made by "before sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka endings" and so on, and s made into ṣ by "substitution" and so on: dyoṣyati, dyoṣyahaḥ, dyoṣyahaḥ, dyoṣyanti, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: adyoṣyata, adyoṣyatāṃ, adyoṣyanas, and so on.

"Yu: in the sense of mixing." For this too the endings apply, and the whole procedure is like the one just explained. In the three of the first person of laṭ: yauti, yutaḥ, yuṅanti. In the three of the middle person: yauṣi, yuthaḥ, yutha. In the three of the last person: yaumi, yuvaḥ, yumaḥ. In liṅ: yuyāta, yuyātāṃ, yuyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: yotu, yutāta, yutāṃ, yuvantu. In the three of the middle person: yuhi, yutāta, yutaṃ, yuta. In the three of the last person: yavāni, yavāva, yavāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: ayota, ayutāṃ, ayuvana. In the three of the middle person: ayauḥ, ayutaṃ, ayuta. In the three of the last person: ayavaṃ, ayuva, ayuma. In luṅ, with iṭ added for endings beginning with val: ayāvīta, ayāvyaṣḍāṃ, ayīviṣuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: yuyāva, yuyuvatuḥ, yuyuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: yuyavitha, yuyuvaśuḥ, yuyuva. In the three of the last person: yuyāva, yulava, yuyuvib, yu; "vṛddhi before sic"; yuvima. In luṭ, with iṭ added for endings beginning with val: yavitā, yavitārau, yavitāraḥ, yavitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, lengthening having been made by "not before a kṛt suffix" and so on: yūyāta, yūyāstāṃ, yuyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, with iṭ given: yaviṣyati and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ayaviṣyata and so on.

"Ṇu: in the sense of praising." The endings are applied to it, and the procedure is like that of yu. In the three of the first person of laṭ: nauti, nutaḥ, nuvanti. In the three of the middle person: nauṣi, nuthaḥ, nutha. In the three of the last person: naumi, numaḥ. In liṅ: nuyātāṃ, nuyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: nautu, nutāta, nivantu. In the three of the middle person: nuhi, nutāta, nutaṃ, nuta. In the three of the last person: navāni, navāva, navāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: anauta, anutāṃ, anuvana. In the three of the middle person: anoḥ, anutaṃ, anuta. In the three of the last person: anuvaṃ, anuva, anuma. In luṅ, with iṭ for endings beginning with val, and vṛddhi made by "vṛddhi before sic, in the parasmaipada endings": anāvīta, anāviṣṭāṃ, anāviṣuḥ, and so on. Or else, since the commentary explains that after nu, iṭ optionally does not occur before endings beginning with val, then in the alternative without iṭ, vṛddhi having been made: anauṣīta, anauṣṭāṃ, anauṣṭāṃ, anauṣuḥ, and so on.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: nunāva, nunuvatuḥ, nunuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: nunuvathuḥ, nunuva. In the three of the last person: nuṭāb, nunaviṅ, nunuvima. In luṭ: navitā and so on, or notā and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, lengthening having been made: nūyāta, nūyāstaṃ, nuyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ having been made optional: napiṣyati and so on, or noṣyadati and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: anaviṣyata and so on, or anoṣyada and so on.

"Kṣu: in the sense of sharpening." This too is like yu. When the endings have been applied, in the three of the first person of laṭ: kṣṇauti, kṣṇutaḥ, kṣṇupanti. In the three of the middle person: kṣṇauṣi, kṣnuthaḥ, kṣṇutha. In the three of the last person: kṣṇaumi, kṣṇuvaḥ, kṣṇamaḥ. In liṅ: kṣṇuyāta, kṣṇuyātāṃ, kṣṇuyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: kṣṇautu, kṣṇatāta, kṣṇutāṃ, kṣṇuvaṭtu. In the three of the middle person: kṣṇuhi, kṣṇutāṃta, kṣṇutaṃ, kṣṇuta. In the three of the last person: kṣṇavāni, kṣṇavāva, kṣṇavāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: akṣnauta, akṣnutāṃ, akṣṇuvana. In the three of the middle person: akṣṇauḥ, akṣṇutaṃ, akṣuta. In the three of the last person: akṣṇavaṃ, akṣnuva, akṣuma. In luṅ, iṭ for endings beginning with val having been added and vṛddhi made: akṣṇāvīta, akṣṇuviṣṭe, akṣapaṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ the root is doubled. By "of the first, the remaining hal," kh and ṇ are elided; by "of ku and h, cu"; and leaving aside ṇal, both of them, and thal, the others are made optionally kit. Thus, in the three of the first person: cukṣāva, cukṣnavatuḥ, cukṣṇuvutuḥ, cukṣnuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cukṣṇavitha, cukṣṇavathuḥ, cukṣṇavathuḥ, cukṣṇathu, cukṣṇava. In the three of the last person: cukṣṇava, cakṣṇava, cukṣṇaviva, cukṣṇuviva, cukṣṇavima, cukṣṇuvima. In luṭ, iṭ having been given: kṣṇavitā, kṣṇavitārau, kṣṇavitāraḥ, kṣṇavitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, lengthening having been made by "not before a kṛt suffix" and so on: kṣṇuyāta, kṣṇuyāstaṃ, kṣṇuyāta, kṣṇuyāstāṃ, kṣṇuyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, with iṭ added for endings beginning with val: kṣṇaviṣyati and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: akṣṇaviṣyata and so on.

"Ṣṇu: in the sense of flowing forth." Since this root too takes the parasmaipada endings, the endings apply and śap is elided. By "of the initial of a root, ṣ becomes s," ṣ becomes s; and by "when the cause is absent, what it causes is also absent," ṇ too reverts to n. When laṭ and the rest are applied to what is now snu, the procedure is like the one just explained. In the three of the first person of laṭ: snauti, snuti, sduvasti. In the three of the middle person: snauṣi, snuthaḥ, snutha. In the three of the last person: snaumi, snuvaḥ, snumaḥ. In liṅ: snuyāta, snuyātāṃ, snuluḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: snotu, snutāta, snutāṃ, snuvanhu. In the three of the middle person: snuhi, snutāta, snutaṃ, snuta. In the three of the last person: snavāni, snavāva, snavāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: asnauta, asnutāṃ, asnuvana. In the three of the middle person: asnauḥ, asnutaṃ, asnuta. In the three of the last person: asnapaṃ, asnuva, asnuma. In luṅ, iṭ for endings beginning with val and vṛddhi having been made: asnāpīta, asnūviṣḍdaṃ, asnāviṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, leaving aside ṇal, both of them, and thal, the other case endings are made optionally kit by "svañja, after a conjunct, first" and so on. Thus, in the three of the first person: sukṣuva, sukṣuvatuḥ, sukṣuvatuḥ, sukṣnuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: suṣṇavitha, suṣṇavavruḥ, suṣṇāvathuḥ, suṣṇava, suṣṇuva. In the three of the last person: suṣṇuviva, suṣṇavama, suṣṭaviva, suṣṭuviva, suṣṇuvima, suṣṭavima. In luṭ, iṭ having been given: snavitā, snavitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, lengthening having been made by "not before a kṛt suffix" and so on: snaṃuyāta, snūyāstāṃ, snālāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ having been given: snaviṣyati and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ too, iṭ having been given: asnaviṣyata and so on.

"Iṇa: in the sense of going." For this too the endings apply, and śap is elided by "ad" and so on. Since the root has the indicatory letter ṇ, guṇa and so on having been made before endings marked with p, in the singular and dual of the first person of laṭ: eti, itaḥ. Iṇo yaṇa: "of iṇ, yaṇ." Before a suffix that is not marked with p and begins with ac, iṇ becomes a letter of the group yaṇ. So in the plural of the first person: yanti. In the three of the middle person: eṣi, ithiḥ, itha. In the three of the last person: emi, ivaḥ, imaḥ. In liṅ: iyāta, iyātāṃ, iyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: etu, itāta, itāṃ, yantu. In the three of the middle person: ihi, itāta, ita. In the three of the last person, in the three of the last person: ayāni, ayāpa, ayāma. In laṅ, āṭ having been added to the root by "āṭ for those beginning with ac," and vṛddhi made by "after āṭ also": in the three of the first person, aita, aitāṃ, āyana. In the three of the middle person: aiḥ, aitaṃ, aita. In the three of the last person: āyaṃ, aiva, aima.

Iṇogāṅi: "in luṅ, kā for iṇ." When luṅ follows, iṇ is to be changed into what is called gā. Iṇ with luṅ: vṛddhi having been made with ā, giving what is called ai; then la, la, ḍbhaṃ; jha becomes anta; by "of it also," i is elided; by "elision of the final of a conjunct," t is elided; sandhi is made by "of ec, ay, av" and so on; and by this sūtra it is changed into gā. Since sic is elided by "gāti, sthā, ghu, pā, bhū" and so on: agāta, agātāṃ, aguḥ. In the three of the middle person: agāḥ, agātaṃ, agāta. In the three of the last person: agī, agāva, agāma.

In the singular of the first person of liṭ, the root is doubled by "iṇ, in liṭ, without the reduplicated syllable" and so on. La becomes tip, and hip becomes ṇal. Vṛddhi is made by "of ac, before what is marked with ñ and ṇ," and by "of ec, al, av" and so on, i becomes āy. By "of the reduplicated syllable, before what is not homogeneous," the earlier i is supplied in order with iyaṅ and the marker ṅ: iyāya. Dīrghaiṇaḥkiti: "before what is marked with k, iṇ is long."

That is, before liṭ endings named as marked with k, the reduplicated syllable of iṇ becomes long. In the dual and plural of the first person, i is doubled; by this sūtra the reduplicated syllable is long; and by "of iṇ, yaṇ," the latter i is drawn into y: īyatuḥ, īyāḥ. Formed in the same way as these, in the three of the middle person: iyayitha, iyetha, īyathuḥ, īya. In the three of the last person: iyāya, iyaya, iyiva, iyima. In luṭ, guṇa having been made by "before sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka endings" and so on: etā, etārau, etāraḥ, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, lengthening is made by "not before a kṛt suffix" and so on: īyāta, īyāstāṃ, īyāsuḥ, and so on.

Eterliṅi: "of eti, in liṅ." When an upasarga is joined before it, iṇ becomes short before the benedictive liṅ. Anu is placed before the established form īyāta; by this sūtra it is short; and yaṇ having been made by "of ik, before ac": anviyāta and so on. In lṛṭ, guṇa having been made: eṣyati, eṣyataḥ, eṣyantaṃ, and so on. Lṛṅ too is like that, except that āṭ is given by "āṭ for those beginning with ac," and vṛddhi is made by "after āṭ also": iṣyata, aiṣyatāṃ, aiṣyana, and so on.

"Ika: in the sense of remembering." For this too the endings apply. The commentary quotes: iṇādika iti ca vaktavyamiti ṇatkaryarūpaṃ ca. "Ik too should be stated as like iṇ: its operation is like iṇ, and so is its form." This ik is to be stated as like iṇ: all the operations in the method of forming iti and the rest are alike, all the sūtras of the iṇ section apply, and all the finished forms too are like those of iṇ. Since one is therefore to extend this by analogy to all ten groups beginning with laṭ, the method of formation, the finished forms and so on have not been set out separately as examples.

"Mā: in the sense of honoring." For this too the endings apply, and since śap is elided by "ad" and so on, in the three of the first person of laṭ: māti, mātaḥ, māṇti. In the three of the middle person: māsi, māthaḥ, mātha. In the three of the last person: māmi, māvaḥ, māmaḥ. In liṅ: māyāta, māyātāṃ, māyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: mātu, mātāta, māṃtāṃ, māntu. In the three of the middle person: māhi, mātāta, mātaṃ, māta. In the three of the last person: māni, māva, māma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: amātāṃ, amuḥ, amāna. In the three of the middle person: amāḥ, amātaṃ, amāta. In the three of the last person: amāṃ, amāva, amāma. In luṅ, sak and iṭ having been given by "yama, rama, nama" and so on: amāsīta, amāsiṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, by the rule read as "śākaṭālaṇasaṅsava," jhi becomes jus. In the three of the first person: mamau, mamatuḥ, mamuḥ. In the three of the middle person: mamitha, mamathuḥ, mama. In the three of the last person: mamau, mamipa, mamema. In luṭ: mātā, mātāro, mātāraḥ, mātāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, ā having been changed into e by "in liṅ, e": meyāta, meyāstāṃ, meyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: māsyati and so on; and in lṛṅ: amāsyata and so on.

"Yā: in the sense of attaining." For this too the endings apply, and since the procedure is for the most part like that of mā, in the three of the first person of laṭ: yāti, yātaḥ, yānti. In the three of the middle person: yāsi, yāthaḥ, yātha. In the three of the last person: yāma, yāvaḥ, yāmaḥ. In liṅ: yāyāta, yāyāstaṃ, yāyāḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: yātu, yātāta, yātāṃ, yāntu. In the three of the middle person: yāhi, latāta, yātaṃ, yāta. In the three of the last person: yāni, yāva, yāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: ayāta, ayātāṃ, ayuḥ, ayāna. In the three of the middle person: ayāḥ, ayātaṃ, ayāta. In the three of the last person: ayāṃ, ayāva, ayāma. In luṅ, sak and iṭ having been given by "yama, rama, nama" and so on: ayāsvyita, ayāsiṣṭāṃ, ayāsiṣuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: yayau, yayatuḥ, yayuḥ. In the three of the middle person: yayitha, yayathuḥ, yaya. In the three of the last person: yayau, yayiva, yayima. In luṭ: yātā, yātārau, yātāraḥ, yātāsī, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, since here it does not change into e: yāyāta, yāyāstāṃ, yāyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: yāsyati and so on; and in lṛṅ: asāsyata and so on.

"Vā: in the sense of going and of smelling," and "drā: in the sense of being despised": the whole procedure of both of these too is like that of yā.

"Khyā: in the sense of telling." This too is for the most part like those just explained. In laṭ: khyāti, khyātaḥ, khyānti, and so on. In liṅ: khyāyāta, khyāyāstāṃ, khyāyuḥ, and so on. In loṭ: khyātu, khyātāta, khyātāṃ, khyāntu, drāva. In the benedictive liṅ, moreover, by "conjunct" and so on, the change into e and its absence are made optional. And so on. In laṅ: akhyāta, akhyātāṃ, akhyāḥ, akhyāna, and so on.

Asyativaktikhyātibhyoñaṅ: "from asyati, vakti and khyāti, aṅ." From asu, increasing, vaca, speaking, and khyā, telling, cli is changed into aṅ. Khyā with luṅ: cli is given by "in luṅ, cli"; by this sūtra cli becomes aṅ; and ā having been elided by "of ā, elision, also before iṭ": akhyata, akhyatāṃ, akhyana, and so on.

In liṭ the root is doubled. By "of the first, the remaining hal"; by "of ku and h, cu," kh becomes ch; and by "of the reduplicated syllable, car also," ch is changed into c, and so on. When this is done, in the three of the first person: cakhyau, cakhyatuḥ, cakvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cakhyitha, cakhyathuḥ, cakhya. In the three of the last person: cakhyau, cakhyiva, cakhyima. In luṭ: khyātārau, khyātāraḥ, khyātāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, the change into e and its absence having been made optional by "moreover, after a conjunct, first" and so on: khyeyāta, khyeyāstāṃ, khyeyāsuḥ, and so on; or khyāyāta, khyāyāstāṃ, khyāyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: khyāsyati and so on. In lṛṅ: akhyāsyata and so on.

"Vida: in the sense of knowing." The parasmaipada endings apply to it. Vidoliṭovā: "after vid, optionally, of laṭ."

That is, after vida, the endings tip and the rest that replace laṭ optionally become ṇal and the rest, in order. Vid with laṭ; śap is elided; and in the alternative where tip and the rest are changed by this sūtra into ṇal and the rest, in the three of the first person: veda, vidtuḥ, viduḥ. In the three of the middle person: vatvra, vadithura, vida. In the three of the last person: veda, pidva, vidma. In the alternative where they are not changed into ṇal and the rest, in the three of the first person: vatti, vattaḥ, viranti. In the three of the middle person: vetsi, vitthaḥ, vittha. In the three of the last person: vedmi, vidraḥ, vidmaḥ. In liṅ, since there is no further operation: vidyāta, vidyātāṃ, vidyāḥ, and so on.

Vidāṃkurvantityanyatarasyā: "vidāṃ kurvantu, optionally." Before loṭ, ām is optionally joined to vit, loṭ is elided, and kṛñ with the loṭ suffix is joined after it; this being treated as a particle, we get vidāṃ karotu and so on. Vidāṃ is preceded by ḍukṛñ, "doing." In loṭ, the indicatory letters are removed, la becomes tip, and by "of e, u," i is changed into u, giving vidī kṛtuva. For this: tanādibhya uḥ, "from tan and the rest, u." From tanu, extending, and the rest, before a sārvadhātuka ending, in the domain of śap with the sense of the agent, u comes in. When u has been joined and guṇa made by "before sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka endings" and so on, vidāṃ karotu is formed. Atautsārvvaṅdhātuke: "of a, ut, before a sārvadhātuka ending." The a of kṛñ ending in u becomes ut before a sārvadhātuka ending named as marked with k or ṅ. In the dual and plural of the first person of loṭ: vidāṃ kurutāṃ, vidāṃ kurvantu. Likewise in the three of the middle person: vidāṃ kuru, vidāṃ kurutāta, pidāṃ kurutāta, vidāṃ kurutaṃ, vidāṃ kuruta. In the three of the last person: pidāṃ karavāṇi, vidāṃ karavāva, vidāṃ karavāma.

In the alternative where ām is not joined, guṇa is made for vit by "ending in puk" and so on, and since śap is elided, in the three of the first person: vettāta, vittāṃ, vi. By "after the suffix ut, also, when not a conjunct" and so on, hi is elided. Dantu. In the three of the middle person: viddhi, vittāta, vittaṃ, vitta. In the three of the last person: vedāni, vedāva, vedāma.

In the singular and dual of the first person, when laṅ is applied to phid: abde, aveta, avitāṃ. The commentary quotes: vetterlaṅojhosva, "after veti, jus for the jhi of laṅ, optionally." After vit, hi is changed into dhi by "after hu and jhal, hi becomes dhi," and the following jhi that replaces laṅ optionally becomes jus: aviduḥ, avidan. In the singular of the middle person: daśca, "of d also." The root-final d without a vowel, when the following sip has been elided, optionally becomes ru; the u is for pronunciation. Aveḥ, aveta, aved. In the dual and plural of the middle person: avittaṃ, avitta. In the three of the last person: avedaṃ, avidva, avitma. In luṅ, iṭ having been given and guṇa made: avedīta, avediṣṭaṃ, avediṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, ām is optionally joined by "uṣa, vid, jāgṛ" and so on: vidāṃ babhūva, vidāṃ cakāra, vidāmāsa, and so on. Or else liṭ itself is joined, and when it is formed by doubling the root and so on, in the three of the first person: vived, vividtuḥ, vividuḥ. In the three of the middle person: viveditha, viviṅathuḥ, vivid. In the three of the last person: vived, vividiva, vividima. In luṭ, iṭ having been given and guṇa made: veditā, veditārau, theditāraḥ, veditāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: vidyāta, vidyāstāṃ, vidyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ having been given and guṇa made: vediṣyati and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: avediṣyata and so on.

"Asa: in the sense of existing." The parasmaipada endings are applied to this too. In the singular of the first person of laṭ: asti. Śnāsorallopaḥ: "of śna and as, a is elided." The letter a of the suffix śna and of as is elided before a sārvadhātuka ending named as marked with k or ṅ. In the dual and plural of the first person of laṭ: staḥ, santi. In the three of the middle person: asi, s being elided by "of tā and asti, elision"; sthaḥ, stha. In the three of the last person: asmi, svaḥ. For as with laṭ, śap is elided; la is changed into vas and mas; a is elided by "of śna and as, a is elided"; and s is supplied: smaḥ.

In liṅ, a being elided by "of śna and as, a is elided," and s supplied with yā: in the three of the first person, syāta, syātāṃ, syāḥ. In the three of the middle person: syāḥ, syātaṃ, syāta. In the three of the last person: syāṃ, syāva, syāma. Likewise in loṭ too, formed by the elision of a before what is marked with k or ṅ and so on, in the three of the first person: asnustāta, stāṃ, santū.

Ghvasoreddhāvabhyāsalepaśca: "of ghu and as, e before hi, and elision of the reduplicated syllable also." Before the hi that replaces loṭ, roots named ghu and as are changed into e, and by "ghu" and so on the reduplicated syllable is also elided. As with loṭ: śap is elided; la becomes sip; by "si, hi," si is changed into hi; by this sūtra as is changed into e; and by "after hu and jhal, hi becomes dhi," hi becomes dhi. Since the earlier asa has a jhal letter, by the sūtra "here, where the basis is common, it is as if accomplished," although the basis is now common, the earlier letter s is the cause: edhi. Or else hi is changed into tātaṅ by "of tu and hi": stāta. In the dual and plural of the middle person: staṃ, sta. In the three of the last person: asāni, asāma.

In laṅ, before the endings consisting of a single consonant, īṭ is added by "asti, sic" and so on, and a is elided before what is marked with k or ṅ, and so on. When this is done, in the three of the first person: āsīta, āstī, āsan. Likewise in the three of the middle person: āsīḥ, āstaṃ, āsta. In the three of the last person: āsaṃ, āsva, āsma.

Astenhviḥ: "of asti, bhū." When case endings named ārdhadhātuka follow, as is to be changed into what is called bhū. Although the a of as is elided, by "from a common basis it is not accomplished," āṭ is given on account of the earlier ā. As with luṅ: by this sūtra it is changed into bhū, and sic is elided by "gāti" and so on. Since the commentary explains that from bhū changed into aha and as changed into bhū, īṭ does not occur before an ending consisting of a single consonant, īṭ is not given. In the three of the first person: abhūta, abhūtāṃ, abhūvana, and so on. All the operations and forms are like those in the section on bhū, "existing."

Although it is an ārdhadhātuka, before liṭ as does not become bhū. In the three of the first person: āsi, āsatuḥ. In the three of the middle person: āstha, āsathuḥ, āsa. In the three of the last person: āsa, āsiva, āsima. For luṭ, the benedictive liṅ, lṛṭ and lṛṅ, as is changed into bhū, so all the operations and forms are like those in the section on bhū, "existing," without the slightest difference.

upasargha prādurgyām astir yacbaranaḥ: "From a prefix and from prādur, [the s] of asti, when y or a vowel follows." From a preceding prefix that contains the cause for changing s into ṣ, and from prādur, which belongs to the class of indeclinables, the letter s of as is changed into ṣ when a suffix beginning with y or with a vowel follows: niṣanti, niṣyāta, prāduḥṣanti, prāduḥṣyāta. When the suffix does not begin with a vowel or with y, it does not change: nistaḥ, prādustaḥ, and so on.

For the root "mṛjūṣ, in purifying," too, the operations of the ad class apply. mṛjer bṛddhiḥ: "The vṛddhi of mṛji." Before suffixes beginning with a vowel or with y that are not kṅit, and before all sārvadhātuka endings and ārdhadhātukas, the ik of mṛji undergoes vṛddhi. In the singular of the first person of laṭ: vṛddhi by this sūtra; j into ṣ by vraśca bhralja and so on; and t changed into ṭ by "ṣṭu with ṣṭu": mānṣṭi. In the dual: since vṛddhi is not made before a kṅit, by vraśca and so on and by ṣaḍra and so on: mṛṣṭaḥ. Quoted in the commentary: kdityaci mṛjo praṅdharba, "before a kṅit beginning with a vowel, the vṛddhi of mṛj is optional." Even before one having k or ṅ as its marker, if it begins with a vowel, the vṛddhi of mṛj is made optionally. In the plural: mājanta, mṛjanti. Formed in the same way as these, in the three of the middle person: mārkṣi, mṛṣṭhaḥ, mṛṣṣa. In the three of the last person: mātdmi, mṛjvaḥ, mṛjmaḥ. For liṅ, since there is no further operation: mṛjyāta, mṛjyātāṃ, mṛjyuḥ, and so on.

For loṭ, formed as in the section on laṭ, in the three of the first person: vṛddhi; j into ṣ before s by vraśca and so on; ṣ into k by "of ṣ and ḍh"; s into ṣ by the rule on substitutes and so on: mānṣṭāḥ, mṛrkṣi, mārjantu, mṛjantu. In the three of the middle person: mṛṭṣa. As for the j: in loṭ, sip is changed into hi; by hujhal, hi becomes thi; j into ṣ by vraśca and so on; ṣ into ḍ by "final jhal" and so on; dh into ḍh by ṣṭu and so on: mṛṣṭaṃ, mṛṣṭa. In the three of the last person: mārjani, mārjāva, mārjāma.

In the three of the first person of laṅ: amārḍā, amārḍā, amṛṣṭāṃ, āmārjana, amṛjana. In the three of the middle person: amārḍā, amārḍa, amṛṣṭa, amṛṣṭa. In the three of the last person: amārjaṃ, amṛjva, amṛjma.

For luṅ, iṭ is made optional by ūdit and so on. In the alternative where iṭ is given, vṛddhi is made by "the vṛddhi of mṛji": amārjīta, amārjiṣṭā, amārjiṣuḥ, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ, by ṛta ubadhā it is made optional whether the āgama am is given or not given. Before endings beginning with jhal, sic is elided by "from jhal." Formed by vraśca and so on, which changes j into ṣ, by "ṣṭu with ṣṭu" and so on, and by "before s, of ṣ and ḍh" and so on: in the alternative where am is given, in the three of the first person: amrākṣīta, amṭaṣṭāṃ, amrākṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: amrākṣiḥ, amṛṣṭa, amrīṣṭu. In the three of the last person: amākṣaṃ, amrākṣā, amrākṣma. In the alternative where the āgama am is not given, in the three of the first person: amākṣīta, amārṣṭaṃ; the long vowel comes from the vṛddhi of mṛj, and the long vowel by vadzāja and so on: amārgṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: amārkṣāḥ, amāṇṭa, amārṣṭa. In the three of the last person: amārkṣaṃ, amārkṣva, amārkṣma.

For liṭ, vṛddhi is optional before vowel-initial suffixes that are kṅit, and vṛddhi is made before both ṇal endings and before thal. So in the three of the first person: mamārja, mamārjatuḥ, mamṛjatuḥ, mamṛjatuḥ, mamārjuḥ. In the three of the middle person: mamārjitha, mamārṣṭva, mamāthuḥ, mamṛjathuḥ, mamārja, mamṛja. In the three of the last person: mamārji, mamārjiva, mamṛjiva, mamārjima, mamṛjima, mamṛjima.

For luṭ, iṭ is made optional by ūdit and so on. So in the alternative with iṭ: mārjitā, mārjitāsi, and so on; and in the alternative without iṭ: mārṣṭa, mārṣṭāsi, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ: mṛjyāta, mṛjyāstaṃ, mṛjyāsuḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ, too, iṭ is made optional. So in the alternative where iṭ is given: marjiṣyati and so on; and in the alternative without iṭ: j into ṣ by vraśca and so on; ṣ into k by "before s, of ṣ and ḍh"; s into ṣ by the rule on substitutes and so on; and with vṛddhi made: mārṣyate and so on. Likewise for lṛṅ: amarjiṣyata and so on, or else amarkṣyata and so on.

For the root "vaca, in speaking," too, the operations of the ad class apply. The commentary explains that sārvadhātuka endings that are not pit, following vac and svap, are also not kṅit; the purpose of this is that saṃprasāraṇa is not made. The commentary further explains that for vac the first-person plural ending of laṭ, anti, does not occur. In the singular and dual of the first person of laṭ, c is changed into k by "the ku of cu": vakti, vaktaḥ. Likewise in the three of the middle person: vakṣi, vakthaḥ, vaktha. In the three of the last person: vacmi, vacvaḥ, vacmaḥ. For liṅ: vacyātāṃ, vacyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: vaktu, vaktāt, vaktaṃ, vacantu. In the three of the middle person: vakdhi, vaktāt, vaktaṃ, vakta. In the three of the last person: vacāni, vacāva, vacāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: avaka, avaga, avaktṝ, avacana. In the three of the middle person: avaka, avaka, avaktaṃ, avakta. In the three of the last person, where by hujhal hi becomes dhi and by "final jhal" and so on k becomes g: avaci, avacva, avacma. For luṅ, by "aṅ from asyati, vakti and khyāti," cli is changed into aṅ: avacra. To what is called atra applies vaca um: "the um of vac."

Before the aṅ that has replaced the cli of vac, the āgama um is given; the m is for the sake of its position. By "from a, guṇa," and by sandhi: avocat. Likewise in the dual and plural: avocana. In the three of the middle person: avocaḥ, avocataṃ, avocata. In the three of the last person: avocaṃ, avocāva, avocāma.

For liṭ, by "of the two ṇal and the two thal" and so on, there is saṃprasāraṇa of the reduplicated syllable; and before those that are kṅit, both are changed into saṃprasāraṇa by vaci svapi yaja and so on. Formed by "lengthening before a like vowel" and so on, in the three of the first person: uvāca, ūcatuḥ, ūcuḥ. In the three of the middle person: uvacitha, uvaktha, ūcathuḥ, ūca. In the three of the last person: uvāca, uvaca, ūciva, ūcima. For luṭ: vaktārau, vaktāraḥ, vaktāsi, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ, saṃprasāraṇa is made by vaci srapi and so on: ucyāta, ucyāstāṃ, ūcyāsuḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ, c into k by "the ku of cu," and s changed into ṣ by the rule on substitutes and so on: vakṣyati and so on. Likewise for lṛṅ: apakṣyata and so on.

For the root "rudira, in shedding tears," too, the parasmaipada endings apply. rudādibhya ssārbadhātuki: "From rud and the rest, before a sārvadhātuka, before val." Rud and the rest are: rudir, shedding tears; ṣvap, sleeping; śvas and an, breathing; and jakṣ, eating and laughing. From these, before a following sārvadhātuka beginning with a letter of the pratyāhāra val, the āgama iṭ occurs. In the singular and dual of the first person of laṭ: roditi, ruditaḥ. In the plural: ruṅnti. Likewise in the three of the middle person: rodeṣi, rudithaḥ, ruditha. In the three of the last person: rodimi, rudithaḥ, rudithaḥ. In the three of the last person: rodimi, rudivaḥ, rudimaḥ. For liṅ: rudyāta, rudyāta, rudyātāṃ, rudyāḥ, and so on. For loṭ, since iṭ is given by "rud and the rest" and so on: roditu, ruditāta, ruditāṃ, rudṇtu. In the three of the middle person: rudihi, ruditāta, ruditaṃ, ruditaṃ. In the three of the last person: rotāni, rodāva, rodāma.

rudaśca pañcabhyaḥ: "And from the five beginning with rud." After rud and the rest, before a suffix consisting of a single consonant, called apṛkta, the āgama īṭ occurs. ardrārgyagālabayoḥ: "aṭ, in the view of Gārgya and Gālava." After the five beginning with rud, before a sārvadhātuka consisting of a single consonant, called apṛkta, aṭ is given: the ancient sages Gārgya and Gālava made īṭ and aṭ optional in the singular of the first person, so: arodīta, arodata. In the dual and plural: aruditāṃ, arudan. Formed in the same way as these, in the three of the middle person: arodaḥ, arodīḥ, aruditaṃ, arudita. In the three of the last person: arodaṃ, arudiva, arurim.

For luṅ, by irit it is optional: the cli is optionally changed into aṅ or into sic. So in the aṅ alternative: arudata, arudatāṃ, arudana, and so on; and in the sic alternative, with iṭ before what begins with val, and with guṇa made by "puk, final" and so on: arodita, arodaṣṭu, arodiṣuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: ruroda, rurudatuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ruroditha, rurudithuḥ, ruruda. In the three of the last person: ruroda, rurudima. For luṭ, since iṭ is given before what begins with val: roditā, roditārau, roditāraḥ, roditrasaṃ, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ: rudata and so on. For lṛṭ, since iṭ is given: rodiṣyati and so on. Likewise for lṛṅ: arodiṣyada and so on.

For the root "ñiṣvapa, in sleeping," too, applying the operations of the ad class, in the three of the first person of laṭ: svapiti, svapitaḥ, svabanti. In the three of the middle person: svapiṣi, svapithaḥ, svabitha. In the three of the last person: svapimi, svabimaḥ, svabimaḥ. For liṅ: sapyāta, svabyātāṃ, svabyāḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: svapitu, svapitāṃ, svabantu. In the three of the middle person: svapihi, svapitī, svapita. In the three of the last person: svapāni, svabāva, svabāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: asvapīta, asvabata, asvabitāṃ, asvabana. In the three of the middle person: asvapīḥ, asvabaḥ, asvapataṃ, asvabita. In the three of the last person: asvapaṃ, asvapipa, asvapima.

For luṅ, before endings beginning with jhal, sic is elided by "from jhal, before jhal," and so on. So in the three of the first person: asvāpsīta, asvāptāṃ, asvāpsruḥ. In the three of the middle person: asvāpsīḥ, asvāptaṃ, asvābha. In the three of the last person: asvāpsaṃ, apsāpsā, asvāsbma.

Joining liṭ to svapi, the root is pronounced twice; by "of the two ṇal and the two thal" and so on there is saṃprasāraṇa of the reduplicated syllable; vṛddhi by vad bhraja and so on; and before those that are kṅit, both undergo saṃprasāraṇa by vaci svapi and so on. So in the three of the first person: suṣvapa, suṣupatuḥ, suṣubuḥ. In the three of the middle person: suṣvapitha, suṣvabtha, suṣupathuḥ, suṣupa. In the three of the last person: suṣapa, suṣvāpa, suṣupiva, suṣupima.

subinirdurbhyaḥ svapisūtismāḥ: "From su, vi, nir and dur, of svapi, sūti and sama." From the prefixes su, vi, ni and dur, the letter s of svapi, sleeping, of sūti, namely ṣūṅ, giving birth to living beings, and of sama, equal, becomes the letter ṣ: suṣuṣvāpa, niṣuthvāba, durṣuṣḍāpa, and so on.

For luṭ: svaptā, svaptārau, sbaptāraḥ, sāptāsi, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ, saṃprasāraṇa is made by vaci svapi and so on: supyāta, subyāstāṃ, subyāsuḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ: svapsyati and so on; and, with the prefixes, sleeping well, sleeping variously, sleeping soundly, sleeping badly. For lṛṅ: asvapsyata and so on.

For the root "śvasa and the rest," too, the operations of the ad class apply. Before sārvadhātuka endings beginning with val, iṭ is given by "ruṅ and the rest" and so on. In the three of the first person of laṭ: śvasiti, śvasitaḥ, śvasanti. In the three of the middle person: śvasiṣi, śvasithaḥ, śvasitha. In the three of the last person: śvasimi, śvasavaḥ, śvasimaḥ. For liṅ: śvasyāta, śvasyātāṃ, śvasyāta, śvasyātāṃ, śvasuḥ, and so on.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: śvasitu, śvasitāta, śvasitāṃ, śvasantu. In the three of the middle person: śvasiti, śvasitāta, śvasitaṃ, śvasita. In the three of the last person: śvasāni, śvasābi, śvasāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: aśvasīta, aśvasata, aśvasaṃtāṃ, aśvasana. In the three of the middle person: aśvasīḥ, aśvasata, aśvasitaṃ, aśvasita. In the three of the last person: aśvasaṃ, aśvasiva, aśvasima.

For luṅ, vṛddhi is not made, by "ending in h, m or y" and so on; and since iṭ is given before what begins with val: aśvasīta, aśvasiṣṭāṃ, aśvasiṣuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person with liṭ joined: śaśvāsa, śaśvasatuḥ, śaśvasuḥ. In the three of the middle person: śaśvasitha, śaśvasthuḥ, śaśvas. In the three of the last person: śaśvāsa, śaśvās, śaśvasiva, śaśvasima. For luṭ, since iṭ is joined: śvasitā, śvasitāsi, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ: śāsyāta, śāmyastaṃ, śāsyāsuḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ: śāsiṣyati and so on.
