For the root "an, breathing," too, the operations of the ad class apply, and the procedure is like the preceding one. In the three of the first person with laṭ joined: aniti, anitaḥ, ananti. In the three of the middle person: aniṣi, aniḥ, anitha. In the three of the last person: animi, anivaḥ, animaḥ. For liṅ: anyāta, anyātāṃ, anyāḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: anitu, anitāta, anitāṃ, anantu. In the three of the middle person: anihi, anitāta, anitaṃ, anita. In the three of the last person: anāni, anāpa, anāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: ānīta, ānata, ānitāṃ, ānana. In the three of the middle person: ānīḥ, ānaḥ, ānitaṃ, ānita. In the three of the last person: āni, ānipa, ānima. For luṅ, since iṭ is given: ānīta, ānīṣṭāṃ, āniṣuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: āna, ānatuḥ, ānuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ānitha, ānathuḥ, āna. In the three of the last person: āna, āniva, ānima. For luṭ: anitā, anitāsi, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ: anyāta, anyāstāṃ, anyāsuḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ: aniṣyati and so on. For lṛṅ: aniṣyada and so on.

aniterbā: "Optionally, of aniti." After a prefix that contains the cause for changing n into ṇ, the letter n of a following aniti is optionally so changed: prāṇiti, prāniti, and so on.

For the root "jakṣa, eating and laughing," too, the operations of the ad class apply. Since iṭ is given by "ruda and the rest" before endings beginning with jhal, in the singular and dual of the first person of laṭ: jakṣiti, jakṣitaḥ. adabhyastata: "at, after an abhyasta." After the roots called abhyasta, namely jakṣa, eating; jāgṛ, waking; daridrā, faring badly; cakāsṛ, shining; śāsu, instructing; dīdhīṅ, shining; vevid, possessing; and so on, a following jha becomes at. So in the plural of the first person of laṭ: jakṣati. In the three of the middle person: jakṣiṣi, jakṣithanaḥ, jakṣitha. In the three of the last person: jakṣimi, jakṣivaḥ, jakṣimaḥ. For liṅ: jakṣyāta, jakṣyātāṃ, jakṣyaḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: jakṣitu, jakṣitāta, jakṣitāṃ, jakṣitu. In the three of the middle person: jakṣihi, jakṣitāta, jakṣitaṃ, jakṣita. In the three of the last person: jakṣāṇi, jakṣāva, jakṣāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: ajakṣāta, ajakṣata, ajakṣitāṃ, ajakṣiḥ, where jhi becomes jus by "sic, abhyasta" and so on. In the three of the middle person: ajakṣiḥ, ajakṣaḥ, ajakṣitaṃ, ajakṣita. In the three of the last person: ajakṣaṃ, ajakṣiva, ajakṣima.

For luṅ, with iṭ joined and vṛddhi made: ajākṣita, ajākṣiṣuḥ, and so on. For liṭ, formed by pronouncing the root twice and so on, in the three of the first person: jajākṣa, jajakṣatiḥ, jajakṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jajakṣitha, jajakṣathuḥ, jajakṣa. In the three of the last person: jajākṣa, jajakṣa, jajakṣeva, jajakṣima. For luṭ, since iṭ is given: jakṣitā, jakṣitāro, jakṣitāraḥ, jakṣitāsi, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ: jakṣyūta, jakṣāstāṃ, jakṣyāsuḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ: ajakṣiṣyati and so on; and for lṛṅ: ajakṣiṣyata and so on.

For the root "jagi, waking from sleep," too, the operations of the ad class apply. In the three of the first person of laṭ: jāgarti, jāgritaḥ, jāgraṃti. In the three of the middle person: jāgarṣi, jāgṛthaḥ, jagṛtha. In the three of the last person: jāgarmi, jāgṛvaḥ, jāgṛmaḥ. For liṅ: jāgṛyāta, jāgṛyatāṃ, jāgṛyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: jāgartu, jāgṛtāta, jāgṛtāṃ, jāgratu. In the three of the middle person: jāgṛhi, jāgṛtāta, jāgṛtaṃ, jāgṛta. In the three of the last person: jāgarāṇi, jāgarāpa, jāgarāma. In the singular and dual of the first person of laṅ: ajāgaḥ, ajāgṛtāṃ.

In the plural: jusica, "and also before jus." Before the jus that replaces jhi, the letter of the pratyāhāra ik at the end of the root takes guṇa. Thus for jāgṛ in laṅ: la becomes jhi; by "sic, abhyasta" and so on, jhi becomes jus; and with guṇa made by this sūtra: ajāgaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: ajāgaḥ, ajāgṛtaṃ, ajāgṛta. In the three of the last person: ajāgaraṃ, ajāgṛva, ajāgṛma.

jāgro 'biciṇṇalditsu: "Of jāgṛ, before what is not vi, ciṇ, ṇal or ṅit." Before suffixes of jāgṛ other than vi, ciṇ and ṇal, and moreover before suffixes called ārdhadhātuka that are not ṅit, guṇa is made. So for luṅ, with iṭ and with guṇa made by this sūtra: ajāgarīta, ajāgariṣṭāṃ, ajāgariṣuḥ, and so on.

For liṭ, after uṣ, vid and jāgṛ it is optional: joining āma or not joining it is made optional. So in the alternative where āma is joined: jāgarāṃcakāra, jāganāmāma, and so on. In the alternative where āma is not joined, in the three of the first person: jajagūra, jajāgaratuḥ, jajāgaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: jajāgaritha, jajāgarathuḥ, jajāgara. In the three of the last person: jajāgāra, jajāgariva, jajāgarima. For luṭ: jāgaritā, jāgaritārau, jāgaritāraḥ, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ too, in this context, guṇa is made by "of jāgṛ, vi, ci, na" and so on: jāgaryāta, jāgaryāstāṃ, jāgaryasuḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ: jāgariṣyati and so on. For lṛṅ: ajāgariṣyata and so on.

For the root "daridrā, faring badly," too, the operations of the ad class apply. In the singular of the first person of laṭ: daridrāti. iddaridrasya: "The it of daridrā." Before a sārvadhātuka that is kṅit and begins with a consonant, the āt of daridrā becomes it. So in the dual of the first person of laṭ: daradritaḥ. śnābhyastayorātaḥ: "Of the āt of śnā and of an abhyasta." Before a sārvadhātuka that is kṅit and begins with a vowel, the āt of the suffix śnā and of roots called abhyasta is elided. In the plural of the first person of laṭ: la becomes jhi; by "at from an abhyasta," jha becomes at; and since ā is deleted by this sūtra: daridrati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three of the middle person: daridrāsi, daridrāsi, daridrīthaḥ, daridrītha. In the three of the last person: daridrāmi, daridrivaḥ. For liṅ, since it is changed into i by "the it of daridrā": daridriyāta, daridriyātāṃ, daridriyuḥ, and so on.

For loṭ too, āt is changed into it before kṅit endings beginning with a consonant, and is elided before those beginning with a vowel, and so on. So in the three of the first person: daridrātu, daridritrita, daridritu. In the three of the middle person: daridrihi, daridrihi, daridritāta, daridritaṃ, daridrita. In the three of the last person: daridrāṇi, daridrāva, daridrāma. Likewise in the three of the first person of laṅ: adaridrita, adaridritāṃ, adaridruḥ, where jhi becomes jus by "sic, abhyasta" and so on, and ā is deleted by "of the āt of śnā and of an abhyasta." In the three of the middle person: adaridrāḥ, adaridritaṃ, adaridrita. In the three of the last person: adaridraṃ, adaridriva, adaridrima.

Quoted in the commentary: daridrāterārṅhadhātuke āllobo, "The āt of daridrāti is elided before an ārdhadhātuka." The āt of daridrāti is elided before a suffix called ārdhadhātuka other than san, ṇul and lyuṭ. The commentary further explains that, although it is an ārdhadhātuka, in luṅ this is optional. So in the alternative where it is elided, with iṭ given before what begins with val: adaridrīta, adaridrīṣṭāṃ, adaridriṣuḥ, and so on. Or else, in the alternative where it is not elided, since sak is given by "yam, ram, nam, āt" and so on, together with iṭ: adaridrāsita, adaridrīsaṣṭāṃ, adaridrāsiṣuḥ, and so on.

For liṭ, the root is pronounced twice; by "the first consonant remains," all the other consonants of the reduplicated syllable are deleted; and the āt is elided by "the āt of daridrāti is elided before an ārdhadhātuka" and so on. So in the three of the first person: dadaridrau, dadaridratuḥ, dadaridruḥ. In the three of the middle person: dadaridritha, dadaridrathuḥ, dadaridra. In the three of the last person: dadaridrau, dadaridriva, dadaridrima.

Quoted in the commentary: anekāca āmbaktabyaḥ, "Āma is to be stated also for what is not of a single vowel." By the statement that āma is to be joined before liṭ after a root that is not of a single vowel, joining āma before liṭ would be obtained, but there is an exception to this. Again, quoted in the commentary: daridrāterāmā, daridrāterāmā, "The āma of daridrāti is optional." Before liṭ of daridrāti, joining āma or not joining it is made optional. The examples where āma is not joined have already been explained. With āma joined, formed by "iṭ is lost" and so on: daridrāṃbabhūva, daridrāṃcakāra, daridrāmāsa, and so on.

For luṭ, iṭ is given, and ā is deleted by "the āt of daridrāti is elided before an ārdhadhātuka": daridritā, daridritāsi, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ, with the āt deleted: daridhyāta, daridhyāstā, daridryāsiḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ, with iṭ given and the āt deleted: daridriṣyahi and so on. Likewise for lṛṅ: adaridriṣyata and so on.

For the root "cakāsri, shining," too, the parasmaipada endings are joined. In the three of the first person of laṭ: cakāsti, cakāstaḥ, cakāsati. In the three of the middle person: cakāssi, cakāsthaḥ, cakāstha. In the three of the last person: cakāsmi, cakāsvaḥ, cakāsmaḥ. For liṅ: cakāsyāta, cakāsyātāṃ, cakasyāḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: cakāstu, cakāstāta, cakāstāṃ, cakāsatu. In the singular of the middle person: sip; by "sip becomes hi" and by "hujhal," hi becomes dhi; and by "the jhals become jaś," s is changed into d; or else, as the commentary explains, s is elided before dhi: cakāddhi, cakāddhi, cakāstāta. In the dual and plural of the middle person: cakāstaṃ, cakāsta. In the three of the last person: cakāsāni, cakāsāva, cakāsāma.

tipyanasteḥ: "Before tip, of what is not asti." The final letter s of a root other than asti becomes d before the tip that replaces laṅ: acakāta. In the dual and plural: acakāstāṃ, acakāsuḥ. sipikhāto rurbā: "Before sip, optionally ru of the root." Before the sip that replaces laṅ, the final letter of the root optionally becomes ru, and optionally does not: acakāḥ, acakād, acakāstaṃ, acakāsta. In the three of the last person: acakāsaṃ, acakāsva, acakāsma. For luṅ, since iṭ is given: acakāsīta, acakāsiṣṭāṃ, acakāsiṣuḥ, and so on.

For liṭ, āma is made optional by "what is not of a single vowel" and so on. So in the alternative without āma, in the three of the first person: cacakāsa, cacakāsatuḥ, cacakāsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cacakāsitha, cacakāsathuḥ, cacakāsa. In the three of the last person: cacakāsa, cacakāsiva, cacakāsima. In the alternative where āma is joined: cakāsāṃbabhūva, cagāsāṃcakāra, cakāsāmāsa, and so on. For luṭ, since iṭ is given: cakāsitā, cakāsitāsi, and so on.

For the benedictive liṅ: cakāsyāta, cakāsyāstaṃ, cakāsāsuḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ too, since iṭ is given: cakāsiṣyati and so on; and for lṛṅ: acakāsiṣyata and so on.

For the root "śāsu, instructing," laṭ and the rest take the ataṅ endings, that is, the parasmaipada. In the singular of the first person of laṭ: śāsti. śāsa idaṅheloḥ: "The it of śās, before aṅ and before a consonant." The ā of the penultimate of śās becomes it before the aṅ that replaces cli and before a kṅit suffix beginning with a consonant. So in the dual of the first person of laṭ: śiṣṭaḥ. Thus śāsu; laṭ, with śap lost; la becomes tas; i by this sūtra; ṣ by śāsi ghasi vasi and so on; and t into ṭ by ṣṭu and so on. In the plural, jha is changed into at by "at from an abhyasta": śāsati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three of the middle person: śāssi, śīṣṭhaḥ, śiṣṭha. In the three of the last person: śāsmi, śiṣaḥ, śiṣmaḥ. For liṅ: śiṣyāta, śiṣyātāṃ, śiṣyuḥ, and so on.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: śāstu, śiṣṭāta, śiṣṭāṃ, śāsatu. In the singular of the middle person of loṭ: śāhau, "śā before hi." Śās becomes śā before the hi that replaces loṭ. Thus śāsu; loṭ, with śap lost; la becomes sip; by "sip becomes hi," hi; and by this sūtra śās is changed into śā. Here, by "from a common basis it is not accomplished," on account of the earlier cause, the s, hi is changed into dhi by "hujhal, hi becomes dhi": śādhi. Or else, with hi changed into tātaṅ: śiṣṭāta. In the dual and plural: śiṣṭi, śiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: śāsāni, śāsāva, śāsāma.

In the singular of the first person of laṅ: la becomes tip; by "of iṭ as well," i is deleted; by "before ti, not of asti," s becomes d; by "hal, dīrgha" and so on, t is deleted; and by "without position" and so on: aśād, aśāta. In the dual and plural: aśiṣṭāṃ, aśīsuḥ. In the singular of the middle person, since ru and d are made optional by "before sip, optionally ru of the root": aśāḥ, aśāta, aśād. In the dual and plural: aśīṣṭaṃ, aśiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: aśāsaṃ, aśiṣā, aśiṣma.

For luṅ, by "from sarti, śāsti and arti too," cli is changed into aṅ; by "the it of śās, before aṅ and before a consonant," the penultimate is changed into it: śāsi; and since s is changed into ṣ by ghasi vasi and so on: aśiṣata, aśiṣatā, aśiṣana, and so on.

For liṭ, formed by pronouncing the root twice and so on, in the three of the first person: śaśās, śaśāsatuḥ, śaśāsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: śaśāsitha, śaśāsathuḥ, śaśās. In the three of the last person: śaśās, śaśāsib, śaśāsima. For luṭ: śāsitā, śāsitāsi, and so on. For the benedictive liṅ, the penultimate becomes i by "the it of śās, before aṅ and before a consonant," and s is changed into ṣ by śāsi ghasi vasi and so on: śiṣyāta, śiṣyāstāṃ, śaṣyāsuḥ, and so on. For lṛṭ, since iṭ is given before what begins with val: śāsiṣyati, śāsiṣyataḥ, śāsiṣyanti, and so on. Likewise for lṛṅ: aśāsiṣyata, aśāṣyatāṃ, aśāsiṣyana, and so on.

For the root "cakṣiṅ, speaking clearly," laṭ and the rest take the ātmanepada. Before endings beginning with jhal there is elision by "the first of a cluster, s and k" and so on, and the forms are made by "ṣṭu with ṣṭu" and so on. So in the three of the first person of laṭ: caṣṭi, cakṣate, cakṣate. In the singular of the middle person: thās; by "se for thās," thās becomes se; by "the first of a cluster, k" and so on, k is deleted; by "before s, k for ṣ and ḍh," ṣ becomes k; and since s is made into ṣ by the rule on substitutes and so on: cakṣe. In the dual: cakṣāthe. In the plural: l becomes dhvāṃ; k is deleted by "cluster" and so on; dh becomes ḍh by ṣṭu and so on; ṭi becomes e by "ṭit" and so on; and since ṣ is made into ḍ by "the jaś of the jhals": caḍḍhvi. In the three of the last person: cakṣe, cakṣvahe, cakṣmahe.

For liṅ, k is deleted by "cluster" and so on, ṣ becomes k by "before s, k for ṣ and ḍh," and the rule on substitutes and so on are applied: cakṣīta, cakṣīyātāṃ, cakṣīran. In the three of the middle person: cakṣīthāḥ, cakṣāāthāṃ, cakṣīdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: cakṣīya, cakṣāvahi. In the three of the first person of loṭ: caṣṭāṃ, cakṣātāṃ, cakṣatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: cakṣva, cakṣathāṃ, caḍhraṃ. In the three of the last person: cakṣai, cakṣāthāṃ, caḍḍhraṃ. In the three of the last person: cakṣai, cakṣāvahai, cakṣāmahai. In the three of the first person of laṅ: acaṣṭa, acakṣātāṃ, acakṣata. In the three of the middle person: acaṣṣāḥ, acakṣāthāṃ, acaḍḍhāṃ. In the three of the last person: acakṣi, acakṣvahi.

cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ: "The khyāñ of cakṣiṅ." Before a suffix called ārdhadhātuka, cakṣiṅ is to be changed into khyāñ; the letter ñ is for the sake of both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings applying. So for luṅ: cakṣiṅ is changed into khyāñ; by "aṅ for asyati, vakti and khyāti," cli is changed into aṅ; and the forms are made with ā elided by "elision by āt" and so on. In the three of the first person with the ataṅ endings: akhyad, akhyatāṃ, akhyan. In the three of the middle person: akhyaḥ, akhyataṃ, akhyata. In the three of the last person: akhyaṃ, akhyāva, akhyāma. Likewise, in the three of the first person with the taṅ endings: akhyata, akhyetāṃ, akhyanta. In the three of the middle person: akhyathāḥ, akhyethāṃ, akhyadhyaṃ. In the three of the last person: akhye, akhyāvahi, akhyāmahi. Quoted in the commentary: ksāñapīṣṭa, "ksāñ is also accepted."

Before a suffix called ārdhadhātuka, cakṣiṅ not only becomes khyā; it is also accepted that it is optionally changed into what is called ksāñ. Cacakṣiṅ. In the option where it is changed into skā, with the ataṅ endings of luṅ, ka and iṭ are added by "yama, rama, nam" and so on. In the three of the first person: aksāsīta, aksāsīṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: aksāsīḥ, aksāsiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: aksāsiṣaṃ, aksāsiṣva, aksāsaṣmi. With the taṅ endings there is only the form that introduces s, in which cli is changed into sic. In the three of the first person: akṣāsta, akṣāsatāṃ, akṣāsta. In the three of the middle person: akṣāsjāḥ, akṣāsāvrāṃ, akṣāṅhāṃ; before ṅh too, the s is elided. In the three of the last person: akṣāsi, akṣāsvahi, akṣāsmahi.

Further, the commentary explains: "When cakṣiṅ is connected with the meaning of avoiding or discarding, it is not changed into khyāñ and ksā, and in that case only the taṅ endings apply." Accordingly, in the option where it is not changed into khyañ and the rest, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val," in the three of the first person of luṅ: acakṣiṣṭa, acakṣiṣātāṃ, acakṣiṣata. In the three of the middle person: acakṣiṣjāḥ, acakṣiṣāthāṃ, acakṣidhva, acakṣiḍhvi. In the three of the last person: acakṣiṣi, acakṣiṣvahi, acakṣiṣmahi.

Vā liṭi: "Optionally before liṭ." Before liṭ, cakṣiṅ remaining just as it is, its change into khyāñ, and its change into ksāñ are all optional. In the option where it remains as cakṣiṅ, applying the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cacakī, cacakṣāte, cacakṣire. In the three of the middle person: cacakṣiṣi, cacakṣāthe, cacakṣidhāe, cacakīḍhre. In the three of the last person: cacakṣe, cacakṣevahe, cacakṣimahe, cacakṣimahe.

In the option where cakṣiṅ is changed into khyāñ, both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings apply. So with the ataṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cakhyo, cakhyatuḥ, cakhyāḥ. In the three of the middle person: cakhyitha, cakhyātha, cakhyathuḥ, cakhya. In the three of the last person: cakhyau, cakhyiva, cakhyima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cakhye, cakhyāte, cakhyire. In the three of the middle person: cakhyiṣe, cakhyāthe, cakhyidhve, cakhyiḍhve. In the three of the last person: cakhyi, cakhyivahe, cakhyimahe.

Again, in the option where cakṣiṅ is changed into ksāñ, both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings apply as well, and since it ends in the letter a, the procedures are the same as for khyāñ. With the ataṅ endings, in the three of the first person: caksau, caksatuḥ, caksuḥ. In the three of the middle person: caksitha, caksātha, caksāthuḥ, caksa. In the three of the last person: caksau, caksiva, caksima. Likewise with the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cakse, caksāte, caksīre. In the three of the middle person: caksiṣe, caksathe, caksidhve, caksiḍhve. In the three of the last person: cakse, caksivahe, caksimahe.

In luṭ, with the ataṅ endings in the option where it is changed into khyāñ: khyātā, khyātāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: khyātā, khyātāse, and so on. With the ataṅ endings in the option where it is changed into ksāñ: ksātā, ksātāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: ksātā, ksātāse, and so on. Further, when it is used in the sense of discarding, cakṣiṅ itself remains; applying the taṅ endings of luṭ and adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": cakṣitā, cakṣitārau, cakṣitāraḥ, cakṣitāse, and so on.

In what is called the benedictive, with the ataṅ endings in the option where it is changed into khyañ, the change into e by "also of another, beginning with a conjunct" and so on, and its absence, are optional: khyāyāta, khyāyāstāṃ, khyāyāsuḥ, and so on; or khyeyāta, khyeyāstāṃ, khyāyāsuḥ, and so on; or khyeyāta, khyeyāstāṃ, khyeyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, since it is not changed into e: khyāsīṣṭa, khyāsīyāstāṃ, khyāsīran, and so on. Likewise in the option where it is changed into ksāñ, with the ataṅ endings, ā itself and e are optional: ksāyāta, ksāyāstāṃ, ksāyāsuḥ, and so on; or kseyāta, kseyāstāṃ, kseyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, since it is not changed into e: ksāsāṣṭi, ksāsīyāstāṃ, ksāsīran, and so on. In the option where cakṣiṅ remains just as it is, applying the taṅ endings and adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": cakṣiṣīṣṭa, cakṣiṣīyāstāṃ, cakṣiṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ, with the ataṅ endings in the option where it is changed into khyāñ: khyāsyati, khyāsyataḥ, khyāsyanti, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: khyāsyate, khyāsyete, khyāsyante, and so on. With the ataṅ endings in the option where it is changed into ksāñ: ksāsyati, ksāsyataḥ, ksāsyanti, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: ksāsyate, ksāsyete, ksāsyante, and so on. In the option where cakṣiṅ remains as it is, only the taṅ endings apply; adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": cakṣiṣyate, cakṣiṣyete, cakṣiṣyante, and so on.

Likewise in lṛṅ too, with the ataṅ endings in the option where it is changed into khyāñ: aksāsyata, aksāsyatāṃ, aksāsyana, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: aksāsyata, aksāsyitāṃ, aksāsyanta, and so on. With the ataṅ endings in the option where it is changed into ksāñ: aksāsyata, aksāsyatāṃ, aksāsyan, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: aksāsyatāṃ, aksāsyanta, and so on. In the option where cakṣiṅ remains just as it is, the taṅ endings are applied, the iṭ of "beginning with val" is added, and the forms are completed by the change of s into ṣ through "of a substitute" and so on: acakṣiṣyute, acakṣiṣyetāṃ, acakṣiṣyanta, and so on.

The taṅ endings are applied to the root listed as "īḍ, in praising." In the singular of the first person of laṭ: with the taṅ of la, śap is elided; by "marked with ṭ" and so on, the final becomes e; by "before khar, car is appropriate," ḍ becomes ṭ; and by "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu is appropriate," t is brought to ṭ, giving īṭṭe. In the dual and the plural: īḍāte, īḍate. Īḍajanordhva: "also before dhva." From īḍ, from jan, "to generate," and also from īś, "to have mastery," the augment iṭ is given before the sārvadhātuka endings se and ṅhva. So in the three of the middle person of laṭ: īḍiṣe, īḍithe, īḍiṅhve. In the three of the last person: īḍe, īḍāhe, āṭmahe.

In liṅ, by "ata, not being final" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is elided and the forms are derived: īḍīta, īḍīyātāṃ, īḍīran. In the three of the middle person: īḍīthāḥ, īḍīyāthāṃ, īḍīdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: īḍīya, īḍīvahi, īḍīmahi.

In loṭ, forming them by "before khar, car" and "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu" and so on, in the three of the first person: īṭṭāṃ, īḍātāṃ, īḍatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: īḍiṣṣa; from īḍ and jan, iṭ is added before ṅhva too; īḍāthā, īḍidhvi; from īḍ and jan, iṭ is added before ṅhva too. In the three of the last person: īḍai, īḍāmahai, īḍāmahai.

In laṅ, forming them by "āṭ for those beginning with ac," "from āṭ too, vṛddhi," "before khar, car," and "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu" and so on, in the three of the first person: aiṭṭa, aiḍātāṃ, aiḍaha. In the three of the middle person: aiṭṭāḥ, aiṭāthāṃ, aiḍiṅhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: aiḍi, aiḍvihi, aiḍmahi.

In luṅ, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": aiḍiṣṭa, aiḍiṣātāṃ, aiḍiṣata. In the three of the middle person: eḍiṣṭāḥ, aiḍiṣāthāṃ, aiḍiṅhvaṃ, aiḍiṅhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: aiḍiṣi, aiḍiṣvahi; from īḍ and jan, iṭ is added before ṅhva too; aiḍiṣmahi.

In liṭ, since by "a root beginning with ic and having a heavy syllable" and so on, ām is optionally applied or not applied: īḍācakre, īḍīvabhūva, and so on. Or else, for īḍ, by "before liṭ the root is reduplicated," "ak with a similar vowel," and so on, in the three of the first person: īḍe, īḍāte, īḍire. In the three of the middle person: īḍeṣe, īḍāthe, īḍiḍhve. In the three of the last person: īḍe, īḍivahe, īvimahe.

In luṭ, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": īḍitā, īḍitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ too, by adding iṭ: īḍiṣīṣṭa, īḍiṣīyāstāṃ, īḍiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, by adding iṭ: īḍiṣyate, īḍiṣyante, īḍiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: āiḍiṣyata, aiḍiṣyetāṃ, aiḍiṣyanta, and so on.

The root listed as "īś, in having mastery," too is like what was just explained in all its operations. In the three of the first person of laṭ: īṣṭe, ūśāte, īśate. In the three of the middle person: īśiṣe, īśāthe, āeśiṅhī. In the three of the last person: īśe, īśvahe, īśvahe. In liṅ, by "āta, not being final" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is elided and the forms are derived: īśīta, īśīyātāṃ, ī... by "vraśca, bhrasja" and so on, s becomes ṣ, and by "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu" and so on... śīran, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: īṣṭāṃ, īśātāṃ, īśatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: īśiṣva, īśāthāṃ, īśiṅhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: īśai, īśāvahai, īśāmahai. In laṅ, by adding the āṭ for those beginning with ac and making vṛddhi: aiṣṭa, aiśātāṃ, aiśata. In the three of the middle person: aiṣṭhāḥ, aiśāthaṃ, aiśiṅhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: aiśi, aiśvahi, aiśmahi. In luṅ, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": aiśiṣṭa, aiśiṣātāṃ, aiśiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, since ām is optionally applied or not applied: īśīcakri, īśāṃvabhūva, īśāmāsa, and so on. And again, without ām, forming them by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: īśe, īśāte, īśīre. In the three of the middle person: īśiṣe, īśāthe, īśidhve, īśiḍhve. In the three of the last person: īśe, īśivahe, īśemahe. In luṭ, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": īśitā, īśitāse, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ: īśiṣīṣṭa, īśiṣīyāstāṃ, īśiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, by adding iṭ: īśiṣyate, īśiṣyante, īśiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aiśiṣyata, aiśiṣyetāṃ, aiśiṣyanta, and so on.

To the root listed as "ās, in sitting near," too the taṅ endings are applied. In the three of the first person of laṭ: āste, āsāte, āsate. In the three of the middle person: āsse, āsāthe, ādhve, āddhve. In the three of the last person: āse, āsvahe, āsmahe. In liṅ, by "ata, not being final" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is elided, and the s of ās is joined to ī, giving āsīta, āsīyātāṃ, āsīran, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: before dhva, by "before dh too, the s is separated," and by "of the jhal, jaś is appropriate," the s is optionally changed into d. Āstāṃ, āsātāṃ, āsatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: āsva, āsāthāṃ, ādhvaṃ, āddhaṃ. In the three of the last person: āsi, āsvāhai, āsvāhe. In laṅ, by adding the āṭ for those beginning with ac, sandhi, and so on, in the three of the first person: āsta, āsātāṃ, āsata. In the three of the middle person: āsthāḥ, āsāthāṃ, āṅhvaṃ, āṅdhaṃ. In the three of the last person: āsi, āsvāhi, āsyahi. In luṅ, by adding the āṭ for those beginning with ac, lengthening with a similar vowel, and adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": āsiṣṭa, āsiṣātāṃ, āsiśata, and so on. In liṭ, since ām is applied by "daya, aya, and from ās too": āsāṃcakre, āsāṃvabhūva, āsāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": āsitā, āsitāse, āsitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ too, by adding iṭ: āsiṣīṣṭa, āsiṣīyāstāṃ, āsiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: āsyaṣyate, āsiṣyete, āsiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: āsiṣyata, āsiṣyetāṃ, āsiṣyanta, and so on.

To the root listed as "vas, in covering," too the taṅ endings are applied. In the three of the first person of laṭ: vaste, vasāte, vasate. In the three of the middle person: vasse, vasāthe, vadhve. In the three of the last person: vase, vasvahe, vasmahe. In liṅ, by "ata, not being final" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is elided, and the forms are derived with vas: vasīta, vasīyātāṃ, vasīrana, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: vastāṃ, vasātāṃ, vasatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: vassva, vasāthāṃ, vadhvaṃ, vaddhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: vasai, vasāvahai, vasāmahai. In the three of the first person of laṅ: avasta, avasātāṃ, avasata. In the three of the middle person: avasthāḥ, avasāthāṃ, avadhvaṃ, avaddhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: avasi, avasvahi, avasmahi. In luṅ, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": avasiṣṭa, avasiṣātāṃ, avasiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: vavase, vavasāte, vavasire. In the three of the middle person: vavasiṣe, vavasāthe, vavasidhve, vavasiḍhve. In the three of the last person: vavasai, vavasivahe, vavasimahe. In luṭ, since by "bhṛ stu," "su ca," "vasti," and so on, iṭ is optional: vasitā, vasitāse, and so on; or vastā, vastāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by adding iṭ: vasiṣīṣṭa, vasiṣīyāstāṃ, vasiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, by adding iṭ: vasiṣyate, vasiṣyente, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: avasiṣyata, avasiṣyetāṃ, avasiṣyanta, and so on.

To the root listed as "ṇisi, in kissing," too the taṅ endings are applied. By "for ṇa, na is appropriate," ṇ becomes n; by "marked with i" and so on, num is added; and the forms are produced by the elision of śap and so on. In the three of the first person of laṭ: ninsti, ninsāte, ninsāte. In the three of the middle person: ninsāe, ninsāthe, nindsve. In the three of the last person: ninse, ninsāhe, ninsmahe. In liṅ, since by "ata, not being final" and so on the s of sīyuṭ is elided: ninsīta, ninsīyātāṃ, ninsīran, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: ninstāṃ, ninsāṃtāṃ, ninsatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: ninssāthāṃ, nindhvaṃ, nainṅhā; before bh too, the s is elided. In the three of the last person: ninsai, ninsāvahai, ninsāmahai. In the three of the first person of laṅ: aninsta, aninsāta. In the three of the middle person: aninsthāḥ, aninsāthāṃ, anindhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: aninsi, aninsvahi, aninsmahi. In luṅ, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": aninsiṣṭa, aninsiṣātāṃ, aninsiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, forming them by reduplication of the root and so on, in the three of the first person: nininse, nininsāte, nininsire. In the three of the middle person: nininsiṣe, nininsāthe, nininsidhve, nininsiḍhve. In the three of the last person: nininse, nininsivahe, nininsimahe. In luṭ, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val": ninsitā, ninsitāse, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ, by adding iṭ: ninsiṣīṣṭa, ninsiṣīyāstāṃ, ninsiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, by adding iṭ: ninsiṣyate, ninsiṣyete, ninsiṣyaṇte, and so on. In lṛṅ: aninsiṣyata, aninsiṣyata, aninsiṣyetāṃ, aninsiṣyetāṃ, and so on.

To the root listed as "ṣūṅ, in living beings' being born from the womb," too the taṅ endings are applied. The forms are produced by "the root-initial ṣ becomes s," and, before endings beginning with ac, by "before ac, śnu" and so on, through which u is changed into uva, and so on. In the three of the first person of laṭ: sūte, suvāte, suvate. In the three of the middle person: sūṣe, suvathe, sūdhve. In the three of the last person: suve, sūvahe. In liṅ, by "ata, not" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is elided, and by changing u into uv: suvīta, suvīyātāṃ, suvīran, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: sūtāṃ, suvātāṃ, suvatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: sūṣa, suvāthāṃ, sūṅhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: suvi, suvāvahai, suvāvahai. In the three of the first person of laṅ: asūta, asupātāṃ, asuvata. In the three of the middle person: asūthāḥ, asupāthāṃ, asūdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: asuvi, asūvahi, asūmahi. In luṅ, by "svarati, sūti, sūyati, dhūña, marked with ū" and so on, iṭ is optional. In the option where iṭ is added: asaviṣṭa, asaviṣātāṃ, asaviṣata, and so on. In the option without iṭ, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on: osoṣṭa, asoṣātāṃ, asoṣata. In the three of the middle person: asoṣṣāḥ, asoṣāthāṃ, asodhvaṃ, asoḍhaṃ. In the three of the last person: asoṣi, asoṣvahi, asoṣmahi. In liṭ, the root is reduplicated, and before endings beginning with ac, by "before ac, ṣnu" and so on, u is changed into uva, and so on. In the three of the first person: suṣuve, suṣuvate, suṣuvite. In the three of the middle person: suṣuviṣe, suṣuvāṣe, suṣuvāthe, suṣuvidhve, suṣuviḍhve, suṣūdhve, suṣūḍhve. In the three of the last person: suṣuve, suṣuvivahi, suṣūvahe, suṣuvimahe, suṣūmahe. In luṭ, since iṭ is optional, in the option with iṭ: savitā, savitāse, and so on; and in the option without iṭ: sotā, sotāse, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ too, since iṭ is optional, in the option with iṭ: saviṣāṣṭa, yāsaviṣīyāstāṃ, saviṣīran, and so on; and in the aniṭ option, by making guṇa: soṣīṣṭa, soṣīyāstāṃ, soṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, since iṭ is optional: sapiṣyate, saviṣyete, saviṣyante, and so on; or, in the option where iṭ is not added: soṣyate, soṣyete, soṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ too, since iṭ is optional, in the option where iṭ is added: asaṃviṣyata, aseviṣyetāṃ, asaviṣyanta, and so on; and in the option where iṭ is not added: asoṣyata, asoṣyatāṃ, asoṣyanta, and so on.

To the root listed as "śīṅ, in lying down," too the taṅ endings apply. Śīṅaḥ sarvadhvatuke guṇaḥ: "Śīṅ takes guṇa before a sārvadhātuka ending."

Before endings that are called sārvadhātuka, śīṅ takes guṇa. In the singular and the dual of the first person of laṭ: śete, śayāte. Śīdo ruṭ: "After śīṅ, ruṭ." For the ātmanepada endings that follow śīṅ, the at into which jh is changed by "āta, not being final" and so on takes the augment ruṭ. Its ṭ serves to fix its position, and its u serves for pronunciation. In the plural of laṭ: among the ātmanepada endings of la, jha; by "ata, not being final" and so on, jha becomes at; by this sūtra, ruṭ is added; and by "śīṅ takes guṇa before sārvadhātuka," guṇa is made, giving śerate. In the three of the middle person: śeṣe, śayāthe, śedhva. In the three of the last person: śaye, śevahe, śemahe.

In liṅ, by "ata, not being final," the s of liṅ is elided; the root takes guṇa; and by "ec" and so on it is changed into ay: śayīta, śayīyātāṃ, śayiran, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: śetāṃ, śayātāṃ, śeratāṃ. In the three of the middle person: śiṣva, śayāthāṃ, śedhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: śayai, śayāvahai, śayāmahai. Likewise, in the three of the first person of laṅ: aśeta, aśayātāṃ, aśerata. In the three of the middle person: aśethāḥ, aśeyāthāṃ, aśedhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: aśayi, aśevahi, aśamahi.

In luṅ, the iṭ of "beginning with val" is added, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on, and by "ac" and so on it is changed into ay: aśayiṣṭa, aśayiṣātāṃ, aśayiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, the root is reduplicated, and before endings beginning with ac, by "before ac, śnu, root" and so on, ī is changed into iy, and so on. In the three of the first person: śiśiye, śiśiyāte, śiśiyira. In the three of the middle person: śiśiyiṣe, śiśiyāthe, śiśiyidhve, śiśiyiḍhve. In the three of the last person: śiśiye, śiśiyivahe, śiśiyimahe. In luṭ, by adding the iṭ of "beginning with val" and making guṇa by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on: śayitā, śayitāse, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ: śayiṣīṣṭa, śayiṣīyāstāṃ, śayiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, by making iṭ, guṇa and so on: śayiṣyate, śayiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aśayiṣyetāṃ, aśayiṣyetāṃ, aśayiṣyanta, and so on.

To the root listed as "iṅ, in reciting words," too the taṅ endings are applied. The commentary explains: "Before iṅ the prefix adhi must always be applied; and since it does not thereby take on another meaning, it remains in the meaning of iṅ alone." Therefore adhi is placed before it, and before endings beginning with ac, by "before ac, śnu, root" and so on, it is changed into iy, and so on. In the three of the first person of laṭ: adhīte, adhīyāte, adhīyate. In the three of the middle person: adhīṣe, adhīyāthe, adhīdhe. In the three of the last person: adhīye, adhīvahe, adhīmahe.

In liṅ, by "at, not being final, is to be elided by liṅ," the s is elided; by "ak before a similar vowel becomes long," the vowel after dhi is merged, and so on. In the three of the first person: adhīta, adhīyātāṃ, adhīran. In the three of the middle person: adhīthāḥ, adhīyāthāṃ, adhīdhāṃ. In the three of the last person: adhīsa, adhīvahi, adhīmahi. In the three of the first person of loṭ: adhītāṃ, adhīyātāṃ, adhīyatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: adhīṣa, adhīyāthāṃ, adhīdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: adhyayai, adhyayāvahai, adhyayāmahi.

In laṅ, forming them by "āṭ for those beginning with ac" and so on, "from āṭ too, vṛddhi," and "ik before ac becomes yaṇ" and so on, in the three of the first person: adhyaita, adhyaiyātāṃ, adhyaiyate. In the three of the middle person: adhyaithāḥ, adhyaiyāthāṃ, adhyaidhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: adhyaiyi, adhyaivahi, adhyaimahi.

Viṣhāṣā luṅlṛṅoḥ: "Optionally before luṅ and lṛṅ." Before luṅ and lṛṅ, after first making iy for the root iṅ by "before ac, śnu" and so on, then āṭ by "for those beginning with ac" and so on, and vṛddhi by "from āṭ too," iṅ is optionally changed or not changed into what is called gāṅ.

Gaṅkuṭādibhyo 'ñiṇt dita: "After gāṅ, kuṭ and the rest, those not marked with ñ are marked with ṅ." The suffixes that follow gāṅ, the substitute of iṅ, and kuṭ and the rest, and that are not marked with ñ or ṇ, receive the technical designation "marked with ṅ." Its purpose is that guṇa and the like are not made.

Ghumāsthāvāpājahātisāṃ hali: "Of ghu, mā, sthā, gā, vā, jahāti and sā, before hal."

For the roots called ghu, for māṅ, "to respect," for ṣṭhā, "to turn back from going," for gāṅ, the substitute of iṅ, for pā, "to drink," for jahāti, that is, ohāk, "to abandon," and for sā, that is, ṣo, "in the act of ending," the ā is to be changed into ī before a suffix called kaṅ-marked that begins with hal. Since the option is appropriate before luṅ and lṛṅ, luṅ is applied in the option where iṅ is changed into gāṅ; by this sūtra ā becomes ī; adhi is prefixed; and the forms are produced by changing cli into sic and so on. In the three of the first person: adhyagīṣṭa, adhyagīṣātāṃ, adhyagīṣata. In the three of the middle person: adhyagīṣṭhāḥ, adhyagīṣāthāṃ, adhyagidhyvaṃ. In the three of the last person: adhyagīṣi, adhyagīṣvahi, adhyagīṣmahi.

In the option where it is not changed into gāṅ, the āṭ for those beginning with ac is added, and vṛddhi is made by "from āṭ too." In the three of the first person: adhyaiṣṭa, adhyaiṣātāṃ, adhyaiṣata. In the three of the middle person: adhyaiṣṣāḥ, adhyaiṣāthāṃ, adhyaiṅhāṃ. In the three of the last person: adhyagīṣi, adhyagīṣahi, adhyagīṣmahi.

In the option where it is not changed into gāṅ, ac... iṅ is to be changed into gāṅ. Liṭ is applied to iṅ preceded by adhi; by this sūtra it is changed into gāṅ; it is reduplicated; and the forms are produced by "before iṭ too, ā is to be elided," by the elision of ā, and so on. In the three of the first person: adhijoge, adhijagāte, adhijagire. In the three of the middle person: adhijagiṣe, adhijagāze, adhijagidhve, adhijagiḍhve. In the three of the last person: adhijage, adhijagivahe, adhijagimahe.

In luṭ, by making guṇa through "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on: adhyetā, adhyetāse, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ: adhyeṣīṣṭa, adhyeṣīyāstāṃ, adhyeṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, by making guṇa: adhyeṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ, by the rule for luṅ and lṛṅ, the change into gāṅ is optional. In the gāṅ option, by changing into ī through "ghu, mā, sthā, gā" and so on: adhyagāṃṣyata, adhyagīṣyedāṃ, adhyagīṣyanta, and so on. In the option where it is not changed, by adding āṭ through "for those beginning with ac" and so on, and making vṛddhi through "from āṭ too": adhyaiṣyata, adhyaiṣyetāṃ, adhyaiṣyanta, and so on.

To the root listed as "dīdhīṅ, in shining and in playing," too the taṅ endings are applied. Before endings beginning with hal there is no operation. Before those beginning with ac, the forms are produced by changing into y through "of a root that has more than one ac" and so on. In the three of the first person of laṭ: dīdhāte, dīdhyate, dīdhyate. In the three of the middle person: dīdhyīṣe, dīdhyīthe, dīdhyīdhyāe. In the three of the last person: dīdhe, dīdhīvahe, dīdhīmahe.

Yāvarṇayor dīdhhivevyoḥ: "Before yi and the letter i, of dīdhī and vevī." Before a suffix yi, that is, before the letter y and the letter i, the final of dīdhī and of vevī is elided. For dīdhī in liṅ: by "at, not being final" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is elided, and by this sūtra the forms are derived through the root's ī: dīdhīta, dīdhīyātāṃ, dīdhīran. In the three of the middle person: dīdhīthāḥ, dīdhīyāthāṃ, dīdhīdhāṃ. In the three of the last person: dīdhīvahe, dīdhīmahi.

In loṭ, forming them as in the case of laṭ, in the three of the first person: dīdhītāṃ, dīdhīdāṃ. In the three of the middle person: dīdhīṣva, dīdhyathāṃ, dīdhīdhāṃ. In the three of the last person: dīdhye, dīdhyāvahai, dīdhyāmahai. Likewise, in the three of the first person of laṅ: adīdhīta, adīdhyatāṃ, adīdhyata. In the three of the middle person: adīdhīthāḥ, adīdhyāthāṃ, adīdhīdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: adīdhi, where the ī is elided by "before yi and the letter i, of dīdhī and vevī"; adīdhīvahi, where by "of dīdhī, vevī and iṭ" guṇa is not made; and adīdhīmahi.

In luṅ, by the iṭ of "beginning with val," and by "before yi, of dīdhī and vevī," the root-final ī is elided: adīdhiṣṭa, adīdhiṣātāṃ, adīdhiṣāta, and so on. In liṭ, by applying ām through "not of one ac" and so on: dīdhīcakre, dīdhyāṃvabhyāv, dīdhyāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, by the iṭ of "beginning with val," and by "before yi and the letter i, of dīdhī and vevī," the ī is elided: dīdhitāṃ, dīdhitāse. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ too, by giving iṭ and so on: dīdhiṣīṣṭa, dīdhiṣīyāstāṃ, dīdhiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, forming them by giving iṭ, eliding ī, and so on: dīdhiṣāte, dīdhiṣyete, dīdhiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: adīdhiṣyata, adīdhiṣyatāṃ, adīdhiṣyanta, and so on.

To the root listed as "vevī, in being alike," too the taṅ endings apply, and every procedure is like the one just explained: vevīte, vevyāte, vevyate, and so on.

To the root listed as "dīṣa, in displeasure," the ataṅ endings apply. For those called p-marked, guṇa is made by "ending in puk" and so on, and "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu" and so on are applied. In the three of the first person of laṭ: dviṣṭi, dviṣṭaḥ, dviṣṭaḥ, dviṣānti. In the three of the middle person: dvikṣi, dīṣṭhaḥ, dviṣṭha. In the three of the last person: dviṣmi, dviṣva, dvaṣmaḥ. In liṅ there is only the form that introduces ṣ: dviṣyāta, dviṣyātāṃ, dviṣyāḥ, and so on.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: dveṣṭu, dvethṭāta, dviṣṭāṃ, dviṣantu. In the three of the middle person: dvindhi, dviṣṭāta, dviṣṭaṃ, dviṣṭa. By "before s, ṣ and ḍh become k," and by the rule on substitutes and so on, ṣ. In the three of the last person: dveṣāṇi, dveṣāva, dveṣāma.

In the singular and dual of the first person of laṅ: adveṭa, adveṭa, adviṣṭaṃ. In the plural: by "dviṣaśca," "also after dviṣ." To dviṣ: sip; si becomes hi; "after hu and jhal, hi becomes dhi"; by "jhal at the end" and so on, ṣ becomes ḍ; by "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu," dh is brought in for dh. After this root too, the jhi that replaces a following laṅ optionally becomes jus: adviṣuḥ, adviṣana. In the three of the middle person: adreṭ. La becomes ti. By "itaś ca," the i of the ṅ-marked endings is dropped. By "hal, dīp" and so on, the t is dropped. By "jhal at the end" and so on, several changes are made. In pause it is made optional: adeḍ, adviṣṭaṃ, adviṣṭe. In the three of the last person: adveṣaṃ, adviṣva, adviṣma.

In luṅ: by "after a root ending in śal, with ik as its penultimate, and without iṭ" and so on, cli is changed to ksa, and the k is dropped. By "before s, ṣ and ḍh become k," ṣ becomes k. By the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed to ṣ, and so forth; thus: advikṣat, advikṣatāṃ, advikṣana, and so on.

In liṭ there is reduplication, and for the others, apart from the two ṇal and thal, kit is made optional by "svañj, a conjunct" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: dedviṣa, didreṣatuḥ, didviṣatuḥ, didveṣuḥ, didviṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: didviṣitha, didveṣṣa, didvaṣathuḥ, didviṣathuḥ, didviṣa, didviṣa. In the three of the last person: didveṣa, didveṣiva, didviṣiva, didveṣima, didviṣima.

In luṭ, guṇa is made by "ending in puk" and so on, and "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu" is applied; thus: dveṣṭu, dveṣṭvasi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, ṣ is introduced; thus: dviṣyāta, dviṣyāstāṃ, driṣyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by "before s, ṣ and ḍh become k," ṣ becomes k, and by the rule on substitutes and so on, s becomes ṣ, and so forth; thus: dvekṣyati, drekṣyataḥ, drekṣyanti, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: advekṣyat, advekṣyatāṃ, advekṣyan, and so on.

To the root listed as "duha, in milking," laṭ and the rest take both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. In the singular of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: la becomes tip. By "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa. By "for a root with initial d, gh," h becomes gh. By "after jhaṣ, t and th, not of dhā, become dh," t becomes dh. By "jhal" and so on, gh is changed to g; thus: dogdhi. In the dual and plural: dugdhaḥ, duhanti. In the singular of the middle person: la becomes sip. By "for a root with initial d, gh," h becomes gh. By "having one vowel" and so on, d becomes dh. By "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa. By "before khar, car," gh becomes k. By the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed to ṣ; thus: dhokṣi. In the dual and plural, with thas: dughaḥ; dugha, tha. In the three of the last person: dohmi, duhāḥ, duhmaḥ, duhmaḥ.

Deriving them in the same way as those procedures, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: dugdhe, duhāte, duhate. In the three of the middle person: dhukṣe, duhāthe, dhugdhe. In the three of the last person: duhe, duhāhe, duhmahe.

In the ataṅ of liṅ there is only the form that introduces h: duhyāta, duhyātāṃ, duhyāḥ, and so on. In the taṅ too, by "not at the end" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped and h is introduced; thus: duhītaṃ, dunīyātāṃ, duhīran, and so on.

In loṭ, deriving as in the case of laṭ, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: dogbhu, dugbhāta, dugbhaṃ, duhantu. In the singular of the middle person: la becomes sip; si becomes hi; "after hu and jhal, hi becomes dhi"; for a root with initial d, h becomes gh; by "jhal" and so on, g is brought in for gh; thus: dugdhi. Or optionally hi is changed to tātaṅ; thus: dugdhāta. In the dual and plural: dugdha, dugdha. In the three of the last person: dohīni, dohīva, dohīva, dohāma. Likewise in the taṅ: dusdhāṃ, duhātāṃ, duhātāḥ, duhatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: dhokṣa, duhāthāṃ, dhugdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: dohai, dohāvahai, dohāmahai.

In the singular of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: la becomes tip. By "itaś ca," the i of the ṅ-marked endings is dropped. For a root with initial d, h becomes gh. By "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa. By "hal, dīp" and so on, the t is dropped. In pause it is optional; being changed to g or k: adog, adog. In the dual and plural: adugdhāṃ, aduhana. Likewise, in the three of the middle person: adhoga, adhoka, adugdhaṃ, adugdha. In the three of the last person: adoha, aduhva, aduhma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: adugdha, aduhātāṃ, aduhaha. In the three of the middle person: asugdhāḥ, aduhāthāṃ, adhugbhāṃ. In the three of the last person: a, by reason of the s, d becomes dh, duhi; aduhvahi, aduhmahi.

In luṅ: by "after a root ending in śal, with ik as its penultimate, and without iṭ" and so on, cli is changed to ksa, and the k is dropped. For a root with initial d, h becomes gh. By "having one vowel" and so on, d becomes dh. By "before khar, car," gh becomes k. By the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed to ṣ, and so forth; thus, in the ataṅ: adhukṣata, adhukṣatāṃ, adhukṣana, and so on. In the singular of the first person of the taṅ: duha. By "liha" and so on, the elision or non-elision of ksa is made optional; thus: adhukṣata, adugdha. In the dual: by "before a vowel, of ksa," the a of the s is dropped; thus: adhukṣātāṃ. In the plural, the elision of a is made optional; thus: adhukṣanta, adhukṣata. Likewise, in the singular of the middle person: adhukṣathāḥ, adhukdhāḥ. In the dual: adhukṣāthāṃ. In the plural: adhukṣadhāṃ, adhugdhāṃ. In the three of the last person: adhukṣi, adhukṣi, adhukṣavahi, adhukṣāmahi.

In liṭ, reduplication and so on being made, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: dudoha, duduhatuḥ, duduhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: dudohitha, dudogdha, duduhathuḥ, duduha. In the three of the last person: dudoha, duduhiva, duduhima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: duduhe, duduhāte, duduhire. In the three of the middle person: duduhiṣe, duduhāthāṃ, duduhidhve, duduhiḍhve. In the three of the last person: duduhe, duduhivahe, duduhimahe.

In luṭ: for a root with initial d, h becomes gh; by "after jhaṣ, not of dhā" and so on, t becomes dh; by "jhal" and so on, gh is changed to g; thus, in the ataṅ: doghā, dogdhāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: dogdhā, dogdhāse, and so on.

In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: duhyāt, duhyāstāṃ, duhyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: by "before liṅ and sic in the ātmanepada," guṇa is not made. By "for a root with initial d, gh," h becomes gh. By "before khar, car," gh becomes k. By the rule on substitutes and so on, the change to ṣ and so forth is made; thus: dukṣīta, dukṣīyāstāṃ, dukṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on, guṇa. H becomes gh. Before khar, car. By the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed to ṣ; thus, in the ataṅ: dokṣyati, dokṣyati, dokṣyataḥ, dokṣyanti, and so on; and in the taṅ: dokṣyate, dokṣyante, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: adokṣyata, adokṣyatāṃ, adokṣyana, and so on; and in the taṅ: adokṣyata, adokṣyatāṃ, adokṣyanta, and so on.

To the root listed as "diha, in accumulating," both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings likewise apply, and apart from the mere difference of o and e in the case of guṇa, the procedure and all the derived forms are like the case of duha just explained: degdhi, digdhaḥ, dihanti, and so on. When a preverb such as ni or pra is prefixed, the n is changed to ṇ by "gada, nada, bada" and so on; thus: praṇidigdhi, and so on.

The root listed as "liha, in tasting," also takes the endings of both voices. In the singular of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: la becomes tip. By "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa. By "ḍh for h," h becomes ḍh. By "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh. By "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu," dh becomes ḍh. By "after ḍh, elision," the preceding ḍh is dropped; thus: leḍhe. In the dual: la becomes tas. H becomes ḍh. By "jhaṣ" and so on, dh becomes ḍh. After ḍh, ḍh is dropped. By "when ḍh or r is dropped, the preceding aṇ becomes long," it is changed to a long vowel; thus: līḍhaḥ. In the plural there is only the form that introduces h: lihanti. In the singular of the middle person: la becomes sip. By "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa. H becomes ḍh. By "before s, ṣ and ḍh become k," ḍh becomes k. By the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed to ṣ, and so forth; thus: lekṣi. In the dual and plural: la is changed to thas and to tha. H becomes ḍh. By "jhaṣ" and so on, th becomes dh. By "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu," dh becomes ḍh. After ḍh, ḍh is dropped. By "when ḍh or r is dropped" and so on, the vowel is made long; thus: līḍha, līḍha. In the three of the last person: lehmi, lihvaḥ, lihmaḥ.

Deriving them in the same way as those procedures, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: līḍhe, lihāte, lihate. In the three of the middle person: likṣe, lihāthāṃ, līḍhve. In the three of the last person: lihe, lihvahe, lihmahe.

In the ataṅ of liṅ there is only the form that introduces h: lihyāta, lihyāstāṃ, lihyuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ too, by "not at the end" and so on, the s is dropped and h is introduced; thus: lihīta, lihīyāthāṃ, lihīran, and so on.

In loṭ, deriving as in the case of laṭ, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: leḍhu, līḍhāta, līḍhe, līhantu. In the three of the middle person: līḍhi, līḍhvata, līḍhaṃ, līḍha. In the three of the last person: lehāni, lehāva, lehāma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: līḍhāṃ, lihātāṃ, lihātāṃ. In the three of the middle person: lekṣva, lihāthā, līḍhāṃ. In the three of the last person: lehe, lehāvahi, lehāmahi.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: aleṭ, aleṭ, alīḍhāṃ, alihana. In the three of the middle person: aleḍ, aleṭ, alīḍhaṃ, alīḍha. In the three of the last person: alehi, alihā, alihma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: alīḍha, alihātāṃ, alihata. In the three of the middle person: alīḍhaḥ, alihāthāṃ, alīḍhva. In the three of the last person: alihi, alihvahi, alihmahi.

In the ataṅ of luṅ: by "after a root ending in śal, with ik as its penultimate, and without iṭ, ksa," cli is changed to ksa. By "ḍh for h," h becomes ḍh. Before s, ṣ and ḍh become k. By the rule on substitutes and so on, it is changed to ṣ; thus: alikṣata, alikṣatāṃ, alikṣana, and so on. In the singular of the first person of the taṅ: by "duha, diha, liha" and so on, the elision or non-elision of ksa is made optional; thus: alikṣata, alīḍha. In the dual: by "before a vowel, of ksa," the a is dropped; thus: alikṣātāṃ. In the plural, the elision or non-elision of a is made optional; thus: alikṣanta, alikṣata. Likewise, in the singular of the middle person: alikṣathāḥ, aliktadhaḥ. In the dual: alikṣāthāṃ. In the plural: alikṣadhāṃ, alīḍhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: alikṣi, alikṣāvahi, alikṣāmahi.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of liṭ: liliha, lilihatuḥ, lilituḥ. In the three of the middle person: lilihitha, liliḍha, lilihāthuḥ, liliha. In the three of the last person: liliha, lilihiva, lilihima. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: lilihe, lilihehe, lilihire. In the three of the middle person: lilihiṣe, lilihāthe, lilihidhvi, lilihiḍhe. In the three of the last person: lilihe, lilihivahe, lilihimahe.

In luṭ: by "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa. H becomes ḍh. By "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh. With ṣṭu, ṣṭu. After ḍh, ḍh is dropped; thus, in the ataṅ: laḍhā, leḍhāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: laḍhāse, and so on.

In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: lihyāta, lihyāstāṃ, lihyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: by "liṅ and sic" and so on, guṇa is not made. H becomes ḍh. Before s, ṣ and ḍh become k. By the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed to ṣ; thus: lakṣīṣṭa, lakṣīyāstāṃ, and so on.

In lṛṭ: by "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa. H becomes ḍh. Before s, ṣ and ḍh become k. Deriving by the rule on substitutes and so on, in the ataṅ: lekṣyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: lekṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: alekṣyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: alekṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ārṇuña, in covering all around," both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings likewise apply. "Ūrṇoteḥ vibhāṣā": it is optional for ūrṇoti.

For ūrṇoti, before a following sārvadhātuka that is called p-marked and has a hal at its beginning, vṛddhi and guṇa are made optional. In the singular of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: ūrṇoti, ūrṇoti. In the dual: ūrṇataḥ. In the plural: by "before ac" and so on, it is changed to uv; thus: īrṇuvanti. Deriving in the same way as those, in the three of the middle person: ūrṇauṣi, ūrṇoṣi, ūrṇuthaḥ, ūrṇutha. In the three of the last person: ūrṇaumi, ūrṇaumi, ūrṇuva, ūrṇuma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: ūrṇate, ūrṇuvāte, ūrṇuvate. In the three of the middle person: ūrṇuṣe, ūrṇāvāthe, ūrṇudhe. In the three of the last person: ūrṇuve, ūrṇuvahe, ūrṇumaha.

In the ataṅ of liṅ: ūrṇuyāta, ūrṇuyātāṃ, ūrṇuyuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: by "not at the end" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped, and by "before ac, śnu, root" and so on, it is changed to uv; thus: ūrṇuvīta, urṇuveyātāṃ, ūrṇuvīran, and so on.

In loṭ, deriving as in the case of laṭ, in the singular of the first person of the ataṅ: ūrṇoṃtu, ūrṇotu, ūrṇutāta. In the dual and plural: ūrṇutāṃ, ūrṇuvantu. In the three of the middle person: ūrṇuhi, ūrṇutāta, ūrṇutaṃ, ūrṇuta. In the three of the last person: ūrṇavāṇi, ūrṇavāva, ūrṇavāma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: ūrṇutāṃ, ūrṇupātāṃ, ūrṇuvatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: ūrṇuṣa, ūrṇuvāthāṃ, ūrṇudhraṃ. In the three of the last person: ūrṇuvi, ūrṇavāvai, ūrṇavāmahai.

"Guṇoñaprikṭhe": before an apṛkta, guṇa. Before a sārvadhātuka of ūrṇoti that is an apṛkta, that is, a p-marked one consisting of a single hal letter, vṛddhi is not made optional, and only guṇa is made. In the singular of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: la becomes tip. By "itaś ca," the i of the ṅ-marked endings is dropped. By this sūtra, guṇa. By "aṭ for a root with initial ac," aṭ, and by "also after aṭ," vṛddhi is made; thus: aurṇota. In the dual and plural: aurṇutāṃ, aurṇuvan. Likewise, in the three of the middle person: aurṇoḥ, aurṇutaṃ, aurṇuta. In the three of the last person: aurṇavaṃ, aurṇuva, aurṇuma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: aurṇuta, orṇuvātāṃ, aurṇuvata. In the three of the middle person: aurṇuthāḥ, aurṇuvathā, aurṇudhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: aurṇuvi, aurṇuvahi, aurṇumahi.

"Ūrṇoterbibhvāṣā": an option for ūrṇoti. For ūrṇoti, before a following sic that has iṭ at its beginning and is in the parasmaipada, vṛddhi and guṇa are made optional. In the ataṅ of luṅ, on the side where vṛddhi is made: aurṇāvīta, aurṇāviṣṭaṃ, aurṇāviṣuḥ, and so on; and on the side of guṇa: aurṇavīta, aurṇaviṣuṃ, aurṇaviṣuḥ.

"Vibhāṣorṇoḥ": optionally for ūrṇu. Whatever suffix with iṭ at its beginning follows ūrṇu is optionally made ṅ-marked; its purpose is that neither guṇa nor vṛddhi be made. On the ṅ-marked side, by "before ac, śnu, root" and so on, it is changed to uv; thus: aurṇuvīta, aurṇuviṣṭaṃ, aurṇuviṣuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, by "optionally for ūrṇu," guṇa and the change to uv are made optional; thus: aurṇuviṣṭa, aurṇuviṣātāṃ, aurṇuviṣata, and so on; or aurṇuviṣṭe, aurṇuviṣātāṃ, aurṇuviṣata, and so on.

Cited in the commentary: "Ūrṇuterāmaniṣeṅhaḥ": after ūrṇuti, ām does not occur. Although it was explained above that ām is added before a following liṭ to a root with initial ic possessing a heavy syllable, other than ṛcch, this is the exception: although it has initial ic and possesses a heavy syllable, ām is not added.

"Ajādirdvitīyasya": of the second of one with initial ac. If the second portion of a root that has an ac at its beginning possesses any ac whatever, then before liṭ and the other suffixes that are the occasion for reduplicating the root, that initial ac is not reduplicated; rather, the portion consisting of a hal together with its vowel is reduplicated.

"Nanadrāḥsaṃyogādayaḥ": not n, d and r that are the first of a conjunct. The letters n, d and r, where they stand first in a conjunct, in the hal with its ac following the initial ac, are not doubled before a following liṭ and so on. To ūrṇu: liṭ. By "of the second of one with initial ac," nu is reduplicated. By this sūtra, r is not doubled. Deriving vṛddhi, guṇa, the change to uv and so on as each suffix entails, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: ūrṇunāva, ūrṇunuvatu, ūrṇunuvatuḥ, ūrṇunuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ūrṇunavitha, ūrṇunuvitha, ūrṇunuvathuḥ, ūrṇuniva. In the three of the last person: ūrṇunāva, ūrṇunāva, ūrṇunaviva, ūrṇunuviva, ūrṇunavimas, ūrṇunuvimas.

Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: ūrṇunuve, ūrṇunuvāte, ūrṇunuṃvire. In the three of the middle person: by "optionally for ūrṇu," guṇa and uv are made optional: ūrṇunuviṣe, ūrṇunaviṣe, ūrṇunuvāthe, ūrṇunavidhve, ūrṇunaviḍhve, ūrṇunuvidhve, ūrṇunuviḍhve. In the three of the last person: ūrṇunuve, ūrṇunavivahe, ūrṇunuvivahe, ūrṇunarimahe, ūrṇuvimahe.

In luṭ: by "optionally for ūrṇu," guṇa and uv are made optional; thus, in the ataṅ: ūrṇuvitā, ūrṇuvitāsi, and so on; or ūrṇuvitā, ūrṇuvitāsi, and so on. Likewise in the taṅ too: ūrṇuvitā, ūrṇuvitāse, and so on; or ūrṇuvitā, ūrṇuvitāse, and so on.

In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: by "not kṛt" and so on, it is lengthened; thus: ūrṇuyāta, ūrṇuyāstāṃ, ūrṇuyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: the iṭ of "beginning with val"; and by "optionally for ūrṇu," guṇa and uv are made optional; thus: ūrṇuviṣīṣṭa, ūrṇaviṣīyāstāṃ, ūrnaviṣīran, and so on; or ūrṇudiṣīṣṭa, and so on.

In lṛṭ too, iṭ is given, and guṇa and u are made optional; thus, in the ataṅ: ūrṇuviṣyati, ūrṇuviṣyataḥ, ūrṇaviṣyanti, and so on; or ūrṇuviṣyati, and so on.

In the taṅ too: ūrṇaviṣyatye, ūrṇaviṣyete, ūrṇaviṣyante, and so on; or ūrṇuviṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: aurṇaviṣyata, aurṇuviṣyatāṃ, aurṇaviṣyana, and so on; or aurṇuviṣyata, and so on. In the taṅ: aurṇaviṣyata, aurṇaviṣyatāṃ, aurṇaviṣyanta, and so on; or aurṇuviṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ṣṭuña, in praising," both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings likewise apply. "Nurustuśamyamaḥ sarbabhātuke": from nu, ru, stu, śama and yama, before a sārvadhātuka. Nu, in praising; ru, in sound; stu, in praising, the initial ṣ of the root ṣṭuña being changed to s; śamu, in pacifying; and yamu, in ceasing: before a sārvadhātuka following these that has a hal at its beginning and is called p-marked, the augment īṭ optionally occurs. Adding laṭ to ṣṭuña, in the singular of the first person of the ataṅ, īṭ is made optional by this sūtra. On the side with īṭ, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on; and on the side without īṭ, vṛddhi is made by "uṭ" and so on; thus: stavīti, stauti. In the dual and plural: stutaḥ, stuvanti. Likewise, in the three of the middle person: stavīṣi, stauṣi, stuthaḥ, stutha. In the three of the last person: stavīmi, staumi, stuvaḥ, stumaḥ.

In the taṅ there is no further operation for those with a hal at the beginning. Those with an ac at the beginning are derived by the change to uv by "before ac, śnu, root" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: stute, snuvāte, stuvate. In the three of the middle person: stuṣe, stuvāthe, studhve. In the three of the last person: stuṅe, stuvahe, stumhe.

In the ataṅ of liṅ there is no further operation; thus: stuyāta, stuyātāṃ, stuyā, and so on. In the taṅ, by "not at the end" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped, and by "before ac, śnu, root" and so on, it is changed to uv; thus: stuvīta, stuvīyātāṃ, stuvīran, and so on.

In loṭ, deriving as for laṭ, in the singular of the first person of the ataṅ: stavītu, stautu, stutāta. In the dual and plural: stutāṃ, stuvantu. Likewise, in the three of the middle person: stuhi, stutāta, stutaṃ, stuta. In the three of the last person: stavāni, stavāva, stavāma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: tutāṃ, stuvātāṃ, stuvatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: stuṣva, stuvāthāṃ, studhāṃ. In the three of the last person: stuvai, stavāvahai, stavāmahai.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: astaut, astavīta, astutāṃ, astuvana. In the three of the middle person: astauḥ, astavīḥ, astutaṃ, astuta. In the three of the last person: astavaṃ, astuva, astuma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: astuta, astuvātāṃ, astuvata. In the three of the middle person: astuthaḥ, astuvāthāṃ, astudhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: astuvi, astuvahi, astumahi.

In the ataṅ of luṅ: by "after stu, su and dhūña, before the parasmaipada," iṭ is given, and by "vṛddhi before sic" and so on, vṛddhi is made; thus: astāpīta, astāviṣṭāṃ, astāviṣuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: astoṣṭa, astoṣātāṃ, astoṣata. In the three of the middle person: astoṣṭāḥ, astoṣāthāṃ, astodhvaṃ, astoḍhva. In the three of the last person: astoṣi, astoṣvahi, astoṣmahi.

In liṭ the root is reduplicated, and by "śar first" and so on, the s is dropped. Before those with val at the beginning, by "kṛ, pṛ, sṛ, stu, sru, dru" and so on, iṭ does not apply. For the others, apart from the two ṇal and thal, by "svañj, a conjunct"; by "also before dh," the s is dropped; and by "p first" and so on, kit is made optional. On the kit side, for those with ac at the beginning, uv is made by "before ac, śnu, root" and so on, and on the side that is not kit, guṇa is made. Thus, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: tuṣḍāva, tuṣṭavutuḥ, tuṣṭūvatuḥ, tuṣṭavuḥ, tuṣṭuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tuṣṭotha, tuṣṭavathuḥ, tuṣṭuvathuḥ, tuṣṭava, tuṣṭuva. In the three of the last person: tuṣṭāva, tuṣṭapa, tuṣṭova, tuṣṭuva, tuṣṭuva, tuṣṭoma, tuṣṭuma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: tuṣṭave, tuṣṭuve, tuṣṭavāte, taṣṭuvāte, tuṣṭvaviri, tuṣṭuvire. In the three of the middle person: tuṣṭoṣe, tuṣṭuṣe, tuṣṭavāthe, tuṣṭuvāthe, tuṣṭodhe, tuṣṭudhve. In the three of the last person: tuṣṭave, tuṣṭuve, tuṣṭovahe, tuṣṭuvahe, tuṣṭomahe, tuṣṭumahe.

Cited in the commentary: "Ḍubhṛṣṭuñostātāpiḍā": after ṭubhṛ and ṣṭuña, iṭ is optional before one with t at the beginning. Before an ārdhadhātuka with the letter t at its beginning, following ḍubhṛña, in bearing, and ṣṭuña, iṭ optionally occurs. Thus, in the ataṅ of luṭ, on the side where iṭ is added: stavitā, stavitāsi, and so on; and on the side without iṭ: stotā, stotāsi, and so on. Likewise, in the taṅ: stavitā, stavitāse, and so on; or stotā, stotāse, and so on.

In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: by "not kṛt" and so on, it is lengthened; thus: stūyāta, stūyādāṃ, stūyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, guṇa is made; thus: stoṣīṣṭa, stoṣīyātāṃ, stoṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, guṇa is made; thus, in the ataṅ: stoṣyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: stoṣyate, and so on. In the ataṅ of lṛṅ: astoṣyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: astoṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ṭukṣu, in sound," the ataṅ endings apply. In the three of the first person of laṭ: kṣauti, kṣutaḥ, kṣuvanti. In the three of the middle person: kṣiṣi, kṣūthaḥ, kṣutha. In the three of the last person: kṣaumi, kṣuvaḥ, kṣumaḥ. In liṅ: kṣuyāta, kṣuyātāṃ, kṣuyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: kṣautu, kṣutāta, kṣutāṃ, kṣuvantu. In the three of the middle person: kṣuhi, kṣutāta, kṣutaṃ, kṣuta. In the three of the last person: kṣavāni, kṣavāva, kṣavāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: akṣauta, akṣutāṃ, akṣuvan. In the three of the middle person: akṣauḥ, akṣutaṃ, akṣutaṃ, akṣuta. In the three of the last person: akṣavaṃ, akṣuva, akṣuma. In luṅ, iṭ is added and guṇa is made; thus: akṣavīta, akṣaviṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, apart from the two ṇal and thal, kit is made optional by "svañj" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: cukṣāva, cukṣāvatuḥ, cukṣuvatuḥ, cukāvuḥ, cukṣuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cukṣavitha, cukṣotha, cukṣavathuḥ, cukṣuvathuḥ, cukṣava, cukṣuva. In the three of the last person: cukṣava, cukṣava, cukṣaviva, cukṣuviva, cukṣavima, cukṣuvima. In luṭ, by "beginning with val," and guṇa being made: kṣavitā, kṣavitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "not kṛt" and so on, it is lengthened; thus: kṣūyāta, kṣūyāstāṃ, kṣūyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made; thus: kṣaviṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: akāviṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ru, in sound," the ataṅ endings also apply. In the singular of the first person of laṭ: by "nu, ru, stu" and so on, the addition of īṭ and vṛddhi are made optional; thus: ravīta, rauti. In the dual and plural: rutaḥ, ruvanti. Likewise, in the three of the middle person: davīṣi, rauṣi, ruthaḥ, rutha. In the three of the last person: ravīmi, raumi, ruvaḥ, rumaḥ. In liṅ: ruyāta, ruyātāṃ, ruyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: ravītu, rautu, rutāta, rutāṃ, ruvantu. In the three of the middle person: ruhi, ritāta, rutaṃ, ruta. In the three of the last person: ravāṇi, ravāva, ravāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: aravīta, arauta, arutāṃ, aruvana. In the three of the middle person: aravīḥ, arauḥ, arutaṃ, aruta. In the three of the last person: aravaṃ, aruva, aruma. In luṅ, the iṭ of "beginning with val" is given and guṇa is made; thus: aravīta, aravikṣāṃ, araviṣuḥ. In liṭ, apart from the two ṇal, for those with ac at the beginning, the change to uv and so on is made by "before ac, śnu, root" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: ruruva, ruruvatuḥ, ruruvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ruruvitha, ruruvathaḥ, ruruva. In the three of the last person: rurāva, rurava, ruruviva, ruruvima. In luṭ, by "ru, du, nu, su" and so on, iṭ is made optional; thus: ravitā, ravitāsi, and so on; or rotā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "not kṛt" and so on, it is changed to a long vowel; thus: rūyāta, rūyāstāṃ, rūyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ too, by "ru, du, nu" and so on, iṭ is made optional; thus: raviṣyati, and so on; or roṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: araviṣyata, and so on; or aroṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ṇu, in praising," the ataṅ endings also apply, and in all its procedure there is not the slightest difference from ru, just explained: navīti, nauti, nutaḥ, nivanti, and so on.

To the root listed as "brūña, in speaking clearly," both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings apply. "Bruva īṭ": after brū, īṭ. Before the sārvadhātukas following brū that have a hal at the beginning and are called p-marked, the augment īṭ occurs. In the singular of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: by this sūtra, īṭ, and by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on, guṇa being made: bravīti. In the dual and plural: brūtaḥ, brūvanti. Likewise, in the three of the middle person: bravīṣi, brūthaḥ, brūtha. In the three of the last person: bravīmi, brāvaḥ. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: brūte, brūvāte, brūvate. In the three of the middle person: brūṣe, brūvāthe, brūdhe. In the three of the last person: bruve, brūvahe, brūmahe.

"Bruvaḥ pañcānāmādita āho bruvaḥ": after brū, of the first five, and āha for brū. Of the parasmaipada endings that replace laṭ following brūña, the first five, tip and so on, optionally become in order the five, ṇal and the rest; and when they are so changed, brū too is to be changed to what is called āha. Brū; laṭ; la is changed in order to the five, tip and so on; by this sūtra the five, tip and so on, are changed in order to the five, ṇal and so on; and brū too is changed to āha; thus, before ṇal, atus and us: āha, āhatuḥ, āhuḥ.

"Āhasthaḥ": of āha, th. The h of āha becomes the letter th before a following jhal. To brū; for laṭ, sip. By "after brū, of the first five" and so on, sip becomes thal, and brū is changed to āha. By this sūtra, h becomes th. By "before khar, car," th is changed to t; thus: āttha. Deriving as above, with thas changed to athus: āhathuḥ. Examples of the side where they are not changed to ṇal and so on have already been given above.

In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: brūyāta, brūyātāṃ, brūyuḥ, and so on. And by "not at the end" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped, and by "before ac, śnu, root, brū" and so on, it is changed to uv; thus: bruvīta, bruvīyātāṃ, bruvīran, and so on.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of loṭ: bravītu, brūtāta, brūtāta, brūtāṃ, bruvantu. In the three of the middle person: brūtaṃ, brūtāta, būta. In the three of the last person: bravāṇi, bravāva, bravāma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: brūtāṃ, bruvātāṃ, bruvatī. In the three of the middle person: brūla, bruvābrāṃ, brūdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: bravai, bravāvahai, bravāmahai.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: abravīta, abrūtāṃ, abruvana. In the three of the middle person: abravīḥ, abrūtaṃ, abrūta. In the three of the last person: abravaṃ, abrūva, abrūma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: abruta, abrūvātāṃ, abrūta. In the three of the middle person: abrūthāḥ, abruvāthāṃ, abrūdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: abruvi, abrūvahi, abrūmahi.

"Bruvo vaciḥ": vaci for brū, vaci for brū. Before a following suffix called ārdhadhātuka, brū is changed to what is called vaci; the letter a is there for the sake of pronunciation. To brū, luṅ. By this sūtra, brū is changed to vaci. By "asyati, vakti" and so on, cli is changed to aṅ. By "um for vac," the augment u is given. Deriving by "guṇa after at" and so on, in the ataṅ: avocata, avocatāṃ, avocana, and so on. Likewise, in the taṅ: avocata, avocatāṃ, avocanta, and so on.

In liṭ, brū is changed to vac. Before those that are not kit, by "of the reduplicated" and so on, the reduplicated syllable takes samprasāraṇa; and before the kit ones, by "vaci, svapi" and so on, both are changed by samprasāraṇa; thus, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: uvāca, ūcatuḥ, ūcaḥ. In the three of the middle person: uvakkra, uvacitha, ūcathāḥ, ūca. In the three of the last person: uvāca, uvaci, ūciva, ūcima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: ūce, ūāte, ūcire. In the three of the middle person: ūciṣe, ūcāthe, ūcidhve, ūciḍhe. In the three of the last person: ūce, ūcivahe, ūcimahe.

In luṭ, by "ku for cu," c is changed to k and brought in; thus, in the ataṅ: vtā, vaktāse, and so on; and in the taṅ: vaktā, vaktāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, by "vaci, svapi" and so on, it is changed by samprasāraṇa; thus: ucāt, ucyāstāṃ, ucyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: by "ku for cu," c becomes k, and by the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed to ṣ; thus: vakṣīkṭa, vaktīyātāṃ, vakṣīrana, and so on. In lṛṭ too, ku for cu and the rule on substitutes and so on being applied, in the ataṅ: vakṣyiti, vakṣyataḥ, vakṣyanti, and so on; and in the taṅ: vakṣyate, vakṣyante, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: avakṣyata, avakṣyatāṃ, avakṣyana, and so on; and in the taṅ: avakṣyata, avakṣetāṃ, avakṣyanta, and so on.

"Iti bāṇinibyakaraṇasya sūtādadādalaḥ samāptāḥ": that is, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, ad and the rest are complete.

With these, from the work called The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down in the form of notes the meaning of the text and its commentary, the procedures, the illustrative examples and so on, of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the rough account of how laṭ and the rest are applied, together with the general rules and the exceptions, to ad and the others, for which the śap that has the sense of the agent is elided, is for the present complete.

Now I shall explain the procedures for juhoti and the rest. "Juhodyādibhyaḥ śluḥ": after juhoti and the rest, ślu. The twenty-four roots beginning with hu, in giving, are juhoti and the rest. The śap that comes after these by "śap in the agent" is to be changed to what is called ślu. "Ślau": before ślu. When śap has been changed to ślu, the root that has no reduplicated syllable is to be reduplicated before the following ślu, and the ślu too is elided.

To the root listed as "hu, in giving and in eating," the ataṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are added. Śap in the agent. By "juhoti" and so on, śap is changed to ślu. By this sūtra the root is reduplicated and the ślu is elided. By "cu for ku and h," h becomes jh, and by "of the reduplicated syllable, car too," h is changed to jh, and so on; deriving thus, in the three of the first person of laṭ: juhoti, juhutaḥ, juhvati. In the three of the middle person: juhoṣi, juhuthaḥ, jujuhutha. In the three of the last person: juhomi, juhuvaḥ, juhumaḥ.

Deriving juhu as above, in liṅ: juhuyāta, juhuyātāṃ, juhuyuḥ, and so on. Likewise, in the three of the first person of loṭ: juhotu; by "jh, at; of hu and śnu" and so on, aṇ; juhutāta, juhutāṃ, juhotu. In the three of the middle person: juhudhi, juhutāta, juhutaṃ, juhuta. In the three of the last person: juhavāni, juhavāva, juhavāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: ajuhota, ajuhutāṃ, ajuhavuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ajuhoḥ, ajuhutaṃ, ajuhuta. In the three of the last person: ajuhavaṃ; "after hu and jhal, hi"; ajuhuma.

In luṅ: by "vṛddhi before sic in the parasmaipada," vṛddhi is made; thus, in the three of the first person: ahauṣīta; by "sic, abhyasta" and so on, jhi becomes jus, and before jus, guṇa: ahauṣṭāṃ, ahauṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ahoṣīḥ, ahauṣṭaṃ, ahauṣṭa. In the three of the last person: ahauṣaṃ, ahauṣa, ahauṣma.

In liṭ: "Bhīhrībhṛhubāṃślubacca": of bhī, hrī, bhṛ and hu, also as with ślu. Before a following liṭ, ām is optionally added to ñibhī, in fearing; hrī, in being ashamed; bhṛña, in bearing; and hu, in giving; and before ām too, reduplication and so on are made as with ślu. On the side with ām: juhavāṃcakāra, juhavāṃbabhūva, juhavāmāsa, and so on. And on the side where ām is not added, in the three of the first person: juhāva, juhuvatuḥ, juhuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: juhavitha, juhotha, juhuvathuḥ, juhuva. In the three of the last person: juhāva, juhava, juhuviva, juhuvima.

In luṭ, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on; thus: hotā, hotāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "not kṛt" and so on, it is lengthened; thus: hūyāta, hūyāstāṃ, hūyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on; thus: hoṣyati, hoṣyanti, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: ahoṣyata, ahoṣyatāṃ, ahoṣyana, and so on.

To the root listed as "ñibhī, in fearing," the ataṅ endings are likewise added, and the procedure, the change of śap to ślu and so on, is mostly like that of hu. In the singular of the first person of laṭ: bibheti. "Bhiyonnyatarasyāṃ": optionally for bhī. The letter ī of bhī is optionally changed to short i before a following sārvadhātuka that has a hal at the beginning and is called k- or ṅ-marked; thus, in the dual of the first person: bibhitaḥ, bibhītaḥ. In the plural, by "not of one ac" and so on, it is changed to yaṇ; thus: bibhyati. Deriving in the same way as those, in the three of the middle person: bibheṣe, bibhithaḥ, bibhithaḥ, bibhitha, bibhītha. In the three of the last person: bibhimi, bibhivaḥ, bibhīvaḥ, bibhimaḥ, bibhīmaḥ. In liṅ, by "optionally for bhī," ī is optionally changed to a short vowel; thus: bibhiyāta, bibhiyātāṃ, bibhiyuḥ, and so on; or bibhiyāta, bibhīyātāṃ, bibhīyuḥ, and so on.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: bibhetu, bibhitāta, bibhitāta, bibhītāṃ, bibhītāṃ, bibhyatu. In the three of the middle person: bibhihi, bibhīhi, bibhitāta, bibhītāta, bibhitaṃ, bibhitaṃ, bibhita, bibhīta. In the three of the last person: bibhayāni, bibhayāva, bibhayāma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of laṅ: abibheta, abibhitāṃ, abibhītāṃ, abibhyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: abibheḥ, abibhitaṃ, abibhītaṃ, abibhita, abibhita. In the three of the last person: abibhayaṃ, abibhiva, abibhīva, abibhima, abibhīma.

In luṅ, by "vṛddhi before sic in the parasmaipada," vṛddhi is made; thus, in the three of the first person: abhaiṣīta, abhaiṣṭāṃ, abhaiṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: abhaiṣīḥ, abhaiṣṭaṃ, abhaiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: abhaiṣaṃ, abhaiṣva, abhaiṣma.

In liṭ, ām is made optional by "bhī, hrī" and so on. On the side with ām: bibhayāṃcakāra, bibhayāṃbabhūva, bibhayāmāsa, and so on. And on the side where ām is not added, in the three of the first person: bibhāya, bibhyatuḥ, bibhyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: bibhayitha, bibhetha, bibhyathuḥ, bibhya. In the three of the last person: bibhāya, bibhaya, bibhyiva, bibhyima, bibhyima.

In luṭ, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on; thus: bhetā, bhetāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: bhīyāṅata, bhīyāstāṃ, bhiyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, guṇa is made; thus: bheṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: abhiṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "hrī, in being ashamed," the ataṅ endings are likewise added, and the procedure is mostly like the one just explained. In the three of the first person of laṭ: jihriti, śahrītaḥ, jihriyati. In the three of the middle person: jihreṣi, juhrīthaḥ, jahrītha. In the three of the last person: jihrīmi, jihrīvaḥ, jihrīmaḥ. In liṅ: jihrīyāta, jihrīyātāṃ, jihrīyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: jihretu, jihrītāta, jihrītāṃ, jihriyatu. In the three of the middle person: jihrīhi, jihrītāta, jihrītaṃ, jvihrītaṃ, jvihrīta. In the three of the last person: jihrayāṇi, jihrayāva, jihrayāma.
