In the three of the first person of laṅ: ajihreta, ajihrītāṃ, ajihrayuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ahraiṣāḥ, ahraiṣṭa, ahraiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: ajaṃhrayaṃ, ajihriva, ajihrīma.

In luṅ, vṛddhi is made before sic; thus, in the three of the first person: ahaiṣīta, ahraiṣṭai, ahraiṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ahraiṣīḥ, ahraiṣṭaṃ, ahraiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: ahraiṣaṃ, ahraiṣva, ahraiṣma.

In liṭ, ām is made optional; thus: jihrayāṃcakāra, ahralāṃbabhūva, jihralāmās, and so on; or else, ām not being added, in the three of the first person: jihrāya, jihriyathuḥ, jihriyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jihrayitha, jihretha, jihiyathuḥ, jihriya. In the three of the last person: jihrāya, jihriya, jihriyiva, jihriyima.

In luṭ, guṇa is made; thus: hretā, hretāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: hrīyāta, hrīyāstāṃ, hrīyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, guṇa is made; thus: hreṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: ahreṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "pṝ, in protecting and in filling," the ataṅ endings are likewise added. "Artipibartyośu": of arti and piparti also. Before the following suffix that has been changed to ślu, the reduplicated syllable of the roots ṛ, in going, and pṛ, in protecting, becomes it. In the singular of the first person of laṭ: la becomes tip. Śap in the agent. By "juhoti" and so on, śap is changed to ślu. Before ślu the root is reduplicated. By this sūtra, the reduplicated syllable takes it. Guṇa being made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on: pibarti.

"Udoṣṭyapūrbasya": uṭ for one whose preceding letter is a labial. The ṝt at the end of a root, when a labial precedes it, is changed to ut before a following suffix called k- or ṅ-marked, other than the us into which jhi is changed as jus. Thus, in the dual of the first person: pipūrtaḥ. In the plural: bipurti. Deriving in the same way as those, in the three of the middle person: piparṣvi, pipūrthaḥ, pipūrtha. In the three of the last person: pipūrvaḥ, pipūrmaḥ. In liṅ: bibūryāt, pipūryātvaṃ, pipūryāḥ, and so on.

In loṭ: by this sūtra, ṝ becomes ut; by "aṇ for ṛ, with r following," r; and by "of the penultimate," it is long. In the three of the first person: pipartu, pipūrtāta, pipūrtāṃ, pipuratu. In the three of the middle person: pipūrti, pipūrtāta, pipūrtaṃ, pibūrta. In the three of the last person: piparāṇi, pibarāva, piparrām. In the three of the first person of laṅ: apibaḥ, apipūrtāṃ, apiparuḥ. In the three of the middle person: apipaḥ, apipūrtaṃ. In the three of the last person: apiparaṃ, apibūrva, apibārma.

In luṅ, the iṭ of "beginning with val," and by "vṛddhi before sic in the parasmaipada," vṛddhi being made: apvaṝta, apariṣṭāṃ, apariṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, vṛddhi is made for those that are the occasion for vṛddhi, and for the others guṇa is made by "of ṛcchati and ṝt"; thus, in the three of the first person: papār, pabartuḥ, paparuḥ. In the three of the middle person: paparitha, papathuḥ, papar. In the three of the last person: bapāra, papara, papariva, paparima.

In luṭ, by "optionally after vṛ and ṝt," iṭ and īṭ are made optional; thus: baritā, baritāsi, and so on; or barītā, parītāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: by "ut for one whose preceding letter is a labial," ṝ becomes ut; by "aṇ for ṛ, with r following," r; and by "of the penultimate," it is changed to a long vowel; thus: pūryāta, pūryāstāṃ, pāryāsuḥ. In lṛṭ, by "vṛ, ṝt" and so on, iṭ and īṭ are made optional; thus: pariṣyata, and so on; or pariṣyata, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aparīṣyata, and so on; or aparīṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "pṛ, in protecting and in filling," the ataṅ endings are likewise added; since it differs slightly from pṝ, in the three of the first person of laṭ: piparti, pipṛtaḥ, piprati. In the three of the middle person: piparṣi, pipṛthaḥ, pipṛtha. In the three of the last person: piparmi, pipṛvaḥ, pipṛmaḥ. In liṅ: pipṛyāta, pipṛyātāṃ, pipṛyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: pipartu, pipṛtāta, pipṛtāṃ, piprati. In the three of the middle person: pipṛhi, pipṛtāta, pipṛtaṃ, pipṛta. In the three of the last person: piparṣaṇi, piparāva, piparāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: apipaḥ, apipṛtāṃ, apiparu. In the three of the middle person: apipaḥ, apipṛtaṃ, apipṛta. In the three of the last person: apiparaṃ, apipṛva, apipṛma.

In luṅ, vṛddhi is made; thus, in the three of the first person: apārṣīt, apāṣṭāṃ, apārṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: apārṣiḥ, aparṣṭaṃ, apārṣṭa. In the three of the last person: apārṣaṃ, apārṣa. In the three of the first person of liṭ: papāra, papratuḥ, papruḥ. In the three of the middle person: papatha, paprathuḥ, papra. In the three of the last person: paprara, papara, papriva, paprima. In luṭ, guṇa is made; thus: bartā, bartāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "śa, yak" and so on, it is changed to riṅ; thus: priyāta, priyātāṃ, priyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is added by "ṛt, han" and so on; thus: bariṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: apariṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ohāk, in abandoning," the ataṅ endings are likewise added. Deriving by the change of śap to ślu and so on, in the singular of the first person of laṭ: jahāti. "Jahāteśca": of jahāti also. The āt of jahāti, which is not called ghu, optionally becomes it before a following sārvadhātuka that has a hal at the beginning and is called k- or ṅ-marked. "Īhalyaghoḥ": ī before a hal, for one that is not ghu. The āt of roots called abhyasta that are not called ghu, and of the suffix śnā, is to be changed to ī before a following sārvadhātuka called k- or ṅ-marked. Thus, in the dual of the first person, it being made optional, by "of jahāti also," to take it, and by this sūtra to take ī: jahitaḥ, jahītaḥ. In the plural, by "at after an abhyasta," jh becomes at, and by "the āt of śnā and an abhyasta," the ā is dropped; thus: jahati. Deriving in the same way as those, in the three of the middle person: jahisi, jihithaḥ, jahīthaḥ, jahitha, jahītha. In the three of the last person: jahāmi, jahivaḥ, jahīvaḥ, jahimaḥ, jahīmaḥ.

"Lopo yi": elision before y. The āt of jahāti is elided before a following sārvadhātuka that has the letter y at its beginning; thus, in liṅ: jahyāta, jahyātā, jahyāḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: jahātu, jahītāta, jahītāta, jahitāṃ, jahītāṃ, jahatu.

"Ā ca hau": ā before hi also. Before the hi that replaces loṭ, jahāti optionally keeps its ā as it is; thus, in the singular of the middle person of loṭ, five forms arise: jahāhi, jahihi, jahīhi, jahitāta, jahītāta. In the dual and plural: jahitaṃ, jahītaṃ, jahīta, jahita. In the three of the last person: jahāni, jahāva, jahāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: ajahāta, ajahitāṃ, ajahītāṃ, ajahuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ajahāḥ, ajahitaṃ, ajahītaṃ, ajahita, ajahīta. In the three of the last person: ajahāṃ, ajahiva, ajahīva, ajahima, ajahīma.

In luṅ, sak and iṭ are given by "yam, ram, nam, and those ending in āt" and so on; thus: ahāsīta, ahāsīṣṭāṃ, ahāsiṣṭāṃ, ahāsiṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ there is reduplication; by "after āt, au for ṇal," the two ṇal become au; and before iṭ too, the elision of āt and so on are made; thus, in the three of the first person: jahau, jahatuḥ, jahuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jahātha, jahitha, jahathuḥ, jaha. In the three of the last person: jahau, jahiva, jahima. In luṭ: hātā, hātāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "e before liṅ," it is changed to e; thus: teyāt, heyāstāṃ, heyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: hāsyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: ahāsyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ṛ, in going," the ataṅ endings likewise apply. To ṛ, tip. Śap is changed to ślu. By "before ślu," reduplication. By "of arti and piparti also," the reduplicated syllable takes i. Deriving by the change to iy and so on by "of the reduplicated syllable, before a vowel not of like kind," in the three of the first person of laṭ: iyarti, iyṛtaḥ, iyrati. In the three of the middle person: iyarṣi, iyrathaḥ, iyṛtha. In the three of the last person: iyarme, iyṛvaḥ, iyṛmaḥ. In liṅ: iyṛyāta, iyṛyātāṃ, iyṛyuḥ, and so on. Likewise, in the three of the first person of loṭ: iyartu, iyṛtāta, ayṛtāṃ, iyratu. In the three of the middle person: iyṛhi, iyṛtāta, iyṛtaṃ, iyṛta. In the three of the last person: iyarāṇi, iyarāva, iyarāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: aiyaḥ, aiyṛtāṃ, aiyaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: aiyaḥ, aiyṛtaṃ, aiyṛta. In the three of the last person: aiyaraṃ, aiyṛva, aiyṛma.

In luṅ: by "also after sarti, śāsti and arti," cli is changed to aṅ. By "of ṛ and dṛś before aṅ," guṇa is made. By "āṭ for a root with initial ac," āṭ; by "also after āṭ," vṛddhi; by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, guṇa; and by "hal, dīp" and so on, the t is dropped; thus: ārata, āratāṃ, āran, and so on. Or else, by the cited rule "aṅ is optional after ṛ and sṛ," cli is changed to sic and vṛddhi is made; thus, in the three of the first person: ārṣīta, ārṣṭi, ārṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ārṣīḥ, āraṣṭaṃ, ārṣṭa. In the three of the last person: ārṣaṃ, ārṣva, ārṣma.

In liṭ the root is reduplicated. By "a for ṛ," the reduplicated syllable takes a. By "of ṛcchati and ṝt," guṇa is made before those that are not the occasion for vṛddhi, and vṛddhi before the two ṇal. Deriving by "like ak" and so on, in the three of the first person: āra, āratuḥ, aruḥ. In the three of the middle person: āritha, ārathuḥ, āra. In the three of the last person: āra, āriva, ārima. In luṭ, guṇa is made; thus: artā, artāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, guṇa is made by "guṇa for arti and for one with a conjunct at the beginning"; thus: aryāta, aryāstāṃ, aryāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ, by "after ṛt and han, before sya," iṭ is given, and guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on; thus: ariṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: āriṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ṇijir, in cleansing and in nourishing," the ataṅ endings are likewise added. "Ṇijāṃtrayāṇāṃ guṇaḥ ślo": of the three, ṇija and the rest, guṇa before ślu. The reduplicated syllable of the three, ṇijir, in cleansing; vijir, in becoming separate; and viṣḷ, in pervading, becomes guṇa before a following ślu. To ṇija: śap. By "juhoti" and so on, śap is changed to ślu. Before ślu, reduplication. By this sūtra, the reduplicated syllable takes guṇa. Deriving by "ku for cu" and so on: nenekte; by "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa; neniktaḥ, nenijati. In the three of the middle person: nenekṣi, nenikṭhaḥ, nenikṭha. In the three of the last person: nenijmi, nenijma, nenijvaḥ. In liṅ: nenijyāta, nenijyātāṃ, nenijyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: neniktu, neniktrata, neniktāṃ, nenijatu. In the three of the middle person: nenigdhi, with "after hu and jhal, hi becomes dhi" and "ku for cu"; neniktāta, neniktaṃ, nenikta.

"Nābhyastasyāci piti sārbaṅhātuke": not of an abhyasta, before a sārvadhātuka that begins with ac and is p-marked. Before a following sārvadhātuka that has an ac at its beginning and is called p-marked, the penultimate of an abhyasta does not become guṇa. Thus, in the three of the last person of loṭ: nenijāni, nenijāva, nenijāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: anenag, anenika, aneniktāṃ, anenijuḥ. In the three of the middle person: anenega, aneneka, aneniktaṃ, anenikta. In the three of the last person: anenijaṃ, nenijva, nenijma.

In luṅ, by "optionally for those marked ir," cli is changed optionally to aṅ or to sic. On the side of aṅ: anijata, anijatāṃ, anijan, and so on. And on the side of sic: by "vada, vraja" and so on, vṛddhi; for those with jhal at the beginning, by "after jhal, before jhal," the elision of sic; "ku for cu"; "before khar, car"; and the rule on substitutes and so on; deriving thus, in the three of the first person: anaikṭhita, anaikṣāṃ, anaiktuḥ. In the three of the middle person: anaikṣiḥ, anaiktaṃ, anaikta. In the three of the last person: anaikṣaṃ, anaikṣva, anaikṣma.

In the three of the first person of liṭ: ninija, ninejatuḥ, ninijuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ninekṭha, ninejitha, ninijuthuḥ, ninija. In the three of the last person: nineja, ninijiva, ninijima. In luṭ, guṇa is made by "ending in puk" and so on; thus: nektā, nektāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: nijyāta, nijyāstāṃ, nijyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: by "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa; by "ku for cu," j becomes g; by "before khar, car," g becomes k; and by the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed to ṣ; thus: nekṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: anektyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "vijir, in becoming separate," both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings apply, and the whole procedure, the change of śap to ślu and so on, is like the one just explained. In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: vevekti, veviktaḥ, vevijati. In the three of the middle person: vevekṣi, vevikṭhaḥ, vevikṭha. In the three of the last person: vevejī, vivijmi, vivijraḥ, vivijmaḥ. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: vevikte, vevijāte, vevijate. In the three of the middle person: vevikṭhe, vivijāthe, vivigdhve. In the three of the last person: vevije, vevijvahe, vevijmahe. In the ataṅ of liṅ: vevijyāta, vevijyātāṃ, vevijyuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, by "not at the end" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped and the rest brought in; thus: vevijīta, vevijītāṃ, vevijīran, and so on.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of loṭ: vevektu, veviktāta, veviktāṃ, vevijatu. In the three of the middle person: vevigdhi, veviktāta, veviktāta, vevikta. In the three of the last person: vevejāni, vevijāva, vevijāma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: veviktāṃ, vevijātāṃ, vevijatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: vevikṣva, vevijāthāṃ, vevijāgdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: vevijai, vevijāvahai, vevijāmahai.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ, guṇa is not made, by "not of an abhyasta, before a sārvadhātuka that begins with ac and is p-marked": avevega, aveviktāṃ, avevijuḥ. In the three of the middle person: avevega, aveveka, aveviktaṃ, avevikta. In the three of the last person: avevijaṃ, avevijva, avevijma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: avevikta, avevijātāṃ, avevijata. In the three of the middle person: avevikṭhaḥ, avevijāthāṃ, avevikdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: aveviji, avevijvahi, avevijmahi.

In the ataṅ of luṅ, by "optionally for those marked ir," the change of cli to aṅ and to sic is made optional; thus, on the side of aṅ: avijata, avijatāṃ, avijana, and so on.

On the side of sic: by "vada, vraja" and so on, vṛddhi; for those with jhal at the beginning, by "after jhal, before jhal," the elision of sic; "ku for cu"; and the rule on substitutes and so on; deriving thus, in the three of the first person: avaikṣīta, avaikṣāṃ, avaikṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: avaikṣīḥ, avaiktaṃ, avaikta. In the three of the last person: avaiktaṃ, avaikṣva, avaikṣma.

In the taṅ, by "before liṅ and sic in the ātmanepada," neither vṛddhi nor guṇa is made. For those with jhal at the beginning, by "after jhal, before jhal," the elision of sic; "ku for cu"; and the rule on substitutes and so on; deriving thus, in the three of the first person: avikta, avikṣātāṃ, avikṣata. In the three of the middle person: avikṣāḥ, avikṣāthāṃ, avigdhāṃ. In the three of the last person: avikṣi, avikṣvahi, avikṣmahi.

In liṭ, deriving by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: viveja, vivijatuḥ, vivijuḥ. In the three of the middle person: vivakṭha, vivejitha, vivijathuḥ, vivija. In the three of the last person: viveja, vivijiva, vivijima. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: vivije, vivijāte, vivijire. In the three of the middle person: vivijiṣe, vivijāthe, vivijidhve, vivijiḍhe. In the three of the last person: vivije, vivijivahe, vivijimahe.

In luṭ: by "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa; by "ku for cu," j becomes g; and by "before khar, car," it is changed to k; thus, in the ataṅ: vektāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: vektā, vektāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ there is only the form that introduces y: vijyāta, vijyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: by "ku for cu," j becomes g; by "before khar, car," g becomes k; and by the rule on substitutes and so on, it is changed to ṣ; thus: vikṣīṣṭa, vikṣīyāstāṃ, vikṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: by "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa; by "ku for cu," j becomes g; before khar, car; and by the rule on substitutes and so on, in the ataṅ: vakṣyataṃ, and so on; and in the taṅ: vekṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: avekṣyat, and so on; and in the taṅ: avekṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "viṣḷ, in pervading," the ataṅ endings likewise apply. Śap is changed to ślu; reduplication; and by "of the three, ṇija and the rest, guṇa before ślu," the reduplicated syllable takes guṇa; deriving thus, in the three of the first person of laṭ: veveṣṭi, viveṣṭaḥ, veviṣati. In the three of the middle person: vevekṣi, viviṣṭhaḥ, viviṣṭha. In the three of the last person: veveṣmi, veviṣvaḥ, veviṣmaḥ. In liṅ: veviṣyāta, veviṣyātāṃ, veviṣyāḥ. In the three of the first person of loṭ: veveṣṭu, veviṣṭāta, veviṣṭāṃ, veviṣatu. In the three of the middle person: veviḍḍhi; by "after hu and jhal, hi becomes dhi"; by "jhal at the end" and so on, ṣ becomes ḍ; by "with ṣṭu, ṣṭu," dh becomes ḍh; viviṣṭāta, viviṣṭa. In the three of the last person: veviṣāṇi, veviṣāva, veviṣāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: aveveḍ, aveveṭ, aveviṣṣāṃ, aveviṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: aveveḍ, aveviṭ, aveviṣṭaṃ, aveviṣṭa. In the three of the last person: aveviṣva, aveviṣma.

In luṅ, by "marked ḷ" and so on, the change of cli to aṅ and to ksa is made optional; thus, on the side of aṅ: aviṣata, aviṣatāṃ, aviṣana, and so on. And on the side of ksa: by "before s, ṣ and ḍh become k," ṣ becomes k, and deriving by the rule on substitutes and so on: avikṣata, avikṣatāṃ, avikṣana, and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: viveṣa, viviṣatuḥ, viviṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: viveṣṭha, viveṣitha, viviṣathuḥ, vivitha. In the three of the last person: viveṣa, viveṣiva, viviṣima. In luṭ: veṣṭā, veṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: viṣyāta, viṣyāstāṃ, viṣyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: by "ending in puk" and so on, guṇa; by "before s, ṣ and ḍh become k," ṣ becomes k; and by the rule on substitutes and so on, s is changed to ṣ; thus: vekṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: avekṣyeta, and so on.

To the root listed as "jāna, in being born," the ataṅ endings are likewise added. The change of śap to ślu and so on being made, in the singular of the first person of laṭ: jajanti. "Janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ": of jana, sana and khana, before san and jhal. The ṭi of jana, in being born, and of sana and khana, in devotion, becomes āt before the suffix san and before a following suffix that has a jhal at the beginning and is called k- or ṅ-marked. Thus, in the dual: jajātaḥ. In the plural: by "at after an abhyasta," at; by "gama, hana, jana" and so on, the penultimate is dropped; by "ś and the c-class for s and the t-class," n becomes ñ; and j and ñ combining are made jñ; thus: jajñati. Deriving in the same way as those, in the three of the middle person: jajaniṣi; by "after īṭ and jana, before dh too," iṭ; jajāthamaḥ, jajātha. In the three of the last person: jajanmi, jajanvaḥ, jajanmaḥ. In liṅ, by "optional before y," the ṭi is optionally made āt; thus: jajāyāta, jajāyātāṃ, jajāyuḥ, and so on; or jajanyata, jajanyātāṃ, jajanyuḥ, and so on.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: jajantu, jajātāta, jajātāṃ, jajñatu. In the three of the middle person: jajāhi, jajātāta, jajātaṃ, jajāta. In the three of the last person: jajanāni, jajanāva, jajanāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: ajajana, ajajātāṃ, ajajñuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ajajana, ajajātaṃ, ajajata. In the three of the last person: ajajanaṃ, jajanā, ajajanma. In luṅ, iṭ is given; thus: ajanīta, ajanoṣṭāṃ, ajaniṣuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of liṭ: jajāna, jajñatuḥ, jajñuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jajanitha, jajñathuḥ, jajña. In the three of the last person: jajāna, jajñiva, jajñima. In luṭ, the iṭ of "beginning with val" is given; thus: janitā, janitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "optional before y," the change to ā is made optional; thus: jāyāta, jāyāstāṃ, jāyāsuḥ, and so on; or janyāta, janyāstāṃ, janyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given; thus: janiṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ too: ajaniṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ḍudāña, in giving," both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings apply. Śap becoming ślu, reduplication and so on being made, in the singular of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: dadāti. In the dual and plural: by "the āt of śnā and an abhyasta," the ā is dropped, and by "before khar, car," d becomes t, and so on; thus: dattaḥ, dadati. Likewise, in the three of the middle person: dadāsi, datthaḥ, dattha. In the three of the last person: dadāmi, dadvaḥ, dadvaḥ. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: datte, dadāte, dadāte. In the three of the middle person: datse, dadātha, daddye. In the three of the last person: dade, dadvahe, dadmahe.

In the ataṅ of liṅ, by "śnā, abhyasta" and so on, the ā is dropped and y brought in; thus: dadyāta, dadyātāṃ, dadyuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, by "not at the end" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped, and by "śnā, abhyasta" and so on, the ā is dropped; thus: dadīta, dadīyātvaṃ, dadīran, and so on.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of loṭ: dadātu, dadāta, dattāṃ, dadatu. In the three of the middle person: dehaṃ, dattāta, dattaṃ, datta. In the three of the last person: dadāni, dadāva, dadāma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: dattvaṃ, dadātāṃ, dadatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: datmā, dadāthāṃ, daddhāṃ. In the three of the last person: dadai, dadāvahai, dadāmahai.

That form is derived by "e for ghu and as before hi, and also elision of the reduplicated syllable." In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: adadāta, adattāṃ, adaduḥ. In the three of the middle person: adadāḥ, adattaṃ, adatta. In the three of the last person: adadāṃ, adadā, adadma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: adatta, adadātaṃ, adadata. In the three of the middle person: adatthāḥ, adadāthāṃ, adaddhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: adadi, adadvahi, adadmahi.

In the ataṅ of luṅ, sic is dropped by "gāti, sthā, ghu, pā, bhū" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: adāta, adātāṃ, aduḥ. In the three of the middle person: adāḥ, adātāṃ, adāta. In the three of the last person: adāṃ, adāva, adāma. In the taṅ, by "of sthā and ghu, it too," ā becomes i; and before sic, which is kit, and before those with jhal at the beginning, the elision of sic and so on are made by "after a short form" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: adita, adiṣātāṃ, adiṣāta. In the three of the middle person: adithāḥ, adiṣāthāṃ, adiddhaṃ. In the three of the last person: adiṣi, adiṣvahi, adiṣmahi.

In liṭ, the two ṇal become au, and before iṭ too, by "elision of āt," the ā is dropped; thus, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: dadau, dadatuḥ, daduḥ. In the three of the middle person: daditha, dadātha, dadathuḥ, dada. In the three of the last person: dadau, dadiva, dadima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: dade, dadāte, dadire. In the three of the middle person: dadiṣa, dadāthe, dadidhe, dadiḍhe. In the three of the last person: dade, dadivahe, dadimahe.

In the ataṅ of luṭ: dādā, dātāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: dātā, dātāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, by "e before liṅ," it is changed to e; thus: deyāta, deyāstāṃ, deyāsuḥ, and so on; and in the taṅ: dāyīṣṭa, dāsīyāstāṃ, dāsāṃran, and so on. In lṛṭ too there is no other operation; thus, in the ataṅ: dāsyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: dāsyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: adāsyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: adāsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ḍudhāña, in holding and in nourishing," likewise takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. Śap being changed to ślu, in the singular of the first person of laṭ: dadhrati. "Dedhastathośca": of dadha, before t and th also. Ḍudhāña is reduplicated, and by "of the reduplicated syllable too," the first dh is changed to d, giving dadhā; by "elision of the āt of śnā and an abhyasta," the ā is dropped. When the letter t or the letter th follows what is called dadha, and, by the word "also," y or dhv, that d is changed to dh again. Thus, in the dual of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: dhattaḥ. In the plural of the first person: dadhati. Likewise, in the three of the middle person: dadhāsi, dhatthaḥ, dhattha. In the three of the last person: dadhāmi, dadhāmi, dattvami, dadtvaḥ, dattmaḥ. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: thatte, dadhāte, daṅhata. In the three of the middle person: dhatse, dadhāthe, dhadthā. In the three of the last person: dadhe, dadhāhe, dadhmahe. In the ataṅ of liṅ, by "śnā" and so on, the ā is dropped; thus: dadhyāta, dadhyātāṃ, dadhyuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, by "not at the end" and so on, the s is dropped, and by "śnā" and so on, the ā is dropped; thus: dadhīta, dadhītāṃ, dadhīran, and so on.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of loṭ: dadhātu, dadhāta, dattāṃ, dadhatu. In the three of the middle person: dhehi, dhattāta, dhettaṃ, dhatti. In the three of the last person: dadhāni, dadhāpa, dadhāma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: dhattaṃ, dadhātāṃ. In the three of the middle person: dhatsra, dadhāthāṃ, daddhāṃ. In the three of the last person: dadho, dadhāvahai, dadhāmahai.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: adadhāta, adadhu. In the three of the middle person: adadhāma, adhattaṃ, adhatta. In the three of the last person: adadhāṃ, adadhva, adhma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: adhatta, adadhātāṃ, adadhata. In the three of the middle person: adhatthāḥ, adadhāthāṃ, adhaddhāṃ. In the three of the last person: adadhi, adadhāhi, adadhāhi.

In the ataṅ of luṅ, sic is dropped by "gāti, sthā, ghu" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: adhāta, adhātāṃ, adhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: adhāḥ, adhātaṃ, adhāta. In the three of the last person: adhaṃ, adhāma. In the taṅ, by "of sthā and ghu, it too," sic is kit and ā is changed to i; and by "after a short form too," the elision of sic and so on are made; thus, in the three of the first person: adhita, adhiṣātāṃ, adhiṣata. In the three of the middle person: adhithāḥ, adhithāṃ, adhidhāṃ. In the three of the last person: adhiṣi, adhiṣahi, adhiṣmahi.

In liṭ, before iṭ too, by "elision of āt," the a is dropped; thus, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: dadhau, dadhatuḥ, dadhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: dadhitha, dadhātha, dadhāthuḥ, dadha. In the three of the last person: dadhau, dadhiva, dadhima. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: dadhe, dadhāte, dadhaṃre. In the three of the middle person: dadhiṣe, dadhāthe, dadhaṃdhe, dadhiḍhe. In the three of the last person: dadhe, dadhivahe, dadhimahe.

In luṭ there is no other procedure; thus, in the ataṅ: dhātāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: dhātā, dhātāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, the change to e by "e before liṅ" and so on being made: dheyāta, dheyāstaṃ, dheyāsuḥ. In the taṅ: dhāsīṣṭa, dhāsīyāstāṃ, dhāsīran, and so on. In the ataṅ of lṛṭ: dhāsyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: dhāsyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: ate, and so on; and in the taṅ: adhāsyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "bhṛña, in holding and in nourishing," both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings likewise apply. "Bhṛñāmit": it for bhṛña and the rest. Bhṛña and the rest are the three, ḍubhṛña, in holding; māṅ, in measuring; and ohāṅ, in going; before ślu, their reduplicated syllable is to be changed to it. Śap becomes ślu; reduplication; and by this sūtra the reduplicated syllable is changed to it, and so on; thus, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: bibharti, bibhṛtaḥ, bibhrati. In the three of the middle person: bibharṣi, bibhṛthaḥ, bibhṛtha. In the three of the last person: bibharmi, bibhṛvaḥ, bibhṛma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: bibhṝte, bibhrāte, bebhrate. In the three of the middle person: bibhṛṣe, bibhrāthe, bibhṛdhve. In the three of the last person: bibhre, bibhṛvahe, bibhṛmahe.

In the ataṅ of liṅ: bibhṛyāta, bibhṛyātāṃ, bibhṛyuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, by "not at the end" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped, and by "ik before ac," yaṇ is made; thus: bibhṛta, bibhrīyātāṃ, bibhrīṅan, and so on.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of loṭ: bibhartu, bibhṛtāta, bibhṛtāṃ, bibhratu. In the three of the middle person: bibhṛhi, bibhṛtāta, bibhṛtaṃ, bibhṛta. In the three of the last person: bibharāṇi, bebharāva, bibharāma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: bibhṛtāṃ, bibhrātāṃ, bibhratāṃ. In the three of the middle person: bibhṛṣa, bibhrāthāṃ, bibhrādhāṃ. In the three of the last person: bibharai, dibharāvahai, bibharāmahai.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: abibhaḥ, abibhṛtāṃ, abibharuḥ. In the three of the middle person: abibhaḥ, abibhṛtaṃ, abibhṛta. In the three of the last person: abibharaṃ, abibhrava, abibhṛma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: abibhṛta, abibhrātāṃ, abibhrata. In the three of the middle person: abibhṛthaḥ, abibhrāthāṃ, abibhṛdhāṃ. In the three of the last person: abibhṛ, abibhṛvahi, abibhṛmahi.

In the ataṅ of luṅ, by "vṛddhi before sic in the parasmaipada," vṛddhi is made; thus, in the three of the first person: abhārṣīta, abhārṣṭaṃ, abhārṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: abhārṣīḥ, abhārṣṭaṃ, abhārṣṭa. In the three of the last person: abhārṣaṃ, abhārṣa, abhārṣma. In the taṅ, since by "after ṛ too" sic is kit, vṛddhi, guṇa and so on are not made; and for those with jhal at the beginning, by "after a short form," the elision of sic and so on are made; thus, in the three of the first person: abhīta, abhṛṣātāṃ, abhṛṣata. In the three of the middle person: abhṛthāḥ, abhṛṣāthāṃ, abhṛdhāṃ. In the three of the last person: abhṛṣi, abhṛṣahi.

In liṭ, by "of bhī, hrī, bhṛ and hu, as with ślu, too," the reduplicated syllable takes it, and ām is made optional. On the side with ām: bibharāṃcakāra, bibharāṃbabhūla, bibharāmāsa, and so on. Or else the root is reduplicated, and by "a for ṛ," the ṛ of the reduplicated syllable is changed to a; thus, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: babhār, babhratuḥ, babhruḥ. In the three of the middle person: babhartha, babhrathuḥ, babhra. In the three of the last person: babhār, babhar, babhṛva, babhṛma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: babhre, babhrate, babhṛre. In the three of the middle person: babhṛṣe, babhrathe, babhṛdhe. In the three of the last person: babhṛ, babhṛvahe, babhṛmahe.

In luṭ, the iṭ of the cited rule is made optional by "bhṛ, ṣṭu" and so on; thus, in the ataṅ: bharitā, bharitāsi, and so on; or bhartā, bhartāsi, and so on. Likewise, in the taṅ: bharitā, bhatitāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, by "riṅ before śa, yak and liṅ," it is changed to riṅ; thus: bhriyāta, bhṛyāstāṃ, bhṛyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, by "after ṛ too," guṇa is not made: bhṛṣīṣṭa, bhṛṣīyāstāṃ, bhṛṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ, by "after ṛt and han, before sya," iṭ is given and guṇa is made; thus, in the ataṅ: bhariṣyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: bhariṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: abhariṣyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: abhariṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "māṅ, in measuring, and also in sound," the taṅ endings are added. Śap becomes ślu; reduplication; by "it for bhṛña and the rest," the reduplicated syllable becomes mi; by "ī before a hal, for those that are not ghu," final ī before those that are k- or ṅ-marked and have a hal at the beginning; and before those with an ac at the beginning, by "the āt of śnā and an abhyasta," the elision of ā and so on are made; thus, in the three of the first person of laṭ: mimīte, mimāte, mimate. In the three of the middle person: mimīṣe, mimātha, mamādhā. In the three of the last person: mimi, mimīvahe, mimīmahe. In liṅ, by "not at the end" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped, and by "śnā" and so on, the ā is dropped: mimīta, mimīyāstāṃ, mimīran, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: mimītāṃ, mimītāṃ, mimatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: mimīṣa, mimāthāṃ, mimīdhāṃ. In the three of the last person: mimai, mimāvahai, mimāmahai. In the three of the first person of laṅ: amimīta, amimītāṃ, amimata, amimātāṃ, amimata. In the three of the middle person: amimīthāḥ, amimāthāṃ, amimīdhāṃ. In the three of the last person: amime, amimīvahi, amimīmahi.

In luṅ there is only the form that introduces the s of sic; thus, in the three of the first person: amāsta, amāsātāṃ, amāsata. In the three of the middle person: amāsthāḥ, amasāthāṃ, amādhāṃ. In the three of the last person: amasi, amāsvahi, amāsmahi. In liṭ, before iṭ too, by "elision of āt," the ā is dropped; thus, in the three of the first person: mame, mamāte, mamāre. In the three of the middle person: mamiṣe, mamāthe, mamidhāṃ. By "before dh too," sic is dropped. In the three of the last person: mame, mamihe, mamimahe. In luṭ: mātā, mātāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: māsīṣṭa, māsīyāstāṃ, māsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: māsyate, and so on; and in lṛṅ: amāsyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ohāṅ, in going," the taṅ endings are likewise added. By "ślu," śap becomes ślu; the root is reduplicated; by "cu for ku and h," h becomes jh; by "car for the reduplicated syllable too," jh becomes j; by "it for bhṛña and the rest," the reduplicated syllable takes it; before those called k- or ṅ-marked that have a hal at the beginning, by "ī before a hal, for those that are not ghu," final ī; and before those with an ac at the beginning, by "śnā, abhyasta" and so on, the ā is dropped; thus, in the three of the first person of laṭ: jihīte, jahāte, jahate. In the three of the middle person: jihīṣe, jihīthe, jihādhe. In the three of the last person: jihe, jihīvahe. In liṅ, by "not at the end" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped, and by "śnā" and so on, the ā is dropped; thus: jihīta, jihīyātāṃ, ṅihīran, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: jihītāṃ, jihātāṃ, jihatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: jihīṣa, jihāthāṃ, jihāṅhāṃ. In the three of the last person: jihai, jihāvahai, jihāvahai, jihāmahai. In the three of the first person of laṅ: ajihīta, ajihātāṃ, ajihata. In the three of the middle person: ajihīthāḥ, ajihāthāṃ, ajihīdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: ajihi, ajihīvati, ajihīmati.

In luṅ there is only the form that introduces the s of sic; thus, in the three of the first person: ahāsta, ahāsātāṃ, ahīsata. In the three of the middle person: ahāsthāḥ, ahāsāthāṃ, ahādhāṃ. In the three of the last person: ahāsi, ahāsvahi, atāsmahi. In liṭ, there is reduplication; by "short for the reduplicated syllable," it is changed to a short vowel; by "cu for ku and h," h becomes jh; by "car for the reduplicated syllable too," jh becomes j; and before iṭ too, by "elision of āt," the ā is dropped; thus, in the three of the first person: jahe, jahāte, jahire. In the three of the middle person: jahiṣe, jahāthe, jahidhve, jahiḍhve. In the three of the last person: jahe, jahivahe, jahimahe. In the benedictive liṅ: hāsīṣṭa, hāsīyāstāṃ, hāsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: hāsyate, and so on; and in lṛṅ: ahāsyata, and so on.

"Iti pāṇinibyakaraṇasya sūtrātahrādayaḥsamāptāṃ": that is, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, hu and the rest are complete. With these, from the work called The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down in the form of notes the meaning of the text and its commentary, the procedures, the illustrative examples and so on, of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the rough account of the procedures, with the general rules and the exceptions, for applying laṭ and the rest to juhoti and the others, for which the śap that has the sense of the agent is changed to ślu, is for the present complete.

Now I shall explain the procedures for divu and the rest, which take śyan in the sense of the agent. To the root listed as "divu, in playing, in desiring to win, in transactions, in delighting, in shining, in praising, in beauty, and in going," the ataṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are added. "Dipādibhyaḥ śyan": after diva and the rest, śyan. After the roots divu and the rest, before following sārvadhātukas, śyan occurs in place of the śap that has the sense of the agent; its n serves the accent, and its ś marks it as ś-marked. To diva, śyan; the marker letters are dropped, and by "of the penultimate too," it is changed to a long vowel; thus, in the three of the first person of laṭ: dīvyati, dīvyataḥ, dīvyanti. In the three of the middle person: dīvyasi, dīvyathaḥ, dīvyatha. In the three of the last person: dīvyāmi, dīvyāpaḥ, dīvyāmaḥ.

In liṅ, by "after at, iy for y," y is changed to iy, and deriving by "elision of v and y before val" and so on, in the three of the first person: dīvyeta, dīvyetāṃ, dīvyeyumaḥ. In the three of the middle person: dīvyeḥ, dīvyetāṃ, dīvyeta. In the three of the last person: dīvyayaṃ, dīvyeva, dīvyema. In the three of the first person of loṭ: dīvyatu, dīvyatāta, dīvyatāṃ, dīvyantu. In the three of the middle person: dīvya, dīvyatāta, dīvyataṃ, dīvyata. In the three of the last person: dīvyani, dīvyani, dīvyāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: adīvyata, adīvyatāṃ, adīvyan. In the three of the middle person: adīvyaḥ, adīvyataṃ, adīvyata. In the three of the last person: adīvyi; by "after at, hi," hi is dropped; adīvyāva, adīvyāma.

In luṅ, the iṭ of "beginning with val" is given, and guṇa is made by "ending in puk" and so on; thus: adivīta, adeviṣṭāṃ, adeviṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, deriving by reduplication of the root and so on, in the three of the first person: dideva, didivtuḥ, didivuḥ. In the three of the middle person: didevitha, didevathuḥ, didiva. In the three of the last person: dideva, didiviva, didivama. In luṭ, iṭ is given; thus: devitā, devitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "of the penultimate too," it is changed to a long vowel; thus: dīvyata, dīvyāstāṃ, dīvyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ of "beginning with val," and guṇa is made by "ending in puk" and so on; thus: deviṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ.

To the root listed as "in sewing," the ataṅ endings are likewise applied, and since the whole procedure is like the one just explained, in laṭ: sīvyati, and so on; in liṅ: sīvyeti, and so on; in liṅ: sīvyeta, and so on; in loṭ: sīvyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: asīvyata, and so on. In luṅ, the iṭ of "beginning with val," and guṇa is made by "ending in puk" and so on; thus: asevīta, asevīṣṭāṃ, aseviṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, reduplication and so on being made, in the three of the first person: siṣeva, siṣivtuḥ, siṣivuḥ. In the three of the middle person: siṣivitha, siṣivathuḥ, siṣivaḥ. In the three of the last person: siṣiva, siṣiviva, siṣivima. In luṭ, iṭ and guṇa are made; thus: sevitā, sevitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "of the penultimate too," it is changed to a long vowel; thus: sīvyāta, sīvyāstāṃ, sīvyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ of "beginning with val," and guṇa by "ending in puk" and so on, being made: seviṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aseviṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "nṛtī, in moving the body," the ataṅ endings are likewise added. In laṭ: nṛtyati, and so on; in liṅ: nṛtyeta, and so on; in loṭ: nṛtyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: anṛtyata, and so on. In luṅ, the iṭ of "beginning with val," and guṇa by "ending in puk" and so on, being made: anartīta, anartiṣṭāṃ, anartiṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, reduplication and so on being made, in the three of the first person: nanarta, nanṛtatuḥ, nanṛtuḥ. In the three of the middle person: nanarti, nanṛtathuḥ, nanṛta. In the three of the last person: nanarta, nanṛtiva, nanṛtima. In luṭ, iṭ is given; thus: nartitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: nṛtyāta, nṛtyāstāṃ, nṛdyāsuḥ, and so on.

"Señasici kṛtacṛtachṝdatṛdanṛtaḥ": after kṛt, cṛt, chṛd, tṛd and nṛt, before an s that is not sic. Before an ārdhadhātuka that has the letter s at its beginning and is not sic, following kṛtī, in cutting; cṛtī, in harming; u-chṛdir, in shining; u-tṛdir, in harming; and nṛtī, in moving the body, iṭ optionally occurs. Thus, in lṛṭ, on the side where iṭ is given: nartiṣyati, and so on; and on the side without iṭ: nartsyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: anartiṣyata, and so on; or anartsyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "trasī, in being afraid," the ataṅ endings are added. By "bhrāśa, bhlāśa, klamu, kramu, trasī" and so on, śap and śyan are made optional; thus, in laṭ: and so on; or trasyati, and so on. In liṅ: traseta, and so on; or trasyeta, and so on. In loṭ: trasatu, and so on; or trasyatu, and so on. In laṅ: atrasata, and so on; or atrasyata, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, and vṛddhi is made by "vada, vraja" and so on; thus: atrāsīta, atrāsiṣṭāṃ, atrāsiṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, before those other than the two ṇal, by "optional for jṝ, bhramu and trasa," the elision of the reduplicated syllable and so on are made optional; thus, in the three of the first person: tatrāsa, tatrasatuḥ, tresatuḥ, tatrasuḥ, tresuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tatrasitha, tresitha, tretrasathuḥ, tresathuḥ, tatrasa, tresa. In the three of the last person: tatrāsa, tatrasa, tatrasiva, tresiva, tatrasima, tresima. In luṭ, iṭ is given; thus: trasitā, srasitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: trasyāstaṃ, trasyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ of "beginning with val" is given; thus: trasiṣyati, and so on. In lṛṅ: atrasiṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "jṝṣa, in the decline of youth," the ataṅ endings are likewise added. By "it for the ṝt of a root," ṛ becomes it; by "aṇ for ṛ, with r following," r; and by "of the penultimate too," it is changed to a long vowel, and so on; thus, in laṭ: jīryati, and so on; in liṅ: jīryita, and so on; in loṭ: jīryatu, and so on; and in laṅ: ajīryata, and so on. In luṅ, by "jṝ, stambhu, mrucu" and so on, the change of cli to aṅ and to sic is made optional. On the side of aṅ, guṇa is made by "guṇa for ṛ and dṛś before aṅ"; thus: ajarata, ajaratāṃ, ajarana, and so on. On the side of sic, iṭ is given, and vṛddhi is made by "vṛddhi before sic" and so on; thus: ajārṛta, ajāriṣṭāṃ, ajāriṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ: reduplication; a for ṛ; vṛddhi before the two ṇal; and before the others, by "optional for jṝ, bhramu and trasa," the elision of the reduplicated syllable is optional, and guṇa is made by "of ṛcchati and ṝt"; thus, in the three of the first person: jajāra, jeratuḥ, jajaratuḥ, jeruḥ, jajaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: jeritha, jajaritha, jerathuḥ, jajarathuḥ, jera, jajara. In the three of the last person: jajāra, jajara, jeriva, jajariva, jerima, jajarima. In luṭ, by "optionally after vṛ and ṝt," iṭ and īṭ are made optional; thus: jaritū, jaritāsi, and so on; or jarītā, jarītāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "it for the ṝt of a root," the change to it and so on being made: jīryāta, jīryāstāṃ, jīryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by "vṛ, ṝt" and so on, iṭ and īṭ are made optional; thus: jariṣyati, and so on; or jarīṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: ajariṣyata, and so on; or ajarīṣyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "śo, in making thin," the ataṅ endings are likewise added. "Otaḥ śyani": of ot, before śyan. The ot at the end of a root is to be elided before a following śyan. To śo, śyan; by this sūtra the o is dropped; thus, in laṭ: śyati, and so on; in liṅ: śyeta, and so on; in loṭ: śyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: aśyata, and so on.

In luṅ: before what does not fall within the domain of the ś-marked, by "āt for ec," e becomes āt. By "optionally after ghrā, dheṭ, śā, chā and sā," the elision of sic; and by "yam, ram, nam and those ending in āt," sak is optional. Sak and iṭ being given: aśāsīta, aśāsīṣṭaṃ, aśāsīṣuḥ, and so on. And on the side where sic is dropped, in the three of the first person: aśāt, aśātāṃ, aśuḥ. After āt, jhi becomes jus, and by "not at the end of a word" and so on, the following form. In the three of the middle person: aśāḥ, aśātaṃ, aśāta. In the three of the last person: aśā, aśāva, aśāma. In liṭ, the two ṇal become au, and before iṭ too, by "elision of āt," deriving by the elision of ā and so on, in the three of the first person: śaśau, śaśatuḥ, śaśuḥ. In the three of the middle person: śaśitha, śāśātha, śaśathuḥ, śaśa. In the three of the last person: śaśau, śaśiva, śaśima. In luṭ: śātā, śātāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: śāyāta, śāyāstāṃ, śāyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: śāsyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: aśāsyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "cho, in cutting," the ataṅ endings likewise apply, and the whole procedure is like that of śo. In laṭ: chyati, and so on; in liṅ: chyet, and so on; in loṭ: chyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: achyata, and so on. In luṅ, on the side with sak and iṭ: achāsīta, achāsiṣṭāṃ, achāsiṣuḥ, and so on; and on the side where sic is dropped, in the three of the first person: achāta, achātāṃ, achuḥ. In the three of the middle person: achāḥ, achātaṃ, achāta. In the three of the last person: achāṃ, achāva, achāma. In the three of the first person of liṭ: cachau, cachatuḥ, cachuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cachitha, cachātha, cachāthuḥ, cacha. In the three of the last person: cachau, cachiva, cachima. In luṭ: chātā, chātāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: chāyāta, chāyāstā, chāyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: chāsyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: achāsyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "ṣo, in bringing to an end," the ataṅ endings are likewise added, and since the whole procedure is like the two just explained, in laṭ: syati, and so on; in liṅ: syeta, and so on; in loṭ: syatu, and so on; and in laṅ: asyata, and so on. In luṅ, on the side where sak and iṭ are given: asāsīta, asāsiṣṭāṃ, asāsiṣuḥ, and so on. On the side where sic is dropped, in the three of the first person: asāta, asātāṃ, asuḥ. In the three of the middle person: asāḥ, asātaṃ, asāta. In the three of the last person: asāṃ, asāva, asāma. In the three of the first person of liṭ: sasau, sasatuḥ, sasuḥ. In the three of the middle person: sasitha, sasātha, sasathuḥ, sasa. In the three of the last person: sasau, sasiva, sasima. In luṭ: sātā, sātāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "e before liṅ," it is changed to e; thus: seyāta, seyāstāṃ, seyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: sāsyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: asāsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "do, in cutting," likewise takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: tyati, and so on; in liṅ: dyeta, and so on; in loṭ: tyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: adyata, and so on. In luṅ there is only the elision of sic, by "gāti, sthā, ghu" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: adāta, adātāṃ, aduḥ. In the three of the middle person: adāḥ, adātaṃ, atāta. In the three of the last person: adāṃ, adāva, adāma. In the three of the first person of liṭ: dadau, dadatuḥ; it is said that in luṅ here, although the root ends in āt, sak and iṭ do not apply; daduḥ. In the three of the middle person: daditha, dadātha, dadathuḥ, dada. In the three of the last person: dadau, dadiva, dadima. In luṭ: dātā, dātāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "e before liṅ," it is changed to e; thus: deyāta, deyāstāṃ, deyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: dāsyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: adāsyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "rādha, in being accomplished," the ataṅ endings are likewise added. In laṭ: rādhyati, and so on; in liṅ: rādhyeta, and so on; in loṭ: rādhyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: arādhyata, and so on. In luṅ, for those with jhal at the beginning, by "after jhal, before jhal," sic is dropped, and deriving by "before khar, car" and so on: arātsīta, arāthāṃ, arātsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: arātsīḥ, arāttaṃ, atātta. In the three of the last person: arātsaṃ, arātsā, arātsā.

"Rādhauhiṅsāyāṃ": of rādhi, in the sense of harming. When rādhi is used in the sense of harming, then before the others, apart from the two ṇal of liṭ, the elision of the reduplicated syllable, the change to e and so on are made optional; but in the sense of being accomplished there is no elision. In the three of the first person of liṭ: rarādha, rarādhatuḥ, redhatuḥ, rarādhuḥ, redhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: rarādhitha, redhitha, rarādhathuḥ, redhathuḥ, rarādha, redha. In the three of the last person: rarādha, rarādhiva, redhiva, rarādhima, redhima. In luṭ, by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh, and by "jhaṣ" and so on, dh is made d; thus: rāddhā, raddhāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: rādhyāta, rāddhyāstāṃ, rāddhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by "before khar, car," dh is changed to t; thus: rātsyāti, and so on; and in lṛṅ: arātsyata, and so on.

To the root listed as "sādha, in accomplishing," the ataṅ endings are likewise added; apart from the difference that in liṭ the reduplicated syllable is not elided, all its operations are like those of rādha. In laṭ: sādhyati, and so on; in liṅ: sādhyeta, and so on; in loṭ: sādhyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: asādhyata, and so on. In the three of the first person of luṅ: asātsīta, asāttāṃ, asātsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: asātsīḥ, asādhima, asātta. In the three of the last person: asātsaṃ, asātsma. In the three of the first person of liṭ: sasādha, sasādhatuḥ, sasādhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: sasādhitha, sasāttha, sasādhathuḥ, sasādha. In the three of the last person: sasādha, sasādhiva, sasādhima. In luṭ: sāddhā, sāddhāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: sādhyata, sādhyāstāṃ, sādhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: sātsyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: asātsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "vyadha, in piercing," likewise takes the ataṅ endings. By "diva" and so on, śyan, and by "grahi, jyā, vayi, vyadhi" and so on, samprasāraṇa is made; thus, in laṭ: vidhyati, and so on; in liṅ: vidhyeta, and so on; in loṭ: vidhyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: avidhyata, and so on.

In luṅ: by "vada-vraja" and so on, vṛddhi is made; before those beginning with a jhal, by "jhalo jhali," sic is elided; and when the form is completed by "khari ca" and so on, in the three of the first person: avyātsīta, avyāttāṃ, avyātsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: avyātsīḥ, avyāttaṃ, avyātta. In the three of the last person: avyātsaṃ, avyātsva, avyātsma.

In liṭ: before the endings that are not kit, by "of the doubled" and so on, samprasāraṇa of the reduplicative syllable (abhyāsa) is made; and before the kit endings, by "grahi" and so on, samprasāraṇa of both is made; thus: vivyādha, vividhatuḥ, vividhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: vivyadhitha, vivyattha, vividhathuḥ, vividha. In the three of the last person: vivyādha, vivyadha, vividhiva, vividhima.

In luṭ: by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh, and by "jhal" and so on, dh is changed to d; thus: vyaddhā, vyaddhāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: samprasāraṇa is made by "grahi" and so on; thus: vidhyāta, vidhyāstāṃ, vidhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: by "khari ca," dh is changed to t; thus: vyatsyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: avyatsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "puṣa, in nourishing," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: puṣyati, and so on; in liṅ: puṣyeta, and so on. In loṭ: puṣyatuḥ, and so on; and in laṅ: apuṣyata, and so on. In luṅ: by the sūtra "puṣādi-dyutādi" and so on, cli is changed to aṅ; thus: apuṣata, apuṣatāṃ, apuṣana, and so on.

In liṭ, when reduplication and so on are made, in the three of the first person: pupoṣa, pupuṣatuḥ, pupuṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: pupoṣitha, pupoṣṭha, pupuṣathuḥ, pupuṣa. In the three of the last person: pupoṣa, pupuṣiva, pupuṣima. In luṭ: by "pug-anta" and so on, guṇa is made, and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," t is changed to ṭ; thus: poṣṭā, poṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: puṣyāta, puṣyāstāṃ, puṣyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: by "pug-anta" and so on, guṇa; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is made ṣ; thus: pokṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: apokṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "śliṣa, in embracing," takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: śliṣyati, and so on; in liṅ: śliṣyeta, and so on. In loṭ: śliṣyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: aśliṣyata, and so on. In luṅ: by "puṣādi-dyutādi" and so on, cli is changed to aṅ; thus: aśliṣata, aśliṣatāṃ, aśliṣata, and so on.

"Śliṣa āliṅgane": "śliṣa, in embracing." When śliṣ expresses the meaning of embracing, cli is to be changed to ksa. The k of ksa is dropped; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ; thus: aślikṣata, aślikṣatāṃ, aślikṣana, and so on.

In liṭ, when it is formed by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: śiśleṣa; śiśliṣatuḥ, śiśleṣatuḥ; śiśliṣuḥ, śiśleṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: śiśliṣitha, śiśleṣṭha; śiśliṣathuḥ, śiśleṣathuḥ; śiśliṣa, śiśleṣa. In the three of the last person: śiśleṣa; śiśliṣiva, śiśleṣiva; śiśliṣima, śiśleṣima. In luṭ: by "pug-anta" and so on, guṇa, and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," t is changed to ṭ; thus: śleṣṭā, śleṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: śliṣyāta, śliṣyāstāṃ, śliṣyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: by "pug-anta" and so on, guṇa; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ; thus: ślekṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aślekṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "radha, in harming," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: radhyati, and so on; in liṅ: radhyeta, and so on. In loṭ: radhyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: aradhyata, and so on. In luṅ: by "puṣādi" and so on, cli is changed to aṅ; and when the augment nuṃ is given by "radhijabhor aci," the forms are: arandhata, arandhatāṃ, arandhana, and so on.

In liṭ also there is reduplication, and when nuṃ is given by "radhijabhor aci": rarandha, rarandhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: rarandhitha, rarandhathuḥ, rarandha. In the three of the last person: rarandha, rarandhiva, rarandhima.

"Radhādibhyaś ca": "also from radha and so on." Radha and so on are these: radha, harming; ṇaśa, disappearing from sight; tṛpa, satisfaction; dṛpa, joy; druha, wishing to do harm; muha, bewilderment; ṣṇuha, vomiting; and ṣṇiha, joy. After these, a following ārdhadhātuka ending that begins with a val optionally takes iṭ.

"Neṭy aliṭi radheḥ": "not before an iṭ that is not of liṭ, for radhi." Above it was explained that radhi and jabha receive the augment nuṃ before a following vowel (ac). But as the exception to that: although iṭ begins with a vowel, it is an iṭ that does not belong to liṭ, so radhi does not take nuṃ before a following iṭ. Thus, when luṭ is applied to radha, iṭ is made optional by "radhādibhyaś ca," and this sūtra does not give the augment nuṃ. In the alternative with iṭ: radhitā, radhitāsi, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ: by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh, and by "jhal" and so on, dh is changed to d; thus: raddhā, raddhāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: radhyāta, radhyāstāṃ, radhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: by "radhādibhyaś ca," iṭ is made optional. In the alternative with iṭ: radhiṣyati, and so on; and in the alternative without iṭ, by "khari ca," dh is changed to t; thus: ratsyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aradhiṣyata, and so on, or aratsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "tṛpa, in satisfaction," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: tṛpyati, and so on; in liṅ: tṛpyeta, and so on. In loṭ: tṛpyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: atṛpyata, and so on. In luṅ: by "puṣādi" and so on, the change of cli to aṅ and its change to sic are made optional. In the alternative with aṅ: atṛpata, atṛpatāṃ, atṛpana, and so on. In the alternative with sic: by "radhādibhyaś ca," iṭ is to be made optional. In the alternative with iṭ, guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on; thus: atarpīta, atarpiṣṭāṃ, atarpiṣuḥ, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ: by "anudāttasya ca rdupadhasyānyatarasyām," am is optional, so am is made optional. In the alternative where am is not given, vṛddhi is made before sic, and before those beginning with a jhal sic is elided, and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: atārptāṃ, atārpsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: atārpsīḥ, atārptaṃ, atārpta. In the three of the last person: atārpsaṃ, atārpsva, atārpsma, and so on.

In the alternative with am: yaṇ is made by "iko yaṇ aci," and then vṛddhi before sic, and before those beginning with a jhal sic is elided, and so on; thus, in the three of the first person: atrāpsīt, atrāptāṃ, atrāpsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: atrāpsīḥ, atrāptaṃ, atrāpta. In the three of the last person: atrāpsaṃ, atrāpsva, atrāpsma, and so on.

In liṭ: when reduplication, the change of ṛ to a, and so on are made, in the three of the first person: tatarpa, tatṛpatuḥ, tatṛpuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tatarpitha, tatarptha, tatṛpathuḥ, tatṛpa. In the three of the last person: tatarpa, tatṛpiva, tatṛpima.

In luṭ: when iṭ is made optional by "radhādibhyaś ca," in the alternative with iṭ: tarpitā, tarpitāsi, and so on. In the alternative where iṭ is not given, am is made optional by "anudāttasya ca rdupadhasyānyatarasyām"; thus: tarptā, tarptāsi, and so on; or traptā, traptāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: tṛpyāta, tṛpyāstāṃ, tṛpyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ also, iṭ is made optional by "radha" and so on, and in the alternative without iṭ am is made optional; thus: tarpiṣyati, and so on; or tarpsyati, and so on; or else trapsyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: atarpiṣyata, and so on; or atarpsyata, and so on; or else atrapsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "dṛpa, in joy and in releasing," also takes the ataṅ endings, and its entire procedure is the same as that of tṛpa just explained, without even the slightest difference.

The root listed as "muha, in bewilderment," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: muhyati, and so on; in liṅ: muhyeta, and so on. In loṭ: muhyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: amuhyata, and so on. In luṅ: by "puṣādi-dyutādi" and so on, cli is changed to aṅ; thus: amuhata, amuhatāṃ, amuhana, and so on.

In liṭ, when reduplication and so on are made, in the three of the first person: mumoha, mumuhatuḥ, mumuhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: mumohitha, mumuhathuḥ, mumuha. In the three of the last person: mumoha, mumuhiva, mumuhima.

In luṭ: iṭ is made optional by "radhādibhyaś ca." In the alternative with iṭ: mohitā, mohitāsi, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ: by the rule "optionally for druha, muha, ṣṇuha and ṣṇiha," the change of h to ḍh and its change to gh are made optional. In the alternative with ḍh: guṇa by "pug-anta" and so on; by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh; by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," dh becomes ḍh; and by "ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ," the former ḍh is dropped; thus: moḍhā, moḍhāsi, and so on. In the alternative where it is changed to gh: guṇa by "pug-anta" and so on; by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh; and by "jhal" and so on, gh is changed to g; thus: mogdhā, mogdhāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: muhyāta, muhyāstāṃ, muhyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ: iṭ is made optional by "radha" and so on. In the alternative with iṭ: mohiṣyati, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ, h becomes ḍh or optionally gh. In the alternative with ḍh, by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," it becomes k; and in the alternative with gh, by "khari ca," gh becomes k; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ. So although the manner of derivation differs, the form is one and the same: mokṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ also: amohiṣyata, and so on; or amokṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ṇaśa, in disappearing from sight," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: naśyati, and so on; in liṅ: naśyeta, and so on. In loṭ: naśyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: anaśyata, and so on. In luṅ: by "puṣādi" and so on, cli is changed to aṅ; thus: anaśata, anaśatāṃ, anaśan, and so on.

The commentary cites the rule "naśer ata etvam aṅi vā": "the a of naśi optionally becomes e before aṅ." Before the aṅ into which cli is changed, the a of naśi is optionally changed to e; thus: aneśata, aneśatāṃ, aneśan, and so on.

In liṭ: before the kit endings, when elision of the reduplicative syllable (abhyāsa) and so on are made, in the three of the first person: nanāśa, neśatuḥ, neśuḥ. In the three of the middle person: neśitha, neśathuḥ, neśa. In the three of the last person: nanāśa, neśiva, neśima.

"Naśeḥ ṣāntasya": "of naśi when it ends in ṣ." When the ś of naśi is changed to ṣ by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, so that it ends in ṣ, then even if a letter that is a cause for n becoming ṇ occurs before it, the n does not become ṇ. Thus, if pra is placed before naśa when it has the affix of luṭ, the n does not become ṇ, as in pranaṣṭā.

In luṭ: iṭ is made optional by "radha" and so on. In the alternative with iṭ: naśitā, naśitāsi, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ: "masjinaśor nuṃ hali": "for masji and naśa, nuṃ before a hal." When suffixes that begin with a hal, and that are not those named kit or ṅit, follow ṭumasji, "purifying," and naśa, the augment nuṃ arises; its m serves to fix its position, and its u is for pronunciation. For naśa in luṭ: by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; this sūtra gives nuṃ; and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," t is changed to ṭ; thus: naṃṣṭā, naṃṣṭārau, naṃṣṭāraḥ, naṃṣṭāsi, and so on.

And the commentary cites the rule "naśer vā": "optionally for naśi." The letter ś of naśa optionally becomes the letter gh before what begins with a letter included in the pratyāhāra jhal: ś becomes gh; by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh; and by "jhal" and so on, gh is changed to g; thus: naṃgdhā, naṃgdhāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: naśyāta, naśyāstāṃ, naśyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ: iṭ is made optional by "radha" and so on. In the alternative with iṭ: naśiṣyati, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ: by "for masji and naśa, nuṃ before a hal," the augment nuṃ; by "masjinaśa" and so on, the augment nuṃ; by "vraśca" and so on, ś is changed to ṣ; and by "optionally for naśa," the change to gh is made optional. In the alternative with ś, by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," it becomes k; and in the alternative with gh, by "khari ca," gh becomes k; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ. So although the procedures differ, the resulting form is one and the same: naṃkṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: anaśiṣyata, and so on; or anaṃkṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "śamu, in calming," also takes the ataṅ endings. "Śamām aṣṭānāṃ dīrghaḥ śyani": "lengthening for the eight beginning with śama before śyan." The eight beginning with śamu are these: śamu and damu, calming; tamu, desire; śramu, austerity; bhramu, not staying still; kṣamuṣ, patience; klamu, dejection; and madī, joy. Their penultimate vowel (upadhā) becomes long before a following śyan. When śyan is added to śamu and the vowel is lengthened by this sūtra, in laṭ: śāmyati, and so on; and in liṅ: śāmyeta, and so on.

In loṭ: śāmyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: aśāmyata, and so on. In luṅ: when the iṭ of what begins with a val is given: aśamīta, aśamiṣṭāṃ, aśamiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ: when, before the kit endings, elision of the reduplicative syllable (abhyāsa) and so on are made, in the three of the first person: śaśāma, śematuḥ, śemuḥ. In the three of the middle person: śemitha, śemathuḥ, śema. In the three of the last person: śaśāma, śaśama, śemiva, śemima. In luṭ, when iṭ is given: śamitā, śamitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: śamyāta, śamyāstāṃ, śamyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, when iṭ is given: śamiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aśamiṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "klamu, in dejection," also takes the ataṅ endings. By "bhrāśa, bhlāśa, bhramu, kramu, klamu" and so on, śap and śyan are made optional. In the alternative with śyan, the vowel is lengthened by "of the eight beginning with śama" and so on. In laṭ: klamati, and so on; or klāmyati, and so on. In liṅ: klameta, and so on; or klāmyeta, and so on. In loṭ: klamatu, and so on; or klāmyatu, and so on. In laṅ: aklamata, and so on; or aklāmyata, and so on. In luṅ, when iṭ is given: aklamīta, aklamiṣṭāṃ, aklamiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, when reduplication and so on are made, in the three of the first person: caklāma, caklamatuḥ, caklamuḥ. In the three of the middle person: caklamitha, caklamathuḥ, caklama. In the three of the last person: caklāma, caklama, caklamiva, caklamima. In luṭ: klamitā, klamitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: klamyāta, klamyāstāṃ, klamyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: the iṭ of what begins with a val is given, and when it is formed by the change to ṣ through "ādeśa" and so on, and so forth: klamiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aklamiṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "asu, in throwing," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: asyati, and so on. In loṭ: asyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: āsyata, and so on.

In luṅ: "asyates thuk": "thuk for asyati." When the aṅ into which the cli of asyati is changed follows, the augment thuk arises; its k serves to fix its position, and its u is for pronunciation. For asyati, by "asyati-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ," cli is changed to aṅ, and this sūtra gives the augment thuk; thus: āsthata, āsthatāṃ, āsthana, and so on.

In liṭ, when it is formed by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: āsa, āsatuḥ, āsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: āsitha, āsathuḥ, āsa. In the three of the last person: āsa, āsiva, āsima. In luṭ, when iṭ is given: asitā, asitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: asyāta, asyāstāṃ, asyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, when iṭ is given: asiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: āsiṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "yasu, in striving hard," also takes the ataṅ endings. "Yaso 'nupasargāt": "from yasa when it has no upasarga." If an upasarga is placed before yasu, "striving hard," only śyan occurs in the sense of the agent; but if there is no upasarga before it, śap and śyan are to be made optional. In laṭ: yasati, and so on; or yasyati, and so on. In liṅ: yaseta, and so on; or yasyeta, and so on. In loṭ: yasatu, and so on; or yasyatu, and so on. In laṅ: ayasata, and so on; or ayasyata, and so on. When an upasarga is applied, there is only śyan: prayasyati, and so on.

"Saṃyasaś ca": "also from saṃ-yasa." From yasu preceded by the upasarga sam also, śap and śyan are to be made optional: saṃyasati, "strives rightly," and so on; or saṃyasyati, and so on. In luṅ, when iṭ is given: ayāsīta, ayāsiṣṭāṃ, "strives hard," ayāsiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ: when it is formed through elision of the reduplicative syllable before the kit endings and so on, in the three of the first person: yayāsa, yesatuḥ, yesuḥ. In the three of the middle person: yesitha, yesathuḥ, yesa. In the three of the last person: yayāsa, yayasa, yesiva, yesima. In luṭ, when iṭ is given: yasitā, yasitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: yasyāta, yasyāstāṃ, yasyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, when the iṭ of what begins with a val is given: yasiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ayasiṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "lubha, in attachment," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: lubhyati, and so on; in liṅ: lubhyeta, and so on; in loṭ: lubhyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: alubhyata, and so on. In luṅ, when iṭ is given and guṇa is made: alobhīta, alobhiṣṭāṃ, alobhiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: lulobha, lulubhatuḥ, lulubhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: lulobhitha, lulubhathuḥ, lulubha. In the three of the last person: lulobha, lulubhiva, lulubhima. In luṭ: when iṭ is made optional by "iṣu, saha, lubha" and so on: lobhitā, lobhitāsi, and so on; or, in the alternative without iṭ, by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh, and by "jhal" and so on, bh is changed to b; thus: lobdhā, lobdhāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: lubhyāta, lubhyāstāṃ, lubhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, when iṭ is given: lobhiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: alobhiṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ñimidā, in being moist," also takes the ataṅ endings. "Mider guṇaḥ": "guṇa for midi." Before a following affix marked with ś, the vowel of ñimidi is changed to guṇa. In laṭ: medyati, and so on; in liṅ: medyeta, and so on. In loṭ: medyatu, and so on; and in laṅ: amedyata, and so on. In luṅ: by "puṣādi" and so on, cli is changed to aṅ; thus: amidata, amidatāṃ, amidan, and so on.

In liṭ, when it is formed by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: mimeda, mimidatuḥ, mimiduḥ. In the three of the middle person: mimeditha, mimidathuḥ, mimida. In the three of the last person: mimeda, mimidiva, mimidima. In luṭ, when iṭ is given and guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on: meditā, meditāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: midyāta, midyāstāṃ, midyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, when iṭ is given and guṇa is made: mediṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: amediṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ṣūṅ, in giving birth to living beings," takes the taṅ endings. The ṣ at the beginning of the root becomes s, and śyan is applied by "divādi" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person of laṭ: sūyate, sūyete, sūyante. In the three of the middle person: sūyase, sūyethe, sūyadhve. In the three of the last person: sūye, sūyāvahe, sūyāmahe.

Likewise, in the three of the first person of liṅ: sūyeta, sūyeyātāṃ, sūyeran. In the three of the middle person: sūyethāḥ, sūyeyāthāṃ, sūyedhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: sūyeya, sūyevahi, sūyemahi.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: sūyatāṃ, sūyetāṃ, sūyantāṃ. In the three of the middle person: sūyasva; then, by "not final" and so on, ī is put in place and guṇa is made with the a: sūyethāṃ; and sūyadhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: sūyai, sūyāvahai, sūyāmahai.

In the three of the first person of laṅ: asūyata, asūyetāṃ, asūyanta. In the three of the middle person: asūyathāḥ, asūyethāṃ, asūyadhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: asūye, asūyāvahi, asūyāmahi.

In luṅ: iṭ is to be made optional by "svarati, sūti, sūyati" and so on, and guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on. In the alternative with iṭ: asaviṣṭa, asaviṣātāṃ, asaviṣata, and so on. In the three of the first person of the alternative without iṭ: asoṣṭa, asoṣātāṃ, asoṣata. In the three of the middle person: asoṣṭhāḥ, asoṣāthāṃ, asoḍhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: asoṣi, asoṣvahi, asoṣmahi.

In liṭ the root is reduplicated, and when it is formed by the change to uv through "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on, in the three of the first person: suṣuve, suṣuvāte, suṣuvire. In the three of the middle person: suṣuviṣe, suṣuvāthe, suṣuvidhve, suṣuviḍhve. In the three of the last person: suṣuve, suṣuvivahe, suṣuvimahe.

In luṭ: when iṭ is made optional by "svarati, sūti, sūyati" and so on: savitā, savitāse, and so on; or sotā, sotāse, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ, when iṭ is made optional: saviṣīṣṭa, saviṣīyāstāṃ, saviṣīran, and so on; or soṣīṣṭa, soṣīyāstāṃ, soṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ also, when iṭ is made optional: saviṣyate, and so on; or soṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: asaviṣyata, and so on; or asoṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "dīṅ, in wasting away," also takes the taṅ endings. In laṭ: dīyate, and so on; in liṅ: dīyeta, and so on. In loṭ: dīyatāṃ, and so on; and in laṅ: adīyata, and so on.

"Mīnātiminotidīṅāṃ lyapi ca": "for mīnāti, minoti and dīṅ, also before lyap." Before a following kṛt suffix lyap and the like, the final of mīñ, "harming," ḍumiñ, "throwing," and dīṅ, "wasting away," is changed to ā; and by the word "also," it is changed to ā as well before the liṭ endings other than the two ṇal and thal, and before suffixes not marked with ś. For dīṅ in luṅ, when it is changed to ā by this sūtra, in the three of the first person: adāsta, adāsātāṃ, adāsata. In the three of the middle person: adāsthāḥ, adāsāthāṃ, adādhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: adāsi, adāsvahi, adāsmahi.

"Dīṅo yuṭ aci kṅiti": "yuṭ for dīṅ before an ac that is kit or ṅit." Before a following vowel named kit or ṅit after dīṅ, the augment yuṭ arises. In liṭ: reduplication; by "hrasvaḥ," the reduplicative syllable is shortened; and when this sūtra gives yuṭ, in the three of the first person: didīye, didīyāte, didīyire. In the three of the middle person: didīyiṣe, didīyāthe, didīyidhve. In the three of the last person: didīye, didīyivahe, didīyimahe.

In luṭ: when it is changed to ā by "for mīnāti, minoti and dīṅ, also before lyap": dātā, dātāse, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ: dāsīṣṭa, dāsīyāstāṃ, dāsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ also, when it is changed to ā by "mīnāti" and so on: dāsyate, and so on; and in lṛṅ: adāsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "jani, in being born," also takes the taṅ endings. "Jñājanor jā": "jā for jñā and jan." Before a following affix named śit, jñā, "understanding," and jan, "being born," are to be changed to jā. For jan with śyan, when it is changed to jā by this sūtra, in laṭ: jāyate, and so on; in liṅ: jāyeta, and so on. In loṭ: jāyatāṃ, and so on; and in laṅ: ajāyata, and so on.

"Janivadhyoś ca": "also for jani and vadhi." Before the ciṇ into which cli is changed, and before kṛt suffixes and the like that are marked with ñ, the penultimate vowel of jani, "being born," and of vadhi is not changed to vṛddhi. When luṅ is applied to jan, in the singular of the first person the ending is ta. By "dīpa, jana, budha" and so on, the change of cli to ciṇ and its change to sic are made optional. In the alternative with ciṇ, this sūtra prevents vṛddhi, and by "luk after ciṇ" the t is dropped: ajani. In the alternative with sic, when iṭ is given: ajaniṣṭa. In the dual and plural: ajaniṣātāṃ, ajaniṣata. In the three of the middle person: ajaniṣṭhāḥ, ajaniṣāthāṃ, ajanidhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: ajaniṣi, ajaniṣvahi, ajaniṣmahi.

In liṭ: the penultimate vowel is dropped by "gama, hana, jana" and so on, and when it is formed by the change of n to ñ through "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ" and so on: jajñe, jajñāte, jajñire. In the three of the middle person: jajñiṣe, jajñāthe, jajñidhve, jajñiḍhve. In the three of the last person: jajñe, jajñivahe, jajñimahe. In luṭ, when iṭ is given: janitā, janitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: janiṣīṣṭa, janiṣīyāstāṃ, janiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ also, when iṭ is given: janiṣyate, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ also, when iṭ is given: ajaniṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "dīpī, in blazing," also takes the taṅ endings. In laṭ: dīpyate, and so on; in liṅ: dīpyeta, and so on. In loṭ: dīpyatāṃ, and so on; and in laṅ: adīpyata, and so on.

In the singular of the first person of luṅ: by "dīpa, jana, budha" and so on, the change of cli to ciṇ and its change to sic are made optional; thus: adīpi, or adīpiṣṭa. In the dual and plural: adīpiṣātāṃ, adīpiṣata. In the three of the middle person: adīpiṣṭhāḥ, adīpiṣāthāṃ, adīpidhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: adīpiṣi, adīpiṣvahi, adīpiṣmahi.

In liṭ, when it is formed by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: didīpe, didīpāte, didīpire. In the three of the middle person: didīpiṣe, didīpāthe, didīpidhve, didīpiḍhve. In the three of the last person: didīpe, didīpivahe, didīpimahe. In luṭ, when iṭ is given: dīpitā, dīpitāse, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ: dīpiṣīṣṭa, dīpiṣīyāstāṃ, dīpiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ also, when iṭ is given: dīpiṣyate, and so on; and in lṛṅ: adīpiṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "pūrī, in being satisfied," also takes the taṅ endings. In laṭ: pūryate, and so on; in liṅ: pūryeta, and so on. In loṭ: pūryatāṃ, and so on; and in laṅ: apūryata, and so on. In the singular of the first person of luṅ: by "dīpa, jana, budha" and so on, ciṇ for cli and sic are made optional; thus: apūri, apūriṣṭa. For the rest, when iṭ is given: apūriṣātāṃ, apūriṣata, and so on.

In liṭ there is reduplication, and when the reduplicative syllable is shortened by "hrasvaḥ," in the three of the first person: pupūre, pupūrāte, pupūrire. In the three of the middle person: pupūriṣe, pupūrāthe, pupūridhve, pupūriḍhve. In the three of the last person: pupūre, pupūrivahe, pupūrimahe. In luṭ, when iṭ is given: pūritā, pūritāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: pūriṣīṣṭa, pūriṣīyāstāṃ, pūriṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: pūriṣyate, and so on; and in lṛṅ: apūriṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "pada, in going," also takes the taṅ endings. In laṭ: padyate, and so on; in liṅ: padyeta, and so on. In loṭ: padyatāṃ, and so on; and in laṅ: apadyata, and so on.

"Ciṇ te padaḥ": "ciṇ before ta after pad." After pada, when the taṅ singular ta, substituted for the l of luṅ, follows, cli is changed to ciṇ. For pada, in luṅ, the ending ta: this sūtra changes cli to ciṇ; by "of the penultimate a," vṛddhi; and by "luk after ciṇ," the t is dropped; thus: apādi. For the rest: before what begins with a jhal, sic is dropped, and when "khari ca" and so on are applied, in the dual and plural of the first person: apatsātāṃ, apatsata. In the three of the middle person: apatthāḥ, apatsāthāṃ, apaddhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: apatsi, apatsvahi.

In liṭ, by elision of the reduplicative syllable and so on, in the three of the first person: pede, pedāte, pedire. In the three of the middle person: pediṣe, pedāthe, pedidhve, pediḍhve. In the three of the last person: pede, pedivahe, pedimahe. In luṭ: when d is changed to t by "khari ca": pattā, pattāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ also: patsīṣṭa, patsīyāstāṃ, patsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ: patsyate, and so on; and in lṛṅ: apatsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "budha, in understanding," also takes the taṅ endings. In laṭ: budhyate, and so on; in liṅ: budhyeta, and so on. In loṭ: budhyatāṃ, and so on; and in laṅ: abudhyata, and so on.

In the singular of the first person of luṅ: by "dīpa, jana, budha" and so on, ciṇ for cli and sic are made optional. In the alternative with ciṇ, when guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on: abodhi. In the alternative with sic: by "jhalo jhali," sic is dropped; by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh; and by "jhal" and so on, dh is changed to d; thus: abuddha. In the dual and plural, when b is changed to bh by "ekāc" and so on: abhutsātāṃ, abhutsata. In the three of the middle person: abuddhāḥ, abhutsāthāṃ, abhuddhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: abhutsi, abhutsvahi, abhutsmahi.

In liṭ, by reduplication and so on: bubudhe, bubudhāte, bubudhire. In the three of the middle person: bubudhiṣe, bubudhāthe, bubudhidhve, bubudhiḍhve. In the three of the last person: bubudhe, bubudhivahe, bubudhimahe. In luṭ: guṇa by "pug-anta" and so on; by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh; and by "jhal" and so on, dh is changed to d; thus: boddhā, boddhāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: by "ekāc" and so on, b becomes bh, and by "khari ca," dh is changed to t; thus: bhutsīṣṭa, bhutsīyāstāṃ, bhutsīran, and so on. Likewise in lṛṭ: bhotsyate, with guṇa by "pug-anta" and so on, and so on; and in lṛṅ also: abhotsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ṇaha, in binding," takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. By "ṇo naḥ," ṇ becomes n; śyan is added by "divādi" and so on; and when the h is brought in, in the ataṅ of laṭ: nahyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: nahyate, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: nahyeta, and so on; and in the taṅ: nahyeta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: nahyatu, and so on; and in the taṅ: nahyatāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: anahyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: anahyata, and so on.

In luṅ: before those beginning with a jhal, sic is elided; by "nah to dh," h becomes dh; and when it is formed by "khari ca" and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: anātsīta, anāddhāṃ, anātsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: anātsīḥ, anāddhaṃ, anāddha. In the three of the last person: anātsaṃ, anātsva, anātsma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: anaddha, anatsātāṃ, anatsata.
