In the three of the middle person: anaddhāḥ, anatsāthāṃ; and, with vṛddhi by "vada-vraja" and so on, t becoming dh by "jhaṣ" and so on, and dh becoming d by "jhal" and so on: anaddhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: anatsi, anatsvahi, anatsmahi.

In liṭ: reduplication, and before the kit endings, elision of the reduplicative syllable, the change to e, and so on; in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: nanāha, nehatuḥ, nehuḥ. In the three of the middle person: nehitha, nanaddha, nehathuḥ, neha. In the three of the last person: nanāha, nanaha, nehiva, nehima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: nehe, nehāte, nehire. In the three of the middle person: nehiṣe, nehāthe, nehidhve, nehiḍhve. In the three of the last person: nehe, nehivahe, nehimahe.

In luṭ: by "nah to dh," h becomes dh; by "jhaṣ" and so on, t becomes dh; and when it is formed by the change of dh to d through "jhal" and so on, in the ataṅ: naddhā, naddhāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: naddhā, naddhāse. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: nahyāta, nahyāstāṃ, nahyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: by "nah to dh," h becomes dh, and by "khari ca," dh is changed to t; thus: natsīṣṭa, natsīyāstāṃ, natsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ also, h becomes dh by "nah" and so on, and when it is changed to car by "khari ca," in the ataṅ: natsyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: natsyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: anatsyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: anatsyata, and so on.

"Iti pāṇinivyākaraṇasya sūtrāt divādayaḥ samāptāḥ": thus are completed the roots beginning with divu, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa.

Thus, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, notes setting down the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great treatise of grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the section on how laṭ and so on are applied, with their general rules and exceptions, to the roots beginning with divu, in which śyan occurs in the sense of the agent, is for the present complete.

Now I shall explain the procedure for ṣuñ and so on.

By the root listed as "ṣuñ, in bringing forth," laṭ and so on become both ataṅ and taṅ. "Svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ": "śnu after su and so on." Ṣuñ, "bringing forth," and the rest are "su and so on," and after them śnu occurs in the sense of the agent. For ṣuñ with śnu, the ś serving to mark it as śit, and with the form completed by "the ṣ at the beginning of the root becomes s" and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: sunoti, sunutaḥ, sunvanti. In the three of the middle person: sunoṣi, sunuthaḥ, sunutha. In the three of the last person: sunomi, sunuvaḥ, sunvaḥ, sunumaḥ, sunmaḥ.

Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: sunute, sunvāte, sunvate. Guṇa comes by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on, and by "for hu and śnu, also before a sārvadhātuka," u is changed to v. In the three of the middle person: sunuṣe, sunvāthe, sunudhve. Before v and m, its elision is also optional: the elision or non-elision of u is made optional. In the three of the last person: sunve, sunuvahe, sunumahe.

In the ataṅ of liṅ: sunuyāta, sunuyātāṃ, sunuyuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: by "not final" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is dropped, and by "for hu and śnu, before a sārvadhātuka," u is changed to v; thus: sunvīta, sunvīyātāṃ, sunvīran, and so on.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of loṭ: sunotu, sunutāt, sunutāṃ, sunvantu. In the three of the middle person: sunu, sunutāt, sunutaṃ, sunuta. In the three of the last person: sunavāni, sunavāva, sunavāma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: sunutāṃ, sunvātāṃ, sunvatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: sunuṣva, sunvāthāṃ, sunudhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: sunavai, sunavāvahai, sunavāmahai.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: asunota, asunutāṃ, asunvana. In the three of the middle person: asunoḥ, asunutaṃ, asunuta. In the three of the last person: asunavaṃ, asunuva, asunva, asunuma, asunma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: asunuta, asunvātāṃ, asunvata. In the three of the middle person: asunuthāḥ, asunvāthāṃ, asunudhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: asunvi, asunuvahi, asunvahi, asunumahi, asunmahi.

In the ataṅ of luṅ: by "v and m" and so on, u is optionally dropped; iṭ is given by "stu, su, dhūñ" and so on; and when vṛddhi is made by "vṛddhi before sic" and so on: asāvīta, asāviṣṭāṃ, asāviṣuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: iṭ is made optional by the commentary's citation "ru, du, su, nu" and so on. In the alternative where iṭ is given: asaviṣṭa, asaviṣātāṃ, asaviṣata, and so on. In the three of the first person of the alternative without iṭ: asoṣṭa, asoṣātāṃ, asoṣata. In the three of the middle person: asoṣṭhāḥ, asoṣāthāṃ, asoḍhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: asoṣi, asoṣvahi, asoṣmahi.

In liṭ there is reduplication, and before those beginning with an ac, u is changed to uv by "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on; thus, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: suṣāva, suṣuvatuḥ, suṣuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: suṣavitha, suṣuvathuḥ, suṣuva. In the three of the last person: suṣāva, suṣuviva, suṣuvima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: suṣuve, suṣuvāte, suṣuvire. In the three of the middle person: suṣuviṣe, suṣuvāthe, suṣuvidhve, suṣuviḍhve. In the three of the last person: suṣuve, suṣuvivahe, suṣuvimahe.

In luṭ: when iṭ is made optional by the commentary's citation "ru, du, su, nu" and so on, in the ataṅ: savitā, savitāsi, and so on; or sotā, sotāsi, and so on. Likewise in the taṅ: savitā, savitāse, and so on; or sotā, sotāse, and so on.

In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, when the vowel is lengthened by "not kṛt" and so on: sūyāta, sūyāstāṃ, sūyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, when iṭ is made optional by "ru, du, su" and so on: saviṣīṣṭa, saviṣīyāstāṃ, saviṣīran, and so on; or soṣīṣṭa, soṣīyāstāṃ, soṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ also, in the ataṅ: saviṣyati, and so on; or soṣyati, and so on. In the taṅ: saviṣyate, and so on; or soṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: asaviṣyata, and so on; or asoṣyata, and so on. In the taṅ: asaviṣyata, and so on; or asoṣyata, and so on.

"Sunoteḥ syasanoḥ": "for sunoti, before sya and san." Even when something that is a cause for changing s to ṣ, such as an upasarga, comes before it, the letter s of sunoti is not changed to ṣ before the affixes sya and san: abhisaviṣyati, and so on.

The root listed as "ḍumiñ, in throwing," takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. For the sārvadhātuka endings, the whole procedure is the same as that just explained. In the ataṅ of laṭ: minoti, and so on; and in the taṅ: minute, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: minuyāta, and so on; and in the taṅ: minvīta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: minotu, and so on; and in the taṅ: minutāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: aminota, and so on; and in the taṅ: aminuta, and so on.

In the ataṅ of luṅ: by "for mīnāti, minoti and dīṅ, also before lyap," the i is changed to ā; and when, by "for yama, rama, nama and what ends in ā, also sak," the augment sak and iṭ are given, in the three of the first person: amāsīta, amāsiṣṭāṃ, amāsiṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: amāsīḥ, amāsiṣṭaṃ, amāsiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: amāsiṣaṃ, amāsiṣva, amāsiṣma. In the taṅ: the i becomes ā by "mīnāti, minoti, dīṅ" and so on, and when cli is changed to sic, in the three of the first person: amāsta, amāsātāṃ, amāsata. In the three of the middle person: amāsthāḥ, amāsāthāṃ, amādhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: amāsi, amāsvahi, amāsmahi.

In the ataṅ of liṭ: before the two ṇal and thal, the i becomes ā by "mīnāti" and so on; and before the kit endings, when it is changed to yaṇ by "not having one ac" and so on, in the three of the first person: mamau, mimyatuḥ. In the three of the middle person: mamitha, mamātha, mimyathuḥ, mimya. In the three of the last person: mamau, mimyiva, mimyima. Likewise, when it is changed to yaṇ, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: mimye, mimyāte, mimyire. In the three of the middle person: mimyiṣe, mimyāthe, mimyidhve, mimyiḍhve. In the three of the last person: mimye, mimyivahe, mimyimahe.

In luṭ: when the i is changed to ā by "mīnāti, minoti, dīṅ" and so on, in the ataṅ: mātā, mātāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: mātā, mātāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: the i becomes ā by "mīnāti" and so on, and when, by "e before liṅ," ā is changed to e: meyāta, meyāstāṃ, meyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, when the i is changed to ā: māsīṣṭa, māsīyāstāṃ, māsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ also, when the i is changed to ā, in the ataṅ: māsyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: māsyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: amāsyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: amāsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ciñ, in accumulating," also takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. In the ataṅ of laṭ: cinoti, and so on; and in the taṅ: cinute, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: cinuyāta, and so on; and in the taṅ: cinvīta, cinvīta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: cinotu, and so on; and in the taṅ: cinutāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: acinota, and so on; and in the taṅ: acinuta, and so on.

In the ataṅ of luṅ, when vṛddhi is made by "vṛddhi before sic" and so on, in the three of the first person: acaiṣīta, acaiṣṭāṃ, acaiṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: acaiṣīḥ, acaiṣṭaṃ, acaiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: acaiṣaṃ, acaiṣva, acaiṣma. In the taṅ, when guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on, in the three of the first person: aceṣṭa, aceṣātāṃ, aceṣata. In the three of the middle person: aceṣṭhāḥ, aceṣāthāṃ, acedhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: aceṣi, aceṣmahi.

"Vibhāṣā ceḥ": "optionally for ci." Before liṭ and san of ciñ, the change of the c of the reduplicated root to k, or its not being changed, is to be made optional. Liṭ is applied to ciñ. In the ataṅ of the alternative where c is changed to k, in the three of the first person: cikāya, cikyatuḥ, cikyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ciketha, cikayitha, cikyathuḥ, cikya. In the three of the last person: cikāya, cikaya, cikyiva, cikyima. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: cikye, cikyāte, cikyire. In the three of the middle person: cikyiṣe, cikyāthe, cikyidhve, cikyiḍhve. In the three of the last person: cikye, cikyivahe, cikyimahe, and so on. And in the ataṅ of the alternative where c is not changed to k: cicāya, cicyatuḥ, cicyuḥ, and so on; and in the taṅ: cicye, cicyāte, cicyire, and so on.

In luṭ, when guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka" and so on, in the ataṅ: cetā, cetāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: cetā, cetāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, when the vowel is lengthened by "not kṛt" and so on: cīyāta, cīyāstāṃ, cīyāsuḥ, and so on; and in the taṅ, when guṇa is made: ceṣīṣṭa, ceṣīyāstāṃ, ceṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ also, when guṇa is made, in the ataṅ: ceṣyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: ceṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: aceṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "stṛñ, in covering all over," also takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. In the ataṅ of laṭ: stṛṇoti, and so on; and in the taṅ: stṛṇute, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: stṛṇuyāta, and so on; and in the taṅ: stṛṇvīta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: stṛṇotu, and so on; and in the taṅ: stṛṇutāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: astṛṇota, and so on; and in the taṅ: astṛṇuta, and so on.

In the ataṅ of luṅ, when vṛddhi is made by "vṛddhi before sic in the parasmaipada," in the three of the first person: astārṣīta, astārṣṭāṃ, astārṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: astārṣīḥ, astārṣṭaṃ, astārṣṭa. In the three of the last person: astārṣaṃ, astārṣva, astārṣma.

"Ṛtaś ca saṃyogādeḥ": "also from what ends in ṛ and begins with a conjunct consonant."

From what ends in ṛ and has a conjunct consonant at its beginning, too, iṭ is optional before sic and the benedictive liṅ when an ātmanepada ending follows. When the taṅ endings of luṅ are applied to stṛ, in the three of the first person of the alternative where iṭ is given: astariṣṭa, astariṣātāṃ, astariṣata. In the three of the middle person: astariṣṭhāḥ, astariṣāthāṃ, astaridhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: astariṣi, astariṣvahi, astariṣmahi.

In the alternative without iṭ: since sic is kit, guṇa, vṛddhi and the like are not made; and before those beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "after a short form"; thus, in the three of the first person: astṛta, astṛṣātāṃ, astṛṣata. In the three of the middle person: astṛthāḥ, astṛṣāthāṃ, astṛdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: astṛṣi, astṛṣvahi, astṛṣmahi.

In liṭ: vṛddhi before the two ṇal; before the others, guṇa by "guṇa also for what ends in ṛ and has a conjunct at its beginning"; reduplication; by "a for ṛ," ṛ becomes a; and when the s is dropped by "preceded by śar" and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: tastāra, tastaratuḥ, tastaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: tastartha, tastarathuḥ, tastara. In the three of the last person: tastāra, tastara, tastariva, tastarima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: tastare, tastarāte, tastarire. In the three of the middle person: tastariṣe, tastarāthe, tastaridhve, tastariḍhve. In the three of the last person: tastare, tastarivahe, tastarimahe.

In luṭ, when guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, in the ataṅ: startā, startāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: startā, startāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, when guṇa is made by "guṇa for ṛ of arti and of what has a conjunct at its beginning": staryāta, staryāstāṃ, staryāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, when iṭ is made optional by "also from what ends in ṛ and has a conjunct at its beginning": stariṣīṣṭa, stariṣīyāstāṃ, stariṣīran, and so on; or starṣīṣṭa, starṣīyāstāṃ, starṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, when iṭ is given by "for what ends in ṛ and for han, before sya," in the ataṅ: stariṣyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: stariṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: astariṣyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: astariṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "vṛñ, in obscuring," also takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. In the ataṅ of laṭ: vṛṇoti, and so on; and in the taṅ: vṛṇute, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: vṛṇuyāta, and so on; and in the taṅ: vṛṇvīta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: vṛṇotu, and so on; and in the taṅ: vṛṇutāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: avṛṇota, and so on; and in the taṅ: avṛṇuta, and so on. In the ataṅ of luṅ, when iṭ is given and vṛddhi is made: avārīta, avāriṣṭāṃ, avāriṣuḥ, and so on.

"Liṅsicor ātmanepadeṣu": "before liṅ and sic, in the ātmanepada." After vṛṅ, "showing respect," vṛñ, "obscuring," and those ending in ṝ, the iṭ given before sic and the benedictive liṅ that have ātmanepada endings is optional. When the taṅ endings of luṅ are applied to vṛ, in the three of the first person of the alternative where iṭ is given: avariṣṭa, avariṣātāṃ, avariṣata. In the three of the middle person: avariṣṭhāḥ, avariṣāthāṃ, avaridhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: avariṣi, avariṣvahi, avariṣmahi.

In the alternative without iṭ: since sic is kit, neither guṇa nor vṛddhi is made at all; and when, before those beginning with a jhal, sic is dropped by "after a short form," in the three of the first person: avṛta, avṛṣātāṃ, avṛṣata. In the three of the middle person: avṛthāḥ, avṛṣāthāṃ, avṛdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: avṛṣi, avṛṣvahi, avṛṣmahi. Or else, when īṭ is given by "optionally after vṛ and what ends in ṝ": avarīṣṭa, avarīṣātāṃ, avarīṣata, and so on; this too is one way.

In liṭ, when it is formed by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: vavāra, vavratuḥ, vavruḥ. In the three of the middle person: vavartha, vavaritha, vavrathuḥ, vavra. In the three of the last person: vavāra, vavara, vavṛva, vavṛma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: vavre, vavrāte, vavrire. In the three of the middle person: vavṛṣe, vavrāthe, vavṛdhve. In the three of the last person: vavre, vavṛvahe, vavṛmahe.

In luṭ, when iṭ and īṭ are made optional by "optionally after vṛ and what ends in ṝ," in the ataṅ: varitā, varitāsi, and so on; or varītā, varītāsi, and so on. In the taṅ: varitā, varitāse, and so on; or varītā, varītāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: when, by "riṅ before śa, yak and liṅ," ṛ is changed to riṅ: vṛyāta, vṛyāstāṃ, vṛyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, when iṭ is made optional by "before liṅ and sic, in the ātmanepada": variṣīṣṭa, variṣīyāstāṃ, variṣīran, and so on; or vṛṣīṣṭa, vṛṣīyāstāṃ, vṛṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ, when iṭ and īṭ are made optional by "optionally after vṛ and what ends in ṝ," in the ataṅ: variṣyati, and so on; or varīṣyati, and so on. In the taṅ: variṣyate, and so on; or varīṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: avariṣyata, and so on; or avarīṣyata, and so on. In the taṅ: avariṣyata, and so on; or avarīṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "dhuñ, in shaking," also takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. In the ataṅ of laṭ: dhunoti, and so on; and in the taṅ: dhunute, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: dhunuyāta, and so on; and in the taṅ: dhunvīta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: dhunotu, and so on; and in the taṅ: dhunutāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: adhunota, and so on; and in the taṅ: adhunuta, and so on.

In the ataṅ of luṅ: iṭ is given by "after stu, su and dhūñ, before the parasmaipada endings," and when vṛddhi is made by "vṛddhi before sic" and so on: adhāvīta, adhāviṣṭāṃ, adhāviṣuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: iṭ is made optional by "svarati, sūti, sūyati, dhūñ, and what has ū as marker" and so on. In the alternative with iṭ: adhaviṣṭa, adhaviṣātāṃ, adhaviṣata, and so on. In the three of the first person of the alternative without iṭ: adhoṣṭa, adhoṣātāṃ, adhoṣata. In the three of the middle person: adhoṣṭhāḥ, adhoṣāthāṃ, adhodhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: adhoṣi, adhoṣvahi, adhoṣmahi.

In liṭ, when it is formed by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: dudhāva, dudhuvatuḥ, dudhuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: dudhotha, dudhavitha, dudhuvathuḥ, dudhuva. In the three of the last person: dudhāva, dudhava, dudhuviva. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: dudhuve, dudhuvāte, dudhuvire. In the three of the middle person: dudhuviṣe, dudhuvāthe, dudhuvidhve, dudhuviḍhve. In the three of the last person: dudhuve, dudhuvivahe, dudhuvimahe.

In luṭ: when iṭ is made optional by "svarati, sūti, sūyati, dhūñ, and what has ū as marker" and so on, in the ataṅ: dhavitā, dhavitāsi, and so on; or dhotā, dhotāsi, and so on. In the taṅ: dhavitā, dhavitāse, and so on; or dhotā, dhotāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, when the vowel is lengthened by "not kṛt" and so on: dhūyāta, dhūyāstāṃ, dhūyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, when iṭ is made optional by "svarati" and so on: dhaviṣīṣṭa, dhaviṣīyāstāṃ, dhaviṣīran, and so on; or dhoṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ also, when iṭ is made optional, in the ataṅ: dhaviṣyati, and so on; or dhoṣyati, and so on. In the taṅ: dhaviṣyate, and so on; or dhoṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: adhaviṣyata, and so on; or adhoṣyata, and so on. In the taṅ: adhaviṣyata, and so on; or adhoṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "hi, in going, and also in increasing," takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: hinoti, and so on; in liṅ: hinuyāta, and so on. In loṭ: hinotu, and so on; and in laṅ: ahinota, and so on.

"Hinumīnā": "for hinu and mīnā." The n of śnu after hi, "going," and the letter n of śnā after mīñ, "harming," are to be changed to the letter ṇ when an upasarga that is a cause for changing n to ṇ comes before them: prahiṇoti, and so on.

In luṅ, when vṛddhi is made by "vṛddhi before sic, in the parasmaipada endings," in the three of the first person: ahaiṣīta, ahaiṣṭāṃ, ahaiṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ahaiṣīḥ, ahaiṣṭaṃ, ahaiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: ahaiṣaṃ, ahaiṣva, ahaiṣma: "went forth," or "greatly increased."

"Her acaṅi": "for h, when not caṅ." Before a following affix that is not caṅ and that is a cause for reduplicating the root, the latter h of hi, "going," is to be changed to the letter gh. Liṭ is applied to hi and the root is reduplicated; by "cu for ku and h," the h of the reduplicative syllable becomes jh; by "also car in the reduplicative syllable," jh becomes j; and when this sūtra changes the latter h to gh, in the three of the first person: jighāya, jighyatuḥ, jighyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jighetha, jighayitha, jighyathuḥ, jighya. In the three of the last person: jighāya, jighyiva, jighyima.

In luṭ, when guṇa is made: hetā, hetāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, when the vowel is lengthened by "not kṛt" and so on: hīyāta, hīyāstāṃ, hīyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, when guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on: heṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aheṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "kṛvi, in harming," also takes the ataṅ endings. "Dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca": "and a, for dhinvi and kṛṇvi." For dhivi, "living," and kṛvi, "harming," u arises in the place of śnu in the sense of the agent, and before that u the final letter v of the two is also to be changed to the letter a. For kṛvi: by "num for a root marked with i," the augment num, its m serving to fix its position and its u for pronunciation; this sūtra changes v to a; by "elision of a," the a is dropped; and when the n of num is joined to the u, "kṛṇu" is formed. When laṭ and so on are applied, in laṭ: kṛṇoti, and so on; in liṅ: kṛṇuyāta, and so on. In loṭ: kṛṇotu, and so on; and in laṅ: akṛṇota, and so on; the whole procedure is the same as in the section on śnu.

In luṅ: the iṭ of what begins with a val is given, and when the augment num is given by "num for a root marked with i": akṛṇvīta, akṛṇviṣṭāṃ, akṛṇviṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ also, when num is given and it is formed by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: cakṛṇva, cakṛṇvatuḥ, cakṛṇvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cakṛṇvitha, cakṛṇvathuḥ, cakṛṇva. In the three of the last person: cakṛṇva, cakṛṇviva, cakṛṇvima. In luṭ, when num and iṭ are given: kṛṇvitā, kṛṇvitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, when num is given: kṛṇvyāta, kṛṇvyāstāṃ, kṛṇvyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: kṛṇviṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ also: akṛṇviṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "dhivi, in living," also takes the ataṅ endings. By "and a, for dhinvi and kṛṇvi," in the place of śnu, u, and v becomes a; by "num for a root marked with i," the augment num; and when the a is dropped by "elision of a," "dhinu" is formed. When laṭ and so on are applied to it, in laṭ: dhinoti, and so on; in liṅ: dhinuyāta, and so on. In loṭ: dhinotu, and so on; and in laṅ: adhinota, and so on.

In luṅ, when num and iṭ are given: adhinvīta, adhinviṣṭāṃ, adhinviṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, num being given, with reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: didhinva, didhinvatuḥ, didhinvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: didhinvitha, didhinvathuḥ, didhinva. In the three of the last person: didhinva, didhinviva, didhinvima. In luṭ: dhinvitā, dhinvitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: dhinvyāta, dhinvyāstāṃ, dhinvyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: dhinviṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: adhinviṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "dambhu, in deceiving," also takes the ataṅ endings. When the n is dropped by "not marked with i" and so on, in the three of the first person of laṭ: dabhnoti, dabhnutaḥ, dabhnuvanti. In the three of the middle person: dabhnoṣi, dabhnuthaḥ, dabhnutha. In the three of the last person: dabhnomi, dabhnuvaḥ, dabhnumaḥ. In liṅ: dabhnuyāta, dabhnuyātāṃ, dabhnuyuḥ, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: dabhnotu, dabhnutāt, dabhnutāṃ, dabhnuvantu. By "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on, u is changed to uv. In the three of the middle person: dabhnuhi, dabhnutāt, dabhnutaṃ, dabhnuta. In the three of the last person: dabhnavāni, dabhnavāva, dabhnavāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: adabhnota, adabhnutāṃ, adabhnuvan. In the three of the middle person: adabhnoḥ, adabhnutaṃ, adabhnuta. In the three of the last person: adabhnavaṃ, adabhnuva, adabhnuma. In luṅ, when iṭ is given: adambhīta, adambhiṣṭāṃ, adambhiṣuḥ, and so on.

The commentary cites the rule "śranthigranthidambhibhyaḥ paro 'pi liṭ kid vaktavyaḥ": "a liṭ that is not pit, following śranthi, granthi and dambhi, is stated to be kit." The liṭ substitutes not named pit that follow śrantha, "releasing," grantha, "stringing together," and dambhu, "deceiving," are to be stated to be named kit.

Again, the commentary cites the rule "kiti liṭi dambha etvaṃ vaktavyaḥ": "before a kit liṭ, the e of dambha is to be stated." Before a following liṭ named kit, the elision of the reduplicative syllable of dambha, the statement of e, and so on are to be made optional; thus, in the three of the first person of liṭ: dadambha, dadambhatuḥ, dadambhuḥ, dembhuḥ.

Again, the commentary cites the rule "śranthigranthidambhāṃ thali lopo vā": "before thal, for śranthi, granthi and dambha, optionally no elision." Before the thal substituted for the liṭ of śranthi, granthi and dambha also, the elision of the reduplicative syllable and the change to e are to be made optional; thus, in the three of the middle person: dadambhitha, dembhitha, dadambhathuḥ, dembhathuḥ, dadambha. In the three of the last person: dadambha, dadambhiva, dembhiva, dadambhima, dembhima.

In luṭ, when iṭ is given: dambhitā, dambhitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, when the n is dropped by "not marked with i" and so on: dabhyāta, dabhyāstāṃ, dabhyāsuḥ. In lṛṭ, when iṭ is given: dambhiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: adambhiṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "aśūṅ, in pervading," takes the taṅ endings. Before those beginning with an ac, u is changed to uv by "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on; and when this and the rest are done, in the three of the first person of laṭ: aśnute, aśnuvāte, aśnuvate. In the three of the middle person: aśnuṣe, aśnuvāthe, aśnudhve. In the three of the last person: aśnuve, aśnuvahe, aśnumahe. In liṅ, when the s is dropped by "not final" and so on and u is changed to uv: aśnuvīta, aśnuvīyātāṃ, aśnuvīran, and so on. In the three of the first person of loṭ: aśnutāṃ, aśnuvātāṃ, aśnuvatāṃ. In the three of the middle person: aśnuṣva, aśnuvāthāṃ, aśnudhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: aśnavai, aśnavāvahai, aśnavāmahai. In the three of the first person of laṅ: āśnuta, āśnuvātāṃ, āśnuvata. In the three of the middle person: āśnuthāḥ, āśnuvāthāṃ, āśnudhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: āśnuvi, āśnuvahi, āśnumahi.

In luṅ, iṭ is made optional by "what has ū as marker" and so on. In the alternative with iṭ: āśiṣṭa, āśiṣātāṃ, āśiṣata, and so on. In the singular of the first person of the alternative without iṭ: by "jhalo jhali," sic is dropped; by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; and when t is changed to ṭ by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ": āṣṭa. In the dual and plural: by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; and when s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: ākṣātāṃ, ākṣata. When the forms are derived in the same way as these, in the three of the middle person: āṣṭhāḥ, ākṣāthāṃ, āḍhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: ākṣi, ākṣvahi, ākṣmahi.

"Aśnoteś ca": "also for aśnoti." Before liṭ of aśnoti, after the reduplicative syllable that the root's reduplication produces and that is lengthened by "of the initial a," the augment nuṭ arises. Aśū with liṭ: the root is reduplicated; by "of the first," "dhas" and so on, ṣ and ḍ; by "of the initial a," it is lengthened; this sūtra gives the augment nuṭ, its ṭ serving to fix its position and its u for pronunciation; and when it is brought in, in the three of the first person: ānaśe, ānaśāte, ānaśire. In the three of the middle person: ānaśiṣe, ānakṣe, ānaśāthe, ānaśidhve, ānaśiḍhve, ānaḍhve. In the three of the last person: ānaśe, ānaśivahe, ānaśvahe, ānaśimahe, ānaśmahe.

In luṭ, when iṭ is made optional: aśitā, aśitāse, and so on; or aṣṭā, aṣṭāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, when iṭ is made optional: aśiṣīṣṭa, aśiṣīyāstāṃ, aśiṣīran, and so on; or, in the alternative without iṭ, by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; and when s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: akṣīṣṭa, akṣīyāstāṃ, akṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ also: aśiṣyate, and so on; or akṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: āśiṣyata, and so on; or ākṣyata, and so on.

"Iti pāṇinivyākaraṇasya sūtrāt svādayaḥ samāptāḥ": thus are completed the roots beginning with su, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa.

Thus, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, notes setting down the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great treatise of grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the section giving in broad outline the procedures, with their general rules and exceptions, for the roots beginning with su, in which śnu occurs in the place of śap in the sense of the agent, is for the present complete.

Now I shall explain the procedures for tuda and so on.

By the root listed as "tuda, in tormenting," laṭ and so on take both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. "Tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ": "śa after tuda and so on."

After the roots tuda and so on, śa occurs in the place of śap; its ś serves to mark it as śit. In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṭ: tudati, tudataḥ, tudanti. In the three of the middle person: tudasi, tudathaḥ, tudatha. In the three of the last person: tudāmi, tudāvaḥ, tudāmaḥ. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: tudate, tudete, tudante. In the three of the middle person: tudase, tudethe, tudadhve. In the three of the last person: tude, tudāvahe, tudāmahe.

In the ataṅ of liṅ: when it is formed by changing the yā of yāsuṭ to iy through "after a, iy for yā" and so on, in the three of the first person: tudeta, tudetāṃ, tudeyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tudeḥ, tudetaṃ, tudeta. In the three of the last person: tudeyaṃ, tudeva, tudema. In the taṅ, when the s is dropped by "not final" and so on, in the three of the first person: tudeta, tudeyātāṃ, tuderan. In the three of the middle person: tudethāḥ, tudeyāthāṃ, tudedhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: tudeya, tudevahi, tudemahi.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of loṭ: tudatu, tudatāt, tudatāṃ, tudantu. In the three of the middle person: tuda, tudatāt, tudataṃ, tudata. In the three of the last person: tudāni, tudāva, tudāma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ of loṭ: tudatāṃ, tudetāṃ, tudantāṃ. In the three of the middle person: tudasva, tudethāṃ, tudadhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: tudai, tudāvahai, tudāmahai.

In the three of the first person of the ataṅ of laṅ: atudata, atudatāṃ, atudan. In the three of the middle person: atudaḥ, atudataṃ, atudata. In the three of the last person: atudaṃ, atudāva, atudāma. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: atudata, atudetāṃ, atudanta. In the three of the middle person: atudathāḥ, atudethāṃ, atudadhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: atude, atudāvahi, atudāmahi.

In the ataṅ of luṅ: vṛddhi by "vada-vraja" and so on; before those beginning with a jhal, sic is dropped by "jhalo jhali"; and when it is formed by changing d to t through "khari ca" and so on, in the three of the first person: atautsīta, atauttāṃ, atautsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: atautsīḥ, atauttaṃ, atautta. In the three of the last person: atautsaṃ, atautsva, atautsma. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: atutta, atutsātāṃ, atutsata. In the three of the middle person: atutthāḥ, atutsāthāṃ, atuddhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: atutsi, atutsvahi, atutsmahi.

In liṭ, when it is formed by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: tutoda, tutudatuḥ, tutuduḥ. In the three of the middle person: tutoditha, tutottha, tutudathuḥ, tutuda. In the three of the last person: tutoda, tutuda, tutudiva, tutudima. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: tutude, tutudāte, tutudire. In the three of the middle person: tutudiṣe, tutudāthe, tutudidhve, tutudiḍhve. In the three of the last person: tutude, tutudivahe, tutudimahe.

In luṭ, when it is formed with guṇa by "pug-anta" and so on and with "khari ca" and so on, in the ataṅ: tottā, tottāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: tottā, tottāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: tudyāta, tudyāstāṃ, tudyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, when d is changed to t by "khari ca": tutsīṣṭa, tutsīyāstāṃ, tutsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, when guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on and d is changed to t by "khari ca," in the ataṅ: totsyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: totsyate, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṅ: atotsyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: atotsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "bhrasja, in frying," takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. For bhrasja, by "grahi, jyā, vayi, vyadhi, vaṣṭi, vicati, vṛścati, bhṛjjati" and so on, it is changed by samprasāraṇa; by "jaś for the jhals," s becomes d; and when it is formed by changing d to j through "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ" and so on, in the ataṅ of laṭ: bhṛjjati, and so on; and in the taṅ: bhṛjjate, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: bhṛjjeta, and so on; and in the taṅ: bhṛjjeta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: bhṛjjatu, and so on; and in the taṅ: bhṛjjatāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: abhṛjjata, and so on; and in the taṅ: abhṛjjata, and so on.

In luṅ, for the singular of the first person of the ataṅ: by "of s and k at the beginning of a conjunct," s is dropped; by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, j becomes ṣ; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; by "ādeśa" and so on, s becomes ṣ; and when vṛddhi is made by "vada-vraja" and so on: abhrākṣīta. In the dual: s is dropped by "at the beginning of a conjunct" and so on; by "jhalo jhali," sic is dropped; by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, j becomes ṣ; and when t is changed to ṭ by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ": abhrāṣṭāṃ. In the plural: s is dropped by "at the beginning of a conjunct" and so on; by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, j becomes ṣ; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; and when s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: abhrākṣuḥ. When the forms are derived in the same way as these, in the three of the middle person: abhrākṣīḥ, abhrāṣṭaṃ, abhrāṣṭa. In the three of the last person: abhrākṣaṃ, abhrākṣma.

In the taṅ, vṛddhi is not made, and when the rest is derived as before, in the three of the first person: abhraṣṭa, abhrakṣātāṃ, abhrakṣata. In the three of the middle person: abhraṣṭhāḥ, abhrakṣāthāṃ, abhraḍḍhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: abhrakṣi, abhrakṣvahi, abhrakṣmahi.

"Bhrasjo bharj anyatarasyām": "for bhrasja, optionally bharj."

Before following ārdhadhātuka endings, bhrasja is optionally to be changed to bharj. For bhrasja with liṭ, this sūtra changes it to bharj; by "also car in the reduplicative syllable," bh becomes b; and when it is formed by "the first hal remains" and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: babharja, babharjatuḥ, babharjuḥ. In the three of the middle person: babharjitha, babharṣṭha, babharjathuḥ, babharja. In the three of the last person: babharja, babharjiva, babharjima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: babharje, babharjāte, babharjire. In the three of the middle person: babharjiṣe, babharjāthe, babharjidhve, babharjiḍhve. In the three of the last person: by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, j becomes ṣ, and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," th becomes ṭh; babharje, babharjivahe, babharjimahe.

In the alternative where bhrasja is not changed to bharj: the root is reduplicated; by "the first hal remains," r and the rest are dropped; by "car in the reduplicative syllable," bh is changed to b; by "jaś for the jhals," s becomes d; and when it is formed by changing d to j through "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ" and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: babhrajja, babhrajjatuḥ, babhrajjuḥ. In the three of the middle person: babhrajjitha, babhraṣṭha, babhrajjathuḥ, babhrajja. In the three of the last person: babhrajja, babhrajjiva, babhrajjima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: babhrajje, babhrajjāte, babhrajjire. In the three of the middle person: babhrajjiṣe, babhrajjāthe, babhrajjidhve, babhrajjiḍhve. In the three of the last person: babhrajje; here, by "of s and k at the beginning of a conjunct," s is dropped; by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, j becomes ṣ; and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," j becomes ṭh; babhrajjivahe, babhrajjimahe.

In luṭ, in the alternative where bhrasja is changed to bharj: by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, j becomes ṣ, and when t is changed to ṭ by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," in the ataṅ: bharṣṭā, bharṣṭāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: bharṣṭā, bharṣṭāse, and so on. In the alternative where it is not changed to bharj: by "of s and k at the beginning of a conjunct," s is dropped; and by the change of j to ṣ through "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, in the ataṅ: bhraṣṭā, bhraṣṭāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: bhraṣṭā, bhraṣṭāse, and so on.

In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, when it is changed by samprasāraṇa through "grahi, jyā, vayi, vyadhi" and so on: bhṛjyāta, bhṛjyāstāṃ, bhṛjyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, for bhrasja, in the alternative where it is changed to bharj: by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, j becomes ṣ; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; and when s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: bharkṣīṣṭa, bharkṣīyāstāṃ, bharkṣīran, and so on. In the alternative where it is not changed to bharj: s is dropped by "at the beginning of a conjunct, s and k" and so on; by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, j becomes ṣ; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; and when s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: bhrakṣīṣṭa, bhrakṣīyāstāṃ, bhrakṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ, when it is formed in the same way as that, in the ataṅ of the alternative where it is changed to bharj: bharkṣyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: bharkṣyate, and so on. In the ataṅ of the alternative where it is not changed to bharj: bhrakṣyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: bhrakṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: in the ataṅ of the alternative where it is changed to bharj: abharkṣyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: abharkṣyata, and so on. In the ataṅ of the alternative where it is not changed to bharj: abhrakṣyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: abhrakṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "mucḷ, in liberation," also takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. "Śe mucādīnām": "for muc and so on, before śa." Mucḷ, "liberation"; lupḷ, "cutting"; vidḷ, "finding"; lipa, "smearing"; ṣica, "trickling"; kṛtī, "cutting"; piśa, "parts"; and ṣida, "setting in place": these are "muc and so on," and for them, before a following affix śa, the augment num arises. When num is given, in the ataṅ of laṭ: muñcati, and so on; and in the taṅ: muñcate, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: muñceta, and so on; and in the taṅ: muñceta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: muñcatu, and so on; and in the taṅ: muñcatāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: amuñcata, and so on; and in the taṅ: amuñcata, and so on.

In the ataṅ of luṅ, when cli is changed to aṅ by "puṣādi-dyutādi" and so on: amucata, amucatāṃ, amucana, and so on. In the taṅ: before those beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "jhalo jhali"; before the others, by "ku for cu," c becomes k; and when it is formed by the change to ṣ through "ādeśa" and so on, in the three of the first person: amukta, amukṣātāṃ, amukṣata. In the three of the middle person: amukthāḥ, amukṣāthāṃ, amugdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: amukṣi, amukṣvahi, amukṣmahi.

In liṭ, when it is formed by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: mumoca, mumucatuḥ, mumucuḥ. In the three of the middle person: mumocitha, mumoktha, mumucathuḥ, mumuca. In the three of the last person: mumoca, mumuciva, mumucima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: mumuce, mumucāte, mumucire. In the three of the middle person: mumuciṣe, mumucāthe, mumucidhve, mumuciḍhve. In the three of the last person: mumuce, mumucivahe, mumucimahe.

In luṭ: by "ku for cu," c is changed to k, and when guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on, in the ataṅ: moktā, moktāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: moktā, moktāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ, the c is simply brought in: mucyāta, mucyāstāṃ, mucyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: by "ku for cu," c is changed to k, and when s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: mokṣīṣṭa, mokṣīyāstāṃ, mokṣīran, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṭ: mokṣyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: mokṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ also, in the ataṅ: amokṣyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: amokṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "lipa, in smearing," also takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. When the augment num is given by "for muc and so on, before śa," in the ataṅ of laṭ: limpati, and so on; and in the taṅ: limpate, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: limpeta, and so on; and in the taṅ: limpeta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: limpatu, and so on; and in the taṅ: limpatāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: alimpata, and so on; and in the taṅ: alimpata, and so on.

In the ataṅ of luṅ, when cli is changed to aṅ by "also from lipi, sici and hve": alipata, alipatāṃ, alipana, and so on. In the taṅ, by "optionally before the ātmanepada endings," the change of cli to aṅ and its change to sic are made optional. In the alternative with aṅ: alipata, alipetāṃ, alipanta, and so on. In the alternative with sic: before those beginning with a jhal, when it is formed by the elision of sic through "jhalo jhali" and so on, in the three of the first person: alipta, alipsātāṃ, alipsata. In the three of the middle person: alipthāḥ, alipsāthāṃ, alibdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: alipsi, alipsvahi, alipsmahi.

In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: lilepa, lilipatuḥ, lilipuḥ. In the three of the middle person: lilepitha, lileptha, lilipathuḥ, lilipa. In the three of the last person: lilepa, lilipiva, lilipima. Likewise, in the three of the first person of the taṅ: lilipe, lilipāte, lilipire. In the three of the middle person: lilipiṣe, lilipāthe, lilipidhve, lilipiḍhve. In the three of the last person: lilipe, lilipivahe, lilipimahe.

In luṭ, when guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on, in the ataṅ: leptā, leptāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: leptā, leptāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: lipyāta, lipyāstāṃ, lipyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ, when guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on: lepsīṣṭa, lepsīyāstāṃ, lepsīran, and so on. In the ataṅ of lṛṭ: lepsyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: lepsyate, and so on. In the ataṅ of lṛṅ: alepsyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: alepsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ṣica, in trickling," also takes both the ataṅ and the taṅ endings. The augment num is given by "for muc and so on, before śa," and when the ṣ is changed to s by "s for the ṣ at the beginning of the root," in the ataṅ of laṭ: siñcati, and so on; and in the taṅ: siñcate, and so on. In the ataṅ of liṅ: siñceta, and so on; and in the taṅ: siñceta, and so on. In the ataṅ of loṭ: siñcatu, and so on; and in the taṅ: siñcatāṃ, and so on. In the ataṅ of laṅ: asiñcata, and so on; and in the taṅ: asiñcata, and so on.

In the ataṅ of luṅ, when cli is changed to aṅ by "also from lipi, sici and hve": asicata, asicatāṃ, asicana, and so on. In the taṅ, when sic and aṅ for cli are made optional by "optionally before the ātmanepada endings," in the alternative with aṅ: asicata, asicetāṃ, asicanta, and so on. In the alternative with sic: before those beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "jhalo jhali"; c becomes k by "ku for cu"; and by "ādeśa" and so on, in the three of the first person: asikta, asikṣātāṃ, asikṣata. In the three of the middle person: asikthāḥ, asikṣāthāṃ, asigdhvaṃ. In the three of the last person: asikṣi, asikṣvahi, asikṣmahi.

In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person of the ataṅ: siṣeca, siṣicatuḥ, siṣicuḥ. In the three of the middle person: siṣecitha, siṣektha, siṣicathuḥ, siṣica. In the three of the last person: siṣeca, siṣiciva, siṣicima. In the three of the first person of the taṅ: siṣice, siṣicāte, siṣicire. In the three of the middle person: siṣiciṣe, siṣicāthe, siṣicidhve, siṣiciḍhve. In the three of the last person: siṣice, siṣicivahe, siṣicimahe.

In luṭ: ku for cu, and when guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on, in the ataṅ: sektā, sektāsi, and so on; and in the taṅ: sektā, sektāse, and so on. In the ataṅ of the benedictive liṅ: sicyāta, sicyāstāṃ, sicyāsuḥ, and so on. In the taṅ: guṇa by "pug-anta" and so on; by "ku for cu," c becomes k; and when it is formed by "ādeśa" and so on: sekṣīṣṭa, sekṣīyāstāṃ, sekṣīran, and so on. Likewise, in the ataṅ of lṛṭ: sekṣyati, and so on; and in the taṅ: sekṣyate, and so on. When lṛṅ also is formed in the same way, in the ataṅ: asekṣyata, and so on; and in the taṅ: asekṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "kṛtī, in cutting," also takes the ataṅ endings. When the augment num is given by "for muc and so on, before śa," in laṭ: kṛntati, and so on; and in liṅ: kṛnteta, and so on. In loṭ: kṛntatu, and so on; and in laṅ: akṛntata, and so on. In luṅ, with the iṭ of what begins with a val, and when guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on: akartīta, akartiṣṭāṃ, akartiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ: reduplication; by "cu for ku and h," k becomes c; and by the change of ṛ to a through "a for ṛ" and so on, in the three of the first person: cakarta, cakṛtatuḥ, cakṛtuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cakartitha, cakṛtathuḥ, cakṛta. In the three of the last person: cakarta, cakṛtiva, cakṛtima. In luṭ, when iṭ is given and guṇa is made: kartitā, kartitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: kṛtyāta, kṛtyāstāṃ, kṛtyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: when iṭ is made optional by "before an s that is not of sic, for kṛt, cṛt, chṛd, tṛd and nṛt": kartiṣyati, and so on; or kartsyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: akartiṣyata, and so on; or akartsyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ṣū, in impelling," also takes the ataṅ endings. By "s for the ṣ at the beginning of the root," ṣ becomes s, and when u is changed to uv by "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on, in laṭ: suvati, and so on; and in liṅ: suveta, and so on. In loṭ: suvatu, and so on; and in laṅ: asuvata, and so on. In luṅ: the iṭ of what begins with a val is given, and when vṛddhi is made by "vṛddhi before sic, in the parasmaipada endings": asāvīta, asāviṣṭāṃ, asāviṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: suṣāva, suṣuvatuḥ, suṣuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: suṣavitha, suṣuvathuḥ, suṣuva. In the three of the last person: suṣāva, suṣava, suṣuviva, suṣuvima. In luṭ, when iṭ is given and guṇa is made: savitā, savitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: sūyāta, sūyāstāṃ, sūyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, with the iṭ of what begins with a val, and when guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on: saviṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: asaviṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ovraścū, in cutting," also takes the ataṅ endings. When it is changed by samprasāraṇa through "grahi, jyā" and so on, in laṭ: vṛścati, and so on; and in liṅ: vṛśceta, and so on. In loṭ: vṛścatu, and so on; and in laṅ: avṛścata, and so on.

In luṅ, iṭ is to be made optional by "what has ū as marker" and so on. In the alternative where iṭ is given: avraścīta, avraściṣṭāṃ, avraściṣuḥ, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ: by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, c becomes ṣ; and by the principle "when the cause is absent, what depends on the cause is absent too," ś reverts to s. By "of s and k at the beginning of a conjunct," s is dropped; before those beginning with a jhal, sic is dropped by "jhalo jhali," and "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" applies; and before those not beginning with a jhal, ṣ becomes k by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si"; and when it is formed by the change of s to ṣ through "ādeśa" and so on, in the three of the first person: avrākṣīta, avrāṣṭāṃ, avrākṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: avrākṣīḥ, avrāṣṭaṃ, avrāṣṭa. In the three of the last person: avrākṣaṃ, avrākṣva, avrākṣma.

In liṭ the root is reduplicated; by "of the doubled" and so on, the reduplicative syllable undergoes samprasāraṇa; by "a for ṛ," ṛ is changed back to a; and when it is formed with vṛddhi by "vada-vraja" and so on, and so forth, in the three of the first person: vavraśca, vavraścatuḥ, vavraścuḥ. In the three of the middle person: vavraścitha, vavraṣṭha, vavraścathuḥ, vavraśca. In the three of the last person: vavraśca, vavraściva, vavraścima.

In luṭ, when iṭ is made optional by "what has ū as marker" and so on, in the alternative with iṭ: vraścitā, vraścitāsi, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ: by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, c becomes ṣ; by "of s and k at the beginning of a conjunct," s is dropped; and when t is changed to ṭ by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ": vraṣṭā, vraṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, when it is changed by samprasāraṇa through "grahi, jyā" and so on: vṛścyāstāṃ, vṛścyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ, iṭ is to be made optional by "what has ū as marker" and so on. In the alternative with iṭ: vraściṣyati, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ: by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, c becomes ṣ. By the principle "when the cause is absent, what depends on the cause is absent too," since the letter c, which was the cause for s becoming ś, has gone to ṣ, the ś too reverts to s. By "of s and k at the beginning of a conjunct," that s is dropped; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ is changed to k; and when s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: vrakṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: avraściṣyata, and so on; or avrakṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "ṛccha, in going, in the senses, in perishing, and in bodily solidity," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: ṛcchati, and so on; in liṅ: ṛccheta, and so on. In loṭ: ṛcchatu, and so on; and in laṅ: ārcchata, and so on. In luṅ, when the iṭ of what begins with a val is given: ārcchīta, ārcchiṣṭāṃ, ārcchiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ: the root is reduplicated; by "a for ṛ," ṛ becomes a; by "of the initial a," it is lengthened; by "nuṭ after it, for what has two hals," nuṭ is given; and when vṛddhi is made by "āṭ for an initial ac" and "also after āṭ," and guṇa by "for ṛccha and those ending in ṝ," in the three of the first person: ānarccha, ānarcchatuḥ, ānarcchuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ānarcchitha, ānarcchathuḥ, ānarccha. In the three of the last person: ānarccha, ānarcchiva, ānarcchima. In luṭ, when iṭ is given: ṛcchitā, ṛcchitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: ṛcchyāta, ṛcchyāstāṃ, ṛcchyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ also, when iṭ is given: ṛcchiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ārcchiṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "kṝ, in scattering," also takes the ataṅ endings. By "i for the ṝ of a root," ṝ is changed to i, and when r is attached by "for ṛ, aṇ followed by r," in laṭ: kirati, and so on; and in liṅ: kireta, and so on. In loṭ: kiratu, and so on; and in laṅ: akirata, and so on. In luṅ, with the iṭ of what begins with a val, and when vṛddhi is made by "vṛddhi before sic, in the parasmaipada endings": akārīta, akāriṣṭāṃ, akāriṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ: the root is reduplicated; by "a for ṛ," ṛ becomes a; by "cu for ku and h," k becomes c; vṛddhi before the two ṇal; and when guṇa is made before the others by "for ṛccha and those ending in ṝ," in the three of the first person: cakāra, cakaratuḥ, cakaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: cakaritha, cakarathuḥ, cakara. In the three of the last person: cakāra, cakara, cakariva, cakarima.

In luṭ, when iṭ and īṭ are made optional by "optionally after vṛ and what ends in ṝ": karitā, karitāsi, and so on; or karītā, karītāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: by "i for the ṝ of a root," ṝ is changed to ir, and when it is lengthened by "of the penultimate": kīryāta, kīryāstāṃ, kīryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: iṭ and īṭ are made optional by "optionally after vṛ and what ends in ṝ," and when guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on: kariṣyati, and so on; or karīṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: akariṣyata, and so on; or akarīṣyata, and so on.

"Kiratau lavane": "for kirati, in the sense of cutting." For kirati after the upasarga upa, in the sense of cutting, the augment suṭ arises: upaskirati. "Aḍabhyāsavyavāye 'pi": "even when aṭ or the reduplicative syllable intervenes." For kirati after upa, even when the augment aṭ or the reduplicative syllable intervenes, the augment suṭ arises before the k. With aṭ intervening: upāskirata, "was cutting near." With the reduplicative syllable intervening: upacaskāra, "cut near."

"Hiṃsāyāṃ prateś ca": "in harming, also after prati." When kṝ is used in the sense of harming, the augment suṭ also arises after upa and prati: upaskirati, pratiskirati, and so on.

The root listed as "gṝ, in making clear," also takes the ataṅ endings. "Aci vibhāṣā": "optionally before ac." Before a following affix that begins with an ac, the change of the letter r of gṛ to the letter l, or its remaining as r, is to be made optional. For gṝ with śa, meaning "harms closely" or "harms one by one": by "i for the ṝ of a root," ṝ becomes i; by "for ṛ, aṇ followed by r," r is given; and when this sūtra makes its change to l or not optional, in laṭ: girati, and so on; or gilati, and so on. Likewise in liṅ: gireta, and so on; or gileta, and so on. In loṭ: giratu, and so on; or gilatu, and so on. In laṅ: agirata, and so on; or agilata, and so on.

In luṅ: iṭ is given; vṛddhi is made by "vṛddhi before sic, in the parasmaipada endings"; and when, by "optionally before ac," the change of r to l or not is made optional: agārīta, agāriṣṭāṃ, agāriṣuḥ, and so on; or agālīta, agāliṣṭāṃ, agāliṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ the root is reduplicated; by "a for ṛ," the ṛ of the reduplicative syllable becomes a; by "cu for ku and h," g becomes j; vṛddhi is made before the two ṇal; and when guṇa is made before the others by "for ṛccha and those ending in ṝ," in the three of the first person: jagāra, jagaratuḥ, jagaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: jagaritha, jagarathuḥ, jagara. In the three of the last person: jagāra, jagara, jagariva, jagarima. Or else, when r is changed to l by "optionally before ac": jagāla, jagalatuḥ, jagaluḥ, and so on.

In luṭ, iṭ and īṭ are made optional by "optionally after vṛ and what ends in ṝ," and, by "optionally before ac," the change of r to l or not is made optional; thus: garitā, garitāsi, and so on; or galitā, galitāsi, and so on. In the alternative with īṭ: garītā, garītāsi, and so on; or galītā, galītāsi, and so on.

In the benedictive liṅ: by "i for the ṝ of a root," ṝ becomes i; by "for ṛ, aṇ followed by r," r is attached; and when it is lengthened by "of the penultimate": gīryāta, gīryāstāṃ, gīryāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ: iṭ and īṭ are made optional by "optionally after what ends in ṝ," and the change of r to l or not is made optional by "optionally before ac"; thus, in the alternative where iṭ is given: gariṣyati, and so on; or galiṣyati, and so on. In the alternative with īṭ: garīṣyati, and so on; or galīṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, in the alternative with iṭ: agariṣyata, and so on; or agaliṣyata, and so on. In the alternative with īṭ: agarīṣyata, and so on; or agalīṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "tṛmpa, in satisfaction," also takes the ataṅ endings. When the n is dropped by "not marked with i" and so on, in laṭ: tṛpati, and so on; and in liṅ: tṛpeta, and so on. In loṭ: tṛpatu, and so on; and in laṅ: atṛpata, and so on.

The commentary cites the rule "tṛmpatumpatṛmpadambhagumpaumbhaśumbhāṃ śe vā num": "for tṛmpa, tumpa, tṛmpa, dambha, gumpa, umbha and śumbha, num optionally before śa." For the roots tṛmpa, "satisfaction"; tumpa, "harming"; dambha and gumpha, "knotting"; umbha, "filling"; and śumbha, "beauty": when, after their m and n have been dropped by "not marked with i" and so on, the affix śa follows, the augment num optionally arises in them again: tṛmpati, tṛmpeta, tṛmpatu, and in laṅ atṛmpata, and so on.

In luṅ, when iṭ is given: atṛmpiṣṭāṃ, atṛmpiṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ: the root is reduplicated; ṛ becomes a; and it is formed with the elision of n before the kit endings by "not marked with i" and so on, and so forth; in the three of the first person: tatṛmpa, tatṛpatuḥ, tatṛpuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tatṛmpitha, tatṛpathuḥ, tatṛpa. In the three of the last person: tatṛmpa, tatṛpiva, tatṛpima. In luṭ, when iṭ is given: tṛmpitā, tṛmpitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, when the n is dropped by "not marked with i" and so on: tṛpyāta, tṛpyāstāṃ, tṛpyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, when iṭ is given: tṛmpiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: atṛmpiṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "spṛśa, in touching all over," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: spṛśati, and so on; and in liṅ: spṛśeta, and so on. In loṭ: spṛśatu, and so on; and in laṅ: aspṛśata, and so on.

In luṅ, by "kṛṣa, mṛśa, spṛśa" and so on, cli is optionally changed to sic. In the alternative where it is changed to sic, am is made optional by "anudāttasya ca rdupadhasyānyatarasyām." In the alternative where am is given: by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; before those beginning with a jhal, sic is dropped by "jhalo jhali"; and when it is formed by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" and so on, and by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si" and so on, in the three of the first person: asprākṣīta, asprāṣṭāṃ, asprākṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: asprākṣīḥ, asprāṣṭaṃ, asprāṣṭa. In the three of the last person: asprākṣaṃ, asprākṣva, asprākṣma.

In the alternative where am is not given, the rest being alike: vṛddhi is made by "vada-vraja" and so on; with r brought in, it is changed to yaṇ by "iko yaṇ aci"; and then, when vṛddhi is made by "vada-vraja" and so on, in the three of the first person: aspārkṣīta, aspārṣṭāṃ, aspārkṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: aspārkṣīḥ, aspārṣṭaṃ, aspārṣṭa. In the three of the last person: aspārkṣaṃ, aspārkṣva, aspārkṣma.

Or else, by "ksa after what ends in śal, has ik as penultimate, and lacks iṭ," cli is changed to ksa; by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," k; and when it is formed by "ādeśa" and so on: aspṛkṣata, aspṛkṣatāṃ, aspṛkṣan, and so on.

In liṭ: the root is reduplicated; by "a for ṛ," ṛ becomes a; and when s is dropped by "preceded by śar" and so on, in the three of the first person: pasparśa, paspṛśatuḥ, paspṛśuḥ. In the three of the middle person: pasparśitha, pasparṣṭha, paspṛśathuḥ, paspṛśa. In the three of the last person: pasparśa, paspṛśiva, paspṛśima.

In luṭ: by "anudāttasya ca rdupadhasyānyatarasyām," the augment am is made optional; by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; and when it is formed by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" and so on: spraṣṭā, spraṣṭāsi, and so on; or sparṣṭā, sparṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: spṛśyāta, spṛśyāstāṃ, spṛśyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: am is made optional by "anudāttasya ca rdupadhasyānyatarasyām"; by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, ś becomes ṣ; and when s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on: sprakṣyati, and so on; or sparkṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: asparkṣyata, and so on.

The root listed as "cṛtī, in harming," also takes the ataṅ endings. In laṭ: cṛtati, and so on; and in liṅ: cṛteta, and so on. In loṭ: cṛtatu, and so on; and in laṅ: acṛtata, and so on. In luṅ, when iṭ is given and guṇa is made by "pug-anta" and so on: acartīta, acartiṣṭāṃ, acartiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ: reduplication, and when ṛ is changed to a by "a for ṛ," in the three of the first person: cacarta, cacṛtatuḥ, cacṛtuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cacartitha, cacṛtathuḥ, cacṛta. In the three of the last person: cacarta, cacṛtiva, cacṛtima. In luṭ, when iṭ is given and guṇa is made: cartitā, cartitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: cṛtyāta, cṛtyāstāṃ, cṛtyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, when iṭ is made optional by "kṛt, cṛt" and so on and guṇa is made: cartiṣyati, and so on; or cartsyati, and so on. In lṛṅ: acartiṣyata, and so on; or acartsyata, and so on.

For pracch, "in the sense of wishing to know," the a-affixes are likewise applied, and samprasāraṇa is substituted by "grahi-jyā" and so on. So in laṭ: pṛcchati, and so on; in liṅ: pṛcchet, and so on. In loṭ: pṛcchatu, and so on; in laṅ: apṛcchat, and so on.

In luṅ: ṣ by "vraśca" and so on; k by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si"; ṣ by "ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ" and so on; and before endings beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "jhalo jhali"; ṣṭu by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ"; and vṛddhi is made by "vada-vraja" and so on. So in the three of the first person: aprākṣīt, aprāṣṭām, aprākṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: aprākṣīḥ, aprāṣṭam, aprāṣṭa. In the three of the last person: aprākṣam, aprākṣva, aprākṣma.

In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: papraccha, papracchatuḥ, papracchuḥ. In the three of the middle person: papracchitha, papraṣṭha, papracchathuḥ, papraccha. In the three of the last person: papraccha, papracchiva, papracchima.

In luṭ: ṣ by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on, and t is changed to ṭ by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," so: praṣṭā, praṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, samprasāraṇa is substituted by "grahi-jyā" and so on, so: pṛcchyāt, pṛcchyāstām, pṛcchyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: ṣ by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on; k by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si"; and s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on, so: prakṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aprakṣyat, and so on.

For sṛj, "in the sense of emission," the a-affixes are likewise applied. In laṭ: sṛjati, and so on; in liṅ: sṛjet, and so on. In loṭ: sṛjatu, and so on; in laṅ: asṛjat, and so on.

In luṅ: by "sṛji-dṛśor jhaly am akiti," the augment am is given before a jhal that is not kit; yaṇ by "iko yaṇ aci"; j becomes ṣ by "vraśca" and so on; ṣ becomes k by "ṣaḍhoḥ" and so on; s becomes ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on; and before endings beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "jhalo jhali"; and "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" and so on apply. So in the three of the first person: asrākṣīt, asrāṣṭām, asrākṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: asrākṣīḥ, asrāṣṭam, asrāṣṭa. In the three of the last person: asrākṣam, asrākṣva, asrākṣma.

In liṭ, the form is produced by reduplication, by "ur at," which changes ṛ to a, and so on. In the three of the first person: sasarja, sasṛjatuḥ, sasṛjuḥ. In the three of the middle person: sasarjitha, sasraṣṭha, sasṛjathuḥ, sasṛja. In the three of the last person: sasarja, sasṛjiva, sasṛjima.

In luṭ: by "sṛji-dṛśor jhaly am akiti," am is given; yaṇ by "iko yaṇ"; j becomes ṣ by "vraśca" and so on; and "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" and so on apply, so: sraṣṭā, sraṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: sṛjyāt, sṛjyāstām, sṛjyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ: by "sṛji-dṛśor jhaly am akiti," the augment am is given; by "iko yaṇ aci," ṛ is changed to r; j becomes ṣ by "vraśca, bhrasja, mṛj, sṛj" and so on; ṣ becomes k by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si"; and s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on, so: srakṣyati, srakṣyataḥ, srakṣyanti, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: asrakṣyat, asrakṣyatām, asrakṣyan, and so on.

For ṭumasj, "in the sense of purification," the a-affixes likewise apply. By "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi," s becomes d, and by "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ," d is changed to j, and so on. So in laṭ: majjati, and so on; in liṅ: majjet, and so on. In loṭ: majjatu, and so on; in laṅ: amajjat, and so on.

In luṅ: s is elided by "skoḥ saṃyogādyoḥ"; vṛddhi by "vada-vraja" and so on; num is given by "masji-naśor" before a hal; j becomes g by "coḥ kuḥ"; g becomes k by "khari ca"; s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on; and before endings beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "jhalo jhali" and so on. So in the three of the first person: amāṅkṣīt, amāṅktām, amāṅkṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: amāṅkṣīḥ, amāṅktam, amāṅkta. In the three of the last person: amāṅkṣam, amāṅkṣva.

In liṭ, the form is produced by reduplication and so on. In the three of the first person: mamajja, mamajjatuḥ, mamajjuḥ. In the three of the middle person: mamajjitha, mamaṅktha, mamajja. In the three of the last person: mamajja, mamajjiva, mamajjima.

In luṭ: s is elided by "skoḥ saṃyogādyoḥ"; the augment num is given by "masji-naśor" before a hal; j becomes g by "coḥ kuḥ"; and g becomes k by "khari ca," so: maṅktā, maṅktārau, maṅktāraḥ, maṅktāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi," s becomes d, and by "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ," d is changed to j, so: majjyāt, majjyāstām, majjyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ: s is elided by "skoḥ saṃyogādyoḥ" and so on; the augment num is given by "masji-naśor" before a hal; j becomes g by "coḥ kuḥ"; g becomes k by "khari ca"; and s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on, so: maṅkṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: amaṅkṣyat, and so on.

For vicch, "in the sense of going," the a-affixes are likewise applied. The commentary quotes: "vicchirāyo vā," that is, "āya after vicch is optional." Although it was stated above that āya comes after gupū, dhūpa, vicch, paṇa and pana, after vicch āya is to be optional. So in laṭ: vicchāyati, and so on, or vicchati, and so on. In liṅ: vicchāyet, and so on, or vicchet, and so on. In loṭ: vicchāyatu, and so on, or the like. In laṅ: avicchāyat, and so on, or avicchat, and so on.

In luṅ, iṭ is given and a is elided by the rule of elision, so: avicchāyīt, avicchāyiṣuḥ, and so on; or avicchīt, avicchiṣṭām, avicchiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, where āya is applied, the form is produced by applying ām through the rule on kās and stems ending in an affix, and so on: vicchāyāṃ cakāra, vicchāyāṃ babhūva, vicchāyām āsa, and so on. Where there is no āya, by reduplication, in the three of the first person: viviccha, vivicchatuḥ, vivicchuḥ. In the three of the middle person: vivicchitha, vivicchathuḥ, viviccha. In the three of the last person: viviccha, vivicchiva, vivicchima.

In luṭ, iṭ is made optional, so: vicchāyitā, vicchāyitāsi, and so on; or vicchitā, vicchitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: vicchāyyāt, vicchāyyāstām, vicchāyyāsuḥ, and so on; or vicchyāt, vicchyāstām, vicchyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, so: vicchāyiṣyati, and so on; or vicchiṣyati, and so on. In lṛṅ: avicchāyiṣyat, and so on; or avicchiṣyat, and so on.

For mṛś, "in the sense of forbearance," the a-affixes are likewise applied. In laṭ: mṛśati, and so on; in liṅ: mṛśet, and so on. In loṭ: mṛśatu, and so on; in laṅ: amṛśat, and so on.

In luṅ, by "kṛṣa, mṛśa, spṛśa" and so on, cli is optionally changed to sic. Where there is sic, by "anudāttasya carḍupadhasya," the augment am is optional; it is made optional. Where am is given: ś becomes ṣ by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on; before endings beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "jhalo jhali"; and the form is produced by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" and so on, and by "ṣaḍhoḥ" and so on. So in the three of the first person: amrākṣīt, with vṛddhi by "vada-vraja" and so on; amrāṣṭām, amrākṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: amrākṣīḥ, amrāṣṭa. In the three of the last person: amrākṣam, amrākṣva, amrākṣma.

Where there is no am, the rest of the procedure is the same; vṛddhi is made by "vada-vraja" and so on, bringing in r, so in the three of the first person: amārkṣīt, amārṣṭām, amārkṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: amārkṣīḥ, amārṣṭam, amārṣṭa. In the three of the last person: amārkṣam, amārkṣva, amārkṣma.

Or else, by "śala igupadhād" and so on, cli is changed to ksa; ś becomes ṣ by "vraśca" and so on; ṣ becomes k by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si"; and s is changed to ṣ by "ādeśa" and so on, so: amṛkṣat, amṛkṣatām, amṛkṣan, and so on.

In liṭ, the root is reduplicated, and by "ur at," ṛ is made a. So in the three of the first person: mamarśa, mamṛśatuḥ, mamṛśuḥ. In the three of the middle person: mamarśitha, mamarṣṭha, mamṛśathuḥ, mamṛśa. In the three of the last person: mamarśa, mamṛśiva, mamṛśima.

In luṭ, am is made optional by "anudāttasya carḍupadhasya" and so on; ś becomes ṣ by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on; and the form is produced by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" and so on, so: mraṣṭā, mraṣṭāsi, and so on; or marṣṭā, marṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: mṛśyāt, mṛśyāstām, mṛśyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, am is made optional by "anudāttasya carḍupadhasya" and so on; ś becomes ṣ by "vraśca-bhrasja" and so on; ṣ becomes k by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si"; and the form is produced by "ādeśa" and so on, so: mrakṣyati, and so on; or markṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: amrakṣyat, and so on; or amarkṣyat, and so on.

For iṣu, "in the sense of desiring," the a-affixes likewise enter, and by "iṣu-gami-yamāṃ chaḥ," ṣ is changed to ch. In laṭ: icchati, and so on; in liṅ: icchet, and so on. In loṭ: icchatu, and so on; in laṅ: aicchat, and so on.

In luṅ, the iṭ that goes with what begins with a val is given; āṭ by "āḍ ajādīnām" and so on; and vṛddhi is made by "āṭaś ca," so: aiṣīt, aiṣiṣṭām, aiṣiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, the form is produced by reduplication and so on. In the three of the first person: āṭ by "ajādi" and so on, and vṛddhi by "āṭaś ca"; iyeṣa, with guṇa by "pugantalaghūpadha" and so on, and the change to iy by "abhyāsasyāsavarṇe" and so on; īṣatuḥ, īṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: iyeṣitha, īṣathuḥ, īṣa. In the three of the last person: iyeṣa, īṣiva, īṣima.

In luṭ, iṭ is made optional by "iṣu, tīṣa, lubha, ruṣa, riṣa," so: eṣitā, eṣitāsi, and so on; or eṣṭā, eṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: iṣyāt, iṣyāstām, iṣyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, guṇa by "pugantalaghūpadha" and so on, and iṭ is given, so: eṣiṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aiṣiṣyat, and so on.

For kuṭ, "in the sense of crookedness," the a-affixes are likewise applied. In laṭ: kuṭati, and so on; in liṅ: kuṭet, and so on; in loṭ: kuṭatu, and so on; in laṅ: akuṭat, and so on.

In luṅ, by "gāṅ-kuṭādibhyo 'ñṇin ṅit," affixes after gāṅ, kuṭ and the rest that are not ñit or ṇit are ṅit, so guṇa, vṛddhi and the like are not made; and iṭ is given, so: akuṭīt, akuṭiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, the form is produced by reduplication and so on. In the three of the first person: cukoṭa, cukuṭatuḥ, cukuṭuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cukuṭitha, cukuṭathuḥ, cukuṭa. In the three of the last person: cukoṭa, cukuṭiva, cukuṭima.

In luṭ, iṭ is given, and by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on guṇa is not made: kuṭitā, kuṭitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: kuṭyāt, kuṭyāstām, kuṭyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, and by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on guṇa is not made: kuṭiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: akuṭiṣyat, and so on.

For vyac, "in the sense of deceiving," the a-affixes are likewise applied, and samprasāraṇa is substituted by "grahi-jyā" and so on, so: vicati, and so on; in liṅ: vicet, and so on. In loṭ: vicatu, and so on; in laṅ: avicat, and so on.

In luṅ, the iṭ that goes with what begins with a val is given. Because the affix is ṅit by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on, samprasāraṇa is made before the ṅit by "grahi-jyā" and so on, so: avicīt, aviciṣṭām, aviciṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, the root is reduplicated. Before the two ṇal endings, the reduplicative syllable is changed by samprasāraṇa through "of both" and so on; before the others, both syllables undergo samprasāraṇa by "grahi-jyā" and so on. So in the three of the first person: vivyāca, vivicatuḥ, vivicuḥ. In the three of the middle person: vivicitha, vivicathuḥ, vivica. In the three of the last person: vivyāca or vivyaca, viviciva, vivicima.

In luṭ, iṭ is given; because the affix is ṅit by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on, samprasāraṇa is made before the ṅit by "grahi-jyā" and so on, so: vicitā, vicitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, samprasāraṇa is made by "grahi-jyā" and so on, so: vicyāt, vicyāstām, vicyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ that goes with what begins with a val is given; because the affix is ṅit by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on, samprasāraṇa is made before the ṅit by "grahi-jyā" and so on, so: viciṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aviciṣyat, and so on.

For truṭ, "in the sense of cutting," the a-affixes are likewise applied. By "vā bhrāśa-bhlāśa-klamu-kramu-trasi-truṭi-laṣaḥ," it is optional, and śa or śyan is made optionally, so in laṭ: truṭati, and so on; or truṭyati, and so on. In liṅ: truṭet, and so on; or truṭyet, and so on. In loṭ: truṭatu, and so on; or truṭyatu, and so on. In laṅ: atruṭat, and so on; or atruṭyat, and so on. In luṅ, by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on, guṇa, vṛddhi and the like are not made, and iṭ is given, so: atruṭīt, atruṭiṣṭām, atruṭiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, by reduplication and so on: tutroṭa, tutruṭatuḥ, tutruṭuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tutruṭitha, tutruṭathuḥ, tutruṭa. In the three of the last person: tutroṭa, tutruṭiva, tutruṭima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, and by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on guṇa is not made: truṭitā, truṭitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: truṭyāt, truṭyāstām, truṭyāsuḥ. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, and by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on guṇa is not made: truṭiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: atruṭiṣyat, and so on.

For sphur, "in the sense of radiating," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. In laṭ: sphurati, and so on; in liṅ: sphuret, and so on. In loṭ: sphuratu, and so on; in laṅ: asphurat, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, and by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on guṇa and the like are not made, so: asphurīt, asphuriṣṭām, asphuriṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, the root is reduplicated; by "śarpūrvāḥ" and so on, s is elided; and by "abhyāse car ca," ph is changed to p, and so on. So in the three of the first person: pusphora, pusphuratuḥ, pusphuruḥ. In the three of the middle person: pusphuritha, pusphurathuḥ, pusphura. In the three of the last person: pusphora, pusphuriva, pusphurima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, and by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on guṇa is not made: sphuritā, sphuritāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, the penultimate vowel is lengthened by the rule on the penultimate, so: sphūryāt, sphūryāstām, sphūryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, and by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on guṇa is not made: sphuriṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: asphuriṣyat, and so on.

"Sphurati-sphulatyor nirnivibhyaḥ": "after nir, ni and vi, of sphurati and sphulati." That is, the s of sphurati and sphulati following nir, ni and vi is optionally changed to ṣ: niḥṣphurati, niḥsphurati; niṣphurati, nisphurati; viṣphurati, visphurati; niḥṣphulati, niḥsphulati, and so on.

For sphul, "in the sense of gathering together," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. Apart only from not lengthening in the case of the benedictive liṅ, the whole procedure is the same as for sphur: sphulati, and so on.

For ṇū, "in the sense of praising," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. By "ṇo naḥ," ṇ becomes n, and by "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on, it is changed to uv, so in laṭ: nuvati, and so on; in liṅ: nuvet, and so on. In loṭ: nuvatu, and so on; in laṅ: anuvat, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given; by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on, guṇa, vṛddhi and the like are not made; and by "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on, it is changed to uv, so: anuvīt, anuviṣṭām, anuviṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, there is reduplication; before the two ṇal endings there is vṛddhi, and before the others the change to uv, so in the three of the first person: nunāva, nunuvatuḥ, nunuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: nunuvitha, nunuvathuḥ, nunuva. In the three of the last person: nunāva or nunava, nunuviva, nunuvima. In luṭ, iṭ is given; by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on guṇa is not made; and by "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on it is changed to uv, so: nuvitā, nuvitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: nūyāt, nūyāstām, nūyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given; by "gāṅ-kuṭādi" and so on guṇa is not made; and by "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on it is changed to uv, so: nuviṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: anuviṣyat, and so on.

Mṛṅ is "in the sense of giving up life." "Mriyater luṅ-liṅoś ca": "after mriyate, also of luṅ and liṅ." After mriyate, the ātmanepada endings are applied in forms ending in an affix marked with ś, in luṅ, and in the benedictive liṅ, and in the others the parasmaipada endings are applied. By "riṅ śa-yak-liṅkṣu," before śa, yak and liṅ, the substitute riṅ is due, and ṛ is changed to ri; and by "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on it is changed to iy, so in laṭ: mriyate, and so on; in liṅ: mriyeta, and so on. In loṭ: mriyatām, and so on; in laṅ: amriyata, and so on.

In luṅ, before endings beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "from a short stem," and so on, so in the three of the first person: amṛta, amṛṣātām, amṛṣata. In the three of the middle person: amṛṣāthām, amṛḍhvam. In the three of the last person: amṛṣi, amṛṣvahi, amṛṣmahi, and so on.

In liṭ, the non-taṅ endings are applied, and the form is produced by reduplication and so on, so in the three of the first person: mamāra, mamratuḥ, mamruḥ. In the three of the middle person: mamaritha, mamartha, mamrathuḥ, mamra. In the three of the last person: mamāra, mamara, mamṛma. In luṭ too the non-taṅ endings are applied, and guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so: martā, martāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, since after mriyati the taṅ endings are applied in luṅ and liṅ: mṛṣīṣṭa, mṛṣīyāstām, mṛṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ the non-taṅ endings are applied; by "ṛd-dhanoḥ sye," iṭ is given before sya; and guṇa is made by the rule on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka, so: mariṣyati, and so on; and likewise, applying the non-taṅ endings in lṛṅ: amariṣyat, and so on.

For ovijī, "in the sense of fearing and trembling," the taṅ endings are applied. In laṭ: vijate, and so on; in liṅ: vijeta, and so on. In loṭ: vijatām, and so on; in laṅ: avijata, and so on.

"Vija iṭ": "after vij, iṭ." An affix beginning with iṭ that follows vij and is not designated ñit or ṇit is given the designation ṅit. Its purpose is to block guṇa and vṛddhi. In luṅ: avijiṣṭa, avijiṣātām, avijiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: vivije, vivijāte, vivijire. In the three of the middle person: vivijiṣe, vivijāthe, vivijiḍhve. In the three of the last person: vivije, vivijivahe, vivijimahe. In luṭ, iṭ is given; and because by "vija iṭ" it is ṅit, guṇa is not made: vijitā, vijitāse, and so on. Likewise in the benedictive liṅ: vijiṣīṣṭa, vijiṣīyāstām, vijiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, iṭ is given; and because by "vija iṭ" it is ṅit, guṇa is not made: vijiṣyate, vijiṣyete, vijiṣyante, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: avijiṣyata, avijiṣyetām, avijiṣyanta, and so on.

iti pāṇinibyākaraṇasya sūtrāttudādayaḥ samābhāḥ That is, the tud class and the rest, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, are complete.

With these, from the work called The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets out in the form of notes the sense, the procedures and the examples of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the rough account, with its general rules and exceptions, of the procedures for tud and the rest, in which śa enters in the domain of śap, the affix with the agentive sense, is for now complete.

Now I shall explain the procedures for rudh and the rest. For rudhir, "in the sense of obstructing," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings of laṭ and the rest are applied. "Rudhādibhyaḥ śnam": "after rudh and the rest, śnam." After rudh and the rest, śnam comes, in the agentive sense, after the final vowel. The ś means that it is śit, and the m, as a marker, means that it is placed after the final vowel.

In the parasmaipada first-person singular of laṭ: tip. By this sūtra śnam is given; the m serves for its position, the ś to make it śit; by "jhaṣas" and so on, t becomes dh; and by "jhal" and so on, dh is changed to d, so: ruṇaddhi. In the dual: tas; śnam is given and its markers are removed; by "śnasor allopaḥ," before a kit or ṅit affix, the vowel a of na is elided; by "jhaṣas" and so on, t becomes dh; by "jharo jhari savarṇe," the preceding dh is elided; and since the n is not at the end of a word, it is made anusvāra by "naś cāpadāntasya jhali," so: rundhaḥ. In the plural, jhi; by "jho 'ntaḥ" and so on: rundhanti. Producing them in the same way, in the three of the middle person: ruṇatsi, rundhaḥ. In the three of the last person: ruṇadhmi, rundhvaḥ.

Likewise for the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: rundhe, rundhāte, rundhate. In the three of the middle person: runtse, rundhāthe, rundhve. In the three of the last person: rundhe, rundhvahe, rundhmahe.
