In liṅ, by "śnasor allopaḥ," a is elided, and since the n is not at the end of a word, it is made anusvāra by "naś cāpadāntasya jhali," so with the non-taṅ endings: rundhyāt, rundhyātām, rundhyuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings the rest of the procedure is the same, and the s of sīyuṭ is elided by "anantyasya" and so on, so: rundhīta, rundhīyātām, rundhīran, and so on.

In loṭ, the forms are produced as in the case of laṭ. With the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: ruṇaddhu or rundhāt, rundhām, rundhantu. In the three of the middle person: rundhi or rundhāt, rundham, rundha. In the three of the last person: ruṇadhāni, ruṇadhāva, ruṇadhāma. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: rundhām, rundhātām, rundhatām. In the three of the middle person: runtsva, rundhāthām, rundhvam. In the three of the last person: ruṇadhai, ruṇadhāvahai, ruṇadhāmahai.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three of the first person: aruṇat, arundhām, arundhan. In the three of the middle person: aruṇaḥ, aruṇat or aruṇad, arundham, arundha. In the three of the last person: aruṇadham, arundhva, arundhma. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: arundha, arundhātām, arundhata. In the three of the middle person: arundhāḥ, arundhāthām, arundhvam. In the three of the last person, and for that form as well, it is produced by d becoming ru, the elision of u, r becoming visarga, ṇ optionally, the rule on what is not word-final, and so on: arundhi, arundhvahi, arundhmahi.

In luṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, by "irito vā" and so on, cli is optionally changed to aṅ or changed to sic. Where it is changed to aṅ: arudhat, arudhatām, arudhan, and so on. Where it is changed to sic, vṛddhi is made by "vada-vraja" and so on; before case endings beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "jhalo jhali"; by "jhaṣas" and so on, t and th become dh; and by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi" and so on, dh becomes d; and before those not beginning with a jhal, the forms are produced by "khari ca" and so on. So in the three of the first person: arautsīt, arauddhām, arautsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: arautsīḥ, arauddham, arauddha. In the three of the last person: arautsam, arautsva, arautsma.

With the taṅ endings: before those beginning with a jhal, sic is elided by "jhalo jhali"; by "jhaṣas" and so on, t and th become dh; by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi," dh becomes d; and before those not beginning with a jhal, car is substituted by "khari ca," and the forms are produced by changing jh to at and so on. So in the three of the first person: aruddha, arutsātām, arutsata. In the three of the middle person: aruddhāḥ, arutsāthām, aruddhvam. In the three of the last person: arutsi, arutsvahi, arutsmahi.

In liṭ, the forms are produced by reduplication and so on. With the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: rurodha, rurudhatuḥ, rurudhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: rurodhitha, rurudhathuḥ, rurudha. In the three of the last person: rurodha, rurudhiva, rurudhima. Likewise with the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: rurudhe, rurudhāte, rurudhire. In the three of the middle person: rurudhiṣe, rurudhāthe, rurudhidhve or rurudhiḍhve. In the three of the last person: rurudhe, rurudhivahe, rurudhimahe.

In luṭ, guṇa by "pugantalaghūpadha" and so on; by "jhaṣas" and so on, t becomes dh; and by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi," dh is changed to d, so with the non-taṅ endings: roddhā, roddhāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: roddhā, roddhāse, and so on.

In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: rudhyāt, rudhyāstām, rudhyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, by "khari ca," dh is changed to t, so: rutsīṣṭa, rutsīyāstām, rutsīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ, guṇa by "pugantalaghūpadha" and so on, and by "khari ca," dh is replaced by t, so with the non-taṅ endings: rotsyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: rotsyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: arotsyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: arotsyata, and so on.

For uchṛdir, "in the sense of shining and playing," the non-taṅ endings are applied. In the first-person singular of laṭ: tip. By "rudh" and so on, śnam is given, and by "khari ca," car is substituted and d is changed to t, so: chṛṇatti. In the dual: tas; śnam; ś and m are removed; by "śnasor allopaḥ," before a kit or ṅit affix, the a of na is elided; by "khari ca," car is substituted and d becomes t; and by "jharo jhari savarṇe," the preceding t is elided, so: chṛntaḥ. In the plural: jhi; jh becomes ant, and by "śnasor allopaḥ" a is elided, so: chṛndanti. Producing them in the same way, in the three of the middle person: chṛṇatsi, chṛnthaḥ, chṛntha. In the three of the last person: chṛṇadmi, chṛndvaḥ, chṛndmaḥ.

In liṅ, a is elided by "śnasor" and so on, so: chṛndyāt, chṛndyātām, chṛndyuḥ. In loṭ, the forms are produced as in the case of laṭ. In the three of the first person: chṛṇattu or chṛntāt, chṛntām, chṛndantu. In the three of the middle person: chṛndhi or chṛntāt, chṛntam, chṛnta. In the three of the last person: chṛṇadāni, chṛṇadāva, chṛṇadāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three of the first person: achṛṇad or achṛṇat, achṛntām, achṛndan. In the three of the middle person: achṛṇaḥ, achṛṇat or achṛṇad, achṛntam, achṛnta. In the three of the last person: achṛṇadam, achṛndva, achṛndma.

In luṅ, by "irito vā" and so on, cli is optionally made aṅ or sic. Where it is aṅ: achṛdat, achṛdatām, achṛdan, and so on. Where it is sic, iṭ. For that laṅ form, d becomes ru and r becomes visarga, optionally where it is not in final position, or else the d itself remains, or t. Iṭ is given, and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so: achardīt, achardiṣṭām, achardiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, there is reduplication; by "ur at," ṛ becomes a; and by "abhyāse car ca," ch is changed to c, and so on. So in the three of the first person: cacharda, cachṛdatuḥ, cachṛduḥ. In the three of the middle person: cacharditha, cachṛdathuḥ, cachṛda. In the three of the last person: cacharda, cachṛdiva, cachṛdima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so: charditā, charditāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: chṛdyāt, chṛdyāstām, chṛdyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ, by "kṛt, cṛt, chṛd, tṛd, nṛt," iṭ is made optional before an s that is not sic, and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on. So where there is iṭ: chardiṣyati, and so on; and where there is no iṭ: chartsyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: achardiṣyat, and so on; or achartsyat, and so on.

For utṛdir, "in the sense of harming and disrespect," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied, and the whole procedure is the same as for chṛd. In the three of the first person of laṭ: tṛṇatti, tṛntaḥ, tṛndanti. In the three of the middle person: tṛṇatsi, tṛnthaḥ, tṛntha. In the three of the last person: tṛṇadmi, tṛndvaḥ, tṛndmaḥ. In liṅ: tṛndyāt, tṛndyātām, and so on.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: tṛṇattu or tṛntāt, tṛntām, tṛndantu. In the three of the middle person: tṛndhi or tṛntāt, tṛntam, tṛnta. In the three of the last person: tṛṇadāni, tṛṇadāva, tṛṇadāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: atṛṇat or atṛṇad, atṛntām, atṛndan. In the three of the middle person: atṛṇaḥ, atṛṇat or atṛṇad, atṛntam, atṛnta. In the three of the last person: atṛṇadam, atṛndva, atṛndma.

In luṅ, by "irito vā" and so on, cli is optionally made aṅ or sic. Where it is aṅ: atṛdat, atṛdatām, atṛdan, and so on. Where it is sic, iṭ is given, so: atardīt, atardiṣṭām, atardiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: tatarda, tatṛdatuḥ, tatṛduḥ. In the three of the middle person: tatarditha, tatṛdathuḥ, tatṛda. In the three of the last person: tatarda, tatṛdiva, tatṛdima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, so: tarditā, tarditāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: tṛdyāt, tṛdyāstām, tṛdyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ, by "kṛt, cṛt, chṛd, tṛd, nṛd," iṭ is made optional before an s that is not sic. So where there is iṭ: tardiṣyati, and so on; and where there is no iṭ: tartsyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ too iṭ is made optional, so: atardiṣyat, and so on; or atartsyat, and so on.

For śiṣḷ, "in the sense of distinguishing," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. In the first-person singular of laṭ: tip. By "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," t is changed to ṭ, so: śinaṣṭi. In the dual: tas. By "śnasor allopaḥ," the a of na is elided; since the n is not at the end of a word, it becomes anusvāra by "naś cāpadāntasya jhali"; and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," t is changed to ṭ, so: śiṃṣṭaḥ. In the plural, a is elided by "śnasor" and so on, and n is made anusvāra, so: śiṃṣanti. In the middle-person singular: sip. By "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k, and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ, so: śinakṣi. In the dual and plural: śiṃṣṭhaḥ, śiṃṣṭha. In the three of the last person: śinaṣmi, śiṃṣvaḥ, śiṃṣmaḥ.

In liṅ, a is elided by "śnasor" and so on, so: śiṃṣyāt, śiṃṣyātām, śiṃṣyuḥ. In loṭ, the forms are produced as in the case of laṭ. In the three of the first person: śinaṣṭu or śiṃṣṭāt, śiṃṣṭām, śiṃṣantu. In the three of the middle person: śiṇḍhi or śiṃṣṭāt, śiṃṣṭam, śiṃṣṭa. In the three of the last person: śinaṣāṇi, śinaṣāva, śinaṣāma.

In laṅ, in the three of the first person: aśinaḍ or aśinaṭ, aśiṃṣṭām, aśiṃṣan. In the three of the middle person: by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi," ṣ becomes ḍ; by "hujhalbhyo her dhiḥ," hi becomes dhi; by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," dh becomes ḍh; and by "jharo jhari" and so on, ḍ is elided. Aśinaḍ or aśinaṭ, aśiṃṣṭam, aśiṃṣṭa. In the three of the last person: aśinaṣam, aśiṃṣva, aśiṃṣma.

In luṅ, by "irito vā" and so on, cli is changed to aṅ, so: aśiṣat, aśiṣatām, aśiṣan, and so on. In liṭ, by reduplication, in the three of the first person: śiśeṣa, śiśiṣatuḥ, śiśiṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: śiśeṣitha or śiśeṣṭha, śiśiṣathuḥ, śiśiṣa. In the three of the last person: śiśeṣa, śiśiṣiva, śiśiṣima. In luṭ, guṇa by "puganta" and so on, and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," t is changed to ṭ, so: śeṣṭā, śeṣṭāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: śiṣyāstām, śiṣyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ, guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ṣ becomes k; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ, so: śekṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aśekṣyat, and so on.

For tṛh, "in the sense of harming," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. "Tṛṇaha im": "after tṛṇah, im." Before a pit affix beginning with a hal, following the śnam of tṛṇah, the augment im comes; the m serves to fix its position.

In the first-person singular of laṭ: tip. By this sūtra im is given; with a, guṇa yields e; by "ho ḍhaḥ," h becomes ḍh; by "jhaṣas" and so on, t becomes dh; by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," dh becomes ḍh; and by "jharo jhari savarṇe," the preceding ḍh is elided, so: tṛṇeḍhi. In the dual: tas. By "śnasor allopaḥ," a is elided; by "ho ḍhaḥ," h becomes ḍh; by "jhaṣas" and so on, t becomes dh; by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," dh becomes ḍh; and by "jharo jhari savarṇe," the preceding ḍh is elided, so: tṛṇḍhaḥ. In the plural, a is elided by "śnasor" and so on, so: tṛṃhanti. In the middle-person singular: sip. By "tṛṇaha im," the augment im is given; the sandhi is made; by "ho ḍhaḥ," h becomes ḍh; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si," ḍh becomes k; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ, so: tṛṇekṣi. In the dual and plural: tṛṇḍhaḥ, tṛṇḍha. In the three of the last person: tṛṇehmi, tṛṃhvaḥ, tṛṃhmaḥ.

In liṅ, a is elided by "śnasor allopaḥ," so: tṛṃhyāt, tṛṃhyātām, tṛṃhyuḥ, and so on. In loṭ, the forms are produced as in the case of laṭ. In the three of the first person: tṛṇeḍhu or tṛṇḍhāt, tṛṇḍhām, tṛṃhantu. In the three of the middle person: tṛṇḍhi or tṛṇḍhāt, tṛṇḍham, tṛṇḍha. In the three of the last person: tṛṇahāni, tṛṇahāva, tṛṇahāma.

In laṅ, in the three of the first person: atṛṇeḍ or atṛṇeṭ, atṛṇḍhām, atṛṃhan. In the three of the middle person: atṛṇeḍ or atṛṇeṭ, atṛṇḍham, atṛṇḍha. In the three of the last person: atṛṇaham, atṛṃhva, atṛṃhma.

In luṅ, iṭ is given, and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so: atarhīt, atarhiṣṭām, atarhiṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, there is reduplication, and the forms are produced by "ur at," which changes ṛ to a, and so on. So in the three of the first person: tatarha, tatṛhatuḥ, tatṛhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tatarhitha, tatṛhathuḥ, tatṛha. In the three of the last person: tatarha, tatṛhiva, tatṛhima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so: tarhitā, tarhitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: tṛhyāt, tṛhyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ, the iṭ that goes with what begins with a val is given; guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ, so: tarhiṣyati, tarhiṣyataḥ, tarhiṣyanti, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, the iṭ that goes with what begins with a val is given; guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ, so: atarhiṣyat, atarhiṣyatām, and so on.

For hisi, "in the sense of harming," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. "Śnān na lopaḥ": "after śna, n is elided." The letter n following śna is to be elided. In the first-person singular of laṭ: tip. Śnam is given, and by "idit" and so on, num is given; by this sūtra that is elided, so: hinasti. In the dual, a is elided by "śnasor" and so on, so: hiṃstaḥ. In the plural: hiṃsanti. Producing them in the same way, in the three of the middle person: hinassi, hiṃsthaḥ, hiṃstha. In the three of the last person: hinasmi, hiṃsvaḥ, hiṃsmaḥ.

In liṅ, by "śnān na lopaḥ" the num that was given is elided, and a is elided by "śnasor" and so on, so: hiṃsyāt, hiṃsyātām, hiṃsyuḥ. In loṭ, the forms are produced as in the case of laṭ. In the three of the first person: hinastu or hiṃstāt, hiṃstām, hiṃsantu. In the three of the middle person: hindhi, where by "hujhalbhyo her dhiḥ," hi becomes dhi, and s is elided before dh; hiṃstāt, hiṃstam, hiṃsta. In the three of the last person: hinasāni, hinasāva, hinasāma.

In laṅ, in the three of the first person: ahinat, ahiṃstām, ahiṃsan. In the three of the middle person: ahinaḥ, ahiṃstam, ahiṃsta. In the three of the last person: ahinasam, ahiṃsva, ahiṃsma.

In luṅ, the augment num is given by "idit" and so on, and the iṭ that goes with what begins with a val is given, so: ahiṃsīt, ahiṃsiṣṭām, ahiṃsiṣuḥ. In liṭ, num is given because the root is idit, and the root is reduplicated; the forms are produced by "kuhoś cuḥ," which turns h into jh, and by "abhyāse car ca," which changes jh to j, and so on. So in the three of the first person: jihiṃsa, jihiṃsatuḥ, jihiṃsuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jihiṃsitha, jihiṃsathuḥ, jihiṃsa. In the three of the last person: jihiṃsa, jihiṃsiva, jihiṃsima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, so: hiṃsitā, hiṃsitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: hiṃsyāt, hiṃsyāstām, hiṃsyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, so: hiṃsiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ahiṃsiṣyat, and so on.

For añjū, "in the senses of manifesting, of eye ointment, of beauty and of going," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. Añjū takes śnam; by "śnān na lopaḥ," ñ is elided; by "coḥ kuḥ," j becomes g; by "khari ca," g is changed to k; and before kit and ṅit affixes, the forms are produced by "śnasor allopaḥ," which elides the a of na, and so on. So in the three of the first person of laṭ: anakti, aṅktaḥ, añjanti. In the three of the middle person: anakṣi, aṅkthaḥ, aṅktha. In the three of the last person: anajmi, añjvaḥ, añjmaḥ. In liṅ: añjyāt, añjyātām, añjyuḥ, and so on.

In the three of the first person of loṭ: anaktu or aṅktāt, aṅktām, añjantu. In the three of the middle person: aṅgdhi or aṅktāt, aṅktam, aṅkta. In the three of the last person: anajāni, anajāva, anajāma. In the three of the first person of laṅ: ānag or ānak, āṅktām, āñjan. In the three of the middle person: ānag or ānak, āṅktam, āṅkta. In the three of the last person: ānajam, āñjva, āñjma.

In luṅ: "añjeḥ sici": "after añj, before sic." Before sic following añj, iṭ always comes, so: āñjīt, āñjiṣṭām, āñjiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, the root is reduplicated; by "ata ādeḥ," the earlier a is lengthened; and after that, by "nuṭ" and so on, the augment nuṭ is given. So in the three of the first person: ānañja, ānañjatuḥ, ānañjuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ānañjitha, ānaṅktha, ānañjathuḥ, ānañja. In the three of the last person: ānañja, ānañjiva, ānañjima.

In luṭ, iṭ is made optional by "ūdit" and so on, so: añjitā, añjitāsi, and so on; or aṅktā, aṅktāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, ñ is elided by "anidit" and so on, so: ajyāt, ajyāstām, ajyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is made optional by "ūdit" and so on. Where there is no iṭ, by "coḥ kuḥ," j becomes g; by "khari ca," g becomes k; and by "ādeśa" and so on, s is changed to ṣ. So: añjiṣyati, and so on; or aṅkṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: āñjiṣyat, and so on; or āṅkṣyat, and so on.

For ñi-indhī, "in the sense of blazing," the taṅ endings are applied. By "śnān na lopaḥ," n is elided; before kit and ṅit affixes, by "śnasor allopaḥ," the a of na is elided; before endings beginning with t and th, by "jhaṣas" and so on, t and th become dh; and the forms are produced by "jharo jhari savarṇe," which elides the preceding dh, and so on. So in the three of the first person of laṭ: indhe, indhāte, indhate. In the three of the middle person: intse, indhāthe, indhve. In the three of the last person: indhe, indhvahe, indhmahe.

In liṅ, by "anantyasya" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is elided, and the a of na is elided, so: indhīta, indhīyātām, indhīran, and so on. In loṭ, the forms are produced as in the case of laṭ. In the three of the first person: indhām, indhātām, indhatām. In the three of the middle person: intsva, indhāthām, indhvam. In the three of the last person: inadhai, inadhāvahai, inadhāmahai.

In laṅ, the rest of the procedure is the same as before; āṭ is given by "ajādi" and so on, and vṛddhi is made by "āṭaś ca," so in the three of the first person: aindha, aindhātām, aindhata. In the three of the middle person: aindhāḥ, aindhāthām, aindhvam. In the three of the last person: aindhi, aindhvahi, aindhmahi. In luṅ, iṭ is given, so: aindhiṣṭa, aindhiṣātām, aindhiṣata.

In liṭ, ām is applied by "ijādeḥ" and so on, so: indhāṃ cakre, indhāṃ babhūva, indhām āsa, and so on. In luṭ: indhitā, indhitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ too, iṭ is given, and the forms are produced by "ādeśa" and so on, so: indhiṣīṣṭa, indhiṣīyāstām, indhiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, and the forms are produced by "ādeśa" and so on, so: indhiṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aindhiṣyata, and so on.

For vid, "in the sense of discerning," the taṅ endings are likewise applied. Śnam is given; before kit and ṅit affixes, the a is elided by "śnasor allopaḥ"; and the forms are produced by "khari ca," which substitutes car, and by "jharo jhari" and so on. So in the three of the first person of laṭ: vinte, vindāte, vindate. In the three of the middle person: vintse, vindāthe, vindhve. In the three of the last person: vinde, vindvahe, vindmahe.

In liṅ, by "anantyasya" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is elided, and by "śnasor allopaḥ," the a of na is elided, so: vindīta, vindīyātām, vindīran, and so on. In loṭ, the forms are produced as in the case of laṭ. In the three of the first person: vintām, vindātām, vindatām. In the three of the middle person: vintsva, vindāthām, vindhvam. In the three of the last person: vinadai, vinadāvahai, vinadāmahai.

In laṅ, in the three of the first person: avinta, avindātām, avindata. In the three of the middle person: avinthāḥ, avindāthām, avindhvam. In the three of the last person: avindi, avindvahi, avindmahi. In luṅ, iṭ is given, so: avediṣṭa, avediṣātām, avediṣata, and so on.

In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: vivide, vividāte, vividire. In the three of the middle person: vividiṣe, vividāthe, vivididhve or vividiḍhve. In the three of the last person: vivide, vividivahe, vividimahe. In luṭ, iṭ is given, and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so: veditā, veditāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, iṭ is given, so: vediṣīṣṭa, vediṣīyāstām, vediṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so: vediṣyate, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: avediṣyata, and so on.

ihi pāṇinibyākaraṇasya sūtruṅhādayanasmābtāḥ That is, rudh and the rest, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, are complete.

With these, from the work called The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets out in the form of notes the sense, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the rough account, with its general rules and exceptions, of the procedures for rudh and the rest, in which śnam enters in the domain of śap, is for now complete.

Now I shall explain the procedures for tan and the rest. For tanu, "in the sense of extending," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings of laṭ and the rest enter. Before sārvadhātuka endings, by "tanādi" and so on, u is due, and the affix u is applied after the root. So with the non-taṅ endings of laṭ, in the three of the first person: tanoti, tanutaḥ, tanvanti. In the three of the middle person: tanoṣi, tanuthaḥ, tanutha. In the three of the last person: tanomi, tanuvaḥ or tanvaḥ, tanumaḥ or tanmaḥ. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: tanute, tanvāte, tanvate. In the three of the middle person: tanuṣe, tanvāthe, tanudhve. In the three of the last person: tanve, tanuvahe or tanvahe, tanumahe or tanmahe.

In liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: tanuyāt, tanuyātām, tanuyuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, by "anantyasya" and so on, the s of sīyuṭ is elided, and by "iko yaṇ aci," the vowel is changed to its semivowel, so: tanvīta, tanvīyātām, tanvīran, and so on.

In loṭ, with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: tanotu or tanutāt, tanutām, tanvantu. In the three of the middle person: tanu or tanutāt, tanutam, tanuta. In the three of the last person: tanavāni, tanavāva, tanavāma. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: tanutām, tanvātām, tanvatām. In the three of the middle person: tanuṣva, tanvāthām, tanudhvam. In the three of the last person: tanavai, tanavāvahai, tanavāmahai. Hi is elided by "after the affix u" and so on.

In laṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: atanot, atanutām, atanvan. In the three of the middle person: atanoḥ, atanutam, atanuta. In the three of the last person: atanavam, atanuva or atanva, atanuma or atanma. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: atanuta, atanvātām, atanvata. In the three of the middle person: atanuthāḥ, atanvāthām, atanvāthām, atanudhvam. In the three of the last person: atanvi, atanuvahi or atanvahi, atanumahi or atanmahi.

In the parasmaipada of luṅ, iṭ is given, and vṛddhi is made optional by "halādi laghu" and so on, so: atānīt, atāniṣṭām, atāniṣuḥ, and so on; or atanīt, and so on.

With the taṅ endings: "tanādibhyas tathāsoḥ": "after tan and the rest, before ta and thās." The sic, the substitute in luṅ, following tan and the rest, is optionally elided before ta and thās. For tan in luṅ, ta: by this sūtra sic is optionally elided or not elided. Where sic is elided, by "anudāttopadeśa, vanati, tanoti and the rest," the nasal is to be elided before a jhal that is kit or ṅit, and n is elided. Where sic is not elided, iṭ is given, so: atata or ataniṣṭa. In the dual and plural of the first person: ataniṣātām, ataniṣata. In the middle-person singular, by "tanādibhyas tathāsoḥ," sic is optionally elided or not elided, so: atathāḥ or ataniṣṭhāḥ. In the dual and plural: ataniṣāthām, ataniḍhvam. In the three of the last person: ataniṣi, ataniṣvahi, ataniṣmahi.

In liṭ, there is reduplication, and before kit and ṅit affixes the reduplicative syllable is elided, and so on. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: tatāna, tenatuḥ, tenuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tatanitha, tenathuḥ, tena. In the three of the last person: tatāna or tatana, teniva, tenima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: tene, tenāte, tenire. In the three of the middle person: teniṣe, tenāthe, tenidhve or teniḍhve. In the three of the last person: tene, tenivahe, tenimahe.

In luṭ, iṭ is given, so with the non-taṅ endings: tanitā, tanitāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: tanitā, tanitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: tanyāt, tanyāstām, tanyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, iṭ is given, so: taniṣīṣṭa, taniṣīyāstām, taniṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: taniṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: taniṣyate, and so on. In lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: ataniṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: ataniṣyata, and so on.

For ṣaṇu, "in the sense of giving," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings enter. In laṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: sanoti, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: sanute, and so on. In liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: sanuyāt, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: sanvīta, and so on. In loṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: sanotu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: sanutām, and so on. In laṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: asanot, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: asanuta, and so on.

In luṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, iṭ is given, and vṛddhi is made optional by "halādi laghu" and so on, so: asānīt, asāniṣṭām, asāniṣuḥ, and so on; or else asanīt, and so on.

With the taṅ endings, before ta and thās, by "tanādibhyas tathāsoḥ," sic is optionally elided or not elided. Where sic is elided, n is elided by "anudāttopadeśa" and so on, and by "jana-sana-khanāṃ sañjhaloḥ," the vowel is lengthened. Where sic is not elided, and in the other forms, iṭ is given. So in the three of the first person: asāta or asaniṣṭa, asaniṣātām, asaniṣata. In the three of the middle person: asāthāḥ or asaniṣṭhāḥ, asaniṣāthām, asaniḍhvam. In the three of the last person: asaniṣi, asaniṣvahi, asaniṣmahi.

In liṭ, there is reduplication, and the forms are produced by the elision of the reduplicative syllable before kit and ṅit affixes, and so on. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: sasāna, senatuḥ, senuḥ. In the three of the middle person: sasanitha, senathuḥ, sena. In the three of the last person: sasāna or sasana, seniva, senima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: sene, senāte, senire. In the three of the middle person: seniṣe, senāthe, senidhve or seniḍhve. In the three of the last person: sene, senivahe, senimahe.

In luṭ, iṭ is given, so with the non-taṅ endings: sanitā, sanitāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: sanitā, sanitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, by "ye vibhāṣā," the final portion is optionally changed or not changed to ā, so: sāyāt, sāyāstām, sāyāsuḥ, and so on; or sanyāt, sanyāstām, sanyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, iṭ is given, so: saniṣīṣṭa, saniṣīyāstām, saniṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, so with the non-taṅ endings: saniṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: saniṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: asaniṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: asaniṣyata, and so on.

For kṣiṇu, "in the sense of harming," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings are applied. The commentary quotes: "u-pratyaye tanāder nopadhāguṇaḥ," that is, "before the affix u, there is no guṇa of the penultimate of tan and the rest." When the affix u follows, if the penultimate of tan and the rest is the letter ṛ, guṇa is made optional, and for the others guṇa is not to be made. So in laṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: kṣiṇoti, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kṣiṇute, and so on. In liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: kṣiṇuyāt, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kṣiṇvīta, and so on. In loṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: kṣiṇotu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kṣiṇutām, and so on. In laṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: akṣiṇot, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: akṣiṇuta, and so on.

In luṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, iṭ is given and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so: akṣeṇīt, akṣeṇiṣṭām, akṣeṇiṣuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, before ta and thās, by "tanādibhyas tathāsoḥ," sic is optionally elided or not elided. Where sic is elided, ṇ is elided by "anudāttopadeśa" and so on. Where sic is not elided, and in the other forms, iṭ is given and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on. So in the three of the first person: akṣita or akṣeṇiṣṭa, akṣeṇiṣātām, akṣeṇiṣata. In the three of the middle person: akṣithāḥ or akṣeṇiṣṭhāḥ, akṣeṇiṣāthām, akṣeṇiḍhvam. In the three of the last person: akṣeṇiṣi, akṣeṇiṣvahi, akṣeṇiṣmahi.

In liṭ, there is reduplication; by "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ," and by "kuhoś cuḥ," k becomes c; and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cikṣeṇa, cikṣeṇatuḥ, cikṣeṇuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cikṣiṇitha, cikṣeṇathuḥ, cikṣeṇa. In the three of the last person: cikṣeṇa, cikṣeṇiva, cikṣeṇima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cikṣeṇe, cikṣeṇāte, cikṣeṇire. In the three of the middle person: cikṣeṇiṣe, cikṣeṇāthe, cikṣeṇidhve or cikṣeṇiḍhve. In the three of the last person: cikṣeṇe, cikṣeṇivahe, cikṣeṇimahe.

In luṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so with the non-taṅ endings: kṣeṇitā, kṣeṇitāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kṣeṇitā, kṣeṇitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: kṣiṇyāt, kṣiṇyāstām, kṣiṇyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, iṭ is given and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so: kṣeṇiṣīṣṭa, kṣeṇiṣīyāstām, kṣeṇiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, iṭ is given and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so with the non-taṅ endings: kṣeṇiṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kṣeṇiṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: akṣeṇiṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: akṣeṇiṣyata, and so on.

For ṛṇu, "in the sense of going," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings are likewise applied, and by the cited rule on ṛ as the penultimate and so on, guṇa is made optional. So in laṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: ṛṇoti, and so on; or arṇoti, and so on. With the taṅ endings: ṛṇute, and so on; or arṇute, and so on. In liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: ṛṇuyāt, and so on; or arṇuyāt, and so on. With the taṅ endings: ṛṇvīta, and so on; or arṇvīta, and so on. In loṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: ṛṇotu, and so on; or arṇotu, and so on. With the taṅ endings: ṛṇutām, and so on; or arṇutām, and so on. In laṅ, āṭ is given by "ajādi" and so on, and vṛddhi is made by "āṭaś ca," so with the non-taṅ endings: ārṇot, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: ārṇuta, and so on.

In luṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, iṭ is given; āṭ is given by "ajādi" and so on; and vṛddhi is made by "āṭaś ca," so: ārṇīt, ārṇiṣṭām, ārṇiṣuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, before ta and thās, by "tanādibhyas tathāsoḥ," sic is optionally elided or not elided. Where it is elided, ṇ too is elided by "anudāttopadeśa" and so on. Where sic is not elided, and in the other forms, iṭ is given. So in the three of the first person: ārta or ārṇiṣṭa, ārṇiṣātām, ārṇiṣata. In the three of the middle person: ārthāḥ or ārṇiṣṭhāḥ, ārṇiṣāthām, ārṇiḍhvam. In the three of the last person: ārṇiṣi, ārṇiṣvahi, ārṇiṣmahi.

In liṭ, before the two ṇal endings and before thal, there is reduplication; by "ur at," ṛ becomes a; guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on; by "ata ādeḥ," the vowel is lengthened; and after that, by "dvihalaḥ" and so on, the augment nuṭ is given. Before the other, kit, endings, the root is reduplicated; by "ur at," the earlier ṛ becomes a; and with a, guṇa and sandhi are made. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: ānarṇa, arṇatuḥ, arṇuḥ. In the three of the middle person: ānarṇitha, arṇathuḥ, arṇa. In the three of the last person: ānarṇa, arṇiva, arṇima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: arṇe, arṇāte, arṇire. In the three of the middle person: arṇiṣe, arṇāthe, arṇidhve. In the three of the last person: arṇe, arṇivahe, arṇimahe.

In luṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so with the non-taṅ endings: arṇitā, arṇitāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: arṇitā, arṇitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: ṛṇyāt, ṛṇyāstām, ṛṇyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, iṭ is given and guṇa is made by "puganta" and so on, so: arṇiṣīṣṭa, arṇiṣīyāstām, arṇiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so with the non-taṅ endings: arṇiṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: arṇiṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: ārṇiṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: ārṇiṣyata, and so on.

For ḍukṛñ, "in the sense of making," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings likewise enter. Before the affix u, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka-ārdhadhātuka" and so on. Before those designated kit or ṅit, by "ata ut sārvadhātuke," the penultimate a becomes u; and before those beginning with a vowel, the forms are produced by "iko yaṇ aci," which changes the vowel to its semivowel, and so on. So with the non-taṅ endings of laṭ, in the three of the first person: karoti, kurutaḥ, kurvanti. In the three of the middle person: karoṣi, kuruthaḥ, kurutha. In the last-person singular: karomi.

"Nityaṃ karoteḥ": "after karoti, always." The affix u following karoti is always elided before v and m, so in the dual and plural of the last person: kurvaḥ, kurmaḥ. Producing them in the same way, with the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: kurute, kurvāte, kurvate. In the three of the middle person: kuruṣe, kurvāthe, kurudhve. In the three of the last person: kurve, kurvahe, kurmahe.

"Ye ca": "and before y." The u following karoti is also elided before an affix beginning with y, so in liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: kuryāt, kuryātām, kuryuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, the s of sīyuṭ is elided by "anantyasya" and so on, and by "iko yaṇ aci," u is changed to its semivowel, so: kurvīta, kurvīyātām, kurvīran, and so on.

In loṭ, the forms are produced as in the case of laṭ. With the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: karotu or kurutāt, kurutām, kurvantu. In the three of the middle person: kuru or kurutāt, kurutam, kuruta. In the three of the last person: karavāṇi, karavāva, karavāma. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: kurutām, kurvātām, kurvatām. In the three of the middle person: kuruṣva, kurvāthām, kurudhvam. Hi is elided by the rule "after u, when not preceded by a conjunct," and so on. In the three of the last person: karavai, karavāvahai, karavāmahai.

In laṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: akarot, akurutām, akurvan. In the three of the middle person: akaroḥ, akurutam, akuruta. In the three of the last person: akaravam, akurva, akurma. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: akuruta, akurvātām, akurvata. In the three of the middle person: akuruthāḥ, akurvāthām, akurudhvam. In the three of the last person: akurvi, akurvahi, akurmahi.

In luṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, vṛddhi is due by "sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu," and when vṛddhi is made, in the three of the first person: akārṣīt, akārṣṭām, akārṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: akārṣīḥ, akārṣṭam, akārṣṭa. In the three of the last person: akārṣam, akārṣva, akārṣma. With the taṅ endings, before those beginning with a jhal, the forms are produced by "hrasvād aṅgāt," which elides sic, and so on. So in the three of the first person: akṛta, akṛṣātām, akṛṣata. In the three of the middle person: akṛthāḥ, akṛṣāthām, akṛḍhvam. In the three of the last person: akṛṣi, akṛṣvahi, akṛṣmahi.

In liṭ, there is reduplication; by "ur at," ṛ becomes a; and by "kuhoś cuḥ," k is changed to c, and so on. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cakāra, cakratuḥ, cakruḥ. In the three of the middle person: cakartha, cakrathuḥ, cakra. In the three of the last person: cakāra or cakara, cakṛva, cakṛma. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cakre, cakrāte, cakrire. In the three of the middle person: cakṛṣe, cakrāthe, cakṛḍhve. In the three of the last person: cakre, cakṛvahe, cakṛmahe.

In luṭ, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so with the non-taṅ endings: kartā, kartāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kartā, kartāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, by "riṅ śayagliṅkṣu," ṛ is changed to ri, so: kriyāt, kriyāstām, kriyāsuḥ, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kṛṣīṣṭa, kṛṣīyāstām, kṛṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, by "ṛd-dhanoḥ sye," iṭ is given, and guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so with the non-taṅ endings: kariṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kariṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: akariṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: akariṣyata, and so on.

"Saṃparyupebhyaḥ karotau bhūṣaṇe": "after sam, pari and upa, for karoti, in the sense of adornment." After the prefixes sam, pari and upa, the augment suṭ comes for karoti in the sense of adornment; the ṭ serves to fix its position, and the u is for pronunciation. Saṃskaroti, "adorns well." Pariṣkaroti, "adorns all over," where the change to ṣ is by "pari, ni, vi" and so on. Upaskaroti, "adorns closely." Paryaskārṣīt, "adorned all over"; paryaṣkārṣīt.

For kṛ preceded by upa, in liṭ, even though aṭ or the reduplicative syllable intervenes, suṭ comes before the k: upacaskāra, "formerly adorned closely." For kṛ preceded by upa and by sam, in liṭ, even though aṭ or the reduplicative syllable intervenes, suṭ is given, and tas and jhi are changed. For kṛ preceded by pari, in luṅ, even though aṭ or the reduplicative syllable intervenes, suṭ is given before the k, and by "sivādīnāṃ vā" and so on, s is optionally made ṣ. Those two endings are changed to atus and us. Because the suṭ arises before the k, the liṭ endings after a conjunct are not kit, and so guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on. This should be applied by analogy to all the rest of both the non-taṅ and the taṅ forms. Upacaskaratuḥ, "the two formerly adorned closely." Saṃcaskaratuḥ, "the two formerly adorned well." Upacaskaruḥ, "they formerly adorned closely." Saṃcaskaruḥ, "they formerly adorned well." Saṃcaskaruḥ, "they formerly adorned well."

Since the commentary states that for kṛ preceded by suṭ, iṭ comes before the liṭ substitutes beginning with a val: "formerly adorned well"; saṃcaskaritha, "you two formerly adorned well"; saṃcaskariva; saṃcaskariṣe, "formerly adorned well," and so on. Saṃskriyāt: the benedictive liṅ.

"Samavāye ca": "also in the sense of assembling." After sam, pari and upa, suṭ also occurs for karoti in the sense of assembling: upaskaroti kanyām, "brings together closely with the girl"; saṃskaroti kanyām, "brings together properly with the girl"; pariṣkaroti kanyām, "brings together completely with the girl," and so on.

"Upāt pratiyatna-vaikṛta-vākyādhyāhāreṣu": "after upa, in the senses of effort, of stating a modification, and of supplying." After upa, suṭ comes for karoti in the senses of effort, of stating a modification, and of supplying. Kaṇṭhaṃ guṇasyopaskurute, "brings a quality to the throat," in the sense of effort. Upaskaroti bhuṅkte, "prepares the food," in the sense of stating a modification. Sopaskaroti śāstram, "furnishes the treatise with supplements," in the sense of supplying.

iti pāṇinibyākaraṇasya sūtrāttanādayaḥ samāptāḥ That is, tan and the rest, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, are complete.

With these, from the work called The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets out in the form of notes the sense, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the rough account, with its general rules and exceptions, of the procedures for tan and the rest, in which u enters in the domain of śap, the affix with the agentive sense, is for now complete.

Now I shall explain the procedures for krī and the rest. For ḍukrīñ, "in the sense of exchanging goods," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings likewise enter. "Kryādibhyaḥ śnā": "after krī and the rest, śnā."

After krī and the rest, śnā comes after the root in the domain of śap. Before those beginning with a hal and designated kit or ṅit, by "ī halyaghoḥ," ā becomes ī where the root is not ghu; and before those beginning with a vowel, ā is elided by "śnābhyastayor ātaḥ," and so on. So with the non-taṅ endings of laṭ, in the three of the first person: krīṇāti, krīṇītaḥ, krīṇanti. In the three of the middle person: krīṇāsi, krīṇīthaḥ, krīṇītha. In the three of the last person: krīṇāmi, krīṇīvaḥ, krīṇīmaḥ. Likewise with the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: krīṇīte, krīṇāte, krīṇate. In the three of the middle person: krīṇīṣe, krīṇāthe, krīṇīdhve. In the three of the last person: krīṇe, krīṇīvahe, krīṇīmahe.

In liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, ā is changed to ī by "not ghu" and so on, so: krīṇīyāt, krīṇīyātām, krīṇīyuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, the s of sīyuṭ is elided by "anantyasya" and so on, and by "śnābhyastayor ātaḥ," ā is elided, so: krīṇīta, krīṇīyātām, krīṇīran, and so on.

In loṭ, the forms are produced as in the case of laṭ. With the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: krīṇātu or krīṇītāt, krīṇītām, krīṇantu. In the three of the middle person: krīṇīhi or krīṇītāt, krīṇīta. In the three of the last person: krīṇāni, krīṇāva, krīṇāma. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: krīṇītām, krīṇātām, krīṇatām. In the three of the middle person: krīṇīṣva, krīṇāthām, krīṇīdhvam. In the three of the last person: krīṇai, krīṇāvahai, krīṇāmahai.

In laṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: akrīṇāt, akrīṇītām, akrīṇan. In the three of the middle person: akrīṇāḥ, akrīṇītam, akrīṇīta. In the three of the last person: akrīṇām, akrīṇīva, akrīṇīma. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: akrīṇīta, akrīṇātām, akrīṇata. In the three of the middle person: akrīṇīthāḥ, akrīṇāthām, akrīṇīdhvam. In the three of the last person: akrīṇi, akrīṇīvahi, akrīṇīmahi.

In luṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, vṛddhi is made by "sici vṛddhiḥ" and so on, so in the three of the first person: akraiṣīt, akraiṣṭām, akraiṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: akraiṣīḥ, akraiṣṭam, akraiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: akraiṣam, akraiṣva, akraiṣma. With the taṅ endings, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so in the three of the first person: akreṣṭa, akreṣātām, akreṣata. In the three of the middle person: akreṣṭhāḥ, akreṣāthām. In the three of the last person: akreṣi, akreṣvahi, akreṣmahi.

In liṭ, there is reduplication; and since this has a conjunct, the endings are not designated kit, so guṇa, vṛddhi and the rest are made. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cikrāya, cikrayatuḥ, cikrayuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cikrayitha or cikretha, cikrayathuḥ, cikraya. In the three of the last person: cikrāya or cikraya, cikrayiva, cikrayima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cikraye, cikrayāte, cikrayire. In the three of the middle person: cikrayiṣe, cikrayāthe, cikrayidhve or cikrayiḍhve. In the three of the last person: cikraye, cikrayivahe, cikrayimahe.

In luṭ, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so with the non-taṅ endings: kretā, kretāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kretā, kretāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: krīyāt, krīyāstām, krīyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on: kreṣīṣṭa, kreṣīyāstām, kreṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so with the non-taṅ endings: kreṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kreṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: akreṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: akreṣyata, and so on.

For skuñ, "in the sense of setting free," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings are likewise applied. "Stambhu-stumbhu-skambhu-skumbhu-skuñbhyaḥ śnuś ca": "after stambhu, stumbhu, skambhu, skumbhu and skuñ, also śnu." After stambhu, stumbhu, skambhu and skumbhu, which mean obstructing, and skuñ, which means setting free, śnā comes after the root in the domain of śap, and śnu also comes. So for skuñ, śnā and śnu are made optional. In laṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: skunāti, and so on; or skunoti, and so on. With the taṅ endings: skunīte, and so on; or skunute, and so on. In liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: skunīyāt, and so on; or skunuyāt, and so on. With the taṅ endings: skunīta, and so on; or skunvīta, and so on. In loṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: skunātu, and so on; or skunotu, and so on. With the taṅ endings: skunītām, and so on; or skunutām, and so on. In laṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: askunāt, and so on; or askunot, and so on. With the taṅ endings: askunīta, and so on; or askunuta, and so on.

In luṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, vṛddhi is due by "sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu," and when vṛddhi is made, in the three of the first person: askauṣīt, askauṣṭām, askauṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: askauṣīḥ, askauṣṭam, askauṣṭa. In the three of the last person: askauṣam, askauṣva, askauṣma. With the taṅ endings, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so in the three of the first person: askoṣṭa, askoṣātām, askoṣata. In the three of the middle person: askoṣṭhāḥ, askoṣāthām, askoḍhvam. In the three of the last person: askoṣi, askoṣvahi, askoṣmahi.

In liṭ, the root is reduplicated; by "śarpūrvāḥ" and so on, s is elided; by "kuhoś cuḥ," the guttural becomes a palatal; and vṛddhi, guṇa and the rest are made. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cuskāva, cuskavatuḥ, cuskavuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cuskavitha or cuskotha, cuskavathuḥ, cuskava. In the three of the last person: cuskāva or cuskava, cuskaviva, cuskavima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cuskave, cuskavāte, cuskavire. In the three of the middle person: cuskaviṣe, cuskavāthe, cuskavidhve. In the three of the last person: cuskave, cuskavivahe, cuskavimahe.

In luṭ, guṇa is made, so with the non-taṅ endings: skotā, skotāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: skotā, skotāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, the vowel is lengthened by "akṛt" and so on, so: skūyāt, skūyāstām, skūyāsuḥ, and so on.

With the taṅ endings, guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so: skoṣīṣṭa, skoṣīyāstām, and so on. In lṛṭ too guṇa is made, so with the non-taṅ endings: skoṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: skoṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: askoṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: askoṣyata, and so on.

For stambhu, "in the sense of obstructing," the non-taṅ endings likewise occur. By "stambhu-stumbhu" and so on, śnā and śnu are made optional, and by "anidit" and so on, m is elided. So in laṭ: stabhnāti, stabhnītaḥ, stabhnanti, and so on; or stabhnoti, stabhnutaḥ, stabhnuvanti, and so on. In liṅ: stabhnīyāt, stabhnīyātām, stabhnīyuḥ, and so on; or stabhnuyāt, stabhnuyātām, stabhnuyuḥ, and so on. In loṭ: stabhnātu or stabhnītāt, stabhnītām, stabhnantu, and so on; or stabhnotu or stabhnutāt, stabhnutām, stabhnuvantu, and so on. In laṅ: astabhnāt, astabhnītām, astabhnan, and so on; or astabhnot, astabhnutām, astabhnuvan, and so on.

In luṅ, by "jṝ, stambhu, mruc, mluc" and so on, cli is optionally made aṅ or sic. Where it is aṅ, m is elided by "anidit" and so on, so: astabhat, astabhatām, astabhatām, astabhan, and so on. Where it is sic, iṭ is given, so: astambhīt, astambhiṣṭām, astambhiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, there is reduplication, and s is elided by "śarpūrvāḥ" and so on, so in the three of the first person: tastambha, tastambhatuḥ, tastambhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tastambhitha, tastambhathuḥ, tastambha. In the three of the last person: tastambha, tastambhiva, tastambhima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, so: stambhitā, stambhitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, m is elided by "anidit" and so on, so: stabhyāt, stabhyāstām, stabhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ that goes with what begins with a val is given, so: stambhiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: astambhiṣyat, and so on.

For stumbhu, "in the sense of obstructing," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. Śnā and śnu are made optional, and m is elided by "anidit" and so on. So in laṭ: stubhnāti, and so on; or stubhnoti, and so on. In liṅ: stubhnīyāt, and so on; or stubhnuyāt, and so on. In loṭ: stubhnātu, and so on; or stubhnotu, and so on. In laṅ: astubhnāt, and so on; or astubhnot, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, so: astumbhīt, astumbhiṣṭām, astumbhiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, there is reduplication, and s is elided by "śarpūrvāḥ" and so on, so in the three of the first person: tustumbha, tustumbhatuḥ, tustumbhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: tustumbhitha, tustumbhathuḥ, tustumbha. In the three of the last person: tustumbha, tustumbhiva, tustumbhima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, so: stumbhitā, stumbhitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, m is elided by "anidit" and so on, so: stubhyāt, stubhyāstām, stubhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, so: stumbhiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: astumbhiṣyat, and so on.

For skambhu, "in the sense of obstructing," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. Śnā and śnu are made optional, and m is elided by "anidit" and so on. So in laṭ: skabhnāti, and so on; or skabhnoti, and so on. In liṅ: skabhnīyāt, and so on; or skabhnuyāt, and so on. In loṭ: skabhnātu, and so on; or skabhnotu, and so on. In laṅ: askabhnāt, and so on; or askabhnot, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, so: askambhīt, askambhiṣṭām, askambhiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, there is reduplication; s is elided by "śarpūrvāḥ" and so on; and by "kuhoś cuḥ," k is changed to c. So in the three of the first person: caskambha, caskambhatuḥ, caskambhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: caskambhitha, caskambhathuḥ, caskambha. In the three of the last person: caskambha, caskambhiva, caskambhima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, so: skambhitā, skambhitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, m is elided by "anidit" and so on, so: skabhyāt, skabhyāstām, skabhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, so: skambhiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: askambhiṣyat, and so on.

"Veḥ skabhnāter nityam": "after vi, of skabhnāti, always." The s of skambhu that has the affix śnā, following the prefix, always becomes ṣ: viṣkabhnāti, and so on. If it does not have the affix śnā, it does not change: viskabhnoti, and so on.

For skumbhu, "in the sense of obstructing," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. Śnā and śnu are made optional, and m is elided by "anidit" and so on. So in laṭ: skubhnāti, and so on; and skubhnoti, and so on. In liṅ: skubhnīyāt, and so on; or skubhnuyāt, and so on. In loṭ: skubhnātu, and so on; or skubhnotu, and so on. In laṅ: askubhnāt, and so on; or askubhnot, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, so: askumbhiṣṭām, askumbhiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, there is reduplication, and s is elided by "śarpūrvāḥ" and so on, so in the three of the first person: cuskumbha, cuskumbhatuḥ, cuskumbhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cuskumbhitha, cuskumbhathuḥ, cuskumbha. In the three of the last person: cuskumbha, cuskumbhiva, cuskumbhima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, so: skumbhitā, skumbhitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, m is elided by "anidit" and so on, so: skubhyāt, skubhyāstām, skubhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, so: skumbhiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: askumbhiṣyat, and so on.

For mīñ, "in the sense of harming," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings are applied. In laṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: mīnāti, and so on. In luṅ: mīnīte. By "mīnāti, minoti, dīṅ," that is, "also before lyap," the vowel is changed to ā. With the non-taṅ endings, by "yama, rama, nama and the roots ending in ā," sak is due; sak and iṭ are given, so: amāsīt, amāsiṣṭām, amāsiṣuḥ, and so on. And so on; and with the taṅ endings: amīnīta, and so on. In luṅ: by "mīnāti, minoti, dīṅ," that is, "also before lyap," the vowel is changed to ā. With the non-taṅ endings, by "yama, rama, nama and the roots ending in ā," sak is due; sak and iṭ are given, so: amāsīt, amāsiṣṭām, amāsiṣuḥ, and so on.

With the taṅ endings, s alone is brought in, so in the three of the first person: amāsta, amāsātām, amāsata. In the three of the middle person: amāsthāḥ, amāsāthām, amādhvam. In the three of the last person: amāsi, amāsvahi, amāsmahi.

In liṭ, before the two ṇal endings and before thal, the vowel is changed to ā by "mīnāti, minoti" and so on, and then there is reduplication. Before the others, the reduplicative syllable is due to be shortened and is shortened, and by "er anekācaḥ" and so on, the vowel is changed to its semivowel. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: mamau, mimyatuḥ, mimyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: mamitha or mamātha, mimyathuḥ, mimya. In the three of the last person: mamau, mimyiva, mimyima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: mimye, mimyāte, mimyire. In the three of the middle person: mimyiṣe, mimyāthe, mimyiḍhve. In the three of the last person: mimye, mimyivahe, mimyimahe.

In luṭ, the vowel is changed to ā by "mīnāti, minoti" and so on, so with the non-taṅ endings: mātā, mātāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: mātā, mātāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, the vowel is changed to ā by "mīnāti, minoti" and so on; by "er liṅi," e is due, and it is changed to e, so: meyāt, meyāstām, meyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, it is changed to ā, so: māsīṣṭa, māsīyāstām, māsīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, by "mīnāti, minoti, dīṅ," that is, "also before lyap," the vowel is changed to ā, so with the non-taṅ endings: māsyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: māsyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: amāsyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: amāsyata, and so on.

For pūñ, "in the sense of purifying," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings enter. "Pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ": "shortening of pū and the rest." The twenty roots pūñ and the rest are to be shortened before an affix that is śit. So in laṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: punāti, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: punīte, and so on. In liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: punīyāt, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: punīta, and so on. In loṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: punātu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: punītām, and so on. In laṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: apunāt, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: apunīta, and so on.

The commentary quotes: "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ, kecid vā," that is, "the shortening of pū and the rest is, in some cases, optional." For pū and the rest, before a śit affix, the change to a short vowel is in some cases made optional, so: punāti or pūnāti, and so on.

In luṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, iṭ is given, and vṛddhi is due by "sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu"; when vṛddhi is made: apāvīt, apāviṣṭām, apāviṣuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, iṭ is given and guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so: apaviṣṭa, apaviṣātām, apaviṣata, and so on.

In liṭ, there is reduplication, and before kit endings the vowel is changed to uv by "aci śnu-dhātu" and so on. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: pupāva, pupuvatuḥ, pupuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: pupavitha, pupuvathuḥ, pupuva. In the three of the last person: pupāva or pupava, pupuviva, pupuvima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: pupuve, pupuvāte, pupuvire. In the three of the middle person: pupuviṣe, pupuvāthe, pupuviḍhve, pupuviḍhve. In the three of the last person: pupuve, pupuvivahe, pupuvimahe.

In luṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so with the non-taṅ endings: pavitā, pavitāsi, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: pavitā, pavitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: pūyāt, pūyāstām, pūyāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: paviṣīṣṭa, paviṣīyāstām, paviṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ too, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so with the non-taṅ endings: paviṣyati, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: paviṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: apaviṣyat, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: apaviṣyata, and so on.

For kṝñ, "in the sense of harming," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings are likewise applied. By "shortening of pū and the rest," it is due to be shortened and is shortened, so in laṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: kṛṇāti, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kṛṇīte, and so on. In liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: kṛṇīyāt, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kṛṇīta, and so on. In loṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: kṛṇātu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: kṛṇītām, and so on. In laṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: akṛṇāt, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: akṛṇīta, and so on.

In luṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, iṭ is given, and vṛddhi is due by "sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu"; when vṛddhi is made: akārīt, akāriṣṭām, akāriṣuḥ. With the taṅ endings, by "vṝto vā," iṭ is optionally lengthened, so that iṭ or īṭ is optional, and guṇa is made by "sārvadhātuka" and so on, so: akariṣṭa, akariṣātām, akariṣata, and so on; or akarīṣṭa, akarīṣātām, akarīṣata, and so on.

In liṭ, there is reduplication; by "ur at," ṛ becomes a; by "kuhoś cuḥ," k becomes c; before the two ṇal endings there is vṛddhi; and before the others, guṇa is made by "ṛcchatyṝtām." So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cakāra, cakaratuḥ, cakaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: cakaritha, cakarathuḥ, cakara. In the three of the last person: cakāra or cakara, cakariva, cakarima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: cakare, cakarāte, cakarire. In the three of the middle person: cakariṣe, cakarāthe, cakaridhve or cakariḍhve. In the three of the last person: cakare, cakarivahe, cakarimahe.

In luṭ, by "vṝto vā," iṭ or īṭ is made optional, so with the non-taṅ endings: karitā, karitāsi, and so on; or karītā, karītāsi, and so on. With the taṅ endings: karitā, karitāse, and so on; or karītā, karītāse, and so on.

In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings, by "ṝta id dhātoḥ," ṛ becomes i; by "uraṇ raparaḥ," r is added after it; and by the rule on the penultimate it is lengthened, so: kīryāt, kīryāstām, kīryāsuḥ, and so on. With the taṅ endings, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: karīṣīṣṭa, karīṣīyāstām, karīṣīran, and so on.

In lṛṭ, by "vṝto vā," iṭ or īṭ is made optional, and guṇa is made, so with the non-taṅ endings: kariṣyati, and so on; or karīṣyati, and so on. With the taṅ endings: kariṣyate, and so on; or karīṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: akariṣyat, and so on; or akarīṣyat, and so on. With the taṅ endings: akariṣyata, and so on; or akarīṣyata, and so on.

For dhūñ, "in the sense of shaking," both the non-taṅ and the taṅ endings likewise apply. By "pū and the rest," it is due to be shortened and is shortened, so in laṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: dhunāti, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: dhunīte, and so on. In liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: dhunīyāt, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: dhunīta, and so on. In loṭ, with the non-taṅ endings: dhunātu, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: dhunītām, and so on. In laṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: adhunāt, and so on; and with the taṅ endings: adhunīta, and so on.

In luṅ, iṭ is made optional by "ūdit" and so on. With the non-taṅ endings, vṛddhi is made, so where there is iṭ: adhāvīt, adhāviṣṭām, adhāviṣuḥ, and so on. Where there is no iṭ, in the three of the first person: adhauṣīt, adhauṣṭām, adhauṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: adhauṣīḥ, adhauṣṭam, adhauṣṭa. In the three of the last person: adhauṣam, adhauṣva, adhauṣma. With the taṅ endings, guṇa is made, so: adhaviṣṭa, adhaviṣātām, adhaviṣata, and so on. Or, where there is no iṭ, in the three of the first person: adhoṣṭa, adhoṣātām, adhoṣata. In the three of the middle person: adhoṣṭhāḥ, adhoṣāthām, adhoḍhvam. In the three of the last person: adhoṣi, adhoṣvahi, adhoṣmahi.

In liṭ, the forms are produced by reduplication and so on. So with the non-taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: dudhāva, dudhuvatuḥ, dudhuvuḥ. In the three of the middle person: dudhavitha, dudhuvathuḥ, dudhuva. In the three of the last person: dudhāva, dudhuviva, dudhuvima. With the taṅ endings, in the three of the first person: dudhuve, dudhuvāte, dudhuvire. In the three of the middle person: dudhuviṣe, dudhuvāthe, dudhuvidhve or dudhuviḍhve. In the three of the last person: dudhuve, dudhuvivahe, dudhuvimahe.

In luṭ, iṭ is made optional by "ūdit" and so on, and guṇa is made, so with the non-taṅ endings: dhavitā, dhavitāsi, and so on; or dhotā, dhotāsi, and so on. With the taṅ endings: dhavitā, dhavitāse, and so on; or dhotā, dhotāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: dhūyāt, dhūyāstām, dhūyāsuḥ, and so on. In the ātmanepada, iṭ is made optional, so: dhaviṣīṣṭa, dhaviṣīyāstām, dhaviṣīran, and so on; or dhoṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ too iṭ is made optional, so with the non-taṅ endings: dhaviṣyati, and so on; or dhoṣyati, and so on. With the taṅ endings: dhaviṣyate, and so on; or dhoṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, with the non-taṅ endings: adhaviṣyat, and so on; or adhoṣyat, and so on. With the taṅ endings: adhaviṣyata, and so on; or adhoṣyata, and so on.

For grah, "in the sense of taking up," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. Samprasāraṇa is substituted by "grahi-jyā" and so on, so in laṭ: gṛhṇāti, gṛhṇītaḥ, gṛhṇanti, and so on; and in liṅ: gṛhṇīyāt, and so on. In loṭ, in the three of the first person: gṛhṇātu, gṛhṇītām, gṛhṇantu.

"Halaḥ śnaḥ śānaj jhau": "after a hal, śnā becomes śānac before hi." The śnā that follows a root ending in a hal is to be changed to what is called śānac before hi, the substitute in loṭ. For grah in loṭ: śnā; samprasāraṇa is substituted by "grahi" and so on; sip; by "ser hy apic ca" and so on, sip becomes hi; by this sūtra, śnā is changed to śānac, the c serving the vowel and the ś making it śit; and by "ato heḥ," hi is due to be elided and is elided, so: gṛhāṇa. In the dual and plural: gṛhṇītam, gṛhṇīta. In the three of the last person: gṛhṇāni, gṛhṇāva, gṛhṇāma. In laṅ: agṛhṇāt, agṛhṇītām, agṛhṇan, and so on.

"Graho 'liṭi dīrghaḥ": "after grah, when not in liṭ, a long vowel." Before ārdhadhātuka endings beginning with a val that follow grah and are not liṭ, iṭ becomes long, so in luṅ: agrahīt, agrahīṣṭām, agrahīṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, the root is reduplicated. Before the two ṇal endings and thal, the reduplicative syllable undergoes samprasāraṇa by "of both" and so on, and before the others both syllables undergo samprasāraṇa by "grahi" and so on; by "ur at," ṛ becomes a; and by "kuhoś cuḥ," g is changed to j, and so on. So in the three of the first person: jagrāha, jagṛhatuḥ, jagṛhuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jagrahitha, jagṛhathuḥ, jagṛha. In the three of the last person: jagrāha or jagraha, jagṛhiva, jagṛhima.

In luṭ, the iṭ that goes with what begins with a val is given; by "graho 'liṭi dīrghaḥ" it is due to be long and is lengthened, so: grahītā, grahītāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, samprasāraṇa is substituted by "grahi-jyā" and so on, so: gṛhyāt, gṛhyāstām, gṛhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ by "valādi" and so on, and it is lengthened by "graho 'liṭi" and so on, so: grahīṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: agrahīṣyat, and so on.

For śṝ, "in the sense of harming," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. By "pū and the rest," it is due to be shortened and is shortened, so in laṭ: śṛṇāti, and so on; and in liṅ: śṛṇīyāt, and so on. In loṭ: śṛṇātu, and so on; and in laṅ: aśṛṇāt, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, and vṛddhi is made by "sici vṛddhiḥ" and so on, so: aśārīt, aśāriṣṭām, aśāriṣuḥ, and so on.

"Śṝ-dṝ-prāṃ hrasvo vā": "shortening of śṝ, dṝ and pṝ, optionally." Before the kit and ṅit substitutes of liṭ, śṝ, "harming," dṝ, "tearing," and pṝ, "nourishing," are optionally shortened. Where they are shortened, "iko yaṇ aci" applies; where they are not, guṇa is made by "ṛcchatyṝtām." So in the three of the first person: śaśāra, śaśratuḥ or śaśaratuḥ, śaśruḥ or śaśaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: śaśaritha, śaśrathuḥ or śaśarathuḥ, śaśra or śaśara. In the three of the last person: śaśāra or śaśara, śaśriva or śaśariva, śaśrima or śaśarima.

In luṭ, by "vṝto vā," iṭ or īṭ is made optional, so: śaritā, śaritāsi, and so on; or śarītā, śarītāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "ṝta id dhātoḥ," ṛ becomes i, and by the rule on the penultimate it is lengthened, so: śīryāt, śīryāstām, śīryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by "vṝto vā," iṭ or īṭ is made optional, so: śariṣyati, and so on; or śarīṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: aśariṣyat, and so on; or aśarīṣyat, and so on.

For dṝ, "in the sense of tearing," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. It is shortened by "pū" and so on, so in laṭ: dṛṇāti, and so on; in liṅ: dṛṇīyāt, and so on; in loṭ: dṛṇātu, and so on; and in laṅ: adṛṇāt, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given and vṛddhi is made, so: adārīt, adāriṣṭām, adāriṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, before kit endings, by "śṝ, dṝ, pṝ," the vowel is optionally shortened. Where it is shortened, yaṇ applies; and where it is not changed, guṇa is made by "ṛcchatyṝtām." So in the three of the first person: dadāra, dadratuḥ or dadaratuḥ, dadruḥ or dadaruḥ. In the three of the middle person: dadaritha, dadrathuḥ or dadarathuḥ, dadra or dadara. In the three of the last person: dadāra or dadara, dadriva or dadariva, dadrima or dadarima.

In luṭ, by "vṝto vā," iṭ or īṭ is made optional, so: daritā, daritāsi, and so on; or darītā, darītāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "ṝta id dhātoḥ," ṛ becomes i, and by the rule on the penultimate it is lengthened, so: dīryāt, dīryāstām, dīryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by "vṝto vā" and so on, iṭ or īṭ is made optional, so: dariṣyati, and so on; or darīṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: adariṣyat, and so on; or adarīṣyat, and so on.

For pṝ, "in the sense of nourishing and of filling," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. It is shortened by "pū" and so on, so in laṭ: pṛṇāti, and so on; in liṅ: pṛṇīyāt, and so on; in loṭ: pṛṇātu, and so on; and in laṅ: apṛṇāt, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given and vṛddhi is made, so: apārīt, apāriṣṭām, apāriṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, by "śṝ, dṝ, pṝ" and so on, the vowel is optionally shortened. Where it is shortened, yaṇ applies; and where it is not changed, guṇa is made. So in the three of the first person: papāra, papratuḥ or paparatuḥ, papruḥ or paparuḥ. In the three of the middle person: paparitha, paprathuḥ or paparathuḥ, papra or papara. In the three of the last person: papāra or papara, papriva or papariva, paprima or paparima.

In luṭ, by "vṝto vā," iṭ or īṭ is made optional, so: paritā, paritāsi, and so on; or parītā, parītāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by "ṝta id dhātoḥ," ṛ becomes i, and by the rule on the penultimate it is lengthened, so: pīryāt, pīryāstām, pīryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by "vṝto vā" and so on, iṭ or īṭ is made optional, so: pariṣyati, and so on; or parīṣyati, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: apariṣyat, and so on; or aparīṣyat, and so on.

For jyā, "in the sense of the loss of youth," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. "Halaḥ": "after a hal." If the end of a root has undergone samprasāraṇa and it stands after a hal, it is to be lengthened. For jyā: śnā; by "grahi-jyā" and so on it is changed by samprasāraṇa, and in what is called jinā this sūtra lengthens it. Then again, by "pū and the rest," it is due to be shortened and is shortened, so in laṭ: jināti, and so on; in liṅ: jinīyāt, and so on; in loṭ: jinātu, and so on; and in laṅ: ajināt, and so on. In luṅ, sak and iṭ are given by "yama" and so on, so: ajyāsīt, ajyāsiṣṭām, ajyāsiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, before the two ṇal endings and thal, the reduplicative syllable undergoes samprasāraṇa by "of both" and so on; before the other, kit, endings, both syllables are changed by samprasāraṇa by "grahi-jyā" and so on; and "iko yaṇ aci" applies. So in the three of the first person: jijyau, jijyatuḥ, jijyuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jijyitha or jijyātha, jijyathuḥ, jijya. In the three of the last person: jijyau, jijyiva, jijyima. In luṭ: jyātā, jyātāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, the vowel is changed by samprasāraṇa by "grahi-jyā" and so on, and lengthened by "akṛt" and so on, so: jīyāt, jīyāstām, jīyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: jyāsyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: ajyāsyat, and so on.

For vrī, "in the sense of obstructing," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. In laṭ: vrīṇāti, and so on; in liṅ: vrīṇīyāt, and so on; in loṭ: vrīṇātu, and so on; and in laṅ: avrīṇāt, and so on. In luṅ, vṛddhi is made, so in the three of the first person: avraiṣīt, avraiṣṭām, avraiṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: avraiṣīḥ, avraiṣṭam, avraiṣṭa. In the three of the last person: avraiṣam, avraiṣva, avraiṣma.

In liṭ, by reduplication, vṛddhi, guṇa and the rest, in the three of the first person: vivrāya, vivrayatuḥ, vivrayuḥ. In the three of the middle person: vivrayitha or vivretha, vivrayathuḥ, vivraya. In the three of the last person: vivrāya, vivraya, vivrayima. In luṭ, guṇa is made, so: vretā, vretāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: vrīyāt, vrīyāstām, vrīyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, guṇa is made, so: vreṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ guṇa is made, so: avreṣyat, and so on.

For jñā, "in the sense of understanding," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. By "jñā-janor jā," it is due to become jā and is changed to jā, so in laṭ: jānāti, and so on; in liṅ: jānīyāt, and so on; in loṭ: jānātu, and so on; and in laṅ: ajānāt, and so on. In luṅ, sak and iṭ are given by "yama, rama, nama" and so on, so: ajñāsīt, ajñāsiṣṭām, ajñāsiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, the forms are produced by reduplication and so on. So in the three of the first person: jajñau, jajñatuḥ, jajñuḥ. In the three of the middle person: jajñitha or jajñātha, jajñathuḥ, jajña. In the three of the last person: jajñau, jajñiva, jajñima. In luṭ: jñātā, jñātāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, furthermore, by the rule on a conjunct and so on, the change to e is made optional, so: jñāyāt, jñāyāstām, jñāyāsuḥ, and so on; or jñeyāt, and so on. In lṛṭ: jñāsyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: ajñāsyat, and so on.

For śranth, "in the sense of loosening and of delighting," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied, and n is elided by "anidit" and so on. So in laṭ: śrathnāti, and so on; in liṅ: śrathnīyāt, and so on; in loṭ: śrathnātu, and so on; and in laṅ: aśrathnāt, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, so: aśranthīt, aśranthiṣṭām, aśranthiṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, the singular of the first person is śaśrantha. The commentary cites: śranthigronthyaḥ ketiliṭisetithayicaetvaṃkecidvā, that is, "For śranth and granth, before liṭ forms that are kit, and before tha with iṭ, the change to e is optional, according to some." When the substitutes of liṭ for śranth and granth that are named kit, and tha together with iṭ, follow, the elision of the reduplicative syllable, the change to e and so on are made optional according to some. So in the dual and plural of the first person: śrethatuḥ, śaśranthatuḥ; śrethuḥ, śaśranthāḥ. In the three of the middle person: śrethitha, śaśranthitha; śrethathuḥ, śaśranthathuḥ; śretha, śaśrantha. In the three of the last person: śaśrantha; śrethiva, śaśranthiva; śrethima, śaśranthima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, so: śranthitā, śranthitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, n is elided by the rule on what does not have i as its indicatory letter and so on, so: śrathyāta, śrathyāsjāṃ, śrathyasuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, so: śranthiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: aśranthiṣyata, and so on.

For granth, "in the sense of composing," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied, and all its procedures are like those of śranth just explained.

For kuṣ, "in the sense of drawing out," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. So in laṭ: kuṣṇāti, and so on; and in liṅ: kuṣṇīyāta, and so on. In loṭ: kuṣṇātu, and so on; and in laṅ: akuṣṇāta, and so on.

niraḥkuṣlaḥ: "After nir, from kuṣ." After kuṣ preceded by the preverb nir, iṭ is optional before a following ārdhadhātuka beginning with a consonant of the class val. In luṅ, in the option where iṭ is given: nirkoṣīta, nirkoṣiṣṭāṃ, nirkoṣiṣuḥ, and so on. In the option without iṭ, the aorist marker is replaced by the rule beginning śalikaubabhā, and by the rule "k in place of ṣ and ḍh," and the rule on the change to ṣ after k and so on, s is changed to ṣ, so: nirkukṣatā, nirakukṣatāṃ, nirakukṣana, and so on. When nir does not precede, iṭ always comes, so: akoṣīta, akoṣiṣṭāṃ, and so on.

In liṭ, there is reduplication, and by the rule "cu in place of ku and h," k is changed to c, so in the three of the first person: cukoṣa, cakuṣatuḥ, cukuṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: cukoṣetha, cukuṣathuḥ, cukuṣa. In the three of the last person: cukoṣa, cukuṣiva, cukṇaṣima. In luṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: koṣitā, koṣitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: kuṣyāta, kuṣyāstāṃ, kuṣyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, the iṭ for what begins with val is given, and guṇa is made by the rule on a stem ending in puk and so on, so: koṣiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: akoṣiṣyata, and so on.

For aś, "in the sense of eating," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. So in laṭ: aśnāti, and so on; and in liṅ: aśmīyāta, and so on. In loṭ: aśnātu, and so on; and in laṅ: āśnāta, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, so: āśīta, āśiṣṭāṃ, āśiṣaḥ, and so on. In liṭ there is reduplication, and the vowel is lengthened before a like a, so in the three of the first person: āśa, āśatuḥ, āśuḥ. In the three of the middle person: āśitha, āśathuḥ, āśa. In the three of the last person: āśa, āśiva, āśima. In luṭ, iṭ is given, so: aśita, aśitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: aśyāta, aśyāstā, aśyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given, so: aśiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: āśiṣyata, and so on.

For vṛ, "in the sense of honoring," the taṅ endings are applied. So in laṭ: vṛṇīte, and so on; and in liṅ: vṛṇīta, and so on. In loṭ: vṛṇītāṃ, and so on; and in laṅ: avṛṇīta, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule "optionally after vṛ and roots in long ṝ," iṭ and the lengthened īṭ are made optional, so: avariṣṭa, avariṣātāṃ, avariṣata, and so on; or avarīṣṭa, and so on. Since the commentary explains that after vṛ, in the following luṅ and in the benedictive liṅ, iṭ optionally does not apply, then in the option where iṭ is not given, before endings beginning with jhal, sic is elided by the rule "also after a short stem," so in the three of the first person: avṛta, avṛṣātāṃ, avṛṣata. In the three of the middle person: avṛthāḥ, avṛṣāthāṃ, avṛdhraṃ. In the three of the last person: avraṃṣa, avṛṣmahi. In liṭ, by reduplication and so on, in the three of the first person: vavre, vavrete, vavrire. In the three of the middle person: vavṛṣe, vavṛbahe, vavṛmahe. In the three of the last person: vavre, vavṛvahe, vavṛmahe. In luṭ, by the rule "optionally after vṛ and roots in long ṝ," iṭ and īṭ are made optional, so: varitā, varitāse, and so on; or parītā, parītāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, iṭ is given, so: variṣīṣṭa, variṣīyāstāṃ, variṣīran, and so on; or, iṭ not being given: vṛṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ, by the rule "optionally after vṛ and roots in long ṝ," iṭ and īṭ are made optional, so: paṛṣyate, and so on; or parīṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: apariṣyata, and so on; or aparīṣyata, and so on.

itipāṇinivyākarṇasyalūtrāṇyādayaḥ samābhaṃ: that is, krī and the rest, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinian Grammar, are complete.

Thus, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, notes that set out the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinian Grammar, the rough account of the procedures, general rules together with exceptions, for krī and the rest, in which śnā applies in place of śap in the sense of the agent, is for now complete.

Now the procedures for cur and the rest will be explained. For cur, "in the sense of stealing," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. satyāpapāśarīpapīṇātūlaṣkhokasenālomatvacavarṇacarmacūrṇacurādibhyoṇica. satyāpa means truth; pāśa, noose; rūpa, form; vīṇā, lute; tūla, fine; śloka, verse; sena, army; loma, hair; tvaca, skin; varṇa, color; carma, hide; cūrṇa, powder. "After cur and the rest, ṇic." After those nominal stems, satyāpa and the rest, and after the roots cur and the rest, ṇic follows in their own sense; its c is for the sake of the accent, and its ṇ for the sake of vṛddhi. For cur, with ṇic, guṇa is made by the rule on a stem ending in puk and so on, and so cori is formed, to which laṭ and the rest are applied. By the rule on śap in the sense of the agent, the rule on all verbal endings, and so on, guṇa is made, and by the rule on ay and so on in place of the vowels ec, sandhi is made. So in laṭ: corayati, and so on; and in liṅ: corayeta, and so on.

In loṭ: corayatu, and so on; and in laṅ: acorayata, and so on.

ṇicaśca: "Also after ṇic." After a stem ending in ṇic, too, the ātmanepada endings apply when the fruit of the action goes to the agent who intends it. So in laṭ: corayate, and so on; and in liṅ: corayata, and so on. In loṭ: corayatāṃ, and so on; and in laṅ: acorayata, and so on.

In luṅ: to cori the luṅ marker cli is added; by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, the root is reduplicated; by the rule on what begins with a consonant and so on, r is elided; by the rule on lengthening a light vowel, the reduplicative syllable is lengthened; by the rule on shortening the penultimate before ṇi with caṅ, the penultimate u is shortened; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic too is elided. So in the three of the first person of the non-taṅ endings: acūcurata, acūcuratāṃ, cucura. In the three of the middle person: acūcuraḥ, acūcurataṃ, acūcurata. In the three of the last person: acūcuraraṃ, acūcurāva, acūcurāma. When the taṅ endings are applied by the rule "also after ṇic": acucurata, acūcuratāṃ, acūcuranta, and so on.

In liṭ, ām is applied by the rule beginning with kās, and guṇa is made by the rules on all verbal endings, on the half verbal endings, and so on, so: corayāṃcakara, corayāṃbabhūva, corayāmāsa, corayāṃcakri, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ is given, and guṇa is made by the rule on all verbal endings and so on, so: corayitā, corayitāsi, and so on; and by the rule "also after ṇic," in taṅ: corayitā, corayitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, ṇic is elided by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, so: coryāta, coryāstāṃ, caryāsuḥ, and so on; and when the taṅ endings are applied by the rule "also after ṇic," the iṭ for what begins with val is given and guṇa is made, so: corayiṣīṣṭa, corayiṣīyāstaṃ, corayiṣīrana, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: corayaṣyati, and so on; and by the rule "also after ṇic," in taṅ: coriyiṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ: acorayiṣyata, and so on; and acorayiṣyata, and so on.

The commentary cites: curādirṇicavākecita, that is, "After cur and the rest, ṇic is optional according to some." After cur and the rest, ṇic is in some cases made optional; then śap is applied by the rule on the agent. So in laṭ: corati, and so on; and in liṅ: coreta, and so on. In loṭ: coratu, and so on; and in laṅ: acorata, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made by the rule on a stem ending in puk and so on, so in the three of the first person: acorīta, acorīṣtāṃ, acoriṣuḥ. In the three of the middle person: acorīḥ, acoriṣtāṃ, aciriṣṭa. In the three of the last person: acoriṣaṃ, acoriṣva, acoriṣma. In liṭ, reduplication and so on are made, so in the three of the first person: cucora, cucuraduḥ, cucuruḥ. In the three of the middle person: cucoritha, cucurathuḥ, cucura. In the three of the last person: cucora, cucuriva, cucurima. In luṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: coritā, ciritāsi, and so on.
