In the benedictive liṅ, the vowel is lengthened by the rule "also of the penultimate," so: cūryāta, cūryāstāṃ, cūryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: corṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: acoriṣyata, and so on.

For kṛt, "in the sense of proclaiming," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. ubaṅhāyāśca: "Also of the penultimate." The ṛ that is the penultimate of the root also becomes it when a suffix follows. For kṛt, with ṇic, by this sūtra ṛ becomes it; by the rule that the aṇ substitute for ṛ is followed by r, r is added; and by the rule "also of the penultimate," the vowel is lengthened, so kīrti is formed, and to it laṭ and the rest are applied. So in laṭ: kīrtayati, and so on; in liṅ: kīrtayeta, and so on; and in loṭ: kīrtayatu, and so on. In laṅ: akīrtayata, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, kir is reduplicated; by the rule on what begins with a consonant and so on, r is elided; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided, so: acikīrtata, acikīrtatāṃ, acilakīrtana, and so on. In liṭ, ām is applied, so: kīrtayāṃcakār, kīrtayāṃbabhūva, kīrtayāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: kīrtayitā, kīrtayītāsaṃ, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, ṇic is elided by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, so: kīrtyāta, kīrtyāstāṃ, kīrtyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: kīrtayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: akīrtayiṣyata, and so on.

For gaṇa, "in the sense of counting," the non-taṅ endings are applied. ṇic is given; by the rule on the elision of a, the final a of the root is elided; because of the elision of a, vṛddhi is not made; and before śap guṇa is made. So in laṭ: gaṇayati, and so on; and in liṅ: gaṇayeta, and so on. In loṭ: gaṇayatu, and so on; and in laṅ: agaṇayata, and so on. In luṅ: īcagaṇaḥ, "Also ī for gaṇa." When ṇi together with caṅ follows, the ī of the reduplicative syllable of gaṇa is optional. By the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, the root is reduplicated; by the rule "cu in place of ku and h," g becomes j; by this sūtra it is optionally changed to ī; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided, so: jīgaṇata, jīgaṇatāṃ, jīgaṇana, and so on; or jagaṇata, and so on. In liṭ, ām is applied, so: gaṇayāṃcakāra, gaṇayāṃbabhūva, gaṇayāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: gaṇayitā, gaṇayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, ṇic is elided by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, so: gaṇyāta, gaṇyāstāṃ. Here, since the a has been elided, the operation as for san does not apply before ṇic. garbhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made, so: gaṇayiṣyataṃ, and so on; and in lṛṅ: agaṇayiṣyata, and so on.

For katha, "in the sense of connected discourse," the non-taṅ endings are likewise applied. By the rule on the elision of a, the a is elided; because of the elision of a, vṛddhi is not made; and before śap guṇa is made. So in laṭ: kathayati, and so on; and in liṅ: kathayeta, and so on. In loṭ: kathayatu, and so on; and in laṅ: akathayata, and so on. For luṅ the commentary cites: katho'bhyāsasyaītvaṃkocedvā, that is, "The change to ī of the reduplicative syllable of katha is optional according to some." When ṇi and caṅ follow, the change to ī of the reduplicative syllable of katha is in some cases made optional. By the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, the root is reduplicated; by this citation, the change to ī is made optional; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided, so: acīgathata, acīkathatāṃ, acīkathana, and so on; or acakathata, and so on.

In liṭ, by attaching ām: kathayāṃcakār, kathayāṃbabhūva, kathayāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: akathayitā, akathayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: kathyāta, kathyāstāṃ, kathyāsuḥ. In this case, since the a has been elided, the operation that applies as when ṇic follows is not carried out. And so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: kathayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: akathayiṣyata, and so on.

To the root aṃka, "in the senses of going and of marking," the parasmaipada endings, the a-taṅ, are likewise applied. By the rule on eliding the a of at, the root-final a is elided, so in laṭ: aṃkayate, and so on; in liṅ: aṃkayatu, and so on. In loṭ: āṃkayata, and so on; and in laṅ: aṃkayitā, and so on. For luṅ, the commentary explains: "When caṅ follows aṃka, the vowel, ac, is not reduplicated; rather ka is reduplicated, or else ka together with ṇic is reduplicated." So on the option where ka is reduplicated: āṃcakāpata, āṃcakābatāṃ, āṃcakā, and so on; and on the option where it is reduplicated together with ṇic, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, the latter ṇi is elided: āṃcikata, āṃcikatāṃ, āṃchikana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: aṃkayāṃbabhūva, aṃkayāṃcakāra, aṃkayāmās, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: aṃkayitā, aṃkayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided: aṃkyāta, aṃkyāstāṃ, aṃkyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: aṃkayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: āṃkayiṣyat, and so on.

The commentary explains: "The final a of aṃka is optionally elided when ṇic follows." So on the option where the a is not elided, vṛddhi is made by the rule "for ac, before what has ñ or ṇ as its it," and aṃkāṇic is formed. Then the sūtra artihrīclīrīkrūyīkṣmāyyātāṃpukṇau: "Arti, hrī, clī, rī, krūyī, kṣmāyī and the roots ending in ā take puk before ṇi." Arti is ṛ, "to go"; hrī, "to be ashamed"; clī, "to go"; rīṅ, "to hear"; krūyī, of uncertain sense; kṣmāyī, "to tremble." For these, and for roots of their own that end in ā, when ṇic follows, the augment puk, āgama, comes in: the k marks its position, and the u is for pronunciation. When ṇi follows aṃkā, this sūtra gives puk, and aṃkāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it, in laṭ: aṃkāpayiti, and so on; in liṅ: aṃkāpayeta, and so on; and in loṭ: aṃkāpayatu, and so on. In laṅ: āṃkābayata, and so on. In luṅ, ka is reduplicated; by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided; and drawing on the rule cited as pracad, we get āṃcakāpata, āṃcakābatāṃ, āṃcakāpana, and so on. Here, since puk stands in between, ṇic is not reduplicated, and so the option is not made. In liṭ, by attaching ām: aṃkāpayāṃcakāra, aṃkāpayāṃbabhūva, aṃkāpayāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: aṃkāpayitā, aṃkāpayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided: aṃkāpyāt, aṃkābyāstāṃ, aṃkāpyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: aṃkāpayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: āṃkāpayiṣyata, and so on.

To the root artha, "in requesting," both the parasmaipada endings, the a-taṅ, and the ātmanepada endings, the taṅ, apply. By the rule on eliding the a of at, the a is elided. So in laṭ, parasmaipada: ārthayata, and so on; ātmanepada: ārthayata, and so on. In liṅ, parasmaipada: arthayitā, and so on; ātmanepada: arthayitā, and so on. In loṭ, parasmaipada: arthayatu, and so on; ātmanepada: arthayitā, and so on. In laṅ, parasmaipada: arthayitā, and so on; ātmanepada: arthyāta, and so on. For luṅ, the commentary explains: "When caṅ follows artha, tha alone is reduplicated, or else tha together with ṇic is reduplicated." So on the option where tha alone is reduplicated, parasmaipada: ārtathāpata, ārtathāpatāṃ, ārtathāpana, and so on; ātmanepada: ārtathāpata, ārtathāpatāṃ, ārtathāpanta, and so on. On the option where it is reduplicated together with ṇic, parasmaipada: ārtithata, and so on; ātmanepada: ārtithata, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: arthayāṃcakāra, arthayāṃbabhūva, arthayāmāsa, arthayāṃcakre, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa, parasmaipada: arthayitā, arthayitāsi, and so on; ātmanepada: arthayitā, arthayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, parasmaipada, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: arthyāta, arthyāstāṃ, arthyāsuḥ, and so on; ātmanepada, by giving iṭ: arthayiṣīṣṭa, arthayiṣīlāstrāṃ, arthayiṣiran, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa, parasmaipada: arthayiṣyati, and so on; ātmanepada: ārthayiṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, parasmaipada: ārthayiṣyati, and so on; ātmanepada: ārthayiṣyata, and so on.

Again, the commentary explains: "The a of artha too is optionally elided when ṇic follows." So on the option where the a is not elided, vṛddhi is made by the rule "for ac, before what has ñ or ṇ as its it"; puk is due by the rule "arti, hrī, clī, rī, krūyī, kṣmāyī and the roots ending in ā take puk before ṇi," so the augment puk is given; and guṇa is made before śap. So in laṭ, parasmaipada: arthapayati, and so on; ātmanepada: arthapayate, and so on. In liṅ, parasmaipada: arthāpayeta, and so on; ātmanepada: arthāpayeta, and so on. In loṭ, parasmaipada: arthāpayatu, and so on; ātmanepada: arthāpayatāṃ, and so on. In laṅ, parasmaipada: ārthāpayata, and so on; ātmanepada: ārthāpayata, and so on. In luṅ, since puk stands in between, ṇi is not reduplicated and tha is reduplicated, so parasmaipada: ārtathāpata, ārtathāpatāṃ, ārtathāpana, and so on; ātmanepada: ārtathāpata, ārtathāpatāṃ, ārtathāpanta, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: arthāpayāṃcakāra, arthāpayāṃbabhūva, arthāpayāmāsa, arthāpayāṃcakre, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa, parasmaipada: arthāpayitā, arthāpayitāsi, and so on; ātmanepada: arthāpayitā, arthāpayitāse, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, parasmaipada, ṇi is elided: arthāpyāta, arthāpyāstāṃ, arthāpyāsuḥ, and so on; ātmanepada, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: arthāpayiṣīṣṭa, arthāpayiṣīyāstāṃ, arthāpayiṣīran, and so on. In lṛṭ, parasmaipada: arthāpayiṣyati, and so on; ātmanepada: arthāpayiṣyate, and so on. Likewise in lṛṅ, parasmaipada: ārthāpayiṣyata, and so on; ātmanepada: ārthāpayiṣyata, and so on.

itipāṇinivyākaraṇasyasūdrāccurādayaḥ samābhāḥ: that is, from the sūtra of the Pāṇinian Grammar, the roots beginning with cur are complete.

With these, from the work called The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down in the form of notes the sense, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the rough account of the procedures for cur and the rest, with their general rules and exceptions, is for now complete.

Thus, having explained the rough variations in the ways verbal action is formed by attaching to the ten classes of roots beginning with bhū the eight and the eighty endings, or the ten groups of l-letters, the lakāras, now we shall explain the verbal forms that end in the suffixes which form roots from roots and form roots from nominals. Of these, first is ṇic: hetumaticāhetuḥ, "also from what has a cause and from what has no cause." "With a cause" means the sense of oneself doing an action for one's own purpose, or of causing someone else to do it; and "without a cause" means oneself doing an action that is someone else's, or causing someone else to do it. For conveying these too, ṇic comes after the root.

To kṛ, ṇic is added; by the rule "for ac, before what has ñ or ṇ as its it," vṛddhi is made, and kāri is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: kāryiṃti, kāriṃyarta, kārayotu, akārayiṃte, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ. By the rule on caṅ, the root is reduplicated. By the rule on a for ṛ, ṛ becomes a. By the rule on cu for ku and h, the guttural becomes a palatal. By the rule on shortening the penultimate, the upadhā, before ṇi when caṅ follows, the upadhā is shortened. By the rule that, where ak has not been elided, the treatment is as with san when caṅ follows, and by the rules on i for the a of the reduplicative syllable, the abhyāsa, and on lengthening the light vowel, it is changed to a long vowel. By the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided, and with r brought in we get acīkarata, acīkaratāṃ, acīkarana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: kārayāṃbabhūva, kārayāṃcakāra, karayāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: kārayitā, kārayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided: kāryāta, kāryāstāṃ, kāryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: kārayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: akārayiṣyata, and so on.

To cur also, with a cause and without a cause, ṇic is attached by the rule; by the rule beginning with what ends in puk, guṇa is made, and cori is formed. Attaching leṭ and the rest to it: coriyaṃte, corayita, corayotu, acoriyeta. In luṅ there is the rule nāgopiśāspriditāṃ: "not for those whose ak has been elided, for śāsu, and for those with ṛ as their it." That is, for a root whose final letter, one of the letters gathered in the ak group, has been elided, for śāsu, "to praise," and for roots with ṛ as their it, the upadhā is not shortened before a ṇi that stands before caṅ. So although shortening of the upadhā is not obtained, the commentary explains: "Since cur and the rest always end in ṇic, then even where ak has been elided, before caṅ the upadhā is optionally shortened or left unshortened." So on the option where it is shortened, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli becomes caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, there is reduplication; the upadhā is shortened; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided: acucurta, acucuratāṃ, acucurana, and so on. Or else, with the other procedures the same but the upadhā left unshortened: acucorata, acucoratāṃ, acucorana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: corayāṃbabhūva, corayāṃcakāra, corayāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: corayitā, coryitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided: coryata, coryāstāṃ, coryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: corayimyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: acorayiṣyata, and so on.

To śāsu, "to praise," with a cause and without a cause, ṇic is attached by the rule, and śāsi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: śāsaṃyati, śāsiyeta, śāsayitu, aśāsayata. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, the root is reduplicated; by the rule "not for those whose ak has been elided, for śāsu, and for those with ṛ as their it," the upadhā is not shortened; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: aśaśāsata, aśaśāsatāṃ, aśaśāsana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: śāsayāṃbabhūva, śāsayāṃcakāra, śāsayāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: śāsayitā, śāsayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided: śāsyāta, śāsyāstāṃ, śāsyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: śāsayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aśāsyiṣyata, and so on.

To ḍhaukṛ, "to go," ṇic is given by the rule beginning "with a cause," and with the indicatory letter elided, ḍhoki is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: ḍhaukiyati, ḍhokayata, ḍhaukayetu, aḍhaukayita, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, there is reduplication; by the rule on shortening, the vowel is shortened, and by the rule on car for the reduplicative syllable, the aspirate becomes unaspirated; by the rule "not for those whose ak has been elided, for śāsu, for those with ṛ as their it," and so on, the upadhā is not shortened; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: aḍuḍhauketa, uḍḍhaukanatāṃ, aḍuḍhaukana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: ḍhaukayāṃcakār, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: ḍhaukayitā, ḍhokayitāsi, and so on; and in the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: ḍhaukyāta, ḍhaukyāsyāṃ, ḍhaukyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: ḍhaukayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aḍhaukayiṣyata, and so on.

To ṭuośvi, "in the senses of going and of growing," ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause"; vṛddhi is made by the rule "for ac, before what has ñ or ṇ as its it," and by the rule beginning "for ac, ay," śvayi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: śvāyayati, śvāyayeta, śvāyiyatu, aśvāyayata, and so on. ṇaucasaṃśrāṅoḥ: "also before ṇi, when san or caṅ follows."

For śvayati as well, before ṇi when san or caṅ follows, samprasāraṇa is optionally made. In luṅ, on the option with samprasāraṇa: to śvi with ṇic, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli becomes caṅ; by this sūtra, samprasāraṇa is made. Then, with śu, ṇi and caṅ, by the rule on caṅ, there is reduplication; by the rule on lengthening the light vowel, it is lengthened; by the rule "for ac, before what has ñ or ṇ as its it," vṛddhi is made; by the rule beginning with ec, au is changed to āv; by the rule on shortening the upadhā before ṇi when caṅ follows, the upadhā is shortened; and then, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: aśūśavata, aśūśavatāṃ, aśūśavana, and so on. On the option where samprasāraṇa is not made: by the rule on caṅ, the root is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "the first hal," v is elided; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided: aśiśvayata, aśiśvayatāṃ, aśiśvayana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: śvāyayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: śvūyeyitā, śvāyayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: śvāyyāta, śvāyyāstāṃ, śvāyyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: śrāyayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aśvāyayiṣyata, and so on.

To stamvū, "in the sense of obstructing," ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and to stambhi, attaching laṭ and the rest: stambhayati, stambhayeta, stamābhayatu, astamhayata, and so on. The sūtra stambhusibusahāṃcadi: "of stambhu, sivu and saha, when caṅ follows." Stambhu means "to obstruct"; ṣivu, "the warp of a weave"; ṣaha, "forbearance." For these, even though a prefix, the reason for changing s to ṣ, comes before, it is not changed to ṣ when caṅ follows. So in luṅ: by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli becomes caṅ; there is reduplication; by the rule beginning "śar first," s is elided; by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided; ava is placed before; and by this sūtra, s is not changed to ṣ: avātastambhata, avātastambhatāṃ, avātastambhana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: stambhayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: stambhayitā, stambhayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, ṇi is elided: stambhāta, staṃmbhāstāṃ, stambhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: stambhayiṣyāti, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: astambhayiṣyata, and so on.

To ṣivu, "in the sense of the warp of a weave," ṇic is likewise attached by the rule beginning "with a cause"; by the rule beginning with what ends in puk, guṇa is made, and savi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: sevayati, sevayata, sevayatu, asevayata, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, the root is reduplicated; by the rule on lengthening the light vowel, it is lengthened; by the rule beginning with substitution, ādeśa, the latter s becomes ṣ; by the rule on shortening the upadhā before ṇi when caṅ follows, the upadhā is shortened; by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided; pari is placed before; by the rule beginning "stambhu, sivu," the s is not changed to ṣ; and with sandhi applied: paryasīṣivata, baryasīṣivatāṃ, baryasīṣivana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: sevayāṃcakāra, and so on; and in luṭ, by giving iṭ: sepayitā, sevayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: sevyāta, sevyāstāṃ, sevyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: sevayiṅhuti, and so on. In lṛṅ: asevayiṣyata, and so on.

To ṣaha, "in the sense of forbearance," ṇic is attached; by the rule on the upadhā, vṛddhi is made, and to sāhi, attaching laṭ and the rest: sāheyati, sāhayatu, asāheyata, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli becomes caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, there is reduplication; by the rule that, where ak has not been elided, on a light syllable, when caṅ follows, the treatment is as with san, and by the rules on i for a and on lengthening the light vowel, it is lengthened; by the rule beginning with substitution, the latter s is affected; by the rule on shortening the upadhā before ṇi when caṅ follows, it is shortened; by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇic is elided; vi is placed before; and by the rule beginning "stambhu, śāsu, saha," the s is not changed to ṣ: vyasīṣatata, vyasīṣahatāṃ, vyasīṣahana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: sāhayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: sahitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: sāhyāta, sāhyāstā, sāhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: sāhayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: asāhayiṣyata, and so on.

To cakāsṛ, "in the sense of a contemptible sound," ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and cakāsi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: cakāsiyati, cakāsayeta, cakīsayatu, cakīsayata, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli becomes caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, ca is reduplicated; by the rule that, where ak has not been elided, on a light syllable, when caṅ follows, the treatment is as with san, and by the rules on i for a and on lengthening the light vowel, it is changed to a long vowel; by the rule beginning "not for those whose ak has been elided, for śāsu, for those with ṛ as their it," the upadhā is not shortened; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: acīcakāsata, acīcakāsatvaṃ, acīcakāsana, and so on. The commentary cites: subhātoranikācaścasanātkacidvā, "For the roots of sup, and for those that do not have a single ac, the treatment as with san is in some cases optional." That is, for the nominal roots, the roots of sup, and for roots that do not have a single vowel, the operation as with san when ṇi and caṅ follow is in some cases made optional. So in luṅ, with the other procedures as before, but without the change to i and the rest: acacakāsata, acacakāsatāṃ, acacakāsan, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: cakāsyāṃcakāra, and so on; and in luṭ, by giving iṭ: cakāsayita, cakāsayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: cakāsyāta, cakāsyāstāṃ, cakāsyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: cakāsayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: acakāsayiṣyata, and so on.

To undi, "to be moist," ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and unī is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: undiyati, undiyeta, andayetu, aundayeta, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli becomes caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, da together with ṇi is reduplicated; by the rules on āṭ for an initial ac and "from āṭ too," vṛddhi is made; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: aundīdata, aundidatāṃ, aundidana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: undayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: undayitā, undayitāsi, and so on.

In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: undyāta, undyāstaṃ, undyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: undayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aundayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ubja, in the sense of propriety": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and ubji is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: ubjayati, ubjayata, ubjayatu, aubjayata, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli becomes caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, ja together with ṇi is reduplicated; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: aubjijata, aubjijatraṃ, aubjijana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: ubjayāṃcakār, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: ubjayitā, ubjayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: ubjyāta, ubjyāstāṃ, ubjyasuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: ubjayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aubjayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "arca, in the sense of worship": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and arci is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: arcayati, arcayeta, arcayatu, arcayata, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, ca together with ṇi is reduplicated, and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, the latter ṇi is elided: ārcicatā, ārcicatāṃ, ārcicana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: arcayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: arcayitā, arcayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: arcyāta, arcyāstāṃ, arcyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: arcayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ārcayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "drai, in the sense of sleeping": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and drāyi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, drāyayati; liṅ, drāyayata; laṭ, drāyayatu; adrāyayata, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, drā is reduplicated; by the rule on the short vowel, it is made short; by the rule beginning "the first hal," r is elided; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: adadrayata, adadrayatāṃ, adadrayan, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: drāyayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: drāyayitā, drāyayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: drāyyāta, drāyyāstāṃ, drāyyāsuḥ, and so on. By the rule on the shortening of the penultimate before caṅ following ṇi, it is made short. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: drāyayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: adrāyayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "rabha, in the sense of beginning": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause." The rule "rabheraśācliṭoḥ" means: for rabhi, before an ac that is not that of śa or of liṭ. When an affix beginning with ac follows, other than one beginning with the ac left after śa is elided or the ac substituted for liṭ, rabhi takes the augment (āgama) num. So num is given, the m, which serves to fix its position, and the u, which serves for pronunciation, are elided, and rambho is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: rambhiyati, rambhiyeta, loṭ, rambhayatu, arambhayita, and so on. In luṅ, since the commentary explains that rambha is not reduplicated before caṅ, it is not reduplicated; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: arambhata, arambhatāṃ, arambhana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: rambhayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: rambhayitā, rambhayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: rambhyāta, rambhyāstāṃ, rambhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: rambhayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: arambhayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ḍulabhaṣ, in the sense of obtaining": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause." The rule "labheśca" means: of labha also. For labhi too, when an affix beginning with ac follows, other than one beginning with the ac left after śa is elided or the ac substituted for liṭ, the augment num comes. So num is given, its markers are elided, and lambhi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, lambhayati; loṭ, lambhayeta; lambhayatu; laṅ, alambhayata, and so on. Since the commentary explains that lambha too is not reduplicated before caṅ, it is not reduplicated; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: alambhata, alambhatāṃ, alambhana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: lambhayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: lambhayitā, lambhayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: lambhyāta, lambhyāstāṃ, lambhyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: lambhayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: alambhayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "hi, in the sense of going": ṇic is given by the rule beginning "with a cause." By the rule that ec takes vṛddhi before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, and by the rule beginning with ec, it is changed to āy, giving hāyi. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, hāyayati; hāyayata, liṅ; hāyāyatu, loṭ; ahāyayata, laṅ; and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli becomes caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, the root is reduplicated; by the rule that ku and h become cu; by the lengthening of the light vowel; and by the elision of ṇi before what lacks iṭ: ajīhayata, ajīhāyātāṃ, ajīhayan, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: hāyayāṃcakara, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: hāyayitā, hāyayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: hāyyāta, hāyyāstāṃ, hāyyāsuḥ, and so on. By the rule on the shortening of the penultimate before caṅ following ṇi, it is made short. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: hāyayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: ahāyayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ūna, in the sense of diminishing": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause." Attaching laṭ and the rest to ūni: ūnayati, ūnayeta, ūnayatu, aunayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "na ūnayati dhvanayati elayati ardayatibhyaḥ" means: not from ūnayati, dhvanayati, ilayati, and ardayati. After ūna, "to diminish," dhvan, and ela and arda, "to go," when they end in ṇic, cli is not changed to caṅ; rather, cli is changed to sic and iṭ is given: aunayīta, aunayisvāṃ, aunayiṣuḥ, and so on. Since the commentary explains that on some occasions, when there is need for it, as in metrical composition and the like, it is changed to caṅ, then on the option where it is changed to caṅ, the syllable is reduplicated together with ṇic, and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: aunaṃnata, auninatāṃ, auninana, and so on.

In liṭ, by attaching ām: ūnayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: ūnayitā, ūnayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by eliding ṇi: ūnyāta, ūnyāstāṃ, ūnyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: ūnayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aunayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "dhvana, in the sense of sound": to it also ṇic is attached. Attaching laṭ and the rest to dhvani: laṭ, dhvaniyati; liṅ, dhvaniyeta; loṭ, dhvanayatu; laṅ, adhvanayata, and so on. In luṅ, since cli is made optionally caṅ or sic, on the sic option, by giving iṭ: adhvanayīta, adhvanayiṣṭāṃ, adhvanayiṣuḥ, and so on. On the caṅ option, the root is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "the first hal," va is elided; by the rule that before a light syllable followed by caṅ, where no ak has been elided, it is treated as before san, it is changed to i; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: adidhvanata, adidhvanatāṃ, adidhvanana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: dhvanayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: dhvanayitā, dhvanayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by eliding ṇi: dhvanyāta, dhvanyāsvāṃ, dhvanyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: dhvanayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ too, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: adhvanayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "aila, in the sense of going": ṇic is attached. Attaching laṭ and the rest to eli: elayati; liṅ, elayeta; loṭ, elayatu; laṅ, ailiyeta, and so on. Since cli is made optionally sic or caṅ, on the sic option, by giving iṭ: ailayīta, ailayiṣṭāṃ, ailayiṣuḥ, and so on; and on the caṅ option, la together with ṇi is reduplicated, and by eliding ṇi: aililata, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: elayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: elayitā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: elyāta, elyāstāṃ, elyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: elayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ too, by giving iṭ: elayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "arda, in the sense of going": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and ardi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, ardiyati; liṅ, ardayeta; loṭ, ardayatu; laṅ, ārdiyata, and so on. In luṅ, since cli is made optionally sic or caṅ, on the sic option, by giving iṭ: ārdayīta, ārdayiṣṭāṃ, ārdayiṣuḥ, and so on; and on the caṅ option, da together with ṇi is reduplicated, and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: ārdidata, ārdidatāṃ, ārdidana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: ārdayāṃcakāra, and so on; and in luṭ, by giving iṭ: ardayitā, ardayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: ardyāta, ardyāstāṃ, ardyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: ardayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: ārdayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "smṛ, in the sense of reciting": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause." By the rule on vṛddhi of ac before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, vṛddhi is made, and smāri is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, smārayati; liṅ, smārayeta; loṭ, smārayatu; laṅ, asmārayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "at smṛdṛtvaraprathamradastṛspaśām" means: a, of smṛ, dṛ, tvara, pratha, mrada, stṛ, and spaśa. For smṛ, "to recite"; dṛ, "to rend"; ñitvara, "to hasten"; pratha, "to proclaim"; mrada, "to crush"; stṛñ, "to cover"; and spaśa, "to moisten," when they have ṇi, before caṅ the reduplicate is changed to at and is not changed to i. So by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule on caṅ it is reduplicated; by this sūtra it is not changed to i; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: asaṃsmarata, asasmaratāṃ, asasmarana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: smarayāṃcakār, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: smārayitā, smārayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: smāryāta, smāryāstāṃ, smāryāsuḥ, and so on. By the rule on the shortening of the penultimate before caṅ following ṇi, it is made short. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ and making guṇa: smārayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: asmārayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "dṛ, in the sense of rending": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause." By the rule on vṛddhi of ac before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, vṛddhi is made, and dāri is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, dāriyati; liṅ, dāriyata; laṅ, dārayatu; adīriyata, and so on. In luṅ, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule beginning with smṛ and dṛ, the reduplicate takes at; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: adadarata, adadātāṃ, adadarana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: dārayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: dārayitā, dārayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: dāryāta, dāryāstvaṃ, dāryāsuḥ, and so on. By the rule beginning "before caṅ following ṇi," it is made short. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: dārayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: adārayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ñitvara, in the sense of hastening": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and tvari is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, tvarayati; liṅ, tvarayeta; loṭ, tvarayatu; laṅ, atvarayata, and so on. In luṅ, cli becomes caṅ and the root is reduplicated; by the rule beginning with smṛ, dṛ and tvara, it is not changed to i; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: atatvarata, atatvaratāṃ, atatvarana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: tvarayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: tvarayitā, tvarayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: tvaryāta, tvaryāstāṃ, tvaryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: tvarayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: atvarayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "pratha, in the sense of proclaiming": ṇic is attached, and prathi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, prathiyati; liṅ, prathayeta; loṭ, prathayatu; laṅ, aprathayata, and so on. In luṅ, cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule beginning with smṛ, dṛ, tvara and pratha, it is not changed to i; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: apaprathata, apaprathatāṃ, apaprathana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: prathayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: prathayitā, prathayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by eliding ṇi: prathyāta, prathyāstāṃ, prathyāsuḥ, and so on.

In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: prathayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: aprathayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "mrada, in the sense of crushing": ṇi is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and laṭ and the rest are attached to mradi: laṭ, mradayati; liṅ, mradayeta; loṭ, mradayatu; laṅ, amradayata, and so on. In luṅ, with caṅ, the root is reduplicated; by the rule beginning with smṛ, dṛ, tvara, pratha and mrada, it is not changed to i; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: amamradata, amamradatāṃ, amamradana, and so on. In liṭ, ām is attached: mradayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: mradayitā, mradayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: mradyāta, mradyāstāṃ, mradyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ: mradayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: amradayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "stṛña, in the sense of covering completely": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause." By the rule on vṛddhi of ac before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, vṛddhi is made, and stāri is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, stārayati; liṅ, stārayeta; loṭ, stārayatu; laṅ, astārayata, and so on. In luṅ, cli is changed to caṅ and the root is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "śar first," s is elided; by the rule beginning with smṛ and dṛ, it is not changed to i; by the rule on the shortening of the penultimate before caṅ following ṇi, it is made short; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: atastarata, atastaratāṃ, atastarana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: stārayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: stārayitā, stārayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by eliding ṇi: stāryāta, stāryāstāṃ, stāryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, by giving iṭ: stārayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: astārayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "spaśa, in the sense of moistening": ṇic is attached. By the rule on the penultimate, vṛddhi is made, and spāśi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: spāśayati; liṅ, spāśayeta; loṭ, spāśayatu; liṅ, aspāśayata, and so on. In luṅ, cli becomes caṅ and the root is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "śar first," s is elided; by the rule beginning with smṛ and dṛ, it is not changed to i; by the rule on the shortening of the penultimate before caṅ following ṇi, it is made short; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: apaspaśata, apaspaśatāṃ, apaspaśana, and so on. In liṭ, by attaching ām: spāśayāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, by giving iṭ: spāśayitā, spāśayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, by eliding ṇi: spāśyāta, and so on. In lṛṭ: spāśayiṣyati, and so on; and in lṛṅ: aspāśayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "veṣṭa, in the sense of winding": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and veṣṭi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, veṣṭayate; liṅ, veṣṭayeta; loṭ, veṣṭayatu; laṅ, aveṣṭayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "vibhāṣā veṣṭeḥ" means: optionally, of veṣṭi. For veṣṭi together with ṇi, before caṅ, changing the reduplicate to at or not changing it is made optional. On the option of changing it to at: avaveṣṭata, avaveṣṭatāṃ, avaveṣṭana, and so on; and on the option of not changing it to at, by the rule on the short vowel it is made short: aviveṣṭata, aviveṣṭatāṃ, aviveṣṭana, and so on. For the remaining ones: liṭ, veṣṭayāṃcakāra; luṭ, veṣṭayitā; benedictive liṅ, veṣṭyāta; lṛṭ, veṣṭayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aveṣṭayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "bhrājṛ, in the sense of blazing": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and bhrāja is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, bhrājayati; liṅ, bhrājayeta; loṭ, bhrājayatu; laṅ, abhrājayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "bhrājabhrāsabhāṣadīpajīvamīlapīḍām anyatarasyām" means: optionally, of bhrāja, bhrāsa, bhāṣa, dīpa, jīva, mīla, and pīṭa. For bhrājṛ and bhrāsṛ, "to blaze"; bhāṣa, "to speak"; dīpa, "to blaze"; jīva, "to live"; mīla, "to join"; and pīṭa, "to press close," when they have ṇi, before caṅ the penultimate is optionally made short. On the option of making it short: by the rule beginning with ṇi and śri, cli becomes caṅ, and the root is reduplicated; it is made short; r is elided; by the rule "in the reduplicate, car too"; by the rule that before a light syllable followed by caṅ, where no ak has been elided, it is treated as before san, a becomes i; by this sūtra the penultimate is short; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: abibhrajata, abibhrajatāṃ, abibhrajana, and so on. On the option of not making it short: abibhrājata, abibhrājatāṃ, abibhrājana, and so on. For the remaining l-affixes: liṭ, bhrājayāṃcakāra; luṭ, bhrājayitā; benedictive liṅ, bhrājyāta; liṭ, bhrājayiṣyati; lṛṅ, abhrājayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "bhrāsa, in the sense of blazing": ṇic is attached, and laṭ and the rest are attached to bhrāsi: laṭ, bhrāsayati; liṅ, bhrāsayeta; loṭ, bhrāsayatu; laṅ, abhrāsayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the sūtra beginning with bhrāja and bhrāsa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: ababhrāsata, and so on; or abibhrāsata, and so on. For the latter l-affixes: liṅ, bhrāsayāṃcakāra; luṭ, bhrāsayitā; benedictive liṅ, bhrāsyāta; lṛṭ, bhrāsayiṣyati; liṅ, abhrāsayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, to bhāṣa, "to speak," ṇic is attached, and laṭ and the rest are attached to it: laṭ, bhāṣayati; liṅ, bhāṣayeta; loṭ, bhāṣayatu; laṅ, bhāṣayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with bhrāja and bhrāśa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: abibhaṣata, and so on; or abibhāṣata, and so on. For the latter l-affixes: liṭ, bhāṣayāṃcakāra; luṭ, bhāṣayitā; benedictive liṅ, bhāṣyāta; lṛṭ, bhāṣayiṣyati; lṛṅ, abhāṣayiṣyata, and so on.

To dīpa, "to blaze," ṇic and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, dīpayati; liṅ, dīpayeta; loṭ, dīpayatu; laṅ, adīpayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with bhrāja and bhrāśa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: adidipata, and so on; or adidīpata, and so on. For the latter l-affixes: laṭ, dīpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, dīpayitā; benedictive liṅ, dīpyāta; lṛṭ, dīpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, adīpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "jīva, in the sense of living": ṇic is attached, and then laṭ and the rest: laṭ, jīvayati; liṅ, jīvayata; loṭ, jīvayatu; laṅ, ajīvayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with bhrāja and bhrāśa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: ajijivata, and so on; or ajijīvata, and so on. For the latter l-affixes: liṭ, jīvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, jīvayitā; benedictive liṅ, jīvyāta; lṛṭ, jīvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajīvayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "mīla, in the sense of joining": ṇic is attached, and then laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, mīlayati; liṅ, mīlayeta; loṭ, mīlayatu; laṅ, amīlayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with bhrāja and bhrāsa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: amimilata, and so on; or amimīlata, and so on. For the latter l-affixes: liṭ, mīlayāṃcakāra; luṭ, mīlayitā; benedictive liṅ, mīlyāta; lṛṭ, mīlayiṣyati; lṛṅ, amīlayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "pīṭa, in the sense of pressing close": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause," and pīḍi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, pīḍayati; liṭ, pīḍayeta; loṭ, pīḍayatu; laṅ, apīḍiyata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with bhrāja and bhrāsa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: apipiḍata, and so on; or apipīḍata, and so on. For the latter l-affixes: liṭ, pīḍayāṃcakāra; luṭ, pīḍayitā; benedictive liṅ, pīḍyāta; lṛṭ, pīḍayiṣyati; lṛṅ, apīḍayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "kaṇa, in the sense of sound": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause." By the rule on the penultimate, vṛddhi is made, and kāṇi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, kāṇayati; liṅ, kāṇayata; loṭ, kāṇayatu; laṭ, akāṇayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "kaṇaraṇabhaṇaśraṇahveñlapalupaluṭhaheṣāṃ ca" means: of kaṇa, raṇa, baṇa, bhaṇa, śraṇa, hveña, lapa, lupa, luṭha, hā, and iṣa also. Kaṇa, raṇa, baṇa, and bhaṇa mean "to sound"; śaṇa, "to cook"; hveña, "to summon"; lapa, "to speak at length"; lupha, "to hide"; luṭha, "to churn"; ohāk, "to abandon"; and iṣu, "to desire." For these too, together with ṇi, before caṅ, the penultimate is optionally made short or not. On the option of making it short, the operation as before san applies; on the option of not making it short, the operation as before san does not apply either: acīkaṇata, and so on; or acakāṇata, and so on. For the remaining l-affixes: liṭ, kāṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, kāṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, kāṇyāta; lṛṭ, kāṇayiṣyati; lṛṅ, akāṇayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "raṇa, in the sense of sound": ṇic is attached. By the rule on vṛddhi of the penultimate, vṛddhi is made, and rāṇi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, rāṇayati; liṅ, rāṇayeta; loṭ, rāṇayatu; laṅ, arāṇayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the sūtra beginning with kaṇa and raṇa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: arīraṇata, and so on; or ararāṇata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, rāṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, rāṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, rāṇyāta; lṛṭ, rāṇayiṣyati; lṛṅ, arāṇayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "paṇa, in the sense of sound": ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to bāṇi: laṭ, bāṇayati; liṅ, bāṇayata; loṭ, bāṇayatu; laṅ, abāṇayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with kaṇa and raṇa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: abībaṇata, and so on; or ababāṇata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, bāṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, bāṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, bāṇyāta; lṛṭ, bāṇayiṣyati; lṛṅ, abāṇayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "bhaṇa, in the sense of sound": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause." By the rule on the penultimate, vṛddhi is made, and bhāṇi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, bhāṇayati; liṅ, bhāṇayata; loṭ, bhāṇayatu; laṅ, abhāṇayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with kaṇa and raṇa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: abībhaṇata, and so on; or ababhāṇata, and so on. For liṭ and the latter ones: liṭ, bhāṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, bhāṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, bhāṇyāta; lṛṭ, bhāṇayiṣyati; lṛṅ, abhāṇayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, regarding "śraṇa, in the sense of cooking": ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to śrāṇi: laṭ, śrāṇayati; liṅ, śrāṇayeta; loṭ, śrāṇayatu; laṅ, aśrāṇayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with kaṇa and raṇa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: aśīśraṇata, and so on; or aśaśrāṇata, and so on. For the remaining l-affixes: liṭ, śrāṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, śrāṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, śrāṇyāta; lṛṭ, śrāṇayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aśrāṇayiṣyata, and so on. The illustration of hveña will be explained below.

Regarding "lapa, in the sense of speaking at length": ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and lāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, lāpayati; liṅ, lāpayeta; loṭ, lāpayatu; laṅ, alāpayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with kaṇa and raṇa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: alīlapata, and so on; or alalāpata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones, in order: liṭ, lāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, lāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, lāpyāta; lṛṭ, lāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, alāpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "lupa, in the sense of hiding": ṇic is attached, and by the rule beginning "ending in puk," guṇa is made, and lopi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, lopayati; liṅ, lopayeta; loṭ, lopayatu; laṅ, alopayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with kaṇa and raṇa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: alūlupata, and so on; or alulopata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, lopayāṃcakāra; luṭ, lopayitā; benedictive liṅ, lopyāta; lṛṭ, lopayiṣyati; lṛṅ, alopayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "luṭha, in the sense of churning": with ṇic, guṇa is made, and loṭhi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, loṭhayati; liṅ, loṭhayeta; loṭ, loṭhayatu; laṅ, aloṭhayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with kaṇa and raṇa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: alūluṭhata, and so on; or aluloṭhata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones, in order: liṭ, loṭhayāṃcakāra; luṭ, loṭhayitā; benedictive liṅ, loṭhyāta; lṛṭ, loṭhayiṣyata; liṅ, aloṭhayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ohāk, in the sense of abandoning": with ṇic, the augment (āgama) puk is given by the rule beginning "arti, hrī, vlī, rī," and hāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, hāpayati; liṅ, hāpayeta; loṭ, hāpayatu; laṭ, ahāpayata, and so on. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning with kaṇa and raṇa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: ajīhapata, and so on; or ajahāpata, and so on. For the remaining l-affixes: liṭ, hāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, hāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, hāpyāta; lṛṭ, hāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ahāpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "iṣu, in the sense of desiring": ṇic is attached and guṇa is made: laṭ, eṣayati; liṅ, eṣayeta; loṭ, eṣayatu; laṅ, aiṣayata, and so on. In luṅ, since vṛddhi must be made by the rules on āṭ for an initial ac and "from āṭ too," the shortening of the penultimate leaves no visible trace. Even so, since ṣa together with ṇi is reduplicated, on the option where the penultimate is made short the operation as before san applies, and so there is lengthening of the light vowel; and on the option where it is not made short, it is not lengthened: aiṣīṣata, and so on; or aiṣiṣata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, eṣayāṃcakāra; luṭ, eṣayitā; benedictive liṅ, eṣyāta; lṛṭ, eṣayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aiṣayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "kṛta, in the sense of proclaiming": ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "with a cause." By the rule "of the penultimate too," it is changed to it; by the rule that aṇ replacing ṛ is followed by r, r follows; and by the rule "of the penultimate too," it is lengthened, and kīrti is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, kīrtayati; liṅ, kīrtayeta; loṭ, kīrtayatu; laṅ, akīrtayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "ur ṛt" means: of ṛ, ṛt. The letter ṛ in the penultimate of a root, before ṇi that has caṅ, optionally stays as ṛt itself without the change to it, guṇa and the like: acīkṛtata, and so on; or, when it is changed to it: acīkīrtata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, kīrtayāṃcakāra; laṭ, kīrtayitā; benedictive liṅ, kīrtyāta; lṛṭ, kīrtayiṣyati; lṛṅ, akīrtayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "vṛtu, in the sense of existing": ṇic is attached. Since the commentary explains that on some occasions the penultimate is not changed to it, ṛ is not changed to it, and by the rule beginning "ending in puk," guṇa is made, and varti is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, vartayati; liṅ, vartayeta; lṛṭ, vartayatu; laṅ, avartayata, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule "of ṛ, ṛt," staying as ṛt itself and guṇa are made optional. On the option where guṇa is made, the operation as before san does not apply. And by the elision of ṇi before what lacks iṭ: avīvṛtata, and so on; or avavartata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, vartayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vartayitā; benedictive liṅ, vartyāta; lṛṭ, vartayiṣyati; lṛṅ, avartayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "mṛjūṣ, in the sense of cleansing": with ṇic, by the rule "of mṛji, vṛddhi," vṛddhi is made, and mārji is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, mārjayati; liṅ, mārjayeta; loṭ, mārjayatu; laṅ, amārjayata, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule "of ṛ, ṛt," the penultimate staying as ṛ itself or taking vṛddhi is made optional. On the vṛddhi option, the operation as before san does not apply. By eliding ṇi: amīmṛjata, and so on; or amamārjata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, mārjayāṃcakāra; luṭ, mārjayitā; benedictive liṅ, mārjyāta; lṛṭ, mārjayiṣyati; lṛṭ, amārjayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ñiṣvapa, in the sense of sleeping": ṇic is given, and by the rule on the penultimate, vṛddhi is made, and svāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, svāpayati; liṅ, svāpayeta; loṭ, svāpayatu; laṅ, asvāpayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "svāpeś caṅi" means: of svāpi, before caṅ. Svapa ending in ṇi, when cli has been changed, takes saṃprasāraṇa before caṅ. So svapi takes caṅ; by the rule on the shortening of the penultimate before caṅ following ṇi, it is made short; by this sūtra, saṃprasāraṇa; by the rule on caṅ, reduplication; by the lengthening of the light vowel, and by the rule beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: asūṣupata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones, in order: liṭ, svāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, svāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, svāpyāta; lṛṭ, svāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, asvāpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "śo, in the sense of making thin": ṇic is attached. By the rule that in the original enunciation an ec becomes ā when not before what is marked with ś, the ec is changed to ā, giving śā with ṇi. The rule "śāchāsāhvāvyāvepāṃ yuk" means: yuk, of śā, chā, sā, hvā, vyā, ve, and pā. For śo, "to make thin"; cho, "to cut"; ṣo, "to end"; hveña, "to summon"; vyeña, "to cover over"; veña, "to weave"; and pā, "to drink," before ṇi the augment yuk comes; its k serves to fix its position and its u serves for pronunciation. So śāyi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, śāyayati; liṅ, śāyayeta; loṭ, śāyayatu; laṅ, aśāyayata, and so on. In luṅ, with reduplication, and by the rule on the shortening of the penultimate before caṅ following ṇi: aśaśayata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, śāyayāṃcakāra; luṭ, śāyayitā; benedictive liṅ, śāyyāta; lṛṭ, śāyayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aśāyayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, regarding "cho, in the sense of cutting": with ṇic, ec becomes ā and the augment yuk is given, and chāyi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, chāyayati; liṅ, chāyayeta; loṭ, chāyayatu; laṅ, achāyayata; luṅ, acachayata; liṭ, chāyayāṃcakāra; luṭ, chāyayitā; benedictive liṅ, chāyyāta; lṛṭ, chāyayiṣyati; lṛṅ, achāyayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ṣo, in the sense of ending": with ṇic, ec becomes ā and the augment yuk is given, and sāyi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, sāyayati; liṅ, sāyayeta; loṭ, sāyayatu; laṅ, asāyayata; luṅ, asasayata; liṭ, sāyayāṃcakāra; luṭ, sāyayitā; benedictive liṅ, sāyyāta; lṛṭ, sāyayiṣyati; lṛṅ, asāyayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "hveña, in the sense of summoning": with ṇic, ec becomes ā and the augment yuk is given, and hvāyi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, hvāyayati; liṅ, hvāyayeta; loṭ, hvāyayatu; laṅ, ahvāyayata. In luṅ: the rule "hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam" means: saṃprasāraṇa of hvā.

For hvā together with ṇi, before caṅ, saṃprasāraṇa always takes place. So hvāyi takes caṅ; by the rule on the shortening of the penultimate before caṅ following ṇi, it is made short; by this sūtra, saṃprasāraṇa; then reduplication, and lengthening of the light vowel. Since the commentary explains that after saṃprasāraṇa the augment yuk is dropped, yuk is elided; by the rule on vṛddhi of ac before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, vṛddhi; by the rule beginning "ec becomes ay," au becomes āv; by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided; and since by the rule beginning with kaṇa and raṇa the penultimate is optionally made short or not: ajuhāvata, and so on; or ajūhavata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, hvāyayāṃcakāra; luṭ, hvāyayitā; benedictive liṅ, hvāyyāta; lṛṭ, hvāyayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ahvāyayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "vyeña, in the sense of covering over": with ṇic, ec becomes ā and the augment yuk is given, and vyāyi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, vyāyayati; liṅ, vyāyayeta; loṭ, vyāyayatu; laṅ, avyāyayata; luṅ, avavyāyata; liṭ, vyāyayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vyāyayitā; benedictive liṅ, vyāyyāta; lṛṭ, vyāyayiṣyati; lṛṅ, avyāyayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "veña, in the sense of weaving": with ṇic, ec becomes ā and the augment yuk is given, and vāyi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, vāyayati; liṅ, vāyayeta; loṭ, vāyayatu; laṅ, avāyayata; luṅ, avavayata; liṭ, vāyayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vāyayitā; benedictive liṅ, vāyyāta; lṛṭ, vāyayiṣyati; lṛṅ, avāyayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, to pā, "to drink," ṇic is attached and the augment yuk is given, and laṭ and the rest are attached to pāyi: laṭ, pāyayati; liṅ, pāyayeta; loṭ, pāyayatu; laṅ, apāyayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "lopaḥ pibater īc cābhyāsasya" means: elision of pibati, and ī of the reduplicate too. Before caṅ together with ṇi, the penultimate of pibati is elided, and the reduplicate too is changed to ī. So pāyi takes caṅ in luṅ, and is reduplicated; by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided; and by this sūtra the penultimate is elided and the reduplicate changed to ī: apīpyata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, pāyayāṃcakāra; luṭ, pāyayitā; benedictive liṅ, pāyyāta; lṛṭ, pāyayiṣyati; lṛṅ, apāyayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ṛ, in the sense of going": with ṇic, by the rule beginning "arti, hrī, vlī," the augment puk; and by the rule beginning "ending in puk," guṇa is made, and arpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, arpayati; liṅ, arpayeta; loṭ, arpayatu; laṅ, ārpayata, and so on. In luṅ, arpi takes caṅ; by the rule on caṅ, the root is reduplicated; by the rule "of ṛ, at"; then with āṭ, vṛddhi is made; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: ārpata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, arpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, arpayitā; benedictive liṅ, arpyāta; lṛṭ, arpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ārpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "hrī, in the sense of being ashamed": with ṇic, the augment puk is given by the rule beginning "arti, hrī"; and by the rule beginning "ending in puk," guṇa is made, and hrepi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, hrepayati; lṛṅ, hrepayeta; loṭ, hrepayatu; laṅ, ahrepayata, and so on. In luṅ, with reduplication, the shortening of the penultimate before caṅ following ṇi, and the elision of ṇi by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ: ajihripata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, hrepayāṃcakāra; luṭ, hrepayitā; benedictive liṅ, hrepyāta; lṛṭ, hrepayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ahrepayiṣyata, and so on.

To vlī, "to go," ṇic is attached; by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk; and by the rule beginning "ending in puk," guṇa is made, and vlepi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, vlepayati; liṅ, vlepayeta; loṭ, vlepayatu; laṅ, avlepayata; luṅ, avivlipata; liṭ, vlepayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vlepayitā; benedictive liṅ, vlepyāta; lṛṭ, vlepayiṣyati; lṛṅ, avlepayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "rīṅ, in the sense of hearing": with ṇic, by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk; and by the rule beginning "ending in puk," guṇa is made, and repi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, repayati; liṭ, repayeta; loṭ, repayatu; laṅ, arepayata; luṅ, ariripata; liṭ, repayāṃcakāra; luṭ, repayitā; benedictive liṅ, repyāta; lṛṭ, repayiṣyati; lṛṅ, repayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "knūya, in the sense of sound": ṇic is attached; by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given; by the rule that v and y are dropped before val, y is elided; and by the rule beginning "ending in puk," guṇa is made, and knopi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, knopayati; liṅ, knopayati; loṭ, knopayatu; laṅ, aknopayata; luṅ, acuknupata; liṭ, knopayāṃcakāra; luṭ, knopayitā; benedictive liṅ, knopyāta; lṛṭ, knopayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aknopayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "kṣmāyī, in the sense of trembling": ṇic is attached, and by the rule that v and y are dropped before val, y is elided, and laṭ and the rest are attached to kṣmāpi: laṭ, kṣmāpayati; liṅ, kṣmāpayeta; loṭ, kṣmāpayatu; laṅ, akṣmāpayata; luṅ, acakṣmāpata; liṭ, kṣmāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, kṣmāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, kṣmāpyāta; lṛṭ, kṣmāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, akṣmāpayiṣyata, and so on.

To ṣṭhā, "to cease from going," ṇic is attached, and by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given, and sthāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, sthāpayati; liṅ, sthāpayata; loṭ, sthāpayatu; laṅ, asthāpayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "tiṣṭhater it" means: i, of tiṣṭhati. Before caṅ together with ṇi, the penultimate of tiṣṭhati is changed to i. So sthāpi takes caṅ; by this sūtra it is changed to i; it is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "śar first," s is elided; by the rule "in the reduplicate, car too," th becomes t; by the rule beginning "substitute," s becomes ṣ; by the rule on ṣ and ṭu, th becomes ṭh; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: atiṣṭhipata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, sthāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, sthāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, sthāpyāta; lṛṭ, sthāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, asthāpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ghrā, in the sense of taking up": with ṇic, by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given, and ghrāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, ghrāpayati; liṅ, ghrāpayeta; loṭ, ghrāpayatu; laṅ, aghrāpayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "jighrater vā" means: of jighrati, optionally.

Before caṅ together with ṇi, the penultimate of jighrati is optionally changed to i: ajighripata, and so on; or ajaghrapata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, ghrāpayāṃcakāra; laṭ, ghrāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, ghrāpyāta; lṛṭ, ghrāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aghrāpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "pā, in the sense of protecting": with ṇic, the commentary cites: "pāter ṇau lugāgamo nityam," that is, for pāti before ṇi, the augment luk, always. Before the ṇi of pāti the augment luk always comes; its u, which serves for pronunciation, and its k, which serves to fix its position, are elided, and pāli is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, pālayati; liṅ, pālayeta; loṭ, pālayatu; laṅ, apālayata; luṅ, apapalata; liṭ, pālayāṃcakāra; luṭ, pālayitā; benedictive liṅ, pālyāta; lṛṭ, pālayiṣyati; lṛṅ, apālayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "vā, in the sense of going": ṇic is attached. The rule "vo vidhūnane juk" means: for vā, in the sense of shaking, juk. Before the ṇic of vā, when it is used in the meaning of shaking, the augment juk comes; since its k serves to fix its position and its u serves for pronunciation, the markers are elided, and vāji is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, vājayati; liṅ, vājayeta; loṭ, vājayatu; laṅ, avājayata; luṅ, avavajata; lṛṭ, vājayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vājayitā; benedictive liṅ, vājyāta; lṛṭ, vājayiṣyati; lṛṅ, avājayiṣyata, and so on. When it does not mean shaking, juk does not come, and puk is given by the rule beginning "arti, hrī": laṭ, vāpayati; luṭ, avavapata, and so on.

Regarding "dhūña, in the sense of shaking": with ṇic, the commentary cites: "dhūñprīñor nuk kvacid vā," that is, of dhūña and prīña, nuk, in some cases optionally. Before the ṇic of dhūña, "to shake," and prīña, "to please," the augment nuk optionally comes on some occasions. On the option where nuk is attached: laṭ, dhūnayati; liṅ, dhūnayeta; loṭ, dhūnayatu; laṅ, adhūnayata; luṅ, adudhunata; liṭ, dhūnayāṃcakāra; luṭ, dhūnayitā; benedictive liṅ, dhūnyāta; lṛṭ, dhūnayiṣyati; lṛṅ, adhūnayiṣyata, and so on. On the option where nuk is not given, vṛddhi is made, and dhāvi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, dhāvayati; liṅ, dhāvayeta; loṭ, dhāvayatu; laṅ, adhāvayata; luṅ, adudhavata; liṭ, dhāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, dhāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, dhāvyāta; lṛṭ, dhāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, adhāvayiṣyata, and so on.

To prīña, "to please," ṇic is attached; and by the rule that nuk is optional in some cases for dhūña and prīña, on the option where nuk is attached: laṭ, prīṇayati; liṅ, prīṇayeta; loṭ, prīṇayatu; laṅ, aprīṇayata; luṅ, aprīṇata; liṭ, prīṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, prīṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, prīṇyāta; lṛṭ, prīṇayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aprīṇayiṣyata, and so on. On the option without nuk, by the rule on vṛddhi of ac before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, vṛddhi is made, and prāyi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, prāyayati; luṅ, apiprayata, and so on.

Regarding "līṅ, in the sense of joining": ṇic. The rule "vibhāṣā līyateḥ" means: optionally, of līyati. Before ṇic and lyap, the end of līyati is optionally changed to ā. On the option where it is changed to ā, the augment puk is attached by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," and lāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, lāpayati; liṅ, lāpayeta; loṭ, lāpayatu; laṅ, alāpayata; luṅ, alalapata; liṭ, lāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, lāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, lāpyāta; lṛṭ, lāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, alāpayiṣyata, and so on.

The rule "līlor nuglukāv anyatarasyām" means: of lī and lī, nuk and luk, optionally. For lī, "to become small," and lī, "to join," in the sense of smearing oil, the augments nuk and luk respectively come optionally: laṭ, līnayati; luṅ, alilinata, and so on.

The commentary cites: "pralambhanābhibhavapūjāsu līlor nityam ātvam aśiti vācyam," that is, in destruction, prior occurrence, and worship, for lī and lī, ā itself is always to be stated when not before what is marked with ś. When līṅ, "to join," and lī, "to become small," are used in the meanings of destruction, prior occurrence, and worship, then whatever affix comes that is not marked with ś, ā itself is always to be stated: laṭ, lāpayati. Both līṅ and lī have the same derivation and the same form: they are changed to ā and then puk is given. Luṅ, alalapata, and so on.

The rule "liyaḥ saṃmānanaśālīnīkaraṇayoś ca" means: from lī, in honoring and in harming, optionally. From lī ending in ṇic, also in honoring, in harming, and in obtaining, laṭ and the rest come as ātmanepada: "jaṭābhir ālāpayate," "śyeno vartikām ullāpayate," "kas tvām ullāpayate," and so on.

Regarding "ñibhī, in the sense of fearing": ṇic. The rule "bibheter hetubhaye" means: of bibheti, in fear arising from a cause. When fear arising from a cause is expressed, the end of bibheti before ṇic is optionally changed to ā. The commentary cites the sense of those examples: by their matted locks they wish to be honored; the hawk wishes to harm the quail; who wishes to obtain you? Further, "prayojakād bhayaṃ ca vācyam," that is, it is also stated of fear from the instigator: not only with the cause of fear, but also from one who fosters fear, the end of bibheti before ṇic is optionally changed to ā.

The rule "bhīsmyor hetubhaye" means: from bhī and smi, in fear arising from a cause. From bhī and ṣmiṅ, "to laugh slightly," when fear arising from a cause is expressed, the taṅ endings are applied. So by the rule "of bibheti, in fear arising from a cause," it is changed to ā; by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given, and bhāpi is formed; and by this sūtra the taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached: laṭ, bhāpayate; liṅ, bhāpayeta; loṭ, bhāpayatāṃ; laṅ, abhāpayata; luṅ, ababhapata; liṭ, bhāpayāṃcakre; luṭ, bhāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, bhāpayiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, bhāpayiṣyate; lṛṅ, abhāpayiṣyata, and so on. Or else: the rule "bhiyo hetubhaye ṣuk" means: for bhī, in fear arising from a cause, ṣuk. Before the ṇic of bhī, in fear arising from a cause, the augment ṣuk comes; giving ṣuk: laṭ, bhīṣayate; luṭ, abhiṣata, and so on.

Regarding "ṣmi, in the sense of laughing slightly": ṇic is attached. The rule "nityaṃ smayateḥ" means: of smayati, always.

When it is connected with a cause of fear, the end of smayati before ṇic always becomes ā: ī becomes ā. By the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given, and smāpi is formed. By the rule "from bhī and smi, in fear arising from a cause," the taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached: laṭ, smāpayate; liṅ, smāpayeta; loṭ, smāpayatāṃ; laṅ, asmāpayata; luṅ, asīṣmapata; liṭ, smāpayāṃcakre; luṭ, smāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, smāpayiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, smāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, asmāpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "sphāyī, in the sense of increasing": ṇic is attached. The rule "sphāyo vaḥ" means: of sphāyī, va. The final letter y of sphāyi is to be changed to the letter v before ṇic. Changing it to v by this sūtra, laṭ and the rest are attached to sphāvi: laṭ, sphāvayati; liṅ, sphāvayeta; loṭ, sphāvayatu; laṅ, asphāvayata; luṅ, asisphāvata; liṭ, sphāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, sphāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, sphāvyāta; lṛṭ, sphāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, asphāvayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "śadḷ, in the sense of perishing": ṇic. The rule "śader agatau taḥ" means: of śadi, when not meaning going, ta. The final letter d of śādi, when it expresses a meaning other than going, such as that of cattle, is to be changed to the letter t before ṇic, and śāti is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, śātayati; liṅ, śātayeta; loṭ, śātayatu; laṅ, aśātayata; luṅ, aśīśatata; liṭ, śātayāṃcakāra; luṭ, śātayitā; benedictive liṅ, śātyāta; lṛṭ, śātayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aśātayiṣyata, and so on. When it does mean going, d is not changed to t: laṭ, śādayati; luṅ, aśīśadata, and so on. The illustrations together with their accompanying words are: "phalāni śātayati," he makes the fruits fall; and "gāḥ śādayati gopālakaḥ," the cowherd drives the cows.

Regarding "ruha, in the sense of growing": ṇic is attached. The rule "ruhaḥ po 'nyatarasyām" means: of ruha, pa, optionally. The final letter h of ruha is optionally changed to the letter p before ṇic, and ropi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, ropayati; liṅ, ropayeta; loṭ, ropayatu; laṅ, aropayata; luṅ, arūrupata; liṭ, ropayāṃcakāra; luṭ, ropayitā; benedictive liṅ, ropyāta; lṛṭ, ropayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aropayiṣyata, and so on. Or else, when it is not changed to p: laṭ, rohayati; luṅ, arūruhata, and so on.

Regarding "krī, in the sense of exchanging goods": ṇic is attached. The rule "krīṅjīnāṃ ṇau" means: of krī, iṅ, and ji, before ṇi. For krīña, "to exchange goods"; iṅ, "to recite"; and ji, "to conquer," the end is changed to ā before ṇic. By the rule beginning "arti, hrī," puk is given, and krāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, krāpayati; liṅ, krāpayeta; loṭ, krāpayatu; laṅ, akrāpayata; luṅ, acikrāpata; liṭ, krāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, krāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, krāpyāta; lṛṭ, krāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, akrāpayiṣyata, and so on.

To iṅ, "to recite," preceded by adhi, ṇic: by the rule beginning "krī, iṅ," the end becomes ā; by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk; and by the rule that ik before ac is changed to yaṇ, laṭ and the rest are attached to adhyāpi: laṭ, adhyāpayeta; loṭ, adhyāpayatu; laṅ, adhyāpayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ" means: before ṇi too, with san and caṅ. Before san and caṅ together with ṇic, iṅ is optionally changed to gāṅ. On the option where it is changed to gāṅ: adhyājīgapata, and so on. On the option where it is not changed: āpi preceded by adhi takes caṅ; ā reverts to i; this is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "initial ac," āṭ; by "from āṭ too," vṛddhi; by the rule beginning "ec becomes ay," ai becomes āy; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: adhyāyipata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, adhyāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, adhyāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, adhyāpyāta; lṛṭ, adhyāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, adhyāpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ji, in the sense of conquering": ṇic. By the rule beginning "krī, iṅ, ji," the end becomes ā, and by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given, and jāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, jāpayati; liṅ, jāpayeta; loṭ, jāpayatu; laṅ, ajāpayata; luṅ, ajījapata; liṭ, jāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, jāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, jāpyāta; lṛṭ, jāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajāpayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ṣidha, in the sense of pleasing fully": ṇic is attached. The rule "siddhyater apāralaukike" means: of siddhyati, when not pertaining to the other world. The letter i of siddhyati, when its meaning does not pertain to the other world, is to be changed to ā before ṇi, and laṭ and the rest are attached to sādhi: laṭ, sādhayati; liṅ, sādhayeta; loṭ, sādhayatu; laṅ, asādhayata; luṅ, asāsadhata; laṭ, sādhayāṃcakāra; luṭ, sādhayitā; benedictive liṅ, sādhyāta; lṛṭ, sādhayiṣyati; lṛṅ, asādhayiṣyata, and so on. Or else: laṭ, sedhayati; luṅ, asīsidhata, and so on. The illustrations of these together with their accompanying words are: "rājā sādhayati," he wishes to please the king; and "guruḥ sedhayati," he wishes to please the teacher.

Regarding "ciña, in the sense of gathering": ṇic is attached. The rule "cisphuror ṇau" means: of ci and sphur, before ṇi. Before the ṇic of ciña and sphura, they are optionally changed to ā. On the option where it is changed to ā, the augment puk is given by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," and cāpi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, cāpayati; liṅ, cāpayeta; loṭ, cāpayatu; laṅ, acāpayata; luṅ, acīcapata; liṭ, cāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, cāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, cāpyāta; lṛṭ, cāpayiṣyati; lṛṅ, acāpayiṣyata, and so on. Or else, by the rule on vṛddhi of ac before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, vṛddhi is made: laṭ, cāyayati; luṅ, acīcayata, and so on.

Regarding "sphura, in the sense of radiating": ṇic. By the rule "of ci and sphur, before ṇi," changing to ā or not is made optional. On the option where it is changed to ā, laṭ and the rest are attached to sphāri: laṭ, sphārayati; liṅ, sphārayeta; loṭ, sphārayatu; laṅ, asphārayata; luṅ, apusphārata; liṭ, sphārayāṃcakāra; luṭ, sphārayitā; benedictive liṅ, sphāryāta; lṛṭ, sphārayiṣyati; lṛṅ, asphārayiṣyata, and so on. On the option where it is not changed to ā: laṭ, sphorayati; luṅ, apusphurata, and so on.

Regarding "veña, in the sense of weaving": ṇic. The rule "prajane vīyateḥ" means: of vīyati, in the sense of generating. When vīyati is used in the meaning of generating, it is changed to ā before ṇic; puk is given, and laṭ and the rest are attached to vāpi: laṭ, vāpayati; liṅ, vāpayeta; loṭ, vāpayatu; luṅ, avāpayata; luṅ, avīvapata; loṭ, vāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, vāpyāta; lṛṭ, vāpayiṣyata, and so on. Or else: by the rule that in the original enunciation an ec becomes ā when not before what is marked with ś, ec becomes ā; by the rule beginning "śā, chā," the augment yuk is given; and laṭ and the rest are attached to vāyi: laṭ, vāyayati; luṅ, avīvayata, and so on.

Regarding "ṣṭuñ, in the sense of praising": ṇic is attached. By the rule on vṛddhi of ac before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, vṛddhi is made, and stāvi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, stāvayati; liṅ, stāvayata; loṭ, stāvayatu; laṅ, astāvayata; luṅ, aṣuṣṭavata; liṭ, stāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, stāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, stāvyāta; lṛṭ, stāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, astāvayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "bhū, in the sense of existing": ṇic. Vṛddhi is made, and bhāvi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: bhāvayati; liṅ, bhāvayeta; loṭ, bhāvayatu; laṅ, abhāvayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "oḥ puyaṇjyapare" means: of u, before pu, yaṇ, or j followed by a. The u of the reduplicate of a root reduplicated before san is changed to the letter i when it is followed by any one of pu, that is, the labial class; the letters comprised in yaṇ, each in turn; the letter j; or the letter a. Here, by the rule that before a light syllable followed by caṅ, where no ak has been elided, it is treated as before san, an operation like that before san applies, so u is changed to i; by the rule on the lengthening of the light vowel, it is lengthened; and by eliding ṇi: abībhavata, and so on. For the remaining l-affixes: liṭ, bhāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, bhāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, bhāvyāta; lṛṭ, bhāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, abhāvayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "yu, in the sense of mixing": ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and yāvi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, yāvayati; liṅ, yāvayeta; loṭ, yāvayatu; laṅ, ayāvayata. In luṅ, since by the rule beginning "where no ak has been elided" an operation like that before san applies, u becomes i and that is lengthened: ayīyavata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, yāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, yāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, yāvyāta; lṛṭ, yāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ayāvayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, regarding "ju, in the sense of going": ṇic is attached, and jāvi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, jāvayati; liṅ, jāvayeta; loṭ, jāvayatu; laṅ, ajāvayata; luṅ, ajījavata; liṭ, jāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, jāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, jāvyāta; lṛṭ, jāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajāvayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "sru, in the sense of going": ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to srāvi: laṭ, srāvayati; liṅ, srāvayeta; loṭ, srāvayatu; luṅ, asrāvayata, and so on. In luṅ: the rule "sravatiśṛṇotidravatipravatiplavaticyavatīnāṃ vā" means: optionally, of sravati, śṛṇoti, dravati, pravati, plavati, and cyavati. For sru, "to go"; śru, "to hear"; dru, "to go"; and pru, pluṅ, and cyuṅ, "to go," before san, and before caṅ together with ṇi, the reduplicate is optionally changed to i: asisravata, and so on; or asusravata, and so on. For the remaining l-affixes: liṭ, srāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, srāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, srāvyāta; lṛṭ, srāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, asrāvayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, to śru, "to hear," ṇic is attached, and laṭ and the rest are attached to śrāvi: laṭ, śrāvayati; liṅ, śrāvayeta; loṭ, śrāvayatu, and so on. In luṅ, since it is optionally changed to i: aśiśravata, and so on; or aśuśravata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, śrāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, śrāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, śrāvyāta; lṛṭ, śrāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aśrāvayiṣyata, and so on.

To dru, "to go," ṇic is attached, and laṭ and the rest are attached to drāvi: lṛṭ, drāvayate; liṅ, drāvayeta; loṭ, drāvayatu; laṅ, adrāvayata. In luṅ, since it is optionally changed to i: adidravata, and so on; or adudravata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, drāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, drāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, drāvyāta; lṛṭ, drāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, adrāvayiṣyata, and so on.

To pru, "to go," ṇic is attached, and laṭ and the rest are attached to prāvi: laṭ, prāvayati; liṅ, prāvayeta; loṭ, prāvayatu; laṅ, aprāvayata, and so on. In luṅ, since it is optionally changed to i: apipravata, and so on; or apupravata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, prāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, prāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, prāvyāta; lṛṭ, prāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aprāvayiṣyata, and so on.

To plu, "to go," ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to plāvi: laṭ, plāvayati; liṅ, plāvayeta; loṭ, plāvayatu; laṅ, aplāvayata, and so on. In luṅ, since it is optionally changed to i: apiplavata, and so on; or apuplavata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, plāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, plāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, plāvyāta; lṛṭ, plāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aplāvayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "cyuṅ, in the sense of going": ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to cyāvi: laṭ, cyāvayati; liṅ, cyāvayeta; laṭ, cyāvayatu; laṅ, acyāvayata. In luṅ, since it is optionally made i: acicyavata, and so on; or acucyavata, and so on. For lṛṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, cyāvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, cyāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, cyāvyāta; lṛṭ, cyāvayiṣyati; lṛṅ, acyāvayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "guhū, in the sense of covering over": ṇic is attached. By the rule on ū for the penultimate of goha, it is lengthened, and gūhi is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, gūhayati; liṅ, gūhayeta; loṭ, gūhayatu; laṅ, agūhayata; luṅ, ajūguhata; liṭ, gūhayāṃcakāra; luṭ, gūhayitā; benedictive liṅ, gūhyāta; lṛṭ, gūhayiṣyati; lṛṅ, agūhayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "duṣa, in the sense of being afflicted": ṇic is attached. The rule "doṣo ṇau" means: of doṣa, before ṇi.

The u of the penultimate of duṣa becomes ū before ṇi, and laṭ and the rest are attached to dūṣi: laṭ, dūṣayati; liṅ, dūṣayeta; loṭ, dūṣayatu; laṅ, adūṣayata; luṅ, adudūṣata; liṭ, dūṣayāṃcakāra; luṭ, dūṣayitā; benedictive liṅ, dūṣyāta; lṛṭ, dūṣayiṣyati; lṛṅ, adūṣayiṣyata, and so on.
