Further, the rule "vā cittavirāge" means: optionally, in affliction of the mind. When duṣa is used for affliction of the mind, the letter u of its penultimate optionally becomes ū before ṇi. The procedure where it is changed to ū has already been shown; on the option where it is not changed, guṇa is made by the rule beginning "ending in puk": laṭ, doṣayati; luṅ, adūduṣata, and so on.

Regarding "ghaṭa, in the sense of doing": ṇic is attached. The rule "mitāṃ hrasvaḥ" means: short, of those marked with m. For roots that bear the designation "marked with m," such as ghaṭa, the penultimate is shortened before ṇic: laṭ, ghaṭayati; liṅ, ghaṭayeta; loṭ, ghaṭayatu; laṅ, aghaṭayata; luṅ, ajīghaṭata; liṭ, ghaṭayāṃcakāra; luṭ, ghaṭayitā; benedictive liṅ, ghaṭyāta; lṛṭ, ghaṭayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aghaṭayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, regarding "vyatha, in the sense of trembling with suffering and fear": ṇic is attached; vṛddhi is made by the rule on the penultimate, and then it is shortened again, and laṭ and the rest are attached to vyathi: laṭ, vyathayati; liṅ, vyathayata; loṭ, vyathayatu; laṅ, avyathayata; luṅ, avīvyathata; liṭ, vyathayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vyathayitā; benedictive liṅ, vyathyāta; lṛṭ, vyathayiṣyati; lṛṅ, avyathayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "janī, in the sense of being born": ṇic is attached. The rule "janījṝṣknasurañjo 'mantāś ca" means: of janī, jṝṣ, knas, and rañja too, ending in m. For janī, "to be born"; jṝṣ, "to grow old"; knas, "sound"; and rañja, "to dye," the designation "ending in m" is also applied before ṇic. Its purpose is that the penultimate be shortened by the rule on the short vowel of those marked with m: laṭ, janayati; liṅ, janayeta; loṭ, janayatu; laṅ, ajanayata; luṅ, ajījanata; liṭ, janayāṃcakāra; luṭ, janayitā; benedictive liṅ, janyāta; lṛṭ, janayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajanayiṣyata, and so on.

To jṝṣ, "to grow old," ṇic: by the rule on vṛddhi of ac before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, vṛddhi; and by the rule that janī, jṝṣ, knas, and rañja too end in m, it is shortened, and laṭ and the rest are attached to jari: laṭ, jarayati; liṅ, jarayeta; loṭ, jarayatu; laṅ, ajarayata; luṅ, ajījarata; liṭ, jarayāṃcakāra; luṭ, jarayitā; benedictive liṅ, jaryāta; lṛṭ, jarayiṣyate; lṛṅ, ajarayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "knasa, in the sense of sound": ṇic is attached, and laṭ and the rest are attached to knasi: laṭ, knasayati; liṅ, knasayeta; loṭ, knasayatu; laṅ, aknasayata; luṅ, acīknasata; liṭ, knasayāṃcakāra; luṭ, knasayitā; benedictive liṅ, knasyāta; lṛṭ, knasayiṣyate; lṛṅ, aknasayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "rañja, in the sense of dyeing": ṇic is attached, and laṭ and the rest are attached to rañji: laṭ, rañjayati; liṅ, rañjayeta; loṭ, rañjayatu; laṅ, arañjayata; luṅ, arīrañjata; liṭ, rañjayāṃcakāra; luṭ, rañjayitā; benedictive liṅ, rañjyāta; lṛṭ, rañjayiṣyati; lṛṅ, arañjayiṣyata, and so on. The commentary cites: "rañjer ṇau mṛgaramaṇe nalopaḥ," that is, for rañja before ṇi, in reference to the color of deer, elision of n. When the ṇic of rañja follows and it is used in reference to the color of deer, n is elided: laṭ, rajayati; luṅ, arīrajata, and so on.

To jña, "to understand," ṇic is attached: laṭ, jñāpayati; luṅ, ajījñāpata, and so on. Further, "māraṇatoṣaṇaniśāmaneṣu jña" means: jña, in killing, pleasing, and sharpening. When it is used in these meanings, killing and the rest, jñā bears the designation "marked with m"; the purpose is that it be shortened. To jña, ṇic; by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given; and by this sūtra the penultimate is shortened, and jñapi is formed. Laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, jñapayati; liṅ, jñapayeta; loṭ, jñapayatu; luṅ, ajñapayata; luṅ, ajījñapata; liṭ, jñapayāṃcakāra; luṭ, jñapayitā; benedictive liṅ, jñapyāta; lṛṭ, jñapayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajñapayiṣyata, and so on. The illustrations, with accompanying words, in which those meanings apply are such as: "saṃjñapayati śatrūn," he wishes his foes to die altogether; "vijñapayati rājānam," he wishes the kings to be pleased; and "jñapayati śastram," he wishes to make the weapon very sharp.

To jvala, "to blaze," ṇic is attached. The rule "jvalahvalahmalanamo 'nupasargād vā glāsnāvanuvamaś ca" means: when without a preverb, of jvala, hvala, hmala, nama, and of glā, snā, vana, and vama too. When not preceded by a preverb, jvala, "to blaze"; hvala and hmala, "to move"; ṇama, "sound"; and also glā, "to waste in body"; snā, "to be clean"; vana, "to beg"; and ṭuvama, "to vomit," bear the designation "marked with m"; the purpose is that they be shortened: laṭ, jvalayati; liṅ, jvalayeta; loṭ, jvalayatu; laṅ, ajvalayata; luṅ, ajījvalata; liṭ, jvalayāṃcakāra; luṭ, jvalayitā; benedictive liṅ, jvalyāta; lṛṭ, jvalayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajvalayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, to hvala, "to move," ṇic is attached and it is shortened, and laṭ and the rest are attached to hvali: laṭ, hvalayati; luṅ, ajīhvalata, and so on. To hmala, "to move," ṇic is attached and it is shortened, and laṭ and the rest are attached to hmali: laṭ, hmalayati; luṅ, ajīhmalata, and so on. To ṇama, "sound," ṇic, and it is shortened: laṭ, namayati; luṅ, anīnamata, and so on.

To glā, "to waste in body," ṇic is attached, the augment puk is given, and it is shortened: laṭ, glapayati; luṅ, ajīglapata, and so on.

Regarding "ṣṇā, in the sense of being clean": ṇic; by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk; and it is shortened, and laṭ and the rest are attached to snapi: laṭ, snapayati; luṅ, asīṣṇapata, and so on.

To vana, "to beg," ṇic, and it is shortened, and laṭ and the rest are attached to vani: laṭ, vanayate; luṅ, avīvanata, and so on.

To ṭuvama, "to vomit," ṇic, and since it is shortened, laṭ and the rest are attached to vami: laṭ, vamayati; luṅ, avīvamata, and so on. When there is a preverb, it is not shortened: laṭ, prajvālayati; luṅ, prājījvalata, and so on.

Regarding "kamu, in the sense of being beautiful": ṇic. The rule "na kamyamicamām" means: not of kama, am, and cam.

Kamu, "to be beautiful"; ama, "illness"; and cama, "to eat," do not bear the designation "ending in m." The purpose is that they not be shortened. So by the rule on the penultimate, vṛddhi is made, and to kāmi, which by this sūtra is not shortened, laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, kāmayati; laṅ, kāmayeta; loṭ, kāmayatu; laṅ, akāmayata; luṅ, acīkamata; liṭ, kāmayāṃcakāra; luṭ, kāmayitā; benedictive liṅ, kāmyāta; lṛṭ, kāmayiṣyati; lṛṅ, akāmayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ama, in the sense of illness": ṇic, and vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to āmi: laṭ, āmayati; liṅ, āmayeta; loṭ, āmayatu; laṅ, āmayata. In luṅ, since ma together with ṇi is reduplicated: āmimata, and so on. For liṭ and the remaining ones: liṭ, āmayāṃcakāra; luṭ, āmayitā; benedictive liṅ, āmyāta; lṛṭ, āmayiṣyati; lṛṅ, āmayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "cama, in the sense of eating": ṇic, and vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to cāmi: laṭ, cāmayati; liṅ, cāmayeta; loṭ, cāmayatu; laṅ, acāmayata; luṅ, acīcamata; liṭ, cāmayāṃcakāra; luṭ, cāmayitā; benedictive liṅ, cāmyāta; lṛṭ, cāmayiṣyati; lṛṅ, acāmayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "śamu, in the sense of becoming calm": with ṇic, vṛddhi is made: laṭ, śāmayati; liṅ, aśīśamata, and so on. The rule "śamo 'darśane mit" means: of śamu, when not meaning seeing, marked with m. When śamu is used in a meaning other than seeing, it bears the designation "marked with m"; the purpose is that it be shortened. By this sūtra it is shortened, and śami is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, śamayati; liṅ, śamayeta; loṭ, śamayatu; laṅ, aśamayata; luṅ, aśīśamata; liṭ, śamayāṃcakāra; luṭ, śamayitā; benedictive liṅ, śamyāta; lṛṭ, śamayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aśamayiṣyata, and so on.

To yamu, "to cease," ṇic, and vṛddhi is made: laṭ, yāmayati; liṅ, yāmayeta; loṭ, yāmayatu; laṅ, ayāmayata; luṅ, ayāṃyamata; liṭ, yāmayāṃcakāra; luṭ, yāmayitā; benedictive liṅ, yāmyāta; lṛṭ, yāmayiṣyati; lṛṅ, ayāmayiṣyata, and so on. Further, the rule "yamo 'pariveṣaṇe" means: of yamu, when not meaning serving. Yamu, when it does not mean serving, is to be given the designation "marked with m"; the purpose is that it be shortened: laṭ, yamayati; luṅ, ayīyamata, and so on.

Regarding "skhadir, in the sense of digging": ṇic is attached. By the rule on the penultimate, vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to skhādi: laṭ, skhādayati; liṅ, skhādayeta; loṭ, skhādayatu; laṅ, askhadayata; luṅ, acīskhadata; liṭ, skhādayāṃcakāra; luṭ, skhādayitā; benedictive liṅ, skhādyāta; lṛṭ, skhādayiṣyati; lṛṅ, askhādayiṣyata, and so on. Further, the rule "skhadir avaparibhyāṃ ca" means: of skhadi, after ava and pari too. Skhadi following ava and pari also bears the designation "marked with m," and since it is shortened: avaskhadayati, pariskhadayati. The commentary cites: "sopasargasya skhadeḥ phaṇeś ca mit kvacid vā," that is, of skhadi with a preverb and of phaṇa, "marked with m," in some cases optionally. Skhadir and phaṇa, when any preverb precedes them, are on some occasions optionally given the designation "marked with m": praskhadayati, praskhādayati, and so on.

Regarding "phaṇa, in the sense of sound": ṇic, and vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to phāṇi: laṭ, phāṇayati; liṅ, phāṇayeta; loṭ, phāṇayatu; laṅ, aphāṇayata; luṅ, apīphaṇata; liṭ, phāṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, phāṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, phāṇyāta; lṛṭ, phāṇayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aphāṇayiṣyata, and so on. When a preverb precedes, since by the citation concerning skhadi and phaṇa with a preverb it is optionally "marked with m": praphaṇayati, and so on; or praphāṇayati, and so on.

Regarding "iṇ, in the sense of going": ṇic. The rule "ṇau gamir abodhane" means: before ṇi, gami, when not meaning understanding. When it does not have the meaning of understanding, iṇ is to be changed to gami before ṇic. Since the i serves for pronunciation, it is elided and joined to the i of ṇic, and gami is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, gamayati; liṅ, gamayeta; loṭ, gamayatu; laṅ, agamayata; luṅ, ajīgamata; liṭ, gamayāṃcakāra; luṭ, gamayitā; benedictive liṅ, gamyāta; lṛṭ, gamayiṣyati; lṛṅ, agamayiṣyata. When it is used in the meaning of understanding, it does not become ga: by the rule on vṛddhi of ac before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, vṛddhi is made, and laṭ and the rest are attached to āyi, thus formed: āyayati, and so on. In luṅ: āyi takes caṅ, and the root is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "initial ac," āṭ; by "from āṭ too," vṛddhi; by the rule beginning "ec becomes ay," āy; by the rule beginning "before caṅ following ṇi," the penultimate is shortened; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: āyayata, and so on.

To han, "to harm," ṇic is attached. The rule "hanas to 'ciṇṇaloḥ" means: of han, t, when not before ciṇ and ṇal. Before an affix marked with ñ or ṇ other than ciṇ and ṇal, the final of han becomes the letter t. By the rule on the h of hanti before what is marked with ñ or ṇ, h becomes gh; by this sūtra, n becomes t; vṛddhi is made; and laṭ and the rest are attached to ghāti: laṭ, ghātayati; liṅ, ghātayeta; loṭ, ghātayatu; laṅ, aghātayata; luṅ, ajīghatata; liṭ, ghātayāṃcakāra; luṭ, ghātayitā; benedictive liṅ, ghātyāta; lṛṭ, ghātayiṣyati; lṛṅ, aghātayiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "īrṣya, in the sense of envy": ṇic is attached, and laṭ and the rest are attached to īrṣyi: laṅ, īrṣyayati; liṅ, īrṣyayeta; loṭ, īrṣyayatu; laṅ, airṣyayata, and so on. In luṅ, īrṣyi takes caṅ; ṣa together with ṇi is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "initial ac," āṭ is added and vṛddhi made; and by the rule on ṇi before what lacks iṭ, ṇi is elided: airṣiṣyata, and so on. Or else: the rule "īrṣyates tṛtīyasya dve" means: of īrṣyati, the third, doubled. Before caṅ together with ṇi of īrṣyati, the third member of the consonant cluster itself is optionally reduplicated; since ya, the third of the cluster, is itself reduplicated: airṣyiyata, and so on. For the remaining l-affixes: liṭ, īrṣyayāṃcakāra; luṭ, īrṣyayitā; benedictive liṅ, īrṣyāta; lṛṭ, īrṣyayiṣyati; lṛṅ, airṣyayiṣyata, and so on.

"Iti pāṇinivyākaraṇasya sūtrāt ṇijantāḥ samāptāḥ," that is: from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the forms ending in ṇic are complete.

From the notes called The Chariot of Mindful Recollection of the Jewel of Good Explanation, which set down as notes the sense, the procedures, the illustrations and so forth of the text and commentary of that great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, here the rough procedures for the forms ending in ṇic are for now complete. By the rule that after hal, y of yam before yam is elided, the former y is elided.

Second, I shall explain the domains of application of the affix san, by which roots are formed into further roots. The rule "dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā" means: after a root that is the object and has the same agent, in the sense of desire, optionally. After a root that is the object of the action and whose agent is the same as the agent of the desire, san optionally comes, in the meaning of conveying the desire together with its agent.

Ad, "to eat": san is attached. By the rule on ghasḷ before luṅ and san, it is changed to ghasḷ, and ḷ is elided. By the rule on san, the root is reduplicated; by the rule that ku and h become cu; by the rule "in the reduplicate, car too," jh becomes j; by the rule on i before san, it is changed to i; and by the rule on car before khar, s is changed to t, and jighatsa is formed. Laṭ and the rest are attached; for the agent, śap; after the markers are elided, by the rule on a before guṇa, the two are changed into the form of the following one, and so on: laṭ, jighatsati; liṅ, jighatseta; loṭ, jighatsatu; laṅ, ajighatsata, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, and by the rule on the elision of a, a is elided: ajighatsita, ajighatsiṣṭāṃ, ajighatsiṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, ām is attached by the rule beginning "kās," and a is elided: jighatsāṃcakāra, jighatsāṃbabhūva, jighatsāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ is given and a is elided: jighatsitā, jighatsitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: jighatsyāta, jighatsyāstaṃ, jighatsyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given and a is elided: jighatsiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ajighatsiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "dīṅ, in the sense of wasting away": san is attached, the root is reduplicated and shortened, and the taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached to didīṣa: laṭ, didīṣate; liṅ, didīṣeta; loṭ, didīṣatāṃ; laṅ, adidīṣata; luṅ, adidīṣiṣṭa; liṭ, didīṣāṃcakre; luṭ, didīṣitā; benedictive liṅ, didīṣiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, didīṣiṣyate; lṛṅ, adidīṣiṣyata, and so on. The commentary cites: "dīṅaḥ sany ātvaṃ kecid vā," that is, for dīṅ before san, ā itself, in some cases optionally. Before san, dīṅ is optionally changed to ā itself on some occasions. On the option where it is changed to ā, the reduplicate is shortened, and by the rule on i before san it is changed to i, and laṭ and the rest are attached to didās: laṭ, didāsate; liṅ, didāseta; loṭ, didāsatāṃ; laṅ, adidāsata; luṅ, adidāsiṣṭa; liṭ, didāsāṃcakre; luṭ, didāsitā; benedictive liṅ, didāsiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, didāsiṣyate; lṛṅ, adidāsiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "dyuta, in the sense of shining": san is attached. By the rule on san, the root is reduplicated; by the rule on the saṃprasāraṇa of dyuta and svāpa, the reduplicate takes saṃprasāraṇa; and by the rule on iṭ for what begins with val, iṭ is given, giving didyut, i, san. The rule "ralo vyupadhād dhalādeḥ saṃś ca" means: from what has u or i as penultimate and begins with hal, and from what ends in r or l, san too. San with iṭ, following a root that begins with a consonant and has either i or u as its penultimate, or a root ending in r or l, is optionally given the designation "marked with k." On the option where it is marked with k, guṇa is not made; on the option where it is not marked with k, guṇa is made by the rule beginning "ending in puk." So didyutiṣa or didyotiṣa is formed, and the taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached: laṭ, didyutiṣate and didyotiṣate; liṅ, didyutiṣeta and didyotiṣeta; loṭ, didyutiṣatāṃ and didyotiṣatāṃ; laṅ, adidyutiṣata and adidyotiṣata; luṅ, adidyutiṣiṣṭa and adidyotiṣiṣṭa; liṭ, didyutiṣāṃcakre and didyotiṣāṃcakre; luṭ, didyutiṣitā and didyotiṣitā; benedictive liṅ, didyutiṣiṣīṣṭa and didyotiṣiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, didyutiṣiṣyate and didyotiṣiṣyate; lṛṅ, adidyutiṣiṣyata and adidyotiṣiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "uccha, in the sense of breaking": san is attached. Since the commentary says that the ccha of ucchi is reduplicated together with iṭ, it is reduplicated, and by the rule "in the reduplicate, car too," ch is changed to c, and ucicchiṣa is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, ucicchiṣati; liṅ, ucicchiṣeta; loṭ, ucicchiṣatu; laṅ, aucicchiṣata; luṅ, aucicchiṣīta; liṭ, ucicchiṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, ucicchiṣitā; benedictive liṅ, ucicchiṣyāta; lṛṭ, ucicchiṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, aucicchiṣiṣyata, and so on.

To iṅ, "to recite," ṇi and san are attached. By the rule "before ṇi too, with san and caṅ," iṅ is optionally changed to gāṅ; it is reduplicated; by the rule that ku and h become cu; by the rule on the short vowel, jā is shortened; by the rule on i before san, i; by the rule on iṭ for what begins with val, iṭ; by the rule beginning "of all roots," guṇa; by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given; by "ec becomes ay," ay; and by placing adhi before it, adhijigāpayiṣa is formed. Laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, adhijigāpayiṣati; liṅ, adhijigāpayiṣeta; loṭ, adhijigāpayiṣatu; laṅ, adhyajigāpayiṣata; luṅ, adhyajigāpayiṣīta; liṭ, adhijigāpayiṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, adhijigāpayiṣitā; benedictive liṅ, adhijigāpayiṣyāta; lṛṭ, adhijigāpayiṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, adhyajigāpayiṣiṣyata, and so on. On the option where it is not changed to gāṅ: by the rule "of krī, iṅ, and ji, before ṇi," it is changed to ā; by the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given; by the rule on san, pa together with ṇi is reduplicated; by the rule on iṭ for what begins with val, iṭ is given; by the rule beginning "of all roots," guṇa; by the rule beginning "ec becomes ay"; and by placing adhi before it, adhyāpipayiṣa is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, adhyāpipayiṣati; luṅ, adhyāpipayiṣīta, and so on.

Regarding "ṭuośvi, in the sense of going and of increasing": ṇi and san. By the rule "before ṇi too, with san and caṅ," it is optionally changed by saṃprasāraṇa. On the option where it is not changed: laṭ, śiśvayayiṣati; luṅ, aśiśvayayiṣīta, and so on. On the option where it is changed: laṭ, śuśāvayiṣati; luṅ, aśuśavayiṣīta, and so on. Further, when san is attached to the bare root without ṇic, iṭ is given and guṇa made: laṭ, śiśvayiṣati; luṅ, aśiśvayiṣīta, and so on.

Regarding "hveña, in the sense of contending": ṇic and san are attached. By the rule beginning "in the original enunciation, when not before what is marked with ś," ec becomes ā; by the rule on the saṃprasāraṇa of hvā, it is changed by saṃprasāraṇa; and derived by reduplication and the rest, juhāvayiṣa is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, juhāvayiṣati; liṅ, juhāvayiṣeta; loṭ, juhāvayiṣatu; laṅ, ajuhāvayiṣata; luṅ, ajuhāvayiṣīta; liṭ, juhāvayiṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, juhāvayiṣitā; benedictive liṅ, juhāvayiṣyāta; lṛṭ, juhāvayiṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajuhāvayiṣiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "ana, in the sense of breathing": san. By the rule on iṭ for what begins with val, iṭ is given; and by the rule on san, na together with iṭ is reduplicated, and aniniṣa is formed. Laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, aniniṣati; liṅ, aniniṣeta; loṭ, aniniṣatu; laṅ, āniniṣata; luṅ, āniniṣīta; liṭ, aniniṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, aniniṣitā; benedictive liṅ, aniniṣyāta; lṛṭ, aniniṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, aniniṣiṣyata, and so on. The rule "ubhau sābhyāsasya" means: both, of what has the reduplicate. Before the san of aniti, when a preverb containing a cause for the change to ṇ precedes, both n-letters, that of the reduplicate and that of the penultimate, are to be changed to the letter ṇ: prāṇiṇiṣati, and so on.

Regarding "vṛtu, in the sense of turning": san is attached. The rule "halantāc ca" means: and from what ends in hal. San without iṭ, following a root whose final is one of the letters comprised in hal and whose penultimate is one of the letters comprised in ik, bears the designation "marked with k." Here, with the non-taṅ endings, iṭ does not come, by the rule beginning "from the four vṛt roots." The root is reduplicated; by the rule on a for ṛ, a; that is changed to i by the rule on i before san; and since by this sūtra the san is marked with k, guṇa and the like are not made, and vivṛtsa is formed. The non-taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached: laṭ, vivṛtsati; liṅ, vivṛtseta; loṭ, vivṛtsatu; laṅ, avivṛtsata; luṅ, avivṛtsīta; liṭ, vivṛtsāṃcakāra; luṭ, vivṛtsitā; benedictive liṅ, vivṛtsyāta; lṛṭ, vivṛtsiṣyati; lṛṅ, avivṛtsiṣyata, and so on.

With the taṅ endings, iṭ is given by the rule on iṭ for what begins with val, and guṇa is made; and laṭ and the rest are attached to vivartiṣa: laṭ, vivartiṣate; liṅ, vivartiṣeta; loṭ, vivartiṣatāṃ; laṅ, avivartiṣata; luṅ, avivartiṣiṣṭa; liṭ, vivartiṣāṃcakre; luṭ, vivartiṣitā; benedictive liṅ, vivartiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, vivartiṣiṣyate; lṛṅ, avivartiṣiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "nṛtī, in the sense of moving the body": san is attached. By the rule on kṛt, cṛt, chṛd, tṛd, and nṛt, iṭ is made optional. On the option without iṭ, since the san is marked with k, guṇa and the like are not made; on the option with iṭ, guṇa is made; and derived by reduplication and the rest: laṭ, ninṛtsati and ninartiṣati; liṅ, ninṛtseta and ninartiṣeta; loṭ, ninṛtsatu and ninartiṣatu; laṅ, aninṛtsata and aninartiṣata; luṅ, aninṛtsīta and aninartiṣīta; liṭ, ninṛtsāṃcakāra and ninartiṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, ninṛtsitā and ninartiṣitā; benedictive liṅ, ninṛtsyāta and ninartiṣyāta; lṛṭ, ninṛtsiṣyati and ninartiṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, aninṛtsiṣyata and aninartiṣiṣyata, and so on.

Regarding "tṝ, in the sense of swimming and of crossing": san is attached. The rule "iṭ sani vā" means: iṭ before san, optionally. Before san following vṛṅ and vṛña and roots ending in ṝ, iṭ comes optionally. The rule "iko jhal" means: after ik, what begins with jhal. San that begins with a jhal, that is, san without iṭ, following a root ending in one of the letters comprised in ik, is to be given the designation "marked with k." On the option without iṭ, since by this sūtra the san is marked with k, guṇa and vṛddhi are not made. By the rule on it for the ṝ of a root, ṝ is changed to it; the root is reduplicated; by the rule that aṇ replacing ṛ is followed by r, r is added; and by the rule "of the penultimate too," it is lengthened, and titīrṣa is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, titīrṣati; liṅ, titīrṣeta; loṭ, titīrṣatu; laṅ, atitīrṣata; luṅ, atitīrṣīta; liṭ, titīrṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, titīrṣitā; benedictive liṅ, titīrṣyāta; lṛṭ, titīrṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, atitīrṣiṣyata, and so on. On the option with iṭ: by the rule "optionally after vṛ and ṝ," iṭ and īṭ are made optional; the root is reduplicated; by the rule on a for ṛ, a, and iṭ before san; and guṇa is made by the rule beginning "of all roots": laṭ, titariṣati; luṅ, atitariṣīta; liṭ, titariṣāṃcakāra, and so on; or laṭ, titarīṣati; luṅ, atitarīṣīta; liṭ, titarīṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

Regarding "vṛṅ, in the sense of honoring": san is attached. The rule "ajjhanagamāṃ sani" means: of what ends in ac, and of han and gam, before san. Before san, the final of roots ending in ac and the penultimate of han and gam are lengthened, so vṛ is changed to vṝ. By the rule "iṭ before san, optionally," iṭ is made optional. On the option without iṭ, since the san is marked with k, by the rule on ut after a labial, ṝ is changed to ut; by the rule that aṇ replacing ṛ is followed by r, r is added; the root is reduplicated; and by the rule "of the penultimate too," it is lengthened, and bubūrṣa is formed. Attaching laṭ and the rest to it: laṭ, bubūrṣati; liṅ, bubūrṣeta; loṭ, bubūrṣatu; laṅ, abubūrṣata; luṅ, abubūrṣīta; liṭ, bubūrṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, bubūrṣitā; benedictive liṅ, bubūrṣyāta; lṛṭ, bubūrṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, abubūrṣiṣyata, and so on. On the option with iṭ: by the rule beginning with vṛ and ṝ, iṭ and īṭ are made optional; the root is reduplicated; by the rule on a for ṛ, a, and i before san; and guṇa is made by the rule beginning "of all roots": laṭ, vivariṣati; luṅ, avivariṣīta; liṭ, vivariṣāṃcakāra, and so on; or laṭ, vivarīṣati; luṅ, avivarīṣīta; liṭ, vivarīṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to ḍukṛñ, "to do." By the rule on lengthening before san for roots ending in a vowel, han, and gam, the vowel is lengthened. By the rule on i for the ṛ of a root, it becomes i; by the rule on the aṇ of ṛ, r follows it. By the rule on c for k and h, the reduplicate takes c. Saṃ is placed in front. By the sūtra beginning with saṃ, pari, and upa for karoti, the augment suṭ is given before the k. Since the commentary explains that here iṭ is not even optional, and that iṭ is never given at all, iṭ is not added. Saṃciskīrṣa is thus formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached to it: laṭ, saṃciskīrṣati; liṅ, saṃciskīrṣeta; loṭ, saṃciskīrṣatu; laṅ, samaciskīrṣata; luṅ, samaciskīrṣīta; liṭ, saṃciskīrṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, saṃciskīrṣitā; benedictive liṅ, saṃciskīrṣyāta; lṛṭ, saṃciskīrṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, samaciskīrṣiṣyata, and so on.

San is applied to dhṛ, "to hold." By the rule on lengthening before san for roots ending in a vowel, han, and gam, the vowel is lengthened. Iṭ before san is made optional. In the option without iṭ, by the rule on a ṛ preceded by a labial, it becomes u; the root is reduplicated; by the rule on the aṇ of ṛ, r follows; and the penultimate is lengthened. Dudhūrṣa is thus formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, dudhūrṣati; luṅ, adudhūrṣīta; liṭ, dudhūrṣāṃcakāra, and so on. In the option with iṭ, guṇa is made: laṭ, didhariṣati; luṅ, adidhariṣīta; liṭ, didhariṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to ji, "to conquer." By the rule on ji before san and liṭ, the j becomes g, and the root is reduplicated: laṭ, jigīṣati; liṅ, jigīṣeta; loṭ, jigīṣatu; laṅ, ajigīṣata; luṅ, ajigīṣīta; liṭ, jigīṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, jigīṣitā; benedictive liṅ, jigīṣyāta; lṛṭ, jigīṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajigīṣiṣyata, and so on.

San is applied to ciñ, "to gather," and the rest. By the optional rule for ci, the change to k is made optional, either made or not made: laṭ, cikīṣati; luṅ, acikīṣīta; liṭ, cikīṣāṃcakāra, and so on; or laṭ, cicīṣati; luṅ, acicīṣīta; liṭ, cicīṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to han, "to harm." The root is reduplicated. By the rule on c for k and h, and by the rule that the reduplicate takes car, the h becomes j. The vowel of the reduplicate becomes i, and by the rule on lengthening before san for roots ending in a vowel, han, and gam, the vowel is lengthened; and by the rule "abhyāsāc ca," the h after the reduplicate becomes gh: laṭ, jighāṃsati; liṅ, jighāṃseta; loṭ, jighāṃsatu; laṅ, ajighāṃsata; luṅ, ajighāṃsīta; liṭ, jighāṃsāṃcakāra; luṭ, jighāṃsitā; benedictive liṅ, jighāṃsyāta; lṛṭ, jighāṃsiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajighāṃsiṣyata, and so on.

San is applied to iṇ, "to go." "Sani ca": also before san. Before a following san, iṇ, when it is not used in the sense of understanding, is to be replaced by gami; this is what the i expresses. It is replaced by gami; by the rule on lengthening before san for roots ending in a vowel, han, and gam, the penultimate is lengthened, and iṭ is given: laṭ, jigāmiṣati; liṭ, jigāmiṣeta; loṭ, jigāmiṣatu; laṅ, ajigāmiṣata; luṅ, ajigāmiṣīta; liṭ, jigāmiṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, jigāmiṣitā; benedictive liṅ, jigāmiṣyāta; lṛṭ, jigāmiṣiṣyati; and ajigāmiṣiṣyata, and so on. When it does have the sense of understanding, it is not replaced by gami. Since the commentary says that for the first single-vowel portion san itself is reduplicated, the sa is reduplicated; the vowel of the reduplicate becomes i; by the rule beginning "of all roots" and the rest, both s's become ṣ; and prati is placed in front: laṭ, pratīṣiṣati; liṅ, pratīṣiṣeta; loṭ, pratīṣiṣatu; laṅ, pratyaiṣiṣata; luṅ, pratyaiṣiṣīta; liṭ, pratīṣiṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, pratīṣiṣitā; benedictive liṅ, pratīṣiṣyāta; lṛṭ, pratīṣiṣiṣyati; lṛṅ, pratyaiṣiṣiṣyata, and so on.

For ik, "to remember," as well, the procedure and all the forms are the same as for iṇ, without even the slightest difference.

San is applied to iṅ, "to study." "Iṅaś ca": also of iṅ. Iṅ too is to be replaced by gami before a following san. It is replaced by gami and reduplicated; by the rule on c for k and h, the g becomes j; the vowel of the reduplicate becomes i; and by the rule on lengthening before san for roots ending in a vowel, han, and gam, the penultimate is lengthened. Jigāmiṣa is thus formed, and the taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached to it: laṭ, jigāmiṣate; liṅ, jigāmiṣeta; loṭ, jigāmiṣatām; laṅ, ajigāmiṣata; luṅ, ajigāmiṣiṣṭa; liṭ, jigāmiṣāṃcakre; luṭ, jigāmiṣitā; benedictive liṅ, jigāmiṣiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, jigāmiṣiṣyate; lṛṅ, ajigāmiṣiṣyata, and so on.

Ṇic and san are applied to īrṣya, "to envy." The commentary cites: "īrṣyateḥ sano vā dvitvam," that is, after īrṣyati, san itself is optionally doubled. After īrṣyati the following san itself is optionally to be reduplicated, so san is reduplicated, and the vowel of the reduplicate, the upper one, becomes i. Īrṣyiṣiṣa is thus formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, īrṣyiṣiṣati; luṅ, airṣyiṣiṣīta; liṭ, īrṣyiṣiṣāṃcakāra, and so on. Alternatively, the third syllable of īrṣyati, ya together with ṇi, is reduplicated, giving īrṣyiyiṣa, to which laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, īrṣyiyiṣati; luṅ, airṣyiyiṣīta; liṭ, īrṣyiyiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to bhū, "to be." "Sani grahaguhoś ca": also of grah and guh before san. Before a san that follows grah, "to take," guhū, "to cover," and, by the word "also," each of the roots ending in the vowels of the uk class, iṭ does not occur. Formed by reduplication and the rest, bubhūṣa results, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, bubhūṣati; luṅ, abubhūṣīta; liṭ, bubhūṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

In the same way, san is applied to hu, "to offer." By this sūtra iṭ is not added. Formed by lengthening through the rule on roots ending in a vowel, han, and gam, by reduplication, and the rest, juhūṣa results, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, juhūṣati; luṅ, ajuhūṣīta; liṭ, juhūṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to guhū, "to cover," and the root is reduplicated. By the rule on c for k and h, the reduplicate takes j; the h becomes ḍh by the rule on h; by the rule on the final bhaṣ of a single-vowel root and the rest, g becomes gh; by the rule on k before s for ṣ and ḍh, the ḍh becomes k; and by the rule beginning "of all roots" and the rest, the s becomes ṣ. Jughukṣa is thus formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, jughukṣati; luṅ, ajughukṣīta; liṭ, jughukṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to grah, "to take." "Rudavidamuṣagrahisvapipracchaḥ saṃś ca": after rud, vid, muṣ, grahi, svapi, and pracch, san too. After rud, "to shed tears"; vid, "to know"; muṣ, "to steal"; grah, "to take"; svap, "to sleep"; and pracch, "to wish to know," the kṛt affix ktvā, and san as well, are called marked with k. Since san is marked with k, saṃprasāraṇa is made by the rule beginning with grahi and jyā. The root is reduplicated, with a for ṛ; the vowel of the reduplicate before san becomes i; by the rule on h, h becomes ḍh; by the rule on the final bhaṣ of a single-vowel root and the rest, g becomes gh; by the rule on k before s for ṣ and ḍh, the ḍh becomes k; and by the rule beginning "of all roots" and the rest, the s becomes ṣ. Jighṛkṣa is thus formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, jighṛkṣati; luṅ, ajighṛkṣīta; liṭ, jighṛkṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to ñiṣvap, "to sleep." Since san is marked with k, saṃprasāraṇa is made by the rule beginning with vaci and svapi. Formed by reduplication and the rest, suṣupsa results, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, suṣupsati; luṅ, asuṣupsīta; liṭ, suṣupsāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to ṣmiṅ, "to smile slightly." "Smipūṅrañjvaśāṃ sani": before the san of smi, pūṅ, ṛ, añjū, and aś. Before a san that follows ṣmiṅ, "to smile slightly"; pūṅ, "to purify"; ṛ, "to go"; añjū, "to make clear"; and aś, "food," iṭ occurs. Iṭ is given; by the rule beginning "of all roots" and the rest, guṇa is made; and formed by reduplication and the rest, siṣmayiṣa results, and the taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached: laṭ, siṣmayiṣate; luṅ, asiṣmayiṣiṣṭa; liṭ, siṣmayiṣāṃcakre, and so on.

San is applied to pūṅ, "to purify." Iṭ is given and guṇa made, and the e-class vowel becomes av; the root is reduplicated. By the rule on the u of pu, yaṇ, and j followed by a, the u becomes i, and so on: pipaviṣa results, and the taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached: laṭ, pipaviṣate; luṅ, apipaviṣiṣṭa; liṭ, pipaviṣāṃcakre, and so on.

San is applied to ṛ, "to go." With guṇa, ar, the syllable ri together with iṭ is reduplicated, and aririṣa is formed; laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, aririṣati; luṅ, āririṣīta; liṭ, aririṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to añjū, "to make clear, to anoint, and to go." Iṭ is given, and ja together with iṭ is reduplicated; añjijiṣa is formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, añjijiṣati; luṅ, āñjijiṣīta; liṭ, añjijiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to aś, "to eat." Iṭ is given, and śa together with iṭ is reduplicated; aśiśiṣa is formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, aśiśiṣati; luṅ, āśiśiṣīta; liṭ, aśiśiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to kṝñ, "to harm." "Kiraś ca pañcabhyaḥ": also after kṝ, from the five. The five beginning with kṝ are kṝñ, "to harm"; gṝ, "to swallow"; dṝ, "to tear apart"; dhṛṅ, "to hold"; and pracch, "to wish to know"; after these too, iṭ occurs before san. By this sūtra iṭ is given and guṇa made; the root is reduplicated, with a for ṛ; and formed by the change of the reduplicate's vowel to i before san and the rest, cikariṣa results, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, cikariṣati; luṅ, acikariṣīta; liṭ, cikariṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

In the same way, san is applied to gṝ, "to swallow." With iṭ given: laṭ, jigariṣati; luṅ, ajigariṣīta; liṭ, jigariṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to dṝ, "to tear apart," and iṭ is given. By guṇa and the rest, didariṣa results, and the taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached: laṭ, didariṣate; luṅ, adidariṣiṣṭa; liṭ, didariṣāṃcakre, and so on.

San is applied to dhṛñ, "to hold," and iṭ is given. Didhariṣa is formed, and the taṅ endings, laṭ and the rest, are attached: laṭ, didhariṣate; luṅ, adidhariṣiṣṭa; liṭ, didhariṣāṃcakre, and so on. Since the commentary says that although these end in ṝ, the long īṭ does not occur, īṭ is not added.

San is applied to pracch, "to wish to know." By the sūtra beginning with rud and vid, san is marked with k, so before what is marked with k, saṃprasāraṇa is made by the rule beginning with grahi and jyā. The root is reduplicated, the reduplicate's vowel before san becomes i, and by this sūtra iṭ is given. Pipṛcchiṣa is formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, pipṛcchiṣati; luṅ, apipṛcchiṣīta; liṭ, pipṛcchiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to dhūñ, "to shake." Iṭ is not added, and the root is reduplicated: dudhūṣa results, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, dudhūṣati; luṅ, adudhūṣīta; liṭ, dudhūṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to divu, "to play." With the iṭ of what begins with val, guṇa is made by the rule on roots ending in puk and the rest. Dideviṣa is formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, dideviṣati; luṅ, adideviṣīta; liṭ, dideviṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to ṣivu, "to sew." Iṭ is given and the root reduplicated; the s does not become ṣ; and guṇa is made. Siseviṣa results, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, siseviṣati; luṅ, asiseviṣīta; liṭ, siseviṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

San is applied to ṛdhu, "to grow." "Sanīvantardhabhrasjadambhuśrisvṛyūrṇubharajñapisanām": before the san of roots ending in iv, and of ṛdh, bhrasj, dambhu, śri, svṛ, yu, ūrṇu, bhara, jñapi, and san. Before a san that follows the roots whose final is the affix iv, and ṛdhu, "to grow"; bhrasj, "to roast"; dambhu, "to deceive"; śri, "to serve"; svṛ, "to sound"; yu, "to mix"; ūrṇuñ, "to cover"; bhara, that is, ḍubhṛñ, "to support"; jñā, "to understand"; and ṣaṇa, "to give," iṭ occurs optionally. In the option where iṭ is given, guṇa is made by the rule on roots ending in puk and the rest; dha together with iṭ is reduplicated; and by the rule on car for the reduplicate, dha becomes da. Ardidhiṣa is formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, ardidhiṣati; luṅ, ārdidhiṣīta; liṭ, ardidhiṣāṃcakāra, and so on. In the option without iṭ: "āpjñapyṛdhām īt": the ī of āp, jñapi, and ṛdh. For āpḷ, "to pervade"; jñā, "to make known"; and ṛdhu, "to grow," before a following san without iṭ, the vowel becomes ī and the reduplicate is also dropped. By the rule on the penultimate, ṛ becomes it, and by this sūtra that becomes īt; by the rule on the aṇ of ṛ, r follows; the reduplicate is dropped; and by the rule on car before khar, dh becomes t. Īrtsa is thus formed, and laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, īrtsati; liṅ, īrtseta; laṭ, īrtsatu; laṅ, airtsata; luṅ, airtsīta; īrtsāṃcakāra; luṭ, īrtsitā; benedictive liṅ, īrtsyāta; lṛṭ, īrtsiṣyati; lṛṅ, airtsiṣyata, and so on.

To bhrasvā, "to fry," san is added. In the case with iṭ: by the rule "bhrasj optionally becomes bharj," the change to bharj is made optional, so that it is either changed or not; reduplication follows. By the rule "it before san," the vowel is changed to i: laṭ, bibhrasjaṣata; luṅ, abibhrasjiṣīta; liṭ, bibhrasjiṣāṃcakāra, and so on; or else: laṭ, bibharjiṣati; luṅ, abibharjiṣīta; liṭ, bibharjiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

In the case without iṭ, bhrasj is optionally changed into bharj or not. In the case where it is not changed, by the rule beginning "the first of a conjunct before k," the s is dropped; by the rule beginning "vraśca, bhrasja," j becomes ṣ; by the rule beginning "ṣ and ḍh before s," ṣ becomes k; by the rule beginning "substitutes throughout," s becomes ṣ; and by the rule of reduplication and the rest it is formed. Pibhrakṣa being thus formed, laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, bibhrakṣati; liṅ, abibhrakṣīta; liṭ, pibhrakṣīcakāra, and so on. In the case where it is changed to bharj, the rest of the procedure is the same, but the r is drawn up above the kṣ: laṭ, bibharkati; luṅ, abibharkṣīta; liṭ, bibharkṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To dasvū, "to deceive," san is attached. By the rule beginning "ending in īv, ṛdhu," iṭ is made optional. In the case with iṭ: laṭ, didamhiṣati; luṅ, adidambhiṣīta; liṭ, didambhiṣāṃcakāra, and so on. In the case where iṭ is not given: "dombha iccha"; that is, dambh also takes it. Before a following san without iṭ, the vowel of dambh is changed to it, and by the word "also" it optionally becomes īt, and the reduplicate too is dropped. Since by the rule "also after a final consonant" san is kit, by the rule beginning "before a following kit, of those without it," the m is dropped. By this sūtra it and īt are made optional. The reduplicate is dropped. By the rule beginning "of a single vowel, baś becomes bhaṣ," d becomes dh. By the rule "car before khar," bh is changed to p: laṭ, dhibsati; luṅ, adhipsīta; liṭ, dhibsāṃcakāra, and so on; or else: laṭ, dhīpsati; luṅ, adhīpsīta; liṭ, dhīpsāṃcakāra, and so on.

To śṛ, "to perish," san is attached. By the rule beginning "ending in īp," iṭ is made optional. In the case with iṭ, guṇa being applied: laṭ, śiśrayiṣati; luṅ, aśiśrayiṣīta; liṭ, śiśrayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on. In the case without iṭ, by the rule "of a vowel, han and gam before san," it is lengthened: laṭ, śiśrīṣati; luṅ, aśiśrīṣīta; liṭ, śiśīṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To spraṃ, "to sound," san is attached. By the rule beginning "ending in īp," iṭ is made optional. In the case with iṭ, guṇa being applied: laṭ, sisvariṣati; luṅ, asisvariṣīta; liṭ, sisvariṣīcakāra, and so on. In the case without iṭ, it is lengthened by the rule beginning "of a vowel, han and gam." By the rule "ut where a labial precedes," ṛ becomes ut; by the rule on the aṇ of ṛ, r follows; reduplication; and by the rule "of the penultimate also," it is lengthened: laṭ, susbūrṣati; luṅ, asusvūrṣīta; liṭ, susvūrṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To yu, "to mix," san is added. By the rule beginning "ending in īp," iṭ is made optional. In the case with iṭ, there is guṇa, and by the rule on u before pu, yaṇ and j followed by a, the u of the reduplicate is changed to i: laṭ, yiyabiṣati; luṅ, ayiyabiṣīta; liṭ, yiyabiṣāṃcakāra, and so on. In the case without iṭ, it is lengthened by the rule beginning "of a vowel, han and gam": laṭ, yuyūṣata; luṅ, ayuyūṣīta; liṭ, yuyūṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To ūrṇuñ, "to cover completely," san is attached. By the rule beginning "ending in īb," iṭ is made optional. In the case with iṭ, guṇa being applied: laṭ, ūrṇunabiṣati; luṅ, arṇunaiṣīta; liṭ, ūrṇunabiṣāṃcakura, and so on. In the case without iṭ, it is lengthened by the rule beginning "of a vowel, han and gam": laṭ, ūrṇūnūṣati; luṅ, aurṇānūṣīta; liṭ, ūrṇunūṣāṃcakura, and so on.

To bhṛñ, "to hold," san is added. By the rule beginning "ending in īp," iṭ is made optional. In the case with iṭ, guṇa being applied: laṭ, bibhariṣati; luṅ, abibhariṣīta; liṭ, bibhariṣāṃcakṣara, and so on. In the case without iṭ: by the rule "ut where a labial precedes," ṛ becomes ut; by the rule on the aṇ of ṛ, r follows; reduplication; by the rule "car of the reduplicate also," bh becomes b; and by the rule "of the penultimate also," it is lengthened: laṭ, bubhūrṣāti; luṅ, abubhūrīta; liṭ, bubhūrṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To jñā, "to understand," ṇic is added. By the rule beginning "arti, hrī," the augment puk is given, and san is attached to jñāpi. By the rule beginning "ending in īp," iṭ is made optional. In the case with iṭ: laṭ, jijñāpayiṣati; luṅ, ojijñāpayiṣīta; liṭ, jijñāpayiṣīcakāra, and so on. In the case without iṭ: by the rule "ṇic before a suffix without iṭ," ṇic is dropped; and by the rule "īt of āp, jñāpi and ṛdh," the vowel becomes īt and the reduplicate is dropped: laṭ, jñīpsati; luṅ, ajñībsāti; liṭ, jñīpsāṃcakāra, and so on.

To ṣaṇa, "to bestow," san is added. By the rule beginning "ending in īp," iṭ is made optional. In the case with iṭ: laṭ, sisniṣati; luṅ, apisaniṣīta; liṭ, sisaniṣācakāra, and so on. In the case without iṭ: by the rule "of jan, san and khan before jhal," the final is changed to āt: laṭ, sisāsati; luṅ, asisāsīta; laṭ, sisāsāṃcakāra, and so on.

To tanu, "to spread," san is attached. Quoted in the commentary: "tanipatidaridrābhyaḥ snīḍvā": after tani, pati and daridrā, iṭ is optional before san. That is, after tanu, "to spread," patḷ, "to fall," and daridrā, "to be poor," iṭ is optional before a following san. In the case where iṭ is given: laṭ, titaniṣati; luṅ, atitaniṣīta; liṭ, titaniṣāṃcakāra, and so on. In the case without iṭ: "tanotirbibhāṣā": for tanoti it is optional. The penultimate of tanoti, before a following san without iṭ, is optionally lengthened or not: laṭ, titānate; luṅ, titānsīta; liṭ, titānsāṃcakāra, and so on; or else titansati, atitansīta, titansāṃcakāra, and so on. In the commentary it is explained that san also occurs after tanatu in the sense of entering into doubt; the method of formation and the forms are like the previous ones.

To mṛṅ, "to give up life," san is attached. It is lengthened by the rule beginning "of a vowel, han and gam." By the rule "ut where a labial precedes," ṛ becomes ut; by the rule on the aṇ of ṛ, r follows; reduplication; and by the rule "of the penultimate also," it is lengthened: laṭ, mumūrṣati; luṅ, amumūrṣīta; liṭ, mumūrṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To patī, "to fall," san is attached. By the citation tanupatidaridrā and so on, iṭ is made optional. In the option with iṭ: laṭ, pipatiṣati; luṅ, apipatiṣīta; liṭ, pipatiṣāṃcakāra, and so on. In the option where iṭ is not given: sanimīmāghurabhalabhaśakapatapadāmaca iśa. That is, before san, the ac of mī, mā, ghu, rabha, labh, śaka, pata and pada is iś. When a san without iṭ follows, the ac of māṅ, "to honor," of mīñ, "to harm," and of those called ghu, and of rabh, "to begin," ḍulabhaṣ, "to obtain," śakḷ, "to be able," patḷ, "to fall," and pad, "to go," becomes iś, and the abhyāsa is also elided. So the ac is changed to is; by the rule beginning "the first of a conjunct, s and k," s is dropped; and the abhyāsa is also removed: laṭ, pitsati; luṅ, apitsīta; liṭ, pitsāṃcakāra, and so on.

To daridrā, "to fall into misfortune," san is attached. By the citation tanupatidaridrā and so on, iṭ is made optional. In the option with iṭ, the ā is dropped by the rule on the elision of āt before iṭ as well: laṭ, didaridiṣati; luṅ, adidaridriṣṝta; liṭ, didaridriṣāṃcakāra, and so on. In the option without iṭ: laṭ, didaridrāsati; luṅ, adidaridrāsīta; liṭ, didaridrāsāṃcakāra, and so on.

To mīñ, "to harm," san. By "before san, mī, mā," and so on, the ac becomes is and the abhyāsa is dropped. By the rule on the s of a root before a half affix, s is changed to t: laṭ, mitsati; luṅ, amitsīta; liṭ, mitsāṃcakāra, and so on.

To mā, "to honor," san is attached. By "before san, mī, mā," and so on, the ac is changed to is, and the abhyāsa is dropped. By the rule on the s of a root before a half affix, s is changed to t. To the resulting mitsa the taṅ endings of laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, pitsate; luṅ, apitsiṣṭa; liṭ, mitsāṃcakre, and so on.

To ḍudāñ, "to give," san is attached. By "before san, mī, mā, ghu," and so on, the abhyāsa is dropped and the ac is changed to is. By the rule on the s of a root before a half affix, s is changed to t: laṭ, tiṛtsati; luṅ, aditsīta; liṭ, ditsīcakāra, and so on.

To ḍudhāñ, "to hold," san is attached, and when it is formed as before: laṭ, dhitsati; luṅ, abhitsīta; liṭ, bhitsāṃcakāra, and so on.

To rabh, "to begin," san is attached. By "before san, mī, mā," and so on, the ac is changed to is and the abhyāsa is dropped. By the rule beginning "the first of a conjunct, s and k," s is dropped. By the rule "car before khar," bh is changed to p. To the resulting ripsa the taṅ endings of laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, ripsata; luṅ, aripsiṣṭa; liṭ, ripsāṃcakre, and so on.

Likewise, when san is attached to ḍulabhaṣ, "to obtain": laṭ, lipsati; luṅ, alipsiṣṭa; liṭ, lipsāṃcakre, and so on.

To śakḷ, "to be able," san is attached. By "before san, mī, mā," and so on, the ac becomes is and the abhyāsa is dropped. By the rule beginning "the first of a conjunct, s and k," s is dropped. By the rule beginning "of a substitute," the s of san is changed to ṣ: laṭ, śikṣati; luṅ, aśikṣīta; liṭ, śikṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To pad, "to go," san is attached. By "before san, mī, mā," and so on, the ac becomes is and the abhyāsa is dropped. By the rule beginning "the first of a conjunct, s and k," s is dropped. By the rule "car before khar," d is changed to t. To the resulting pitsa the taṅ endings of laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, pitsate; apitsiṣṭa; liṭ, pitsāṃsāṃcakre, and so on.

To āpḷ, "to pervade," san is attached. By the rule giving īt for āp, jñapi and ṛdh, the ac becomes īt and the abhyāsa is dropped: laṭ, īpsati; luṅ, aipsīta; liṭ, īpsāṃcakāra, and so on.

To rādh, "to be accomplished," san is attached. The commentary cites: radho hedseyāṃ sanīsyācya. That is, for rādh in the sense of harming, is is prescribed before san. When rādh is used in the sense of harming, then before san the ac is changed to is and the abhyāsa is elided. So the ac is changed to is and the abhyāsa dropped; by the rule beginning "the first of a conjunct," s is dropped; and by the rule "car before khar," dh is changed to t: pratiṛtsati, in laṭ, and so on. When it is not in the sense of harming, it does not become is, and so, formed with reduplication and the rest: laṭ, ārirātsati; luṅ, ārirātsīta; liṭ, ārirātsāṃcakāra, and so on.

To mucḷ, "to release," san is attached. The commentary says: mucoñakarmasyaguṇopā. That is, for muc, when it takes no object, guṇa is optional. When muc is not applied in the sense of an object but is used solely in the sense of wishing, this is held to be established throughout: before a san without iṭ, the penultimate vowel is optionally changed to guṇa, and when it is so changed the abhyāsa is also elided. So guṇa is made and the abhyāsa is dropped, and by the rule "ku in place of cu," c is changed to k: laṭ, moti; luṅ, amokṣīta; liṭ, mokṣāṃcakāra, and so on. When it is in the sense of an object, guṇa is not made: laṭ, mumukṣati; luṅ, amumukṣīta; liṭ, mumukṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To sphura, "to spread," ṇic is attached. By the rule for the ṇi of ciñ and sphur, the vowel is optionally changed to āt, and to the resulting spāri san is attached and it is reduplicated. By the rule beginning "śar first," s is dropped; by the rule on car in the abhyāsa, ph becomes p; and iṭ is given: laṭ, puspāryiṣāti; luṅ, apuspāryiṣīta; liṭ, pusyārayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on. And in the option where it is not changed to āt, guṇa is made: laṭ, pusphorayiṣati; luṅ, apusphorayiṣīta; liṭ, pusphorayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To kṣu, "sound," ṇi is attached and vṛddhi is made, and to the resulting kṣāvi san and iṭ are attached, and it is reduplicated. Formed by the rule "the first hal remains," by the rule "cu in place of ku and h," which changes k to c, and so on: laṭ, cukṣāvayiṣati; luṅ, acukṣāvayiṣīta; liṭ, cukṣāvayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To pū, "to be pure," ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and to the resulting pāvi san and iṭ are attached, and it is reduplicated. Formed by the rule that u before pu, yaṇ or j followed by a is changed to i, and so on: laṭ, pipāvayiṣati; luṅ, apipāvayiṣīta; liṭ, pipāvayiṣīta; liṭ, pipāvayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To bhū, "to be," ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and to the resulting bhāvi san and iṭ are attached, and it is reduplicated. By the rule that u before pu, yaṇ or j followed by a is changed to i: laṭ, pribhāvayiṣati; luṅ, bibhāpayiṣīta; liṭ, bibhāvayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To yu, "to mix," ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and to the resulting yāvi san and iṭ are attached, and it is reduplicated. By the rule beginning "u before pu, yaṇ," u is changed to i: laṭ, yiyāvayiṣati; luṅ, ayiyāvayiṣīta; liṭ, yiyāvayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

Likewise, to ru, "to sound," when it ends in ṇic, san and iṭ are attached, and it is reduplicated. By the rule beginning "u before pu, yaṇ," u is changed to i: laṭ, rirāvayiṣati; luṅ, arirāvayiṣīta; liṭ, rirāvayiṣīcakāra, and so on. Formed in the same way, for lūñ, "to cut": laṭ, lilāvayiṣati; luṅ, alilāvayiṣīta; liṭ, liyāvayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

For ju, "to go": laṭ, jijāvayiṣati; luṅ, ajijāvayiṣīta; liṭ, jijāvayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To ṇu, "to praise," ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and to the resulting nāvi san and iṭ are attached. Formed with reduplication and the rest: laṭ, nunāvayiṣati; luṅ, anunāvayiṣīta; liṭ, nunāvayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To sru, "to go," ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made, and to the resulting srāvi san and iṭ are attached, and it is reduplicated. By the rule giving an option for sravati śṛṇiti dravati pravati pāvati byavati, the abhyāsa is changed to i: laṭ, sisrāvayiṣati; luṅ, asisrāvayiṣāṃta; liṭ, sisrāvayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To ruc, "to shine," san is attached and iṭ is given. By the rule "san also, after a root with u or i as penultimate, beginning with hal and ending in ral," san together with iṭ is optionally made kit. So in the kit option there is no guṇa. In the option where it is not kit, guṇa is made by the rule beginning "ending in puk": laṭ, rurociṣati; luṅ, arurociṣīta; liṭ, rurociṣāṃcakāra, and so on; or else laṭ, ruruciṣati, and so on.

Likewise, to likh, "to draw lines," san is attached and iṭ is given, and san is optionally made kit: laṭ, lilekhiṣati; luṅ, alilekhiṣīta; liṭ, lilekhiṣīcakāra, and so on; or else laṭ, lilikhiṣati; luṅ, alilikhiṣīta; liṭ, lilikhiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To rud, "to shed tears," san and iṭ. By the rule beginning "rud, vid, muṣ," san together with iṭ is kit, so guṇa is not made: laṭ, rurudiṣati; luṅ, arurudiṣīta; liṭ, rurudiṣīcakāra, and so on.

Likewise, for vid, "to know": laṭ, vividiṣati; luṅ, avividiṣīta; liṭ, vividiṣāṃcakāra, and so on. To muṣ, "to steal," san is attached and iṭ is given; since it is kit, guṇa is not made: laṭ, mumuṣiṣati; luṅ, amumuṣiṣāta; liṭ, mumuṣiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To ṣṭuñ, "to praise," san is attached, and it is reduplicated. stauti ṇyauḥ abhyāsasya: of the abhyāsa, for stauti and ṇi. That is, the letter s of stauti and of roots ending in ṇic becomes the letter ṣ after the pratyāhāra iṇ in the abhyāsa. By this sūtra s is changed to ṣ. By the rule "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," t becomes ṭ. By the rule beginning "of a vowel, han and gam," it is lengthened: laṭ, tuṣṭūṣati; luṅ, tuṣṭuṣīta; liṭ, tuṣṭūṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To ñiṣvap, "to sleep," ṇic is attached, and by the rule on the penultimate, vṛddhi is made. To the resulting svāpi san is attached, iṭ is given, and it is reduplicated. By the rule giving saṃprasāraṇa for dyuti and svāpi, the abhyāsa is changed by saṃprasāraṇa. By the rule on the abhyāsa of stauti and ṇi, s is changed to ṣ: laṭ, suṣvāpayiṣyati; luṅ, asuṣāpayiṣīta; liṭ, suṣāpayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To ñiṣvid, "to make an indistinct sound," ṇic is attached, and guṇa is made by the rule beginning "ending in puk." To the resulting svedi, san and iṭ. saḥ svidisvadisahānāṃ ca: and also of svidi, svadi and sah. That is, the letter s of svid, "an indistinct sound," svad, "to taste," and sah, "to forbear," even when it comes after the pratyāhāra iṇ in the abhyāsa and the root ends in ṇic, is not changed to ṣ, and so stays as the letter s. It is reduplicated; by the rule "the first hal remains," v is dropped; and by this sūtra s is not changed to ṣ: laṭ, sisvedayiṣati; luṅ, asisvedayiṣvita; liṭ, sisvedayiṣīcakāra, and so on.

For svad, "to taste," ṇic is attached and by the rule on the penultimate vṛddhi is made. To the resulting svādi san is attached and iṭ given; it is reduplicated and v is dropped. By the rule on i before san, the a is changed to i, and by this sūtra s is not changed to ṣ: laṭ, sisvādayiṣati; luṅ, asisvādayiṣīta; liṭ, sisvādayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

To sah, "to forbear," ṇic is attached and vṛddhi is made. To the resulting sāhe san is attached, iṭ is given, and it is reduplicated. By the rule on i before san, the a is changed to i, and by this sūtra s is not changed to ṣ: laṭ, sisvāhayiṣati; luṅ, asisāhayiṣīta; liṭ, sisādayiṣāṃcakāra, and so on.

The commentary explains that where there is a purpose, san is attached even to a stem ending in a san that was given in its own sense. So to gupū, "to hide," san is given by the rule on san after gup, tij and kit, and it is formed with reduplication and the rest. To the resulting jugupsa, san is given once more by the rule allowing it optionally after a root that is the object of the wishing and shares its agent. Since it has already been reduplicated, it is not reduplicated again. By the rule on the elision of a before an iṭ beginning with val, the a is dropped, and to the resulting jugupsiṣa the endings of laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, jugupsiṣati; liṅ, jugupsiṣita; loṭ, jugupsiṣitu; laṅ, ajugupsiṣata; luṅ, ajugupsiṣīta; liṭ, jugupsiṣāṃcakāra; luṭ, jugupsiṣitā; the benedictive liṅ, jugupsiṣyāta; lṛṭ, jugupsiṣiṣyāti; lṛṅ, ajugupsiṣiṣyata, and so on.

iti pāṇinivyākaraṇasya sūtātsanantaḥ smāptāḥ: that is, from the sūtra of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the forms ending in san are complete.

With these, the rough procedures for the forms ending in san, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down as notes the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, are for now complete.

Third, I shall explain the domains in which the affix yaṅ applies, by which roots are formed into roots. dhātorekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ: from a root with a single ac that begins with hal, yaṅ also comes in the sense of the intensification of an action. That is, after a root that has a single ac and begins with a hal, other than ruc, "to shine," and śuc, "to grieve," yaṅ also follows in the sense of the intensification of an action, that is, in the sense of "greatly" and "again and again." The letter ṅ serves the rule by which the root is reduplicated before san and yaṅ.

The commentary cites: sūcisūtrimūdyaṭrtyaśūrṇotibhyo yaṅ. That is, yaṅ also comes after sūci, sūtri, mūtri, aṭati, arti, aśa and ūrṇoti. From sūc, "to tell tales," sūtr, "to release in between," mūtr, "to flow forth," aṭ, "to go," ṛ, "to go," aś, "to eat," and ūrṇuñ, "to cover," yaṅ comes in the sense of "greatly" and "again and again."

nityaṃ kauṭimye gatau: in going, only in the sense of crookedness. That is, from a root meaning going, when it is used solely in the sense of going crookedly, and not in the sense of "greatly" and "again and again," yaṅ follows.

lupasṅacarajapajabhadahadaśagrībsyebhābagartāyāṃ: from lup, sad, car, jap, jabh, dah, daś and gṛ, only in the sense of contempt. That is, from lupḷ, "to cut," ṣadḷ, "to fall apart," car, "to go," jap, "in the mind," jabh, "the decline of the body," dah, "to burn to ashes," daś, "to bite," and gṝ, "to make clear," yaṅ also comes when they are used in the sense of contempt alone, but not for the mere intensification of an action.

To sūc, "to tell tales," yaṅ is attached, and by the rule "before san and yaṅ," it is reduplicated. By the rule on shortening, it is shortened, giving susūca. Then, with yaṅ: guno yaṅlukoḥ: guṇa before yaṅ and its elision. That is, before the affix yaṅ, whether it is elided or not, the abhyāsa is changed to guṇa. By this sūtra guṇa is made, and to the resulting sosūcya the taṅ endings of laṭ and the rest are attached. By the rule "śap for the agent," and by the rule on a before guṇa, the two are changed into one with the form of the former: laṭ, sosūcyate; liṅ, sosūcyeta; loṭ, sosūcyatāṃ; laṅ, asosūcyate, and so on. For luṅ: yasya halaḥ: of ya, after a hal. That is, a ya that follows a hal at the end of a root is to be elided before a half affix. By this sūtra ya is dropped, and by the rule on iṭ for a half affix beginning with val, iṭ is given: asosūciṣṭa, asosūciṣātāṃ, asosūciṣata, and so on. For liṭ, ām is attached by the rule beginning "kās," and ya is dropped by the rule "of ya, after a hal": sosūcāṃcakre, sosūcāṃbabhūva, sosūcāṃmāsa, and so on. For the remaining la letters, iṭ for an affix beginning with val is given and ya is dropped by the rule "of ya, after a hal": luṭ, sosūcitā; the benedictive liṅ, sosūciṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, sosūciṣyate; lṛṅ, asosūciṣyata, and so on.

To mūtr, "to flow forth," yaṅ is also attached, and it is reduplicated. By the rule on shortening it is shortened, and by "guṇa before yaṅ and its elision," guṇa is made: laṭ, momātyate; liṅ, momūtyeta; loṭ, momūtryatāṃ; laṅ, amomūtryata, and so on. For luṅ, iṭ for an affix beginning with val is given, and ya is dropped by the rule "of ya, after a hal": amomūtriṣṭa, and so on. For liṭ, ām is attached and ya is dropped by the rule "of ya, after a hal": momūtāṃcakre, and so on. For the rest, iṭ is given and ya dropped: luṭ, momūtritā; the benedictive liṅ, momūtriṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, momūtriṣyate; lṛṅ, amomūtriṣyata, and so on.

To aṭ, "to go," yaṅ is also attached. By the rule "before san and yaṅ," ṭa is reduplicated together with its vowel. dīrbho'kitaḥ: the long vowel, of what is not kit. That is, an abhyāsa that is not called kit is lengthened before the affix yak, before yaṅ, and before the elision of yaṅ. By this sūtra ṭa is lengthened. By the rule on the elision of at, the a of the second ṭa is dropped, and to the resulting aṭāṭya the taṅ endings of laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, aḍāṭyate; liṅ, aḍāṭyeta; loṭ, aḍāṭyatāṃ; laṅ, āṭāṇyate, and so on. For luṅ, iṭ is given and ya is dropped by the rule "of ya, after a hal": āṭāṭiṣṭa, and so on. For liṭ, ām is attached and ya dropped: anāḍāṃcakre, and so on. For the rest, iṭ is given and ya dropped by the rule "of ya, after a hal": luṭ, aṭāṭitā; the benedictive liṅ, aṭāṭiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, aṭāṭiṣyate; lṛṅ, āṭāṭiṣyata, and so on.

To aś, "to eat," yaṅ is attached, and śa is reduplicated together with its vowel. Since it is not kit, it is lengthened by the rule on the long vowel, and to the resulting aśāśya the endings of laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, aśāśyatāṃ; liṅ, āśāśyata; loṭ, arāryatāṃ; laṅ, āśāśyata, and so on. For luṅ, iṭ is given and ya is dropped by the rule "of ya, after a hal": ārāriṣṭa, and so on. For liṭ, ām is attached, and ya is dropped by the rule "of ya, after a hal": arārāṃcakre, and so on. For the rest: luṭ, aśāśitā; the benedictive liṅ, arāriṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, arāriṣyate; lṛṅ, ārāriṣyata, and so on.

To ṛ, "to go," yaṅ is attached. yadi ca: also before yaṅ. That is, the ṛ of ṛ, "to go," and the ṛ at the beginning of a conjunct also become guṇa before yaṅ. By the rule "before san and yaṅ," ṛ is reduplicated. By "guṇa before yaṅ and its elision," the abhyāsa takes guṇa, and by this sūtra the second ṛ takes guṇa, so that ar ar yaṅ is set out in order. By the rule on the long vowel of what is not kit, it is lengthened, and to the resulting arārya the endings of laṭ and the rest are attached: laṭ, arāryate; liṅ, arāryeta; loṭ, arāryatāṃ; laṅ, ārāryate, and so on. For luṅ, iṭ is given and ya is dropped by the rule "of ya, after a hal": ārāriṣṭa, and so on. For liṭ, ām is given and ya dropped: arārāṃcakre, and so on. For the rest: luṭ, arārihā; the benedictive liṅ, arāriṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, arāriṣyate; lṛṅ, ārāriṣyata, and so on.

To ūrṇuñ, "to cover," yaṅ is attached, and ṇu is reduplicated. Guṇa is made by the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on: laṭ, ūrṇonūyate; liṅ, ūrṇonūyeta; loṭ, ūrṇonūyatāṃ; laṅ, aurṇonūyata, and so on. For luṅ, iṭ is given, and by the rule on the elision of at, the a of ya is dropped: aurṇonūyiṣṭa. Likewise, with the a dropped, for the rest: liṭ, ūrnonūyāṃcakre; luṭ, ūrṇonūyitā; the benedictive liṅ, ūrṇonūyiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, ūrṇonūyiṣyate; lṛṅ, aurṇonūyiṣyata, and so on.

To ḍudāñ of the ghu class, "to give," yaṅ is given. By the rule beginning "ghu, mā, sthā, gā, pā," the ac is changed to ī, and guṇa is made by the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on: laṭ, dedīyate; liṅ, dedīyeta; loṭ, dedīyatāṃ; laṅ, adedīyata, and so on. For luṅ, iṭ is given and a is dropped by the rule on the elision of at: adedīyiṣṭa, and so on. For liṭ, ām is attached and a dropped: dedīyāṃcakre, and so on. For the rest: luṭ, dedīyitā; the benedictive liṅ, dedīyiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, dedīyiṣyate; lṛṅ, adedīyiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, to ḍudhāñ, "to hold," yaṅ is attached. The ā is changed to ī, it is reduplicated, and guṇa is made by the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on: laṭ, dedhīyate; luṅ, adidhīyiṣṭa; liṭ, dedhīyāṃcakre; luṭ, dedhīyitā, and so on.

To māṅ, "to honor," yaṅ is also attached. The ā becomes īt, it is reduplicated, and guṇa is made: laṭ, memīyate; luṅ, amemīyiṣṭa; liṭ, memīyāṃcakre; luṭ, memīyitā, and so on.

To ṣṭhā, "to turn back from going," yaṅ is also attached. The ā is changed to īt, and it is reduplicated. By the rule beginning "śar first," s is dropped; by the rule on car in the abhyāsa, th becomes t; by the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on, guṇa is made; by the rule beginning "of a substitute," s becomes ṣ; and by the rule "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," th is changed to ṭh. Formed in this way: laṭ, teṣṭhīyate; luṅ, ateṣṭhīyiṣṭa; liṭ, teṣṭhīyāṃcakre; luṭ, teṣṭhīyiṣṭa, and so on.

To gai, "to sound," yaṅ is also attached. By the rule giving āt for ec where it is not in the immediate domain of śit, the ec becomes āt. By the rule beginning "ghu, mā, sthā, gā," it is changed to īt. It is reduplicated, and with cu in place of ku and h, and guṇa made: laṭ, jegīyate; luṅ, ajegīyiṣṭa; liṭ, jegīyāṃcakre; luṭ, jigīyitā, and so on.

To ohāk, "to abandon," yaṅ is also attached. By the rule beginning "ghu," ā becomes ī. It is reduplicated; cu comes in place of ku and h; by the rule on car in the abhyāsa, jh becomes j; and guṇa is made: laṭ, jehiyati; luṅ, ajehīyiṣṭa; liṭ, jehāyāṃcakre; luṭ, jihīyitā, and so on.

To ṣo, "the act of ending," yaṅ is also attached. By the rule on what is not in the immediate domain of śit, and so on, ec becomes āt; by the rule beginning "ghu," it becomes it. It is reduplicated, guṇa is made, and by the rule beginning "of a substitute," it is changed to ṣ: laṭ, seṣīyate; luṅ, asīṣīyiṣṭa; liṭ, seṣiāṃcakre; luṭ, seṣīyitā, and so on.

To ṭuośvi, "to go and to grow," yaṅ is also attached. By the rule on the option for śvi, change by saṃprasāraṇa is made optional. In the option where it is changed: laṭ, śośūyate; luṅ, aśośūyiṣṭa; liṭ, śośūyāṃcakre; luṭ, śośūyitā, and so on. In the option where it is not changed: laṭ, śeśīyate; luṅ, aśeśīyiṣṭa; liṭ, śeśvīyāṃcakre; śeśvīyitā, and so on.

To smṛ, "to remember," yaṅ is also attached, and it is reduplicated. By the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on, the abhyāsa takes guṇa. By the rule beginning "the first hal remains," m and r are dropped. By the rule on the long vowel of what is not kit, it is lengthened, and by the rule "also before yaṅ," guṇa is made: laṭ, sāsmaryate; luṅ, asāsmariṣṭa; liṭ, sāsmarācakre; luṭ, sāsmaritā, and so on.

To ḍukṛñ, "to do," yaṅ is also attached. By the rule giving rīṅ for ṛt, it is changed to rīṅ. It is reduplicated; by the rule on shortening it is shortened; r is dropped; cu comes in place of ku and h; and by the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on, guṇa is made: laṭ, cekrīyate; luṅ, acekrīyiṣṭa; liṭ, cekrīyāṃcakra; luṭ, cekrīyitā, and so on. When sam comes before it, suṭ is given before the k: laṭ, sāṃceskrīyate, and so on.

To ṣic, "to protect," yaṅ is also attached. It is reduplicated, and guṇa is made by the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on: laṭ, sesicyate; luṅ, asesiciṣṭa; liṭ, sesicīcakre; luṭ, sasicitā, and so on. sico yadi: of sic, before yaṅ. That is, the letter s of sic does not become ṣ before yaṅ, even when it is preceded by what would be a reason for changing s to ṣ, namely a prefix or the abhyāsa. The example with the abhyāsa has already been shown; with a prefix, sesicyate, and so on.

To vraj, "to go," yaṅ is also attached. It is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "the first hal," r is dropped; and by the rule beginning "of what is not kit," it is lengthened: laṭ, vāprajyate; luṅ, apāprajiṣṭa; liṭ, vāprajīcakre; luṭ, vāvrajitā, and so on.

To grī, "to make clear," yaṅ. gro yaṅi: of gṝ, before yaṅ. That is, the letter r of gṛ is to be changed to the letter l before yaṅ. By the rule giving it for the ṝt of a root, ṝ becomes iṭ; by the rule that r follows the aṇ of ṛ, and by this sūtra, r is changed to l. It is reduplicated, and with cu in place of ku and h, and guṇa made by the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on: laṭ, jegilyate; luṅ, ajegiliṣṭa; liṭ, jegilāṃcakre; luṭ, jegilitā, and so on.

To lupḷ, "to cut," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated, and guṇa is made by the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on: laṭ, lolupyate; luṅ, alolupuṣṭa; liṭ, lolupāṃcakre; luṭ, lolupitā, and so on.

To ku, "to blaze," yaṅ is attached. nakavateryaṅi: not of kavati, before yaṅ. That is, the letter k of the abhyāsa of kavati is not changed to the letter c before yaṅ. It is reduplicated, guṇa is made by the rule on the elision of yaṅ and so on, and by this sūtra k is not changed to c: laṭ, kokūyate; luṅ, akokūyiṣṭa; liṭ, kokūyāṃcakre; luṭ, kokūyitā, and so on. Since the commentary explains that sometimes it is changed: laṭ, cokūyate, and so on.

To vañcu, "to go," yaṅ is attached. nīgvañcusraṃsudhvaṃsukasapatapadaskandāṃ: nīk for vañcu, sraṃsu, dhvaṃsu, kasa, pata, pada and skanda. That is, for vañcu, "to go," sraṃsu and dhvaṃsu, "to fall down," kas, "to go," patḷ, "to fall," pad, "to go," and skand, "to go," before the affix yaṅ, whether it remains or is elided, the augment nīk comes to the abhyāsa; the k serves to fix its position. It is reduplicated, and by this sūtra the augment nīk is added. Since the augment is kit, the abhyāsa is changed to a long vowel. By the rule beginning "of what does not have it," the n is dropped before what is ṅit: laṭ, vanīpacyate; luṅ, avanīvaciṣṭa; liṭ, vanīvacīcakre; luṭ, vanīvacitā, and so on.

To sraṃsu, "to fall down," yaṅ is attached, and it is reduplicated. By this sūtra the augment nīk is given. Because of the kit, the abhyāsa does not become long. By the rule beginning "of what does not have it," n is dropped: laṭ, sanīsrasyate; luṅ, asanīsrasiṣṭa; liṭ, sanīsrasāṃcakre; luṭ, sanisrasasitā, and so on.

To yamu, "to cease," yaṅ is attached. nugato'nunāsikāntasya: nuk for the at of what ends in a nasal. That is, to the abhyāsa of a root that ends in a nasal and has a as its penultimate vowel, the augment nuk comes before the affix yaṅ, whether it remains or is elided; the k serves to fix its position, and the a is for pronunciation. It is reduplicated; by the rule beginning "the first hal remains," m is dropped; by this sūtra the augment nu is given; by the rule beginning "pṛṣodara," it is made anusvāra; and because of the kit it does not become long: laṭ, yaṃyamyate; luṅ, ayaṃyamiṣṭa; liṭ, yaṃyamāṃcakre; luṭ, yaṃyamitā, and so on.

To ṭuvamu, "to vomit," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated, m is dropped, and by this sūtra the augment nuk is given. By the rule "and of n not at the end of a word, before jhal, anusvāra," it becomes anusvāra. Being kit, it is not lengthened: laṭ, vaṃvamyate; luṅ, avaṃvamiṣṭa; liṭ, vaṃvamāṃcakre; luṭ, vaṃvamitā, and so on.

To the root given as tanu, "to extend," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated and nu is dropped. By this sūtra the augment nuk is given, and it is not made long: laṭ, tantanyate; luṅ, atantaniṣṭa; liṭ, tantanīcakre; luṭ, tantanitā, and so on.

Even though a root ends in a nasal, if its penultimate is long ā, nuk does not occur. Thus to bhāma, "to be angry," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated, and by the rule "car also in the abhyāsa" bh becomes b. By the rule "short," bhā is made short, and by the rule beginning "not kit" it is made long again: laṭ, bābhāmyate; luṅ, abābhāmiṣṭa; liṭ, bābhāmāṃcakre; luṭ, bābhūmitā, and so on.

To jana, "to be born," yaṅ is attached. By the rule "optionally before ya," the final is optionally changed to ā or left unchanged. In the alternative where it is not changed, the augment nuk is given to the abhyāsa in a by the rule for roots ending in a nasal: laṭ, jaṃjanyate; luṅ, ajaṃjanāṃniṣṭa; liṭ, jaṃjanāṃcakre; luṭ, jaṃjanitā, and so on. In the alternative where it is changed to ā, the root is reduplicated, made short by the rule "short," and made long again by the rule beginning "not kit": laṭ, jājāyate; luṅ, ajājāyiṣṭa; liṭ, jājāyāṃcakre; luṭ, jājāyitā, and so on.

To ṣana, "to give," yaṅ is attached. By the rule "optionally before a," the final is optionally changed to ā or left unchanged. In the alternative where it is not changed, nuk is given by the rule beginning "ending in a nasal": laṭ, saṃsanyate; luṅ, asaṃsanīṣṭa; liṭ, saṃsanīcākre; luṭ, saṃsanitā, and so on. In the alternative where it is changed to ā: laṭ, sāsāyate; luṅ, asāsāyiṣṭa; liṭ, sāsāyāṃcakāra, and so on.

Likewise for khana, "to dig": laṭ, cikhanyate; luṅ, acikhaniṣṭa; liṭ, cikhanāṃcakre; luṭ, cikhanitā, and so on; or else laṭ, cākhāyate; luṅ, acākhāyiṣṭa; liṭ, cakhāyāṃcakre; luṭ, cākhāyitā, and so on.

To han, "to harm," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated and n is dropped. By the rule "cu for ku and h," and by the rule "car also in the abhyāsa," jh becomes j. By the rule beginning "ending in a nasal," the augment nuk is given, and by the rule "also from the abhyāsa," h is changed to gh, and so on: laṭ, jaṃghanyate; luṅ, ajighaniṣṭā; liṭ, jikhanīcakre; luṭ, jighanitā, and so on.

The commentary cites: hanteḥ hidlayāṃ yaṅi ghībhāvo baktabyaḥ. That is, for hanti in the sense of harming, before yaṅ, its becoming ghī is to be stated: when yaṅ follows hanti in the sense of harming, it should be changed to ghī. So hana is changed to ghī. It is reduplicated and made short by the rule "short." N is dropped. By the rule "cu for ku and h," and by the rule "car also in the abhyāsa," jh becomes j. By the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made: laṭ, jaghiyate; luṅ, ajeghvāgiyiṣā; liṭ, jeghvīyāṃcakre; luṭ, jeghvīyitā, and so on.

To jaba, "mentally," yaṅ is attached. The sūtra: japa jibha daha daśa bhañja paśāṃ ca, "Also of japa, jabha, daha, daśa, bhañja and paśa." To the abhyāsa of japa, "mentally"; jabha, "bodily decline"; daha, "to burn to ashes"; daśa, "to bite"; bhañju, "to crush utterly"; and paśa, "to bind," the augment nuk is added when the suffix yaṅ follows, whether it remains or is elided. The root is reduplicated, and by this sūtra the augment nuk is given: laṭ, jaṃjapyate; luṅ, ajaṃjapiṣṭa; liṭ, jaṃjapāṃcakre, and so on.

Likewise for jabha, "bodily decline": yaṅ, reduplication, and nuk is given: laṭ, jaṃjabhyate; luṅ, ajaṃjabhiṣṭa; liṭ, jaṃjabhāṃcakre, and so on.

For daha, "to burn to ashes": yaṅ is attached and nuk is given: laṭ, didahyato; luṅ, adaṃdahiṣṭa; liṭ, daṃdahāṃcakre, and so on.

For daśa, "to bite": yaṅ, reduplication, and nuk is given: laṭ, daṃdaśyate; luṅ, adidaṣiṣṭa; liṭ, daṃdaśāṃcakre, and so on.

For bhañju, "to crush": yaṅ is attached, and by the rule beginning "of those that do not have the marker i," n is dropped. It is reduplicated and the augment nuk is given: laṭ, baṃbhajyati; luṅ, abaṃbhajiṣṭa; liṭ, baṃbhajāṃcakre, and so on.

For paśa, "to bind": yaṅ, reduplication, and the augment nuk is given: laṭ, paṃpaśute; luṅ, apaṃpaśiṣṭa; liṭ, paṃpaśācakre, and so on.

To cala, "to move," yaṅ is attached. The commentary cites: sacayāntasyābhyāsasya nugvā, "For the abhyāsa of what ends in la, ca or ya, nuk is optional." For the abhyāsa of a root ending in the letter ca, the letter la or the letter ya, the augment nuk optionally occurs when the suffix yaṅ follows, whether it remains or is elided. In the alternative where nuk is given: laṭ, cicalyate; luṅ, acaṃcaliṣṭa; liṭ, caṃcalāṃcakre, and so on. In the alternative where nuk is not given, it is made long by the rule beginning "not kit": laṭ, cācalyate; luṅ, acācaliṣṭa; liṭ, cācalāṃcakre, and so on.

Likewise to mañca, "couch," yaṅ is attached. By the rule beginning "of those that do not have the marker i," n is dropped, and by this cited rule nuk is optionally given to the abhyāsa: laṭ, maṃmacyate; luṅ, amaṃmaciṣṭa; liṭ, maṃmacīcakre, and so on; or else laṭ, māmacyate; luṅ, amāmaciṣṭa; liṭ, māmacīcakre, and so on.

For daya, "to give," nuk is optionally given: laṭ, daṃdayyate; luṅ, adaṃdayiṣṭa; liṭ, daṃdayāṃcakre, and so on; or else laṭ, dādayyate; luṅ, adādayiṣṭa; liṭ, dādayāṃcakre, and so on.

To cara, "to go," yaṅ is attached. The sūtra: cara phalo ca, "Also of cara and phala." To the abhyāsa in a of cara and phala, the augment nuk is added when yaṅ follows, whether it is elided or remains. The sūtra: utparasyātaḥ, "u for what follows a." The a that follows the abhyāsa in a of cara and phala is changed to u when yaṅ follows, whether it remains or is elided. So the root is reduplicated; by this sūtra a becomes u; by the preceding sūtra the augment nuk is given; and by the rule beginning "before a consonant," it is made long: laṭ, caṃcūryate; luṅ, acaṃcūriṣṭa; liṭ, caṃcūrāṃcakre, and so on.

To phala, "to be complete," yaṅ is attached, and the procedure is carried out just as for cara: laṭ, paṃphulyate; luṅ, apaṃphuliṣṭa; liṭ, paṃphulāṃcakre, and so on.

To nṛti, "to move the body," yaṅ is attached. The sūtra: rī gṛdupadhasya ca, "Rīk also for what has ṛ as its penultimate." For the abhyāsa of a root that has ṛ as its penultimate, too, the augment rīk is added when the suffix yaṅ follows, whether it is elided or remains; the k serves to fix its position. The sūtra: kṣubhvādiṣu ca, "Also in kṣubhā and the rest." For kṣubha, "to be agitated," and the rest, even where the root text does not cover them, the forms are to be made correct and easy to pronounce. By the rule "before san and yaṅ," the root is reduplicated; by the rule "ṛ becomes a," ṛ becomes a; the preceding sūtra gives the augment rīk; and by this sūtra n is not changed to ṇ: laṭ, narīnṛtyate; luṅ, anarīnṛtiṣṭa; liṭ, narīnṛtāṃcakre, and so on.

To graha, "to take up," yaṅ is attached. By the rule beginning "grahi jyā," it is changed to samprasāraṇa. It is reduplicated, and ṛ becomes a. By the rule "rīk also for what has ṛ as its penultimate," the augment rīk is given: laṭ, jarīgṛhyaṃte; luṅ, ajarīkṛhiṣṭa; liṭ, jarīgṛhaṃcakre, and so on.

To kṛpū, "to be able," yaṅ is attached. By the rule that the r of kṛpa becomes l, ṛ is changed to ḷ. It is reduplicated and ṛ becomes a. Since the commentary explains that for a root with ḷ as its penultimate the augment līk occurs, līk is given: laṭ, calīklṛpyate; luṅ, acalīklṛpiṣṭa; liṭ, calīklṛpāṃcakre, and so on.

To braścu, "to cut," yaṅ is attached. By the rule beginning "grahi jyā," it is changed to samprasāraṇa. It is reduplicated and ṛ becomes a. Since the commentary says that the augment rīk also occurs for a ṛ that stands before conjoined consonants, rīk is given: laṭ, barīpṛbhyate; luṅ, abavībṛścīṣṭa; liṭ, parībṛścāṃcakre, and so on.

Likewise to praccha, "to wish to know," yaṅ is attached. By the rule beginning "grahi jyā," it is changed to samprasāraṇa. It is reduplicated, ṛ becomes a, and the augment rīk is given: laṭ, parīpṛcnyahe; luṅ, aparīpṛcchiṣṭa; liṭ, parīpṛcchaṃcakre, and so on.

To ñiṣvapa, "to sleep," yaṅ is attached. The sūtra: svapi syami byeñāṃ yaṅi, "Of svapa, syama and byeña, before yaṅ." When yaṅ follows ṣapa, "to sleep"; syami, "to think discursively"; and byeña, "to cover completely," they are changed to samprasāraṇa. So it is changed to samprasāraṇa, reduplicated, and by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made: laṭ, sosubyate; luṅ, asosupiṣṭa; liṭ, sosupāṃcakre, and so on.

Likewise to syama, yaṅ is attached. It is changed to samprasāraṇa, reduplicated, and guṇa is made: laṭ, sesimyate; luṅ, asesimiṣṭa; liṭ, sesimāṃcakre, and so on.

To byeña, "to cover completely," yaṅ is attached. It is changed to samprasāraṇa; by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made; and by the rule beginning "not kit," it is made long: laṭ, bapīyati; luṅ, abebayiṣṭa; liṭ, bebīyāṃcakre, and so on.

To baśa, "to be lovely," yaṅ is attached. The sūtra: napaśaḥ, "Not of paśa." When yaṅ follows, baśa is not changed to samprasāraṇa. It is reduplicated and made long by the rule beginning "not kit": laṭ, bābaśyate; luṅ, abābaśiṣṭa; liṭ, bābaśīcakre, and so on.

To ciña, "to accumulate," yaṅ is attached. The sūtra: cūyaḥkī, "Kī for ci." When yaṅ follows ciña, it should be changed to kī. So ci is changed to kī. It is reduplicated and made short by the rule "short." By the rule "cu for ku and h," and by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made: laṭ, cekīyate; luṅ, acekīyiṣṭa; liṭ, cekīyāṃcakre, and so on.

To ghrā, "to take up," yaṅ is attached. The sūtra: īdhyādho, "Ī for ghrā and dhmā." When yaṅ follows, the final of ghrā and dhmā should be changed to ī. So the final is changed to ī. It is reduplicated, r is dropped, by the rule "cu for ku and h" and by the rule "short" it is made short, and by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made: laṭ, jeghīate; luṅ, ajeghyīyiṣṭa; liṭ, jeghyīyāṃcakre, and so on.

Likewise to dhmā, "to make a sound and to kindle a fire," yaṅ is attached. By this sūtra the final is changed to ī. It is reduplicated, m is dropped, and it is made short by the rule "short." By the rule "car also in the abhyāsa," dh becomes d, and by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made: laṭ, deḍhyīyate; luṅ, adedhmeyiṣṭa; liṭ, dedhyīyāṃcakre, and so on.

To śīṅ, "to lie down," yaṅ is attached. The sūtra: ayaṅkīti, "Ayaṅ before what has k or ṅ as its marker." When a suffix beginning with the letter ya and bearing the marker k or ṅ follows, the final of śīṅ is changed to ayaṅ.
