The ṅ serves to block the vowel operation, and the a of ya serves for pronunciation. So ī is changed to ayaṅ, and it is made long by the rule beginning "not kit": laṭ, śāśayyate; luṅ, aśāśayiṣṭa; liṭ, śāśayāṃcakre, and so on.

To ḍhaukṛ, "to go," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated and made short by the rule "short," au becoming ū. By the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made again, and by the rule "car also in the abhyāsa," ḍh is changed to ḍ: laṭ, ḍoḍhokyate; liṅ, ḍoḍhokyeta; loṭ, ḍoḍhaukyatāṃ; laṅ, aḍoḍhaukyata; luṅ, aḍoḍhaukiṣṭa; liṭ, ḍoḍhaukāṃcakre; luṭ, ḍoḍhaukitā; benedictive liṅ, ḍoḍhaukiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, ḍoḍhaukiṣyate; lṛṅ, aḍoḍhaukiṣyata, and so on.

iti pāṇinibyākaraṇasya sūtrāt yadantāḥ samāptāḥ. That is: from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the forms ending in yaṅ are complete.

With these, in The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down in the form of notes the meaning of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, together with its procedures, illustrative examples and so on, the procedures for forms ending in the suffix yaṅ, in their general rules together with their exceptions, are for now complete in rough outline.

Now I shall explain the procedures for the elision of the suffix yaṅ. yaṅoñcica, "Of yaṅ, also before a vowel." The general rule is that the suffix yaṅ is elided when a suffix beginning with a vowel follows, and in many other cases as well. Even though the suffix is dropped, the operations it brings about, such as reduplication, do not fail to remain. Wherever the suffix yaṅ remains, laṭ and the rest take the ātmanepada endings; wherever the suffix yaṅ is elided, laṭ and the rest take the parasmaipada endings, and after the elision of yaṅ, śap too is always elided.

yaṅobā, "Optionally after yaṅ." After the elision of yaṅ, for every root, the augment īṭ optionally occurs before a suffix that begins with a consonant and bears the marker p. Thus to bhu, "to be," yaṅ is attached. By the rule "before san and yaṅ," the root is reduplicated, and by the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is elided.

By the rule "short," it is made short. By the rule "guṇa when yaṅ or its elision follows," the abhyāsa takes guṇa. By the rule "car also in the abhyāsa," bh becomes b. In laṭ, tip is added. By this sūtra īṭ is optionally given, and guṇa is made: bobhavīti, or else bobhoti.

In the dual of the first person and in all the rest, bhū is changed to bobhū, and the procedure is the same. L is changed to tas: botūtaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh is changed to at, and by the rule beginning "before a vowel, of śnu, of a root," it is changed to uv: bobhūvati. Formed in the same way, in the three forms of the middle person: bobhavīṣi, bobhoṣi, bobhūthaḥ, bobhūtha. In the three forms of the last person: bobhavīmi, bobhomi, bobhūvaḥ, bobhūmaḥ.

In liṅ, in the three forms of the first person: bobhūyāt, bobhūyātāṃ, bobhūyuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: bobhūyāḥ, bobhūyātāṃ, bobhūyāta. In the three forms of the last person: bobhūyāṃ, bobhūyāva, bobhūyāma.

In loṭ, in the three forms of the first person: bobhavītu, bobhotu, bobhūtāta, bobhūtāṃ, bobhūvatu. In the three forms of the middle person: bobhūti, bobhūtāta, bobhūtāṃ, bobhūta. In the three forms of the last person: bobhavīni, bobhavāva, babhavāma.

In laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: abobhavīt, abobhota, abobhūtāṃ, abobhūvuḥ, where by the rule beginning "after sic and a reduplicated stem," jhi becomes jus. In the three forms of the middle person: abobhavīḥ, abobhoḥ, abobhūtaṃ, abobhāta. In the three forms of the last person: aboghavi, abobhūva, abobhūma.

In luṅ, sic is dropped by the rule beginning "gāti sthā bhū," so in the three forms of the first person: apobhūta, abobhūtāṃ, abobhabu. In the three forms of the middle person: abobhūḥ, abobhūtaṃ, abobhūta. In the three forms of the last person: abebhūvaṃ, abobhūva, abobhūma.

In liṭ, ām is attached by the rule beginning "kās": bobhavāṃcakāra, bobhipāṃbabhūva, bobhavāmāsa, and so on. The commentary says that in some cases, after the elision of yaṅ (by the rule beginning "after sic and a reduplicated stem," jhi becomes jus, and by the rule "also before jus," guṇa is made), ām may also not be attached before liṭ. Accordingly, in the alternative where ām is not attached, by the rule "vuk for bhū in luṅ and liṭ," the augment vuk applies. Before endings beginning with a vowel, the augment vuk is given by the rule "vuk for bhū in luṅ and liṭ," so in the three forms of the first person: bobhūva, bobhūvatuḥ, bobhūvuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: bobhūvitha, bobhūvathuḥ, bobhūva. In the three forms of the last person: bobhūpa, bobhūviva, bobhūvima.

Or else, without giving vuk, vṛddhi is made in the two singular endings and guṇa before thal, and before the other endings it is changed to uv by the rule beginning "before a vowel, of śnu, of a root," so in the three forms of the first person: bobhāva, bobhūvatuḥ, bobhūvuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: bobhavitha, bobhūvathuḥ, bobhuva. In the three forms of the last person: bobhāva, bobhava, bobhuviva, bobhuvima.

In luṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made: bobhavitī, bobhavitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: bobhūyāt, bobhūyāstāṃ, bobhūyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given and guṇa is made: bobhaviṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: abobhaviṣyat, and so on.

To vañcu, "to go," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated, and by the rule beginning "vañcu, sraṃsu, dhvaṃsu, bhraṃsu," the augment nīk is given. By the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to vanīṅañca. In the singular of the first person, by the rule "optionally after yaṅ," īṭ is optional. In the alternative without īṭ, ku replaces cu: vanīvaṃcīti, panīvikti. In the dual, by the rule beginning "of those that do not have the marker i," n is dropped, and by the rule "ku for cu," c is changed to k: panīvaṃktaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh is changed to at: vanīvaṃcati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: vanīvaṃcīṣi, vanīvaṃkṣi, vanīvakthaḥ, vanīvaktha. In the three forms of the last person: vanīvaṃcīmi, vanīvaṃcmi, vanīvaṃcvaḥ, vanīvaṃcamaḥ.

In liṅ, n is dropped by the rule beginning "of those that do not have the marker i": bahanīvacyat, vanīvacyātāṃ, vanīvicyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: vanīvaṃcītu, vanīvoktu, vanīvaṃktāta, vanīvaktāṃ, vanīvacatu. In the three forms of the middle person: vanīvagdhi, vanīvaktāta, vanīvaktaṃ. In the three forms of the last person: vanīvaṃcāni, vanīvaṃcāva, vanīvaṃcāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: avanīvaṃccita, avanīvanra. By the rule "also of it," i is dropped; by the rule beginning "after hal and long ī," t is dropped; and by the rule "elision of the final of a conjunct," c is dropped: avanīvaktāṃ, avanīvacuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: avanīvicīḥ, apanīvana, avanīvaktaṃ, avanīvakta. In the three forms of the last person: aṅnīvaṃci, avanīvacā, avanīvacma.

In luṅ, iṭ is attached: avanīvaṃcīta, avanīvaṃciṣṭaṃ, avanīvaṃciṣuḥ, and so on.

In liṭ, ām is attached by the rule beginning "kās" (by the rule beginning "after sic and a reduplicated stem," jhi becomes jus): vanīvaṃcikṣar, and so on.

In luṭ, iṭ is given: vanīvicitā, vanīvaṃcitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, n is dropped by the rule beginning "of those that do not have the marker i": vanīvacyat, vanīvacyastāṃ, vanīvacyīsuḥ. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given: vanivaṃciṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: avanīvaṃciṣyata, and so on.

To gamḷ, "to go," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated, and by the rule beginning "ending in a nasal," the augment nuk is given. By the rule "cu for ku and h," and with n made anusvāra and yaṅ dropped, laṭ and the rest are attached to jigama. In the singular of the first person, by the rule "optionally after yaṅ," īṭ is optional: jigamīti, jigaṃti. In the dual, m is dropped by the rule beginning "of what ends in a nasal, in the domain of what is near." In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh becomes at, and by the rule beginning "gama, hana," the penultimate is optionally dropped: jigamati. Likewise in the three forms of the middle person: jigamīṣi, jigaṃsi, jaṃgathaḥ, jigatha. In the three forms of the last person: jigamimi, jaganmi, jiganva, jiganma. In liṅ: jigamyat, jigamyātāṃ, jigamyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: jaṃgamītu, jaṃgaṃtu, jaṃgatāta, jigatāṃ, jaṃgamatu, jigmatu. In the three forms of the middle person: jaṃgahi, jaṃgatāta, jaṃgataṃ, jaṃgata. In the three forms of the last person, where by the rule "also before v and m," m becomes n: jaṃgamāni, jaṃgamāpa, jaṃgamāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: ajaṃgamāta, ajaṃgama, ajaṃgatāṃ, ajaṃgamuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: ajagamīḥ, ajaṃgama, ajaṃgataṃ, ajaṃgata. In the three forms of the last person: ajaṃgamaṃ, ajaṃganva, ajaṃganma, and so on.

In luṅ, iṭ is given: ajaṃgamīta, ajaṃgamaṣḍaṃ, ajaṃmiṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, ām is attached: jaṃgamāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ is given: jaṃgamitā, jaṃgamitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: jaṃgamyāta, jaṃgamyāstāṃ, jaṃgamyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given: jaṃgamiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ajaṃgamiṣyat, and so on.

To hana, "to harm," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated. By the rule "cu for ku and h," and by the rule "car also in the abhyāsa," jh becomes j. By the rule beginning "ending in a nasal," the augment nuk is given, and that is made anusvāra. By the rule "also after the abhyāsa," h is changed to gh, and laṭ and the rest are attached to jaṃghana. In the singular of the first person, by the rule "optionally after yaṅ," iṭ is optional: jaṃghanīti, jaṃganti. In the dual, n is dropped by the rule beginning "of what ends in a nasal, in the domain of what is near": jaṃghataḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh becomes at, and by the rule beginning "gama, hana," the penultimate is optionally dropped: jaṃghanati, jaṃghati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: jaṃganīṣa, jaṃbhansi, jaṃghathaḥ, jaṃghatha. In the three forms of the last person: jaṃghanīmi, jaṃghanīmi, jaṃghanvaḥ, jaṃghanmaḥ. In liṅ: jaṃghanyat, jaṃghanyātāṃ, jighanyāsuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: jaṃghanītu, jaṃghantu, jaṃghatāta, jaṃghatāṃ, jaṃghanatu. In the three forms of the middle person: jighahi, jigatātā, jighati, jighata. In the three forms of the last person: jighanāni, jaṃghanāva, jaṃghanāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: ajighanīta, ajighana, ajighatāṃ, ajighanuḥ, ajibhūḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: ajighaniḥ, ajighana, ajighataṃ, ajighata. In the three forms of the last person: ajighanaṃ, ajighanva, ajighanma.

In luṅ, iṭ is given: ajighanīt, ajighaniṣṇvaṃ, ajighaniṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, ām is attached: jighanāṃcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ is given: jighanitā, jighanitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ: jighanyata, jighanyastaṃ, jighanyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given: jighaniṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: ajighaniṣyata, and so on.

To cara, "to go," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated, and by the rule "also of cara and phala," the augment nuk is given. By the rule "u after a," it is changed to u. By the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to cicur. In the singular of the first person, by the rule "optionally after yaṅ," īṭ is optional, and guṇa is not made: caṃcurīti, caṃcūrti. In the dual, by the rule "also before hal," it is made long: caṃcūrtaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh is changed to at: cicurati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: cicurīṣi, caṃcūrī, cicūrthaḥ, cicūrtha. In the three forms of the last person: cicurīmi; and, made long by the rule "also before hal," cicūrmi, cicūrvaḥ, cicūrmaḥ. In liṅ, made long by the rule "also before hal": cicūryāta, cicūryuta, caṃcūryuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: cicurītu, cicūrtu, cicūrtāta, cicūrtaṃ, cicurtatu. In the three forms of the middle person: cicūrthi, cicūrtāta, cicūrtaṃ, cicūrta. In the three forms of the last person: cicurāṇi, cicurāva, cicurāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: acicurīt, acicuḥ, acicūrtā, acicuryaḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: acicūrīḥ, acicuḥ, acicūrtaṃ, acicūrta. In the three forms of the last person: acicuraṃ, acicūrva, acicūrma.

In luṅ, iṭ is given: acicurīta, acicuriṣṭaṃ, acicuriṣuḥ, and so on. In liṭ, ām is attached: cicurīcakāra, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ is given: cicuritā, cicuritāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, made long by the rule "also before hal": cicūryata, cicūryāstāṃ, cicūryāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given: cicuriṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: acicuriśyata, and so on.

To khana, "to dig," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated. By the rule "cu for ku and h," kh becomes ch, and by the rule "car also in the abhyāsa," ch becomes c. By the rule beginning "ending in a nasal," the augment nuk is given. By the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to cikhana. In the singular of the first person, by the rule "optionally after yaṅ," īṭ is optional: cikhanīti, cikhanti. In the dual, by the rule beginning "jana, khana, sana," the final syllable is changed to ā: cikhātaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh is changed to at, and by the rule beginning "gama, hana, khana," the penultimate is optionally dropped: cikhanati, cikhnati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: cikhanīṣi, cikhansi, cikhāthaḥ, cikhātha. In the three forms of the last person: cikhanīmi, cikhanmi, cikhanvaḥ, cikhanma. In liṅ: cikhanyāt, cikhanyātāṃ, cikhanyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ: cikhanītu, cikhantu, cikhātāta, cikhātāṃ, cikhanatu, cikhnatu. In the three forms of the middle person: cikhāhi, cikhātāta, cikhātaṃ, cikhāta. In the three forms of the last person: cikhanāni, cikhanāva, cikhanāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: acikhanīta, acikhana, acikhātāṃ, acikhanuḥ, acikhnuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: acikhanīḥ, acikhana, acikhataṃ, acikāta. In the three forms of the last person: acikhanaṃ, acikhanva, acikhanma. In the remaining l-suffixes, in order: luṅ, acinīta; liṭ, cikhanāṃcikara; luṭ, cikhanitā; benedictive liṅ, cikhanyāta; lṛṭ, cikhaniṣyati; lṛṅ, acikhanaṣyata, and so on.

To divu, "to play," yaṅ is given. It is reduplicated, and by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made. By the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to the resulting dediva. In the singular of the first person, by the rule "optionally after yaṅ," īṭ is optional. In the alternative with īṭ: dedivīti.

In the alternative without īṭ, the sūtra: chvoḥ śūṭhanunāsike ca, "Ś and ūṭh for ch and v, also before a nasal." The letter ch and the letter v at the end of a root are to be changed respectively to ś and ūṭh before the kṛt suffix kvi, before a nasal, and before suffixes beginning with jhal and bearing the marker k or ṅ. The commentary cites: yaṅluki śūthau bā jhali bakare, "In the elision of yaṅ, ś and ūṭh optionally before jhal and the letter v." When yaṅ is elided, the root-final letters ch and v, even when the suffix does not bear the marker k or ṅ, are optionally changed respectively to ś and ūṭh before what begins with jhal and before the letter v. In the alternative of changing to ūṭh, by the rule "yaṇ for ik before a vowel," and then guṇa; in the alternative of not changing to ūṭh, by the rule "elision of v and y before val," v is dropped and guṇa is made: dedyoti, dedeti.

In the dual, changing to ūṭh or not is optional. In the alternative where it is not changed, by the rule "elision of v and y before val," v is dropped: dedhūtaḥ, deditaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh is changed to at: dedivati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: dedivīṣi, dediṣi, dedeṣi, dedyātha, dedithaḥ, dedithaḥ, dedyūtha, deditha. In the three forms of the last person: dedivīmi, dedyomi, dedemi, dedyāvaḥ, dedyūmaḥ, dedimaḥ. In liṅ: dedibyātāṃ, dedibyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: dedithītu, dedyotu, dedetu, dedyūtāṃ, deditāṃ, dedivatu. In the three forms of the middle person: dedyūti, dedyūtāta, dedyūtaṃ, deditaṃ, dedyūta, deditaḥ. In the three forms of the last person: dedivīnaṃ, dedivāva, dedivāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: adedivīt, adedyod, adedeta, adedyūtāṃ, adeditāṃ, adedipuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: adedivīḥ, adedyoḥ, adedeḥ, adedyūto, adedetaṃ, adedyūta, adedita. In the three forms of the last person: adedivaṃ, adedyūva, adediva, adedyūma.

In luṅ, iṭ is given: adedivīt, and so on. Likewise in the remaining l-suffixes: liṭ, dedivāṃcakāra; luṭ, dedivitā; benedictive liṅ, dedībyāta; lṛṭ, dediviṣyataṃ; lṛṅ, adedipiṣyata, and so on.

To vicha, "to go," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated, and by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made. By the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to vevicha. In the singular of the first person, by the rule "optionally after yaṅ," īṭ is optional. In the alternative without īṭ, by the rule beginning "vraśca, bhrasja," ch or ś becomes ṣ; by the rule "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," t becomes ṭ; and guṇa is made: vevichīti, veviṣṭi. In the dual, by the rule beginning "vraśca, bhrasja," ch or ś becomes ṣ, and by the rule "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," t is changed to ṭ: veviṣṭaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh is changed to at: vevichati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: vevichīṣi, vevikṣi, veviṣṭhaḥ. In the three forms of the last person: vevichīmi, veviśmaḥ, veviśvaḥ, vevichvaḥ, veviśmaḥ. In liṅ: vivichyāt, vevichyātāṃ, vevichyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: vivichītu, veviṣḍaṃ, veviṣḍaṃ, vevichatu. In the three forms of the middle person: vevibhi, veviṣḍāta, veviṣṭaṃ, veviṣṭa. In the three forms of the last person: vevichāni, vevichāpa, vevichāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: avevichita, avebeṭ, aveviṣṭāṃ, avevichuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: avevichīḥ, aveviṭ, aveviṣṭaṃ, aveviṣṭaḥ. In the three forms of the last person: avevichi, aveviśva, avevichva, aveviśma. In the remaining l-suffixes: luṅ, avevichīt; liṭ, vevichīcakāra; luṭ, vevichitā; benedictive liṅ, vevichyāt; lṛṭ, vevichiṣyati; lṛṅ, avevichiṣyata, and so on.

To yu, "to mix," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated, and by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made. By the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to yoyu. In the singular of the first person, by the rule "optionally after yaṅ," īṭ is optional, and guṇa is made: yoyavīti, yoyoti. In the dual: yoyutaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh is changed to at, and by the rule beginning "before a vowel, of śnu, of a root," it is changed to uv: yoyuvati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: yoyavīṣi, yoyoṣi, yoyuthaḥ, yoyutha. In the three forms of the last person: yoyavīmi, yoyomi, yoyuvaḥ, yoyumaḥ. In liṅ, made long by the rule beginning "not kit": yoyūyāt, yoyūyātāṃ, yoyūyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: yoyavītu, yoyotu, yoyutāta, yoyutāṃ, yoyuvatu. In the three forms of the middle person: yoyuhi, yoyutāta, yoyutaṃ, yoyuta; yoyāvāni, yoyavāva, yoyavāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: ayoyavīt, ayoyot, ayoyutāṃ, ayoyavuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: ayoyavāḥ, ayoyoḥ, ayoyutāṃ, ayoyuta. In the three forms of the last person: ayoyavaṃ, ayoyuva, ayoyuma. In the remaining l-suffixes: luṅ, ayoyavīta; liṭ, yoyavāṃcakāra; luṭ, yoyavitā; benedictive liṅ, yoyūyāt; lṛṭ, yoyaviṣyati; lṛṅ, ayoyaviṣyata, and so on.

To ohāk, "to abandon," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated and made short by the rule "short." By the rule "cu for ku and h," and by the rule "car also in the abhyāsa," jh becomes j. By the rule beginning "not bearing the marker k," it is made long. By the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," y is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to jāhā. In the singular of the first person, īṭ is optional; in the alternative with īṭ, īṭ is joined in sandhi: jāhiti, jāhāti. In the dual, since it is not a ghu root, by the rule "ī before hal," ā is changed to ī: jāhātaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh becomes at, and by the rule "of the ā of śnā and of a reduplicated stem," a is dropped: jāhati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: jāheṣi, jāhāsi, jāhīthaḥ, jāhītha. In the three forms of the last person: jāhemi, jāhāmi, jāhīvaḥ, jāhīmaḥ. In liṅ, by the rule "elision before y," ā is dropped: jāhyāt, jāhyātāṃ, jāhyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: jāhetu, jāhātā, jāhītāta, jāhītāṃ, jāhatu. In the three forms of the middle person: jāhīhi, jāhītāta, jāhītāṃ, jāhīta. In the three forms of the last person: jāhāni, jāhāva, jāhāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: ajātita, adāhāta, ajāhītāṃ, ajāhuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: ajāhiḥ, ajātāḥ, ajāhītaṃ, ajāhīta. In the three forms of the last person: ajāhāṃ, ajāhīva, ajāhīma. In the remaining l-suffixes: luṅ, ajāhiṣṭa; liṭ, jāhāṃcakāra; luṭ, jāhitā; benedictive liṅ, jāhyāta; lṛṭ, jāhiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajāhiṣyata, and so on.

To daṃśa, "to bite," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated, and by the rule beginning "japa, jabha," the augment nuk is given. Yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to daṃdaṃśa. In the singular of the first person, īṭ is optional; in the alternative with īṭ, n is dropped: daṃdaśīti, daṃdaṃṣṭi. In the dual, by the rule beginning "of those that do not have the marker i," n is dropped; by the rule beginning "vraśca, bhrasja," ś becomes ṣ; and by the rule "ṣṭu with ṣṭu," t is changed to ṭ: daṃdaṣṭaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh is changed to at: daṃdaśati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: daṃdaśiṣi, daṃdaṃkṣi, daṃdaṃṣṭhaḥ, daṃdaṣṭha. In the three forms of the last person: daṃdaśīmi, daṃdaṃśmi, daṃdaśvaḥ, daṃdaśmaḥ. In liṅ, n is dropped by the rule beginning "of those that do not have the marker i": daṃdaśyāt, daṃdaśyātāṃ, daṃdaśyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ: daṃdaśītu, daṃdaṃṣṭu, daṃdaṣṭāta, daṃdaṣṭāṃ, daṃdaśatu. In the three forms of the middle person: daṃdaḍñha, daṃdaṣṭāta, daṃdaṃṣṭaṃ, daṃdaṃṣṭa. In the three forms of the last person: daṃdaṃśāni, daṃdaṃśūva, daṃdaṃśāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: adaṃdaśita, adaṃdana, adaṃdaṣṭāṃ, adaṃdaśuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: adaṃdaśīḥ, adadana, adaṃdaṣṭaṃ, adaṃdaṣṭa. In the three forms of the last person: adaṃdaṃśi, adaṃdaśva, adaṃdaśma. In the later l-suffixes: luṅ, adaṃdaṃśīta; liṭ, daṃdaṃśāṃcakāra; luṭ, daṃdaṃśyītā; benedictive liṅ, daṃdaśyāta; lṛṭ, daṃdaṃśiṣyati; lṛṅ, adaṃdaṃśiṣyata, and so on.

To ñiṣvapa, "to sleep," yaṅ is attached. By the rule "of svapi and syami, before yaṅ," it is changed to samprasāraṇa. It is reduplicated, and by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made. By the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to soṣupa. In the singular of the first person, īṭ is optional: soṣupīti, soṣobti. In the dual: soṣubhaḥ. In the plural, jh is changed to at: soṣupati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: soṣupīṣi, soṣopli, soṣupthaḥ, soṣuptha. In the three forms of the last person: soṣupīmi, soṣupmi, soṣupvaḥ, soṣupmaḥ. In liṅ: soṣupyāt, soṣupyātāṃ, soṣupyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: soṣuvītu, soṣuptu, soṣubtāta, soṣuptāṃ, soṣuvatu. In the three forms of the middle person: soṣubhi, soṣuptāta, soṣuptaṃ, soṣupta. In the three forms of the last person: soṣupāni, soṣupāva, soṣupāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: asoṣupīt, asoṣova, asoṣuptāṃ, asoṣuvuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: asoṣupīḥ, asoṣova, asoṣuptaṃ, asoṣupta. In the three forms of the last person: asoṣupaṃ, asoṣupva, asoṣupma. In the remaining ones: luṅ, asoṣupīt; liṭ, soṣuvāṃcakāra; luṭ, soṣuvitā; benedictive liṅ, soṣubyāt; lṛṭ, soṣupiṣyati; lṛṅ, asoṣupiṣyata, and so on.

Or else, in the alternative where it is not changed to samprasāraṇa, the abhyāsa is made long by the rule beginning "not bearing the marker k": sāsvapīti, sāsvapti, and so on; the procedure is the same as the preceding one.

To bhidir, "to split," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated; by the rule "car also in the abhyāsa," bh becomes b; by the rule beginning "when yaṅ or its elision follows," guṇa is made; and by the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to bebhid. In the singular of the first person, iṭ is optional: bebhidīti, bebhetti. In the dual, by the rule "car before khar," d is changed to t: bebhittaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," it is changed to at: bebhidati. Likewise in the three forms of the middle person: bebhidīṣi, bebhetsi, bebhitthaḥ, bebhittha. In the three forms of the last person: bebhibīmi, bebhidmi, bebhidāḥ, bebhidmaḥ. In liṅ: bebhidyāt, bebhidyātāṃ, bebhidyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: bebhidītu, bebhiṇṭu, bebhittāta, bebhittāṃ, bebhetatu. In the three forms of the middle person: bebhiddhi, bebhittāta, bebhittaṃ, bebhitta. In the three forms of the last person: bebhidāni, bebhidāva, bebhidāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: abebhidīt, abebheta, abebhittāṃ, abebhiduḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: abebhidīḥ, abebhita, abebhittaṃ, abebhitta. In the three forms of the last person: abebhidaṃ, abebhidvo, abebhidma.

The sūtra: na bhātulobaārdhadhātuke, "Not before an ārdhadhātuka suffix for one whose root has undergone elision." After part of a root has been elided, as when yaṅ is elided, before an ārdhadhātuka suffix (jhi becoming jus), even when a cause for guṇa and vṛddhi arises, guṇa, vṛddhi and the like are not applied to that root. In the remaining l-suffixes: luṅ, abebhidīt; liṭ, bebhidīcakāra; luṭ, bebhiditā; benedictive liṅ, bebhidyāt; lṛṭ, bebhidiṣyati; lṛṅ, abebhidiṣyata, and so on.

To vṛtu, "to proceed," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated and t is dropped. The sūtra: rugrikau ca luki, "Also ruk and rik before elision." When the elision of yaṅ follows, the abhyāsa of a root that has ṛ as its penultimate receives the augment ruk, the augment rik, and, by the word "also," the augment rīk. The k of these adventitious elements serves to fix their position, and the u of ruk serves for pronunciation. So laṭ and the rest are attached to whichever of the three is formed, varbṛta, varibṛta or varibṛt. In the singular of the first person, īṭ is optional: varbṛtīti, varbartti. In the dual: varbṛttaḥ. In the plural, jh is changed to at: varbṛtati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: varbṛtīṣi, varbartsi, varbṛtthaḥ, varbṛtha. In the three forms of the last person: varbṛtīmi, varbartmi, varbṛtvaḥ, varbṛtmaḥ. In liṅ: varbṛtyāt, varbṛtyātāṃ, varbṛtyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: varbṛrtītu, vavartta, varbṛttāta, varbṛttāṃ, varbṛtatu. In the three forms of the middle person: varbṛtthi, varbṛttaṃta, varbṛttaṃ, varbṛtta. In the three forms of the last person: varbṛtāni, varbṛtāva, varbṛtāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: avarbṛtīt, avarbaḥ, avarbṛtāṃ, avarbṛtuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: avarbṛtīḥ, avarbaḥ, avarbṛttaṃ, avarbṛtta. In the three forms of the last person: avarbṛtāṃ, avarbṛtva, avarbṛtma. In the remaining ones: luṅ, avarbṛtīt; liṭ, varbṛtāṃcakāra; luṭ, varbṛtitā; benedictive liṅ, varbṛtyāt; lṛṭ, varbṛtiṣyati; lṛṅ, avarbṛrtiṣyata, and so on.

Or else (jhi becoming jus): varibṛtīti, varibartti, and so on; and varībṛtīti, varībartti, and so on. Apart from the single difference of the augment, the other procedures are the same.

To gṛdhu, "to covet," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated; ṛ becomes a; by the rule "cu for ku and h," and by the rule "also ruk and rik before elision," the augment ruk is given. Yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to jarbṛdha. In the singular of the first person, īṭ is optional, and by the rule "of jhar before a like jhar," dh is dropped: jargṛdhīti, jargarddhi. In the dual, by the rule beginning "after a final jhaṣ," t becomes dh, and by the rule "jaś for jhal before jhaś," dh is changed to d: jargṛddhaḥ. In the plural, jh is changed to at: jargradhati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: jargṛdhīṣi, jargadhardhmi, jargṛddhaḥ, janṛtṭha. In the three forms of the last person: jarṇṛdhīmi, jargardhmi, jargṛdāḥ, jargṛdhmaḥ. In liṅ: jargṛdhyāt, jargṛdhyātāṃ, jargṛrdhyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: jargṛdhītu, jargardhu, jargṛddhāta, jargṛdhatu. In the three forms of the middle person: jargṛddhī, jargṛddhāta, jargṛddhi, jargṛddha. In the three forms of the last person: jargṛdhāni, jargṛdhāva, jargidhāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: ajargṛdhīt, ajargaḥ, ajargṛdṭhāṃ, ajargṛdhuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: ajargṛdhīḥ, ajargaḥ, ajargṛdṭhāṃ, ajargṛdṭha. In the three forms of the last person: ajargṛdhaṃ, ajargṛdhma, ajargṛdhma. In the remaining ones: luṅ, ajargṛdhīt; liṭ, jargṛdhāṃcakāra; luṭ, jargṛdhitā; benedictive liṅ, jargṛdhyāt; lṛṭ, jargṛdhiṣyati; lṛṅ, ajargṛdhiṣyata, and so on. Or else, with the augment rik or rīk attached: jarigṛdhīti, jarigardhi, and so on; or jarīgṛdhīti, jarīgardhi, and so on.

To ḍukṛñ, "to do," yaṅ is attached. It is reduplicated; ṛ becomes a; and by the rule "cu for ku and h." The sūtra: rita śca, "Also from ṛt." From a root ending in ṛ too, when the elision of yaṅ follows, the abhyāsa receives the augments ruk, rik and rīk. By this sūtra the augment ruk is given. By the rule "of yaṅ, also before a vowel," yaṅ is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to carkṛ. In the singular of the first person, iṭ is optional: carkarīti, carkarti. In the dual: cirkṛtaḥ. In the plural, by the rule "at after a reduplicated stem," jh becomes at, and by the rule "yaṇ for ik before a vowel": carkrati. Formed in the same way as these, in the three forms of the middle person: carkarliṣi, carkirṣa, carkṛthaḥ, carkṛtha. In the three forms of the last person: carkarīmi, carkarmi, carkṛpaḥ. In liṅ: carkṛyāt, carkṛyātāṃ, carkṛyuḥ, and so on.

In loṭ, formed as in laṭ, in the three forms of the first person: carkarṝtu, carkartu, carkṛtāta, carkṛtāṃ, carkratu. In the three forms of the middle person: carkṛhi, carkṛnāta, carkṛta. In the three forms of the last person: carkarāṇi, carkarāva, carkarāma.

Likewise in laṅ, in the three forms of the first person: acarkarīt, acarkaṣa la carkṛtāṃ, acarkatuḥ. In the three forms of the middle person: acarkarīḥ, acarkraḥ, acarkṛtaṃ, acarkṛta. In the three forms of the last person: acarkari, acarkṛva, acarkṛma. In the remaining ones: luṅ, acarkrita; liṭ, carkṝcakāra; luṭ, carkritā; benedictive liṅ, carkrithāta; lṛṭ, carkriṣyati; lṛṅ, acarkṛṣyata, and so on.

For the two augments rik and rīk as well, apart from the difference in the adventitious element, the procedure on meeting laṭ and the rest is the same: carikarīti, carikarti, and so on; or carīkarāti, carīkarti, and so on.

iti bāṇinibyākaraṇa (liṭ is given; for k before a vowel, ya, ṣa, da; ām is attached; yaṇ for the letter before a vowel) sya sūtrāta (before the letter ś and liṅ, by the rule "long," ṛ is changed to rīṅ) yaṅlugannāḥ samābhāḥ. That is: from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the forms ending in the elision of yaṅ are complete.

With these, in The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down in the form of notes the meaning of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, together with its procedures, illustrative examples and so on, the procedures for forms ending in the elision of yaṅ, in their general rules together with their exceptions, are for now complete in rough outline.

Third, I shall explain the scope and the procedures of kyac, by which a nominal is made into a root. The sūtra: sup ārmana kyacha, "Kyac after a sup-ending word, in the sense of wishing for oneself." Where a sup ending has been applied to what was already formed into a noun from a root, in the sense of wishing for something for oneself, the suffix kyac, which makes that noun into a root again, optionally occurs. The letter c serves to block the vowel operation, and the letter k serves for the rule "also before kyac." The sūtra: kyaci ca, "Also before kyac." When the suffix kyac follows, the letter a at the end of a stem is changed to ī.

To the stem putra, kyac is attached and the marker is dropped. By this sūtra a is changed to ī, and laṭ and the rest are attached to the resulting putrīya. Śap is added for the agent, and by the rule "of the two, before guṇa after a, one takes the form of the following," it is changed: laṭ, phutrīyati; liṅ, putrīyata; loṭ, putrīyatu; laṅ, aputrīyata, and so on. In luṅ, iṭ is given, and by the rule "elision of a," a is dropped: aputrīyīta, and so on. In liṭ, ām is attached and a is dropped: putrāṃyāṃcakāra, butñiyāṃbabhūva, putrīyāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ is given and a is dropped: butrīyitā, butrīyitāsi, and so on. (One wishes for a son.) In the benedictive liṅ, a is dropped: butrīyyāstāṃ, putrīyyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given and a is dropped: butrīyiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: aputrīyiṣyat, and so on.

To the stem go, kyac is attached. By the rule "av for what ends in o, before a suffix beginning with y," it is changed to av, and laṭ and the rest are attached to gavya: laṭ, gavyati; luṅ, ugavyit; liṭ, gavyāṃcakāra; luṭ, gavyitā; benedictive liṅ, gavyāt, and so on.

Further, before ārdhadhātuka suffixes, by the rule "option of kya," ya is optionally dropped: luṅ, agavīt; liṭ, gavāṃcakara; luṭ, gavitā; benedictive, gavyāt; lṛṭ, gavibyāt; lṛṭ, gaviṣyati; lṛṅ, agaviṣyat, and so on; or agavyīt, and so on.

Likewise to the stem nau, kyac is attached. Before the suffix beginning with y, for what ends in au (by the rule "option of kya," yra), it is changed to āv, and laṭ and the rest are attached to nābya: laṭ, nābyati; anābyīt; luṅ, anābīt; nābyāṃcakāra; liṭ, nābāṃcakāra, and so on.

To the stem tvat, kyac is attached, and laṭ and the rest are attached to tvaṅya: laṭ, tāṅyati; atvadyītā; luṅ, atādīta; tvaryāṃcakāra; liṭ, tādāṃcakāra, and so on.

Likewise, when kyac is attached to mat: laṭ, maṅyati; amaṅyīta; luṅ, amaṅīt; madyīcakāra; liṭ, madāṃcakāra, and so on.

When kyac is attached to yaṣmat: laṭ, yuṣmaṅyati; ayuṣmadyīt; luṅ, ayuṣmadit; yuśaṃṣmaṅyṇaṃcakāra; liṭ, yuṣmadāṃcakāra (one wishes for you), and so on.

Likewise: laṭ, asmaṅyati; āsmaṅyīt; luṅ, āsmadyīta; asmaṅyāṃcakāra; liṭ, asmadācakāra (one wishes for me), and so on.

To the stem gira, kyac is attached. By the rule "also before hal," the penultimate is made long (one wishes for you): laṭ, gīryati (one wishes to speak); agīryīta; luṅ, agīrīt; gīryāṃcakāra; liṭ, gīrācakāra, and so on.

What is called deb (one wishes for me): to the stem, kyac is attached. By the rule "also before hal," the penultimate is made long: laṭ, drībyati (one wishes for heaven); adībyīta; luṅ, adībīt; dībyāṃcakāra; liṭ, dīpāṃcakāra, and so on.

When kyac is attached to the stem adas: laṭ, adasyati (one wishes for that); ādasyīta; luṅ, ādasīt; adasyāṃcakāra; liṭ, adasāṃcakāra, and so on.

To the stem kartṛ, kyac is attached, and by the rule "rīṅ for ṛ," it is changed to rīṅ: laṭ, kartrīyati (one wishes to act); luṅ, akartrīyīta; liṭ, kartrīyāṃcakāra, and so on.

To the stem gārga, kyac is attached, and by the rule "also before kyac," it is changed to ī: laṭ, gārgīyati; luṅ, agārgīyīta; liṭ, gārgīyācakāra, and so on.

The sūtra: naḥkye, "Of n, before kya." When the suffixes kyac, kyaṅ and kyaṣ follow, the letter n of a stem ending in n is elided, as at the end of a word. To rājan, kyac is attached; by this sūtra n is dropped, and by the rule "also before kyac," it is changed to ī: laṭ, rījāyati (one wishes for a king); luṅ, arījīyīta; liṭ, rījīyāṃcakāra, and so on.

When kyac is attached to the stem vac: laṭ, bacyatī; abacyit; luṅ, abacīt; bacyīt; bacyāṃcakāra; leṭ, bacīcakāra, and so on.

To the stem kavi, kyac is attached, and it is made long by the rule beginning "not kit": laṭ, kavīyati; luṅ, akavāeyīta; liṭ, kapīyāṃcakāra, and so on.

When kyac is attached to the stem samiṅgha: laṭ, samiṅghyati (one wishes for fuel for the fire offering; one wishes to speak), and so on. And: kyasya bibhāṣā, "option of kya."

After a stem ending in a consonant, kyac, kyaṅ and kyaṣ are optionally elided before an ārdhadhātuka suffix: asamidhyīt; luṅ, asamibḍīt; saṃmiṅhyāṃcakāra; liṭ, samiṅhraṃcakāra, and so on.

The sūtra: namānūbyayebhyāḥ kyac, "Kyac does not occur after what ends in m or after indeclinables." After stems ending in m and after indeclinables the suffix kyac does not occur. For one ending in m: kimicchati. For an indeclinable: uccairicati, and so on.

The sūtra: aśanāyodanyaṅhanāyābubhukāpibāsāgarṅheṣu, "Aśanāya, udanya and dhanāya, in the senses of hunger, thirst and greed." When hunger, thirst and greed are expressed, aśanāya, udanya and dhanāya, ending in kyac, are to be taken as irregularly formed words: aśanā (one wishes for something) yati; udanya (one wishes to drink) ti; dhanāyati, and so on. If the sense is not hunger and the rest, then by the rule "also before kyac," it is changed to ī: aśanīyati (one wishes to pervade); udakīyati (one wishes for water); dhanīyati (one wishes for wealth), and so on.

The sūtra: aśvakṣīrabraṃṣlabaṇāmārmabrītaukyaci, "Of aśva, kṣīra, vṛṣa and lavaṇa, before kyac, in the sense of one's own delight." When kyac follows the stems aśva and the rest, used in the sense of desire for one's own delight, the augment suk occurs; the k serves to fix its position and the u serves for pronunciation: aśvasyati baḍavā, kṣīrasyati bāla, vṛṣasyati gauḥ, lavaṇasyatyuṣṭraḥ, and so on.

The commentary explains that after a stem ending in a vowel, when kyac follows in the sense of desire, the augments suk and asuk optionally occur, and that because of these two adventitious elements the s does not become ṣ: dadhisyati, dadhyasyati, and so on (the mare desires a stallion; the child desires milk; the cow desires a bull; the she-camel desires salt). Or else, without giving the augment, it is made long by the rule beginning "not kit": dadhīpati, and so on.

Fourth, the scope of kāmyac is explained. The sūtra: kāmyaccha, "Also kāmyac." After a stem, in the sense of wishing for oneself (one wishes for curd), not only kyac but also kāmyac occurs; the c serves for the accent.

When kāmyac is attached to the stem putra: laṭ, putrakāmyati; liṅ, putrakāmyet; liṭ; loṭ, putrakāmyatu; laṅ, aputrakāmyata; luṅ, aputrakāmyīt (one wishes for curd); liṭ, butrakāmyāṃcakāra; luṭ, putrakāmyitā; benedictive liṅ, putrakāmyāt; lṛṭ, putrakāmyiṣyati; lṛṅ, aputrakāmiṣyat, and so on.

Likewise, when kāmyac is attached to the stem yaśas: laṭ, yaśaskāmyati; luṅ (one wishes for asu), ayaśaskāmyit; liṭ, yaṅśaskāmyāṃcakā, and so on.

Likewise, when kāmyac is attached to the stem sarveṣ: laṭ, sarviṣkāmya (by the rule "elision of y in yam after a consonant," y is dropped) te, and so on.

When kāmyac is attached to kima, when kāmyac is attached: laṭ, kiṃkāmyati, and so on. Likewise: laṭ, sraḥkāmyate (one wishes for fame), and so on.

The sūtra: upamānādācāre, "From a standard of comparison, in the sense of conduct." After a stem, in the sense of behaving toward something as toward a standard of comparison (one wishes for fresh butter), kyac too follows. Kyac is attached in the sense of putram ivācarati, "one behaves toward him as toward a son," and by the rule "also before kyac," it is changed to ī (what one wishes): putrīyati māṇavakaṃ, "one treats the young brahmin as a son." Likewise (one wishes for heaven): viṣṇuyati dvijaḥ, "one treats the twice-born as Viṣṇu," and so on.

The sūtra: aṅhikaraṇācca, "Also from a locus." For a noun, from a locus such as a house serving as the basis, in the sense of the action of behaving toward something as toward a standard of comparison (one behaves toward him as toward a son), kyac also occurs. In the sense of prāsādāḥ ivācāra tikuṭyaṃ (one treats him as a son: the young brahmin; one treats the hut as a palace; the twice-born treats him as Viṣṇu): prāsādīyati kunyaṃ, "one treats the hut as a palace," and so on.

The sūtra: kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaśca, "From the agent also kyaṅ, and elision of s." After a noun, in the sense of the agent behaving like a standard of comparison, kyaṅ occurs, and before the suffix kyaṅ the s at the end of the stem is optionally elided. The letter ṅ serves for applying the taṅ (ātmanepada) endings, and the k has the general purpose of the rule "option of kya."

To the stem payas, kyaṅ is attached, and the elision or non-elision of s is optional. In the alternative where s is dropped, it is made long by the rule beginning "not kit": laṭ, payāyate (it behaves like milk); liṅ, ṅayāyita; loṭ, payāyatāṃ; laṅ, apayāyata; luṅ, apayāyiṣṭa; liṭ, payāyāṃcakre; luṭ, payāyitā; benedictive liṅ, bayāyiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, bayāyiṣyate; lṛṅ, abayāyiṣyata, and so on. In the alternative where s is not elided: laṭ, payasyate; luṅ, apayasyiṣṭa; luṅ, apayasiṣṭa; liṭ, payasyīcakri; liṭ, payasāṃcakre.

Likewise kyaṅ is attached to kumārī. By the rule "also before kyaṅ and māni," the feminine suffix is dropped, and it is made long by the rule beginning "not kit": kumārāyati bṛddhā, and so on.

The sūtra: ojasoñabsarasonityaṃ, "Always of ojas and apsaras." Before kyaṅ, the letter s of ojas and apsaras is always elided. S is dropped and it is made long by the rule beginning "not kit": ojāyate durbalaḥ, apsārāyate kurūpā, and so on.

The sūtra: supūrbasyamansonityaṃ, "Always of manas preceded by su" (the old woman behaves like a young girl). Before kyaṅ, the letter s of manas preceded by the prefix su is always elided. S is dropped and it is made long by the rule beginning "not kit": sumanāyate duṣṭamanaḥ (the weakling fancies himself strong; the ugly woman fancies herself an apsaras), and so on.

The sūtra: ācāreglmaklībahoṇhebhyaḥkvipbā, "Optionally kvip after galbha, klība and hoḍha, in the sense of conduct." After galbha, klība and hoḍha, in the sense of conduct, kyaṅ occurs and kvip also occurs. To the kvip-ending form (one who fancies himself exhausted in mind, that is, of dark or evil thoughts) laṭ and the rest are applied with the taṅ endings.

To galma, kvip is attached and kvip is dropped entirely. Before sārvadhātuka suffixes, śap is added and the rule "guṇa after a" applies; before ārdhadhātuka suffixes, iṭ is added before what begins with val; in liṭ ām is attached; and by the rule "elision of a," a is dropped: laṭ, galmate; liṅ, galmeta; loṭ, gmatā; laṅ, agalmata; luṅ, agalmiṣṭa; liṭ, galmvaṃcakre; luṭ, galmitā; benedictive liṅ, galmiṣīṣṭa; lṛṭ, galmiṣyate; lṛṅ, agalmiṣyata, and so on. Or else, kyaṅ is attached and it is made long: galmāyate, and so on. Likewise klāṃbate, and so on, or klībāyate; hoḍjate, haḍhayate, and so on.

Examples of these joined with accompanying words: galmate tīkṣṇaḥ (the harsh one fancies himself gentle); klībate puruṣaḥ (the man behaves like a eunuch); hoḍhate paṇḍitaḥ (the learned one behaves like a fool). The commentary explains that this occurs not only for galbha and the rest but for every stem in the sense of conduct: kṛṣṇati (one behaves like Kṛṣṇa); svati (one behaves like oneself); devati (one behaves like a god); and so on without end.

The sūtra: bhraṃśādibhyo bhubyacverlapaśca halaḥ, "After bhṛśa and the rest, in the sense of becoming, when not ending in cvi, and also elision of a final consonant." After bhṛśa and the rest, in the sense of something newly arising, such as what was not intense becoming intense, when the form does not end in the suffix cvi, kyaṅ also occurs in those senses, and before kyaṅ the final consonants of those stems are also elided: bhraṃśāyaste (one acts intensely); unmanāyate (one becomes elated), and so on. Bhṛśa and the rest are: bhṛśa, intense; unmanas, elated; śīghra, swift; paṇḍita, learned; utsuka, eager; abhimanas, proud; durmanas, unhappy; nṛvat, manlike; śuci, pure; nīla, blue; vajra, diamond; phena, foam; excrement; harita, green; madra, deep-voiced, and so on. The commentary explains that for these, in the sense of newly arising, kvip also optionally occurs: bhṛśate, and so on.

The sūtra: lohitīṅiṇājbyaḥkyaṣa, "Kyaṣ after lohita and the rest and after ḍāc." After lohita and the rest, and after what ends in ḍāc, in the sense of newly arising, kyaṣ occurs. The letter ṣ serves for the rule "optionally after kyaṣ," and the letter k has the general purpose of the rule "option of kya." The sūtra: bākyaṣaḥ, "Optionally after kyaṣ." After what ends in kyaṣ, laṭ and the rest take the taṅ endings, and optionally the non-taṅ endings as well (it becomes very red): lohitāyeti; laṭ, lohitāyata; lohiṇāyet; liṅ, lohitāyaṭha; lohitāyeha; lohitāyaṅtu; loṭ, lohiṇāñāṃ; alohitāyata; laṅ, alohidāyata; alohitāyīta; luṅ, alohitāyiṣṭa; lohitāyāṃcakāra; liṭ, lohitāyāṃcakri; lohitāyitāsi; luṭ, lohitāyitāse; lohitāyyāta; benedictive liṅ, lohitāyiṣāṣṭa; lohitāyiṣyati; lṛṭ, lohitāyiṣyate; alohitāyiṣyata; lṛṅ, alohitayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise carmāyati (it becomes hide), carmāyatai, and so on; and for one ending in ḍāc: paṭapaṭvayati (it flickers intensely), paṭapaṭvayati, and so on.

The sūtra: kaṣṭāyakarmaṇe, "Kaṣṭa, for an action." For kaṣṭa, in the sense of an action done deliberately for what is nonvirtuous, kyaṅ also occurs: kaṣṭāyate (one goes for the sake of trouble), and so on.

The sūtra: satrakakṣakakṭakraṃchraghanebhyaḥ pāpacikīrṣāyāṃ, "After satra, kakṣa, kaṣṭa, kṛcchra and gahana, in the sense of wishing to do evil." After satra, kakṣa, kaṣṭa, kṛcchra and gahana, in the sense of wishing to go about doing evil, kyaṅ also occurs: satrāyate (one goes in deceit); kakṣāyate (one goes for the sake of the brush); kakṭāyate (one goes for the sake of trouble); kṛcchrāyate; gahanāyati (one goes into the thicket), and so on.

The sūtra: karmaṇoromanthatapobhyāṃbarticaroḥ, "Romantha and tapas, applied to an action of moving." When romantha applies in the sense of moving the cheek, and tapas in the sense of moving, kyaṅ also occurs: romanthāyate gauḥ (the cow chews the cud); tapasyate (one goes into austerity), and so on. The commentary says that the non-taṅ endings apply to tapas ending in kyaṅ.

The sūtra: bāṣpoṣmabhyaṃmudvamane, "After bāṣpa and ūṣma, in the sense of giving off upward." After bāṣpa and ūṣma, in the sense of giving off upward, kyaṅ also occurs: bāṣbāyate (it gives off vapor); ūṣmāyate (it gives off heat), and so on.

The sūtra: phenācca, "Also after phena." After phena too, in the sense of giving off upward, kyaṅ also occurs: phenāyate (it gives off froth), and so on.

The commentary cites: ṅhūmābvā, "Optionally after dhūma." After dhūma, in the sense of giving off upward, kyaṅ also occurs, and laṭ and the rest optionally take the non-taṅ endings: dhūmāyate (it gives off smoke), and so on.

The sūtra: śabdeberkalahābhākaṇṭhamṅhyebhyaḥ karṇe, "After śabda, vaira, kalaha, abhra, kaṇṭha and madhya, in the sense of making." After śabda and these others, in the sense of making, kyaṅ also occurs: śaphāyate (one makes a sound); vairāyate (one makes enmity); kalahāyate (one makes a quarrel); abhrāyate (it makes clouds); kaṇṭhāyate (one makes it thin); madhyāyate (one makes the middle), and so on.

The sūtra: sudinaṅurdinanīhārebñyaśca, "Also after sudina, durdina and nīhāra." After sudina and these others too, in the sense of making, kyaṅ also occurs: sudenāyate (it makes a fine day); durdinayatre (it makes a bad place); nīhārāyate (it makes mist), and so on.

The sūtra: sukhādibhyaḥkartṛbadenāyāṃ, "After sukha and the rest, in the sense of the agent's experiencing." After sukha and the rest, in the sense of knowing, experiencing or obtaining, kyaṅ also occurs: sukhāyate (one experiences happiness); duḥkhāyata (one experiences suffering), and so on. Sukha and the rest are: sukha, happiness; duḥkha, suffering; tṛpra, blood, peace, offering; kṛccha, difficulty; agra, supreme; alīka, falsehood or untruth; kṛpaṇa, horse, edge, seng sna, wretched one, and sword; aruṇa, ruddy; karuṇa, compassion; soḍha, prime; pradīpa, lamp or radiance; madra, deep-voiced, and so on.

The sūtra: namobariścitraṅkyac, "Kyac after namas, varivas and citraṅ." For namas and varivas in the sense of showing reverence, and for citra in the sense of marveling, kyac occurs; the letter ṅ of citraṅ serves for applying the taṅ endings: namasyati devān (one pays homage to the gods); varivasyati gurūn (one makes offerings to the teachers); citrīyate tvaṃ (one marvels at you), and so on.

The sūtra: pucchadudsane, "After puccha, with ut, in the sense of throwing." For puccha preceded by the prefix ut, in the sense of throwing, kyaṅ also occurs: utpucchayate (it swishes its tail upward), and so on.

The sūtra: paryudśaneca, "Also with pari and ut, in the sense of spreading." For puccha preceded by the prefixes pari and ut, in the sense of spreading, kyaṅ also occurs: paripucchayate (it spreads its tail fully); utbucchayate (it spreads its tail), and so on.

The commentary cites: bhāṇṇātsamācayane, "After bhāṇḍa with sam, in the sense of accumulating." For bhāṇḍa preceded by sam, in the sense of accumulating, kyaṅ also occurs: saṃghāṇṇāyate (one gathers things into a vessel), and so on.

The sūtra: cibarādrjane bariṅhāne pā, "Optionally after cīvara, in the sense of gathering what was cast off." For cīvara preceded by sam, in the sense of gathering up again what others have cast off, kyaṅ optionally occurs: cīvarāyate bhikṣuḥ (the mendicant gathers rags into a patchwork).

The sūtra: muṇḍamiśraślakṣṇalapaṇabratabstrahalakṛtadūstebmyoṇica, "Ṇic after muṇḍa, hair; miśra, mixed; ślakṣṇa, of fine characteristics; lavaṇa, salt; vrata, a vow; vastra, cloth; hala, a plough; kṛta, a deed; and tūsta, a thread." After muṇḍa and these others, in the sense of making, ṇic occurs. The sūtra: ṇābiṣṭhapatprātipadikasya, "Before the ṇi of a noun, as before iṣṭha." When ṇic is attached to a noun, the elision of the noun's final syllable and the other operations are carried out as for the suffix iṣṭhan; all the procedures of the iṣṭhan section apply.

To muṇḍa ṇic is attached; by this sūtra a is dropped; and laṭ and the rest are attached to muṇḍi: laṭ, muṇḍayati; liṅ, muṇḍayeta; loṭ, muṇḍayatu; laṅ, amuṇḍayaha, and so on. In luṅ, by the rule beginning "ṇi, śri, dru," cli is changed to caṅ; by the rule "before caṅ," mu is reduplicated; and by the rule "of ṇi, before what lacks iṭ," ṇi is dropped: amumuṇḍata, amumuṇḍatāṃ, amumuṇḍan, and so on. In liṭ, ām is attached by the rule beginning "kās": muṇḍayācakāra, muṇḍayāṃbabhūva, muṇḍayāmāsa, and so on. In luṭ, iṭ is given: muṇḍayitā, muṇḍayitāsi, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, ṇi is dropped before what lacks iṭ: muṇyāt, muṇḍyāsṛāṃ, muṇḍyāsuḥ, and so on. In lṛṭ, iṭ is given: muṇḍayiṣyati, and so on; and likewise in lṛṅ: amuṇḍayiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, when ṇic is attached to miśra: miśrayati, and so on. In luṅ, cli is changed to caṅ, mi is reduplicated, and before what lacks iṭ ṇi is dropped: amimiśrata, and so on. In liṭ, ām is attached: miśrayāṃcakāra, and so on. In the remaining ones: luṭ, miśrayitā; benedictive liṅ, miśryāt; lṛṭ, miśrayiṣyati; lṛṅ, amiśayiṣyat, and so on.

Likewise, when ṇic is attached to ślakṣṇa: laṭ, śākṣṇayati; luṅ, aśaślakṣṇata; liṭ, ślakṣṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, ślakṣṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, ślagṣṇyat, and so on.

When ṇic is attached to lavaṇa: laṭ, lavaṇayati; luṅ, alalavaṇata; liṭ, lavaṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, lavaṇayitā; benedictive, lavaṇyāt, and so on.

When ṇic is attached to vrata: laṭ, vratayati; luṅ, abvratata; liṭ, vratayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vratayitā; benedictive, vradyāt, and so on.

When ṇic is attached to vastra: laṭ, vastrayati; luṅ, avastata; liṭ, vastrayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vastayitā; benedictive liṅ, vaskyuta, and so on.

When ṇic is attached to hala: laṭ, halayati; luṅ, ajahalata; liṭ, halayāṃcakāra; luṭ, halayitā; benedictive liṅ, halyāt, and so on.

When ṇic is attached to kṛta: laṭ, kṛtayati; luṅ, acīkyaṃtata, where by the rule beginning "before ṇi with caṅ, as before san," a becomes i, with lengthening of the light syllable; liṭ, kṛtayāṃcakāra; luṭ, kraṃtayitā; benedictive liṅ, kṛṅyāt, and so on.

Ṇic is attached to tūsta: laṭ, tūsteyeti; luṅ, atutūstatā; liṭ, tustayāṃcakāra; luṭ, tūstayitā; benedictive liṅ, trasñyat, and so on.

For the stem satya, ṇic is attached by the rule beginning "satyāpa, pāśa, rūpa." The commentary cites: arthabedastyānāmābuka, "Āpuk for artha, veda and satya." When ṇic follows at the end of artha, veda and satya, the augment āpuk occurs; the k serves to fix its position and the u serves for pronunciation. Laṭ and the rest are attached to satyāpi: laṭ, saṅyāpayati (one makes it true); luṅ, asasṅyapata; liṭ, satyābāṃcakāra; luṭ, satyapitā; benedictive liṅ, satyāṅhata, and so on.

Likewise for artha: laṭ, arthāpayati (one acts for a purpose); luṅ, artathapata (the commentary says that before caṅ, for artha, tha itself is reduplicated, as cited earlier in the passage beginning "ba'a ma"); liṭ, arthāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, arthāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, arthāpyat, and so on.

For veda: laṭ, vedāpayati (one makes it known); luṅ, avivedavata; liṭ, vedīpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vedāvayitā; benedictive liṅ, vedābyāt, and so on.

Ṇic is attached to what is called pāśa. By the rule "before the ṇi of a noun, as before iṣṭhan," a is dropped, and laṭ and the rest are attached to pāśi: laṭ, pāśayati (one makes a snare); luṅ, apabaśata; liṭ, pāśayāṃcakṅara; luṭ, pāśayitā; benedictive liṅ, bāśyāt, and so on.

Likewise for rūpa: laṭ, rūbayati (one makes form); luṅ, arurubata; liṭ, rūpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, rūbayitrā; benedictive liṅ, rāpyāta, and so on.

For vīṇā: laṭ, vīṇayati (one makes sweet music); luṅ, avibiṇata; liṭ, vīṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, vīṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, vīṇyāta, and so on.

For tūla: laṭ, tūlayati (one makes it fine); luṅ, atutlulta; liṭ, tūlayāṃcakāra; luṭ, tūlayitā; benedictive liṅ, tūlyāt, and so on.

For śloka: laṭ, ślokayati (one composes verses); luṅ, aśuślukata; liṭ, ślokayāṃcakāra; luṭ, ślokayitā; benedictive liṅ, ślokyāt, and so on.

For senā: laṭ, sernāyati (one forms an army); luṅ, asisinta; liṭ, senayācakāra; luṭ, senayitā; benedictive liṅ, senyāta, and so on.

For loma: laṭ, lomayati (one makes a sound); luṅ, alulumat; liṭ, lomayāṃcakāra; luṭ, lomayitā; benedictive liṅ, lomyāt, and so on.

For tvaca: laṭ, tvacayata (eight hands); luṅ, atazhvacāte; liṭ, tracayāṃcakāra; luṭ, tvacayitā; benedictive liṅ, tvacyāt, and so on.

For varṇa: laṭ, varṇayati (one makes color); luṅ, avarṇata; liṭ, varṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, varṇayitā; benedictive, varṇyat, and so on.

For carma: laṭ, carmayati (one makes hide); luṅ, acacarmat; luṭ, carmayitā; benedictive liṅ, carmyāt, and so on.

For cūrṇa: laṭ, cūrṇayati (one makes powder); luṅ, acucurṇat; liṭ, cūrṇayāṃcakāra; luṭ, cūrṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, curṇyāta, and so on.

The commentary explains that ṇic also occurs in the sense of making intensively. So ṇic is attached to hasta: laṭ, hastayati (one makes it very much a hand); luṅ, ajahastata; liṭ, hastayāṃcakāra; luṭ, hastayitā; benedictive liṅ, hasdyat, and so on.

When ṇic is attached to ṣaṇṭha: laṭ, ṣaṣṭhayati (one makes six); luṅ, aṣaṣaṣṭhat; liṭ, ṣaṣṭhāthāṃcakāra; luṭ, ṣaṣṭhayitā; benedictive liṅ, ṣaṣyāt, and so on.

Ṇic is attached to kavi, and by the rule "before the ṇi of a noun, as before iṣṭhan," the final syllable is dropped: laṭ, kavayati (one composes poetry); luṅ, acīkavat, where by the rule beginning "when ak is not elided," as before san, it becomes i and is made long; liṭ, kavayāṃcakāra; luṭ, kaphayitā; benedictive liṅ, kavyāta, and so on.

Likewise for paṭu: laṭ, baṭayatri (one makes clever); luṅ, ubīpaṭata; liṭ, baḍayāṃcakāra; luṭ, paṭayitā; benedictive liṅ, paṭyāt, and so on.

Further, since the commentary says that ṇic also occurs in the sense of what the noun expresses, ṇic is attached to ghata: laṭ, ghatayati; luṅ, ajaghatata; liṭ, ghatayāṃcakāra; luṭ, ghatayitā; benedictive liṅ, ghatyāt, and so on. An example joined with an accompanying word is ghatayati śadrūn, which is explained as killing enemies.

Likewise, when ṇic is attached to bandha: laṭ, bandhayati; luṅ, ababandhata; liṭ, bandhayāṃcakāra; luṭ, pandhayitā; benedictive liṅ, bandhāt, and so on; as in bandhayati cauraḥ, one binds the thief.

To the stem called ūḍhi ṇic is attached, and the final syllable is dropped: laṭ, uḍhayati (one causes to obtain), and so on. For luṅ, the commentary explains at this point that either ḍha itself together with ṇic is reduplicated, or, since the first ḍha is a transformed h, it optionally reverts to its state in the abhyāsa and is treated accordingly: aḍiḍhata, and so on; or else ojiḍñata, and so on. In the remaining ones: liṭ, ūḍhayāṃcakāra; luṭ, ūḍhayitā; benedictive liṅ, ūḍhyāt, and so on.

Likewise, when ṇic is attached to ūḍha: laṭ, ūḍhayati (having obtained, one acts); auḍaḍhata; luṅ, aujaḍhata; liṭ, ūḍhayāṃcakāra; luṭ, ūḍhayitā; benedictive liṅ, ūḍhyāta, and so on.

The commentary cites: brakṛtyaiśācabṛṅṅhibugāgamau, "Vṛddhi and the augment puk for what has by nature a single vowel." For a stem that has a single vowel, not one whose final syllable has been elided and so on, vṛddhi is made before ṇic, and the augment puk also occurs. To the stem sva ṇic is given, and by this citation vṛddhi and the augment puk are given: laṭ, svāpayatī; luṅ, asasvābata; liṭ, svāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, svāyayitā; benedictive liṅ, svāpyāt, and so on.

To the stem eṇī ṇic is attached, and by the rule "before the ṇi of a noun, as before iṣṭha," the feminine suffix is dropped: laṭ, enayati; luṅ, aiṇaṇata; liṭ, anayāṃcakāra; luṭ, eṇayitā; benedictive liṅ, etsyāt, and so on (one makes it one's own).

Ṇic is attached to pṛthu and the final syllable is dropped; by the rule "r for ṛ," ṛ is changed to r: laṭ, prathayati; luṅ, apaprathat; liṭ, prathayāṃcakāra; luṭ, prathayitā; benedictive liṅ, prathyāt, and so on.

To the stem sthūla (one behaves like a doe) ṇic is attached. By the rule "before the ṇi of a noun, as before iṣṭha," the final syllable together with the semivowel is dropped and guṇa is made: laṭ, sbravayati; luṅ, asthabata; liṭ, sthavayāṃcakāra (one makes it broad); luṭ, sthavayitā; benedictive liṅ, sthavyāt, and so on.

To the stem priya ṇic is attached. By the rule "as before iṣṭha," priya is changed to pra, and by the cited rule beginning "what has by nature a single vowel," vṛddhi and puk are given: laṭ, prāpayati (one makes it stout); luṅ, apaprabata; liṭ, brapayāṃcakāra; luṭ, brāpayitā; benedictive liṅ, brāpyāt, and so on.

Likewise, to the stem sthira ṇic is attached. By the rule "as before iṣṭha," sthira is changed to stha, and vṛddhi and puk are given: laṭ, sthāpayati; luṅ, atasthapata; liṭ, sthāpayāṃcakāra; luṭ, sthāpayitā (one makes glad); benedictive liṅ, sthābyāta, and so on.

Likewise, to the stem sādhu ṇic is attached. By the rule "before the ṇi of a noun, as before iṣṭha," sādhu is changed to sādha, and the final syllable is dropped: laṭ, sādhayataṃ; luṅ, asasādhat; liṭ, sādhayāṃcakāra (one makes it firm); luṭ, sādhayitā; benedictive, sādhyāt, and so on.

To the stem yuva ṇic is attached. By the rule "as before iṣṭha," yuva is changed to kana, and vṛddhi is not made: laṭ, kanayati; luṅ, acakanata; liṭ, kanayāṃcakāra; luṭ, kanayitā; benedictive liṅ, kanyāt (good), and so on.

To the stem sragvin ṇic is attached, and by the rule "as before iṣṭha," the suffix vin is dropped: laṭ, srajayati (having garlands); luṅ, asasrajat; liṭ, srajayāṃcakāra; luṭ, srajayitā; benedictive liṅ, srajyat (young), and so on.

To the stem iśamat ṇic is attached, and by the rule "as before iṣṭha," the suffix matup is dropped: laṭ, iśayati; luṅ, aiśaśata; liṭ, eśayāṃcakāra; luṭ, eśayitā; benedictive liṅ, eśyāt, and so on.

The sūtra: śvetāśvāśvataragaloṭitāhvarakākṇāṃmantakalopaśca, "And elision of the final of śveta, aśva, aśvatara, galoḍi, āhvara and kāka." After śveta and these others, ṇic occurs in their own sense (glorious), and before ṇic the final of these stems is to be elided: laṭ, śvetayati; luṅ, aśiśvitat; liṭ, śvatayāṃcakāra (white; horse; supreme horse; majestic; harming all; crow); luṭ, śvetayitā; benedictive liṅ, śvetyāt, and so on.

Likewise: laṭ, aśvayati; luṅ, āśaśvat; liṭ, aśvayāṃcakāra; luṭ, aśvayitā; benedictive, aśvyat, and so on. Laṭ, aśvatarayati; luṅ, āśaśvatarata; liṭ, aśvatarayāṃcakāra; luṭ, aśvatarayitā; benedictive liṅ, aśvataryāt, and so on. Laṭ, galoḍayahi; luṅ, ajagaluḍata; liṭ, galoḍayāṃcakāra; luṭ, galoḍayitā; benedictive liṅ, galoḍhyāt, and so on. Laṭ, āhvarayati; luṅ, ājahvarata; liṭ, āhvarayāṃcakāra; luṭ, āhvarayitā; benedictive liṅ, ahvaryāt, and so on. Laṭ, kākayati; luṅ, acakakat; liṭ, kvakayāṃcakāra; luṭ, kākayitā; benedictive liṅ, kākyāt, and so on.

The sūtra: kaṇḍādibhyoyak, "Yak after kaṇḍū and the rest." After kaṇḍū and the rest, in the sense of making, yak occurs; the k serves to make it kit. For those of kaṇḍū and the rest that do not bear the marker ṅ, laṭ and the rest after what ends in yak take both the taṅ and the non-taṅ endings; for those bearing the marker ṅ, only the taṅ endings are applied: kaṇḍūyati; laṭ, kaṇḍūyate; akaṇḍūyīt; luṅ, akaṇḍūyiṣḍa; kaṇḍuyāṃcakāra; liṭ, kaṇūyāṃcakre; kaṇūyitāsi; luṭ, kaṇḍūyitāse; kaṇḍūyyāt; benedictive liṅ, kaṇḍūyiṣīṣṭa, and so on.

Kaṇḍū and the rest are: kaṇḍū; vandū; asū; kvuṇit; maniṅ; hraṃṇīṅ; sakhrago; veṅ; nāṅ; veṭ; lāṭ; tiras, invisible; iyas; uras, a plain; kusubha, saffron; magadha, holding the central land; medha, clear-minded; bhiṣaj, medicine; triṣṭubh, the three-part meter; anar; arra; samar; uṣṇih; iṣubha; urṇa; turaṇa; bharaṇa; elā; velā; kelā; khela; leṭ; loṭ; sukha; duḥkha, and so on.

The sūtra: kyajantātsan, "San after what ends in kyac."

When kyac has been attached to a noun, san follows what ends in kyac in the sense of desire. To putrīya san is attached, and iṭ is given before what begins with val. The commentary explains that for the roots formed from nouns (cardamom; time; play; sport; happiness; suffering), when a cause for reduplication follows, whichever syllable one wishes is reduplicated. For example, reduplicating any one of the three, pu, ti or yi: pupṛtrīyiṣati, and so on; or putitrīyiṣati, and so on; or else putrīyiyiṣati, and so on.

The commentary further explains that if the noun begins with a vowel, that vowel is not reduplicated, but any one of the consonants with their vowels that follow the vowel is reduplicated. To aśvīya san is attached (one wishes to treat him as a son), and iṭ is given; reduplicating either yi or śi: aśiśvīyiṣate, and so on; or aśvīyiyiṣati, and so on. Likewise san is attached to indrīya, and with iṭ applied: indrīyiṣati, and so on; or indrīyiyaṃṣati, and so on.

The commentary cites: kaṇḍvādestṛtiyasyab, "Of kaṇḍū and the rest, the third" (one wishes to behave like the Lord). For kaṇḍū and the rest ending in yak, san also occurs, and the third syllable of these is to be reduplicated (one wishes to behave like Indra). To kaṇḍūya san is attached; iṭ is given; by the rule "elision of a," a is dropped; and by this citation the third syllable, yi, is reduplicated: kaṇḍūyiyiṣati, and so on.

Since the commentary says that san also occurs after what ends in ṇi, san is attached to kāmi, iṭ is given, and it is reduplicated: cikāmayiṣati, and so on.

iti plaṇaṃnibyākarṇasya sūtrānlāmaṅhātabaḥ samāptāḥ. That is: from the sūtras of the Pāṇinian Grammar, the nominal roots are complete.

With these, in The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down in the form of notes the meaning of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinian Grammar, together with its procedures, illustrative examples and so on, the procedures for forming nouns into roots are for now complete in rough outline.

Now I shall explain the procedures for the way roots and prefixes are joined. The sūtra: anubarābhyāṃkṛñaḥ, "After kṛñ with anu and parā." For kṛñ following the prefixes anu and parā, laṭ and the rest take the parasmaipada endings for an agent who possesses the fruit of the action: anukaroti, parākaroti, and so on.

The sūtra: abhipratyatibhyaḥkṣipaḥ, "After kṣip with abhi, prati and ati." For kṣip following abhi, prati and ati, laṭ and the rest take the parasmaipada endings for an agent who possesses the fruit: abhikṣipati, prati (one imitates; one makes it supreme) kṣipati, atikṣibati, and so on.

The sūtra: prādvahaḥ, "After vah with pra." For vah following pra, the parasmaipada endings occur for an agent who possesses the fruit: pravahati, and so on.

The sūtra: parermraṃṣaśca, "Also after mṛṣ with pari" (one hurls forth). For mṛṣ and vah following pari (one throws in different directions; one throws hard), the parasmaipada endings also occur for an agent who possesses the fruit: parimṛṣyati, parivahati, and so on (one fully obtains).

The sūtra: byāṅparibhyaḥramaḥ, "After ram with vi, āṅ and pari." For ram following vi, āṅ and pari, the parasmaipada endings occur for an agent who possesses the fruit: viramati, āramati, pari (one fully forbears; one fully obtains) ramati, and so on.

The sūtra: upāccha, "Also after upa." For ram following upa too, the parasmaipada endings occur for an agent who possesses the fruit: uparamati, and so on.

The sūtra: bibhāṣākarmakāta, "Optionally, when without an object" (one delights thoroughly; one delights completely; one delights fully). For ram following upa without an object, the parasmaipada and ātmanepada endings are optional: uparamati (one rejoices nearby), uparamate (one rejoices nearby), and so on.

The sūtra: buṅhayuṅhanaśajerprudrusrubhyoṇe, "After ṇi for budh, yudh, naś, jan, iṅ, pru, dru and sru." After these, budh and the rest, ending in ṇic, the parasmaipada endings are applied in the sense of possessing the fruit: bodhayati, yodhayati, nāśayati, jānayati; with adhi preceding, adhyāpayati, where by the rule beginning "krī, iṅ," āt is given, and by the rule beginning "arti," puk; brjavayati, drāvayati, srāvayati (one causes to go), and so on.

The sūtra: nigaraṇacalanārthabhyaśca, "Also after those meaning going, moving and eating" (one causes to understand; one causes to fight; one causes to perish; one causes to be born; one causes to request). After roots meaning going, moving and eating (one causes to obtain; one causes to do, or causes to go, or causes to flee), ending in ṇic, the parasmaipada endings also occur in the sense of possessing the fruit: cālayati, kambayati, bhojayati, and so on. Although it has the sense of eating, for ad ending in ṇi the parasmaipada endings do not occur: ādayate, and so on.

The sūtra: aṇābakarmakāccittabatkarjraṃkāṇṇeḥ, "After ṇi, when without ṇi the agent is sentient and there is no object" (one causes to go; one causes to move; one causes to eat). When, without the ṇi ending, the sentient agent is without an object, then after its ṇi ending, in the sense of possessing the fruit (one causes to eat), the parasmaipada endings occur. Without the ṇic ending: āste vipraḥ; with the ṇi ending: āsayati vipraṃ.

The sūtra: napādamāyamāyasaparimuharucinṛtipadabasaḥ, "Not after pā, dam, āyam, āyas, parimuh, ruc, nṛt, vad and vas." After these, pā and the rest, ending in ṇic, in the sense of possessing the fruit, the parasmaipada endings (the young brahmin stays; one makes the young brahmin stay) do not occur: pāpayate, dāmayate, āyāmayate, āyasayate, parimohayate, rocayati, nartayate, vādayate, vāsayate, and so on.

The commentary says that after dheṭ too the non-taṅ endings do not apply (one causes to drink): dhāpayate, and so on.

The sūtra: kartṛkarmabyatihāro, "In reciprocal exchange of the agent's action" (one causes to drink; one causes to be calm; one causes to restrain fully; one causes to desire fully; one causes to be fully deluded; one causes to shine; one causes to dance; one causes to speak; one causes to dwell). In the sense of one agent engaging in one of many actions done in exchange, the ātmanepada endings occur: vyatibhavate; vyatiste, by the rule called śnas. The sūtra: nagatihiṅsārthebhyaḥ, "Not after those meaning going and harming."

Even though one agent engages in one of many actions shared among agents, if that action has the sense of harming or of going, the parasmaipada endings do not occur: vyatighnanti, vyatisarpanti (they become one; they come together), and so on.

Since the commentary explains that for has and the rest, too, the ātmanepada endings do not occur: vyatihasati, vyatipaṭhati, vyatijalpati, and so on.

The commentary further explains that although it has the sense of harming, hṛñ does not take the non-taṅ endings (one strikes very much in various ways; one goes very much in various ways) but is applied only with the taṅ endings: saṃpraharate, and so on.

The sūtra: binamayeca, "Also in exchange" (one harms very much in various ways; one reads very much in various ways; one speaks very much in various ways). For an action engaged in as a mutual exchange of acts, too, the parasmaipada endings do not apply: vyatilunate, vyatisunate, and so on (one plunders completely).

The sūtra: nerbiśa, "After viś with ni." For viś following ni, the ātmanepada endings occur: niviśate, and so on.

The sūtra: paribyabebhyaḥkriyaḥ, "After krī with pari, vi and ava." For krī following pari, vi and ava (one cuts; one purifies), the ātmanepada endings occur: parikrīṇīte, by the rule beginning "śnā"; vikrīṇīte, avakrīṇīte, and so on.

The sūtra: biṅ (one enters decisively) rābñyājeḥ, "After ji with vi and parā." For ji following vi and parā, the taṅ endings occur: vijayate, and so on.

The sūtra: āṅodonāsyabaṃharṇe, "After dā with āṅ, when not in the sense of opening the mouth" (one sells fully; one sells in various ways; one sells completely). For dā following āṅ, when not in the sense of opening the mouth, the taṅ endings occur (one conquers in various ways; one conquers others): ātte (one gives completely), and so on. If it is in the sense of opening the mouth, the non-taṅ endings are applied (one gave by opening the mouth): āsyaṃ vyādadāti, and so on.

The sūtra: kriṭoñanusaṃparibhyaśca, "After krīḍ, also with anu, sam and pari." For krīḍ following anu, sam and pari, and also āṅ, the taṅ endings occur: anukrīḍate, saṃkrīḍate, parikrīḍate, ākrīḍate, and so on.

The sūtra: āṅogmeḥkṣamāyāṃ, "After gam with āṅ, in the sense of forbearance." For gam ending in ṇic and following āṅ, when used in the sense of forbearance, the taṅ endings occur: āgamayate. The commentary explains that for nāth, when used in the sense of wishing (one plays along; one plays well; one plays fully; one plays completely), the taṅ endings occur: sarviṣanāthate, and so on.

The commentary further explains that for hṛñ, in the sense of taking on a manner of going, the taṅ endings occur (one forbears): anuharateñśvaḥ, and so on.

The sūtra: apāccatuṣnācchakuniṣālekhane, "After apa, of quadrupeds and birds, in the sense of scratching" (one wishes for fresh butter). For kṝ following apa, when used in the sense of quadrupeds and birds scratching lines, the taṅ endings apply and the augment suṭ also occurs (one follows the horse): apaskirate gṛṣaḥ; by the rule "the root's ṛ becomes ir"; apaskirate kukuṭaḥ.

Since the commentary explains that for nu and pracch following āṅ the taṅ endings occur: ānute śṛgāla, āpṛcchate gurūn, and so on. The commentary further explains that for śap, in the act of swearing an oath, the taṅ endings apply (the bull scratches; the rooster scratches): devadattāya śapate, and so on.

The sūtra: sambaprabibhyaḥsthaḥ, "After sthā with sam, ava, pra and vi" (the jackal wishes; one asks the teachers). For sthā following these prefixes, sam and the rest, the taṅ endings occur: saṃtiṣṭhate, avatiṣṭhate, pratiṣṭhate, vitiṣṭhate (one swears by Devadatta), and so on. Since the commentary explains that for sthā following āṅ the taṅ endings always occur: ātiṣṭhate (one stands completely), and so on.

The sūtra: prakāśanstheyākhyayośca, "Also in the senses of making manifest and of declaring definitively" (one stands firmly; one stands completely; one stands well; one stands in various ways). When sthā is used in the senses of making manifest and of declaring definitively, too, the taṅ endings occur: naṃtyaṃ mā tiṣṭhate; tiṣṭhate kanyāchatrebhyaḥ, and so on.

The sūtra: udoñnūrṅhakarmaṇi, "After ut, in an action that is not upward." For sthā following ut, when used of an action that is not upward, the taṅ endings occur: muktāvuttiṣṭhate, and so on. When it is upward they do not apply (sound abides permanently; the girl stands for the shades): āsanāduttiṣṭhati, and so on.

The sūtra: upānmaṃtrakaraṇe, "After upa, when a mantra is the instrument." For sthā following upa, when used with a mantra as the instrument, the taṅ endings are applied (arisen from a pearl): sāvitryā upatiṣṭhate, and so on.

Since the commentary explains that for sthā following upa, when used for the acts of worship, rising from one's seat, joining together, and friendship or a road, the taṅ endings occur: buddhaṃ upatiṣṭhate; gaṃgā yamunām upatiṣṭhate; mitraṃ upatiṣṭhate; gaṃgāṃ (one stands near to recite the Vedas) upatiṣṭhate panthāḥ.

The sūtra: lipsāyāṃbā, "Optionally, in the sense of wishing to obtain." For sthā following upa, when it conveys a wish to obtain, the taṅ endings optionally occur (one stands near to worship the Buddha; the rivers Gaṅgā and Yamunā stand together; one stands near a friend; one stands near the Gaṅgā), or else the non-taṅ endings occur (a road): bhikṣuko brāhmaṇakulam upatiṣṭhate, or upatiṣṭhati.

The sūtra: akarmakācca, "Also when without an object." For sthā following upa, when it is without an object too, the taṅ endings occur: bhojanakāle upatiṣṭhate, and so on.

The sūtra: udāṃbhyāṃtapa, "After tap with ut and vi." For tap following ut and vi, when used without an object (the monk stands near the brahmin household), the taṅ endings occur: uttapate, vitapata, and so on (one stands near at mealtime).

The sūtra: āṅoyamahanaḥ, "After yam and han with āṅ." For yam and han following āṅ, when used without an object or for an action of one's own limb, the taṅ endings occur: ācchate (one gives); āhate (one strikes) (one torments greatly; one torments in various ways); āyacchate pādaṃ (one strikes one's foot); āhate ūruṃ (one strikes one's thigh), and so on.

For luṅ, the sūtra: hanaḥsica, "Sic after han." The sic following han is treated as bearing the marker k when ātmanepada endings follow.

Before what bears the marker k, the n is dropped by the rule on stems ending in a nasal and so on; and since the sic is also dropped by the rule "after a short stem, before those beginning with jhal" and so on, we get āhata, āhasātāṃ, āhasāta, and so on. Or else: the sūtra ātmanepadeṣvanyatarasyāṃ, "Optionally before the ātmanepada endings." Before the ātmanepada endings into which luṅ is converted, han is optionally changed to baṅha. In the option where it is changed to baṅha, iṭ is added, giving ābṅhiṣḍa, ābaṅhiṣādāṃ, ābaṅhiṣata, and so on.

yamaśca, "And after yam." The sic following yam is also treated as bearing the marker k when ātmanepada endings follow. Before what bears the marker k, the nasal is dropped; and since the sic is also dropped by "after a short stem, before those beginning with jhal" and so on, we get āyata, āyasātāṃ, āyasata, and so on.

samogmṛchiprachisvaratyartiśrubidibhyaḥ, "After sam: from gam, ṛchi, prachi, svarti, arti, śru and bidi." From these, gam and the rest, following sam, the ātmanepada endings occur: saṃgacchate.

For luṅ: bāgamaḥ, "Optionally after gam." The sic following gam, and the benedictive liṅ with ātmanepada endings, are optionally treated as bearing the marker k. In the option with k, the m is dropped by the rule on stems ending in a nasal and so on; and since the sic is also dropped by "after a short stem, before those beginning with jhal" and so on (one goes together correctly), we get samgata, samagasātāṃ, samgasata, and so on. In the option without k, the m is not elided, giving samagaṃsta, samgaṃsātāṃ, samgaṃsata, and so on. Likewise for the benedictive liṅ: saṃgasīṣṭa and so on, or saṃgaṃsīṣṭa and so on.

samṛcchate; saṃpṛcchate (one questions thoroughly); saṃsvarte (one proclaims everywhere). For ṛṅ preceded by saṃ, by "ta, hu" and so on, there is reduplication and the śaṅ is lost. For arti, the abhyāsa takes i by "piparti" and so on, and iya by "for what is not like the abhyāsa" and so on: samiyṛte (one goes everywhere). śṭu, śru, śṛ: saṃśṛṇute (one listens correctly). (One abides correctly:) saṃvitte, and so on.

bitterbibhāṣā, "An option after bitti." The jh following vid is changed to ad, and the augment ruk optionally occurs: saṃvidrate and so on, or saṃvidate and so on. Since the commentary explains that the taṅ endings also occur after dṛśa following saṃ, we get saṃpaśyate (one discerns fully), and so on.

nisamupabiphyohvaḥ, "From hvā after ni, sam, upa and vi." From hvā following ni, sam, upa and vi the taṅ endings occur: nihvayate, saṃhvayate, ubahvayate, pihvayate, and so on.

Cited in the commentary (one sees correctly): upasargāsyatyuhobā, "Optionally from asyati and ūh after a preposition." From asyati and ūh following prepositions the taṅ endings optionally (one calls decisively; one calls from all sides; one calls near; one calls in various ways) occur: niraṃsyate, samūhate, and so on; or else nirasyati, samūhati, and so on.

ubasrgāṅṅhrasvaūhateḥ, "Shortening of ūhati after a preposition." The upaṅhā of ūhati preceded by a preposition is made short before a suffix beginning with y that bears the marker k or ṅ. For the benedictive (one does not throw; one gathers, or one assembles) liṅ: samuhyāt, and so on.

sbarḍhāyāmāṅaḥ, "After āṅ, in rivalry." When rivalry is to be expressed, the taṅ endings occur after hvā following āṅ: mallo mallamāhvayate, and so on.

ganṅhanābakṣepaṇsebanasāhasikyapratiyatnaprakathanopayogekṛñaḥ, "From kṛñ in the senses of reviling, harming, serving, acting together, effort, speech, and employing."
