When kṛñ is used in these senses, reviling and the rest, (a wrestler challenges a wrestler) the ātmanepada endings occur: sūcaayamiyamutūrute; śyeno bartikām apakurute; gaṇakān prakurute (one shows respect to the assembly); parākanyāṃ prakurute (one acts together with another's daughter); eṅhodakasyo baskurute (one makes effort in the work of increasing the water); janbāṅān brakurute (one has people speak); (one employs for a hundred) śataṃ (one applies this and that) (the hawk harms the little bird, or the hawk harms the shrub) prakurute, and so on.

aṅheḥprahasane, "After aṅhi, in the sense of capability." When capability is to be expressed, the taṅ endings occur after kṛñ following aṅhi: daiṅyān abhikurute biṣṇuḥ.

baiḥśabdakarmaṇaḥ, "After vi, when the karman is sound." When a karman of sound is to be expressed, the taṅ endings occur after kṛñ following vi: svarān bikurute bipraḥ.

akarmakācca, "Also when without a karman." Also when there is no karman, the taṅ endings (Viṣṇu's might over you asuras) occur after kṛñ following vi: bāyurbakurute, and so on.

saṃmānnotsaṃjanṅacāryakarṇajñānbhṛtibigaṇanabyayeṣuniyaḥ, "From nī in the senses of honoring respectfully, anger, (the brahmin chants the notes) performing worship, knowing how to accomplish, fee, and wage." When these meanings, honoring respectfully and the rest, (Vāyu acts in various ways) are to be expressed, the taṅ endings occur after nī: śāstranyate; maṇi bakamubaṅānanayate; śatrunupanayate; debānupanayate; byākaruṇenayate (one guides in grammar); śataṃnayate; śataṃ nayate ṅānaḥ, and so on.

kartṛsthecāśarīrekarmaṇi, "And when an incorporeal (one leads through the treatise. The sense of honoring respectfully: one brought near to a brahmin boy. Anger: one leads off the enemies. Worship: one leads near to the gods. Knowing how to accomplish:) karman is located in the agent." (Fee: one takes a hundred. Wage: having taken a hundred, one gives.) When it is understood that the karman of the action is incorporeal and located in the agent, the taṅ endings occur after nī: kroṅhaṃ binayate, and so on.

bhṛntisargatāyaneṣukamaḥ, "From kram in the senses of entering, zeal and teaching." When entering, zeal and teaching are to be expressed, the taṅ endings occur after kram: ṛkṣvosya kramate buṅṅhiḥ; kramta byākarṇāṅhyayanām; prajñe śāstrā (one subdues anger) ṇiprakamte (one teaches the treatises to the learned one), and so on.

upaparābhyāṃ, "After upa and parā."

After upa and parā, the taṅ endings occur after kram. (The mind enters. One is zealous for the reading of grammar.) upakramate, one steps near; parākramte.

ād uṅgamane, "After āṅ, in the sense of spreading forth." When kram following āṅ refers to spreading rays upward, the taṅ endings occur: ākramate sūryaḥ.

beḥ pāṅā biharte, "After vi, in the sense of parting the feet." When kram following vi expresses the parting of the feet, (one steps elsewhere,) the taṅ endings occur: bikramate bādaḥ, and so on.

propābhyamārambhe, "After pra and upa, in the sense of beginning." (The sun spreads its rays.) When kram following pra and upa refers to beginning an action, the taṅ endings occur: prakramate bhoktuṃ, ubakramte bhoktuṃ, and so on. Since the commentary says that, when there is no preverb, (one strides,) the taṅ endings occur optionally after kram, one has kramate and so on, or kramati and so on.

apahnabe jñaḥ, "After jñā, in the sense of denial." When it expresses a falsehood, such as claiming to know what one does not know, (one sets about the food; one proceeds to the food,) the taṅ endings occur after jñā: śatamupajānīte, and so on.

akarmakācca, "And also when it has no object." When it has no object too, the taṅ endings occur after jñā: sarbiṣo jānīte.

saṃpratibhyāmanābṅyāne, "After sam and prati, when not in the sense of remembering." When jñā following sam and prati does not refer to remembering, (one knows a full hundred,) the taṅ endings occur: saṃjānīte, pratijānīte, and so on.

bhāsanopasaṃbhāṣājñanayatnabimatyupamaṃtraṇeṣu padaḥ. (One knows of fresh butter.) "After vad, in the senses of illuminating, conciliating, knowledge, effort, difference of opinion, and close praise." When vad expresses these meanings, illuminating and the rest, (one knows fully; one acknowledges,) the taṅ endings occur: śāstra prabadata; karmakadānubadate, conciliating; pāṇinirbadate; koñasminkṣetre badate; gahe bibadate, difference of opinion; (one speaks variously to the pupil;) bibadate śiṣyāḥ, close praise; and so on.

byāktabācīsamuccāraṇe, "In the sense of speaking together in clear voices." When vad expresses the joint utterance of words (one speaks out on the treatise with great clarity: illuminating; one speaks agreeably to the workers; one reads Pāṇini: knowledge; in which field does one speak: effort; one disputes in the house) in clear voices together, the taṅ endings occur: saṃprabadate gramyaḥ, and so on.

anorakarmakāt, "After anu, when there is no object." When vad following anu has no object of the action, the taṅ endings occur: anubadate kaṭha kalāpasya, and so on.

bibhāṣā biprālāpe, "Optionally, in the case of contentious speech." In contentious speech, that is, (the people of the village all speak out together,) after vad following vi and pra joined together, taṅ and e-taṅ are made optional: bipra badate mauhūrtāḥ, and so on, or biprabadati mauhūrtāḥ, (the assembly of talkers follows along in disagreement,) and so on.

abāṅgraḥ, "After gṝ following aba." The taṅ endings occur after gṝ following aba: abgirate, and so on.

samapratijñāne, "After sam, in the sense of promising." (The astrologers dispute variously. The astrologers dispute variously.) When gṝ following sam refers to promising, the taṅ endings occur: śataṃ saṃgirte, and so on.

udaścaraḥ sakarmakātra. (One makes fully clear.) "After car following ut, when it has an object." The taṅ endings occur after car following ut when it has an object: gehamuccarati.

samastṛtīyāyuktāt, "After sam, when joined with the third case." (One promises a full hundred.) When car following sam is joined with a word ending in the third case ending, the taṅ endings occur: aśvena saṃcarte, and so on.

dāṇaśca sā cecca turthyarthe, "And after dāṇ, if (one goes about in the house) that has the sense of the fourth case." When dāṇ follows sam, if that word ending in the third case has the sense of the fourth, the taṅ endings occur: dāsyāsaṃprayacchate puṣpamālāṃ, and so on. (One goes about together on horseback.)

upāṅyamaḥ svakaraṇe, "After yam following upa, in the sense of making one's own." When yam following upa refers to making one's own, that is, to taking a bride, the taṅ endings occur: kānyāmupayaccate. (One closely gives the maiden. The maidservant gives a garland of flowers.) And so on.

pibhāṣopayamane, "Optionally, after upayam." After yam preceded by upa, the sic accompanied by taṅ is optionally given the designation kit. On the kit alternative, the m is deleted by the rule beginning "ending in a nasal," and before jhal and the rest, the sic too is lost by the rule beginning "short form." On the alternative where it is not kit, it is simply carried through: upāyata, upāyasātāṃ, upāyasata, and so on; or upāyaṃta, upāyaṃsātāṃ, upāyaṃsata, and so on. rāmaḥ sītāmupāyata.

jñāśrūsmṛdṛśāṃsanaḥ, "After the san of jñā, śrū, smṛ and dṛś." The taṅ endings occur after these, jñā and the rest, when they end in san: jajñāste ṅharmaṃ, śuśūṣate gurūn, susmūrṣate mitraṃ, didṛkṣate janbhūmī, and so on.

anorjñaḥ, "After jñā following anu." (Rāma took Sītā as his bride.) The taṅ endings also occur after jñā ending in san preceded by anu: anujijñāste putraṃ, and so on. (One wishes to know the Dharma. One wishes to listen to the teachers. Of that which is not preceded by a labial. One wishes to remember a friend. One wishes to see one's birthplace.) On this point, the Cāndra explains that the taṅ endings do not apply to jñā ending in san preceded by anu, whereas here it is explained that they do apply, and since the Indian commentary also allows it, giving it as an example, (one wishes to acknowledge the son,) there is a slight disagreement.

bratyāṅbhyāṃ śrubaḥ, "After śru following prati and āṅ." The taṅ endings do not occur after śrū ending in san following prati and āṅ: prati śuśrūṣati, āśuśrūṣati, and so on.

yathāṃpāṭhaṃ, "As read." In the sense of the action, the taṅ endings occur just as the roots are read: bartate, barṅhate, and so on.

bhābā syaso, "After the state and the action." In the sense of the state and of the object of its action, (one wishes to listen in response; one listens fully,) the taṅ endings occur: bhabate, pacate, kurute kaṣaṃ, and so on.

propābhyāṃ yujerayajñapātreṣu, "After yuj following pra and upa, (one abides; one grows,) when not referring to sacrificial vessels." When yuj following pra and upa does not refer to sacrificial vessels, the taṅ endings occur (one obtains; one cooks; one makes a mat): prayuṃkte, one employs thoroughly; upayuṃkte, one applies closely; and so on.

samaḥkṣṇubaḥ, "After kṣū following sam."

The taṅ endings occur after kṣṇu following sam: saṃkṣnute śastraṃ, and so on.

bhujañanabane, "After bhuja, when not in the sense of protecting." The taṅ endings occur after bhuja when it does not mean protecting: odanaṃ bhuṃkte, and so on. When it does mean protecting, the a-taṅ endings, those other than taṅ, are applied: bhunakti pṛthirājā, and so on.

ṇaḥ phalabatāḥ kartare, "After ṇi, (one sharpens the weapon thoroughly,) when the agent possesses the fruit." After what ends in ṇic, the taṅ endings occur when the agent possesses the fruit of the action: kārayate, (one eats food,) hārayate, and so on.

pāṭhe bibhāṣitāt, "After what is read as optional." (The king protects the earth.) After what is read as optional in the root list, the taṅ endings occur when the agent possesses the fruit: pacate, kurute, and so on.

gṛṅhibaṃcyoḥ pralaṃbhane, (one causes to do; one causes to take,) "After gṛdh and pañc, in the sense of thorough obtaining." When gṛdh and pañc ending in ṇi apply to thorough obtaining, the taṅ endings occur: baṭuṃgarṅhayate, māṇabakaṃ bañcayate, and so on. (One cooks. One makes.)

mithyopapāṅāt kṛño ñabhyāse, "After kṛñ with mithyā as an adjoining word, in the sense of repetition." When kṛñ ending in ṇi, with the word mithyā adjoining it, applies to repetition, the taṅ endings occur: padaṃ mithyā kārayate, and so on. (One makes the pupil desirous. One deceives the young brahmin.)

apādbadaḥ, "After pada following apa." After pada following apa, the taṅ endings occur when the agent possesses the fruit: apabaṅte, and so on.

samudāṅbhyo yamoñagranthe, "After yam following sam, ut and āṅ, (one has it done in the wrong place,) when not referring to a text." When yama following sam, ut and āṅ applies to an object that is not a text, and the agent possesses the fruit, the taṅ endings occur: (one slanders) brīhīn saṃyaccate; bhātamuṅyaccote, one lifts the load; rajjumāyaccate, one draws up the rope entirely; and so on.

anupasargāt jñaḥ, "After jñā without a preverb." After jñā not preceded by a preverb, the taṅ endings occur when the agent possesses the fruit: gāṃjānīte, (one gives the grains,) and so on.

bibhāṣopapādena pratiyamāne, "Optionally, when it is understood through an adjoining word." When the agent's possession of the fruit is understood through an adjoining word, the taṅ and a-taṅ endings are made optional: svayajñaṃ yājate, svayajñe yajati, and so on.

iti pāṇinibyākarṇasya sūtāṅhyā (one knows the cattle) tūpasargayogāḥ samāptāḥ. Thus, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinian Grammar, the combinations of roots and preverbs are complete.

With these, (one performs one's own sacrifice,) from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, a set of notes setting down the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinian Grammar, the rough outline of how roots and preverbs are combined, of the distinctions in how the ātmanepada and parasmaipada endings are applied depending on the preverbs, and so on, is for the present complete.

Now I shall explain the procedures for the affixes and so on that are needed in the context of the state (bhāva) and the object (karman).

bhbabakarmaṇi, "In the state and the object." After a root, in the sense of the state and of the object, the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest always occur, and of the ātmanepada endings, only the singular of the first person always occurs. This, however, is said with regard to the case where there is no preverb before the root. When a preverb comes before it, this is not fixed: all nine ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest apply. Not only that, but through the great power of the preverbs, roots without an object come to take one, roots with an object come to be without one, and so on without end.

sarbaṅhātuke yaka, "Yak, before the sārvadhātuka endings." When the sārvadhātuka endings follow, in the sense of the object for roots that take an object, and in the sense of the state for roots without an object, the affix yak occurs. The k serves to prevent guṇa.

By adding yak to bhū, and then adding to bhūya the first person singular ātmanepada endings of laṭ, liṅ, loṭ and laṅ, one gets bhūyate, bhūyata, bhūyatāṃ, abhūyata, and so on. anubhūyate ānandaścaitreṇa tvayā: "Joy is experienced by you, Caitra." anuṅhūyate ānantaścetreṇa māyā. When a preverb is placed before, all the ātmanepada endings are applied: anubhūyate, anubhūyete, anubhāyanhe, and so on.

Since yak does not occur before the ārdhadhātuka endings, in luṅ:

ciṇ bhābakarmaṇoḥ, "Ciṇ, in the state and the object." (Joy is experienced by me, Caitra.) When luṅ is transformed in the sense of the state and the object, with ta following, cli becomes ciṇ. To bhū one adds luṅ; by the rule "cli in luṅ," cli is changed to ciṇ, and ta is added; by the rule "of ac, before what has ñ or ṇ as its marker," vṛddhi is made; and since ta is deleted by the rule "after ciṇ, it is lost," one gets abhābi. When a preverb comes before, all the taṅ endings are applied, so one gets anubhābi. For the dual and the rest:

syasicsīyuṭtāsiṣubhābakarmaṇorubadesehanagrahadṛśāṃcaṇbadiḍā, "In the state and the object, roots in the upadeśa, and han, grah and dṛś, before sya, sic, sīyuṭ and tāsi, optionally take iṭ, as with ciṇ." In the sense of the state and the object, for roots in the upadeśa, that is, roots ending in ac that take iṭ, and for grah, vṛddhi is made optional with the iṭ, as with ciṇ. For roots ending in ac that do not take iṭ, and for han and dṛś, iṭ is optional, and in the alternative where iṭ is given, vṛddhi is always made, as with ciṇ. This applies when any one of the affixes sya, sic, sīyuṭ or tāsi follows. Since bhū ends in ac and takes iṭ, vṛddhi as with ciṇ is made optional. So in the alternative with vṛddhi: anrabhābiṣātāṃ, anvabhābiṣata, and so on; and in the alternative without vṛddhi: anvabhabiṣātāṃ, anvaṅhabiṣata, and so on.

In liṭ: since vuk is given by the rule "vuk in luṅ and liṭ," one gets babhūbe. If a preverb is not placed before: babhūbāte, babhūbire, and so on.

In luṭ: since iṭ is made optional, as with ciṇ, one gets bhābitā, or else bhābitā. When a preverb comes before: anubhābitārau, anubhābitāraḥ, and so on, or anubhabitā, and so on.

Likewise, in the benedictive liṅ: anubhābiṣīṣvṭa, anughābiṣīyāstāṃ, anubhāyiṣīyuḥ, and so on; or else anubharbaṣāṣṭa, and so on. Likewise, in lṛṭ: bhāpiṣyate, and so on, or bhabaiṣyati, and so on. In lṛṅ: anubhābiṣyata, and so on, or anubhabiṣyata, and so on.

To ṣṭuñ add yak; since it is lengthened by the rule beginning "not a kṛt," one gets: laṭ stūyate, liṅ stūyeta, loṭ stūyatāṃ, laṅ asthuyata, and so on. In luṅ, in the singular, since cli is changed to ciṇ, astābi. In the others, since iṭ is made optional: astābiṣātāṃ, asnābiṣata, and so on, or astoṣātāṃ, astoṣata, and so on. In liṭ: tuṣḍube, tuṣḍubāte, tuṣḍubire, and so on. In luṭ, since iṭ is made optional: stābitā, and so on, or stotā, and so on. Likewise, in the benedictive liṅ: stābiṣīṣṭa, and so on, or gtoṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: stābiṣyate, and so on, or stoṣyata, and so on. In lṛṅ: astābiṣyata, and so on, or astoṣata, and so on.

To smṛ, "in the sense of remembering," add yak; since guṇa is made by the rule beginning "arti and what has a conjunct at the beginning," one gets: laṭ smaryate, liṅ smaryeta, loṭ smaryatāṃ, laṅ asmaryata, and so on. In luṅ: asmāti, asmāriṣātāṃ, and so on, or else asmṛṣātlaṃ, and so on. In liṭ: sasmare, sasmarāte, sasmarire, and so on. In luṭ, since iṭ is made optional: smāritā, and so on, or smartā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, since iṭ is made optional: smārṣīṭaṃ, and so on, or smraṃṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ: smāriṣyate, and so on, or smarṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in lṛṅ: asmāriṣyata, and so on, or asmarṣyata, and so on.

To kṛñ add yak. By the rule "riṅ before śa, yak and liṅ," ṛ is changed to riṅ, and it is lengthened by the rule beginning "not a kṛt." Adding the sārvadhātuka endings to kīrya, one gets: laṭ kīryate, liṅ kīryeta, loṭ kṅiryatāṃ, laṅ akīryāta, and so on. In luṅ, in the singular, akāri; in the others, since iṭ is made optional: akāriṣātāṃ, and so on, or akraṃbātāṃ, and so on. In liṭ: cakre, cakrāte, and so on. In luṭ: kṣaritā, and so on, or kartā, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, since iṭ is made optional: kāriṣīṣta, and so on, or kṛṣīṣṭa, and so on. In lṛṭ too, since iṭ is made optional: kāriṣyate, and so on, or karṣyate, and so on. Likewise, in lṛṅ: akāriṣyata, and so on, or akarṣyata, and so on.

To sraṃs add yak; since the n is deleted by the rule beginning "of what does not have i as its marker," one gets: laṭ sresyate, liṅ srasyeta, loṭ srasyatāṃ, laṅ asrasyata, and so on. In the singular of luṅ, asrasi; in the remaining forms, since iṭ is given: asraṃsiṣātāṃ, asraṃsiṣata, and so on. In liṭ, since the n is deleted: sasrase, sasrasāte, sasrasire, sasrasiṣe, and so on. In luṭ, since iṭ is given: sraṃsitā, and so on. Likewise, in the remaining ones: benedictive liṅ sraṃsiṣāṣṭi, lṛṭ sraṃsiṣyate, lṛṭ sraṃsiṣyate, lṛṅ asraṃsiṣyata, and so on.

To nanṅhi add yak; since num is given by the rule beginning "what has i as its marker," one gets: nanṅhyate, nanṅhyata, nanṅhrahāṃ, ananṅhyata, and so on. In luṅ: ananṅhi, ananṅhiṣātāṃ, ananḍhiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: nananṅhe, nananṅhāte, and so on. In the remaining ones: luṭ nanṅhitā, benedictive liṅ nanṅhīṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ nanṅhiṣyate, lṛṅ ananṅhiṣyata, and so on.

To yaja add yak; since it is changed to saṃprasāraṇa by the rule beginning "baci, svapa," one gets: laṭ ijyate, liṅ ijyita, loṭ ijyatāṃ, laṅ aijyata, and so on. In luṅ, in the singular, since cli is changed to ciṇ, ayāji. In the dual and the rest, since sic is elided by the rule beginning with jhal, j is changed to ṣ by the rule beginning "braśca bhasja," and so on: ayakṣātāṃ, ayakṣata, and so on. In liṭ, the abhyāsa is changed to saṃprasāraṇa by the rule beginning "of both," and the latter part too is made saṃprasāraṇa by the rule beginning "baci, sapi": īje, ījāti, and so on. In luṭ, j becomes ṣ by the rule beginning "braśca bhrasṛsa," and the form is completed by the rule beginning "ṣṭu with ṣṭu": yalṭā, yaṣṭāro, and so on. In the benedictive liṅ, j becomes ṣ, and the form is completed by the rule that changes ṣ and ḍh entirely to k before s, and so on: akṣīṣṭa, yakṣīyāstāṃ, and so on. Likewise, in lṛṭ and lṛṅ: yakṣyate, ayakṣyata, and so on.

To śīṅ, yak. Since it is changed to ayaṅ by the rule "ayaṅ before what has k as its marker," one gets: laṭ śayyate, liṅ śayyeta, loṭ śayyatāṃ, laṅ uśayyata, and so on. In the singular of luṅ, since cli is changed to ciṇ, aśāyi. In the dual and the rest, iṭ is given, and since vṛddhi is made optional as with ciṇ: aśāyiṣātāṃ, and so on, or aśayiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: śiśye, śiśyate, and so on. In luṭ, since iṭ is given and vṛddhi is made optional as with ciṇ: śāyitā, and so on, or śayitā, and so on. Likewise, in the remaining ones: śāyiṣīṣṭa, benedictive liṅ śayiṣīṣṭa; śayiṣyate, lṛṭ śvayiṣyate; aśāyiṣyata, lṛṅ aśayiṣyata; and so on.

To tanu add yak.

tanoterya ki, "Of tanoti, before yak." When yak follows, the final of tanoti is optionally changed to āt: tāyate, laṭ tanyate; tāyeta, liṅ tanyeta; tāyatāṃ, loṭ tānyatāṃ; atāyata, laṅ atanyata; and so on. In luṅ: atāni, ataniṣātāṃ, and so on. In liṭ, by the rule beginning "elision of the abhyāsa": teni, tenāte, and so on. In the remaining ones: luṭ tanitā, benedictive liṅ taniṣīṣta, lṛṅ taniṣyate, lṛṅ ataniṣyata, and so on.

To jan, yak. By the rule "optionally before ya," changing the final to āt or not changing it is made optional, so: jāyate, laṭ janiti; jāyeta, liṭ janyeta; jāyatāṃ, loṭ janyatāṃ; ajāyata, laṅ ajanyata; and so on. In luṅ, since vṛddhi is not made: ajani, ajaniṣātāṃ, ajaniṣata, and so on. In liṭ there is reduplication; the penultimate (upadhā) is deleted by the rule beginning "gam, han, jan," and since n is changed to ñ by the rule "ścu, of stu," one gets jajñā, jajñīte, jajñire, and so on. In the remaining ones, since iṭ is given: luṭ janitā, benedictive liṅ janiṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ janiṣyate, lṛṅ ajaniṣyata, and so on.

Adding yak to tapa: laṭ tapyate, liṅ tapyeta, loṭ tapyatāṃ, laṅ atabyata, and so on.

tapoñanutape ca, "Of tapa, and also of anutapa." The cli following tapa, and following tapa preceded by anu, is not changed to ciṇ. So, completing the form with the elision of sic by the rule "after jhal, before jhal," and so on: anutapta, anutapsātāṃ, anutabsata, and so on. In liṭ: tepe, tepāte, and so on. In the remaining ones: luṭ taptā, benedictive liṅ tapsīṣṭa, lṛṭ tapsyate, lṛṅ atabsyata, and so on.

To ḍudāñ, yak. Since it is changed to īt by the rule beginning "ghu, mā, sthā," one gets dīyete, dīyeta, dīyatāṃ, adīyata, and so on.

ātoyukacinkṛtoḥ, "Before cin and kṛt, yuk after āt." When the ciṇ into which cli has been changed, or a kṛt affix or the like that has ñ or ṇ as its marker, follows, the augment yuk occurs after a root ending in āt. The k serves to show its position, and the u is for pronunciation. In the singular of luṅ, since this sūtra gives the augment yuk, one gets adāyi. In the dual and the rest, iṭ is made optional. In the alternative where iṭ is given, yuk is given as with ciṇ: adāyiṣātāṃ, adāyiṣata, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ, since it is changed to īt by the rule "of sthā and ghu, also īt," one gets adiṣātāṃ, adīṣata, and so on. In liṭ: dade, dadāde, dadire, and so on. In the remaining ones, since iṭ is made optional: dāyitā, luṭ dātā; dāyiṣīṣṭa, benedictive dāsīṣṭa; dāyiṣyate, lṛṭ dāsyate; ādāyiṣyate, lṛṅ adāsyata; and so on.

Adding yak to han, "in the sense of harming," one gets: laṭ hanyate, liṅ hanyeta, laṭ hanyatā, laṅ ahanyata, and so on. By the rule "of the h of hanta, before what has ñ or ṇ as its marker," h becomes gh, and since cli is changed to ciṇ, in the first person singular of luṅ one gets aghāni. In the dual and the rest, iṭ is made optional. In the alternative with iṭ, since the procedure is carried out as with ciṇ: aghāniṣātāṃ, aghāniṣata, and so on. In the alternative without iṭ, since the n is deleted by the rule beginning "ending in a nasal": ahasātaṃ, ahasata, and so on. In liṭ: jaghne, jaghnāte, jaghnire, and so on. In the remaining ones: ghāntā, luṭ hantā; ghāniṣīṣṭa, benedictive liṅ haṃsīṣṭa; ghāniṣyate, lṛṭ haniṣyate; aghāniṣyata, lṛṅ ahaniṣyata; and so on.

To graha add yak. Since it is changed to saṃprasāraṇa by the rule beginning "grahi, jyā," one gets: laṭ gṛhyate, liṅ gṛhyeta, loṭ gṛhyatāṃ, laṅ agṛhyata, and so on. In the singular of luṅ, agrāhi. In the dual and the rest, iṭ is given, and since vṛddhi is made optional as with ciṇ: abrāhiṣātāṃ, and so on, or agrahiṣātāṃ, and so on. In liṭ: jagṛhe, jagṛhāte, jagṛhire, and so on. In the remaining ones: grāhitva, luṭ grahitā; grāhiṣāṣṭi, benedictive liṅ grahiṣiṣṭa; grāhiṣyate, lṛṭ grahiṣyate; agrāhiṣyata, lṛṅ agrahiṣyata; and so on.

Adding yak to dṛśa, one gets: laṭ dṛśyate, liṅ dṛśyata, loṭ dṛśyatāṃ, laṅ adṛśyata, and so on. In the singular of luṅ, adārśi. In the dual and the rest, since iṭ is made optional: adārśiṣātāṃ, and so on; and in the alternative without iṭ, ś becomes ṣ by the rule beginning "braśca," and by the rule beginning "k before s," one gets adṛkṣātāṃ, and so on. In liṭ: dadṛśe, dadṛśāte, and so on. In the remaining ones: dārśitā, laṭ darṣḍu; dārśiṣīṣṭa, benedictive liṅ dṛkṣīṣṭa; dārśiṣyate, lṛṭ darkṣyate; adārśiṣyata, lṛṅ adarkṣyata; and so on.

Adding yak to śamu, one gets: laṭ śamyate, liṅ śamyeta, loṭ śamyatāṃ, laṅ aśamyata, and so on. In luṅ:

ciṇṇamulordīrghānyatarasyāṃ, "Before ciṇ and ṇamul, optionally long." When ciṇ or ṇamul follows, the penultimate (upadhā) of roots that bear the designation of having m as their marker is optionally lengthened: aśāmi, aśami. In the dual and the rest, since iṭ is given: aśamiṣātāṃ, and so on. In liṭ: śeme, śemāte, and so on. In the remaining ones, since iṭ is given: luṭ śamitā, benedictive liṅ śamiṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ śamiṣyate, lṛṅ aśamiṣyate, and so on.

Likewise, for damu: laṭ damyate, liṅ damyete, loṭ damyatāṃ, laṅ adamyata, and so on; and in the singular of luṅ, adāmi, adami. In the dual and the rest, since iṭ is given: damiṣātāṃ, damiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: deme, demāte, demiri, and so on. In the remaining ones, since iṭ is given: luṭ damitā, benedictive liṅ damiṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ damiṣyata, lṛṅ adamiṣyata, and so on.

For kamu: laṭ kamyate, liṅ kamyeta, loṭ kamyatāṃ, laṅ akamyata, and so on. In the singular of luṅ, by the rule "before ciṇ and ṇamul, optionally long": akāmi, akami. In the dual and the rest, since iṭ is given: akamiṣātāṃ, akamiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: cakame, cakamāte, and so on. In the remaining ones, since iṭ is given: luṭ kamitā, benedictive liṅ kamiṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ kamaṣyate, lṛṅ akamiṣyata, and so on.

Giving yak to baṅha, one gets baṅhyate, baṅhyeta, baṅhyatāṃ, abaṅhyata, and so on. In luṅ, since vṛddhi is not made: abaṅhi, abaṅhiṣātāṃ, abaṅhiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: babaṅhe, babaṅhāte, babaṅhire, and so on. In the remaining ones: luṭ baṅhitā, benedictive liṅ baṅhiṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ baṅhiṣyate, lṛṅ abaṅhiṣyata, and so on.

To jāgṛ add yak. By the rule "riṅ before śa, yak and liṅ," ṛ is changed to riṅ, and since it is lengthened by the rule beginning "not a kṛt," one gets: laṭ jāgrīyate, liṅ jāgrīyeta, loṭ jāgrīyatāṃ, laṅ jāgrīyata, and so on. In the singular of luṅ, ajāgāri. In the dual and the rest, iṭ is given, and since vṛddhi is made optional as with ciṇ: ajāgāriṣātāṃ, and so on, or ajāgariṣātāṃ, and so on, or ajāgariṣātāṃ, and so on. In liṭ, by adding ām: jāgarāṃ cakre, and so on. In the remaining ones: jāgāritā, luṭ jāgaritā; jāgāriṣīṣā, benedictive liṅ jāgariṣīṣṭa; jāgāriṣyate, lṛṭ jāgariṣyate; ajāgāriṣyata, lṛṅ ajāgariṣyata; and so on.

To bhañjū, yak. Since the n is deleted by the rule beginning "of what does not have i as its marker," one gets: laṭ bhajyate, liṅ bhajyeta, loṭ bhajyatāṃ, laṅ abhajyata, and so on. In luṅ:

bhaṃjeściṇi, "Of bhañji, before ciṇ." The letter n of bhañji is optionally elided when ciṇ follows: abhāji, abhañji. In the dual and the rest, since iṭ is given: abhañjiṣātāṃ, and so on. In liṭ, since the n is deleted: babhaje, babhajāte, babhajīre, and so on. In the remaining ones, since iṭ is given: luṭ bhañjitā, benedictive liṅ bhañjiṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ bhañjiṣyate, lṛṅ abhañjiṣyata, and so on.

Adding yak to labha, one gets: laṭ labhyate, liṅ labhyeta, loṭ labhyatāṃ, laṅ alabhyata, and so on.

bibhāṣā ciṇṇamuloḥ, "Optionally before ciṇ and ṇamul." When ciṇ or ṇamul follows, the augment num optionally occurs for labha: alabhi, alābhi. In the dual and the rest, by the rule "car before khar," bh is changed to p, and so on: alabsātāṃ, alapsāta, and so on. In liṭ: lebhe, lebhāti, and so on.

In the remaining ones, since bh is changed to p by the rule "car before khar," one gets: luṭ lab, benedictive liṅ lapsīṣaṭa, lṛṭ lapsyate, lṛṭ alapsyata, and so on. Since the commentary explains that when a preverb comes before, num always occurs for labha when ciṇ or ṇamul follows, one gets prālaṃbhi, and so on.

karmabatkarmaṇā tulyakriyaḥ, "Where the action is the same as with the object, it is like the object." "The action is the same" means this: when the thing that is the object of an action is accomplished easily, without requiring any great effort on the part of the agent, that is called the object together with the agent. For example, as in bhiṅyate kāṣṭhaṃ svayame, it is as if the sense of the agent were also complete within the very thing that is acted upon. laṭ bhiṅyate, liṅ bhidyeta, loṭ bhiṅyatāṃ, laṅ abhiṅyata, and so on. In luṅ: abhedi, abhitsātāṃ, abhitsata, and so on. In liṭ: bibhide, bibhidāte, and so on. (The wood breaks into pieces of its own accord.) In the remaining ones: luṭ bhettā, benedictive liṅ bhedsīṣṭa, lṛṭ bhetsyate, lṛṅ abhetsyata, and so on.

Adding yak to paca, one gets: laṭ pacyate, liṅ pacyeta, loṭ pacyatāṃ, laṅ apacyata, and so on. In luṅ: apāci, apakṣātāṃ, apakṣata, and so on. In liṭ: pece, becāte, and so on. In the remaining ones: luṭ paktā, benedictive liṅ pakṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ pakṣyata, lṛṅ abakṣyata, and so on.

Adding yak to sṛja, one gets: laṭ sṛjyate, liṅ sṛjyeta, loṭ sṛjyatāṃ, laṅ asṛjyata, and so on. In luṅ: asarji, asṛkaṣṅataṃ, asṛkṣata, and so on. In liṭ: sasṛje, sasṛjāte, and so on. In the remaining ones: luṭ sarṣṭā, benedictive liṅ sṛkṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ sarkṣyate, lṛṅ asarkṣyata, and so on.

kuṣirañjoḥ prācāeśyanparasmaibadaṃ ca, "For kuṣi and rañja, according to the Easterners, śyan, and also the parasmaipada." For kuṣi and rañja, in the sense of the object together with the agent, the Eastern teachers hold that śyan is applied, and the parasmaipada endings of laṭ and the rest also optionally occur: kuṣyati, laṭ kuṣhate; kuṣyeta, liṅ kuṣyeta; kuṣyatu, loṭ kuṣyatāṃ; akuṣyata, laṅ akuṣyata; and so on. In luṅ: akoṣi, akoṣiṣātāṃ, akoṣiṣata, and so on. In liṭ: cukuṣe, cukuṣāte, cukuṣāri, and so on. In the remaining ones: luṭ koṣitā, benedictive liṅ koṣiṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ koṣiṣyate, lṛṅ akoṣiṣyata, and so on.

Likewise, to rañja, śyan; since the n is deleted by the rule beginning "of what does not have i as its marker," one gets rajyati, rajyate, and so on. In luṅ: araṃkṣātāṃ, araṃkṣata, and so on. In liṭ: rarañje, rarañjāte, and so on. In the remaining ones: luṭ raṃktā, benedictive liṅ raṃkṣīṣṭa, lṛṭ raṃkṣyate, lṛṅ araṃkṣḍyata, and so on.

acaḥ karmakartari, "After ac, in the object-agent." When the cli following a root ending in ac is applied in the sense of the object together with the agent, it optionally becomes ciṇ before the ta of luṅ: akāri; or else, since sic is deleted by the rule beginning "short form," akṛta.

na ruṅhaḥ, "Not after ruṅh." The cli following ruṅh, in the sense of the object together with the agent, does not become ciṇ. Cli becomes sic; by the rule "after jhal, before jhal," sic is deleted; by the rule beginning "jhaṣ," t becomes dh; and since dh is changed to d by the rule beginning "jhal," one gets aruṅdha, and so on. Since the commentary explains that for paca and duha, roots with two objects, cli optionally does not become ciṇ, one gets apakta, aṅhugṅha, and so on.

na duhasnuhanamāṃ yakciṇo, "Not yak and ciṇ for duh, snuh and nam." For duh, snuh and nam, in the sense of the state, the object and so on, yak, the change of cli to ciṇ, and the like are not made: ṅhugdhe, snuhate, namate, and so on.

ṇiśranthiganthibrūñātmanepaṅākarmakāṇīyakaciṇo na, "Not yak and ciṇ for ṇi, śranthi, granthi and brūñ, taking the ātmanepada, in the object." For roots ending in ṇic, and for śrantha, grartha and brūñ, yak and ciṇ do not occur in the sense of the object, and the ātmanepada endings of laṭ and the rest are applied: kārayate, śraṣṭhīte, grathnīte, brūte, and so on.

The commentary quotes: kṝgṝśriñbhūṣārthebhyaḥ sannñācca yakaciṇo na, "Not yak and ciṇ for kṝ, gṝ and śriñ, for those meaning adornment, and also for what ends in san." Yak and ciṇ do not occur after kṝ, gṝ and śṛña, after roots meaning adornment, or after roots ending in san either: kīrate, gīrate, śrayate, taṃsate, cikīrṣate, and so on.

The verse that occurs in the commentary on the distinction between roots without an object and roots with an object is as follows: lajjāsattāsthitijāgaraṇaṃ braṅṅhikṣayabhayabhayajībitamaraṃ, śayanakriḍāruci dīpkyarthaṃ ṅhātubaṇaṃtamakarmakamāhuḥ. Rendered into Tibetan, this is: Shame, existence, (one adorns,) abiding, and wakefulness, Growth, excellence, perishing, and living, Lying down, play, desire, and the sense of blazing: The groups of roots with these meanings are said to be without an object. That is to say: taking the case where no preverb precedes, roots having the meanings of these twelve categories, shame and the rest, are without an object, and the others are called roots with an object.

iti pāṇibyākarṇasya sūtrāṅbhābakarmanaḥ samāphāḥ. Thus, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinian Grammar, the sections on the state and the object are complete.

With these, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, a set of notes setting down the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the rough account of the affixes, procedures and so on for the sense of the state and the object is for the present complete.

Now I shall set out the general explanations of the domains in which laṭ and the rest apply.

abhijñābacane lṛṭ, "Lṛṭ, when there is a word of direct knowing." When a word expressing direct knowing is used with reference to something that happened, but not today, lṛṭ occurs. To bal, lṛṭ; by the rule "of s, before an ārdhadhātuka," s is changed to t: smarasi kṛṣā mathudāyāṃ badsyamaḥ.

na yadi, "Not with yat." When the word yat is used with reference to something that happened, not today, in an expression of recollection by direct knowing, lṛṭ does not occur: abhijānāsi kṛṣṇa yadva zhe 'bhuṃjmahi.

bibhāṣā sākāṃkṣe, "Optionally, when it expects something further."

When an intervening action is expected, (Do you remember, Kṛṣṇa, that we stayed in Mathurā?) and a word of recollection is used, lṛṭ optionally occurs, whether or not yat is present: lṛṭ smarasi debadatta bane batsyāmaḥ; laṅ smarsi debadatta bana yabasām. To bhūjā, laṅ. (Do you truly know, Kṛṣṇa, that we ate in the forest?)

paroñakṣe leṭ, "Liṭ for what is out of sight." When something that happened, not today, is expressed in the domain of what is accomplished out of sight, liṭ occurs: rāmo rājyaṃ cakāra. (Do you remember, Devadatta, that we stayed in the forest? Do you remember, Devadatta, that we stayed in the forest?)

The commentary quotes: utmaphuruṣe beecittyā baroñakṣaṃ, "The first person of the out-of-sight past, when the mind is impaired." When, with the mind impaired, something that happened out of sight is expressed, the first person of liṭ (Rāma ruled the kingdom.) occurs: suptoñahaṃ kila bilalāpa. Liṭ: since the commentary says that liṭ also occurs when censure is expressed, one has nāhaṃ kaliṅhaṃ jagāma.

liṭ ha śaśāto rliṅca, "After ha and śaśvat, also liṅ." When the words ha and śaśvat are used, laṅ occurs in the domain of liṅ, and liṭ also occurs: laṅ hā (Being asleep, I babbled nonsense.) karota; liṭ ha cakāra; laṅ śaśvadakarota; liṭ śaśvaccakāra.

praśne (I do not go to the Kali age.) cāsannakāle, "Also in a genuine question, in the time of remaining." In the sense of a genuine question too, when the time of abiding or remaining is expressed, laṅ occurs, and liṭ also occurs: laṅ ā (one did it wondrously) gacchat kiṃ; liṭ jagā (one did it of old) ma ka.

lṛṭ sme, "With sma, lṛṭ." When the word sma is used, laṭ occurs in the domain of lṛṭ: yajatisma yuṅhiṣṭhira. (Yudhiṣṭhira performed a sacrifice.)

aparoñakṣe ca, "Also for what is not out of sight." Even when something not out of sight is expressed, when the word sma (where does one go?) is used, laṭ occurs: brulīṭ; brabīti sma drahmā. (Brahmā speaks.)

nanoo pṛṣṭaprati bacane, "With nanu, in answering a question." When nanu is used and applies in the sense of answering a question, laṭ occurs: nanu karoti babhoḥ.

nanvorbibhāṣā, "Optionally after na and nu." When the separate particles na and nu are used, in the sense of what has happened, laṭ optionally occurs: ahaṃ na karomi; laṭ, ahaṃnākārṣaṃ; luṅ, luṭ, ahaṃ nu karomi; luṅ, ahaṃ nvakārmi.

buri lubhāsme, "With pur, when there is no sma, also luṅ." (Done in the former time of Viṣṇu.) When pur is used without the word sma, in expressing what has happened, laṭ occurs, and luṅ also occurs: basanti ha purāchātrāḥ; abātsu (I did not do it) raṃ ha purāchātrāḥ. When sma is used, (I did it by turns,) luṅ does not occur: luṭ yajati sma purṣa.

yābatpurānibatayorlaṭ, "After yāvat and purā as particles, laṭ." When yāvat and purā are used in the sense of particles, (Formerly the pupils stayed here.) in expressing what is to come, laṭ occurs: yāpaṅṅhuṃkte; laṭ purā bhuṃkte.

bibhāṣā kadākanyoḥ, "Optionally after kadā and karhi." (One performed a sacrifice formerly.) When the words kadā and karhi are used, in the sense of the future, laṭ optionally occurs: laṭ kadā bhuṃkte, lṛṭ kādā bhokṣyete; laṭ karhakhe, lṛṭ karhi bhokṣyate; laṭ karha bhuṃkhe, lṛṭ karhi bhokṣute.

kimbṛttelibsāyāṃ, "When kim is applied, in desire." (Who will eat? Heard before.) When kim is applied, that is, when it is used with kim itself or with words ending in a kim affix, and desire is expressed, laṭ occurs for the future: kim pi (on what will one feed?) praṃ bhojayisi (on what does one feed?); laṭ katara bipraṃ bhojayasi, and so on; or lṛṭ bhojyiṣyate pipraṃ kima.

lipsāsān siṅṅhau ca, "Also in the accomplishment of what is desired." When a future is expressed in which the thing desired is accomplished, laṭ also occurs: laṭ yoñannadatāti; lṛṭ yoñannadāsyati.

loṭrthamkṣaṇe ca, (bhuja with ṇi. The brahmin who wishes to eat what?) "Also in characterizing the sense of loṭ." (The brahmin who wishes to eat what?) When a characteristic of a future that has the sense of loṭ is expressed, laṭ also occurs: laṭ kṛṣṇaḥ bhuṃkte (May Kṛṣṇa eat!); loṭ kṛṣṇa bhuṃkhāṃ.

bartamānasāmīpye bartamāna (who will give food?) badvā, "In proximity to the present, optionally as in the present." In the domain near the present, that is, for both a past that is not long gone and a future that is not long off, the present affixes, laṭ and the rest, optionally occur as in the present: laṭ kadā gacchati; laṅ yadā gacchati; or else luṅ kaṅā gacchata; lṛṭ yadrva gamiṣyati.

āśaṃsāyāṃbhātabacca, "In doubt, optionally as in the past." When the action is doubtful, the past affixes optionally occur also in the sense of the future and the present: luṅ debenā barṣīta; or else luṭ debena barṭhati; (Where does it come? Where does it go?) lṛṭ deben parṣiṣyate. (Where does it come? Where does one go?)

kṣiprabacane lṛṭ, "Lṛṭ, when quickness is expressed." For a future in which quickness is expressed, lṛṭ alone occurs: lṛṭ āyāsyati śīghraṃ. (Will the god send rain, or is it about to send rain? The god sent rain.)

āśaṃsābacani (The god will send rain.) liṅ, "Liṅ, when doubt is expressed." For a future in which doubt is expressed, liṅ alone occurs: gurūpeāta. Since the commentary says that when ut and api are used, (one will obtain; in parting,) lṛṅ occurs in the domain of liṅ, one has utbhokṣye, apyabhokṣye.

garhāyāṃ lañaḍ pijātāoḥ, "After api and jātu, laṭ in censure." When api and jātu are used and censure (liṅ, to iṇ, "to go," preceded by u. One will come near the teacher.) is expressed, laṭ occurs in all three times: laṭ api jāyāṃ tyajasi; laṭ jātu gāṇikā (the iṭ of lṛṅ; very; even food) mādtse.

bibhāṣā kathamlipca, "With katham, optionally liṅ as well." When the word katham is used and censure is expressed, laṭ occurs, and liṅ also optionally occurs: liṅ kathaṃ ṅharmaṃ tyajeḥ; laṭ kathaṃ ṅharmaṃ tyajasi. The commentary (or even abandons; at some time one takes a courtesan) says that when the word katham is present and censure is expressed, lṛṅ always occurs for the future: kathanāma tatra bhabāna ṅharmaṃ atyakṣyata. (Laṭ: How indeed would you abandon the Dharma there?)

kimbritte liṅlṛṭoo, "Liṅ and lṛṭ when kim (how one abandons the Dharma) is applied."

When kim is applied, that is, when it is used with kim itself or with words ending in a kim affix, and censure is expressed, liṅ and lṛṭ occur: katarobhapān nideta; liṅ katarobhabāna nidiṣyati.

kimkilāshyartheṣu lṛṭ, "Lṛṭ with kiṃkila and with words meaning 'exists.'" When the word kiṃkila or words meaning existence are used, lṛṭ occurs in all three times: kiṃ kila tpaṃ śūdrānnaṃ bhokṣyase; asti śūdrīṃ gamikṣyasi; bhabatiṅ būdrīṃ gamikṣyasi; biṅyate śrudrī gamikṣyar (What, do you disgrace yourself?) ti.

jātuyaṅorliṅ, "After jātu and yaṅ, liṅ." When jātu and yaṅ are used, liṅ occurs in censure in all three times: jātu tatra bhabān śūdraṃ yāja (How shocking that you would eat a śūdra's food! lṛṭ) yeta; yattatratvi (Is it so? You will go to a śūdra woman!) śūdraṃ yājayeta.

yadāyaryoryoge ca, "Also when yadā and yadi are used." When the words yadā and yadi are used too, and censure is expressed, liṅ occurs: yadā tvaṃ śūdraṃ (At some time you perform a sacrifice there for a śūdra!) yājayet; yadi tvaṃ śūdraṃ yājayet.

yacca yatrayoḥ, (That you perform a sacrifice there for a śūdra!) "Of yacca and yatra." When yacca and yatra are used too, and censure is expressed, liṅ occurs: yacca tatra bhabān bṛṣalaṃ yājayet; yatra tatra hvaṃ bṛṣalaṃ (Whenever you perform a sacrifice for a śūdra! Whenever you perform a sacrifice for a śūdra!) yājayit.

citrīkarṇe ca, "Also in expressing wonder." When yacca and yatra are present and wonder is expressed, liṅ occurs: (That you even perform a sacrifice there for a śūdra! Wherever it is, you perform a sacrifice there for a śūdra!) yacca tvaṃ śūdraṃ yājayet; yatra tvaṃ śūdraṃ yājayeta.

śeṣe lṛḍ yadau, "Lṛṭ in the remaining cases, and where there is no yadi." "The remaining cases" means: otherwise than when yacca and yatra or yadi are used, when wonder is expressed, lṛṭ occurs: aścāryāṃ anṅhanāma kṛṣṇa drakṣyati; āścaryaṃ (That you even perform a sacrifice for a śūdra! Wherever it is, you perform a sacrifice for a śūdra!) baṅhiro nāma śaśḍa śroṣyati.

utabyoḥ samarthayorliṅ, "After ut and api, liṅ in the sense of capability." When ut and api are used and the sense of capability is expressed, (Wonderful! The one called blind sees Kṛṣṇa. Wonderful! The one called deaf hears the sound.) liṅ occurs: uta hanyāta deetyaṃ hari (Hari destroys the asuras); api hanyata teetyaṃ hari.

liṅ nimitte kṛyātipattoo ghūteñ nityaṃ lṛṅ, "In the domain of liṅ, when the action has failed, and in what has happened, always lṛṅ." In the domain of liṅ, when the action has failed and a past time is expressed, lṛṅ always occurs: kamo meñabhokṣyata bhabān.

saṃbhābaneñalamiti cetsihñāprayige, "In possibility, if alam, though implied, is not used." When possibility is expressed, in the domain of the sense of alam, if the word alam itself, though implied, is not used, liṅ does not occur: api giriśirasābhiṃdyata.

bibñāṣāṅhātoosaṃbhābanabaniñyadi, (Please protect my work.) "For a root, when possibility is expressed and it is not with yad, optionally." When possibility is expressed for a root and the word yad is not used, liṅ occurs, and optionally lṛṭ: liṅ bhuñjīta bhabān; lṛṭ bhokṣyate bhabāna.

hetuhetumatorliṅ, (He could pierce even a mountain with his head.) "Liṅ for the cause and for what has the cause." When engagement in an action involving a cause and what has that cause is expressed, liṅ occurs, and optionally lṛṭ: buṅṅhāyanamet sukhaṃ yāyāt; buṅṅhāyanmet sukhaṃ yāsyati. (You ate. You will eat.)

icchārthiṣu liṅloṭoo, "Liṅ and loṭ for meanings of desire." When meanings of desire are expressed for a root, liṅ and loṭ (By bowing to the Buddha one obtained happiness. By bowing to the Buddha one will obtain happiness.) occur: bhuṃjīta bhabān; bhuṃktāṃ bhabān.

liṅ ca, liṅ ca, "Also liṅ." In the sense of desire, when an action sharing its agent with the desiring is expressed, liṅ also occurs: bhuṃjīta yacchati.

icchartheṅhyo bibhāṣā bartamāne, "After roots meaning desire, optionally in the present." When meanings of desire are expressed, (You will eat.) not only does laṭ occur in the present, but liṅ also optionally occurs: bhabān iccheta; bhabān icchati.

preeṣānujñāprāptakāleṣu kraṃtyāgca, (Having eaten, give.) "In commanding, permitting, and when the time has come, also the kṛt affixes." In commanding, permitting, and when the time has come, loṭ occurs, and the kṛt and other affixes also occur: grāmaṃ gacchatu (Go to the village! Come as you wish.); kartuma cchadu (Do as you wish!); eba kuru (Do it thus!); kaṭa kuru.

arhe kṛtyatṛcaśca, "In worthiness, also the kṛt affixes and tṛc." When worthiness is expressed, liṅ occurs, and the kṛt and other affixes, and tṛc, also occur: tvaṃ kanyāṃ baheḥ.

śakilihu, "In capability, also liṅ." When capability is expressed, liṅ occurs, and the kṛt and other affixes also (Make a grass mat!) occur: tvaṃ bhāraṃ baheḥ.

samucchayeñnyatarasyāṃ, "Optionally in aggregation." When aggregation or combination is expressed, (The maiden is fit for you.) loṭ occurs, and optionally the kṛt and other affixes also occur.

samucchaye sāmānyabacanasya, "Of a common expression, in aggregation." When an aggregation (The load is fit for you.) expressed in common is conveyed, loṭ also occurs, and many others besides, laṭ and the rest: loṭ yāhi; laṭ yāta; luṅ ayāsīt; lṛṭ yāsyati. Since the commentary says that in cases such as repetition by doubling, where loṭ does not apply, laṭ remains as it is, one has punpunaḥ pibati, punpunaḥ khādati, punapun svasti, and so on.

iti pāṇinibyākarṇasya sūtrāta (May one obtain. One obtains. One has obtained. One will obtain.) kālārthabartāḥ samāptāḥ. Thus, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the applications in the sense of time are complete. (One drinks again and again. One eats again and again. Again and again may there be well-being!)

With these, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, a set of notes setting down the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinian Grammar, the rough account of the domains in which laṭ and the rest apply, in the sense of the distinctions of time, past, future, present and so on, has been given. As the commentary says: dtratūnāmanntatācca nānārthatvācca sarbathā, api ṅhātumaśakyamityalamākhyātakhyātakhyāpane. And also: The roots are without end, And their meanings are various in every way; Making the roots manifest according to one's ability, The conjugation is fully explained. Since this is what it says, the meaning is: single roots apply to many meanings, many roots apply to a single meaning, and so on, without end; and of what must be clearly stated about their meanings, the matters of the conjugation have been fully explained in keeping with one's own ability.

Thus, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, a set of notes setting down the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the sūtras of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinian Grammar, together with the commentary composed by the great master Rāmacandra, the chapters on the conjugation, which set out in detail how the later groups of endings, the ten groups, laṭ and the rest, or the hundred and eighty, ti and the rest, are applied to roots, and so on, are for the present complete.

With respectful body, speech and mind, I bow to the gurus and to the hosts of Dharma protectors and guardians.

Having thus set out the procedures of the conjugation, by which roots are formed into verbs, I shall now explain the domains of application, the procedures, the examples and so on of the affixes, kṛt and the rest, by which roots are formed into nouns.

ṅhātoḥ, "After a root." These affixes to be explained, kṛt and the rest, tavya and so on, occur after a root, and they are called the affixes that form roots into nouns.

tatropapadaṃ saptamīsthaṃ, "There, what stands in the seventh is the adjoining word." The word standing in the seventh that comes before that which has a kṛt or other affix, that is, the word expressing the sense of the seventh case, is given the designation "adjoining word" (upapada).

bāsarūpoñastriyāṃ, "Optionally, what is not of the same form, except in the feminine." A general affix that is not of the same form as an affix governed by a special rule, one that is not an affix forming the feminine, nor of the same form as what has already been formed, optionally occurs even in the domain of the special rule.

kṛtyāḥ prāṅṇvulaḥ, "Before ṇvul, the kṛt affixes." Those affixes that come before the affix ṇvul, which is given below, and not only those but all the noun-forming affixes to be explained, are given the designation kṛt.

kartari kraṃt, "Kṛt in the agent." In the agent, that is, in the sense of the one who acts and of the action, affixes with the designation kṛt occur after a root. This is the general rule.

tayoreba kṛtyaktakhalarthāḥ, "Kṛt, kta and khal in those same senses." Although it was said above that affixes designated kṛt occur in the sense of the agent, as an exception to this, the two affixes kta and khal, though they are designated kṛt, occur only in those same senses, that is, in the sense of the state and of the object, and not in the sense of the agent.

tabyattabyānīyaraḥ, "Tavyat, tavya and anīyar." Not only kta and khal: after roots, in the sense of the action, tavyat, tavya and anīyar occur in the state and the object. The t of tavyat serves to indicate its class, and the r of anīyar serves to block the accent. To iṅha, "to grow," add tavyat, tavya and anīyar. To the two tavya affixes, the iṭ for what begins with bal is given by the rule beginning "ārdhadhātuka," and since in the neuter su is changed to am, and so on, one gets aṅhitabyaṃ, eṅhanīyaṃ. The commentary also says that for words with affixes in the sense of the state, only su and the other singular endings apply, and the gender, too, is only neuter.

Likewise, to ciñ, "to accumulate," add tavya and anīyar; since guṇa is made by the rules on sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka and so on: tabya ceta (it has been made to grow) byaḥ tvayāṅtarmaḥ; cayanīyaḥ tvayāṅharmaḥ.

baseḥ tabyat, "Tavyat after basi." After basi, tavyat occurs in the sense of the agent.

kartari ṇicca, "In the agent, it also has ṇ as its marker." When tavyat is applied in the sense of the agent, tavyat is given the designation of having ṇ as its marker; its purpose is to bring about vṛddhi. (You have accumulated the Dharma.) To bas, "to dwell," add tavyat by the preceding sūtra, and since this sūtra brings about vṛddhi, one gets bāshābyaḥ.

The commentary quotes: karmakartari kelim, "Kelima in the object and the agent." Kelima occurs in the object and the agent. To paca, "to cook," add kelima; since the k serves to block guṇa, it is deleted, and by bringing in the c, one gets pacelimāḥ taṇḍulāḥ.

kṛtyacaḥ, (one stays, and one does not dwell) "Of a kṛt, after ac." When a preverb that is a cause for the change to ṇ comes before, the letter n after ac in a kṛt or other affix is changed to the letter ṇ. To yā, "to obtain," preceded by pra, add anīyar, and since this sūtra changes it to ṇ, (the rice cooks) one gets prayāṇīyaṃ. (It is to be thoroughly obtained.)

ṇerbibhāṣā, "Optionally after ṇi." After a root ending in ṇic that follows a preverb that is a cause for the change to ṇ, changing or not changing to ṇ the letter n after ac in a following kṛt or other affix is made optional. Adding anīyar to yā ending in ṇi, one gets prayāpaṇīyaṃ, prayāpanīyaṃ.

halaścejupaṅhāt, "Also after a hal, from one with ic as its penultimate." For a root that begins with hal and has ic as its penultimate, the letter n after ac in a following kṛt or other affix is optionally changed to ṇ when a preverb that is a cause comes before. To kupa, "to be angry," add anīyar; guṇa is made by the rule beginning "puk-final" (it is wished to be thoroughly obtained), and since this sūtra optionally changes it to ṇ, one gets prakopaṇīyaṃ, prakopanīyaṃ.

ijādeḥ sanumaḥ, "From one that begins with ic and has num."

Even when roots beginning with ic and the like have num, the letter n of a kṛt after ac is changed to ṇ when a preceding preverb is a cause for it. To ikhi, "to go," add anīyar; (it has been made very angry) num is added by the rule beginning "what has i as its marker"; pra is placed before; and since this sūtra changes n to ṇ, one gets prenkhaṇīyaṃ.

na bhābhūpūkamigamibyāyībepāṃ, "Not for bhā, bhū, pū, kami, gami, pyāyī and bepa." The letter n of a kṛt or other affix after ac following these, bhā, "to shine," bhū, "to be," pūñ, "to purify," kamu, "to be beautiful," gamḷ, "to go," opyāyī, "to grow," and bepṛ, "to tremble," (go!) is not changed to ṇ. Adding anīyar to these roots, one gets prabhānīyaṃ, prabhabanīyaṃ, brapapanīyaṃ, prakamanīya, pragamanīyaṃ, prabyāyanīyaṃ, brabepanīyaṃ. Since the commentary explains that for bhā and the rest ending in ṇic, too, it does not change to ṇ, one gets prabhāpanīyaṃ, and so on. Further, since the commentary explains that after khyā and the like (to be made to shine brightly; to be fully; to be made thoroughly pure; to be made very beautiful; to be made to go forth; to be made to grow greatly; to be made to tremble greatly) it does not change to ṇ either, one gets prakhyānīyaṃ (to be spoken of thoroughly), prasnā (wished to shine brightly) nīyaṃ (to be thoroughly washed), pradānī brāhmaṇaḥ (the brahmin, a thoroughly worthy recipient of gifts). Further, since the commentary explains that after pūñ it optionally changes to ṇ, one gets prapabiṇīyaṃ yomaḥ, and so on.

kṛtyalyuṭo bahulaṃ, "Kṛt and lyuṭ in many senses." In many senses, the action and the rest, the affix lyuṭ, which bears the designation kṛt, occurs. Examples will be given below.

aco yat, "Yat after ac." After roots ending in ac, in the sense of the action, (thoroughly pure and fine) yat occurs. To ciñ, "to accumulate," and ji, "to conquer," add yat; since guṇa is made by the rules on sārvadhātuka and so on, one gets ceyaṃ puṇyaṃ tvayā, jeyaṃ mayā, and so on. Since the commentary explains that yat also occurs for a root that originally ends in ac and afterwards comes to end in hal: to dā add san; by the rule beginning "mā, ghu, rabha, labha," ac is changed to is; the abhyāsa is deleted; and by the rule "of s, before (merit is to be accumulated by you; it is to be conquered by me) an ārdhadhātuka," s is changed to t. To what is called detsa, add yat, and since a is deleted by the rule on the elision of at, one gets ditsyaṃ.

īdyati, "Īt before yat." A root ending in āt is to be changed to īt when the affix yat follows. To dā, "to give," jñā, "to understand," and pā, "to drink," add yat; by this sūtra ā becomes īt, and since guṇa is made by the rules on sārvadhātuka and so on, one gets deyaṃ, jñeyaṃ, peyaṃ, and so on. (To be given.)

The commentary quotes: takiśasaṃcatiyatijanibhyaśca yat, "Yat also after taki, śasi, cati, yati and jani." After these roots, too, yat occurs in the sense of the action: takyaṃ, śasyaṃ, catyaṃ, yatyaṃ, janyaṃ. The commentary (to be given; to be known; to be drunk) quotes: hanobā yat, "Optionally after han." Yat optionally occurs after han, "to harm." The commentary further quotes: "Also badha." When yat is given after han, han itself (to be laughed at; to be harmed; to be begged; to be striven for; to be born) becomes paṅha. To han, the yat of the preceding quotation is given, and since by this quotation han is changed to baṅha, one gets baṅhyaṃ. (To be harmed.)

por dupaṅhāt, "After pu, with at as the penultimate." After a root whose penultimate is at and which has pu, that is, any letter of the pa class, at its end, yat occurs. To labha, "to obtain," japa, "to recite," and rapa, "to speak," yat is applied by this sūtra; by bringing it in, one gets labhyaṃ, japyaṃ, rapyaṃ, and so on.

āṅoñapi, "Also after āṅ." When an affix beginning with ya follows labha, "to obtain," after the preverb āṅ, the augment num occurs. The m indicates the position, and the u is for pronunciation: ālamṅhyaṃ gauḥ.

upātaśaṃsāyaṃ, "After upa, in doubt." (To be obtained; to be recited; to be spoken.) When doubt is expressed for labha after the preverb upa, the augment num occurs: upalambhyaṃ.

śakisahośca, "Also after śaki and saha." After śaklṛ, "to be able," (the ox to be fully obtained) and ṣaha, "to endure," yat also occurs: śakyaṃ, sahyaṃ.

gadamadacarayamaścānupasarge, "Also after gada, mada, cara and yama, when there is no preverb." When no preverb precedes, (obtained, or near) yat also occurs after gada without n, "to speak clearly," madī, "to be pure," cara, "to move," and yamu, "to restrain": gaṅyaṃ, maṅyaṃ, caryaṃ, yamyaṃ. (Able; to be endured.)

careraādicāgurau, "Of cari, also after āṅ, when it is not a teacher." After cara following āṅ, too, yat occurs when a teacher is not meant: ācaryaṃ deśaḥ. When it is a teacher, ṇya is applied, and since vṛddhi is made by the rule "of the penultimate," (a line, that is, without prose; intoxicating liquor; conduct; to be restrained) one gets ācāryaḥ.

abaṅyapaṇyabrajyāgahyapaṇitabyānirobheṣuḥ, "Apaṅya, paṇya and brajya, (to be censured; to be sold) in the absence of obstruction and so on." Adding yat to bad, "to speak," preceded by nañ, (conduct in every region; to eat) to pana, "to trade," and to braja, "to go," one gets abaṅyaṃ, paṇyaṃ and prajyaṃ, (teacher) which respectively are set forms (nipāta) for expressing what is to be censured, what is to be sold, and the absence of obstruction.

bahyaṃ karaṇaṃ, "Vahya, for the instrument." Adding yat to baha, "to obtain," the form bahyaṃ is made a set form for expressing the agent: bahyaṃ śakaṭaṃ. (It makes a chariot. Blameless. Merchandise. To be gone.)

aryaḥ shāmibaiśyayoḥ, "Arya, for a master and a vaiśya." Adding yat to ṛ, "to go," the form aryaḥ is a set form for expressing a master and a vaiśya.

ṛtumatyupasaryā, "Upasaryā, for one in her season." Adding yat to sṛ, "to go," preceded by upa, the form upasaryā is a set form for expressing a woman who is in her season.

ajaryaṃ saṅgataṃ, "Ajarya, for what is joined together." Adding yat to jṝ, "to lose one's youth," preceded by nañ, the form ajarya is to be made a set form for expressing what is joined together.

rihalorṇyat, "Ṇyat after ṛ and hal." After roots ending in ṛ and roots ending in hal, ṇyat occurs in the sense of the action. The ṇ serves for vṛddhi, and the t serves for the accent. To kṛñ, "to do," and hṛñ, "to harm," ṇyat is applied by this sūtra; (past one's prime, or grown old) and since vṛddhi is made by the rule "of ac, too, before what has ñ or ṇ as its marker," one gets kāryaṃ, hāryaṃ, and so on.

To han, "to harm," ṇyat. By the rule "of han, t, when not before ciṇ and ṇal," n becomes t; by the rule "of the h of hanta, before what has ñ or ṇ as its marker," h becomes gh; and since vṛddhi is made by the rule "of the penultimate," one gets ghādyaṃ.

cajoḥ kughiṇyatoḥ, "Ku for c and j, before ghi and ṇyat." The letters c and j at the end of a root (to be needed; to be taken) are changed to the corresponding letter of the ka class when affixes that have gh as their marker, or ṇyat, follow. To baca, "to cook," ṇyat is added by the rule beginning "ṛ and hal"; by this sūtra c becomes k; (to be harmed) and since vṛddhi is made by the rule "of the penultimate," one gets pākyaṃ. Likewise, to ruja, ṇyat; by this sūtra j becomes g; and since guṇa is made by the rule beginning "puk-final," one gets rogyaṃ.

na kvādeḥ, "Not of a root that begins with ku." The final c and j of a root that has ku, that is, a letter of the ka class, at its beginning are not changed to the ka class when ghit or ṇyat follows. To garja, "in the sense of sound," ṇyat; by this sūtra (to be cooked) j is not changed to g: garjyaṃ, and so on.

ajibrajyośca, "Also of aji and braji." (Illness.) The roots aja, "to throw," and braja, "to go," and, by the word "also," baja, "to go," are not changed to the ka class either; since vṛddhi is made by the rule "of the penultimate," one gets ājyaṃ, brājyaṃ, bājyaṃ.

bañcergatau, "Of pañci, in the sense of going." (To be sounded aloud.) When the sense of going of bañci is expressed, it is not changed to the ka class: bañcuṃ. (To be gone.) When it is not the sense of going, it is changed: baṃkyaṃ kāṣṭhāṃ. (A crooked or bent piece of wood.)

ṇya ābaśyake, "Before ṇya, in the sense of necessity." When ṇya follows and it applies in the sense of what is especially to be done, (mad; to be gone) c and j are not changed to the ka class: abaśyapācyi, and so on.

yajayācarucaprabacarcaśca, "Also of yaja, yāca, ruca, prabaca and ṛca." Of yaja, "to worship the gods," yāca, "to beg," ruca, "to shine," baca, "to speak," preceded by pra, and ṛca, "to worship," there is also no change to the ka class when ṇya follows: yājyaṃ, yācyaṃ, (one cooks of necessity) rocyaṃ, prabācyaṃ, arcāṃ. Since the commentary explains that tyaja, "to lose one's youth," and pūja, "to worship," are also not changed to the ka class when ṇya follows, one gets tyājyaṃ, pūjyaṃ.

baconñaśabṅasaṃjñayāṃ, "Of baca, when it is not a name for speech." When it is not the name of speech of baca, (to be worshipped; to be begged; to be kindled; to be proclaimed; to be worshipped) that is, not the sense of expression, it is not changed to the ka class: bācyaṃ. In the sense of expression, since it is changed to the ka class, one gets bākyaṃ.

prayojyaniyo (an elder; to be worshipped) jyoo śakyārtha, "Prayojya and niyojya, in the sense of capability." Adding ṇyat to yuji, "to join," preceded by pra and by ni, prayojya and niyojya are set forms for expressing the sense of capability. When it is not (one who does not speak) the sense of capability, since j is changed to g, one gets prayogyaṃ, (to be spoken) niyogyaṃ. Since the commentary explains that bhuja, too, is not changed to the ka class in the sense of eating, one gets bhojyamannaṃ; when it is not the sense of eating, it is changed to the ka class: bhogyaṃ.

orābaśyake, "After u, in what is necessary." After a root ending in the letter u, ṇyat occurs (to be thoroughly employed; to be definitely employed) in the sense of expressing a state that is unavoidable or necessary. To lūñ, "to cut," ṇyat; (to be eaten) vṛddhi is made by the rule "of ac, too, before what has ñ or ṇ as its marker"; (to be protected) and since au is changed to āb by the rule "ending in ba, before an affix of ya," one gets abaśyalābyaṃ, and so on.

āsuyubapirbilapitrapicamaśca, "Also after āsu, yu, bapi, rapi, lapi, trapi and cam." After ṣuñ, "to come forth," preceded by āṅ, yu, "to mix," ṭubapa, "to sow seed," rapa and lapa, "to speak clearly," trapūṣ, "to be ashamed," and camu, "to eat," (to be necessarily cut) ṇyat also occurs: āsābyaṃ (to be brought forth completely), yābyaṃ (to be mixed), pāpyaṃ (to be sown), rāpyaṃ (to be clearly spoken), lāpyaṃ, trāpyaṃ, cāmyaṃ.

dambheśca, "Also after dambhi." After dambhi, ṇyat occurs and the n is also elided: dābhyaṃ.

The commentary quotes: bhajjayyajānmāṃ yadvā, "Optionally yat for bhaja, jaya, yaja and āṅ-nama." After bhaja, "to resort to," jaya, yaja, "to worship the gods," and nama preceded by āṅ, (ashamed; to be eaten) "to bow deeply," ṇyat occurs, and optionally yat. (Hypocrisy.) In the ṇyat alternative, since vṛddhi is made by the rule "of the penultimate": ṇyat bhājyaṃ, yat bhajyaṃ; ṇyat jāyyaṃ, yat jayya; ṇyat yājyaṃ, yat yajyaṃ; ṇyat ānāmyaṃ, yat ānmyaṃ.

ānāyyoñnitye, "Ānāyya, for what is impermanent." Adding ṇyat to nīñ, "to lead," preceded by āṅ, ānāyya is a set form for expressing what is impermanent, that is, the southern fire. Otherwise, āneyaṃ.

pra (to be resorted to) ṇāyyoñsaṃ (to be worshipped) matau, pra (to be worshipped) ṇāyyaḥ, (bowing down completely) "Praṇāyya, for what is not approved." Adding ṇyat to ṇīñ, "to lead," preceded by pra, (cora; the southern fire) praṇāyyaḥ is to be made a set form for expressing what is not approved. (To be led straight.) Other than what is not approved, praṇeyaṃ sādhuḥ.

pāyyasāncāyyanikāyyamānahabirṇibāssāmiṅhenīṣuḥ, "Bāyya, sānnāyya, nikāyya and ṅhāyya for pride, (thief) oblation substance, dwelling and kindling sticks." Adding ṇyat to pā, "to drink," ṇī, "to obtain," preceded by sam, ciñ, "to accumulate," preceded by ni, and ṅheṭ, (leads well) "to drink," the forms pāyya, sānnayya, nikāyya and ṅhāyya are, respectively, set forms for expressing pride, oblation substance, dwelling and kindling sticks. In senses other than these, adding yat, one gets peyaṃ, sanneyaṃ, niceyaṃ, ṅheyaṃ.

kratau kuṇḍapāyyasaṃcāyau, "Kuṇḍapāyya and sañcāyya, (that pride; a kind of ghee; a dwelling; kindling sticks) for a sacrifice." Adding ṇyat to phā, "to drink," preceded by kuṇḍa, and to ciñ, "to accumulate," preceded by saṃ, kuṇḍapāyya and (Śiva drinks; to be drunk; leading completely; accumulated definitely; drink; sacrifice) sañcāyya are to be made set forms for denoting a sacrifice.

amābasyatarasyaṃ, "Optionally after amābas." Ṇyat occurs for bas, "to dwell," preceded by amā, and vṛddhi is to be made optional: amābāsyā, amābasyā.

padaḥ supi kyapca, "After bad, when there is a sup, also kyap." Yat occurs for bad, "to speak," after a sup, and kyap also occurs. The p of kyap serves for the augment tuk, and the letter k serves for its having k and ṅ as markers and so on. To bad preceded by brahna, kyap; by the rule "of baci, svapi, yaja and the rest, before what has k as its marker," (the new moon) it is changed to saṃprasāraṇa, and since it is joined by the rule "guṇa after a," one gets brahmodyaṃ. Or else, adding yat, brahmabadyaṃ.

bhubo bhābe, "After bhū, in the state."

After bhū, "to be," following a sup, when the state is expressed, kyap occurs: brahmabhūyaṃ gata. When it does not follow a sup, adding yat, one gets bhabyaṃ.

hanasta ca, "After han, also t." (Speech about Brahmā.) When no preverb comes before, (speech about Brahmā) after han, "to harm," following a sup, when the state is expressed, kyap occurs, and the n is to be changed to t. (Having become Brahmā is understood.) With ḍāp, one gets brahmahadyā.

etistuśāsbṛdṛjāṣaḥ kyap, (endowed with excellence) "Kyap after eti, stu, śās, bṛ, dṛ and juṣ." Eti, that is, iṇ, "to go," ṣṭuñ, "to praise," śāsu, "to instruct," bṛñ, "to cover," dṛṅ, "to disrespect," and juṣī, "to delight": after these too, kyap occurs.

hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk, (the slaying of Brahmā) "Tuk for a short vowel, before a kṛt that has p as its marker." When a kṛt or other affix that has p as its marker follows a root ending in a short ac, the augment tuk occurs. To iṇ and stu, kyap; since this sūtra gives tuk, one gets ihyaṃ, stutyaṃ. To śāsu, kyap; by the rule "of śās, before aṅ and hal, it," ā is changed to it, and by the rule "ṣ after iṇ," s is changed to ṣ: śiṣyaḥ. To pṛñ and dṛṅ, kyap; since the augment tuk is given, one gets pṛtyaḥ (covering), ādṛtyaḥ (wholly disrespected). Adding kyap to juṣ, (thus; praised) one gets juṣyaḥ. (Delight.)

śaṃsiguhiduhibhyo bā, "Optionally after śaṃsi, guhi and duhi." After śisu, "to praise," duha, "to milk," (pupil) and guhū, "to conceal," kyap optionally occurs. Since the n is deleted by the rule beginning "of what does not have i as its marker," one gets śasyaṃ, duhyaṃ, guhyaṃ; or else, adding yat, śisyaṃ, dohyaṃ, gohyaṃ.

āṅpūrbādajeśca saṃjñāyāṃ, "Also after aji preceded by āṅ, for a name." Adding kyap to aja, "to throw," preceded by āṅ, ājyi too is a set form for expressing a name.

ṛdupadhāccākḷbicṛtaḥ, (crops; a milch cow; secret) "Also after one with ṛt as its penultimate, (praise; to milk; secret) except kḷpa and cṛt." After roots with ṛt as their penultimate, too, except kḷpū, "to be able," and cṛtī, "to cook," kyap (ghee) occurs. Adding kyap to dṛtu, "to enter," one gets dṛtyaṃ; adding ṇyat to kḷpū and cṛtī, one gets saṃkalbyaṃ, bicartyaṃ.

pāṇau sṛjerṇyat, "Ṇyat after sṛja, with pāṇi." After sṛja, "to cut off," preceded by pāṇi, ṇyat occurs; j is changed to g by the rule beginning "ca, ja," and since guṇa is made by the rule beginning "phuk-final," one gets pāṇisargyā rajjuḥ.

samabapūrbācca, (entering) "Also when sam and aba precede." (Fully understood; analysis.) After sṛj preceded by the preverbs saṃ and apa, ṇyat also occurs: samabasargyaṃ.

īcakhanaḥ, "Also ī for khana." For khanu, "to destroy," kyap occurs, and n is changed to ī. (A rope twisted by hand.) To khana, kyap; n is changed to ī; and since guṇa is made by the rule "after a," one gets kheyaṃ.

bhṛñoñrasaṃjñāyāṃ, "After bhṛñ, when not a name." For bhṛñ, "to hold," (full; well and wholly cut off) when it is not a name, kyap occurs; since tuk is given by the rule beginning "short," one gets bhṛtyaṃ. When it is not a name, adding ṇyat and making vṛddhi, one gets bhāryā.

saṃbhṛñobā, "Optionally after saṃbhṛñ." (Destroying.) After bhṛñ preceded by saṃ, kyap optionally occurs, and optionally ṇyat: saṃbhṛtyaḥ, saṃbhāryaḥ.

sṛjerbibhāṣā, "Optionally for sṛji." For sṛja, "to cut off," kyap and (a hireling) ṇyat are to be made optional: kyap sṛjyaḥ (cut off); ṇyat sārjyā.

rājasūyasūryamṛṣodyarucyakupyakṛṣṭapacyābyathyā, "Rājasūya, sūrya, mṛṣodya, rucya, kupya, kṛṣṭapacya (accumulated; an excellent kṣatriya) and abyathya." Adding kyap to ṣu, "to drive," preceded by rāja, sṛ, "to go," bada, "to speak," preceded by mṛṣa, ruca, "to shine," kupa, "to be angry," paca, "to cook," preceded by kṛṣṭa, and byatha, "to suffer," preceded by nañ, the forms rājasūya, sūrya, mṛṣodya, rucya, kupya, kṛṣṭapacya and abyathya are, respectively, to be made set forms for expressing "the king performs ablution," "the sun," "makes untrue," "makes clear," "makes angry," "is to be cooked after being taken up," and "is to be made free of disease." (The king performs ablution. The sun. Makes untrue. Makes clear. Is to be made angry. Is to be cooked after being taken up. Is to be made free of disease.)

bhidyodhhyau nade, "Bhadya and adhhya, for a river." Adding kyap to bhidir, "to destroy," and ujjha, "to give up," bhidya and udṭhya are to be made set forms for expressing the names of rivers.

puṣyasidṭhyau nakṣatre, "Puṣya and sidhya, for a lunar mansion." Adding kyap to puṣa, "to flourish," and ṣidhū, "treatise," puṣya and sidhya are set forms for expressing a lunar mansion.

bipūyabinīyajityamuñjakalkahaliṣu, "Vipūya, vinīya (river; river) and jitya, for muñja grass, sediment and the plough." Adding kyap to pūṅ, "to purify," preceded by bi, ṇīñ, "to obtain," and ji, "to conquer," (Puṣya; a lunar mansion) bipūya, binīya and jitya are set forms for expressing a girdle of muñja grass, sediment, and a plough.

pratyabibhyāṃ graheḥ chandasi, "After grahi following prati and api, in metrical language." After graha, "to take up," (a girdle of muñja grass; turbid, or mixed, or sediment; having a plough) following prati and api, kyap occurs in metrical language; since it is changed to saṃprasāraṇa by the rule beginning "grahi, jyā," one gets pratigṛhyaṃ, apigṛhyaṃ.

padāsvairipāhyāpakṣeṣu ca, "Also for a word, one who is dependent, the outside, and a side." When the senses of a word, one who is dependent, the outside, and a side are expressed, kyap also occurs after graha: apagṛhya padaṃ (a word not joined in sandhi; held separately; even held); gṛhyaḥ asvairi (a dependent is held); grāmagṛhyā sena (an army outside the village); rvamagṛhyaḥ (Rāma's side).

bibhāṣā kṛbṛṣoḥ, "Optionally after kṛ and bṛṣ."

For kṛñ, "to do," and bṛṣu, "to wash," kyap and ṇyat are to be made optional: kyap kṛtyaṃ, ṇyat kārya; kyap bṛṣyaṃ, ṇyat barṣyaṃ.

The commentary quotes: praiṣātisargaprāptakaleṣu kṛtyaśca, "Also the kṛt affixes in urging, in birth, and when the time has been reached." When the times of urging, of birth or reading, and of reaching are expressed, (an action, or a need, or a result, or an activity; to be bathed) affixes that bear the designation kṛt also occur. To iṣu, "to desire," preceded by pra, iṅ, "to read," preceded by adhi, and āplṛ, "to pervade," preceded by pra: adding kta to the first and the last, and yat to the middle one, one gets preṣitatvaṃ, adhyeyaṃ, prāptate kālaḥ.

bhabyageyaprabacanīyopasthānīajenyāplābyāpātyāḥ, "Bhavya, geya, pravacanīya, upasthānīya, janyā, plāvyā and pātyā." Adding yat to bhū, "to be," and to gai, "sound"; anīyar (you, having strongly desired; to be read; the time reached by you) to paca, "to speak," preceded by pra, and to sthā, "to stand," preceded by upa; and ṇyat to the three, jan, "to be born," plu, "to go," and patḷ, "to fall," the forms bhabya, giya, prabacanīyaḥ, upasthānīya, jānyā, blābyā and pātyā are also to be made set forms.

The commentary quotes: śakiliṅca, "In capability, also liṅ." When capability is expressed, liṅ occurs, and the kṛt affixes also occur. Adding anīyar to baha (existing; proclaimed; the scriptures; an attendant; birth; to be gone; to be fallen), one gets bahanīyaḥ.

iti pāṇinibyākaraṇasya sūtrṝtkṛtaḥ samāptaḥ. Thus, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the kṛt affixes are complete.

With these, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel (able to obtain) of Excellent Explanation, a set of notes setting down the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great grammatical treatise, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the rough outline, together with the procedures, of the domains of application of the affixes that apply in the sense of the state and the object, the most important among the kṛt and other affixes, is for the present complete.

Now I shall explain the procedures for the affixes in the sense of the agent.

ṇbultṛcau, "Ṇvul and tṛc." After roots, in the agent, that is, in the sense of the one who acts and of the action, ṇvul and tṛc occur. The l of ṇvul and the c of tṛc serve for the accent, and the ṇ serves for vṛddhi and so on. To kṛñ, ṇvul; vṛddhi is made by the rule beginning "of ac, too, before what has ñ or ṇ as its marker"; after the markers are deleted, since vu is changed to aka by the rule "ana and aka for yu and vu," one gets kārakaḥ. To kṛñ, tṛc; guṇa is made by the rules on sārvadhātuka and so on, and when su is given, one gets kartā. Likewise, adding both ṇvul and tṛc to ṇīñ, "to obtain," one gets ṇvul nāeyakaḥ, tṛc netā. To kuṭa, ṇvul and tṛc: for ṇvul, guṇa; for tṛc, the iṭ for what begins with bal; and since it is kit by the rule beginning "kuṭa and the rest," (agent) guṇa is not made: ṇvul koṭakaḥ, tṛc with su kuṭitā. To ḍudāñ, ṇvul (agent) and tṛc. In the ṇvul alternative, since the augment yuk is given by the rule "yuk after āt, before ciṇ and kṛt," (one who leads) one gets ṇvul dāyakaḥ, tṛc with su dātā. To śamu and damu, ṇvul and tṛc; by the rule beginning "m-final," vṛddhi is not made, and since iṭ is given, (kyu, maker) one gets ṇvul śamakaḥ, tṛc śamitā; ṇvul damakaḥ, tṛc danitā; and so on. Since the commentary says that ṇvul also occurs in the sense of the object, adding ṇvul to hṛñ and making vṛddhi, (one who performs giving) one gets padahārakaḥ.

nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇibyaca, "Lyu, ṇini and ac (one who pacifies) after nandi, grahi, paca and the rest." (One who pacifies.) In the sense of the agent, lyu occurs after nanda and the rest, ṇini after llahi and the rest, and ac after paca and the rest. (One who does it with the foot.) The l of lyu serves as a marker; the i of ṇini is for pronunciation, and the ṇ serves for vṛddhi; and the c of ac serves for the accent. To nanda, "to delight," pasa, "to dwell," mada, "to delight," dūṣa, "to corrupt," sādha, "to accomplish," śubha, "to be beautiful," bṛdha, "to grow," ṣaha, "to endure," tapa, "to burn," and jalpa, "to recite," lyu; the l is deleted, and since yu is changed to ana, one gets nandanaḥ (one who delights), basanaḥ (one who dwells), madanaḥ (one who intoxicates), dūṣaṇaḥ (one who corrupts), sādhanaḥ (one who accomplishes), śobhanaḥ (one who beautifies), bardhanaḥ (one who increases), sahanaḥ, tapanaḥ, jalpana, and so on. To graha and sthā, ṇini: for graha, vṛddhi; for sthā, since puk is given by the rule "puk after āt," one gets grāhrī, sthāpī, and so on. To paca and dipu, "to play," since ac is given, one gets pacaḥ, debaḥ, and so on.

yaṅoñcicitiyaṅoluk, "After yaṅ (one who endures; one who burns; one who speaks), ac, and yaṅ too is lost." For a root ending in yaṅ, too, ac occurs, and when ac follows, yaṅ (one who holds; one who stands) is lost. To ṇī and lū with the yaṅ affix, (one who cooks; god) that is, to nenīya and lolūya, ac is given, and yaṅ is lost. Since this comes after the deletion of yaṅ, guṇa is not made; and since, for the former, yaṇ is made by the rule beginning "not of a single ac," and for the latter, before ac, it is changed to ub by the rule beginning "śnu, root," one gets nenyaḥ, lolubaḥ, and so on. Since the commentary explains that after what ends in u the yaṅ affix is optionally not lost, one may also, not deleting the yaṅ affix and deleting a by the rule on the elision of at, get rorūyaḥ, and so on.

caricalipatipadīnāṃ bātvitvamapyākcābhyrasase, "Of cari, cali, (one who leads greatly; one who cuts greatly) pati and badi, doubling optionally, and also āk for the abhyāsa." When ac follows cara and cala, "to move," pada, "to fall," and bada, "to speak," (one who speaks greatly) they are optionally doubled, and when they are doubled, the augment āk occurs for the abhyāsa: the a is for pronunciation, the c serves for distinction, and the k indicates position. Since ac, doubling and the augment āk are given to these roots, one gets carācaraḥ, calācalaḥ, patāpataḥ, padāpadaḥ, and so on; or else, when they are not doubled, caraḥ, calaḥ, pataḥ, padaḥ, and so on. Since the commentary explains that ka occurs for kṛñ in the sense of the state, and that doubling also occurs when ka follows: to kṛ, ka, and it is doubled; (one who goes; one who moves; one who falls; one who speaks) by the rule "at of ṛ" and the rule "cu for ku and h," and since the k serves to make it kit, (one who goes; one who moves; one who falls; one who speaks) the k is deleted; and by adding yaṇ for the ac of ik, one gets cakraṃ (action); or else, by adding ac, karaḥ (doer).

rātreḥ kṛti bibhāṣā, "Optionally for rātri before a kṛt." When a noun with a kṛt affix follows, giving or not giving rātri the augment mum is made optional: rātriṃcaraḥ, rātricaraḥ, and so on.

igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ, "Ka after roots with ik as their penultimate, and after jñā, prī and kṝ."

Ka comes after a root that has ik as its penultimate (upadhā), and after jña, "understanding," prīñ, "satisfaction," and kṝ, "scattering." The k serves to make it kit. For a root with ik as its penultimate: to kṣip preceded by vi (one who goes about at night; growth), ka is given, so vikṣipaḥ. For jñā, ka; and since the ā is deleted by the rule that deletes ā before iṭ as well, jñaḥ. For prī, ka; and since it is changed to iy before ac by "śnu, roots and so on," priyaḥ. For kṝ preceded by ut, ka: by "it for the ṝ of a root," ṝ becomes it, and since r is given to the aṇ of ṛ with r following, utkiraḥ. Because the commentary explains that ka also comes after kṝ, "swallowing" (scattering), giraḥ (knowing).

ātaś copasarge, "Also after ā, when there is an upasarga." (Joy.) Ka also comes after a root ending in ā that has some upasarga before it: prasthaḥ, sudaḥ, prajñaḥ (scattering), abhijñaḥ, and so on.

pāghrādhmādheṭdṛśaḥ śaḥ, "Śa after pā, ghrā, dhmā, dheṭ and dṛś" (it makes a swallower). Śa follows pā, "drinking," ghrā, "smelling," dhmā, "sound," dheṭ, "drinking," and dṛśir, "seeing"; the letter ś serves to make it śit. (A measure; good giver; wisdom; direct knowledge.) Since pā, ghrā and so on are changed to piba and so on, one gets utpibaḥ, ujjighraḥ, vidhamaḥ, uddhayaḥ, utpaśyaḥ, and so on.
