anupasargāl limpavindadhāripārivedyudejicetisātisāhibhyaś ca, "Also after limpa, vinda, dhāri, pāri, vedi, udeji, ceti, sāti and sāhi, when there is no upasarga." From lipi, "smearing," and vidi, "portion" (one who drinks from above; one who smells from above; one who blows hard; one who drinks deeply; one who looks upward), with num by the rule on idit roots going and so on; and from dhṛñ, "holding," pṛ, "pleasing," vida, "knowing," ejṛ, "shining," preceded by ut, citī, "notion," sata, the root of sūtra, and ṣaha, "patience," these ending in ṇic: from dhāra and the rest, with no upasarga before them, śa comes. Guṇa is made, and so: limpaḥ, vindaḥ, pārayaḥ, pedayaḥ, udejayaḥ, catayaḥ, sātayaḥ, sāhayaḥ.

dadātidadhātyor vibhāṣā, "Optionally after dadāti and dadhāti." Śa comes after ḍudāñ, "giving," and ḍudhāñ, "holding," and before śa there is optionally doubling, as before ślu (one who smears; one who apportions; one who wishes to hold; one who pleases; one who makes known; one who makes blaze brightly; one who makes known; one who makes sūtras or treatises; one who makes patience). It is stated that for dāñ and dhāñ, before śa, doubling takes place. Since the a is deleted, as is due for an abhyasta, dadaḥ, dadhaḥ; or else, by giving yuk after ā, dāyaḥ, dhāyaḥ, and the like.

jvalādibhyo ṇo 'nyatarasyām, "Optionally ṇa after jvala and the rest." The roots from jval, "burning," up to kab, are jvala and the rest, and after them ṇa comes optionally; the ṇ serves for vṛddhi and so on. (One who gives; one who holds.) jvālaḥ, cālaḥ, and so on; and (one who gives; one who holds) or else, with ac added, jalaḥ, calaḥ, and so on.

śyādvyadhāsrusaṃsrvatīṇavasāvahṛliḥśliṣaśvasaś ca, "Also after śyā, roots ending in ā, vyadha, āsru, saṃsru, atīṇ, avasā, avahṛ, liha, śliṣa and śvas." (Burning; moving.) Ṇa also comes after śyā from śyaiṅ, "going," after roots ending in ā, after vyadha, "piercing" (burning; moving), after śru, "hearing," preceded by āṅ, after sru, "going," preceded by sam, after in, "going," preceded by ati, after ṣo, "ending action," preceded by ava, after hṛñ, "harming," after lih, "tasting," after śliṣa, "embracing," and after śvas, "breath." The ec vowels are changed to ā by the rule "not in the domain near where ś goes" and so on, and the forms are produced by giving yuk after ā and so on: śyāyaḥ, dāyaḥ, pyādhaḥ, āśvābaḥ, saṃsrāvaḥ, atyāyaḥ, avasāyaḥ, avahāraḥ, lehaḥ, śleṣaḥ, śvāsaḥ.

dunyor anupasarge, "After du and nī, when there is no upasarga." Ṇa comes after ṭudu, "tormenting," and ṇīñ, "leading," when no upasarga stands before them (frost or hoarfrost; giving; inside; hearing all around; going together; going far beyond; utterly ending; carrying off; tasting; embracing; breathing out): dāvaḥ (forest fire), nāyaḥ.

vibhāṣā grahaḥ, "Optionally after graha." Ṇa comes optionally after graha: grahaḥ (an obscure interlinear gloss stands here); or else, with ac added, grahaḥ, "the sun and so on."

gehe kaḥ, "Ka, for a house." After graha, when a house is meant, ka comes. Since it is changed to saṃprasāraṇa by "grahi, jyā and so on" (a leader or guide), gṛhaḥ.

śilpini ṣvun, "Ṣvun, for an artisan." From nṛtī, "moving the body" (seizer of crocodiles; one who moves in water), khanu, "destroying" (graha, that is, the sun and the other planets), and rañja, when an artisan is meant, ṣvun comes. The n serves the vowel; the ṣ makes it ṣit, for the sake of ṅīṣ; and since yu and vu are changed to ana and aka, vu becomes aka (a sheath, or a covering, or a house): nartakaḥ, khanakaḥ, tajakaḥ (one who dyes and washes).

gas thakan, "Thakan after gā." For gai, "sound," the ec is changed to ā by the rule "not in the domain near where ś goes" and so on, and after gā thakan comes: gāthakaḥ.

ṇyuṭ ca, "Ṇyuṭ as well." After gā, ṇyuṭ also comes. The ṭ serves to make it ṭit (dancer; digger); in the set form the n is deleted; it serves its purpose and the purpose of vṛddhi by ṇ. Since yu is changed to ana and the augment yuk is given after ā, gāyanaḥ.

haś ca vrīhikālayoḥ, "Also after hā, for grain and for time" (a singer or a maker of verses). After ohāk, "abandoning," when grain or time is meant, ṇyut comes: hāyanaḥ, the name of a kind of rice; hāyanaḥ, a year.

prusṛlvaḥ samabhihāre vun, "Vun after pru, sṛ and lū, for repeated action" (female singer). After pruṅ and sṛ, "going," and lūñ, "cutting," when repeated action is meant, vun comes. The n serves the vowel, and vu is changed to aka (grain, the grain so called; grain so called; the one that abandons, that is, the year): pravakaḥ, sarakaḥ, lavakaḥ.

āśiṣi ca, "Also for a wish." Vun also comes after a root when a wish is to be conveyed. Adding vun to jīva, "living," and nanda, "rejoicing": jīvakaḥ, "may he live"; nandakaḥ, "may he rejoice"; and so on.

ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām (bather; cup maker; barber), "Also ktic and kta, for a name." After a root, when the sense of a name is to be expressed, ktic and kta come.

titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca, "Also before ti, tu, tra, ta, tha, si, su, sara, ka and sa." Iṭ does not come before these kṛt affixes, ti and the rest. To bhū, "being," ktic is given by the preceding sūtra; the c serves the vowel, and the k serves to block guṇa. By this sūtra iṭ does not come: bhūhiḥ. In the same way, adding ktic to sū, "bringing forth many living beings," sūtaḥ, and so on.

anunāsikasya kvijhaloḥ kṅiti, "For a root ending in a nasal, before kvi and before jhal that are kṅit."

The penultimate (upadhā) of a root that ends in a nasal becomes long when there follows a kṛt or similar affix beginning with jhal and bearing the name "going to kaṅ," that is, kṅit (prosperity), and also kvip. (Birth.)

na ktici dīrghaś ca, "Nor is there lengthening before ktic." Above it was explained that the penultimate of a nasal-final root is made long before a kṅit affix beginning with jhal. As the exception to that, when the affix ktic follows, van and the rest and tan and the rest, which take no iṭ, do not make the penultimate long, nor delete the n, and so on. Adding ktic to yamu, "restraining," vanu, "begging," and tanu, "extending," one gets yaṃtiḥ, baṃtiḥ, taṃtiḥ, and so on.

sanaḥ ktici lopaś cānyatarasyām, "Optionally deletion as well for san before ktic." San, that is ṣaṇu, "giving": the deletion of its letter n, the change to ā, and so on, take place optionally when ktic follows: sātiḥ, sayiḥ, santiḥ.

karmaṇy aṇ, "Aṇ after an object (karman)." (Whatever is the object of the action. Restraint; begging; extension.) Aṇ comes in the sense of an action that follows that object: kumbhakāraḥ, kāṇḍalāvaḥ, and so on.

hvāvāmaś ca, "Also after hvā, vā and mā." The ec of hveñ, "calling," and veñ, "the thread of weaving" (giving; giving), is changed to ā, and so aṇ also comes after hvā and the like and after māṅ, "measuring." Since the augment yuk is given after ā: svargahvāyaḥ, tantuvāyaḥ (one who makes pots, that is, a potter; one who reaps thorns), dhānyamāyaḥ.

āto 'nupasarge kaḥ, "Ka after ā, when there is no upasarga." Ka comes after a root ending in ā that follows an object and has no upasarga. To dā, "giving," ka is added; and since the ā is deleted, as the ā of ā is due to be deleted before iṭ as well (one who calls to heaven; the thread of weaving), godaḥ (giver of cattle; the measure of grain, that is, its maker; giver of curds), kanpaladaḥ.

supi sthaḥ, "After a sup, from sthā." After sthā, "standing," which follows something ending in sup, ka comes, not aṇ: samasthaḥ, vanasthaḥ.

ambāmbagobhūmisavyāpadvitrikuśekuśaṅkvaṅgumañjipuñjiparamebarhirdivyagnibhyaḥ sthaḥ, "Of sthā, after amba, āmbā, go, bhūmi, savya, apa, dvi, tri, ku, śeku, śaṅku, aṅgu, mañji, puñja, parame, barhi, divi and agni." (Dwelling together; dwelling in the forest.) The letter s of sthā following any of these becomes ṣ. To sthā preceded by them ka is added, and the ā is deleted; by this sūtra s becomes ṣ, and th is changed to ṭh, as is due by the rule for ṣ and ṭu. So: amāṣṭhaḥ, āmāṣṭhaḥ, goṣṭhaḥ, bhūmiṣṭhaḥ, savyāpaṣṭhaḥ, dviṣṭhaḥ, triṣṭhaḥ, kuṣṭhaḥ, śekuṣṭhaḥ, aṃguṣṭhaḥ, puñjaṣṭhaḥ, parameṣṭhaḥ, barhiṣṭhaḥ, diviṣṭhaḥ, agniṣṭhaḥ.

tundaśokayoḥ parimṛjāpanudoḥ, "After parimṛja and apanuda, for laziness and for grief" (dwelling in the mother; dwelling among cattle; dwelling on the ground; dwelling on the right; dwelling in two; dwelling in three; dwelling in the bad; dwelling in the drill; dwelling on the peg; dwelling on the thumb; madder; heap; dwelling in the highest; peacock; dwelling with the gods; dwelling in fire). After parimṛja and apanuda respectively, when laziness and grief are expressed, ka comes: parimṛjaḥ, alasaḥ; apanudaḥ, śokā.

mūlavibhujādayaś ca, "Also after vibhuja and the rest, for a root." After vibhuja and the rest, too, ka comes when a root is expressed: vibhujaḥ, kumudam.

prade jñaḥ, "From dā and jñā after pra." After dā, "giving," and jñā, "knowing," preceded by pra, ka (laziness) comes: pradaḥ (grief), prajñāḥ.

gāpoṣ ṭak, "Ṭak after gā and pā." After gai, "sound," and pā, "drinking," following a sup, ṭak comes. The k serves to make it kit, and the ṭ serves for ṅīp. (The root of the kumuda.) baktragaḥ, samagaḥ, sūrapaḥ (a drinker of liquor), śidhupaḥ.

harater anudyamane 'c, "Ac after harati, also when it is not a matter of capacity" (great giving; wisdom). Harati, that is hṛñ, "harming": after it, in a sense that is not capacity, ac comes: aṃśaharaḥ (seizing a share). If it is capacity, ṇa is added (spoken from the mouth; the supreme ear's ...), and so bhārahāraḥ.

śaktilāṅgalāṅkuśayaṣṭitomaraghaṭaghaṭīdhanuṣṣu graheḥ, "From grahi, after śakti, lāṅgala, kuśa, yaṣṭi, tomara, ghaṭa, ghaṭī and dhanu." After graha preceded by any of these, śakti and the rest, ac comes: śaktigrahaḥ, lāṅgalagrahaḥ, kuśagrahaḥ (one who seizes a load), yaṣṭigrahaḥ, tomaragrahaḥ, ghaṭagrahaḥ, daṭigrahaḥ, dhanugrahaḥ.

vayasi ca, "Also for age." When an age is expressed, ac comes after hṛñ here: kavacaharaḥ kumāraḥ. (Spear holder; plough holder; kuśa holder; staff holder; axe holder; pot holder; bow holder.) Since the commentary explains that ac comes after hṛñ preceded by āṅ when a disposition is expressed, phalāharaḥ. Again, (the youth snatched the armour) since the commentary explains that ac also comes for dwelling after a seventh case, giving ac to ramu preceded by stambe gives stamberamaḥ, an elephant. This is cited in the commentary.

adhikaraṇe śeteḥ, "From śeti, for a locus." (One who snatched flowers.) After śīṅ, "lying down," when a locus is to be conveyed, ac comes: khaśayaḥ, udaraśayaḥ, and so on.

girau ḍaḥ, "Ḍa from śeti after giri." (Elephant.) After śīṅ following giri, ḍa comes. The ṭi is deleted, as is due for ṭi, by the special purpose of the ḍ: giriśaḥ.

care ṭaḥ, "Ṭa from cari." After cara, "moving," following a sup (one who lies in the sky; one who lies on the chest), ṭa comes. The ṭ makes it ṭit, serving ṅīp and so on: kurucaraḥ.

bhikṣāsenādāyeṣu ca, "Also after bhikṣā, senā and dāya." After cari (lies) following these, bhikṣā and the rest, ṭa also comes: bhikṣācaraḥ, senācaraḥ, dāyacaraḥ.

puro 'grato 'greṣu sarteḥ, "From sarti after puraḥ, agrataḥ and agre." (Going with a bad sound.) After sṛ, "going," following these, pura and the rest, ṭa comes: puraḥsaraḥ, going before; agrataḥsaraḥ, going before; agresaraḥ, going to the front. (Going to beg; moving with an army; moving having taken.)

pūrve kartari, "From pūrva, for an agent." After sṛ following pūrva, ṭa comes in the sense of the agent: pūrvasaraḥ.

kṛño hetutācchīlyānulomyeṣu, "From kṛñ, for a cause, for a habit, and for conformity." After kṛñ, ṭa comes for the agent who is a cause, for conveying that habit, and for an agent who conforms: bidyāśaskaraḥ, an agent who is a cause; śrāddhākaraḥ, a habit (one who makes go before); vacanakaraḥ, conforming; and so on.

kṛkamikaṃsakunmbhapātrakuśarṇīṣvanapyayasya. "Before kṛ, kami, kaṃsa, kumbha, pātra, kuśā and karṇī, of what is not an indeclinable." The visarga of a word that is not an indeclinable (one who makes famous through knowledge; one who makes faith), when these, kṛ and the rest, follow it (one who makes speech), becomes sa alone and nothing else. An example is the visarga of bidyāśaḥyi, explained above, being changed to sa before kṛ.

dibābibhāniśābrabhābhasarntānantādibahunāndikiṃlipilipibalibhaktikartṛcitrakṣetrasaṃkhyājaṃghabāgvaṅaryadtaddhanuraruṣṣu. "Before dibā, bibhā, niśā, prabhā, bhas, anta, ananta, ādi, bahu, nāndi, ki, lipi, lipo, bali, bhakti, kartṛ, citra, kṣetra, saṃkhyā, jaṃgha, bahu, uras, yad, tada, dhanus and arus." After kṛñ following these, dibā and the rest, ṭa comes: dibākaraḥ and so on (day, night, day, extreme, limitless, first, many, joy, what, smearing, good, strength, portion, maker, drawing, field, number, thigh, arm, chest, which, that, bow, suffering), up to aruskaraḥ. In the commentary it is explained that after kṛ following keṃ, yad, tad and bahu (maker of day), ac may optionally come instead; hence kiṃkaraḥ, yatkaraḥ, tatkaraḥ, bahukaraḥ.

karmaṇibhṛtau. "From karman, for a servant." After kṛñ following karman, ṭa comes when a servant is meant (one who toils in suffering): karmakaraḥ, bhṛtviḥ.

naśabdaślokakelahagāthābairacāṭusūtramantrapadeṣu. "Not before śabda, sound; śloka, verse (what-maker, which-maker, that-maker, much-maker); kalaha, quarrel; gāthā, speech; baira, enemy; cāṭu, falsehood; sūtra, sūtra; mantra, mantra; word, pada." After kṛñ following these, śabda and the rest (one who does action, that is, a servant), ṭa does not come; instead an is applied to kṛ following them, giving śabdakāraḥ and so on, up to padakāraḥyi.

stambaśakṛtīrina. "Before stamba and śakṛti, in." After kṛñ following stamā and śakṛt, in comes when grain and a calf, respectively, are meant; the n serves the vowel, and with guṇa made: stambakariḥ, drīhiḥ; śakṛtkariḥ, batsaḥ.

hara (sound-maker, word-maker) teḥdṛtināthayoḥpśau. "From harati, after dṛti and nātha, for an animal." After harati, that is, hṛñ, following dṛti and nātha, in comes for an agent that is an animal: dṛtihati, paśuḥ; nāthahariḥ (stem-maker, that is, grain; once-maker, that is, a calf, or what a buffalo has left), paśuḥ.

phalegrahirātmabhariśca. "phalegrahiḥ, and ātmambha as well." Applying in to graha preceded by phale and to bhṛñ preceded by ātmaṃ gives phalegrahiḥdaṅ and ātmambhariḥ (the wild animal with a hide; animal; marsh lion); these two are set forms.

kukṣimbhariḥc. "kukṣimbhariḥ as well." Applying in to bhṛñ preceded by kukṣiṃ (animal), kukṣimbhariḥ too is a set form.

ejeḥkhśa. "From eji, khaś." After eji following a nominal (supa) (fruit-grasper; self-grasper), khaś comes; the ś serves the purpose of śit, and the kh the purpose of mum.

arurdviṣadajantasyamuma. "Before suffering and hostile, mum for what ends in ac." (Belly-filler.) When a word bearing an affix marked with kh follows, the augment mum comes to the preceding stem ending in ac, and in the senses of suffering and hostile; the m is for the position, and the u is for pronunciation. To eji preceded by jana, khaś is given by the preceding sūtra, then guṇa, and the augment mum by this sūtra, giving janamejaya.

bātaśunītilsrāddheṣvajadheṭatudajahātibhyaḥkhśabā. "When bāta, śunī, til and srāddhā precede, khaś from aja, dheṭ, tud and jahāti." After aja preceded by bāta, dheṭ preceded by śunī, tud preceded by til, and hāk preceded by srāddhā, khaś comes; and with the augment mum given: (one who moves people) bātamajaḥ (a deer that goes like the wind); śuniṃdhayaḥ (one who drinks at a bitch); tilntudaḥ (sesame-pounder; one who discards the food of the dead); srāddhaṃjahaḥ. Before an affix marked with ś there is reduplication, as with ślu.

khityanabyayase. "Before what is marked with kh, of what is not an indeclinable." When an affix marked with kh follows, the augment muṃ comes to the stem preceding it, and if the end of that stem is a long ac, it is made short. Examples are the forms with mum shown above, and the shortening of the finals of śunī and śrādhñā.

nāsikāstanyordhmādheṭoḥ. "From dhmā and dheṭ, after nāsikā and stan." After dhmā preceded by nāsikā, and dheṭ preceded by stana, khaś also comes: nāsikandhamaḥ, stanandhayaḥ.

nāḍīmuṣṭyośca. "From nāḍī and muṣṭī as well." After dhmā and dheṭ following nāḍī and muṣṭi, khaś also comes: nāḍindhamaḥ, nāḍīndhayaḥ, nāḍīndhayaḥ, muṣṭindhamaḥ, muṣṭindhayaḥ.

udikūlerujibahoḥ. (By the rule of ghā, pā, dhma and the rest, dhma is changed to dhama before a śit affix. Nose-breaker. Breast-drinker.) "With kūla, from ruji and baha after ut." After ruji and baha preceded by ut, following kūla, khaś comes: kūlamudrujaḥ (vein-breaker, fist-breaker), kūlamudvahaḥ.

bahā (vein-drinker, fist-drinker) bhrilihaḥ. "From liha, after baha and abhra." After liha following baha and abhra, khaś comes: bahaṃlihaḥgoḥ, abhraṃlihaḥ, vāyuḥ.

parimānepacaḥ. "For a measure, from paca." After paca following a word that does the measuring of a measure (a very sick lineage; one who has attained a high lineage), khaś comes: droṇaṃpacāsthali, prasthaṃpacā.

mitankheca. "Also for mita and nakha." After paca following mita and nakha (obtaining and tasting, that is, a cow; a cloud or a thistle; wind), khaś also comes: mitaṃpacaḥ, brāhmaṇī; nakhaṃpacā, yabāgūḥ.

asūryalalāṭyordṛśatpo. "With asūrya and lalāṭa (one that cooks a full large measure; cooks a measure full), from dṛśa and tapa."

After dṛśa and tapa, following asūrya and lalāṭa respectively, khaś comes: asūrmaṃpaśyaḥ (a brahmin woman; gruel or vegetables) mukha (a face that does not look at the sun); lalāṭaṃtapaḥsūryaḥ (forehead-burner, that is, the sun).

ugraṃpaśyerammadapāṇindhamāśca. "ugraṃpaśya, irammada and pāṇindhama as well." By applying khaś to dṛśa preceded by ugra, to mada preceded by ir, and to dhmā preceded by pāṇi, ugraṃpaśya, irammada and pānindhama too are set forms. In the commentary it is explained that khaś also comes after dhmā following kara; hence karandhamaḥ.

priyabaśebadaḥkhca. "With priya and baśa, khac from bada." After bada following preya and baśa, khac comes (one who looks with fierce force; one who delights in liquor; hand-scrutinizer). The c serves the vowel, and the kh serves the purpose of khit: griyaṃbadaḥ, baśambadaḥ. In the commentary it is explained that khac comes after gama following a nominal (halved and divided); hence phujigamaḥ.

bihāyaspihaca. "And biha for yihāyasa." After gam following bihāyas, khac comes, and bihayas is to be changed into biha (one who speaks joy; one who speaks what is good): bihaṃgamaḥ. In the commentary it is explained that optionally khac is treated as marked with ṅ, and the anusvāra is elided (hand-goer); hence bhujigaḥ, bihaṃgaḥ, and so on.

dviṣaparayaḥtāpiḥ. "With dviṣa and para, from tāpi." After tapa ending in ṇic, following dviṣa and para, khac comes. (One who goes in the sky, that is, a bird.)

khacihrasvaḥ. "Before khac, short." When khac follows, the penultimate (upadhā) arising from ṇic (action-goer; sky-goer), where a woman is not meant, becomes short. To tāpi preceded by dviṣa and para, khac is applied by the preceding sūtra, ṇi is dropped where there is no iṭ, and by this sūtra the penultimate is shortened: dviṣaṃtapaḥ. If it is a woman: dviśatītāpaḥ.

bāciyamoprate. "For a vow, yama after bāca." When it applies to a vow of silence, khac comes after yamu following dāca.

bācaṃyamapuraṃdarauca. "bācaṃyama and puraṃdara as well." (Enemy-tormentor; tormentor of others.) By applying khac to yamu preceded by bāca and to dṛ preceded by pura (tormentor of a hostile woman), bāciyama (one who does not speak, whose speech is restrained, or who has cut off speech) and puraṃdara (destroyer of towns, that is, Indra) are set forms.

sarbesahaḥ. "With sarba, from saha." After saha preceded by sarba, khac comes: sarbaṃsahaḥ (forbearing first). In the commentary it is explained that khac also comes after dṛ preceded by bhaga; hence bhagaṃdaraḥ.

sarbakūlābhrakaryiṣeṣukaṣaḥ. "With sarba, kūla, abhra and kariṣa, from kaṣa." After kaṣa following these three, sarba and the rest, khac comes: sarbaṃkaṣaḥ, khalaḥ; kūlaṃkaṣaḥ, najīḥ; abhraṃkaṣaḥ, giriḥ; karīṣaṃkaṣaḥ, pātyā.

medhartibhayeṣukṛñaḥ. (Sign-destroyer.) "With medha, riti and bhaya, from kṛñ." After kṛñ following midha, riti and bhaya, khac comes: medhaṃkaraḥ, ṛtiṅkaraḥ, (one who harms all, that is, a villain) bhayaṃkaraḥ (river), abhayaṃkaraḥ (mountain).

kṣemabriyamadreca. (Wind.) "With kṣema, priya and madra as well." After kṛñ following kṣema, preya and madra, khac comes, and aṇ comes as well: kṣemaṃkaraḥ, kṣemaṃkāraḥ (intelligence-maker; truth-maker); priyaṃkaraḥ (fear-maker); madruṃkaraḥ (maker of fearlessness), madrakāraḥ.

āśitebhupaḥ karaṇabhābayoḥ. "With āśita, from bhū, for the instrument and the state." After bhū following āśita, when it applies to the instrument and to the state (maker of happiness), khac comes (maker of joy): alamāśidaṃbhabaodanaḥ, sukhanāśitiṃbhabaṃ (maker of a deep melody).

saṃjñāāṃbhṛtṝbṛjidhārishitapidamaḥ. "From bhṛ, tṝ, bṛ, ji, dhāri, sahi, tapi and dama, for a name." After these roots following a nominal, khac comes in a name: biśvambharaḥ, rathaṃtaraṃ, patimbarā, śatruñjayaḥ, basundharaḥ (you have eighty powers of food; you have eighty happinesses), śatrunsahaḥ, śadrunhapaḥ, arindamaḥ.

gamaśca. "From gama as well." After gam following a nominal, khac also comes in a name: plurbaṃgamaḥ, panthānaḥ, hṛdayaṃgamāḥ (all-bearer; chariot-crosser; one who chooses you; victorious over enemies; holder of wealth), bācaḥ.

antāntyatādhvoraspārakhānandeṣuḍaḥ. "With anta (one who forbears enemies; enemy-tormentor; enemy-tamer), antyata, adhva, uras, pāra, kha and ananta, ḍa." After gam following these stems, anta and the rest (going before; path; descending into the heart), ḍa comes; the ṭi being due, the ṭi is dropped, the ḍ whose purpose is to qualify it being dropped: antagaḥ (goer to the extreme), andyatagaḥ, adhvagaḥ, uragaḥ, pāragaḥ, khagaḥ, anantagaḥ.

urasaḥslopaśca. "And elision of the s of uras." When gam follows, the s of uras is elided; the example has already been given.

sarbapanhayośca. "With sarba and panna as well." After gam following sarba and panna (one who goes far; path-goer; belly-goer; one who goes to the far side; one who goes in the sky; one who goes to the limitless), ḍa also comes: sarbagaḥ, pannagaḥ. In the commentary it is explained that optionally khac comes after gam following uras; hence uraṃgamaḥ.

suduro'dhikaraṇe. "From su and dur, for the locus." After gam following su and dur, ḍa comes for the locus: sugaḥ, durgaḥ (one who goes everywhere; one who does not go on feet). In the commentary it is explained that not only after these but also after many others ḍa comes to gama (belly-goer); hence nirgaḥ, sarbatragaḥ, turagaḥ, grāmagaḥ, and so on.

aśiṣihanaḥ. "For a wish, from han." After hana following a nominal (one who goes well; hard to go), ḍa comes when a wish is expressed: śatrūhaḥ, kleśāpahaḥ, tamo'phaḥ, duḥkhapahaḥ, and so on.

lakṣaṇejā (one who does not go; one who goes everywhere; swift-goer; village-goer) yāpatyoṣṭak. "With jāya and pati, for a characteristic." After han following jāya and pati, when it applies to a characteristic, ṭak comes (destroyer of enemies; han preceded by apa; destroyer of afflictions; destroyer of darkness; destroyer of suffering). The k serves the purpose of kit, and the ṭ the purpose of dīp.

By the rule on gama, han and the rest, the penultimate vowel (upadhā) is elided, and by the rule on the h of hanta, h is changed to gh: jāyāghno nā, "a man who kills his wife"; patighnī strī, "a woman who kills her husband."

amanuṣyakartṛke ca. "And also where the agent is not human." When an agent that is not human is to be understood as the agent, ṭak comes after han following a nominal: śleṣmaghnaṃ trikaṭukaṃ; pittabhnaṃ, "bile-destroying," ghṛtaṃ, "ghee"; vātaghnaṃ, "wind-destroying" (gloss: wife-killer, that is, a man; husband-killer, that is, a woman), tailaṃ, "sesame oil."

pāṇighatāḍaghauśilpini. "pāṇigha and tāḍagha, for a craftsman." By adding ṭak to han preceded by pāṇi and by tāḍa, pāṇigha (the craftsman who strikes with the palm; gloss: phlegm-destroying, the three pungents) and tāḍagha are set forms (nipātana). The commentary also says that rājaga, formed by adding ṭak to han preceded by rāja, is likewise a set form.

āḍhyasubhagasthūlapalitanghānthapriyeṣu cvyartheṣacvau kṛñaḥ karaṇe khyun. To uḍhya, subhaga, sthūla, palita, nagna, andha and priya (gloss: a craftsman), in the sense of cvi where cvi is absent, khyun comes after kṛñ for the instrument. After kṛñ following these, āḍhya and the rest (gloss: king-slayer), in the sense of something newly coming to be, where cvi has not been added, khyun comes for the instrument and for the agent. The n serves accent, the kh serves the purpose of khit, that is, of the augment mum, and yu is changed to ana; thus: āḍhyaṃkaraṇaṃ, sughagaṃkarṇaṃ, sthūlaṃkaraṇaṃ, balitaṃkaraṇaṃ, nagnaṃkaraṇaṃ, andhaṃkaraṇaṃ, priyaṃkaraṇaṃ.

kartaribhubaḥ khiṣṇucakhukañau. "For the agent, after bhū, khiṣṇuc and khukañ." After bhū following āḍhya and the rest, in the sense of something newly coming to be, where cvi has not been added (gloss: making rich, making fortunate, making stout, making grey-haired, making naked, making blind, making joyful), khiṣṇuc and khukañ come for the agent. The c serves accent, the ñ serves vṛddhi, and the two kh's serve the augment mum; guṇa being applied, we get āḍhyaṃbhaviṣṇu, āḍhyaṃbhābukaḥ, and so on through briyaṃphaniṣṇuḥ and priyaṃbhābukaḥ.

satsūdviṣadruhaduhayujavidabhidachidajinyaḥ kvipa. "sat, sū, dviṣa, druha, duha, yuja, vida, bhida, chida, ji and nī take kvip." Preceded by a nominal or by a preverb (upasarga): sat, that is ṣana, reverence on every side; ṣū, the birth of living beings (gloss: became rich, possessed of attachment, became joyful); dviṣa, enmity; druha, harming; duha, milking; yujir, joining; vida, knowing; bhidir, splitting apart; chidir, cutting into pieces; ji, conquering; nī, obtaining. To these, kvip comes. The p serves the augment tuk, the k serves the purpose of kit, the i is for pronunciation, and the v is also elided. Thus suciṣana, or "pure"; or else, the n being dropped and tuk being added, upaniṣat, "close reverence"; aṇḍasūḥ, "egg-born"; dviṭ, "adversary"; dhuṭ, "evil one"; godtuk, "cow-milker"; suyuk, "one who joins with happiness"; prabhit, "one who thoroughly splits apart"; pracchita, "cut in two"; mitrajit, "conqueror of friends"; grāmaṇīḥ. Since the commentary explains that the n of nī after grāma and after agra is changed to ṇ, the n is changed to ṇ.

bhajoṇviḥ. "From bhaja, ṇvi." After bhaja following a nominal, ṇvi comes. The ṇ serves vṛddhi, and since the i, which is for pronunciation, is also dropped, we get ardhabhāk and pādabhāk.

chandasisahaḥ (gloss: the village's slanderer). "In metrical language, from saha." In metrical language (chandas), ṇvi also comes after saha: prasāṭ, prasāṭ.

anebaheḥ kvip. "From vahi after ana, kvip." Kvip comes to vaha preceded by ana; samprasāraṇa is also applied, and between them the affix ḍa (gloss: a half share, a quarter share) is also added, giving anaḍuh; adding su to this gives anaḍāna.

janasanakhanakramagamobiṭ. "From jan, san (gloss: perfect patience), khan, krama and gama, viṭ." Viṭ comes to these roots following a nominal or a preverb. The ṭ serves the purpose of dīp, and by the rule on vi, the v is elided. chanāsi: "In metrical language." In metrical language, when viṭ or vin follows (gloss: bull of the herd), the roots with a nasal become āt. To these roots with viṭ, the nasal ones take ā, sandhi is applied and viṭ is dropped: ajāḥ, goṣāḥ, kūpakhāḥ, udadhikrāḥ, agregāḥ.

sanoteranaḥ. "Of sanoti lacking its n." When it is preceded by a nominal stem or a preverb that is a cause for changing s to ṣ, the s of sanoti lacking its n is changed to ṣ, as in goṣāḥ, the example given above.

duhaḥ kapaghaśca (gloss: unborn, cow-giver, well-digger, ocean's wave, one who goes to the front). "From duha, kap, and also gha." After duha following a nominal, kap comes, and h also becomes gh. The p serves accent and the k serves the purpose of kit: kāmadughā.

maṃtreśvebahokthaśaspuroḍāśoṇvin. "In a mantra, from śvetapaha, ukthaśas and puroḍāśa, ṇvin." Adding ṇvin to śvetapaha and the others gives śvetabāḥ, ukthaśāḥ and puroḍāḥ, which are set forms used in reciting mantras.

ātomaninkvanipabanipaśca. "From āt, manin (gloss: wish-milker), and kvanip and panip as well." To a root ending in ā following a nominal, in the sense of the action, manin, kvanip and banīp come. Of those three affixes, the affixes ḍava, the two p's and the n serve accent, the three i's are for pronunciation, and the k serves the purpose of kit. Thus, with tāvanin, sudāmā, "giving well"; with kvanip, sudābā, "giving well"; with kanīp, bhuridābā, and so on. Since the commentary explains that these affixes also apply to many other roots that do not end in ā, there is sugnbha and so on.

kvipca. "And kvip as well." Whether following a nominal or with no nominal, and, by the rule beginning "for all that is not saṃbuddhi, standing...," whether a preverb comes before or not (gloss: earth-giver or gold-giver), kvip comes to all roots in the sense of the action: ukhāsrat (gloss: going at ease), parṇadhvat, sasrāṭ, birāṭ, and so on without end.

anteḥ. "Of anti." When a nominal stem or a preverb that is a cause comes before it, the letter n of an, "to breathe," becomes ṇ: prāṇ, after kvip has been added.

arciśuciruciciusṛpichadichṛdibhyais. arciḥ (gloss: branch fallen), śuciḥ (gloss: leaf fallen, beautiful all over, beautiful in every way), ruciḥ, cihuḥ, sṛpiḥ, chadiḥ and chṛdi take is. From these roots, is comes in the sense of the action: arciḥ, śociḥ, rociḥ, cehiḥ (gloss: living being), sarbiḥ, chadiḥ, chardiḥ.

dhanartichakṣiṅprīpapitrapijaniyajerus. From dhan, arti, cakṣiṅ, prī, bapi, trapi, jan and yaj, us. To these roots, us comes: dhanuḥ, aruḥ, cakṣuḥ, paruḥ, bapuḥ, trapuḥ, januḥ, yajuḥ (gloss: worship, pure, blazing, angry, fresh butter, vomiting).

sarbadhātubhyastran. "From all roots, tran."

From all roots, bhū and the rest, tran comes: cetraṃ, patraṃ, and so on. The commentary says that when is, man, tran (gloss: bow, going, eye, protecting, body, shame, born, worship) and kvip follow, chād and the rest become short; hence chadiḥ, chadmā, chattvaṃ, and so on.

jvaratvarasṛbyavimadāmupadhāyāśca. Of jvaraḥ (gloss: asking; vessel, or leaf), tvaraḥ, sṛviḥ, aviḥ and map, and of the penultimate (upadhā) as well. When the affix kvip, or an affix beginning with a jhal consonant and marked with k or ṅ, follows, the v of the penultimate of the two, jvar and tvar, together with its vowel, and the final v of the two, sriv and av (gloss: vomiting; crooked; suffering), and the final v of mav together with the a of the penultimate, become ū. Kvip is added to jvar and to tār; kvip is dropped entirely; and by this sūtra the change to ū is made. Thus with su, jūḥ; with au, jūrau; with su, tūḥ; with au, tūrau.

Kvip is added to sṛv; kvip is dropped; v becomes ū; and by applying yaṇ to ik before ac, with su we get sūḥ, and with au, srupau. Kvip is added to av; kvip is dropped; v becomes ū. Since the commentary explains that vṛddhi is applied when the change to ū is made, vṛddhi is applied, and au is established. With jan placed before it: janauḥ (gloss: blazing), janāvau (gloss: swift).

Kvip is added to mav; kvip is dropped; v together with the a becomes ū; and drawing on this, with su we get mūḥ (gloss: going), and with o, muvau.

rāllopaḥ. "After r, elision." When kvip, or an affix beginning with a jhal consonant and marked with k or ṅ, follows, the ch and the v that come after r are elided, and r too becomes ū. To mūrcha and dhurvi (gloss: protector of men) kvip is added and kvip is dropped; ch and v are also dropped; and what is like ū is lengthened. Thus with su, mūḥ (gloss: binding); with au, ṅhūḥ (gloss: two bindings).

gamaḥkvau. "Of gam, before kvi." When kvip follows, the m of gam is elided and the augment tuk also comes: aṃgagat, and so on. The commentary explains that with yam, man and tan too, before kvip, the nasal is elided and the augment tuk comes (gloss: attachment, extended): yat, mat, tat, and so on. Again, the commentary says that before kvip the nasal of yam, gam (gloss: limb-goer), man and tan, together with the penultimate, becomes ū: agreyūḥ, agregūḥ, agremūḥ, agretūḥ.

supyajātauṇinistācchīlye. "After a nominal, where it is not a class, ṇini, for a habitual disposition." After a root following a nominal (gloss: worship, reverence, conquering), in the sense of an action that does not express a class, when a disposition toward it is to be understood, ṇini comes. The i of the n is for pronunciation, and the ṇ (gloss: worshipping the sign, going to the root, knowing the supreme, extended at the tip) serves the purpose of ṇit. Adding ṇini to vada preceded by eva and to bhyaja preceded by uṣṇa gives evampādī (gloss: one who speaks thus) and uṣṇabhoji (gloss: hot food).

manaḥ. "From man." After man following a nominal, ṇini comes even where there is no habitual disposition: paṭumānī, "one who thinks himself skilled."

ātmanekhaśca. "For oneself, khaś." After man following a nominal, when its object is oneself, khaś comes, and ṇini as well. In the case of khaś, since the ś is marked, yak and mum are added: paṇḍitamanyaḥ, paṇḍitamānī.

icekāco'mrapratyayavacca. "ic: for a single-vowel stem, also as with the affix am." When an affix marked with kh follows, if the nominal stem before it is a single one ending in a vowel of the ic class, then mum is added and the procedure is also carried out as for am, the second case ending. Adding khaś to man preceded by go and by strī (gloss: one who fancies himself learned) gives gāṃmanyaḥ and strīṃmānyaḥ.

bhūteyajaḥ. "In the past, from yaj." After yaj following a nominal, when the agent of a past action is to be understood, ṇini comes: agniṣṭomayājī.

karmaṇihanaḥ. "For the object, from han." After han following a nominal, in the sense of the object (karman), ṇini comes (gloss: one who thinks himself a cow, one who thinks herself a woman). By the rule on the h of hanti becoming gh, and by the rule on the t of han and the rest, n is changed to t: pitṛghātī.

brahmabhruṇavṛteṣuḥ. "With brahma, bhruṇa and vṛt" (gloss: one who has performed the fire sacrifice). After han following brahma, bhruṇa and vṛt, in the past, kvip comes: brahmahā, bhruṇahā, vṛtahā.

sukarmapāpamatrapuṇyeṣuḥkṛñaḥ. "With sukarma, pāpha, matra and puṇya (gloss: father-killer), from kṛñ." After kṛñ following sukarma and these others, when the past is to be understood, kvip comes, and the augment tuk is added (gloss: slayer of a brahmin): sukarmakṛt (gloss: embryo; the obstructer), pāpakṛt, matrakrit, purṇyakṛt.

dṛśeḥkvanip. "From dṛś, kvanip." After dṛś, in the past, kvanip comes. The p serves the purpose of pit, the k serves the purpose of kit, and the i is for pronunciation: pāradṛśvā.

rājanikarmaṇe. "With rājan, for the object." After kṛñ and after yudha following rājan (gloss: did good deeds, did evil, merely did, did meritorious deeds), for the action of fighting, in the past, kvanip comes: rājākṛtva, "made by the king"; rājayudhvā, "who fought the king." Since the commentary explains that kvanip also applies after kṛñ and yudha following saha (gloss: who has seen the far shore): sahakṛtvā, "made together"; sahayudhvā, "who fought together."

saptamyāṃjanerḍaḥ. "With the seventh, ḍa from jani." After jani following a nominal that has the sense of the seventh case ending, ḍa comes; the ḍ serves to elide the ṭi. Ḍa is added to jan preceded by ambu: ambujaṃ.

pañcamyāmajātau. "With the fifth, where not a class." After jan following a nominal that has the sense of the fifth, when it does not express a class, ḍa comes: padmajaḥ.

upasargecasaṃjñāyāṃ. "And with a preverb, for a name." After jan following a preverb (upasarga), for a name, ḍa comes (gloss: born from water): prajā, sujaḥ.

suyajodvanipa. "From su and yaj, dvanip." After su and yaj, in the past, dvanip comes. The p (gloss: born from a lotus) serves the purpose of tuk, the i is for pronunciation, and the ṅ serves the purpose of ṅit: sutvā, yajvā.

ktaktapatūniṣṭhā. "kta and ktavatu are niṣṭhā." The affixes kta and ktavatu (gloss: creatures, well-born) are given the name niṣṭhā. Of these two, kta occurs in the sense of the state and of the object, expressing the past, while ktavatu occurs in expressing the agent. Of these two affixes (gloss: made pure, did worship), the k serves the purpose of kit, and the u serves the purpose of usuṭ. Adding kta to snā and to stu gives snātaṃ mayaḥ and stutaṃ buddhaḥ tvayā. Adding ktavatu to kṛñ gives viṣṇuḥ viṣṇaṃ kṛtavān.

niṣṭhāyāṃṇyadarthe. "Niṣṭhā in the sense of ṇyat." This is the general statement that the two affixes named niṣṭhā also occur in the senses in which the affix ṇyat, explained above, applies.

kṣiyodīrghāt. "From the long vowel of kṣī."

(Gloss: bathing was done by me; the Buddha was praised by you.) When a niṣṭhā affix follows (gloss: Viṣṇu pervades), the i of kṣī is lengthened, and after the long vowel the t of kta and of ktavatu is also changed to n: kṣīṇavān, kṣīnaḥ.

śryukaḥkiti. "From śri and from uk, before what is marked with k." After the root śri, and also after other roots having a single vowel and roots ending in uk, iṭ does not come before kṛt and the other affixes marked with k: śritaḥ, śritavāna (gloss: shows reverence); bhūtaḥ (gloss: arisen), bhūtavān (gloss: makes exhausted; exhausted). The commentary says that before niṣṭhā, ūrṇu becomes short: urṇutaḥ, "covered."

radābhyāṃniṣṭhātanaḥpūrvasyacaṅaḥ. "After r and d, the t of niṣṭhā becomes n, and so does the preceding d." After roots ending in the letter r and (gloss: by reverence) in d, the t of niṣṭhā that follows becomes n, and the d before it also becomes n. Kta is added to the root śṝ; by the rule on ṝ becoming it, ṝ becomes it; by the rule that the aṇ replacing ṛ is followed by r, r is added; by hal and the rest it is lengthened; and by this sūtra t is changed to n: śīrṇaḥ. Kta is added to bhidir, and by this sūtra both t and d are changed to n: bhinnaḥ.

saṃyogāderātodhātoryaṇvataḥ. "From a root ending in ā, containing yaṇ, and beginning with a conjunct." After a root ending in ā that has in its penultimate a letter of the yaṇ class and begins with a conjunct consonant, the t of the following (gloss: harmed) niṣṭhā is also changed to n: drāṇaḥ, glānaḥ, and so on (gloss: split apart).

lrādibhyaśca. "And from lū and the rest." After lū and the rest, too, the t of the following niṣṭhā is changed to n: lūnaḥ, jīnaḥ (gloss: aged). The commentary says that du and gu become long before niṣṭhā: pūnaḥ, gūnaḥ.

ktaoditaśca (gloss: to be disparaged; joy exhausted). "And from those marked with o." After roots marked with o, too, the t of niṣṭhā is changed to n. Kta is added to bhujo (gloss: crooked); by the rule on cu becoming ku, and by this sūtra, t is changed to n (gloss: cut). Kta is added to jyīpa, and by grahijyā and the rest, samprasāraṇa: bhyagnaḥ. To ohāk, by this sūtra t becomes n; by ghumāsthā and the rest (gloss: gone) it is changed to īt; with pra before it: prahīṇaḥ.

svvādayo'nuditaḥ. "Sū and the rest are not marked with u." Sū and the rest, namely ṣūṅ, giving birth to living beings; dūṅ, tormenting; dīṅ, wasting away; mīṅ, harming; rīṅ, listening (gloss: made to move); līṅ, embracing; and vrīṅ, obscuring, are not called u-marked, and, as with those marked with o (gloss: abandoned), the t of niṣṭhā is changed to n: sūnaḥ, dūnaḥ, vīnaḥ, mīnaḥ, rīṇaḥ, līnaḥ, vrīṇaḥ, sūnavān, and so on.

sphāyaḥsphīniṣṭhāyāṃ. "Before niṣṭhā, sphāyī becomes sphī." Before niṣṭhā, sphāyī becomes sphī: sphītaḥ. Since the commentary explains that it optionally becomes sphā: sphātaḥ (gloss: increased).

dravamūrtisparśayoḥśyaḥ. "For a solid form of a liquid and for touch, of śyā" (gloss: born, tormented, wasted, harmed, listened, embraced, obscured, already born). When a congealed liquid or touch is expressed, śyā undergoes samprasāraṇa before niṣṭhā (gloss: increased): śīto vāyuḥ, "a cool wind."

śyoñasārśe. "From śyā, where it is not touch." After śyā, the letter t of niṣṭhā becomes n when touch is not expressed. Kta is added to śya; by the previous sūtra, samprasāraṇa; and by this sūtra t is changed to n: śīnaṃ ghṛtaṃ.

pratiśca. "And from prati." Since śyā following prati undergoes samprasāraṇa before niṣṭhā: pratiśīnaṃ, pratiśīnavān.

vibhāṣābhyavapūrvasya. "Optionally, when preceded by abhi or ava." Śyā preceded by abhi or ava optionally undergoes samprasāraṇa before niṣṭhā: abhiśīnaṃ, abhiśyānaṃ (gloss: a lump of ghee), avaśīnaṃ, avaśyānaṃ.

añco'navādāne. "From añc, where it is not the source." (Gloss: arisen; congealed, respectively.) When not connected with the expression of a source, the t of niṣṭhā after añc becomes n; by the rule on cu becoming ku, and by the rule on what is not marked with i and the rest, the n is dropped: agnaḥ.

divo'vijigīṣāyāṃ (gloss: put to use). "From div, where it is not the wish for victory" (gloss: congealed all over). The letter t of niṣṭhā after div is changed to n when victory is not expressed. Kta is added to diva; by the rule that ch and v take ś and ūṭh, also before a nasal, v is changed to ū; and by ik before ac (gloss: worshipped) it is changed to yaṇ: dyūnaḥ. When victory is expressed, t is changed to n: dyūtāḥ.

nirvāṇo'vāte. "Nirvāṇa, where it is not wind." Formed by adding kta to vā, going, preceded by nir, nirvāṇa is a set form (nipātana) when wind is not expressed. When it is wind, t is not changed to n: vādaḥ.

śuṣakaḥ. "From śuṣ, k." After śuṣ, the t of niṣṭhā is changed to k: śuṣkaḥ.

vacovaḥ (gloss: clear). "From paca, v." After pac, the t of niṣṭhā is changed to v, and by changing cu to ku (gloss: fire): pakvaḥ.

kṣāyomaḥ. "From kṣai, m." After kṣai, the t of niṣṭhā is changed to m (gloss: wind): kṣāmaḥ, kṣāmavān.

prastyo'nyaratasyāṃ. "Optionally from prastyā." After prastyā (gloss: dried), the t of niṣṭhā optionally becomes m: prastīmaḥ, prastītaḥ.

styaḥpravūrvasya. "Of styā preceded by pra." Styā preceded by pra (gloss: ripened) undergoes samprasāraṇa before niṣṭhā; the example has already been shown.

kṣivakṛ (gloss: wasted) śollāghāḥ. Kṣiva (gloss: swollen), kṛśa (gloss: thin; capable), ullāgha and the rest. Kṣepa, kṛśa (gloss: fully able) and ullagha are forms in which the t of kta is made into the letter a, as set forms.

āditaśca. "And from those marked with ā." Iṭ does not come before niṣṭhā following roots marked with ā.

tica. "And before t." When a kṛt affix beginning with t follows, the a in the penultimate of cara and of phala becomes ut. Kta is added to palā preceded by pra; by the previous sūtra iṭ does not come; and by this sūtra the penultimate becomes ut, and by a set form t is changed to l: praphullaḥ.

nudavidondatrāghrābhyo'nyatarasyāṃ. "Optionally from nud, vid, und, trā and ghrī." After nud and these others, the t of niṣṭhā optionally becomes n: nunnaḥ, nuttāḥ; vinnaḥ, vittaḥ; unnaḥ, uttaḥ; trāṇaḥ, trātaḥ; ghracaḥ, ghrātaḥ; hrīṇaḥ, hrītaḥ (gloss: fully blossomed).

śviditoniṣṭhāyāṃ. "Before niṣṭhā, from śvi and from those marked with i." Iṭ does not come before niṣṭhā following śvi and roots marked with i, just as above iṭ was not added to undi (gloss: certain; knew).

naṅtyā (gloss: klé, glé) khyāpṛ (gloss: born) mūrchimadī (gloss: smelled). Not of dhyā, khyā (gloss: ashamed), prī, mūrchi and ma.

After dhyā and these others, the t of niṣṭhā does not become n: dhyātaḥ, khyātaḥ, pūrtaḥ (gloss: protected, or filled), mūrṅdhaḥ, maṅtaḥ (gloss: intoxicated).

vittobhogapritātayoḥ. "Vittaḥ, for wealth and for being well known." By adding kta to vit, knowing, vittaḥ is a set form (nipātana) when it expresses wealth or being well known: vittaḥ pratītaḥ, vittaṃ dhanaṃ.

ṛṇamādhamarṇye (gloss: mind; dashé; ut where not preceded by a labial; stupefied; by the rule of elision after r; dropped). "Ṛṇaṃ, for a debt in excess." By adding kta to ṛ, going, ṛṇaṃ is a set form when it expresses a debt in excess: ādhamarṇaṃ.

iṭniṣṭhāyāṃ. "Before niṣṭhā, iṭ." After kuṣa preceded by nir (gloss: known as famous; known wealth), iṭ comes before the following niṣṭhā: niṭhkuṣitaḥ.

vastikṣudhoriṭ. "From vasti and kṣudha, iṭ." Before niṣṭhā and ktvā following vasati and kṣudha, iṭ always comes. By pacasvapi and the rest (gloss: one who carries a debt), the change by samprasāraṇa is made: uṣitaḥ (gloss: dwelt), kṣuditaḥ (gloss: hungry).

añcepūjāyāṃ. "Of añc, for worship" (gloss: robbed). After añc in the sense of worship, aṭ comes before niṣṭhā and ktvā: añcitaḥ devaḥ.

kliśaḥniṣṭhayoḥ. "From kliśa, before niṣṭhā." After kliśa, iṭ optionally comes before the following niṣṭhā: kliśitaḥ, kliṣṭaḥ. Since the commentary explains that iṭ optionally comes before niṣṭhā after vam, after japi, and after śvas preceded by vi and by āṅ: vamitaḥ, vanta; travitaḥ, jabtaḥ; viśvasitaḥ (gloss: the god worshipped), viśvastaḥ; āśvasitaḥ, āśvasta.

pūduśca. "And from pūṅ." After pūṅ, iṭ (gloss: by vraścabhrasja and the rest, ś becomes ṣ) optionally comes before niṣṭhā and ktvā.

pūṅaḥktvaca. "From pūṅ, ktvā as well." After pūṅ, a niṣṭhā with iṭ, and (gloss: vomited; muttered) ktvā as well, are not designated as marked with k. By the previous sūtra iṭ is made optional, and in the iṭ alternative guṇa is applied by this sūtra: pavitaḥ, pūtaḥ.

niṣṭhāśīṅsvidimidikṣīdidhṝṣaḥ. "From śīṅ, svidi, midi, kṣvidi and dhṛṣa, niṣṭhā." A niṣṭhā with iṭ following śīṅ and these others is not marked with k; iṭ being added and guṇa applied: śayitaḥ, sveditaḥ, meditaḥ, kṣveditaḥ, dharṣitaḥ.

ādikarmaṇiktaḥ (gloss: purified, or clean) kartarica. "For the initial action, kta, and for the agent as well." For the initial action, that is, an action that consists in beginning an act, kta comes for both the object and the agent.

vibhāṣābhāvādikarmaṇoḥ. "Optionally, for the state and for the initial action" (gloss: lay down, moistened, friend). Before a niṣṭhā given in the sense of the state or of the initial action, iṭ optionally comes: prasveditayaḥ, prasvinna; meditaḥ, minna; and so on.

mṛṣastitikṣāyāṃ. "From mṛṣa, for forbearance." When mṛṣa is used for forbearance, a niṣṭhā with iṭ is not designated as marked with k: marṣitaḥ.

udupadhāṅbhāvādikarmaṇiranyatarasyāṃ. "Optionally, after a root with u as its penultimate, for the state and for the initial action" (gloss: thoroughly moistened; friend). After roots with u as their penultimate, a niṣṭhā with iṭ given in the sense of the state or of the initial action is optionally designated as marked with k (gloss: was forbearing): pradyotitaḥ (gloss: thoroughly bright), pradyutitaḥ, and so on.

nopadhātthaphāndādvā. "Optionally, after a root with n as its penultimate and ending in th or ph." After roots with n as their penultimate and ending in th or ph, a niṣṭhā with iṭ is optionally designated as marked with k: manthitaḥ, mathitaḥ; guṃphitaḥ, guphitaḥ; and so on.

niṣṭhāyvaṃseṭvi. "Before a niṣṭhā with iṭ." Before a following niṣṭhā with iṭ, ṇic is elided: bhāvetaḥ, bhāvitavān, and so on.

ānikarmaṇi. "For the initial action." Before a niṣṭhā given to śakli in the sense of the initial action, iṭ (gloss: churned) optionally does not come (gloss: moved; moved): śaktaḥ, śakitaḥ.

kṣubdasvāṃtadhvaṃtalagnamliṭaviribdhaphāṃṭavāḍhānimanthamanastamaḥsaktāvisyaṣṭasvaranāāsabhṛśeṣu. Kṣubda (gloss: arisen), svāṃta, dhvaṃta, lagna, mliṭa, viribdha, phāṃṭa and vāḍhā, for churning, mind, darkness, being joined, indistinct sound, tone, ease and swiftness. Adding kta to kṣu (gloss: able) bha, moving; svan and dhvan, sound; lagi, being joined; mleccha, indistinct sound; vṛ and rebṛ, sound; phāṃṭ, going; and vāhu, exerting oneself, the forms kṣubda, svāṃta, dhvāṃta, lagna, mliṭa, diribdha, phāṃṭa and vāḍha are set forms when they express, respectively, churning, mind, darkness, being joined, indistinct sound, tone, ease and swiftness.

dhṛṣaśaśīvaiyate. "Dhṛṣa and śasaṃ, for being puffed up." When being puffed up, that is, lofty boldness, is expressed, iṭ does not come before niṣṭhā after dhṛṣ and śaśi: dṛṣṭaḥ, viśaśtaḥ.

dṛḍhaḥsthūlabalayoḥ. "Dṛḍha, for stout and for strong." By adding kta to dṛhi, blazing, dṛḍha is a set form when it expresses stout or strong.

parivṛḍhaḥ. "Parivṛḍha." By adding kta to vṛhi, increasing, preceded by pari, parivṛḍhaḥ is a set form when it expresses a lord (gloss: disobedient; harmed).

kṛchugahanayoḥkaṣaḥ. "For difficult and for deep, from kaṣ." When difficult or deep is expressed, iṭ does not come before niṣṭhā after kaṣ: kaṣṭo'gniḥ, kaṣṭaḥ parvataḥ.

ghuṣiraviśabdana. "From ghuṣi, where it is not a particular kind of sound." After ghuṣi, where it is not a particular kind of sound, iṭ does not come before niṣṭhā: ghuṣṭā rajjuḥ (gloss: rope). Where it is a particular kind of sound, iṭ is added: avaghuṣitaṃ vākyamāha (gloss: spoke words).

ardeḥsaṃnivibhyaḥ. "Of ardi, after saṃ, ni and vi" (gloss: fire; mountain). After ard following saṃ, ni and vi, iṭ does not come before niṣṭhā: samarṇṇaḥ, nyarṇṇaḥ, vyarṇaḥ.

abheścāvidūrye. "And after abhi, for what is not far." When ard after abhi is used for what is not far, iṭ does not come before niṣṭhā: abhyarṇṇaḥ.

ṇeraṅhyapanevṛttaṃ. "Of what has ṇi, for reading, vṛttaṃ." By adding kta to vṛta ending in ṇic, vṛttaṃ is a set form (gloss: eaten together, eaten for certain, eaten in excess) when it is used for reading.

vādāntaśāntapūrṇadāṣṭaspaṣṭachannajñaptāḥ. "Optionally dānta, śānta, pūrṇa, dāṣṭa, spaṣṭa, channa and jñapta." Adding kta to these when they end in ṇic, namely damu and (gloss: eating closely in excess) śamu, being calm; pūrī, being satisfied; dasu, placing near; spaśa, vessel; chada, covering; and jña, firm application, dānta and the rest are optionally set forms. Alternatively, iṭ being added: damitaḥ (gloss: tamed, calmed, filled, fanged, cleared, covered, firmly applied), śamitaḥ, pūritaḥ, dasitaḥ, spaśitaḥ, śaditaḥ, jñānaḥ, and so on.

ruṣyamatvarasaṃghuṣāsvanāṃ. "Of ruṣa, ama, tvara, saṃghuṣa and āsvan." Before a niṣṭhā following ruṣ and these others, iṭ optionally does not come: ruṣṭaḥ, aṃtaḥ, tūrṇaḥ, saṃghuṣṭaḥ, āsvaṃtaḥ. Alternatively, iṭ being added: ruṣitaḥ, amitaḥ, tvaritaḥ, saṃghuṣitaḥ, āsvānitaḥ.

hṛṣerlomasu. "Of hṛṣa, for body hair." After hṛṣ, when body hair is expressed, iṭ optionally does not come before niṣṭhā: hṛṣṭaḥ, hṛṣitaḥ. (Gloss, as cited in the commentary: angry, sick, swift, proclaimed all around, proclaimed everywhere.)

pismitapratighātayośca. "And also vismita and pratighāta." By adding kta to ṣmiṅ, smiling slightly, preceded by vi, and to han, harming, preceded by prati, vismita and pratighāta (gloss: body hair, or delighted) are also set forms (nipātana).

avacitaśca. "And apacita as well." By adding ta to vaca preceded by the negative nañ, apacita too is a set form.

byāyaḥpīḥ. "Of pyāyī, pī." Before niṣṭhā, pyāyī becomes pī. Kta is added to opyāyī (gloss: considered; destroyed individually); by this sūtra it is changed to pī, and by the rule on those marked with o and the rest, t is changed to n: pīnaṃ mukhaṃ (gloss: a full face). The commentary explains that when a preverb comes before it (gloss: uncooked), it is not changed to pī. Kta is added to pyāyī preceded by pra; by the rule of elision of v and y, the y is dropped; and by the rule on those marked with o and the rest, t is changed to n: prapyānaṃ, and so on.

ādpūrvasyāndhudhasoḥ. "When preceded by āṅ, for a well and for an udder." When pyāyī preceded by āṅ, before niṣṭhā, is used of a well or of an udder, it becomes pī: āpīno'ndhūḥ, āpīnamūṅhaḥ.

dyatisyitimīsthāmitkati. "Dyati, syati, mā and sthā take it before what is marked with k" (gloss: greatly increased). Dyati, that is, do, dividing in two; syati, that is, ṣo, bringing to an end; māṅ, measuring with respect; and sthā, standing: when an affix beginning with t and marked with k follows, their final is changed to it: ditāḥ, sitaḥ, mitaḥ (gloss: a well, its source swollen; an udder swollen), sthitaḥ.

śācho'anyarasyāṃ. "Optionally, of śā and chā." The final of śo, making thin, and of cho, cutting, is optionally changed to it: śitaḥ, śātaḥ; chitaḥ, chātaḥ. The commentary says that śyaiṅ, going, becomes it: śyitaḥ (gloss: cut into pieces, brought to an end, revered).

dadhāherhiḥ (gloss: stood). "Of dadhāti, hi." When an affix beginning with t and marked with k follows, dadhāti is changed to hi: hitaḥ.

dodarghoḥ. "Of the dā of ghu, dad." When an affix beginning with t (gloss: made thin; already cut) and marked with k follows, the dā called ghu becomes dad (gloss: gone), or alternatively thāṃ: kiṃdattaḥ, kiṃthāntaḥ.

acaupasargātaḥ. "After a preverb ending in a vowel, t." After a preverb ending in a vowel (gloss: held), dāñ becomes t when an affix beginning with t and marked with k follows; the vowel a of ta is for pronunciation. Kta is added to dāñ preceded by pra and by apa, and by this sūtra it is changed to t: prattaḥ, avattaḥ, and so on (gloss: what was given). Since the commentary explains that it is optionally changed to dad: avadattaṃ, pradattaṃ, sudattaṃ, and so on.

dasti. "Before the t of dā." A preverb ending in a vowel of the ik class becomes long before the t into which dā has been changed. Kta is added to dā preceded by ni and by su; by the rule "after a preverb ending in a vowel, t" (gloss: thoroughly given, given all around), dā becomes t; and by this sūtra the vowel is lengthened (gloss: given all around, thoroughly given, well given): nīttaṃ (gloss: given by that), sūttaṃ (gloss: well given). Excellent.

To dheṭ, drinking; gai, sound; and vā, drinking, kta is added; by ghumāsthā and the rest they are changed to ī: dhītaṃ (gloss: drunk), gītaṃ (gloss: song), pītaṃ (gloss: drunk), and so on.

To jan, san and khan, kta is added; by the rule on jan, san and khan before a jhal consonant, they are changed to āt: jātaṃ, sātaṃ, vātaṃ.

adojagdhilyaphikiti. "Of ad, jagdhi, before lyap and before t marked with k." When lyap, which replaces ktvā, or an affix with t marked with k, follows, ad, eating, becomes jagdhi. Kta is added to ad, eating; by this sūtra ad is changed to jagdhi, the i being for pronunciation; by jhaṣ and the rest, t becomes dh; and by the rule on a jhar before a similar jhar (gloss: born, given, dug), the former dh is dropped: jagṅhaḥ.

vākrośadainyayoḥ. "Optionally, for abusive speech and for dejection." When the niṣṭhā of kṣi, wasting, is used for abusive speech or for dejection, the vowel is optionally lengthened: kṣīṇimanana, kṣiṇaṃmanena; kṣīṇāyuḥ, kṣiṇāyuḥ.

ninadībhyāṃsnātekauśale. "After ni and nadī, of snāti, for skilfulness" (gloss: eaten). After ni and nadī, the letter s of snāti becomes ṣ when skilfulness (kauśala) is expressed: niṣṭhātaḥ, nadīṣṭhātaḥ.

gatyārthākarmane'dhāreca. "For verbs meaning going and for verbs without an object (gloss: thinks it wasted; greatly wasted), and for the locus as well." For verbs whose action is going and for verbs without an object, kta comes, from the sense of the action, for the locus, and for the agent too: idameṣāṃ yātaḥ, iha te āsitaḥ.

śliṣaśīṅsthāsavasajanaru (gloss: bé dak; a pure river) hajvṝbhyaḥ. "From śliṣ, śīṅ, sthā, ās, vas, jan, ruh and jṝ." After śliṣ and these others, kta comes for the agent: āśliṣṭaḥ, adhiśayitaḥ, upasthitaḥ, upāsitaḥ, anūṣitaḥ (gloss: this one went to this; he stays here), anujātaḥ, ārūḍhaḥ, anujīrṇaḥ.

āhārārthāt. "From verbs meaning food." After verbs meaning food, kta comes for the locus: idameṣāṃbhuktaṃ, idameṣāṃ pītaṃ.

ñītaḥktaḥ. "From those marked with ñ, kta" (gloss: attained or connected; lay over; stood near; was near; dwelt after; born after; mounted, or standing, or placed; aged after). After roots marked with ñ, kta comes for the present. By adding kta to ñikṣvid, becoming moist (gloss: these were eaten by this one; these were drunk by this one): kṣviṇṇaḥ (gloss: makes moist), and so on.

matibutdhipūjārthebhyaśca. "And from verbs meaning thinking, understanding and worship." After man, budh and pūja, when their meanings are expressed, kta also comes for the present: rājñīmataḥ, iṣṭabuṅṅhaḥ, devapūjitaḥ.

nabunsakebhāvektaḥ. "For the state, in the neuter, kta." After a root, when a state is expressed and takes the neuter gender, kta comes: hasitaṃ, jalpitaṃ, and so on.

liṭaḥkānjrā. "Of liṭ, kānac, optionally." In the sense of the action, liṭ optionally becomes kānac (gloss: the king's understanding; regarded as awakened; worshipped by the gods). The c serves accent, and the k serves the purpose of kit. To kṛ, liṭ is added; it is reduplicated; ṛ becomes at; by the rule on k and h becoming c; liṭ is changed to kānac (gloss: laughter, or laughing; muttered); and by ik before ac it is changed to yaṇ: cakrāṇaḥ, and so on.

kvasuśca. "And kvasu as well." In the sense of the action, liṭ optionally becomes kvasu. The u serves the purpose of num, and the k serves the purpose of kit: cakṛvān, upaśuśrūvān, jagmivān, and so on.

vasvekājādghasāṃ. "Of single-vowel roots, of those ending in ā, and of ghas, before vasu." Before vasu, that is, kvasu substituted for liṭ, following roots having a single vowel (gloss: made), roots ending in ā, and ghas, iṭ comes. Ad, eating: ādipān (gloss: eaten, made, listened closely). Ṛ, going: āripān (gloss: gone, gone). Dā: dadivān (gloss: given). Dhā: dadhivān (gloss: held). Ad is changed to ghasḷ: jakṣivān (gloss: food). And so on.

vibhāṣāgamahanavidaviśāṃ. "Optionally, of gam, han, vid and viś." Before kvasu following gam and these others, iṭ optionally comes: jagmivān (gloss: gone), jagamvān; jaghnivān (gloss: gone), jagnanvān; vividivān (gloss: knew), vividvān; viviśvān. Since the commentary explains that iṭ is optional also before kvasu following dṛś: dadṛśivān, dadṛśvān.

dāśvānsāhvānīyavānca. "Dāsvān, sāhvān, and īyavān as well." By changing liṭ to kvasu for dāś, not seeing; ṣah, enduring; and iṇ, going, the forms dāsvān, sāhvān (gloss: sat, sat) and iyavān are set forms (nipātana).

laṭaḥśatṛśānacausamānādhikaraṇe. "For co-reference (gloss: looked), śatṛ and śānac of laṭ." In the sense of co-reference, laṭ commonly becomes śatṛ and śānac. The two ś's serve the purpose of śit; the c (gloss: not seeing; endured) serves accent; and the ṛ (gloss: gone) serves the purpose of num. To paca, laṭ is added; laṭ is changed to śatṛ; for the agent, śap; and by the rule on at before guṇa, the following form replaces both: pacan.

ānemuk. "Before āna, muk." When āna, that is, śānac, follows a stem ending in at, the augment muk comes. To paca, laṭ and śap are added; laṭ is changed to śānac; and by this sūtra muk is added: pacamdanaḥ. Likewise, for vṛtu, occurring: vartamānaḥ, and so on (gloss: cooks).

lakṣaṇahetvoḥkriyāyāḥ. "For an action that is a characteristic or a cause." When an action that is a characteristic or a cause is to be understood, laṭ becomes śatṛ and śānac: prapīyan (gloss: makes one drink thoroughly), prapīyamānaḥ.

ī (gloss: cooks) dāsaḥ. "From ās, īt" (gloss: makes to enter, or the present). After ās, sitting near, the ā of śānac substituted for laṭ is changed to īt: āsīnaḥ.

videḥśaturvasuḥ. "After vidi, vasu for śatṛ." After vid, knowing (for those ending in prāyat, laṭ is changed to śatṛ and śānac), the śatṛ substituted for laṭ is optionally changed to vasu: vidan, vidvān.

tausat. "Those two are sat." Śatṛ and śānac are given the name sat (gloss: sits).

lṛṭaḥsadvā. "Of lṛṭ, sat, optionally." Lṛṭ too is optionally and commonly changed to sat, that is, to śatṛ and śānac. To kṛñ, lṛṭ is added; by syatāsī and the rest, sya is added (gloss: makes known, or makes understood); iṭ is added at the start of what begins with val; and by this sūtra lṛṭ is changed to sat: karidhyān, kariṣyamāna, and so on.

pūdyajoḥśānan. "After pūṅ and yaja, śānan." After pūṅ, purifying, and yaj, worshipping the gods, laṭ is changed to śānan; the final n serves accent: pābamānaḥ, yajamānaḥ.

ticchālyavayovacanaśaktiṣuśānaca. "For habitual disposition, for expressing age (gloss: will play), and for capacity, śānac." When a habitual disposition, an expression of age, or a capacity is to be understood, laṭ is changed to śānac: katīhanṛtyamānaḥ, "how many here are dancing?" (gloss: purifies; worships); katīhajalpamānaḥ, "how many here are talking?"; katīhakaṇṭuṃghnānaḥ, "how many here are destroying thorns?"

iṅdhāryoḥśatrukṛchriṇi. "From iṅ and dhṛ, for an enemy and for something difficult." After iṅ, reading, and dhṛñ, holding, respectively, when an enemy or something difficult is to be understood, laṭ becomes śatṛ: adhīyan, ṅharan, and so on.

ākvestacchīlataddhārmatatsādhukāriṣu. "Up to kvip, for those whose disposition is that, whose custom (dharma) is that, and who do that well." This is the general rule that the affixes from kvip up to tṛc apply in the senses of having that disposition, having that custom, and doing that well (gloss: reads; holds).

alaṃkṛñnirākṛñjanotpaconmadarucyapatrapagṛtuvṛdhusahacaraiṣṇucaḥ. "From alaṃkṛñ, nirākṛñ, jana, utpata, utpaca, unmada, ruci, apatrapa, pṛtu, vṛdhu, saha and cara, iṣṇuc." After kṛñ preceded by alaṃ and by nirā, jana, pata, paca and mada preceded by ut, ruca, trapūṣ preceded by apa, vṛtu, vidhi, saha and cara, iṣṇuc comes: alaṃkarṛṣṇuḥ, nirākarṛṣṇuḥ, prajaniṣṇuḥ, utpatiṣṇuḥ, utpaciṣṇuḥ, unmadiṣṇuḥ, rociṣṇuḥ, apatrapiṣṇuḥ, vartiṣṇuḥ, varthiṣṇuḥ, sahiṣṇuḥ, cariṣṇuḥ.

bhuvaśca. "And from bhū." After bhū, iṣṇuc comes, and by the word "also" it comes for others too: bhaviṣṇuḥ, bhrājiṣṇuḥ, and so on.

ṇaḥ (gloss: adorns, disparages, born forth or creatures, falls from on high, cooks thoroughly, mad, ray of light, ashamed) chandasi (gloss: occurring, growing, enduring, moving about). "From ṇi, in metrical language." After a root ending in ṇic, in metrical language (chandas), iṣṇuc comes: karayiṣṇuḥ (gloss: arisen; cooks).

glājisthaścaksnuḥ. "From glā, ji and sthā, ksnu as well." After glā, ji and sthā, ksnu comes as well, and by the word "also" it comes after bhū too: glāsnuḥ, jiṣṇuḥ, sthāsnuḥ (gloss: abiding), bhūṣṇuḥ.

hrasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣepeknuḥ. "From trasi, gṛdhi, dhṛṣi and kṣeba, knu." After trasi and these others (gloss: made), knu comes: trasnuḥ, gṛrnūḥ, ghraṣṇuḥ (gloss: brazen, or impudent), kṣisnuḥ (gloss: throwing away). The commentary says that snu also comes after mlā, kṣi, paca and parimṛja (gloss: sick; conquering; in a set form, īt does not come; arisen): mlāsnuḥ (gloss: sick), kṣeṣṇuḥ (gloss: wasted), pakṣṇu (gloss: cooks), parimikṣṇuḥ (gloss: thoroughly purified).

cāla (gloss: frightened; desiring) śabhāṇhākarmakātyuca. "From roots meaning going and sound that take no object, yuc."

After cal and the rest, which mean moving or going, and du and the rest, which mean sound, when they take no object, yuc comes for habitual disposition and the rest; yu being changed to ana: calanaḥ, copanaḥ, varaṇaḥ, śabdanaḥ.

anudāttetaścahalādeḥ. "And from those marked with an anudātta vowel, when they begin with a consonant." From roots marked with an anudātta and beginning with a consonant, apart from the letter ṅ, which brings in taṅ, of the two, taṅ and ataṅ, yuc comes for habitual disposition and the rest: vajhanaḥ, and so on (gloss: moving; frightened; sound).

laṣapadapatasthvabhūvṛṣahanakamagamaśrībhyaukañ. "From laṣa, pada, sthā, bhū, vṛṣ, han, kama, gama and śṝ, ukañ." After laṣ and these others, ukañ comes for habitual disposition and the rest: apalāṣukaḥ (gloss: increasing), upapādukaḥ, prapātukaḥ, upasnyāyukaḥ, prabhrabukaḥ, vūrṣukaḥ, āghātukaḥ, kāmukaḥ, āgāmukaḥ, praśārukaḥ.

jalpabhikṣukuṭṭaluṇḍavṛṅaḥṣākan. "From jalpa, bhikṣu, kuṭṭa, liṇḍa and priṅ, ṣākan." To jalpa and these others, for habitual disposition and the rest, ṣā (gloss: beautiful all over; going near, or miraculously born; falling thoroughly; dwelling near; arising forth; rain; destroying all around; desirous; going everywhere; living thoroughly) kan comes. The n serves accent, and the ṣ serves the purpose of ṣīṣ: jalpākaḥ, bhikṣākaḥ, kuṇṭākaḥ, luṇṭakaḥ, badākaḥ.

spṛhigṛhipatidayinipratandraśraddhāghyaāluca. "From spṛhi, gṛhi, pati, dayi, nidra, tandra and śraddhā, āluc." To spṛhi and these others, āluc also comes in the sense of one endowed with that habitual disposition and the rest: sprihayāluḥ (gloss: talking, begging, beating, dré dok), spṛhayaluḥ (gloss: reverence), patayāluḥ, dayāluḥ, nidrāluḥ, tandrāluḥ, śraṅdhāluḥ.

dāṅheṭsiśadasadoruḥ. "From dā, ṅheṭ, si, śad and sad, ru." After dā and these others, ru comes for habitual disposition and the rest: dāruḥ (gloss: giving), ṅhāruḥ (gloss: drinking; desirous), seruḥ (gloss: binding; having a household, or possessive; tormented; compassionate; sleepy; lazy; faithful), śadruḥ (gloss: perishing), sadruḥ (gloss: placing).

sṛghasadaḥkamaraca. "From sṛ, ghas and ad, kmarac." After sṛ, ghas and ad, kmarac comes: sṛmaraḥ, ghasmaraḥ, atmaraḥ.

bhañjabhāsamidoghuraca. "From bhañja, bhās and mid, ghurac." To bhañja, bhās and mid also, ghurac comes for habitual disposition and the rest: bhadguraḥ, bhasuraḥ, meduraḥ.

pidibhidichideḥkuraca. "From vidi, bhidi and chidi, kurac." To vidi, bhidi and chidi (gloss: please go; able to eat; able to eat) kurac comes: viduraḥ, bhiduraḥ, chiduraḥ.

iṇanaśijisartibhyaḥkvaraba. "From iṇ, naśi, ji and sṛ (gloss: wood; white stone; ray of light; fatty, or oily), kvarap." After iṇ and these others, kvarap comes: itvaraḥ, naśvaraḥ, jitvaraḥ, sṛtvaraḥ.

yajajapadhadaśoyadaḥ (gloss: wise; destroyer, or vajra; enemy-watcher, or cutter). "From yaja, japa, daha and daśa, with yaṅ." After yaj and these others ending in the affix yaṅ, ūk comes: yāyajūkaḥ, jaṃjapūkaḥ (gloss: going; tuk; perishing; victorious in battle; tuk; going), daṃdahūkaḥ, daṃṅaśūkaḥ.

namikampismyajasakamahiṃsadīporaḥ. "From nami, kampi, smi, ajas, kam, hiṃsa and dīpa, ra." To nami and these others, ra comes: namraḥ, kampraḥ, smeraṃ (gloss: worshipped again and again; muttered again and again), ajasraṃ, kamra, hriṃsraḥ, dīpraḥ.

sanāśaṃsabhikṣauḥ (gloss: burns again and again; eats again and again). "From san, ā-śaṃsa and bhikṣa, u." To roots having the affix san, to āśaṃsa and to bhikṣa, u comes: cikīrṣuḥ, āśansuḥ (gloss: desiring; bowing, or bent; moving, or trembling; smiling; uninterrupted; beautiful, or attached; harming, or sinful; a lamp, or shining), bhikṣu.

vinduricchuḥ. "Vinduḥ and icchuḥ." By adding u to vidi and to iṣu, vinduḥ and icchu are set forms (nipātana).

sahicalahiveḥkikinau. "From sahi (gloss: wishing to do), cali and vahi, ki and kin." To sahi and the others ending in yaṅ, ki and kin come: sāsahiḥ (gloss: endures again and again; one whose disposition is to beg, that is, a monk), cācaliḥ (gloss: moves again and again), vāvahiḥ (gloss: obtains again and again; drop; desiring).

vāpatiḥ. "Pāvati." By adding ki and kin to pad having the affix yaṅ, vāpatiḥ is a set form.

svapitṛponajiṅ. "From svapi and tṛpa, najiṅ." To svapi and tṛpa, najiṅ comes, the d and the i being markers: sāpnaku, tṛpnak.

śṝvanhyorāruḥ. "From śṝ and vanda, āru." After śṝ and vandi, āru comes: śarāruḥ, vandāruḥ.

bhiyaḥkruklukankru (gloss: goes again and again) kanaḥ. "From bhī, kru, klukan and krukan." After bhī, for habitual disposition and the rest, kru, klukan and krukan come: bhīruḥ, bhīluk (gloss: lying; satisfied), bhīrukaḥ.

stheśabhāsapisakasovaraca. "From sthā, īśa, bhāsa, pisa and kas, varac" (gloss: harmful; reverence). After sthā and these others, varac comes: sthāvaraḥ, īśvaraḥ, bhāsvaraḥ, pesvaraḥ.

yaścayaṅ. "And from yā, with yaṅ." After yā, obtaining, having the affix yaṅ (gloss: fearful; fearful), varac also comes: yāyāvaraḥ.

bhrājabhāsadhūrvidyutorjipṝjurgravastuvaḥkvip. "From bhrāja, bhāsa, dhūrva, vityut, urji, pṝ, jur and gravastu, kvip" (gloss: abiding; the Lord; clear; flour). After bhrāja and these others, kvip comes for habitual disposition and the rest: bhrāṭ, btāḥ, ṅhuḥ, vityut, ūrk, pūḥ, jūḥ (gloss: obtains again and again), gravastut.

kvibbaciprachyāyatastukaṭaprujuśrīṇāṃdīrghaśca. "Vaci, praci, āyatastu, kaṭapru, ju and śrī: before kvip, lengthening as well." Before kvip following vaci and these others, samprasāraṇa does not apply and they become long (gloss: cooking; clear; ground; very clear; giving; protecting; sick): vāk (gloss: praise), prāṭ, āyatastūḥ, kaṭaprūḥ, jūḥ, śrīḥ.

tyutikamijuhotīnāṃdveca. "Of dyuti, gami and juhoti, reduplication as well." Before kvip, dyuti, gami and juhoti are also to be reduplicated: didyuta, jagata.

juhoterdāerghaśca. "Of juhoti, lengthening as well." Of juhoti (gloss: speech; asking; obtained praise; tsa lhé; gone; glory), before kvip, the final also becomes long. To hu, kvip is added; by the previous sūtra it is reduplicated, and by this one lengthened: juhūḥ (gloss: given).

bhūvaḥsaṃjñānhrarayoḥ. "From bhū, for a name and for what comes after it" (gloss: clear; sopa).

After dhū following a name or a preverb, kvip comes: midtabhūḥ (gloss: having friends), pratibhūḥ (gloss: become separately).

viprasaṃbhyoḍāsaṃjñāyāṃ. "After vi, pra and saṃ, where it is not a name, ḍu." After bhū following vi, pra and saṃ, where it is not a name, ḍu comes, and by the rule of ṭi the ṭi is dropped: vibhuḥ, prabhuḥ, sraṃbhuḥ.

dāmnīśasayuyujastuñudasisicamihapatadaṃśanahaḥkaraṇe. "From dāp, nī, śasa, yu, yuja, stu, tud, si, sica, miha, pata, daṃśa and naha, for the instrument." After dāp and these others, tran comes in the sense of the action: dātraṃ, netraṃ, śastraṃ, yotraṃ (gloss: Viṣṇu, the all-pervading lord; master; well arisen), yoktraṃ, stotraṃ, tothraṃ, setraṃ, sektraṃ, meḍhraṃ, pattraṃ, daṃṣhā, naṃḍhraḥ.

artilūdhūsūkhanasahacaraitraḥ. "From ṛ, lū, dhū, sū, khana, saha and cara, itra." After ṛ, going, and these others (gloss: cutting; a leader, or the eye, or silk; a harmer, or a weapon; arranging; a joiner; praise; tormenting; a binder; a scatterer; washing; a vessel, or a leaf; tsa; a binder), itra comes in the sense of the action: aritraṃ, lapitraṃ, savitraṃ, khanitraṃ, sahitraṃ, caritraṃ.

puvaḥsaṃjñāyāṃ. "From pū, for a name." After pūṅ, for a name, iṭ comes: pavitraṃ.

iti pāṇinivyākaraṇasyasūtyātkārakadayaḥsamāptāḥ. Thus, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the agent and the rest are complete. (Gloss: going, cutting, born, digging, enduring, going.)

With these, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down in the form of notes the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and (gloss: pure) commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the coarse account of the domains of application, together with the procedures, of the affixes for the agent and the rest, from among the kṛt affixes and the others, is for the time being complete.

Now I shall explain briefly the domains of application and so on of the affixes to be examined, uṇ and the rest.

uṇādayobahulaṃ. "Uṇ and the rest, variously." The affixes that form nouns applying to all three times are un and the rest. This is the general rule that those affixes apply variously, in the sense of the action and so on.

kṛvāpājimisvadsādhyaśūbhyauṇ. "From kṛ, vā, pā, ji, mi, svada, sādhi and aśū, uṇ." After kṛ, making; vā, going; pā, drinking; ji, conquering; ḍumiñ, increasing greatly; svada, tasting; sādha, accomplishing perfectly; and aśū, pervading, uṇ comes: kāruḥ, vāyuḥ, pāyuḥ, jāyuḥ, māyuḥ, svāduḥ, sādhuḥ, āśuḥ.

gameḍeḥ. "From gama, ḍo." After gamḷ, going, ḍo comes, and by the rule of ṭi the ṭi is dropped: gauḥ.

glānudibhyāṃḍau. "From glā and nuda, ḍau." To glai, the exhaustion of joy, and nud, driving, ḍau comes: glauḥ, nauḥ (gloss: craftsman; wind; anus; conquering; increasing; refined; good; pervading).

sitanigamisasisacyavidhāñkruśabhyastun. "From si, tani, gami, sasi, saci (gloss: from go, ṇit; cow), avi, dhāñ and kruśa, tun." After si, binding; tanu, extending; gamḷ, going (gloss: the moon; a boat); sasi, going about; saci, mixing; avi, protecting; dhāñ, holding; and kruśa, crying out, that is, calling, tun comes: setuḥ, tantuḥ, gantuḥ, sastuḥ, saktuḥ, otuḥ, dhātuḥ (gloss: a verbal root, or an element, or an expanse), sthoṣṭuḥ.

avitṝstvṝtaṃtribhyaḥī. "From av, tṝ, stṝ and tantri, ī." To ap, protecting; tṝ, crossing; stṝñ, covering; and tantrī, tormenting all around, ī comes: avīḥ (gloss: binding; a thread, or a string; going; even; barley flour; by sripi, avi and the rest, the letter p becomes uṭ; a jackal), tarīḥ, starīḥ, tantrī.

lakṣermuṭca. "From lakṣa, and muṭ as well." After lakṣa, ī comes, and the augment muṭ as well: lakṣhyiḥ.

styāyaterḍraṭ. "From styāyati, ḍraṭ." (Gloss: purifying.) To styai, sound and gathering all around, ḍraṭ comes; the ṭ is dropped, and dīp being added: strīḥ.

jṝviśibhyāṃjhata. "From jṛ (gloss: crossing; covering; echo) and viśi, jhat." After jṝ and viśi, jhat comes; the t serves the purpose of its time; and by the rule on jh becoming ant (gloss: glory, or excellence), jh is changed to ant: jarantaḥ (gloss: aged), veśantaḥ (gloss: a portion).

gaṇḍimaṇḍijaninaṃdibhyaśca (gloss: woman). "And from gaṇḍi, maṇḍi, jani and nandi." After gaṇḍa and these others ending in ṇic, jhat also comes. With ṇic: gaṇḍayantaḥ, maṇḍayantaḥ, janayataḥ, nandayantaḥ.

śrudakṣimpṛhigṛhidṛjibhyaāpyaḥ. "From śru, dakṣi, spṛhi, gṛhi, dṛ and ji, āpya." After śru and these others, āpya comes: śravāpyaḥ; with ṇic, dakṣayāvyaḥ, spṛhābhyaḥ, gṛhāpyaḥ, darāpyaḥ, jayāpyaḥ. The commentary cites:

stanidūṣigadihṛdbhyoṇyantebhyaitnuḥ. "From stani, dūṣi, gadi and hṛd, ending in ṇi, itnu." After stani and these others ending in ṇic, itnu comes (gloss: hearing; skilled; desire; appropriating; destroying; conquering), and, as with what is marked with m, vṛddhi is not made: stanayitūḥ, dūṣayitnuḥ, gadayitnuḥ, hṛdayitnuḥ.

kṝgṝstṝjāgṛdbhaḥkvin. "From kṝ, gṝ, stṝ and jāgṛ, kvin." After kṝ and these others, kvin comes: kīrviḥ, gīrviḥ, stīrviḥ, jāgṛviḥ.

As the commentary says, "anyāsyuṇadayaḥ," that is, there are also other affixes, un and the rest (gloss: an udder, or a breast; suffering; speaking; a friend, or one who is like-minded). This indicates that what is explained here of uṇ and the rest is only a rough summary, and that since there are more, at length, elsewhere (gloss: harming; clear; covering; fallen asleep), one should look there.

iti pāṇinivyākaraṇasyasūdhāduṇaduyaḥsamābhāḥ. Thus, from the sūtras of the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, uṇ and the rest are complete.

With these, from The Chariot That Draws the Jewel of Excellent Explanation, which sets down in the form of notes the meaning, the procedures, the examples and so on of the root text and commentary of the great treatise on grammar, the Pāṇinivyākaraṇa, the coarse procedures of un and the rest, which apply to all three times, are for the time being complete.

Now I shall explain the affixes of action and the rest.

tumunṇvulaukriyāyāṃkriyārthāyaṃ. "For an action that is for the purpose of an action, tumun and ṇvul." After a root, when an action for the purpose of another action is expressed, tumun and ṇvul come: duṣṇuṃ (gloss: sick); vu becomes aka: darśakaḥ (gloss: one who makes see).

samānakartṛkeṣutumun. "When the agent is the same, tumun."

In the sense of an action that expresses the same agent, tumun comes: icchati bhoktuṃ.

śakadhṛṣajñāgñāghaṭarabhalabhakamasahārtāstyartheṣutumun. "With śaka, dhṛṣ, jñā, glāṭ, rabha, labha, krama, saha, arha, and verbs meaning to be, tumun." When śaka and these others are present as the accompanying word, tumun comes in the sense of the action (gloss: wishes to eat): śaknoti bhoktuṃ, janati bhoktuṃ, and so on.

kālasamayapelāsuḥtumun. "With kāla, samaya and velā, tumun." When kāla, samaya or velā is the accompanying word, tumun comes: kāla bhoktuṃ, samaya bhoktuṃ, vela bhoktuṃ.

bhrāvapacanāśca. "And for expressing the state" (gloss: is able to eat; knows how to eat). When it is used in a future sense, tumun comes for expressing the state: pākaḥ, pāktūṃ; tyaktuṃ, tyāgaḥ; and so on.

padarujaviśaspṛśobhhañ (gloss: the time for eating; the appointed time for eating; the hour for eating). "From pada, ruja, viśa and spṛśa, ghañ." After pada and these others, ghañ comes in all three times: pādaḥ, rogaḥ, veśaḥ, sparśa (gloss: ripened, or cooked; scattered).

byādhimatsabaleṣuca. "And for disease, fish and strength." When disease, fish or strength is expressed, and also with many others preceded by a preverb, ghañ comes: byādhiviśeṣaḥ, visāraḥ (gloss: foot; disease; attire; touch), matsyaḥ, sāraḥ, balaṃ, prasāraḥ, susāraḥ, and so on.

ikaḥkāśe. "Of ik, before kāśa." A preverb ending in a vowel of the ik class is to be lengthened before kāśa having the affix ghañ: nīkarśaḥ (gloss: a particular kind of disease; going apart, that is), anūkāśaḥ, and so on (ha) (gloss: the essence, that is, strength; going forth; going well). When it does not end in ik, this does not happen: prakāśaḥ.

erca. "From i, ac." From roots ending in the letter i, it is not ghañ that comes for the state but ac itself (gloss: clear on its face): jayaḥ (gloss: victory; clear afterward), cayaḥ (gloss: accumulating).

ṝdorapa. "From ṝ and u, ap." From roots ending in ṝ and in the letter u (gloss: thoroughly clear), ap comes: kṝ, karaḥ (gloss: hand); gṛ, giraḥ; yu, yavaḥ; pū, pavaḥ.

iṅaśca. "And from iṅ." After iṅ, reading, ghañ also comes: upādhyāyaḥ, upādhyāyī.

prathaneviraśabde. "For spreading, after vi, where it is not sound." When spreading is expressed, after stṛ following vi, where it is not sound (gloss: compounded poison; barley; purifier), ghañ comes: paṭasya vistāraḥ. When it is sound, ac is added: pākyamya vistāraḥ (gloss: female teacher).

ghañapośca. "And before ghañ and ap." Before ghañ and ap, ad, eating, becomes ghasḷ: ghāsaḥ.

upasargeñadaḥ. "From ad, after a preverb." After ad preceded by a preverb (gloss: the cloth is spread), ap comes. With pra before it (gloss: speech expanded), ap is added to ada by this sūtra, and by the previous sūtra ad is changed to ghasḷ: praghasaḥ.

samudojaḥpaśuṣa. "After saṃ and ud, from aja, for livestock" (gloss: food). After aj following saṃ and ud, when livestock is the object expressed, ap comes: samajaḥ, udajaḥ. When it is not livestock, ghañ is added: samājo brāhmaṇanaṃ, and so on.

hanaścavaṅhaḥ. "And of han, vadha" (gloss: eaten thoroughly). Ap comes to han without a preverb, and before ap han itself becomes vadh: vaṅhaḥ. Alternatively, ghañ being added: gphātaḥ (gloss: a herd of livestock; driving livestock).

karmavyatitāreṇacastriyāṃ (gloss: an assembly of brahmins). "For reciprocal action, ṇac, in the feminine." For reciprocal action, ṇac comes, and it is optionally also in the feminine gender.

ṇacastriyāmañ (gloss: harming). "From ṇac, for the feminine (gloss: harming), añ." After what ends in ṇac, when the feminine is expressed, añ comes.

nakarmapyatehāre. "Not for reciprocal action." Although it was explained above that añ applies to what ends in ṇac when the feminine is expressed, as an exception to that, where the ṇac is given in the sense of reciprocal action, añ does not come. To hasa preceded by vi, āṅ and ava, ṇac is added; by this sūtra añ does not come; and dīp being added: byāvahāsī (gloss: filled).

ibhibaṃdtaubhabaanuṇa. "For the state of full pervasion, inuṇ." When the state of full pervasion is expressed, inuṇ comes: saṃrāviṇaṃ.

aṇinuṇa. "From inuṇ, aṇ." After what has the affix inuṇ, aṇ comes in its own sense; with hīpa: surāvaṇī.

upasargātakhalubhañoḥ. "After a preverb, before khal and ghañ." When khalu or bhañ follows labha preceded by a preverb, the augment num comes: pralaṃbhaḥ (gloss: fully pervaded by sound).

nasudurbhyāṃ. "Not after su and dur." After labha following su and dur, num (gloss: she who is fully pervaded by sound) does not come: sulabhaḥ, durlabhaḥ.

spurtisphulatyorghañe. "Of sphurati and sphulati, before ghañ." The vowel of sphurati and sphulati (gloss: thoroughly obtained) becomes āt before ghañ: spāraḥ, spālaḥ.
